# Decision Log

Locked decisions were made by the owner during planning on 23 October 2026. Do not change a locked decision without the owner's approval. Claude Code adds new entries in the last section using the same format.

Entry format:

```
D<number>: <decision>
Status: Locked | Default | Open | Superseded by D<number>
Reason: <why>
```

## Locked decisions

D1: The app is named FDCAD ("Fully Defined CAD"). Native files use the `.fdef` extension.
Status: Locked
Reason: Easter egg for CAD users (a fully defined sketch), no conflicting software or file extension found. Earlier candidate names were rejected for trademark or tone reasons.

D2: License is GPL v3 or later.
Status: Locked
Reason: Derivatives must stay open source.

D3: Platforms are macOS on Apple Silicon and Windows x64. No Intel Mac build. No web or browser version.
Status: Locked
Reason: OCP ships separate Intel and Apple Silicon Mac packages, and GitHub is retiring Intel Mac runners. A browser version would need a different, slower, less proven stack.

D4: Released on GitHub only, unsigned. Mac DMG (ad hoc signed), Windows installer.
Status: Locked
Reason: No app store distribution; no paid signing certificates.

D5: Stack is Python 3.13, PySide6, OCP (OpenCascade), planegcs, OpenCascade's own viewer.
Status: Locked
Reason: Native kernel speed with fast development. planegcs supports Python 3.12 and later; the SolveSpace Python bindings stop at Python 3.11.

D6: Scope is part modeling plus basic sheet metal. Out of scope: surface tools, mass properties, assemblies, drawings, weldments, sheet metal edge cases. Amended by the owner on 23 October 2026: a volume and print weight estimate is allowed (D29). Amended by the owner on 2026-11-02 (D750): full mass properties, part material, centre of mass and section properties are now in scope (TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC_2 TR78 to TR81).
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's scope choice.

D7: Native format is `.fdef`, plain JSON with an open published schema (`FDEF_SPEC.md`). Imported STEP data is embedded in the file. The solid cache is stored locally, not in the file. Part and face colours are stored.
Status: Locked
Reason: Human readable, diffable, documented. No existing open format fits a feature tree of this kind.

D8: Exports are STEP (AP214 default, AP242 option) and STL. Import is STEP as a non editable base body. build123d Python script export is added in Phase 5. Extended by D28 with 3MF, DXF and SVG export and mesh import.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice.

D9: Units are chosen per part (mm or inch) in the New Part dialog, with the preselected default set in preferences. Fields accept mm, cm, m, in, ft, fractions, mixed numbers, feet and inches, arithmetic, global variables and radians. Micrometres are not accepted.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice.

D10: Topological naming uses origin based names first, a stored position snapshot as fallback, a yellow warning when the fallback is used and a red error when no confident match exists.
Status: Locked
Reason: Names survive dimension changes; positions survive renumbering. Never guess silently.

D11: Feature names use FDCAD's own style, for example "Extrude 1", "Fillet 2". Owner approved on 2026-10-29: names are a plain generic word, a space and a number ("Extrude 1", "Cut 1", "Revolve 1", "Revolve Cut 1", "Sketch 1", "Fillet 1", "Shell 1"), never hyphenated.
Status: Locked
Reason: Stay clearly distinct from commercial products.

D12: UI follows familiar CAD conventions (feature tree, property panel, command tabs, status bar) with original icons, colours and generic terminology. Light and dark themes plus follow system.
Status: Locked
Reason: Familiar workflow without copying any product's identity.

D13: Default shortcuts and gestures come from the owner's existing mapping (`SHORTCUTS.md`). On Mac, Ctrl becomes Cmd except where it collides with macOS system shortcuts; those stay on the Control key.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's muscle memory, adapted to Mac conventions.

D14: Shift+S is swept boss (the owner's original mapping pointed at a surface command, which is out of scope).
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice.

D15: Development is done by Claude Code from these planning files, with one owner review per phase.
Status: Locked
Reason: Minimal owner input.

## Defaults set during planning

These were set during planning rather than chosen explicitly by the owner. Claude Code treats them like locked decisions; the owner may change them at any time.

D16: Part gestures: up top view, left left view, right right view, down bottom view.
Status: Default (unconfirmed, owner may adjust in the gesture editor)
Reason: Read from the owner's gesture screenshot; icons were too small to confirm.

D17: Autosave every 5 minutes. Update check off by default. No telemetry.
Status: Default
Reason: Safety and privacy.

D18: Default planes follow the common convention: Front is XY, Top is XZ, Right is YZ, Y is up.
Status: Default
Reason: Familiar to users of mainstream CAD tools.

D19: On Mac, Cmd+Shift+Z keeps the owner's mapping (previous view). Redo is Cmd+Y. Changed by the owner on 2026-11-02 (D750, TR375): on a Mac, Redo also takes Cmd+Shift+Z and Previous View moves; the implementer records the new Previous View key.
Status: Default (owner may change in the shortcut editor)
Reason: Owner's mapping takes priority over the usual Mac redo shortcut.

D20: On Mac, full screen is also available on Control+Cmd+F (the macOS standard), because F11 shows the desktop on most Mac keyboards.
Status: Default
Reason: Avoid a system shortcut collision.

D21: Design tables are stored inside the `.fdef` and edited in a built in table editor, with CSV import and export. Excel files are not required.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeps the file self contained and avoids an Excel dependency.

## Locked decisions added 23 October 2026: Rhino and Grasshopper style tools

D22: Add Rhino style solid and curve tools: pipe, array along curve, transform handles, contour curves and curvature graph in Phase 3; flow along curve, twist, bend, taper and stretch in Phase 4. No surface tools; D6 is unchanged.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice (groups 1 and 2, no surfacing).

D23: Add a Grasshopper style node editor as Phase 7 (v1.1), after v1.0. Nodes both drive variables and feature parameters, and generate geometry that is added to the feature tree as a `graph_body` feature.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice. The core modeler ships stable first.

D24: No code execution from files. There is no script node; graph expressions use the safe expression parser only.
Status: Default
Reason: A shared `.fdef` must never be able to run code on the reader's computer.

D25: Deformations work by converting the body to NURBS, moving control points, then rebuilding and validating the solid.
Status: Default
Reason: OpenCascade has no native solid deformation; this is the established approach.

D26: A graph has a position in the feature tree. It reads model geometry only from features above that position, and no feature above it may use a value the graph drives.
Status: Default
Reason: Prevents rebuild cycles between the graph and the model.

D27: Files that contain graphs are saved as schema 2 so that versions without the node editor refuse to open them instead of silently ignoring the graph.
Status: Default
Reason: Avoids silent data loss.

D28: Add 3D printing and prototyping tools: 3MF export (Phase 1); DXF and SVG export, open in slicer, overhang analysis, build volume check, sketch picture (Phase 2); direct face editing, split for printing, scale, mesh import (Phase 3); fit presets, heat set insert and nut trap holes, modeled threads, fastening features, wall thickness analysis (Phase 4); flat pattern DXF and SVG (Phase 5).
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice (all 14 proposed tools).

D29: Add a volume and print weight estimate (volume times material density) in the Evaluate tab. Full mass properties stay out of scope. Amended by the owner on 2026-11-02 (D750): full mass properties are now in scope (TR79).
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice; useful for printing without the full mass properties tool.

D30: The 3MF writer is written in house, since OpenCascade has no 3MF support. It covers the 3MF core specification: units, multiple bodies and colours.
Status: Default
Reason: Small, well defined format; avoids a new dependency.

D31: Printer profiles (build volume, fit tolerance, overhang angle, minimum wall thickness, slicer application) and material densities are app preferences, not stored in `.fdef` files. The chosen print orientation is stored in the file (`print_setup`).
Status: Default
Reason: Printer settings belong to the user's machine; orientation belongs to the part.

D32: Heat set insert hole sizes come from common published insert dimensions in an editable table. Users can add their own sizes.
Status: Default
Reason: Insert sizes vary by manufacturer; no single standard exists.

D33: Imported meshes and sketch pictures are embedded in the `.fdef` (gzip and base64), like imported STEP.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeps files self contained (same reason as D7).

D34: Claude Code runs on the owner's Windows x64 PC. Mac builds and tests run in CI only.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice. planegcs and OCP ship prebuilt Windows packages, so local setup is simple.

D35: The GitHub repository stays private until the owner makes it public. While private, Mac CI runs only on pull requests to `main`, version tags and manual runs.

D36: Copyright holder in LICENSE and file headers is the owner's GitHub handle, Muffism.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice.

D37: Default printer profile is a generic printer with a 220 x 220 x 250 mm build volume. Open in slicer uses the system's default app for 3MF files unless the user sets one.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice.

D38: Display precision is adjustable from 0 to 8 decimal places per unit, default 2 for mm and 3 for inches. Values are stored and computed at full double precision regardless of display.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner wanted at least 5 decimals in mm. 8 matches common CAD practice and stays above the kernel's modeling tolerance (0.0000001 mm), so extra digits are never misleading.

D39: English only for now, with all UI strings in one module. Bundled fonts use the SIL Open Font License. Docs and sample parts use the same GPL license as the code.
Status: Default

D40: CI runs engine tests headless and UI tests on Qt's offscreen platform. The real 3D viewport is checked by hand by the owner in Phase 0 and in every phase review.
Status: Default

## Locked decisions added 23 October 2026: performance

D41: Speed and memory use are first class requirements from Phase 1, with budgets enforced as automated tests (`PLAN.md` section 11).
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice.

D42: Budgets are measured on two baseline machines: the owner's MacBook Air M1 (2020), assuming 8 GB RAM, and a mid range Windows laptop (4 cores, 16 GB RAM, integrated graphics). The owner's MacBook Air is also used for every manual Mac check.
Status: Locked
Reason: The owner has this Mac. It is fanless and throttles under load, so it is a realistic low end target.

D43: The app is packaged as a PyInstaller one folder build, not a single file build.
Status: Default
Reason: Single file builds unpack to a temporary folder on every launch, which slows startup.

D44: The disk cache uses OpenCascade's binary BRep format. The in memory cache is capped at 25 percent of system RAM or 2 GB, whichever is smaller.
Status: Default
Reason: Fast loading and predictable memory use on 8 GB machines.

## Locked decisions added 23 October 2026: geometry robustness

D45: Add the geometry robustness measures in `PLAN.md` section 5A: tolerant booleans, zero thickness detection, unexpected body warnings, pre checks, pinpointing, errors panel, sketch checks and a geometry check tool. Foundations in Phase 1, the rest in Phase 2.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice, to reduce the zero thickness, non merged body and geometry failures common in mainstream CAD.

D46: Fixes for geometry errors are offered as one click buttons that the user confirms. Geometry is never changed automatically.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner's choice.

D47: Default boolean fuzzy tolerance is 0.00001 mm. Default zero thickness fix adds 0.01 mm to the responsible dimension.
Status: Default
Reason: Small enough not to affect real geometry, large enough to absorb rounding from unit conversion.

## Decisions added during development

(Claude Code adds entries from D52 onward.)

D52: Free models served by the owner's local FreeLLMAPI router are used as helpers. Claude stays in charge and writes the core and hard code (kernel, naming, rebuild, solver wrapper, architecture). Free models may draft docs, tests, boilerplate and repetitive code. Claude reviews every line before it is committed. Amends D49 for helper work only.
Status: Locked (owner approved, 23 October 2026)
Reason: Owner's choice, to save Claude usage without lowering quality.

D53: Initial pinned versions on Windows: Python 3.13.17, cadquery-ocp 8.0.1.1.0, planegcs 0.9.6, PySide6 6.12.0, numpy 2.5.4. Exact versions live in `uv.lock`.
Status: Default
Reason: Latest releases at project start; all installed from prebuilt Windows wheels and passed a smoke test (OCP box volume, planegcs import, PySide6 import).

D54: Git commits use the name Muffism and the GitHub noreply address, so no personal email enters the history.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner's choice; the repository may become public later.

D55: `executing-plans` from obra/superpowers calls helper scripts stored in `subagent-driven-development/scripts` and reads `requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md`. Those files are copied too, but their folders have no `SKILL.md`, so the two excluded skills stay inactive. Source commit is recorded in `.claude/skills/SUPERPOWERS_NOTICE.md`.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeps `executing-plans` working without adding the skills excluded by D51.

D56: Python code lives in `src/fdcad` (the uv `src` layout), not `fdcad/` at the repo root. Everything else follows `PLAN.md` section 4.
Status: Default
Reason: The `src` layout stops tests importing the working folder by accident and is what `uv init` creates.

D57: The UI dependency is `pyside6-essentials` (core Qt modules), not the `pyside6` meta package. Same PySide6, same LGPL 3 license.
Status: Default
Reason: The meta package adds Qt WebEngine, PDF and add-on modules FDCAD does not use, about 580 MB in the environment and a much larger installer.

D58: Pinned developer tools: ruff 0.17.2, mypy 2.4.0, pytest 9.1.1, pytest-qt 4.5.0, pre-commit 4.7.0, PyInstaller 6.22.3. Exact versions live in `uv.lock`. Licenses: MIT (ruff, mypy, pytest, pytest-qt, pre-commit), GPL 2 with bootloader exception (PyInstaller, which allows any license for the bundled app).
Status: Default
Reason: Latest releases at project start. None of them is shipped as part of FDCAD except the PyInstaller bootloader.

D59: The viewport embeds OpenCascade with `Aspect_NeutralWindow` given the Qt widget's native handle (HWND on Windows, NSView on macOS), on a native `QWidget` with no Qt painting. Sizes and mouse positions are passed to OpenCascade in device pixels. Qt's high DPI rounding policy is `PassThrough`, so fractional Windows scaling (125, 150 percent) stays exact.
Status: Default
Reason: One code path for both platforms, no platform window classes, and correct Retina and high DPI output. Verified on Windows at 1x and 2x scale.

D60: The bundle excludes the `vtk` and `matplotlib` Python packages, which `cadquery-ocp` installs but FDCAD never imports. The VTK DLLs (about 130 MB) stay, because the single OCP binary links against them. Windows build: 389 MB folder, 70 MB installer.
Status: Default
Reason: Removing the DLLs needs a custom OCP build, which is not worth it before v1.0.

D61: File type identifiers: Windows ProgID `FDCAD.Part`, MIME type `application/vnd.fdcad.part+json`, macOS bundle id `org.fdcad.FDCAD` and exported type `org.fdcad.part` conforming to `public.json`. The Windows installer AppId is `8F3C2A71-5D4E-4B9A-9C61-2E7F0D5A3B14` and must never change. The installer lets the user choose an all users or a per user install, and writes the association under `HKA` to match.
Status: Default
Reason: Stable identifiers are needed so upgrades replace the old install and keep the association.

D62: Commit hooks use pre-commit with local hooks that run `uv run ruff format` and `uv run ruff check --fix`. Mypy and pytest run in CI, not on every commit.
Status: Default
Reason: Local hooks use the pinned tools and need no downloads. Type checks and tests are too slow for every commit.

D63: The release workflow installs Inno Setup with Chocolatey and calls `ISCC.exe` by its full path from PowerShell, because Git Bash rewrites the `/D` switch as a file path. Line endings are LF in the repository (`.gitattributes`).
Status: Default
Reason: Chocolatey does not put ISCC on the PATH. LF endings are required for the macOS shell scripts and stop git line ending warnings on Windows.

D64: The Mac build installs Boost headers from Homebrew as well as Eigen (`brew install eigen boost`), because planegcs 0.9.6 needs both to compile from source. Boost is used only at build time, under the Boost Software License 1.0, which is GPL compatible.
Status: Default
Reason: The first Mac CI run failed with "Could NOT find Boost". `PLAN.md` and `CLAUDE.md` mention only Eigen.

D65: Releases numbered 0.0.x are published as GitHub pre-releases. Pull requests to `main` build both installers and smoke test the packaged app, without publishing.
Status: Default
Reason: v0.0.1 only proves the technical pipeline (owner question, 24 October 2026). Building installers on pull requests caught two packaging bugs before release.

D66: Expression rules not fixed by `FDEF_SPEC.md` section 12. (1) A formula (`=`) whose result is a plain number takes the field's default unit: the part unit for lengths, degrees for angles. Only mixing a plain number with a length or angle by `+` or `-` is an error inside formulas. (2) Outside formulas, a bare number added to a length or angle takes the part unit or degrees; in `*` and `/` it stays a plain number, so `2in * 3` is 6 in. (3) `number/number` directly after each other is a fraction, so `10/2in` is 5 in, except right after a division sign: `24mm / 2 / 3` is 4 mm. (4) Length values written next to each other add up only when both have units (`1' 3"`, `1ft 3in`). (5) `abs`, `round`, `min` and `max` keep the unit; `round` rounds the internal value (mm or radians). `sqrt` takes plain numbers only. Trig functions take radians, or an angle value. (6) Variables, functions and `pi` are allowed only after `=`. The parser is hand written and never uses `eval`.
Status: Default
Reason: These choices keep everyday typing forgiving (bare numbers just work) while formulas stay strict, as the spec intends.

D67: Default sketch plane axes, with Y up (FDEF_SPEC 5.2). Front (XY): normal +Z, sketch X is +X, sketch Y is +Y. Top (XZ): normal +Y, sketch X is +X, sketch Y is -Z. Right (YZ): normal +X, sketch X is -Z, sketch Y is +Y. Each plane is seen from the positive side of its normal.
Status: Default
Reason: The usual convention for Y up CAD, so sketches look as expected when viewed normal to each plane.

D68: Sketch checks (open contours, branches, duplicates, overlaps, crossings) run in pure Python on a tessellation of 32 segments per arc, with a bounding box filter. Points closer than 0.000001 mm, or joined by a coincident relation, count as one. Profiles are built only from a sketch with no issues; each region becomes one face with its holes, and islands inside holes become new faces.
Status: Default
Reason: Fast enough for Phase 1 sketches and needs no kernel call. Revisit with numpy if sketch checks show up in the performance budgets.

D69: Topological naming implementation. Names live in a list of (name, face) pairs per solid, and one face may carry several names (after faces merge, every old name still resolves). Names pass through each operation by its OpenCascade history (BRepTools_History): unchanged faces keep their names, a face split into several gets `#1`, `#2` ordered by centroid. Every boolean is followed by ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain, so coplanar faces merge and face counts stay stable. Edges and vertices are named on demand from the first name of each neighbouring face. Snapshot fallback accepts only one match within 0.001 mm (centroid), 0.01 percent (area) and the same normal.
Status: Default
Reason: Follows PLAN section 6 and FDEF_SPEC 7 and 8 with the least stored state. Aliases make references survive merges without guessing.

D70: Phase 1 feature details. Through All works for cuts only, in one direction, with a length of twice the part size plus 10 mm. A revolve axis is a line in the same sketch (`refs.axis = {"sketch_entity": "e9"}`); axes from model edges come with reference geometry in Phase 2. The zero thickness fix offers "Add 0.01 mm" to the feature's own depth (D47). OCP 8 collection classes are imported through `fdcad/core/occ.py`.
Status: Default
Reason: Matches common CAD behaviour and keeps Phase 1 references inside the feature tree.

D71: Rebuild caching. Each feature result is cached in memory under a SHA256 key of the feature's canonical JSON, the keys of the features it references, and the key of the part it starts from when it uses the part (solid features and sketches on faces). Results are dropped least recently used first when the estimated size passes the D44 limit; the estimate is 16 KB per face. The disk cache stores only the finished part (BRep binary with triangles, face names by face index, and feature states); intermediate solids stay in memory for now. Values are re-evaluated from their expressions before every rebuild (FDEF_SPEC 3.3).
Status: Default
Reason: Content keys give dependency based rebuild and the per feature cache with one mechanism and no separate dependency graph to keep in sync. Measuring real shape memory is costly; the per face estimate is cheap and errs high.

D72: Sketches are edited in a 2D editor that replaces the 3D view while a sketch is open, always looking normal to the sketch plane. The part's outline on the sketch plane (a plane cut made off the UI thread) is drawn as grey reference. Smart dimension labels are placed automatically beside the geometry; their position is not stored.
Status: Default
Reason: A 2D canvas gives exact picking, smooth dragging and full UI tests on the offscreen platform, which has no GPU (CLAUDE.md 9.8). Every sketch is seen normal to its plane anyway. Storing label positions would need a file format change.

D73: Sketch editing details. A new sketch starts with a fixed construction point at the origin (as in the FDEF_SPEC 6 example), so snapping to the origin is a normal point snap. Snaps add relations: coincident for points, centres, quadrants and curves, midpoint for line midpoints, two coincident relations for intersections; lines within 3 degrees of horizontal or vertical snap to it and get the relation. Points are joined by coincident relations, never shared. Dragging holds the dragged points at the cursor and solves only their connected group; when that conflicts, the solver starts from the cursor and finds the nearest valid position. An entity is drawn as fully defined when holding it in place removes no freedom; this is found by holding groups of points and halving the groups, with coincident points counted once, and runs 120 ms after the last change. Inside an open sketch, undo and redo work on the sketch's own steps; OK writes the whole sketch as one undoable command.
Status: Default
Reason: Matches common CAD behaviour, keeps the file format unchanged, and keeps dragging within the PLAN 11.2 budget (about 7 ms per update at 200 entities).

D74: A sketch on a flat face is placed with its origin at the model origin projected onto the face, and its X axis along model X projected onto the face, or along model -Z when the face is square to X. Seen from outside the part. This matches the default planes (D67), so the same face always gives the same sketch axes whatever OpenCascade's own face axes are.
Status: Default
Reason: Predictable coordinates for sketches on faces, independent of how the kernel built the face.

D75: Viewport input and commands. Picking uses OpenCascade's interactive context on the UI thread; turning a picked face, edge or vertex into a reference (name and snapshot) and finding a face's plane are tiny kernel queries and also run on the UI thread, unlike rebuilds, meshing and booleans (CLAUDE.md rule 2). Hover highlight updates at most 60 times a second. Every command has an id, a label and its SHORTCUTS.md default in `ui/input/commands.py`; the user's changes are stored as overrides, and assigning a used key moves it and names the command that lost it. On macOS, Qt shows Ctrl as Cmd, so only the commands that keep Control list a Mac shortcut ("Meta"). A right drag of 40 pixels or more is a gesture (Control and left drag on a trackpad); a short right click in the 3D view opens the shortcut bar. Repeat last command (Enter or Z) works only while the document area has focus, so Enter in text fields is never taken. Normal To snaps the up direction to the nearest model axis on the face.
Status: Default
Reason: Follows PLAN section 8 and SHORTCUTS.md with one command list for menus, toolbars, shortcuts, gestures and the shortcut bar.

D76: Robustness in the UI. The Errors tab of the left panel lists every warning and error of the last rebuild (errors first), shows the cause and the suggested fixes as buttons, highlights the named faces, edges and vertices in red in the 3D view, and opens the feature. "Add 0.01 mm" changes the value with one undoable command; a formula stays a formula with "+ 0.01mm" added. "Keep separate body" hides that warning for the rest of the session only, because storing it would add a key to the `.fdef` format (a locked decision); the tree still shows the feature in warning colour. A Bodies folder appears at the top of the tree when the part has more than one body, and the status bar shows the body count. Issues carry a short code (for example `zero_thickness`) so the UI can recognise them.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN 5A items 3, 6 and 7 without a file format change.

D77: Faster rebuilds of long trees (measured on the generated 200 feature sample: 42 s down to 1.8 s on the development PC). OCP shape lists are read with `occ.shape_list`, because `list()` on them takes about 1 ms per call. After a boolean, only new edges, and new or changed faces with at most 8 edge loops, are checked for validity; a face with more loops is checked through its new edges, since a full face check compares every pair of loops. Faces and edges are merged (ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain) only when a new edge has two faces on the same surface, or continues another edge between the same two faces; otherwise the merge cannot change the result. Face and edge counts and every face name of all samples were confirmed unchanged. OCP handles are never used as hash keys; shape identity uses OpenCascade maps.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN 11.2 budgets 3 and 4. Untouched geometry was already checked when it was made.

D78: Sample parts are built in code (`fdcad/samples/parts.py`), saved to `samples/` with `uv run python -m fdcad.samples.make`, and checked against golden results in `tests/golden/samples.json` (volume, face and edge counts, optimal bounding box). Every sample sketch is fully defined. The plate is driven by global variables. The generated part is a block with 98 blind holes, each with its own sketch and cut: 200 features after the origin and planes.
Status: Default
Reason: Code is the source of truth, so the files can be regenerated when the format or features change; a test fails when a saved file no longer matches its builder.

D79: Performance tooling. Opening a saved part first shows the finished part from the disk cache (with each feature's state), then runs the full rebuild in the background so later edits use the per feature cache. The budgets of PLAN 11.2 run as tests in `tests/perf` with a 50 percent margin for slower runners; the startup test launches the app with `FDCAD_STARTUP_REPORT` set, which makes it write its startup times and memory to that file and quit. Process memory is the working set on Windows and the peak resident size on macOS (an upper bound). The rebuild statistics panel is in the Tools menu. Measured on the development PC: window visible 0.08 s, ready 0.87 s, 253 MB with an empty part, 232 MB with the 200 feature part, 0.075 s to change a dimension near its end, 1.8 s to rebuild it fully.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN 11.2, 11.3 item 2 and 11.5 item 1.

D106: Context toolbar (owner approved 2026-10-25, Phase 1 corrections). When the user selects a face, plane, edge or feature in the viewport or feature tree, a small floating row of icon buttons appears near the cursor with the common actions for that selection: Sketch (planes and flat faces), Extrude, Edit Feature, Hide, Normal To, Zoom to Selection. It fades when the cursor moves away and never takes focus. Numbered D106 because the Phase 2 to 4 branches already use D80 to D105.
Status: Owner approved
Reason: Owner testing found starting a sketch and editing features took too many clicks. Added to scope by the owner (D48 scope freeze allows owner additions).

D107: Icons (C5) are original SVG files in `src/fdcad/ui/icons/`, drawn on a 24 by 24 grid and named by dotted command ids (`sketch.line.svg`, `feature.extrude.svg`). They use `currentColor` for the main colour and the literal `#ACCENT` for the highlight colour; `fdcad.ui.icons.icon(name)` swaps in the theme's colours, so one file serves light and dark. A missing icon gives an empty icon instead of an error. QtSvg ships with pyside6-essentials, so no new dependency. Numbered D107 for the same reason as D106.
Status: Default
Reason: One recoloured set is easier to keep consistent than two sets, and the plain file names let several people work on icons and the command tabs at once.

D108: Look of the Phase 1 overhaul (L4 to L6). (1) The view toolbar sits in a thin strip just above the 3D view, painted in the view's top background colour, with the icons on a semi transparent plate at the top centre. A real overlay on the native OpenGL view cannot be see through on every platform. (2) The feature tree shows a part name row and a Solid Bodies folder (always, with the body count) above the default planes; the planes are shown before Origin although Origin comes first in the file. Only the display order changes. (3) The Evaluate tab holds Rebuild, Force Rebuild and Rebuild Statistics until the measuring tools arrive. (4) New commands: Zoom to Area (`view.zoom_area`, no default shortcut) and Rebuild Statistics (`tools.stats`). (5) `#DANGER` is a third icon colour, used only for the red cancel mark. (6) Hidden command tabs are saved in the preferences.
Status: Default
Reason: Follows PHASE1_CORRECTIONS L4 to L6 and WORKFLOW_SPEC W7.3, W7.4 and W8 within what Qt can draw reliably.

D109: Feature preview and property panel (C2, L3, L7, W6). Extrude and Revolve build their own solid in `tool()`; `execute()` combines it with the part. `fdcad.core.features.preview.build_preview` uses `tool()` and the last rebuild's results, so the preview shows only the feature's own solid (for a cut, the material it removes) and never rebuilds the whole part. `FeaturePreview` (in `ui/viewport/preview.py`) waits 40 ms after the last change, builds and meshes a private copy on the shared thread pool, and drops stale results by generation number. Drag arrows are small cones made on the worker; while dragging, the view only moves the arrow (no kernel work on the UI thread) and the solid follows when the next preview arrives. Only Extrude has drag handles in Phase 1. `merge` is a new optional boolean on Extrude and Revolve (default true): false keeps a boss as a separate body and silences the separate body warning. It is written only when the panel offers it (a boss after the first body), so older files and cache keys are unchanged. New features are named "Extrude 1", "Cut 1", "Revolve 1" and "Revolve Cut 1" (W6.6), numbered one above the highest number in use. Owner approved the generic names on 2026-10-29.

D110: Tutorial workflow details (docs/WORKFLOW_SPEC.md W1 to W5, C8). (1) Showing or hiding a sketch on purpose is view state of the open part, not saved in the file, so the file format does not change. (2) A sketch nests under the first feature that uses it, unless the rollback bar lies between them. (3) A selected sketch is used by a new feature even when another feature already uses it; with nothing selected, the only unused sketch is used, else a sketch starts for the feature. After OK the new feature is selected so the next command starts fresh. (4) New feature names are generic words with a space and a number: "Extrude 1", "Cut 1", "Revolve 1", "Revolve Cut 1", "Sketch 1"; later types follow the same pattern ("Fillet 1", "Shell 1"). Owner approved on 2026-10-29. `core.features.names.default_name` gives these names, also for sketches. (5) Panel OK while a sketch tool is active ends the tool; a second OK exits the sketch. (6) Centres revealed on round edges of the part outline snap without a relation, since the outline is not part of the sketch. (7) Relation tags leave out corner joins between end points and the origin's fixed relation, to keep the view readable. (8) The trimetric view looks from (0.56, 0.42, 0.72) with Y up. (9) The context toolbar offers Sketch, Extrude and Normal To for planes and flat faces, Edit Sketch, Extrude, Hide and Normal To for sketches, and Edit Feature for solid features; it opens on clicks only, not when code selects a row. (10) Any sketch line can be a revolve axis; a lone centerline is chosen automatically.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec leaves these open. Each choice keeps the file format, the locked decisions and the existing tests intact.

D111: Polish pass look (C7). (1) Themes are two colour sets in `ui/themes/theme.py`: `Palette` for what FDCAD paints (view gradient, sketch, states) and `Chrome` for Qt widgets. `apply_theme` sets the Fusion style, a Qt palette from `Chrome` and one application style sheet from `ui/themes/style.py`; widgets are styled by object name, not inline colours. The chosen theme is remembered in the theme module, so light and dark also work where the platform ignores the colour scheme (offscreen). (2) One accent colour, the icon accent (#1F6FD1 light, #5B9BFF dark), used for focus, the current tab mark, the panel OK button and progress. (3) Sizes are multiples of a unit of a quarter of the UI font's line height (4 logical pixels at the default font): tree rows 6 units, spacing 1, 2 and 4 units. Two corner radii: 1 unit for controls, 1.5 units for panels, plates and popups. Qt scales logical pixels with the display setting, so the look holds from 100 to 200 percent. (4) Command tabs read as flat tabs over a lighter tab body; document tabs use a top accent line and the view's top colour when selected, with a theme coloured close button (new icon `ui.close_tab`) in place of the style's red one. The left panel tabs elide instead of scrolling. (5) The Features tab gains Sketch (large, as in the Sketch tab) and a Rebuild group with Rebuild and Force Rebuild (compact). Round 2: Revolved Cut is large, so Add Material and Remove Material mirror each other. Compact rows have one height (a third of a large button) and each compact column is centred on the large buttons, so a lone tool sits on the middle row of a full column, in every tab. (6) View gradients run top to bottom, light #F4F6F9 to #C3CCD8 and dark #424955 to #1B1E23 (round 2), with a sketch grid colour per theme; the PLAN 8.5 sketch colours are unchanged and were checked on both. The view takes the theme colours as sRGB (`Quantity_TOC_sRGB`) with a vertical fill. Round 1 passed them as linear RGB with the kernel's default left to right fill, which washed the gradient out to a barely visible mid grey and made the view strip a different band; now the strip and the selected document tab show exactly the view's top colour. (7) Style sheet arrows and tick marks are small SVG files written to a Qt temporary folder at start, because Qt style sheets only take image files. (8) New icons for the property panel fields, the reverse direction button and the context toolbar (edit, show, hide); the context toolbar reuses the Sketch, Extruded Boss and Normal To command icons, and the panel header uses the confirmation corner icons. Revolve and Revolved Cut icons were redrawn without the axis line through the body, which made them unreadable at 16 px. The panel header icon for cuts now uses the existing cut icons (`feature.extruded_cut`, `feature.revolved_cut`). (9) Round 2 (reviewer run on Windows 11, 1920 by 1080, 100 percent). Large buttons paint their own icon and label: the icon on one row and a label area of two lines for every button, lines centred across and starting at the top of the area, so one line labels such as Sketch start level with two line labels; the content is centred vertically like the compact columns. The left panel tabs and the document tabs share margin, padding, a 2 px border top and bottom and a minimum height, so both bars sit on one line at the same height. Tree rows get 1 unit more room at the left and 1.5 units before the icon; expand arrows are small chevrons in the muted colour. The status bar top border (1 px, border colour) was already drawn; a test now keeps it. `tools/screenshot_tabs.py` takes the window shot from the screen when it runs on a display, so the after screenshots, made on Xvfb with software OpenGL at 1920 by 1040, show the real 3D view.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner judged earlier builds as looking poor (PHASE1_CORRECTIONS C7). One token set and one style sheet keep every panel consistent and are easy to adjust after owner review.

D112: Revolve drag handle and model edge axis (W6.3, W6.4). (1) `PreviewHandle` gains an optional `centre`: with it the handle turns about the axis through `centre` along `direction` (right hand rule) and its value is an angle. Revolve shows one curved arrow at the end of the preview, on the circle swept by the profile's area centre: one handle for one direction, one at half the angle for mid plane (scale 2), and an `angle2` handle turning the other way for two directions. The arrow is a thin arc of 2.5 arrow sizes ending in a cone, built and meshed on the worker like the extrude cone. While dragging, the view finds the point of the handle's circle nearest the cursor on screen (2 degree samples, then 0.1 degree), keeps the angle continuous past a full turn and clamps it to 0.1 to 360 degrees; the arrow turns at once and the solid follows with the next preview. The callout shows degrees, and a dragged angle is typed into the field in degrees rounded to 0.01. (2) The revolve axis ref may be an edge reference (FDEF_SPEC 7: `kind`, `name`, `snapshot`) instead of `{"sketch_entity": ...}`. The edge is resolved by name, then by snapshot with a warning, else a missing reference error. It must be straight and lie in the sketch plane (within 0.0001 mm), so the profile side check works in sketch coordinates. The snapshot direction fixes which way the angle turns, so a kernel flip of the edge never reverses the revolve. Only edges of features before the revolve are accepted in the panel. No schema change: older files keep their sketch line axes. (3) `FeaturePreview.drag_to(param, value)` is the public drag API; the view's `handle_dragged` signal calls it.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for an arc handle and edge picking but leaves the placement, limits and storage open. These choices reuse the extrude handle (D109) and the existing reference format, so the file format stays the same.

D113: Dimensions to part edges in a sketch (Box test). With Smart Dimension, clicking a straight edge of the part outline shown in a sketch on a face adds a fixed construction line on that edge (or reuses one already there) and uses it as the pick. A circle or arc picked together with a line measures from its centre. The construction line is a copy: it does not follow later changes to the part. Linked edge references in sketches would need a new sketch entity type and a file format change, which is not in Phase 1.
Status: Default
Reason: The Box test dimensions a circle to two edges of the face. A fixed copy needs no file format change and keeps the sketch fully defined.

D114: Spec gaps closed for the 0.1.0 build. (1) Show and hide of sketches and planes is saved in the file, in `appearance.hidden` and `appearance.shown` (FDEF_SPEC 10, optional keys, no schema change), and changes through an undoable command (`SetVisibility`) that redraws without a rebuild. This replaces D110 item 1. Planes are hidden by default; the tree menu of a plane offers Show or Hide beside Sketch, and shown planes are drawn as see-through squares sized to the part, never picked. (2) Opening a sketch turns the 3D view to face it in 250 ms with a smooth start and stop, then the sketch editor takes the view's place (D72). The new preference "Animate view changes" (on by default) makes the turn instant when off. Qt and OCP have no camera blend, so `ui/viewport/views.py` blends the target, direction, up, distance and scale in pure Python. (3) Outside sketch mode the status bar shows the model point under the cursor as X, Y and Z in the part's units, from the hover pick; it is blank off the part. (4) Grouped tool dropdowns remember their last tool across restarts in the preferences (`appearance/tool_groups`), keyed by the id of the group's first tool.
Status: Default
Reason: These items were listed as open by earlier agents. The choices keep older files byte for byte unchanged and follow CLAUDE.md rule 3 now that the state is part of the document.

D115: Installer builds by hand (packaging for the owner's 0.1.0 test). (1) The Release workflow's manual run (workflow_dispatch) has a `platforms` choice: `windows` (default) builds only the Windows installer, `both` adds the Mac DMG, so Mac minutes are spent only when asked (D35). Manual runs never publish; publishing still needs a version tag. Non tag builds are versioned as the app version plus `-dev` (for example 0.1.0-dev) instead of 0.0.0-dev. (2) The PyInstaller spec bundles every non Python file of `src/fdcad/ui/icons` and fails the build if no SVG is found. Theme images need no files: they are written at start (D111 item 7) and use Qt's SVG image plugin, which the PySide6 hooks bundle. (3) The smoke test also starts the built app with `FDCAD_BUNDLE_CHECK` set to a file; the app writes what is missing (icon files, drawable icons, Qt SVG support, theme images, the four samples) and quits, and the smoke test fails on any problem. The variable is never set in normal use, like `FDCAD_STARTUP_REPORT`.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner needs a Windows installer from this branch without a release, and missing data files must fail CI instead of reaching the owner.

D116: Owner answers to the tool audit spec questions (docs/GAP_REPORT.md section 3), approved by the owner on 2026-10-29. (1) Selected regions (T5.3): crossing curves stop being a sketch error. They split the sketch into regions that can be picked for Extrude, Cut and Revolve. This changes D68 for crossings only; open contours, branches and duplicates are still errors when no regions are picked. Built last, after the other packages. (2) Right click in the empty 3D view opens a context menu (T9.1). The shortcut bar opens with Q only. (3) Snapping to part geometry (T1.2.2) adds a relation to a fixed construction copy of the edge or centre, as D113 does for Smart Dimension. When a later change to the part moves the original, the sketch shows a warning; the copy is never moved without the user's confirmation. This replaces D110 item 6. (4) Body commands (I, H for bodies, Shift+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Hide or Show Body) stay in Phase 3 as PLAN says. (5) Dimension label positions are stored in the file so labels can be dragged (T4.2.1, T4.4.2). This changes D72 and needs an FDEF_SPEC update and a format version bump; older files open with automatic placement. (6) Added later the same day: the From list of Extrude and Extruded Cut offers Sketch Plane, Surface/Face/Plane, Vertex and Offset in Phase 1 (TOOL_SPEC T5.1.2), moved forward from Phase 2 at the owner's request. It adds a start condition and a start reference to the feature data, so FDEF_SPEC changes; older files open as Sketch Plane. (7) Added late on 2026-10-29: the owner lifted the phase order ("the phase doesnt matter"). Work from later phases may be built now, in parallel, from specs in docs/. CLAUDE.md section 1 item 1 is relaxed by this owner decision; each phase still needs its own done criteria before its release tag.
Status: Owner approved
Reason: These answers unblock work packages WP8, WP12, WP14 and WP15 of the gap report. Items 1 and 5 change the file format, so older files must keep opening (CLAUDE.md section 4 item 4).

D117: Value box details (TOOL_SPEC T4.2.2 to T4.2.4, owner note 2). (1) The box of a dimension opens right of its text, centred on it vertically, or left of it when there is no room on the right, always inside the sketch view. The text rectangle is worked out from the dimension geometry, not from the last paint, so a dimension placed a moment ago gets the right place. (2) The spin step is shown in the box as a small number field. It defaults to 1 mm, 1 degree, or 0.1 in for inch parts (1 mm is an awkward 0.03937 in). The wheel over the box and the up and down arrows in the value change the text by one step, ten steps with Ctrl and a tenth with Alt; Alt plus wheel also works where the platform turns it into a sideways scroll. Stepping only changes the text: Enter, the check button or the rebuild arrow still applies it, so a model dimension does not rebuild the part on every wheel notch. (3) Formulas (text starting with "=") are never stepped, so a link to a variable is not replaced by a number; lengths never step to zero or below. (4) Escape or the cross on a dimension placed a moment ago removes it again, with any change made while its box was open (the sketch rolls back to before the placement). Once the rebuild arrow has applied a value, the dimension counts as kept. (5) Reverse in the box is not built: no sketch dimension is signed in Phase 1 (gap report question 6 is still open).
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the behaviour but not the placement, the step for inch parts or what stepping does to formulas. These choices keep formulas safe and avoid rebuilding the part while the wheel turns.

D118: Sketch preferences (TOOL_SPEC T11.1 to T11.5, T1.2.7, T1.2.8 first three, T1.3.3). (1) A new Sketch page in Preferences holds six switches, all on by default: turn the view normal to the sketch on open, show circle and arc centres, show end points as dots, snapping, snap to model geometry and automatic relations, plus "Over defining dimension" (Ask or Always make reference). They are stored under `sketch/` in the preferences, read as `Settings.sketch_options` (a frozen `SketchOptions` in `ui/sketch_tools/options.py`), and handed to the open sketch canvas when the dialog closes with OK, so an open sketch follows them at once. (2) With "turn normal" off the 3D view does not turn before the sketch editor shows; the editor itself always looks normal to the sketch (D72). (3) Hidden centres and end point dots are a display choice only: the points still snap, and a selected or hovered point always shows. (4) Snapping off, or Ctrl held during a mouse move or click in a drawing tool, gives a free cursor: no point, curve, alignment, model centre or line direction snap. (5) Snap to model geometry covers the revealed centres of round part edges, the only model snap in Phase 1; picking part edges in Smart Dimension (D113) is a pick, not a snap, and stays. (6) Automatic relations off keeps snapping but adds none of the relations of T1.3.1 (coincident, on curve, midpoint, centre, horizontal and vertical lines). Joins that are part of the shape stay: the shared end point of the next segment in a line chain, the corners and sides of rectangles, and the start and Tangent of a tangent arc, since without them the tool would not draw the shape it names. (7) "Always make reference": when a new dimension leaves the sketch over defined or unsolvable and making it a reference dimension clears that, it is added as a reference dimension, the status bar says so and no value box opens. "Ask" keeps the current behaviour until the prompt of T1.4.4 is built (gap report WP8).
Status: Default
Reason: The spec lists the switches but not their storage, what Ctrl covers, or which joins survive with automatic relations off. Keeping shape joins means a chain or a tangent arc still draws what its name says.

D119: Polish pass from the tool audit (gap report WP3). (1) The tree puts "(-) " before an under defined sketch and "(+) " before an over defined one (T1.4.3), from the last rebuild's solve result. The prefix is display only: renaming strips it, and planes and solid features never get one. (2) Discarding a sketch (the red X, after the question) puts the 3D camera back where it was before the sketch turned the view (T1.5.2); exit and keep leaves the view as it is. (3) The shortcut bar gets a search box at the top (T10.1). It has the focus when the bar opens; typing lists up to 15 enabled commands whose name contains the text, names starting with it first. Up and Down move, Enter runs the highlighted or first command, Escape closes. (4) The gesture guide (T10.2) appears after a 10 px right drag: a dashed inner circle of the gesture distance (40 px, unchanged) and the context's commands around it, with the one the drag points to highlighted. Releasing inside the circle runs nothing, as before; a plain right click shows no guide. It is a small see-through tool tip window that ignores the mouse, so it also draws over the native 3D view and adds no kernel work. (5) Selected sketch items use the theme accent (T1.4.1, D111) and hovered ones a lighter accent. The accent is nearly the under defined blue (#1F6FD1 against #1F5FD1 in light, the same #5B9BFF in dark), so selected curves also get a soft accent band under the line. Drawing tool previews and snap marks keep their orange, as they are not a state. The owner may want a different accent or under defined colour after testing. (6) Circle and arc centres are drawn as a plus mark instead of a dot (T2.4.1). (7) Revolve wording (T6.2.1, T6.2.3): "Revolve 1 failed: the profile crosses the axis. Move the profile to one side of the axis or pick regions on one side." and "Pick the axis of revolution: ...". Highlighting the crossing is not built: gap report question 18 (where to highlight) is still open.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec states the behaviour but not these details. The accent and under defined colours clash; the band keeps selection readable without changing locked colours.

D120: Phase 1 shortcuts from TOOL_SPEC T12.4 and T12.5 (gap report WP4). New commands, each in `ui/input/commands.py` so they show in the shortcut editor, the shortcut bar search and the gesture editor, with an original icon. (1) View Selector, Ctrl+Space (Control+Space on Mac): a popup cube at the cursor drawn from the front, right and top corner. Each visible face is a 3 by 3 grid: the middle cell picks the face view, side cells the view across that edge, corner cells the corner view; Back, Left and Bottom buttons below the cube pick the hidden faces. The view turns with the existing look and fit, so Previous View goes back. WORKFLOW_SPEC W7.2 also names Space; SHORTCUTS.md wins (T12.1), so Space is not bound. (2) Hide or Show, H: hides the sketch or plane selected in the tree, or shows it again, as one undoable `SetVisibility` command (D114). Bodies are not covered: they stay in Phase 3 (D116 item 4). (3) Hide All Reference Geometry, Ctrl+H (Control+H on Mac): a view state toggle of the open part that hides every shown plane and shows them again; the part has no drawn origin or axes in Phase 1. It is not saved in the file and changes no document data, like the display style, so it is not an undo step. (4) Snap Options, F3: a popup at the cursor with snapping, snap to model geometry and automatic relations (T1.2.8), saved at once and passed to the open sketch. (5) Flat Tree View, Ctrl+T: a checkable toggle; sketches leave their features and every feature gets its own top level row in document order. (6) Switch Line and Arc (T12.5) is registered with no default key. The switch itself (T2.1.3) is not built; in the Line tool the command says so in the status bar and the tool stays active. (7) Not built here: I (isolate), Shift+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (bodies, Phase 3) and F8 (gap report question 13, not in T12.3 or T12.4).
Status: Default
Reason: T12.4 asks for these keys now. The cube design is original; buttons for the hidden faces keep every standard view one click away without turning the cube.

D121: Reference plane look in the 3D view (TOOL_SPEC T13). (1) Shown planes (D114) and planes offered for picking (W1) share one look from `ui/viewport/plane_look.py`: a 1 px outline, a smoke grey fill at 88 percent transparency, and the plane's tree name as 11 px text placed 4 percent of the plane's size inside the corner of low u and high v, left and top aligned so it reads inward. The label is a 3D text label, so it follows the plane when the view turns; it is never picked. (2) Theme colours in `Palette`: light outline #7C848E and fill #C9CDD2, dark outline #A7AEB7 and fill #D5D9DE (a lighter outline so it reads on the dark view). (3) The plane under the cursor while picking uses the accent colour for outline and label (D111); the kernel's own hover highlight of those planes is given the same accent look so the two never clash. (4) "Selection colour": a plane selected in the feature tree shows its outline and label in `Palette.selection`, the orange the 3D view already uses for picking and preview bands (#F28C28 light, #FFA654 dark). The fill stays the same in every state. (5) The old orange look of shown planes and the 75 percent orange fill of pickable planes are gone.
Status: Default
Reason: T13 gives the look but not exact colours, sizes or which corner. The 3D view had no named selection colour, so the existing orange selection band colour is reused.

D122: Relations completion (docs/GAP_REPORT.md WP5, TOOL_SPEC T1.3.2, T3.1 to T3.3). (1) Two new relation types, `coradial` (concentric plus equal radius) and `intersection` (a point on two lines, stored point first), and wider entity lists for existing types: horizontal and vertical take two or more points (each lines up with the first), collinear takes two or more lines, concentric takes two or more circles or arcs or a point with circles or arcs, midpoint takes a point and an arc, symmetric takes two points, lines, circles or arcs with the mirror line stored last. These are additions to schema 1 with no schema bump: the spec says the schema increases only for changes that are not backward compatible, and every older file opens byte for byte unchanged (test `test_old_files_open.py`). FDEF_SPEC section 6 item 4 lists what each type holds. (2) planegcs expresses every T3.1 relation. A midpoint on an arc is "on the arc's circle and on the perpendicular bisector of its chord"; the solver keeps the point on the side it starts on, so it can in theory settle on the opposite side of the circle if dragged there. Symmetric lines and arcs pair their end points by which mirrored ends lie closest at solve time, so a mirror pair never crosses over. Circles mirror the centre and share the radius. (3) A Symmetric selection of three lines needs exactly one construction line (the centerline); with points, circles or arcs the single line is the mirror line, construction or not. (4) Clicking a relation tag selects that relation (selection item `r<index>`, Ctrl adds or removes); its items draw in the selection colour; Delete removes it as one step on the sketch's undo list. (5) The sketch panel lists the selection's relations with a delete button on each row and shows the selection's state (under, fully or over defined): over when a selected item is in a conflict, fully when every selected item is defined. (6) The Relations panel is a new Sketch tab command (`sketch.relations`, no default key, in the shortcut bar list) that shows in the left panel with Back to return. Filters: All; Over defining or not solved (relations named in a conflict or as not needed, or every relation when the sketch cannot be solved); Model references (relations that touch a fixed construction copy of part geometry, D113 and D116 item 3). Delete All removes every relation the current filter lists. The origin's own fixed relation is internal and never listed, so Delete All cannot free the origin.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec lists the relations and panels but leaves storage, ordering and these edge cases open. The choices keep older files unchanged and use the solver only through `fdcad/core/sketch`.

D123: Smart Dimension rules (docs/GAP_REPORT.md WP6, TOOL_SPEC T4.1, T4.3, owner note 10). (1) A circle or arc picked with any other item (a point, the origin, a model point copy, a line, a model edge copy, or another circle or arc) measures to its centre: the circle is swapped for its centre point, and the two point placement rule then applies (text above or below gives horizontal, left or right gives vertical, along gives true distance). (2) Measure to Nearest or Farthest (T4.3.2) is stored on the dimension: the circle or arc id replaces the centre point and `measure_to` names the side (FDEF_SPEC 6 item 5). The solver adds the radius for each farthest side and subtracts it for each nearest one, so nearest assumes the other item lies outside the circle. It is offered, as T4.3.2 says, for a circle or arc with a line or another circle or arc, never with a point, in a Measure To group of the sketch panel when one such distance is selected. This is the part of WP8's Dimension panel the owner asked for in WP6; the rest of that panel stays in WP8. Changing it keeps the geometry and sets the value to the new measured size, as one undoable step. The UI spells the default "Center" like the rest of the app. (3) A single line gives its length wherever the text is placed (T4.1, gap report question 20); the tests that expected horizontal or vertical projections were updated. (4) Angles store which of the angles between two lines is meant (`supplement`, FDEF_SPEC 6 item 5), from where the text was placed: the four angles around the crossing point pair up into the angle between the line directions and the one beside it. The solver then holds that side, so a typed value can open the angle past 90 degrees without flipping to the other side. Angle dimensions saved before this have no key and keep the old closest side rule, so older files solve to the same shape. (5) A line and a parallel centerline (construction line) with the text beyond the centerline give a `doubled_distance`, shown with the diameter sign, for revolve profiles (T4.1 last row); text between them gives a plain distance. Only a line or point with a centerline counts. (6) Esc removes the last pick; with no picks left the next Esc ends the tool. With two items picked, the next click places the dimension even when it lands on geometry. (7) Arc length (an arc then its two end points) is Later (Phase 2) and not built.
Status: Default
Reason: T4.1 and T4.3 say what to measure but not how to store sides and angle choices. Optional keys keep older files opening and solving unchanged (CLAUDE.md section 4 item 4).

D124: Snapping completion (docs/GAP_REPORT.md WP7, TOOL_SPEC T1.2, T1.3.1, T2.5.4). (1) Smart Dimension snaps like the drawing tools: the snap marker shows while moving, and a click on an end point, sketch point or centre snap picks that point. A click on a revealed centre of the part outline adds a fixed construction point there (or reuses a fixed construction point already there, the origin included) and picks it, as D113 does for straight edges. (2) Drawing tools tie a point snapped to a revealed part centre to the same kind of fixed construction copy with a Coincident relation, following D116 item 3; this replaces D110 item 6. The warning D116 item 3 asks for when the part later moves the original needs projected model geometry, which is WP14, so it is not built here. (3) Dragging a sketch point snaps it (items that move with it, its coincident partners and their curves, are left out so it never snaps to itself). On release the point gets the snap's relations only for point snaps (end point, centre, midpoint, quadrant, intersection, part centre), never for on curve or guide snaps, and only when the sketch stays solvable and not over defined; otherwise the move stays and nothing is added. Whole lines, arcs and circle edges drag without snapping. (4) Arcs offer a midpoint snap at the middle of their sweep, with a Midpoint relation (D117 item 2), in the same tier as line midpoints, so the T1.2.3 order holds. (5) Alignment guides also line up with revealed part centres; as before, a guide adds no relation (gap report question 21 is still open) and guides only apply when no point snap is in range. (6) Line direction snaps: horizontal and vertical first, then parallel or perpendicular to any sketch line within the same 3 degrees (D73). A free end turns onto the direction keeping its projection; a snapped end keeps its place and gets the relation only when it already fits. The new line gets Parallel or Perpendicular with that line, and the snap label names it. (7) A circle drawn from the centre of a sketch circle or arc gets Concentric with it instead of a coincident centre (T1.3.1). (8) Centres show as a small cross in every mode: revealed part centres, and the centre of any sketch circle or arc that is hovered or selected (T2.5.4). Hovering the part outline reveals its centres in select mode and Smart Dimension too. Sketch centre points stay visible as dots and always snappable, since gap report question 7 is still open.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for these snaps but leaves the drop rules, guide relations and centre copies open. These choices keep the T1.2.3 priority order and never over define a sketch by a drag.

D140: Extrude From list (TOOL_SPEC T5.1.2, D116 item 6). (1) Stored as the optional `start_condition` parameter (`sketch_plane`, `surface`, `vertex`, `offset`), `start_offset` and `start_reverse` for Offset, and `refs.start` for a pick: a face reference, a plane feature, a vertex reference, or a sketch point given as the sketch feature and entity id (`{"feature": "f7", "sketch_entity": "e3"}`). The panel lists the points of earlier sketches other than the feature's own, and the default planes; faces and vertices come from clicks in the view. (2) A flat face or plane parallel to the sketch plane, a vertex and an offset all move the profile along the sketch normal, so the feature is an ordinary prism with the usual face names. Any other face or plane is reached by a long prism of the profile cut to the space between the start surface and the same surface moved by the depth; the faces keep the roles `cap/start`, `cap/end` and `side/<entity>`. (3) "Lands fully on the face" is checked by area for flat faces (the moved profile minus the face has no area left) and by volume for other faces (the solid's volume must equal profile area times depth). So a curved face that the direction meets twice, such as the whole side of a cylinder, is an error too: pick a face that the direction meets once. (4) A lost pick is an error: "Extrude 1: the From face f6/cap/end was lost. Pick the face again or choose Sketch Plane.", with the lost name highlighted. A pick found again by its position snapshot gives the usual warning (PLAN 6 item 6), never a silent change. (5) The Offset field defaults to 10 in the part's unit. The drag handles start where the profile centre meets the start.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the four choices and the error rules but not the storage or the method. Reusing the plain prism where it fits keeps names and speed the same as a sketch plane start.

D141: Direction 2 end conditions (TOOL_SPEC T5.1.4, GAP_REPORT Q15). Direction 2 has its own list with Blind and Through All. It may follow Blind or Through All in Direction 1, and is off with Mid Plane only, as the spec says. Storage: Blind plus Blind stays `end_condition: "two_directions"` exactly as before. Any other pair adds the optional `end_condition2` key, with `end_condition` holding Direction 1's choice (`"two_directions"` means Blind). `depth2` is written only when Direction 2 is Blind.
Status: Default
Reason: Older files keep their exact meaning and bytes, and the new key only appears when it carries information.

D142: Through All for bosses (TOOL_SPEC T5.1.3, GAP_REPORT Q3). A boss may use Through All, in either direction, once the part has a body. It ends at the far side of the existing body along the direction, measured from the lowest point of the start along that direction (for a flat start this is exact; for a curved start the end is the start surface moved that far). No body: "Extrude 1: Through All needs a body to go through. Choose Blind, or add a body first." No body ahead: "Through All finds no body in that direction. Reverse the direction or choose Blind." Cuts keep their old Through All length. The panel offers Through All for a boss only when a body exists before it.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner's question in the gap report proposed this meaning; it needs no new data.

D143: Cut Outside (TOOL_SPEC T5.1.5, T6.1.4). An extruded cut with Cut Outside removes what lies outside the profile but within the cut's depth range; material beyond the depth stays. It is built as a large square on the sketch plane (larger than the part) swept the same way as the profile, minus the profile's solid, then cut from the part. A revolved cut does the same with a large rectangle from the axis outwards on the profile's side, turned by the same angles. The preview shows the material that will be removed (the part inside that region). The optional `cut_outside` boolean is written only when true; for a boss it is an error.
Status: Default
Reason: Limiting the removal to the depth or angle range keeps the option useful with Blind depths and turned parts, and matches how a cut inside the profile is limited.

D144: Value stepping in panel fields (TOOL_SPEC T4.2.3 applied to T5.1.2, T5.1.3, T6.1.2). The mouse wheel over a field, or Up and Down in it, step a plain number: 1 mm, 0.1 in in inch parts, or 1 degree. Ctrl is ten steps, Alt a tenth. A typed unit stays (2 cm steps to 2.1 cm). Formulas and variable names are left alone, so a link is never replaced by a number. A step that would reach zero or less is not taken. Implemented in `ui/property_panel/stepping.py` as an event filter, so the handle value box can use it too; the sketch value box is left to the sketch work package.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the step and the modifiers for the dimension value box and asks for the same behaviour in panel fields; inch parts need a step that fits their unit.

D145: File format for the WP10 options. `start_condition`, `start_offset`, `start_reverse`, `end_condition2`, `cut_outside` and `refs.start` are optional keys of schema 1, left out at their defaults, like `merge` (D109). Older files open, rebuild and save byte for byte the same (tested with the samples and `tests/fixtures/extrude_revolve_0_1_0.fdef`, saved by the code before this change). No schema bump is needed for them; the dimension position change of D116 item 5 is separate. Also fixed: the merge check compared two cylinder faces with a method that does not exist (`gp_Ax1.Distance`), which failed any feature whose new edge joined two cylinder faces.
Status: Default
Reason: CLAUDE.md section 4 item 4. Optional keys keep older files and their cache keys unchanged.

D146: Drag handle ruler (TOOL_SPEC T5.2.2, T6.3.1, GAP_REPORT Q16). The length tick step is tied to the size of the profile, not to the zoom: about a tenth of the profile's diagonal, rounded to 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten in the part's unit (mm or inches), so it never changes during a drag. Angle ticks are 5 degrees. A length ruler runs from two ticks behind the start (for handles that can flip) to at least ten ticks or twice the current depth, at most 200 ticks; an angle ruler is the full circle. Every fifth length tick and every 45 degree tick is longer. The ruler is built with the preview on the worker thread and shown only while that handle is dragged. The value snaps to whole ticks while the cursor is within 14 logical pixels of the ruler on screen, and is free elsewhere. Mid Plane handles snap the total depth to twice the tick step, since each tick is one step on each side.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives 5 degree ticks for angles and leaves the length step open. A step fixed by the profile size keeps the ticks still under the cursor while dragging and gives round numbers.

D147: Dragging past the start flips (TOOL_SPEC T5.2.5, GAP_REPORT Q17). Only the Direction 1 handle of a Blind extrude without Direction 2 flips. Dragging it back past the start toggles the panel's Reverse Direction button and keeps the depth positive; dragging forward again toggles it back. Mid Plane handles, Direction 2 handles and revolve handles stop at their smallest value instead. With a From start (D140) the start, not the sketch plane, is where the flip happens. The arrow turns round at once on the screen; the solid follows with the next preview.
Status: Default
Reason: Flipping a symmetric or two sided extrusion would only swap the two sides, which the user can do with Reverse Direction, and could surprise the user mid drag.

D148: Clickable value beside the handle (owner note 7, TOOL_SPEC T5.2.3, T6.3.2). A click on the value label beside the active handle opens the existing value box (from the dimension work, used as is) at the click point, holding the panel field's text. Enter or OK types the text into the panel field, keeping units and formulas, so the field and preview update; the rebuild arrow does the same and keeps the box open; Escape or the cross closes it; a wrong value keeps the box open with the reason. Up, Down and the wheel step the value (D144). Closing the panel closes the box. The label's click box is estimated from its text length and height, with a margin, since the view draws it with OpenGL. The view sends `value_clicked` and `handle_flipped` signals; `FeaturePreview` handles them, so the view stays small.
Status: Default
Reason: Reusing the value box keeps one look and one behaviour for typed values everywhere.

D150: Dimension label positions (docs/GAP_REPORT.md WP8, TOOL_SPEC T4.2.1, T4.4.2, D116 item 5). The text position is stored per dimension as the optional key `label`, an offset `[dx, dy]` in millimetres from the dimension's anchor (FDEF_SPEC 6 item 5): the middle of the two measured points for linear dimensions, the centre for radius and diameter, the middle of the two line midpoints for angles. An offset from the anchor makes the text move with the geometry. A placed dimension keeps its text where the placing click was; files without the key place text automatically as before (D72 for those). The schema stays 1: the owner's WP8 brief asks for an optional key, FDEF_SPEC 15 item 1 raises the schema only for changes that are not backward compatible, and D122 and D123 did the same. D116 item 5 mentions a version bump; that wording is left for the owner to confirm.
Status: Default
Reason: Older files open and save byte for byte unchanged (tests `test_old_files_open.py`, `test_dimension_labels.py`), and stored text follows its geometry.

D151: Dimension panel (TOOL_SPEC T4.2.5, T7.4, owner note 3). (1) It is a group at the top of the sketch panel, shown while Smart Dimension is active and when exactly one dimension is selected. (2) It shows, in this order of preference, the preview that follows the cursor, the dimension whose value box is open, the selected dimension, and in Smart Dimension the dimension placed last. (3) It holds the type, the value field (expressions and units as in the value box; Enter applies, as one undo step), Driving or Reference, Measure To (moved here from the sketch panel, D123 item 2), and Place Text Automatically when the text was placed by hand. (4) Reference dimensions show the measured value: after every solve their stored value follows the geometry, so the file holds the last measured size. Their value field is read only and double click does not open the value box. (5) Switching a reference dimension to driving keeps the geometry; it is refused, with a status message, when it would over define the sketch.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec lists the panel's contents but not where it sits, which dimension it shows, or what a refused toggle does. Refusing keeps the sketch solvable without changing geometry (CLAUDE.md 5.12).

D152: Over define prompt (TOOL_SPEC T1.4.4, completes D118 item 7). With the Sketch preference on Ask, a new dimension that leaves the sketch over defined or unsolvable, where making it a reference clears that, shows the question beside its text in a small frame like the value box, not a modal dialog: "This dimension over defines the sketch. Make it a reference dimension?" with Make Reference and Keep Driving. Make Reference turns it into a reference dimension and opens no value box; Keep Driving opens the value box; Escape removes the new dimension, as Escape in the value box does (D117 item 4). Clicking elsewhere in the sketch closes the question and keeps the dimension driving. When the sketch was already over defined before the dimension, no question is asked.
Status: Default
Reason: An inline question keeps the sketch visible and never blocks the window or the offscreen tests.

D153: Value preview and dragged text (TOOL_SPEC T4.2.1, T4.4.2). (1) Once Smart Dimension has its items, the dimension follows the cursor half transparent with its value, also in the Dimension panel, while the cursor is not over another pickable item (or two items are picked). (2) Dimension text can be dragged in Select and in Smart Dimension: a press and release more than 5 px apart is a drag, saved as one step on the sketch's undo list. In Smart Dimension a plain click on the text opens the value box on release (it opened on press before). (3) Linear dimensions with placed text draw the dimension line through the text, square to the measured direction, with extension lines from the measured points; text beyond the ends extends the dimension line to it. Dragging the text across the geometry moves the dimension to that side; the type and value never change by a drag.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec says what the user sees but not the drag threshold or how lines reach a placed text.

D154: Doubled distance from a point (completes D123 item 5). A point and a centerline (construction line) with the text beyond the centerline give a `doubled_distance`; the text on the same side, or a point on the centerline, gives a plain distance. A point with a line that is not construction never doubles.
Status: Default
Reason: D123 item 5 names points and lines; only lines were built.

D155: Click drag in sketch tools (TOOL_SPEC T1.1.3, T14.1.1). While a tool is in the middle of a shape, a left press and release more than 5 px apart counts the release as the next click. So two point tools (Line, Centerline, both rectangles, Circle) draw the same shape by click click or by press, drag, release, and three point tools take their first two points by a drag and the last by a click. A Line chain continues after a dragged segment as after a clicked one.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for both input styles with the same result; reusing the click path guarantees it.

D156: Tool panels (TOOL_SPEC T1.1.4, T7.2, T2.1.4, T2.4.3). (1) While a drawing tool or Smart Dimension is active the sketch panel shows that tool's panel: an Options group and the shape's values, or the Dimension panel; the relation groups return when the tool ends. (2) Options stay set while the sketch is open and are not saved in the preferences. For construction applies to every tool except Point and Centerline. (3) Line orientation Horizontal or Vertical keeps the line on that direction and adds the relation even with automatic relations off, since it is the shape asked for. Angle keeps the direction only: Phase 1 has no relation for an angle to the sketch axis, and fixing typed sizes with dimensions is T11.6 (Later).
Status: Default
Reason: The spec lists the options but not their lifetime or which relations they add.

D157: Typed shape values (TOOL_SPEC T7.3, T14.1.3, gap report WP9 risk). The values group shows the shape drawn last while a tool is active, or the one selected entity otherwise: point X and Y, line length and angle, circle and arc centre X, Y and radius, rectangle width and height (its first two sides). Typed values never move points directly: a length or radius is solved with a passing dimension of that value, which is then removed; a position or angle goes through the solver's drag with the other end held. When relations or dimensions hold the value, the sketch goes back to how it was, the field turns red and the status bar says what to change. Each accepted value is one step on the sketch's undo list. Values show in the part's units and accept expressions.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec says values can be typed and that relations win, but not how; the solver keeps every relation and dimension.

D158: Line to arc switch and cursor values (TOOL_SPEC T2.1.3, T2.1.5, T12.5). After a segment the cursor must first leave the end point (the pick distance, 8 px), come back onto it and leave again; then the next segment is a tangent arc, previewed as one. Doing it again switches back. The Switch Line and Arc command (no default key) switches at once. The arc gets the chain join and Tangent, kept even with automatic relations off as for the Tangent Arc tool (D118 item 6), and the chain then continues with a line. Centerlines have no switch. While drawing, the line's length and angle, or the circle's radius, show next to the cursor.
Status: Default
Reason: Leaving first stops the switch firing as the cursor moves off a point it just placed.

D159: Square rectangles (TOOL_SPEC T2.3.2, T14.1.1). With Shift held while the second point is placed (by click or release), the side becomes the larger of the width and height, and two adjacent sides get Equal. Equal is a shape join and stays with automatic relations off.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for a square with Equal but not which size wins.

D160: Normal arcs (TOOL_SPEC T2.5.2). The Tangent Arc tool decides when the cursor first leaves the end point by more than the pick distance: within 45 degrees of the end direction (either way along it) gives a tangent arc, otherwise a normal arc that leaves square to the curve on the side the cursor went. Going back onto the end point decides again. A normal arc from a line gets the join and Coincident between its centre and the line, which keeps it square to the line. A normal arc from an arc gets only the join: no Phase 1 relation says "square to an arc".
Status: Default
Reason: The spec names the gestures but not the angle that splits them or the relations.

D161: Edit Sketch Plane (TOOL_SPEC T14.2).
