A feature tree menu item on sketches and the command `sketch.edit_plane` (no default key; it acts on the open sketch or the sketch selected in the tree) open a small panel with one pick box. Picking a plane in the view or tree, or a flat face, fills it; another pick replaces it. OK replaces the sketch's `refs.plane` as one undoable command and the part rebuilds; Cancel or Escape changes nothing. A plane or face made after the sketch in the feature tree is refused with a message, since the sketch could not be built from it. Sketch coordinates are kept, so the sketch keeps its shape on the new plane. Fixed copies of part edges and centres (D113, D116 item 3) are copies, so nothing in the sketch changes silently; a face that later cannot be found is the usual lost reference error.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the panel and the error rule but not the order check or what happens to fixed copies.

D190: Sketch regions and their names (TOOL_SPEC T5.3.1, T5.3.4, D116 item 1, PLAN section 6). (1) `core/sketch/regions.py` splits the sketch's non construction curves where they cross or touch, using exact line and circle formulas (no tessellation), leaves out curves that only dangle (open ends, and bridges between loops, found as graph bridges), and takes the faces of the remaining planar graph as regions. A loop of one outline that lies inside a region of another outline is a hole of that region. (2) A region is named by the curves around it, outer loop and holes, each with the side the region lies on: `region(e3+|e5+|e9-)`. For a line `+` is the left of its first point to second point direction; for a circle or arc `+` is the side of its centre, so the arc's stored direction does not matter. Sides are sorted by entity number, then sign. Two regions with the same sides (rare) get `#1`, `#2` by area centre X, then Y, as in FDEF_SPEC 8 item 2. (3) Why this scheme: entity ids are permanent (PLAN 6.1), and a region's bounding curves and sides do not change when dimensions change or curves move, as long as the region keeps its neighbours; names change only when a curve that bounds the region is added or removed, which is exactly when the region itself changed. Position or index based names would shift with every edit.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for picks that survive edits but gives no scheme (GAP_REPORT Q2). Naming by bounding curves follows the edge naming of FDEF_SPEC 8 item 3 and needs no kernel.

D191: Resolving region picks (T5.3.4, PLAN 6.6, CLAUDE.md rule 12). (1) A pick resolves to the region with the same name. (2) Failing that, if exactly one region holds every curve and side of the stored name plus more (a new curve cut into the region, or a hole was added), it is used and the feature gets a warning naming the pick ("Region 1 of Selected Regions now has more curves around it ..."); picking it again clears the warning. (3) Otherwise the pick is lost: the feature fails with "<Feature> failed: Region <n> of Selected Regions is lost because <Sketch> changed. Pick the region again in Selected Regions." There is no position fallback: a snapshot (area centre and area) is stored with each pick for display only, because a region found by position after its curves changed would be a silent geometry change. Picks are numbered in the order they are listed in the box.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec wants an error that names the lost pick and no silent change. Item 2 follows PLAN 6.6 (one clear match gives a warning) while never guessing between candidates.

D192: Regions and the whole sketch (T5.3.3, D116 item 1, changes D68 for crossings only). (1) `topology.check` no longer reports crossings; `topology.intersections` still finds them for the profile builder. (2) No picks and no crossings: the profile is built exactly as before (D68), so older parts rebuild with the same faces and names. (3) No picks with crossings: every outline is used with its holes. Each connected group of curves is one outline (the union of its regions); outlines inside a region of another outline count by nesting depth, even depths are material and odd depths holes, which is D68's rule with crossing loops joined. Open contours, branches and duplicates are still errors here. (4) With picks only the picked regions count: open ends and loose curves elsewhere are ignored, an exact copy of a curve is ignored, and lines or arcs that partly overlap stop the regions with "Two curves overlap. Trim or delete one of them." (5) Picked regions that touch make one face: curves between two picked regions are dropped. Side faces of a curve split into several pieces are `side/e3`, `side/e3#2` and so on along the curve. (6) Revolve checks that only the picked regions stay on one side of the axis; a solid line on the axis splits a profile into regions on each side.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeps every older sketch and sample unchanged, gives a crossing sketch a sensible result before anything is picked, and lets regions be used even when the rest of the sketch is not closed.

D193: File format for Selected Regions. Extrude and Revolve store picks in the optional `refs.regions` list, each `{"kind": "region", "name": ..., "snapshot": {"point": [u, v], "area": a}}` in sketch coordinates (FDEF_SPEC 5.3.3). The key is left out when nothing is picked, so older files open, rebuild and save byte for byte the same (tested with the samples and the 0.1.0 fixture). No schema bump: like D145 it is an optional key of schema 1.
Status: Default
Reason: CLAUDE.md section 4 item 4. References belong in `refs` (FDEF_SPEC 7); the dependency scan ignores region names because they hold no feature ids.

D194: Selected Regions in the panel, the 3D view and the tree (T5.1.6, T5.3.2, T5.3.5). (1) The Selected Regions group comes after Direction 2 in Extrude and Revolve panels. It lists picks as "Region 1", "Region 2" in pick order, with a Clear button; Delete or Backspace removes the selected rows. Changing the sketch clears the picks. (2) The box is active after a click in its list and stays active until a value field of the panel takes the focus or the panel closes, so clicks in the 3D view (which take the focus) keep picking. Only while it is active does hovering highlight a region and a click toggle it; clicks elsewhere select as before. (3) Regions are shown while the box is active or the feature has picks: idle regions with a faint accent fill (90 percent see-through), the hovered one light (70), picked ones stronger (45, 35 when hovered). They are drawn on the top layer so a sketch on a part face does not flicker against that face. (4) `ui/viewport/regions.py` makes the regions and one meshed face per region once per sketch result on the shared thread pool, and again only after a rebuild; hover only asks the view which shown face is under the cursor, inside the existing 60 per second hover timer. `FeaturePreview` owns the `RegionPicker`, so the main window needs no new wiring. (5) A feature that uses a sketch an earlier feature already uses gets a child row "<sketch name> (shared)" with the link icon (`tree.link`); it carries the sketch's id, so double clicking it edits the sketch. (6) No new commands: picking happens in the box and the view, which have no keys to rebind.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec says what hover and click do but not when the box is active, how the fills look, or how the link row reads. These choices keep the view responsive (CLAUDE.md rule 2, PLAN 11.3.11) and avoid new window wiring that other work packages are changing.

D170: Context toolbar and right click menus (docs/GAP_REPORT.md WP12, TOOL_SPEC T8, T9, owner note 6, D116 item 2). (1) A plain right click in the 3D view or the sketch editor opens a menu for what is under the cursor; a right drag of more than 6 px is still a gesture (T10.2), so the two never meet. Q is now the only way to open the shortcut bar. Menus are built in `ui/main_window/context_menu.py`; each action keeps a key in `QAction.data()` so tests can read the menu without running it. (2) Context toolbar contents follow T8.2 and replace D110 item 9: a plane gives Sketch, Normal To, Hide or Show; a flat face Sketch and Normal To (Hide Body is Phase 3, D116 item 4); Extrude and Revolve features Edit Feature, Edit Sketch, Hide or Show of their sketch and Delete; a finished sketch Edit Sketch, Extrude, Revolve, Hide or Show; selected sketch items in an open sketch with no tool the fitting relations, Construction Geometry and Smart Dimension (with up to two of them already picked). Gap report question 9 is closed this way; Zoom to Selection from D106 moves to the View menu (T14.4). (3) A right click on a face, edge or vertex selects it first when it is not selected yet. The face and edge menus end with a submenu named after the feature that made the item, holding that feature's tree menu, so every feature type gets the T9.10 items in the view too. Normal To is offered for flat, cylindrical and conical faces. (4) Shown planes stay unpickable by a left click (D114); a right click checks them on purpose, so the plane menu (T9.5) works in the view as in the tree. Plane rows can now be renamed. (5) In a sketch, Normal To is left out of the empty space menu: the sketch editor always looks normal to its sketch (D72), so the item would do nothing (T9: items that do not apply are hidden). The last used tool shows as "Last Tool: Line". Snapping on or off changes the same preference as F3 (D118, D120 item 4). (6) Select Midpoint (T9.7) selects a vertex made at the edge's midpoint by length and marks it; it is used by later picks that take a vertex. (7) Reference or Driving on a dimension: making a dimension driving again sets its value to the size it measures now, so nothing moves; it is one step on the sketch's undo list. (8) Delete of a feature whose sketch no other feature uses asks Delete Sketch Too, Keep Sketch or Cancel (gap report question 14); a shared sketch is always kept. Deleting both is one undo step (an undo macro). (9) Shift+F10 and the Menu key run the new command Context Menu (`ui.context_menu`, group Interface), which opens the menu of the tree row in focus, the open sketch's selection, or the 3D view's selection. (10) Recent Commands lists the last five repeatable commands (sketch tools and features) run in this session; it is not saved. (11) Select Other (T9.13, T14.3.1) lists the faces, edges and vertices under the cursor nearest first, then a shown plane, with type icons. The 3D view shows the part as an `AIS_ColoredShape`, an `AIS_Shape` that can hide one face, so a right click on a face row hides that face until the list closes. Sketches in the 3D view are not pickable in Phase 1, so no sketch rows appear yet; the sketch type icon exists for later.
Status: Default
Reason: Follows TOOL_SPEC T8 and T9 and D116 item 2; the choices in items 3 to 11 fill gaps the spec leaves open.

D171: Selection filters and box selection (TOOL_SPEC T14.3.2, T14.3.3). (1) The filter bar is a toolbar on the right edge of the window, hidden until F5 (`select.filter_bar`); F5 was free in SHORTCUTS.md. Its buttons are vertices, edges, faces, solid bodies, planes, axes, sketches, sketch segments, sketch points and dimensions, then Clear All and Select All, with the on or off switch (F6, `select.filters_toggle`) first. E, X and V (`select.filter_edges`, `select.filter_faces`, `select.filter_vertices`) switch one type; switching a type on also turns the filters on, so the key acts at once. The new commands sit in a Selection group of the shortcut editor, with Select Other (`select.other`, no key: opens the list for what is under the cursor). (2) "Filter on" means: at least one type chosen and the switch on. Then only the chosen types highlight and select, in the 3D view (faces, edges, vertices of the part) and in the sketch editor (segments, points, dimensions); with no type chosen everything selects as before. Types with nothing to pick yet in Phase 1 (bodies, axes, planes and sketches in the 3D view) are kept in the bar so the layout does not change later. The filter is view state of the window, not saved. (3) While filters are on, the cursor is an arrow with a small orange funnel, drawn in code (`ui/input/filter_cursor.py`), in the 3D view and in the sketch editor when no tool is active. (4) Box rules in `ui/input/selection_rules.py`, pure and tested: a left to right drag takes items fully inside, a right to left drag also items the box crosses (OCCT overlap detection in the 3D view; a segment test on the screen outline in the sketch, with circles and arcs drawn as 48 segments and dimensions as their label boxes). Shift adds, Ctrl toggles, with neither the box replaces the selection; items outside the box keep their state. In a part the box picks edges by default, or the filtered types while filters are on. A plain click with Ctrl or Shift still toggles one item, as before.
Status: Default
Reason: Follows TOOL_SPEC T14.3; the bar place, key behaviour and cursor art are not given by the spec.

D172: View rules (TOOL_SPEC T14.4). (1) Normal To lives in `ui/main_window/view_commands.py` with pure helpers in `ui/viewport/views.py`. It looks at, in this order: two or more selected flat faces (the first toward the screen, the second's normal made square to it as up; parallel faces fall back to the first face alone), a flat face, a cylindrical or conical face (along its axis, from the end nearer the current eye), then the plane, sketch or sketch based feature selected in the tree (its sketch's plane). Two faces selected with Ctrl are simply the first two picked faces; the key needs not be held when Normal To runs. (2) "The same item again" means the same face (by its plane or axis, rounded) or tree row as the last Normal To, while the view still looks from where that Normal To left it; then the view turns 180 degrees (looks from the other side, up unchanged). Any other view change in between starts afresh. (3) With nothing usable selected it snaps to the nearest of the six axis views; with something selected that cannot be looked at (an edge) it says so in the status bar, as before. In a sketch Normal To does nothing, since the sketch editor always looks straight at the sketch (D72). Normal To on a default plane from the tree uses the plane's own placement (it failed before because a plane has no `plane` reference). (4) View menu: Previous View, Zoom to Fit, Zoom to Area and the new Zoom to Selection (`view.zoom_selection`, D106, no key) sit together; the four display styles move into a Display Style submenu; a Hide or Show submenu holds Planes, Origins, Sketches and Sketch Relations. Planes is the same view state as Hide All Reference Geometry (Ctrl+H) and stays in step with it. Sketches hides every sketch in the 3D view. Origins draws the part origin as three small axes (an `AIS_Trihedron`, never picked), off by default; Phase 1 had no drawn origin (D120 item 3). All three are view state of the window, not saved, so the file format does not change. Zoom to Selection fits the 3D view to the picked faces, edges and vertices, or the sketch editor to the selected sketch items. (5) View selector: it now opens at the centre of the active view (T14.4.2; D120 item 1 opened it at the cursor), slightly see through (90 percent opacity). Hovering shows a small preview beside the cube: the cube seen from that direction with the faces toward the eye filled, and the view name in a corner ("Front", "Front Right", "Back Left Top"; the front right top corner is "Isometric"). The preview draws the cube, not the part, because a second live camera of the part is not possible on every platform without more GPU work. The three back faces are drawn small and dashed, pushed out past the cube outline (2.25 times a face centre's distance), and can be clicked at any time. Holding Alt makes every cell pick its opposite (the faces at the back), and the cube darkens to show it. The Back, Left and Bottom buttons stay for keyboard use.
Status: Default
Reason: Follows TOOL_SPEC T14.4; items 2, 3 and 5 fill details the spec leaves open.

D173: Feature tree rollback, reorder and problem marks (TOOL_SPEC T14.5). (1) Rollback positions live in `core/document/rollback.py`. The bar can sit from just below the default planes (stored as `rollback: "f4"`, drawn below the Origin row) to the end; a bar after the last feature counts as the end. The bar row is selectable and draggable: Up and Down move it one feature, and it stays selected; dropping it on the upper half of a row puts it just above that feature, on the lower half just below. (2) Roll Forward (one step), Roll to Previous and Roll to End appear where they apply, on the bar row, on feature rows and on empty tree space, and are commands in the shortcut editor with no default key (`tree.roll_back`, `tree.roll_forward`, `tree.roll_previous`, `tree.roll_end`), also under Edit > Rollback Bar. "Previous" is where the bar was before its last move, kept for the open part only, not saved; the bar position itself is saved as before (`rollback`, FDEF_SPEC 2 item 9), so no file format change. (3) While rolled back, `AddFeature` inserts a new feature just above the bar and moves the bar below it (one undo step), so new sketches and features are built and later features stay rolled back. (4) Deleting a rolled back feature lists every feature that uses it, directly or through others, and deletes them all after Yes, as one undo step (an undo macro). Deleting a feature that is not rolled back keeps the old warning (its children show errors) and the keep sketch question of D170. (5) Reorder by drag: while dragging, Qt's drop line shows where the feature lands and a not allowed cursor shows where it cannot, using the same parent before child rule as before (`dependencies.move_problem`); the reason is kept in `FeatureTree.message`. (6) Problem marks: a feature with an error has red text and the red dot; with a warning the warning colour and dot; a feature used by a feature with a warning gets a smaller warning dot; the part name row gets a red dot when any feature has an error, else a warning dot when any has a warning. Clicking a marked feature opens a small box to the right of its row with each message (messages already say what to do next, CLAUDE.md 8.4) and Edit Feature and Edit Sketch buttons (Edit Sketch only when the feature has a sketch). Clicking the part name lists every error and warning, errors first; clicking a row selects that feature. The mark icons `tree.error_mark` and `tree.warning_mark` are used in the box and the list.
Status: Default
Reason: Follows TOOL_SPEC T14.5; items 1 to 3 and 6 fill details the spec leaves open.

D174: Icons draw on demand. `fdcad.ui.icons.icon()` now returns a QIcon backed by a small `SvgIconEngine` that renders the themed SVG only at the sizes Qt asks for and keeps those pixmaps, instead of rendering five sizes at two scales for every icon at start (about 90 KB each). The new commands of D170 to D173 would otherwise have added about 4 MB at start; with this the empty part starts at about 363 MB on Linux, down from about 379 MB. Disabled icons are drawn at 40 percent opacity. Note for the memory budget test: on Linux `process_memory` reads `ru_maxrss`, the peak resident size, which a child keeps from the forked pytest process before `exec`; inside a full test run the startup test therefore reports pytest's own size (about 420 MB in this container) rather than the app's. The budget and the test were not changed (owner instruction); the Mac and Windows numbers are not affected.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeps the startup memory budget (PLAN 11) with more commands; measured before and after.

D175: Expressions in feature panel fields (TOOL_SPEC T14.6). (1) Every number field of a feature panel already took values and `=` expressions with variables and functions (PLAN section 7); its tooltip now says so and gives an example. (2) While a field holds an expression, a small button at its start switches between the expression (editable) and its result (a read only box with the value in the part's units). The stored text is always the expression; the result box never changes it. Typing a plain value hides the button and shows the expression box again. (3) `="Name"` with a new valid name, then Enter, asks "Make a global variable Name = value and use it here?". The value is the field's last good value: its typed text when it was a plain value, or the current result (in the part's units, or degrees) when it was an expression. Yes adds the variable as one undoable step (`SetVariables`) and puts `=Name` in the field; No puts the last good text back. Enter on such a request never accepts the panel. A name already in use simply links the field to it (`=Name`); an invalid name says why. The handle value box (D148) goes through the same path, since it types into the panel field. The sketch dimension value box belongs to the sketch work package and is not changed here. (4) The parser for the request lives in `core/units/variables.py` (`requested_variable`, `valid_name`), so it is tested without Qt. No file format change: variables already exist in schema 1 (FDEF_SPEC 4).
Status: Default
Reason: Follows TOOL_SPEC T14.6; the value used for a new variable and the Enter behaviour are not given by the spec.

D176: Shortcut editor (TOOL_SPEC T14.7). (1) Columns are Category, Command, Shortcut and Search Words. The category list holds All and each command group; the group Interface, whose commands sit in no menu of their own, is shown as Other. The search box matches any column, search words included. (2) Search words are extra words the shortcut bar search matches. A few commands have plain English defaults in `commands.DEFAULT_WORDS` (for example "whole" for Zoom to Fit); the user edits them by double clicking the cell, and only changes from the defaults are saved, under `input/search_words` in the preferences. (3) Assigning a key in use asks "L is used by Line. Move it to Wireframe?"; Yes moves it and removes it from the other command, No changes nothing. (4) The key box (`KeyCapture`) reads the key code and the Ctrl, Shift, Alt and Meta modifiers only, never the typed text, so Caps Lock never acts as Shift; Caps Lock and modifier keys alone are ignored. Letters show in upper case everywhere in the editor. App shortcuts already match by key code, so Caps Lock never changes which command a key runs. (5) Buttons: Assign, Remove Shortcut (the selected command keeps no key), Reset to Defaults (asks Shortcuts Only, Everything or Cancel; Everything also resets search words, gestures and the shortcut bar, applied with OK like other changes) and Copy List (one line per command: category, command and shortcuts, separated by tabs, to the clipboard).
Status: Default
Reason: Follows TOOL_SPEC T14.7; the meaning of "everything" and the default search words are not given by the spec.

D210: Extrude end conditions Up to Vertex, Up to Face and Offset from Face (PHASE2_SPEC P2.1 item 1). (1) Both directions offer them; `end_condition` (Direction 1) and `end_condition2` (Direction 2) take `"up_to_vertex"`, `"up_to_face"` and `"offset_from_face"`, and the pick is `refs.end` or `refs.end2`: a vertex reference or a sketch point for Up to Vertex, a face reference or a plane feature for the other two. Offset from Face adds `end_offset`, `end_offset_reverse` and `end_translate` (suffix `2` for Direction 2). (2) An end on a plane parallel to a flat start (a vertex plane, a parallel plane or flat face, or such a face offset) is a plain depth, so the feature is the usual prism with the usual names; a parallel flat face must still hold the whole moved profile. Any other end uses a long prism of the profile cut away beyond the end face and behind the start; the end face is named `cap/end` and the start `cap/start`. If anything is left beyond the end face's reach along the direction, the face does not cover the profile and the feature fails with "the Direction 1 end face does not cover the whole profile". (3) Offset from Face moves the end toward the start by default; Reverse offset puts it beyond the face. A flat face is moved along its normal; a curved face is offset with the kernel's simple offset; Translate surface moves either face along the extrude direction instead. (4) A lost pick is an error naming it, as for the From pick (D140 item 4). (5) The new end conditions have no drag handle.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the choices and the coverage rule but not the storage or the method. Reusing the plain prism where the end is a depth keeps names and speed; the cut back method works for any face the kernel can sweep.

D211: Thin Feature for extrudes (PHASE2_SPEC P2.1 item 3). Stored as optional keys: `thin_type` (`"one_direction"`, `"mid_plane"`, `"two_direction"`), `thin_thickness`, `thin_thickness2` (Two Direction), `thin_reverse`, `thin_cap` and `thin_cap_thickness`. The wall is the region between the curves offset `a` mm to the outside and `b` mm to the inside (sharp corners, the kernel's intersection join). One Direction puts the wall inside a closed profile, so the outer size stays what the sketch shows, and on the kernel's positive offset side of an open profile; Reverse swaps the sides; Mid Plane splits the thickness; Two Direction takes the first thickness outside and the second inside. Open profiles must be one chain without branches. Side faces are named `side/<entity>/outer` and `side/<entity>/inner`, and the two end walls of an open profile `side/<first entity>/start` and `side/<last entity>/end`. Cap ends (closed profiles only, flat start and Blind ends) adds a lid of the cap thickness inside each end; the lids' inner faces are `thin_cap/start` and `thin_cap/end`. Thin Feature is not offered for revolve, since P2.1 names only the extrude.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the three types, Reverse and Cap ends but not which side One Direction takes or how faces are named. Keeping the sketch as the outer size of a closed wall matches the most common use (a box wall).

D212: Draft while extruding (PHASE2_SPEC P2.1 item 2). Stored as optional `draft_angle` and `draft_outward`, with suffix `2` for Direction 2; the angle's presence turns the draft on. Every side face of that direction leans by the angle from the extrude direction about the start plane, inward unless Draft outward is ticked (0 to 89 degrees). Draft needs a flat start and an end given by a depth (Blind, Mid Plane, Through All, or Up to Vertex on a flat start); with Up to Face, Offset from Face or a curved start the feature fails with a message saying so. With a draft each direction is built as its own prism and the two are joined, so Direction 2's side faces are named `side2/<entity>`. The draft uses the kernel's draft angle operation on the prism's side faces.
Status: Default
Reason: The kernel drafts faces about a neutral plane reliably; drafting a face that follows a curved end face is not reliable, so it is left out (PHASE2_SPEC: offer only what OpenCascade does reliably).

D213: Fillet (PHASE2_SPEC P2.4, PLAN 5A items 4 to 6). (1) Type `fillet`. Params: `fillet_type` (`"constant"` or `"variable"`), `radius`, optional `multiple_radius` with `radius_<k>` for picked edge `k` (1 based, in `refs.edges` order); variable size uses `vr_<k>_start`, `vr_<k>_end`, `control_points` (0 to 5, evenly spaced, the same count for every edge), `vr_<k>_<j>` and `transition` (`"smooth"` or `"straight"`). Numbered radii are re-evaluated like other lengths through a new `FeatureType.kind_of`. Refs: `edges`, `faces` (all edges of each face) and `features` (all edges of the faces that feature made). (2) Smooth transition is the kernel's interpolated radius law; Straight adds evenly spaced extra points on straight lines between the given radii, so the law follows the straight segments closely. (3) New faces are named `fillet/<edge name>` (FDEF_SPEC 8.1), corner blends `corner/face#k`. (4) Pre check and pinpointing: when the kernel cannot round every edge at once or the result is invalid, each edge is tried alone, and for each failing edge the largest working radius is found by eight halving steps. The feature then fails with the list of failing edges and their largest radius, highlights them, and offers two fix buttons: "Fillet the rest (skip N edges)" (removes them from `refs.edges`) and "Reduce the radius to X mm" (just under the smallest largest radius, rounded down to three digits). The preview shows the partial result (the edges that work) and the panel lists the failures with the same buttons; nothing changes until the user clicks a button and then OK (or clicks the fix in the errors panel, which is one undoable command). (5) Left out because the kernel has no reliable way to do them: Asymmetric (two distance) fillets, turning off tangent propagation (the kernel always rounds a whole smooth chain), Keep features, Round corners, the closed edge overflow choices, loops as a separate pick kind (pick the face or the edges), and the [Later] items. Select through faces depends on viewport selection, which another work package owns, so it is not in this panel. (6) Preview modes: Full, Partial (one item at a time, a Next Item button steps on) and None. The Next Item button replaces the A key, which already moves the confirmation corner. The panel remembers the type, radius, Multiple radius and transition for the next new fillet in the same session. The owner approved on 2026-11-02 (D750, TR131) a tick to turn tangent propagation off, to be built after a kernel test.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for the checks and partial results with the user confirming, and to offer only what OpenCascade does reliably.

D214: Panels of the Phase 2 features that do not start from one profile (fillet, chamfer, shell, draft, sweep, loft). They are forms in `ui/property_panel/forms`, one module per type, plugged into the existing property panel, which keeps the header, OK, Cancel, the message line, Enter and Esc (TOOL_SPEC T5). A form lists picked items in a list with Remove (and Move Up and Move Down where order matters); a click in the view adds faces or edges to the list (never removes them), a pick made by the feature itself or a later one is refused with a message, and lost picks are listed first in red. The command opens the panel at once, with the current selection as the first picks. While a feature is edited the view shows the finished part; picks are stored by name, so edges the feature did not change keep working. The preview of a feature that changes the part (fillet, chamfer, shell, draft) shows the new and changed faces only. The preview's failure message and fixes reach the panel through a new `checked` signal of the feature preview. Fix actions that edit a feature (`skip_items`, `set_param`) live in `core/features/fixes.py` and run as one undoable command from the errors panel.
Status: Default
Reason: The extrude and revolve panel is built around one sketch; a form per type keeps each module small (CLAUDE.md 6.5) and shares the panel's conventions.

D215: Shortcuts of the Phase 2 feature commands follow SHORTCUTS.md section 5: Fillet Shift+F, Chamfer Ctrl+Shift+F, Draft Shift+D, Swept Boss Shift+S, Lofted Cut Shift+L; Lofted Boss and Shell have none. Swept Cut gets no default key because Ctrl+Shift+S, which SHORTCUTS.md also lists for it, is Save As. The owner can bind it in the shortcut editor. The Features tab has a new Modify group (Fillet and Chamfer large, Shell and Draft in a column) and Sweep and Loft in columns beside the boss and cut tools.
Status: Default
Reason: Two commands cannot share a default key; Save As is the long standing meaning.

D216: Chamfer (PHASE2_SPEC P2.5). (1) Type `chamfer`. Params: `chamfer_type` (`"angle_distance"`, `"distance_distance"` or `"vertex"`), `distance`, `angle`, `method` (`"symmetric"` or `"asymmetric"`) with `distance2`, optional `flip`, and for the vertex type `distance2`, `distance3` or `equal`. Refs: `edges` and `faces` (all edges of each face) for the edge types, `vertices` for the vertex type. New faces are named `chamfer/<edge name>` and `chamfer/<vertex name>`. (2) The reference face of an edge (where the first distance, or the angle and distance, are measured) is the neighbouring face whose name sorts first; Flip uses the other face. The spec's handle in the view that shows the side is left out, because the view's handles belong to another work package; the Flip button does the same. (3) The vertex chamfer is not a kernel chamfer: it cuts off the tetrahedron between the corner and the points at the three distances along the three edges, ordered by edge name. It needs exactly three straight edges at the corner and a distance shorter than each edge; otherwise the feature fails and says so. (4) Edge chamfers are pinpointed like fillets (D213 item 4) with the fixes "Chamfer the rest" and, for one distance, "Reduce the distance". (5) Lost picks fail the feature naming them, and the panel lists them first in the error colour so the user can pick again or remove them (P2.5 item 4). (6) Tangent propagation is always on and Keep features and Select through faces are left out for the reasons in D213 item 5. Preview modes and remembered settings follow D213 item 6.
Status: Default
Reason: The kernel chamfers edges with two distances or a distance and an angle; it has no corner chamfer, and a plane through three points is exact for straight edges.

D217: Shell (PHASE2_SPEC P2.6, PLAN 5A item 4). (1) Type `shell`. Params: `thickness`, optional `outward`, and `thickness_<k>` for face `k` of `refs.thick_faces` (Multi Thickness). Refs: `faces` (faces to remove), `thick_faces`, and `body` (one face of the body to shell) when the part has several bodies and no face is removed. With faces removed the kernel's thick solid is used; with none, the part minus its inner offset (or the outer offset minus the part) gives a closed hollow part. Other bodies pass through unchanged. Wall faces are named `shell/<face name>`. (2) Diagnostics run before the kernel as a pre check and name the tightest face: each curved face is sampled on a 5 by 5 grid, and a face that bulges out (inward wall) or curves in (outward wall) with a radius smaller than the largest wall thickness stops the feature with "face X bends with a radius of R mm, smaller than the T mm wall", highlighting every such face. A kernel failure without such a face gives a general message. Sampling the curvature is used because the kernel can return a valid looking but wrong solid when a wall cannot fit, so the check must come first. (3) Show preview is a session setting of the panel; with it off no preview is built.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for a check that finds faces with a curvature radius smaller than the thickness; checking before the kernel catches cases the kernel does not report.

D218: Draft, neutral plane method (PHASE2_SPEC P2.7). (1) Type `draft`. Params: `angle`, optional `reverse` and `propagation` (`"none"` default, `"tangent"`, `"all"`, `"inner"`, `"outer"`). Refs: `neutral` (a plane feature or a flat face reference) and `faces`. The pull direction is the neutral plane's normal (the face's outward normal for a face); Reverse flips it. Drafted faces keep their names. (2) The kernel always carries a draft across faces joined smoothly, so None and Along tangent give the same result where faces meet smoothly; both stay in the list as the spec asks, and Along tangent also adds smooth neighbours to the list sent to the kernel. (3) All faces means every side face along the pull: flat faces square to the neutral plane and cylinders or cones whose axis follows the pull. Inner faces are side faces from which a line leaving the face outward meets the part again (holes and pockets); Outer faces are the rest. (4) A flat face square to the pull, or a face the kernel cannot tilt, fails the feature naming the face. A lost neutral plane or face is an error naming it. (5) The preview shows the changed faces in the preview colour (P2.7 item 3); untick Show changed faces to see the whole drafted part. In the panel the first flat face clicked while Pick Neutral Face is on sets the neutral plane, later clicks add faces to draft.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the fields and propagation modes; the ray test is a simple, exact way to tell holes from the outside for prismatic parts.

D219: Sweep, boss and cut (PHASE2_SPEC P2.2). (1) Type `sweep`. Params: `operation`, optional `merge`, `profile_type` (`"circular"` with `diameter`), `orientation` (`"keep_normal"`), `twist` (`"minimum"`, `"angle"` with `twist_angle`, `"direction"`) and the extrude's `thin_*` keys for bosses. Refs: `profile` (a sketch), `path` (a sketch whose curves form one chain) or `path_edges` (a chain of edge references), and `twist_direction` (a plane feature, a flat face or a straight edge). Faces: `cap/start`, `cap/end`, `side/<entity>` (`#k` for each further path segment); a circular profile's side is `side/circle`. (2) Twist mapping to the kernel: None is the kernel's Frenet frame (fine for flat paths), Minimum Twist its corrected Frenet frame, Keep Normal Constant a fixed frame, Specify Direction Vector its constant binormal mode. Specify Twist Angle has no kernel mode: an auxiliary spine is built that turns about the path by the angle, evenly along the length, around a frame carried with the least turning (double reflection on 49 samples); the result's volume matches the untwisted sweep to about 1 percent because the spine is an approximated curve. (3) The path must start or end on the profile's plane (an end on it is used as the start); otherwise the feature fails and says so. A path whose non neighbouring segments touch fails with "the path crosses itself"; an invalid result fails with "the swept result intersects itself". (4) Left out because the kernel has no reliable way to do them as the spec describes: guide curves and the guide based twists (the kernel's guide mode keeps the section rigid instead of shaping it to the guides), the path through the middle of the profile with Direction 1, 2 or Both, Start and End tangency (the section follows the path; a profile not square to the path start keeps its angle), Tangent to Adjacent Faces, whole turn rules for closed paths, Merge Tangent Faces and Merge Smooth Faces as options (the part's faces are merged where they lie on one surface, as for every feature), and Show Sections. The owner approved on 2026-11-02 (D750, TR55) guide curves for sweeps, to be built after a kernel test.
Status: Default
Reason: PHASE2_SPEC P2.2 item 5 and PLAN: offer only what OpenCascade does reliably and record what is left out.

D220: Loft, boss and cut (PHASE2_SPEC P2.3). (1) Type `loft`. Params: `operation`, optional `merge`, `start_constraint` and `end_constraint` (`"default"`, `"none"`, `"normal"`, `"direction"`) with `start_length` and `end_length`, `connect_<k>` (the edge where profile `k` starts), `close_loft`, and the extrude's `thin_*` keys for bosses. Refs: `profiles` (sketches or flat faces, in order) and `start_direction`, `end_direction` (a plane feature, a flat face or a straight edge). Faces: `cap/start`, `cap/end` and `side/<entity>` from the first profile's curves; other faces get fallback names. (2) Each profile must be one closed region; holes in a solid loft's profiles are not joined. Every profile is turned to face along the loft before joining, so profiles on planes facing either way join correctly. (3) Default is the kernel's smooth surface through the profiles; when both ends are None the faces are straight between profiles. Normal to Profile and Direction Vector have no kernel option: a copy of the end profile is placed a quarter of the tangent length out along the normal (toward the next profile) or the picked direction, and the smooth surface passes through it, so the loft leaves that way; a longer length reaches further. (4) Connection points are a number per profile (the edge it starts on) set in the panel for the selected profile; when any is set, or the loft is closed, the kernel's own alignment is off and the wires are used as given. (5) Close loft joins the last profile back to the first through the same smooth surface; start and end constraints do not apply then. (6) Left out because the kernel has no reliable way to do them: dragging connection points and tangent handles in the view (the view's handles belong to another work package), connector lines in the preview, the draft angle of the end constraints, Tangency to Face, Curvature to Face and Next Face, guide curves with their influence and tangency, the centerline with its section count, Merge tangent faces as an option, Show preview see through or solid toggle, and Show Sections. The owner approved on 2026-11-02 (D750, TR55) guide curves and a centerline for lofts, to be built after a kernel test.
Status: Default
Reason: PHASE2_SPEC common rules and PLAN: offer only what OpenCascade does reliably and record the rest.

D230: Phase 3 feature layout (PHASE3_SPEC, round 4e). Each Phase 3 type is its own module in `core/features` and registers through `core/features/phase3.py`, so the shared `__init__` gains one line. Shared kernel helpers live in new modules instead of the Phase 1 ones: `direct.py` (face editing), `booleans.py` (booleans on plain and named shapes), `geometry_refs.py` (directions, axes, points and planes from stored references), `bodies.py` (multibody), `face_picks.py` (helper bar), `lookup.py` (late imports of the reference resolver, which imports the feature package). Offset Face is a command, not a type: it opens Move Face with Offset chosen (PHASE3_SPEC P3.1.3), so the planned `offset_face` type name in FDEF_SPEC 5.3 is not used. Every kernel result is checked for a null shape before any other kernel call: an offset that reported success with a null shape crashed the process on the next call (found while testing an imported body).
Status: Default
Reason: Other sessions edit `solids.py`, `extrude.py` and the Phase 2 modules at the same time; new modules keep the merge clean, and the null check keeps the app from crashing (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

D231: Face helper bar (PHASE3_SPEC P3.1.1 item 2). Meaning of each button: all coplanar faces (every face of the part on the same plane); all inner loops (the faces across the edges of the picked face's inner loops, for example each hole wall and boss side in it); all outer and inner loops (the faces across every edge of the picked face); all faces around it (every face sharing a vertex with it); all tangent faces (faces reached across smooth edges, repeated); all coplanar and connected faces (coplanar faces reached through shared vertices, repeated); full cylinders or cones with the same axis direction, or on the same axis (faces that go all the way round; for a flat picked face its normal is the direction). The bar appears beside the cursor after a face goes into the Faces box, works out every helper on the thread pool, greys out buttons that add nothing, and highlights a button's faces on hover with the view's existing highlight (the only highlight style it has). A click adds the faces without removing any already picked.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec names the helpers but not their exact reach; these are the plain readings, and running them off the UI thread follows CLAUDE.md rule 2.

D232: Move Face and Delete Face methods (PHASE3_SPEC P3.1). Offset Faces runs the kernel's per face offset (skin mode, intersection joins), so neighbours stretch. It fails when the part has tangent fillets elsewhere, so a second method adds or cuts a thin slab grown from each face when every neighbour meets it at a right angle (bosses, holes, end faces); a round face that would shrink to nothing is refused first, naming the face. Translate with only flat faces offsets each face by the move's normal part (a flat face's outline comes from its neighbours, so this is the same as moving it). Other moves use the face group's volume: the group is patched away, the material it added (a boss) and removed (a hole) are moved and added or cut again. Rotate tries the volume first, then turns flat faces about the line where the old and new planes meet (a draft). After every method each flat picked face must lie on its target plane, else the next method is tried; when none works the message names the faces and what to do. Moved faces keep their names (found by position for the volume method). Copy uses the volume method only: it needs faces that form a whole feature, and the copy must join the body. Up to Face needs a parallel target; Offset from Face stops the distance short of the target on the side the face is on now; Up to Body moves along the first face's normal until the extents touch. Delete and Patch uses the kernel's defeaturing; because the kernel can hand back a face rebuilt in the same place, every picked face must really be gone. When several faces fail together, each is tried alone and the message names those that cannot go, with the fix "Keep the faces that worked" (fix action `drop_refs`, one undoable step, never automatic). Delete and Fill closes each opening with one filling face (touching, or smooth with Tangent fill), sews and checks the solid. Delete without healing is shown greyed with the reason, since surface bodies are not in PLAN.
Status: Default
Reason: These are the operations OpenCascade does reliably on both native and imported bodies; each was tested on flat and curved faces, holes, fillets and bosses of our own test parts and of a STEP round trip body.

D236: Phase 3 user interface (TOOL_SPEC T5 conventions). (1) Text is in `ui/strings_phase3.py` beside `strings.py` while several sessions add tools; it moves into `strings.py` when Phase 3 merges. (2) The panel of every Phase 3 type is built from a table in `ui/body_tools/forms.py` by `FeatureForm`; the property panel only hands over to it, so Extrude and Revolve are unchanged. Fields that do not apply are hidden and not written, so they never change the result. (3) Pick boxes: the active box (marked) takes clicks in the view; a click on a face already listed removes it; a single pick box is replaced and the next empty box takes the next click; Delete removes selected rows; selecting a row highlights it in the view. Boxes that take planes also list the plane features in a dropdown. (4) Transform handles reuse the drag handles of D146 to D148 (ruler, protractor, clickable value): an arrow for Distance, arrows for Delta X, Y and Z, rings for angles. A drag keeps a delta's sign; dragging past the start flips Reverse, or the sign of a delta. (5) The new commands have no default keys, so nothing is taken from the user's shortcuts; they are in the shortcut editor, the Insert menu and the Features tab (Direct Editing, Pattern and Bodies groups before Rebuild). (6) Right click on a face (when no panel is open) offers Move Face, Offset Face and Delete Face with that face picked; the other face menu items of TOOL_SPEC T9.6 belong to the viewport work. (7) Tree rows of Phase 3 types use their command icon.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the behaviour; these choices keep edits to shared files small (one hook each) and reuse the Phase 1 handle and value box code.

D234: Patterns and mirror (PHASE3_SPEC P3.2, P3.3). (1) Seeds: earlier boss and cut features (each feature's own solid, as its preview builds it, is moved and added or cut again), faces that form a whole feature (the volume they add or remove, found by patching them away, D232), or bodies (copies are new bodies; Merge result fuses them with the seed). Geometry pattern copies the faces a seed feature made instead of building it again; it fails with a clear message when those faces were merged away. (2) Every copy is its own tool in one boolean, so copies that touch or overlap each other join cleanly (a compound of touching copies as one tool gave wrong volumes). (3) A copy that does not reach the part is an error naming it, with the fix "Skip copies that failed" (action `skip_instances`), which the user confirms; the other copies are kept. (4) Instances are numbered from 1 along each direction; the seed is 1.1. Instances to skip are stored in the feature's top level `skip` key as `[i, j]` pairs and typed in the panel as "3, 5, 2.2". Clickable dots in the view are not built in this round: the view's picking belongs to another work package; the typed list gives the same control. (5) Linear: the direction comes from an edge, flat face, plane, axis or sketch line (a linear dimension as a direction is not built); Up to reference counts the instances that fit between the seed's centre and the reference less the offset. Direction 2 is turned on by `second_direction`; Pattern seed only repeats only the seed along it. (6) Circular: Equal spacing shares the total angle (a full turn: count gaps; less: the last copy lands on the end); otherwise the angle is between copies. Direction 2 turns the other way; Symmetric uses direction 1's values. (7) Sketch driven: one copy per sketch point that is not the end or centre of a curve; the reference point is the seed's centre or a picked vertex. (8) Partial preview shows only the first copy in each direction. (9) Propagate colours is stored; it takes effect when face colours exist (Phase 2 appearance work), by giving each copy the colour of the seed face named in its role. (10) At most 1000 instances per pattern. (11) Mirror: one or two planes or flat faces, up to three copies; Mirror seed only (two square planes) leaves out the copy mirrored about both; parallel planes are refused.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the options; these choices keep patterns to one boolean per seed (PLAN 11.3 item 4), never change geometry without a click (CLAUDE.md rule 12), and keep the file format additive.

D233: Multibody features (PHASE3_SPEC P3.4 items 1 to 5). (1) A feature refers to a body by a face reference to any face of it, so bodies follow the PLAN 6 naming and snapshot rules; bodies are numbered in the order of the part's solids and shown as "Body 1", "Body 2" in pick boxes. (2) Combine: Add fuses the picked bodies, Subtract cuts the tool bodies from the main body, Common keeps where all picked bodies overlap (an error when they do not); bodies not picked stay as they are. Make main body see through is not built (it is display work in the viewport package). (3) Intersect uses the kernel's volume maker on the picked bodies and planes (planes and flat faces as large squares): a region counts as overlap when it lies inside two or more picked bodies (inside one when one body is cut only by planes), and as internal when it lies inside none; "inside" is judged by the shared volume of region and body (more than half). Regions are numbered by centre position; the region list stores excluded numbers in the top level `exclude` key. The kept regions replace the picked bodies; Merge result fuses touching regions. Cap flat openings is stored but changes nothing until surface bodies exist. (4) Split: each body is split on its own (overlapping bodies never cut each other); planes and flat faces are endless, curved faces are used as they are, sketches cut through all both ways along their normal. The Cut button lists the resulting bodies on the thread pool; ticks are stored in the top level `keep` key (piece numbers by centre position), left out when every piece is kept. Numbered callouts in the view are not built (viewport work); the list shows the numbers. Saving bodies to files is Later in the spec. (5) Move and Copy Body: translate by Delta X, Y, Z, along an edge by a distance, or vertex to vertex; rotate about an edge or about an origin with X, Y and Z angles (turned in that order). Copies are numbered `copy1`, `copy2` and each moves one step further. Its transform handles are arrows and rings as in D236. (6) Delete and Keep Body: deleting every body is refused with a message. (7) Isolate, hide and show bodies (P3.4 item 6) are not in this round.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the tools; these choices keep body references stable through rebuilds and keep the file format additive.

D235: Scale (PHASE3_SPEC P3.8 item 1, PLAN Phase 3). Bodies to scale are optional; with none picked, every body is scaled. Scale about the centre of the picked bodies (centre of volume), the origin, or a point typed as X, Y, Z (the spec's "picked coordinate system" waits for the Phase 2 coordinate system feature). Uniform uses one factor; per axis uses X, Y and Z factors through a general transform, so circles become ellipses. Factors must be between 0.001 and 1000. Sketch scale (P3.8 item 2) is a Sketch tab tool and is not built here, since the sketch tools belong to another session this round. The PLAN item "Transform handles" stays open: handles exist for Move Face and Move Body, but there are no scale arrows yet.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeps the feature to what the kernel does exactly, and leaves shared sketch and viewport code to their own work packages.

D270: Phase 2 sketch tool framework (PHASE2_SPEC P2.8, owner brief of 2026-10-30). (1) The geometry work of every Phase 2 sketch tool lives in `core/sketch/ops/` (no Qt, mypy strict): `geom.py` parametrises curves (a line by 0 to 1 from `p1`, a circle or arc by the angle turned counter clockwise from its counter clockwise start) and finds crossings with exact line and circle formulas; `pieces.py` moves ends, splits and deletes curves. The tools are new classes in new modules of `ui/sketch_tools/` (`pick_tools.py`, `trim_tools.py` and later ones), found by `make_tool` through `registry.py`, so the Phase 1 tool table and the canvas were not restructured. The canvas got four small hooks: a tool with `raw_cursor` gets the cursor without snapping (it picks curves rather than placing points), a tool with `release` handles the button release itself, a tool with `take_message` leaves a status bar note, and pick tools receive the part outline. (2) Each tool is a command `sketch.<name>` in `ui/input/commands.py` with no default key (so none clash with SHORTCUTS.md; users can bind them), sits in a new Modify group of the Sketch tab, and has a small panel built from its `options` list (`ui/sketch_tools/pick_panel.py`) with a prompt line. Tool text lives in `ui/sketch_tools/tool_text.py` and is merged into `ui/strings.py`. (3) Every tool action is one step on the sketch's undo list, and OK writes the sketch as one undoable command, as for the Phase 1 tools (CLAUDE.md rule 3). (4) Removed relations and dimensions are collected in a report and named in the status bar: "Removed with the deleted pieces: 2 relations (Coincident, Horizontal) and 1 dimension (d4)."
Status: Default
Reason: The brief asks for new modules rather than a restructure of `tools.py` and `canvas.py`, because other sessions change those files at the same time.

D271: Trim and Extend rules (P2.8 items 2 and 3). (1) Crossings count with every other curve, construction curves included, within both curves' bounds; meetings at the trimmed curve's own ends do not count. (2) Removing an end piece moves that end point; its relations and dimensions go (they described where it was), and a point shared with another curve is replaced by a new point first. Removing a middle piece splits the curve: the curve keeps its id and the piece at its start, a new curve takes the far piece with the old far end point and its relations; lines are tied by Collinear, arcs share their centre and get Equal. A circle needs two crossings and becomes an arc with the same id, so its relations stay. A curve that nothing crosses is deleted. (3) A line whose length changes loses Fix, Equal, Midpoint, Symmetric and its own length dimension; an arc loses Fix, Midpoint and Symmetric. Relations that act on the full line or circle (Horizontal, Parallel, Tangent, Concentric, point on curve) and the radius stay. (4) With automatic relations on, each new end gets Coincident with the curve that cut it, or with that curve's end point when the cut is there; Corner gives the two ends a Coincident. (5) Corner uses the meeting of the two full lines or circles closest to both picks and keeps the picked side of each curve; it works on lines and arcs. Trim inside and Trim outside take the two boundaries from the first two clicks and keep them until Escape, so several curves can be cut in a row; they work on lines and arcs (on a circle "between" has two answers). Trim outside also extends a curve that stops short of a boundary. (6) Drag trim acts on release: each curve the path crosses loses the piece at its first crossing. A press on the end of a line or arc that is dragged on along the curve's path extends the curve to the release point. A click without a drag trims the clicked piece. Trim to nearest also extends a line or arc when the click lies on its path past an end. (7) Extend takes the end on the half under the cursor to the next curve along its path (lines along their direction, arcs around their circle). Holding the button and dragging on extends again past each further curve the cursor passes.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec gives the modes but not what happens to ids, relations and points; keeping ids and relations that still fit keeps dimensions and later features working.

D272: Offset (P2.8 item 1). (1) The source link is one new relation type, `offset`, per offset operation: its entities are (source, copy) pairs and its optional `value` is the distance in mm (FDEF_SPEC 6 item 4). A relation without `value` is written exactly as before, so older files open and save byte for byte the same (schema 1, as D122 and D150). (2) In the solver all pairs share one distance: fixed at `value`, or free when Add dimension put a distance dimension between the first line and its copy (the dimension then drives every pair; a chain of only arcs and circles keeps the fixed value). A line copy is parallel at the distance; an arc or circle copy shares the source's centre point and its radius is larger or smaller by the distance (the side is read from the geometry). (3) A copy end that no Coincident ties to another curve and that sits square across from its source end (or on the ray from the arc centre through it) is held there, so lone copies follow the source's length; corners between copies get Coincident at the meeting point of the moved curves, and smooth joins (tangent) need nothing more, which avoids a redundant relation. (4) The side and the dragged distance come from the cursor; typing a distance in the panel keeps it until the offset is placed. Select chain is on by default and adds every line and arc joined end to end. A click on a straight part edge or a round part edge offsets a fixed construction copy of it (D113, D116 item 3). Offsetting a model face's outer loop is not built: the part outline in the sketch is a set of section polylines without face names (the reference geometry package owns that). (5) Refused with a message: an arc turned inside out, a line that would reverse, copies that cross each other, corners whose moved curves no longer meet, and branching picks. (6) Cap ends close open chains: lines (perpendicular to a line end, through the centre of an arc end) and arcs (sharing their end points with the source and copy ends, Tangent there, D277) leave nothing free.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for a stored link that follows the source; one relation with a shared distance keeps a dimension on one pair driving the whole offset.

D273: Mirror (P2.8 item 4). (1) Picks are lines, arcs, circles and points; a click on a centerline (construction line) or on a straight part edge, once something is picked, is the mirror line. Pick Mirror Line in the panel makes the next clicked line the mirror line, so a solid line can be used; a part edge becomes a fixed construction copy. Mirroring about a plane or flat face is not built: the sketch canvas has no plane picks (the reference geometry package owns them). (2) Mirrored line ends get one Symmetric relation per pair of points, a circle gets Symmetric on the circle (centre and radius), and an arc gets Symmetric on its two ends plus Equal; mirroring the arc centre as well would add a dependent relation. A point on the mirror line is shared by the copy. (3) Copy off deletes the originals (their relations and dimensions are listed in the status bar), and the mirrored curves are left without Symmetric relations.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec says each pair of mirrored points gets Symmetric; for arcs that over counts by one, so Equal replaces the centre pair.

D274: Sketch fillet and sketch chamfer (P2.8 items 6 and 7). (1) Both work on two lines: picked as a corner point where exactly two line ends meet, or as two lines clicked on the side to keep. Lines that do not touch are trimmed or extended to their corner first. Fillets and chamfers between arcs are not built: the corner of a line and an arc or of two arcs has up to four tangent arc solutions and needs its own picking rules, which the spec does not give. (2) A fillet arc is joined to the new line ends by Coincident and gets Tangent to both lines. Dimension each fillet on gives every fillet a radius dimension; off gives the first fillet made since the tool started a radius dimension and later ones Equal to it. A radius larger than the lines allow is refused with the largest radius that fits. (3) Keep constrained corners (on by default): relations and dimensions on the corner points, other than the join of the two lines, move to a new construction point held at the corner by an Intersection relation with both lines. Off: the first click says how many would be deleted and a second click on the same corner deletes them; no modal question, so the sketch stays usable and the offscreen tests run. (4) A chamfer always keeps a construction corner point (Intersection) and is dimensioned from it: Distance 1 on the first picked line and Distance 2 on the second (Equal distance uses Distance 1 for both), or Distance 1 and the angle between the first line and the chamfer.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec names the options but not what holds the corner or how the question is asked.

D275: Convert Entities (P2.8 item 5). (1) A click on an edge of the part outline on the sketch plane (the section polylines the sketch canvas already draws) copies it: a straight edge becomes a line, a round edge an arc or a full circle (matched to the outline's circles), each with Fix, as D113 and D116 item 3 do for snaps. Edges of other shapes are refused with a message. Select chain copies every outline edge joined end to end with the clicked one; For construction makes construction curves. An edge already copied (a fixed curve on both its ends) is not copied twice. (2) Not built here: the link that moves the copy when the part changes, and copying curves of another sketch. The outline polylines carry no edge names, and other sketches are not handed to the sketch canvas; both belong to the reference geometry and model snapping work that another session is doing (the owner's brief for this round). A copy is fixed, so a later part change never moves it silently.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeps Convert useful now without touching the canvas snapping and reference geometry code that other sessions are changing.

D276: Sketch patterns (P2.8 items 8 and 9). (1) Instances are copies of the picked items; each copied curve gets Equal with its original, and Coincident joins among the picked points are copied, so sizes and joins follow the original. (2) A construction frame keeps the spacing: one anchor per grid place (the copy of the first point of the first pick; a skipped place keeps a construction point there and no geometry, so skipping never breaks the frame), joined by construction lines. Linear: every line along Direction 1 is Equal and Parallel (lines in a row share end points, so Parallel also makes them collinear; Collinear would repeat it), and the same for Direction 2 down the first column. Circular: a construction line from the centre to each anchor, all Equal. (3) Add spacing dimension puts a distance on the first frame line of each direction; Fix direction makes Direction 1 Horizontal or Vertical when its angle is 0 or 90 degrees, or Parallel to the line picked with Pick Direction 1; Direction 2 likewise. A linear pattern with both is fully defined by its original. Circular Add dimensions puts the radius on the first radial line and an angle on each pair of neighbouring radial lines; the copies can still turn about their anchors, since the solver has no rotation relation, so a circular pattern of a shape that can turn shows as under defined. (4) The centre is the sketch origin by default; typing Center X and Y makes a new construction point there; Pick Center Point uses a clicked point, which gets the radial lines' Coincident. Equal spacing shares the total angle (a full turn leaves no instance on the original); off uses the angle as the step. (5) Instances to skip: each new instance has a mark in the preview; clicking it toggles a cross. Changing an instance count clears the skips. Make Pattern in the panel adds the pattern as one undo step.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for patterns that can be made fully defined with dimensions; a frame of construction lines does this with the existing relations.

D277: Slots and polygons (P2.8 items 11 and 12). (1) A slot is two lines and two arcs (or two arcs and two caps for arc slots) that share their end points, with a construction centerline (a line or an arc) whose ends are the cap centres. Tangent between curves that share an end point id is solved as an angle at that point (`angle_via_point`), because the distance form adds a dependent equation there; the Phase 1 tools join curves with Coincident relations and are not affected. With this a straight slot has exactly its five freedoms (two centres and a width) and an arc slot six. Sketch fillets share their end points with the lines the same way. (2) Add dimensions: straight slots get the width (distance between the two lines) and the length, centre to centre on the centerline or overall as a distance between the caps measured to their far sides; arc slots get the cap radius and the centerline radius. The center straight slot has a construction centre point with Midpoint on the centerline. A click on a snap ties the slot's first centre (and for straight slots its second) to it. (3) A polygon is a construction circle and n lines with Equal: inscribed puts the corners on the circle with Coincident, circumscribed makes the sides Tangent to it; it has four freedoms (centre, size, turn). Its values (centre and diameter) are edited through the construction circle's Parameters panel; New Polygon starts the next polygon afresh. The slot's centre, width and length values are set by its dimensions and the Parameters panel of its centerline rather than by fields of their own.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec says a slot is stored as lines and arcs with the relations that keep it a slot; the end point form keeps them fully definable.

D278: Ellipse, partial ellipse and spline (P2.8 items 10 and 13). (1) planegcs supports ellipses, arcs of ellipse and B-splines, so all three were built as new sketch entity types (FDEF_SPEC 6 item 3): `ellipse` (centre, major axis end and minor axis end, all points, so axes are dimensioned with ordinary distances between points), `ellipse_arc` (the same plus start and end points, counter clockwise) and `spline`. Older files have none of them and open unchanged. (2) Solver: an ellipse is a planegcs ellipse on the centre with a hidden focus point, held by its two axis end points (internal alignment); a partial ellipse adds a planegcs arc of ellipse on the same centre and focus whose start lies on that ellipse, which makes them one ellipse without a second size. A point can be Coincident with an ellipse or partial ellipse (on the full ellipse, like arcs, T3.1 note 2). Other relations and Smart Dimension do not take ellipses. (3) A spline is a chain of cubic Bezier pieces through its points; each point has one tangent handle point, and the curve arrives from the handle mirrored through the point, so the curve is always smooth. The solver needs no curve for it: its points and handles are ordinary points that can be dragged, related and dimensioned (the spec's tangent handles that can be dragged and dimensioned); new handles are construction points at a third of the neighbouring chord. The point list with X and Y fields is the normal point panel of each selected point; a separate list panel was not built. Curvature combs are Later in the spec. (4) Kernel: ellipses become `gp_Elips` edges and splines one degree 3 B-spline edge with knots of multiplicity 3, so faces and side faces are exact and named after the entity like other curves. Sketch checks, loops, drawing and picking use 64 samples per curve. (5) Not supported with these curves: crossings and Selected Regions (the region code uses exact line and circle formulas; a profile with crossings and an ellipse or spline gives an error that says so), snapping to points on the curve (their own points snap), and Trim, Extend, Offset, Mirror, fillets and Convert, which work on lines, circles and arcs. Patterns copy them. (6) Tools: Ellipse takes the centre, an axis end and the other axis size (the longer axis becomes the major one); Partial Ellipse also starts its sweep at the third click and ends at the fourth, either way round; Spline adds a point per click, a press and drag sets that point's handle, and a double click, Escape or right click finishes the spline (one undo step) while the tool stays active.
Status: Default
Reason: The brief asks for ellipses only if planegcs supports them; it does, and keeping the shapes as points keeps every existing dimension and relation usable on them.

D279: Sketch picture (P2.9, D33). (1) Pictures belong to the sketch: an optional `pictures` list in the sketch feature (FDEF_SPEC 6 item 7), so they are part of the sketch's own undo list and of the OK command; sketches without pictures save byte for byte as before. The image file is an `image` block in the document's `embedded` section (FDEF_SPEC 11), gzip and base64, with its id taken from a hash of the bytes so the same image is stored once. OK in the sketch writes the sketch and adds the new image blocks as one undoable command, and drops image blocks that no sketch uses any more; undo puts both back. (2) The image's pixel size is read by Qt in the user interface; the core only stores sizes, so `core` stays free of Qt. A new picture sits with its lower left corner on the sketch origin at one pixel to one millimetre, aspect locked. (3) The Sketch Picture command (no default key, Sketch tab) is a tool with a panel: Insert Picture (file dialog; PNG, JPEG or BMP recognised by their first bytes), Origin X and Y, Angle, Width, Height, Lock aspect ratio, Flip horizontally and vertically, Transparency in percent, Enable scale tool, Scale line length and Delete Picture. While the tool is active, dragging inside a picture moves it and dragging a corner resizes it about the opposite corner; each drag is one undo step. The scale tool shows a line with two handles across the lower quarter of the picture; dragging the handles onto two known points and typing the true length scales the picture about the first handle. The handles are tool state, not saved. (4) Pictures draw in the sketch editor under the sketch geometry, with their transparency, and have no snaps. They are not drawn in the 3D view in this round: the 3D view work is with other sessions, so "hiding the sketch hides the picture" holds trivially (a closed sketch shows no picture).
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for an embedded picture with a scale tool and transparency; keeping it in the sketch makes undo and OK work like every other sketch change.

D290: STEP import as a base body (PHASE3_SPEC P3.5). (1) Type `import_step` with `refs.source` pointing at an embedded `step` block (FDEF_SPEC 11, 5.3.15). File, Open accepts `.step` and `.stp` and makes a new unsaved part whose first feature after the default planes is the import; Insert, Import STEP Body adds one to the open part as one undoable step (the block and the feature are added and removed together). Only the file bytes are read on the UI thread; reading and healing run in the rebuild worker. (2) The file is read through OpenCascade's document reader so face and solid colours come with the shape; a face without its own colour takes its solid's. Colours are returned in a new `FeatureResult.extras` dictionary (`face_colors` by face name) and drawn in the view; they are not copied into `appearance.faces`, so the user's own face colours stay separate and win. `extras` also carries `report` (healing lines) and `reference` (a curve or mesh drawn but not part of the body), used by the later Phase 3 features. (3) Healing: `ShapeFix_Shape` with a maximum tolerance of 0.001 mm; loose faces and open shells are sewn at 0.001 mm and every closed shell becomes a solid. The report names what changed: invalid faces repaired, how many open pieces were joined into how many solids, open pieces left out. A file with no closed solid after healing is an error (surface bodies are out of scope); a solid that is still invalid gives a warning that suggests Delete Face. The report shows in the status bar after the rebuild. (4) Faces are named `face/<k>` in the kernel's face order of the healed shape; the same file always gives the same order, so later features keep their references. (5) An import into a part with a body stays a separate body unless `merge` is set (not shown in a panel yet; the feature has no editable values). Imported faces are not merged by the same domain step, so the file's faces and colours stay as they were. (6) Blocks are written with a gzip header without a time stamp, so saving twice gives the same text. A block whose feature is deleted stays in the file so undo works. (7) Sample part `imported_step_with_features`: an L bracket made in code, written as a coloured STEP file (header time stamp and product counter replaced by fixed text so the sample is stable), imported, with a boss and a through hole added on its top face.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN Phase 3 and PHASE3_SPEC P3.5; healing tolerances follow the fuzzy boolean tolerance of D47 scaled for imported data.

D291: Curves: helix and spiral, projected curve, composite curve (PHASE3_SPEC P3.6, FDEF_SPEC 5.3.16). (1) Curve features keep the part as it is and return their curve in `FeatureResult.extras["curve"]` (a wire, or a compound of wires) and `extras["reference"]` for display; they do not create faces, so they have no naming roles. Later features take a curve through a feature reference, like a sketch. The sweep path list and the sweep's path resolution now accept helix, projected and composite curves. (2) Helix: the sketch must hold exactly one non construction circle; its centre, plane and diameter place the curve. Start angle is measured on the sketch plane from the sketch X direction toward its Y direction. Counterclockwise is seen from the side the helix grows toward (right hand rule about the growth direction); Reverse flips the growth direction and, for a spiral, winds it inward. (3) A constant pitch helix is exact: a straight line on a cylinder or, with taper, a cone, turned into a 3D curve by the kernel at 0.000001 mm. Variable pitch and spirals have no exact form: they pass through 64 points per turn (at most 4000 points) with an interpolating spline; this bounded point list is the only Python loop. Turns are limited to 1000. (4) Variable pitch rows are (turn, pitch, diameter); row 1 is at turn 0; pitch and diameter change evenly between rows, so the height of each row is the running integral of the pitch and is shown beside the rows, not stored. A spiral cannot use variable pitch, and taper is for constant pitch helices only (spec P3.6 item 1). A taper that narrows the helix to nothing is an error. (5) Projected curve, Sketch on Faces: each joined chain of the sketch is projected along the direction (the sketch normal unless a plane, flat face or straight edge is picked); without Both directions only pieces on the direction's side of the sketch plane are kept, Reverse uses the other side. Nothing landing on the faces is an error. Sketch on Sketch: both sketches are pulled both ways along their normals into surfaces sized from the sketches, and the curve is where those surfaces cross. Parallel sketch planes are an error. (6) Composite curve: sketches (construction left out), curve features and model edges are joined end to end at 0.0001 mm in any order and direction; more than one resulting piece is an error naming the count. (7) Panels: a Curves group on the Features tab and an Insert, Curves submenu hold the three commands (no default keys). The panels have no live preview; the curve shows after OK. Curves cannot be picked in the 3D view yet; a composite curve takes sketches and curves from a list and edges from the view.
Status: Default
Reason: PHASE3_SPEC P3.6 and PLAN Phase 3; exact geometry where the kernel has it, a bounded point list where it does not.

D292: Pipe, array along curve, contour curves and the curvature graph (PHASE3_SPEC P3.7 items 1, 2, 4 and 5, FDEF_SPEC 5.3.17). Transform handles (item 3) belong to the move and copy body work package and are not built here. (1) Pipe: a round section swept along the path with the least turning frame. Sharp corners in the path get mitred corners, like a welded tube frame: the kernel's round corner option writes corner surfaces that come back from STEP with the wrong volume (about 12 percent less), while mitred corners reimport exactly (CLAUDE.md section 4 item 3). A smooth path is not changed by this. (2) Cap Ends is read as closing both ends of a hollow pipe with a wall as thick as the pipe wall, so the tube is sealed; the void stops one wall thickness from each end (the inner tube is cut back by a box square to the path at each end). A closed path has no ends, so Cap Ends does nothing there. A solid pipe always has flat ends. Inner diameter must be smaller than outer. Boss and cut are both offered; merge as for other bosses. (3) Array along curve: the seed keeps its place and copy k gets the motion that takes the curve's start frame to the frame k along it (least turning frames from the kernel, so copies do not twist on a straight or planar curve); Keep orientation only moves the copies. Count spreads the copies evenly over the whole curve (a closed curve does not put a copy on top of the seed); Spacing places them that far apart and is an error when they would run past the end. Instances to skip are stored as text of numbers separated by commas, because parameter values cannot be lists in the file; the seed (1) cannot be skipped. At most 1000 instances. (4) Features are copied as their own solid (the feature's tool, built where the feature sits in the tree), then added or cut in one boolean for all copies of each operation (PLAN 11.3 item 4). This is the geometry pattern way: a feature that depends on the faces around it is copied as it was built at the seed. Bodies are picked by any face; copies stay separate bodies unless Merge result is ticked. Copies share the seed's geometry with a placement (PLAN 11.4 item 3). (5) Contour curves section the whole part with planes square to the direction, through the reference point (plane origin, face centre or edge start) plus whole steps of the spacing, strictly inside the part; at most 500 planes. The loops are a curve feature like P3.6. Turning a contour into sketch geometry needs the sketch tools' convert command, which belongs to the Phase 2 sketch work package; noted in IDEAS.md.
