(3) Maps: twist turns linearly with the position between the planes; taper scales across the axis from 1 to the factor; stretch lengthens the region by the distance; bend is about an axis along the first axis at the signed radius `(end - start) / angle` on the second axis, so the bent length at the triad origin stays the same and angle and radius are linked (`bend_by` picks which one is typed); flow lays the third axis on the curve from its start (one curve millimetre per millimetre, or spread over the curve with `fit`), with a frame carried along the curve without twisting (double reflection) and the triad's first axis as the start normal; past the curve's ends the part goes on straight along the end tangents. Maps run on whole numpy arrays (CLAUDE.md 5A item 2). (4) The PLAN method, in `core/deform/nurbs.py`: copy the body (the input is shared with other features and the live preview and must never change), convert it with `BRepBuilderAPI_NurbsConvert`, then for every face and edge raise the degree to 3 and insert knots, and solve new control points so the curve or surface passes through the exactly mapped points at its Greville parameters (weights kept; for rational surfaces the system is solved for weighted points). Knots and parameters do not change, and the face's own surface object is changed in place, so the edges' curves on the faces stay attached and valid. Moving control points directly was tried first: it converges only at second order and was replaced. Each surface or curve is refined from about four spans per region length, doubling up to 48 spans, until the largest deviation at sample points is within the tolerance. Vertices are moved by the map; tolerances are updated and the shape is healed (`ShapeFix_Shape`), then checked (`BRepCheck_Analyzer` and a positive volume). (5) Warning (code `approximate`) when the deviation that remains is above the tolerance; the feature's report always gives the largest deviation. Error when the result is not a valid solid, with what to change. Kernel exceptions become feature errors as for every feature. The deviation is measured against the converted body; the NURBS conversion of curved faces can itself differ from the exact surface by a small amount (about 0.05 percent of the volume of a cylinder), which is not included. (6) Control points are read and written one at a time because the kernel binding has no bulk transfer for them; the counts are bounded by the 48 span limit and the maps and solves are numpy. (7) UI: the Phase 3 form tables (`ui/body_tools/deform_forms.py`), commands `feature.bend`, `feature.twist`, `feature.taper`, `feature.stretch` and `feature.flow` (no default keys) in Insert and a Deform group on the Features tab, original icons. The live preview shows the deformed bodies and the two trim planes as square faces; drag arrows move the triad origin along X, Y and Z and each trim plane along the third axis, and the panel values follow (Stretch adds an arrow for the distance). The triad's turn and axis are set in the panel; dragging a rotation ring is left out, as the generic preview has no rotation handle for a frame.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN fixes the method (NURBS, control points, rebuild and validate, tolerance, warning, error) and P4.9 the triad, trim planes and per type rules; the frame storage, map formulas and the fitting step are the simplest choices that keep faces named and results valid.

D394: Phase 4 sample parts for configurations and deformation (PLAN Phase 4, 10 items 2 and 8). (1) `configured_bolt_family`: a socket head bolt (head and shank, two fully defined sketches) driven by the variables D, L, DK and K, with three configurations made by a design table: M6 x 20, M8 x 30 and M10 x 40, head sizes from the published ISO 4762 nominal values (CLAUDE.md 7.6). The file is schema 2 and is saved with M8 x 30 active; a test rebuilds every configuration and checks its volume. (2) `twisted_bar`: a 20 x 20 x 120 bar twisted a quarter turn between its ends. (3) `flowed_strap`: a 12 x 4 x 100 strap with two 5 mm holes laid along a quarter circle of radius 80 (a fully defined arc sketch). (4) PLAN 10 item 8 asks for a tolerance stated per test for deformation samples: the golden file may now hold `volume_rel` and `bbox_abs` for a sample (here 1e-4 and 0.001 mm, since the NURBS fit can differ in its last digits between platforms); samples without them keep 1e-6 and 0.0001 mm. (5) The PLAN sample item also lists the tapped housing and the printable enclosure, which need the holes and fastening work of another session, so the item stays open with a note.
Status: Default
Reason: These are the PLAN Phase 4 samples that configurations, design tables and deformation make possible; per sample tolerances follow PLAN 10 item 8 without loosening the existing samples.

D410: Isolate, hide and show bodies (PLAN Phase 3, PHASE3_SPEC P3.4 item 6, D116 item 4, FDEF_SPEC 10.1). (1) A body is known by its face names, as features refer to bodies (D233). Hiding stores the body's shortest face name in `appearance.hidden_bodies`; a body is hidden while any of its face names is listed, so it stays hidden when the bodies are numbered again. Hiding is display only: hidden bodies still take part in features, measuring and exports. It is saved in the part and goes on the undo list as one step, like hiding a sketch (D114). (2) H hides the bodies of the faces, edges or vertices picked in the view, or the body row picked in the Solid Bodies folder; when all of them are already hidden it shows them. Bodies come before the existing sketch and plane rows. (3) I isolates the picked bodies: only they are drawn until I is pressed again or all hidden bodies are shown. Isolate is a view state of the open part (like the section view, D253): not saved, not on the undo list. (4) Shift+Tab shows the hidden body under the cursor: the view ray at the cursor is intersected with the hidden bodies in a kernel job and the nearest one hit is shown (undoable). With nothing hidden or nothing hit, the status bar says so. The spec gives no temporary preview, so the body stays shown. (5) Ctrl+Shift+Tab (Control+Shift+Tab on a Mac, SHORTCUTS.md 1.2.5) shows every hidden body and leaves isolate. (6) The Solid Bodies folder menu offers Show All Hidden Bodies; a body row adds Hide Body or Show Body and Isolate. Hidden body rows are drawn like suppressed rows. (7) Finding the body of a pick and building the compound of the shown bodies are small topology queries on the UI thread (D75); the ray test intersects geometry and runs off it (CLAUDE.md rule 2, D400). The commands are in a Bodies submenu of the View menu.
Status: Default
Reason: Face names already identify bodies for every multibody feature, so hidden state follows the same rules and needs no new identifiers; display only hiding cannot change geometry (CLAUDE.md 5.12).

D411: Transform handles (PLAN Phase 3, PHASE3_SPEC P3.1.1 item 6, P3.4 item 4, P3.7 item 3, FDEF_SPEC 5.3.14.1). (1) Transform Handles is a command (Features tab, Bodies group; also on a body row of the Solid Bodies folder). It opens Move and Copy Body with the selected body picked: a picked face, edge or vertex of it, or its body row. Every tool that takes bodies now also starts from a picked edge, vertex or body row. (2) While nothing is moved yet, the body shows three move arrows (Delta X, Y, Z) and three turn rings (about X, Y and Z through the centre of the picked bodies). Dragging an arrow keeps Translate by Delta; dragging a ring switches the panel to Rotate about the centre of the bodies, so a move starts with either kind of handle. Once a value is set, only that kind stays, so one feature is always one move or one turn; a further move is a new feature. (3) Turning about the centre is a new `rotate_by` choice, `"centroid"`, computed in the build from the picked bodies, so no kernel work runs on the UI thread to fill origin fields. (4) Scale shows scale handles: small cubes instead of arrow heads, one along X for a uniform factor, or one along each axis. A cube sits half the bodies' size times the factor from their centre, so dragging it twice as far doubles the factor; the ruler ticks every 0.1. Factors are typed as plain numbers. (5) The ruler and protractor snapping, the clickable value and the panel fields following the drag are the shared handle code (D146, D148), unchanged. The result is an ordinary Move and Copy Body or Scale feature in the tree, editable like any other.
Status: Default
Reason: Writing each drag as one existing feature keeps the tree editable and the file format nearly unchanged; switching mode on the first drag gives arrows and rings together without a combined move and turn feature that the spec does not describe.

D412: Finishing mesh import (PLAN Phase 3, PHASE3_SPEC P3.9, D294 item 5, FDEF_SPEC 5.3.19.1). Checked against the PLAN line: display, the warning above 100,000 triangles, convert to a faceted solid and the embedded original were built (D294); measure, section and use as a boolean tool were missing. (1) Measure: a reference mesh has no faces to pick, so when the Measure box is open with nothing picked and an imported mesh is selected in the feature tree, the box shows the mesh's triangle count, size along X, Y and Z, surface area, volume (closed meshes only) and centre (of volume when closed, else of its box). The numbers come from `fdcad.core.mesh_tools` with whole array numpy work, computed in the rebuild and kept in the feature result; a 300,000 triangle test checks the speed. A converted mesh is a solid and measures like any body. The Measure box gains two value kinds: count and volume. (2) Section: the section view's clipping planes belong to the 3D view, so they cut a drawn reference mesh like the part. A mesh has no solid to cap, so the section panel lists where Section 1 cuts each reference mesh: the cut area (closed meshes) and the outline length, from the same numpy module (triangles crossing the plane give one segment each, turned to run round the cut so the areas add up). (3) Boolean tool: a converted mesh can be ticked Subtract from the part, which cuts it out of the part's body (Merge and Subtract exclude each other). A converted mesh kept as its own body also works as a tool body in Combine. A reference mesh must be converted first, since the kernel needs a closed solid to cut with.
Status: Default
Reason: Numpy keeps every mesh number free of Python loops (CLAUDE.md 5A); reusing the Measure box, the section panel and the existing convert step adds the missing uses without a new tool.

D413: Fit presets on Offset Face (PLAN Phase 4, D311, FDEF_SPEC 5.3.14.2). (1) Offset Face (Move Face in Offset mode) gets a Printing fit choice, None, Clearance, Slip or Press, and a Fit tolerance field shown once a fit is chosen. (2) A fit moves every picked face a further gap into the material, whichever way the offset goes: one tolerance for Clearance, half for Slip and none for Press. A hole picked by its wall then grows by the same two, one or no tolerances on the diameter as a Hole Tool fit (D311), and a peg shrinks by the same amount, so mating printed parts get the same gap. (3) The tolerance is copied from the active printer profile (D351) into the feature when the command starts, so the file rebuilds the same on any machine; it is written only while a fit is chosen, and `print_fit` is left out while None. (4) The printer profiles of D351 now exist, so `fit_tolerance()` in the preferences reads the active profile for holes too. Before any profile is saved it still reads the older `printer/fit_tolerance` key (D311 item 2), and setting it writes both. This replaces D311 item 2's storage for new settings; older preferences keep working.
Status: Default
Reason: A per side gap equal to half the hole's diameter change keeps one meaning for every fit preset, and copying the tolerance into the feature keeps rebuilds independent of the machine.

D414: Wall thickness analysis (PLAN Phase 4). (1) Evaluate, Wall Thickness Analysis is an on and off view overlay like the overhang analysis (D354): it is worked out again after every rebuild, runs in a kernel job and changes nothing in the part. (2) Method: the part is triangulated as for the overhang analysis. From the middle of every triangle a ray goes into the material against the outward normal; the wall is as thick as the distance to where the ray meets the surface again. This measures across a wall, not along it, so a long thin plate is thin only through its thickness. (3) Only walls thinner than the minimum matter, so each ray is a short segment and is tested only against triangles whose boxes it can reach: triangles sorted by their lowest X give a slab per block of rays, a box test picks the candidates, and the ray and triangle test runs on all candidate pairs at once. Rays go in blocks that bound the memory (CLAUDE.md 5A rule 2: whole array numpy, no loop per triangle or ray). A 58,000 triangle thin shelled sphere takes about 3.5 s in the test container. (4) A face whose area is thin for at least 90 percent is purple, from 2 percent it is pink in part (the shares of D354). The status bar names the counts and the thinnest wall found. The minimum is the active printer profile's minimum wall (D351).
Status: Default
Reason: A ray across the wall is the plain meaning of wall thickness, needs only the triangles the overhang analysis already makes, and stays fast with a slab and box filter in numpy.

D415: The last Phase 3 and Phase 4 sample parts (PLAN Phase 3 and 4, PLAN 10 item 2). (1) `patterned_flange`: a 100 mm flange, 10 mm thick, with a 40 mm hub 15 mm tall above it, a 20 mm bore and six 8 mm bolt holes on a 70 mm circle, made as one hole and a circular pattern about the hub's side face. (2) `multibody_split_part`: a 120 by 40 by 20 mm block with a 20 mm boss, split by the Right plane into two kept bodies. (3) `tapped_housing`: an 80 by 60 by 30 mm block with a 30 mm bore, four M5 tapped holes on the top and two M4 tapped holes on the front, all with cosmetic threads (Hole Tool table sizes, CLAUDE.md 7.6). (4) `printable_enclosure`: a 100 by 70 by 40 mm box shelled to 2 mm walls with an open top, a 1 by 2 mm lip on the rim, four 9 mm mounting bosses on the floor with M3 heat set insert holes on their tops, and two snap hooks. The PLAN Phase 3 and Phase 4 sample lists are then complete with the samples of D292 to D294 and D394. (5) The hole position sketches are fixed points with no construction origin, because the Hole Tool puts a hole at every point of a sketch it uses; the other sketches are dimensioned from the origin as before. Every feature builds without warnings, every sketch is fully defined, and the golden results were made with `fdcad.samples.make`, which left every older sample file unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: Each sample exercises the features its PLAN line names with round numbers that can be checked by hand, as the earlier samples do.

D430: Final `.fdef` schema review (PLAN Phase 6). (1) `tests/core/io/test_schema_keys.py` walks the writer output of every sample part, graph sample and fixture and checks each key is documented in FDEF_SPEC.md (in backticks, in a JSON example, as a placeholder form such as `radius_<k>`, or in a range such as `length2` to `length8`), and each `params` and `refs` key of a feature is documented in its own type's subsection. Map objects whose keys are names (face colours, embedded block ids, overrides, comments, `measure_to`) are skipped. The other direction checks that every key or quoted value named in backticks in the spec is a string in the source (an f string stem for placeholder keys); a short list names the prose tokens that are not keys (example ids, `null`, the function `migrate_1_to_2`) and the keys built by f strings whose literal parts differ. The review found no undocumented key. (2) `tests/core/io/test_migrations_all.py` covers schema 1, the only earlier schema: 15 hand made schema 1 fixtures in `tests/fixtures/schema1`, one per optional key group, each open, rebuild without errors and save byte for byte; loading through `migrate_1_to_2` gives the same document; a schema 1 file whose configurations list suppressed features saves as schema 2 with `<id>.suppressed` overrides (D391). A schema 1 form of every sample (graphs and graph bodies left out, configured values reduced to suppressed lists) opens, and samples already at schema 1 save unchanged. (3) The spec cleanup renumbered FDEF_SPEC 5.3 to 5.3.1 to 5.3.33 and section 6 items to 1 to 10, with every reference updated; section 12A keeps its number because it is unique and in order.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN Phase 6 asks for a final schema review and migration tests; tests that compare the writer with the spec keep them in step after v1.0.

D431: Naming stress tests (PLAN Phase 6, PLAN 10 item 3). (1) `tests/core/naming/test_stress.py` makes random upstream edits with a fixed seed (20261030, mixed with the sample name) on every sample part and graph sample: variables and feature values changed by 5 or 10 percent (whole number values such as counts by one), sketch dimensions changed the same way, a construction point added to a sketch, a feature suppressed, and a feature moved one step up or down where `move_problem` allows it. Only values typed as plain numbers are changed; formulas follow their variables. (2) While a part rebuilds, every face and edge looked up by name is recorded with the feature that asked. After an edit, a name passes when it gives the closest face or edge of the same kind to the one it gave before (centroid distance over the part's box diagonal, plus normal or axis change and area ratio); a name that gives one clearly farther than another candidate (more than twice as far plus 0.05) is reported as a wrong face. A test plants a wrong face to prove the check finds it. A name that no longer resolves must end in the snapshot warning or an error; every error must end with a full stop, name a feature, and never name one by its id. A cached rebuild after each edit must match a full rebuild, and unsuppressing must give the part and every lookup back exactly. (3) The quick run (3 edits on each sample except the 200 feature part and the lattice block, about 15 s) runs by default; the full run (40 edits on every sample, about 6 minutes, most of it the 200 feature part) is marked `slow`. Tests marked `slow` are skipped unless pytest gets `--run-slow` or `FDCAD_RUN_SLOW=1` is set (`tests/conftest.py`). (4) Result: no name resolved to a wrong face in the full run (about 840 edits). One unclear error was found and fixed: a reference to a suppressed feature, a feature lower in the tree or a deleted feature said "Feature f5 is missing or after this one". `BuildContext` now has an `owner` (the building feature's name, set by the rebuild engine and passed on by patterns and Array Along Curve) and the message names both features and the case, for example "Extrude 1: Plate Sketch is suppressed. Unsuppress Plate Sketch or choose another reference." (regression tests in `tests/core/rebuild/test_reference_messages.py`). (5) A move that `move_problem` allows can still fail at rebuild with a clear message, for example moving a body below the graph that reads it, or a deformation above the body it deforms; these are left as they are, since the message says what to change.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN Phase 6 asks for random upstream edits checking every downstream reference; comparing each lookup with its closest continuation catches silent wrong faces without a per sample answer key.

D432: Phase 6 performance pass (PLAN Phase 6 and section 11, report in `docs/PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md`). (1) Every sample and graph sample was profiled from a cold rebuild; the five slowest steps are kernel work (the hole cuts of the 200 feature part, the hollow pipe boolean, the graph body booleans, the NURBS fit of deformations) and the checks after each boolean. None of them can be made faster without changing how geometry is made, so they were left as they are; the kernel options for oriented bounding boxes and for skipping the inverted solid check were measured and gave no clear gain. (2) Two rebuild overheads were removed without changing any result: equations are solved once per rebuild (`document_variables` takes the solution the rebuild already made, through `namespace_from`), and a feature's cache key uses `feature_to_json_data`, the feature's own canonical file data, instead of writing a one feature document. On the 200 feature part an edit near the end went from 88 to 74 ms and a rebuild with no change from 22 to 11 ms (regression tests in `tests/perf/test_rebuild_overhead.py`). (3) Budget 4 now also covers the four graph samples, and `test_every_budget_has_a_test` maps each PLAN 11.2 budget to its tests (budget 6 stays a manual check, as it needs a GPU). Budgets and margins are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN 11.5 item 3: measure first, fix only what is clearly fixable, and add a regression test for every fix.

D433: User guide (PLAN Phase 6). (1) `docs/user_guide/README.md` is the index: getting started, view and selection, typing values, then one page per tool group in command tab order (sketching, boss and cut, modify, patterns and bodies, curves, reference geometry, holes and fastening, deform, sheet metal, import export and print, evaluate, equations and configurations, node editor). Each tool page has an introduction, where to find the tools, and per tool what it does, steps, main options, tips and common errors. (2) Twelve tutorials in `docs/user_guide/tutorials/` rebuild sample parts step by step with the values of their builders in `src/fdcad/samples`, and end by comparing with the sample file and its volume from the golden results. The node editor tutorial uses the attractor plate graph sample. (3) The pages were written from this repository only (specs, decisions, UI strings and code), with FDCAD names (CLAUDE.md 7). Where a tool is not built yet, the page leaves it out. (4) `tests/docs/test_user_guide.py` checks every page: no em or en dashes, none of the protected product names, a title line, links that resolve, every page reachable from the index, and every command label of the app named somewhere in the guide, so a new command cannot ship without a mention.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN Phase 6 asks for a complete user guide with the sample parts as tutorials; tests keep it in step with the commands and the writing rules.

D434: Owner notes after the 2026-10-30 build. (1) Snapping held only while the cursor stayed within the pick distance, so a snap could drop just before a click. A strong snap (point, centre, midpoint, quadrant, intersection) now holds until the cursor is 1.5 pick distances from it; a click uses the held snap once and then drops it, and Ctrl, snapping off, a raw cursor tool or any sketch change drops it too, so the next point of a tool (a circle's radius, say) is never pulled back onto the point just placed. The pick distance grows from 8 to 10 screen pixels. A point within the pick distance now wins over the curve through it when picking, so a click near a line's end takes the end point, as the snap highlight shows. (2) The sketch grid is off by default: a new Sketch preference "Show the grid" turns it on. The origin marks stay. Stored sketch switches keep their stored value; a missing one takes its default. (3) The view background of the light theme is a neutral light grey gradient (#F2F3F4 to #BEC2C7), and the light theme is the default for new installs instead of following the system. "Follow system" and Dark stay in Preferences. (4) Owner request: values typed in the work area for every feature and sketch tool with a number (TOOL_SPEC T15), built by a cloud session.
Status: Default
Reason: owner test notes 1 to 3 of 2026-10-30.

D435: Owner notes 2026-10-30, second batch. (1) Save As offers FDCAD Part, STEP, STL and 3MF. Picking an export type (or typing a name ending in .step, .stp, .stl or .3mf) runs the same export as File, Export to that file; the part is not saved and keeps its name, so the unsaved changes prompt still protects the features. Save and the close prompt still save only `.fdef`. (2) The Features tab was too crowded (labels cut off at 1920 px). Each family of tools now shares one large button with a dropdown that shows the tool used last: Fillet and Chamfer; Shell and Draft; Rib, Dome and Wrap; the four patterns and Mirror; Move Face and Offset Face; Hole Tool and the threads; the four reference geometry tools; the six curve tools. Sweep and Loft stay compact beside Extrude and Revolve, and likewise for the cuts. Body tools, deformations and imports move to a new Bodies tab; Split for Printing, the printing fastener features and the print checks (from Evaluate) move to a new 3D Print tab. Rebuild leaves the Features tab (Evaluate tab, Edit menu, Ctrl+B). Tab order: Features, Sketch, Bodies, 3D Print, Sheet Metal, Evaluate, Graph. The grouping follows the common CAD convention of families behind one button; the layout and names are FDCAD's own (CLAUDE.md 7.4). (3) Every large button reserves the dropdown arrow's room, so plain buttons and dropdowns line up. (4) End conditions: Through All for both directions of Extrude, and Through All (a full turn), Up To Vertex, Up To Face and Offset From Face for Revolve and Revolved Cut, are specified in TOOL_SPEC T16 and built by a cloud session.
Status: Default
Reason: owner test notes of 2026-10-30.

D436: Left panel tabs as icons (owner screenshot 2026-10-30). Five named tabs (Feature Tree, Properties, Variables, Errors, Configurations) were cut off at the default panel width. Each now shows an icon with its name as tooltip (`main_window/left_tabs.py`); the Errors tab shows its count beside the icon and "Errors (n)" in the tooltip. Icons reuse existing FDCAD icons: part, value field, equations, warning mark, configurations.
Status: Default
Reason: every tab must stay reachable at any panel width.

D437: Four colour themes (owner request 2026-10-30). Preferences, General, Theme offers Beige, Light Gray (the default, stored as `light`), Dark Grey (stored as `dark`), Stealth (black) and Follow system; older settings keep working. Each theme has its own view palette and window chrome in `themes/theme.py` (`SCHEMES`). Beige and Light Gray use the light icon set, Dark Grey and Stealth the dark one, and each family keeps the one accent of D111 so icons and chrome match. Contrast is tested with the WCAG 2 formula in `tests/ui/test_theme_contrast.py`: body text at least 7:1 on every panel colour, captions and error text at least 4.5:1, text on selected rows 4.5:1, the accent 3:1, and the three sketch state colours at least 3:1 against both ends of the view gradient. Dark Grey's view and sketch colours were made lighter and brighter to pass. The left panel tab icons are redrawn when the theme changes.
Status: Default
Reason: owner asked for these four schemes with proper contrast.

D440: Where feature value labels sit (TOOL_SPEC T15.2). (1) `PreviewGeometry` gets an `anchor`, worked out with the preview on the worker thread (`fdcad.core.features.preview_anchor`). It is the first picked reference of the feature that the part can name, looking at the draft's `neutral` reference first and then the references in the order the feature stores them: the middle of an edge (found as the edge the two named faces of `edge(A|B)` share, so no part wide edge naming runs on every preview), or the centre of area of a face. With no such pick (a sketch, a hole position, a shell with no face) it is the middle of the bounding box of the first solid of the feature's own preview shape, which is the first hole for the Hole Tool and the rib, dome or boss itself for the others; with no preview shape either, the middle of the part. (2) A preview that fails still has its anchor, so the labels stay in the view to type a better value. (3) Labels that would overlap move down the screen by their own height, in panel order, starting clear of the drag handle's value (`spread_labels`). The move is done in the view plane at the time the labels are shown; it is not redone while the view turns.
Status: Default
Reason: The first pick is where the user is looking; a face centre and an edge middle are cheap and always on the geometry the value changes.

D441: Which panel fields get a label, and how they stay in step (TOOL_SPEC T15.2, T15.3, T15.8). (1) Every length, angle and number field of the panel (the panel's own fields and its form's fields) that is shown and enabled gets a label, in panel order, which is also the Tab order. Number fields are counts and factors; they show as plain numbers. Fields with a drag handle keep the single value beside the handle (T5.2.3, unchanged) and get no second label. (2) Label text is made from the panel field every time (`label_text`), so the field and the label never disagree: a change in the panel updates the labels at once, and a change in the box goes through `panel.set_text`, the path the handle value box already used. OK on the panel stays the one undoable command; nothing is stored in `.fdef` files. (3) Tab and Shift+Tab apply the box and move it to the next or previous label, round from the last to the first; a wrong value keeps the box where it is. Moving to a value with a drag handle makes it the active handle, so the box opens beside it. (4) Escape closes the box and puts back every field the box changed since it was opened, including values applied with Tab or the rebuild arrow. (5) Typing a digit, minus, dot or `=` with the 3D view focused (no Ctrl, Alt or Meta) opens the box on the label used last, or the first one, with that character typed and the cursor after it. The view only takes these keys while a feature panel listens for them, so they do nothing new at other times. (6) Enter in a value box is kept by the box, so it no longer also reaches the view or sketch behind it. (7) Opening the helix panel on a bare feature with no sketch blocks in the test container; the label test leaves helix and the two import types out, which use the same field code.
Status: Default
Reason: One source of truth (the panel field) keeps the labels, the preview and the undo step the same as typing in the panel.

D442: Sketch tool value labels (TOOL_SPEC T15.5). (1) Every option of kind length, angle or int of the active sketch tool gets a label, in option order: today Offset, Sketch Fillet, Sketch Chamfer, Linear and Circular Sketch Pattern, Polygon and Sketch Picture. A new tool with such an option gets labels with no extra code. (2) Labels show once the tool has something to preview: a pick, a first click, or a curve under the cursor. They sit just below and right of the first pick (its relation tag anchor), else the curve under the cursor, else the first click, else the cursor, stacked one under the other. (3) Clicking a label, or typing a digit, minus, dot or `=` with the sketch focused, opens the shared value box there (`CanvasValues`). Enter sets the tool attribute through `SketchCanvas.set_tool_option`, the same call the tool panel field now makes, so the panel field, the label and the preview always agree and Offset's distance locks as when typed in the panel. The tool keeps going; its own finish (a click, Make Pattern, Place Offset) works as before. (4) Counts must be whole numbers within the option's range; a wrong value keeps the box red with the message in its tooltip and the status bar. (5) Tab and Shift+Tab move between the labels; Escape puts back the values the box changed. (6) TOOL_SPEC T15.5 also names move, copy, rotate, scale and stretch sketch tools. FDCAD has no such sketch tools yet (they are not in PLAN.md), so none were built (CLAUDE.md 1.5); they would get labels from their options automatically.
Status: Default
Reason: The tool options table already describes every number a sketch tool takes, so one generic label set covers every tool and stays in step with the panel.

D443: Sizes typed while drawing (TOOL_SPEC T15.6). (1) When the active tool has no value labels, typing a number while a shape is being drawn opens the value box at the cursor for: the length of a Line or Centerline after its first click (not a tangent arc segment), the width and then the height of a Corner or Center Rectangle after its first click, the radius of a Circle or Centerpoint Arc after its centre, and the length and then the width of a straight slot (both straight kinds) after its first and second click. (2) Enter locks the size on the tool (`tool.locks`, the typed text with its value). The shape keeps following the cursor for its direction (`typed_size.constrain`, applied after the tool's own snapping, so a horizontal snap still holds), and the next click places it. Enter again, with no box open, finishes the shape where the cursor is. A rectangle asks for its height right after its width; Tab switches between them. (3) When the shape is made, each locked size adds a driving dimension with the typed text, as Smart Dimension would: Distance on the line, Distance on the bottom and left sides of a rectangle, Radius on a circle or arc, Distance on a slot's centre line and Diameter on one slot end. They are added in the same undo checkpoint as the shape, so one Ctrl+Z removes both. A dimension that would over define the sketch becomes a reference dimension (T11.5). (4) Escape in the box closes it without locking; Escape in the sketch drops the shape and its locks. A size must be above zero.
Status: Default
Reason: Locking the size and letting the cursor set the direction matches "the direction still follows the cursor" in T15.6, and adding the dimension with the shape keeps the size the user typed.

D444: `mypy` on phase1 (housekeeping, not a code change). `uv run mypy` reports 105 errors in 24 UI files on `phase1` before this work (for example `fdcad/ui/body_tools/form_widget.py` and `fdcad/ui/main_window/window.py`); `fdcad/core` is clean. This round adds no new errors and leaves the older ones for a separate cleanup, since fixing 24 unrelated files would collide with the parallel Extrude and Revolve round. Update (cloud/round8r, D480 to D486): the cleanup is done. `uv run mypy` now reports no errors in all 406 source files, with no mypy settings changed and no new `type: ignore` comments.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeps this round to T15 and avoids merge conflicts with cloud/round8q.

D460: Extrude Up to Next (TOOL_SPEC T16 item 1). (1) Each direction with Up to Next is swept on its own as a long prism from the start (as far as Through All reaches for a cut) and clipped: for a boss the prism less the part, for a cut the prism inside the part. Only the solid pieces that touch the start (within 0.0001 mm) are kept, so each part of the profile stops at its own first face. (2) A kept boss piece that still reaches the far end of the prism met nothing, and the feature fails with "Up to Next finds no face for the whole profile ... Choose Blind or Through All." A cut with no piece at the start fails the same way. (3) Faces the clip takes from the part are renamed `cap/end` (`#k` by position when there are several) so a separate boss body never shares face names with the part; in Direction 2 they are `cap/start`. (4) Without Up to Next or Up to Body directions the sweep is built exactly as before, so old files give the same shapes and names. (5) Draft is refused with these ends (the draft needs an end given by a depth).
Status: Default
Reason: Clipping one prism with booleans handles any number of profile regions and any part shape in two kernel calls, and keeps the old path untouched.

D461: Extrude Through All Both and Up to Body (T16 item 1). (1) Through All Both is Through All forward and back at once. For a boss a side with no body in it reaches 0 mm, and the feature fails only when both sides find nothing. `end_condition2` and draft are refused with it, and the panel hides Direction 2. (2) Up to Body stores the pick in `refs.end` or `refs.end2` as a face reference to any face of the body (FDEF_SPEC 5.3.10 item 2), resolved with `bodies.body_of_ref`. (3) Boss: as Up to Next but clipped against the picked body only, so it runs through other bodies on the way and ends on the picked one. A boss that does not fully meet the body fails with a message that names the cause. (4) Cut: a depth from the start to the far side of the picked body along the direction ("through it"), like Through All for a boss (D142); a body behind the start is an error.
Status: Default
Reason: T16 asks for a boss that runs fully into the body and a cut through it; a depth to the far side is the simplest exact rule for the cut.

D462: Revolve end condition keys (T16 item 2). (1) `direction` stays the main key and is always written: `"mid_plane"`, `"two_directions"` when Direction 2 is on, else `"one_direction"`. (2) `end_condition` is written only for Through All, Up to Vertex, Up to Face and Offset from Face; `end_condition2` only for a Direction 2 that is not Blind. So a revolve edited with Blind or Mid Plane saves exactly as before, and old files open, rebuild and save unchanged. (3) Picks use `refs.end_ref` and `refs.end_ref2` as T16 names them. (4) Direction 2 Offset from Face needs its own angle: `end_offset2`, by the same rule as Extrude's `end_offset2` (T16 lists `end_offset` only). (5) With Through All and the Up to ends the stored `angle` is kept but not used, as Extrude keeps `depth`. (6) The new keys are optional additions within schema 2 (FDEF_SPEC 14 item 4); no schema change.
Status: Default
Reason: Keeping `direction` as the source of truth for the old choices is the only way old files save byte for byte the same.

D463: Revolve Up to Face and Offset from Face geometry (T16 item 2). (1) The end must be a flat face or a plane; a curved face is an error that suggests a flat face, Up to Vertex or Blind. (2) A plane that holds the axis gives an end angle. For a face the half of the plane the face lies on (its centre) is used; for a plane feature the half reached first. (3) Any other plane is reached by turning the profile 2 pi less 0.01 radians and cutting off everything beyond the plane; the piece that touches the profile is kept. When nothing is cut off the face cannot be reached, and the error suggests Up to Vertex or Blind. A picked face counts as its whole plane. (4) Offset from Face turns the face back about the axis, toward the start, by the offset angle; a negative offset is an error. (5) Each direction is built on its own when either one ends on such a plane; with angles only the old single sweep is used. (6) Two directions that add up to more than a full turn are an error.
Status: Default
Reason: An axis plane is the common case and gives an exact angle; the cut off sweep covers the "crossed by the turning profile" case of T16 with two kernel calls.

D464: Revolve Up to Vertex (T16 item 2). The end angle is the turn about the axis (the way the direction goes) from the profile centre's half plane to the half plane through the picked vertex or sketch point. A point on the axis, or one in the sketch's own half plane (a zero turn), is an error with a fix to try.
Status: Default
Reason: The plane of the profile passes through the vertex exactly at that angle, which is what T16 item 2 asks.

D465: Drag arrows for the new ends (T16 item 3). Through All, Through All Both, Up to Next, Up to Vertex, Up to Face and Up to Body directions have no arrow. Offset from Face gets an arrow for `end_offset` or `end_offset2`: on Extrude it starts where the line from the profile centre along the direction meets the face and points back toward the start (away from it with Reverse offset); on Revolve it is a curved arrow at the profile centre turned to the face, turning back toward the start. A face the line misses gives no arrow.
Status: Default
Reason: The arrow sits on the face the offset is measured from, and grows the way the offset moves the end.

D466: Hole Tool Up to Next and Up to Vertex (T16 item 4). (1) Up to Next: each hole goes along its axis to where the axis first comes out of the material (the first hit whose segment before it is inside a solid). A hole with no such point fails and suggests Blind or Through All. (2) Up to Vertex: each hole stops at the level of the picked point along its own axis. The pick is `refs.up_to_vertex`, a list with one vertex reference or sketch point; `refs.up_to` stays the Up to Face face, because the hole form keeps one pick list per ref key. A point not below the start is an error. (3) List order: Blind, Through All, Up to Next, Up to Vertex, Up to Face.
Status: Default
Reason: The axis test is exact and per hole, so holes on stepped parts each stop at their own next face.

D467: Panel lists for the new ends (T16 items 1 and 2). (1) Extrude Direction 1 follows the T16 order; Through All, Through All Both, Up to Next and Up to Body are offered for cuts and for bosses once a body exists (as Through All since T5.1.3), or when already stored. Mid Plane moves to the end of the list. (2) Through All Both hides Direction 2; Revolve Through All hides the angle and Direction 2. (3) The Revolve end pick and offset reuse the Extrude end controls with `refs.end_ref` and an angle offset, without draft and without Reverse offset or Translate surface. (4) Changes stay inside the end condition fields so the in view value labels work (cloud/round8p) merges cleanly.
Status: Default
Reason: One set of end controls keeps picks, messages and tests the same for both tools.

D468: Code export and the T16 ends. A Revolve with Through All exports as a 360 degree revolve; other Revolve end conditions export as a "Not exported" comment, as Extrude's picked ends already do. No new background kernel work was added: every new end runs inside the feature's build in the rebuild job (D400).
Status: Default
Reason: The export must never write a wrong angle for an end it cannot express.

D480: Text dialog field names (round 8r, type check cleanup). The sketch Text dialog stored its font, X and Y fields as `self.font`, `self.x` and `self.y`. These replaced `QWidget.font()`, `x()` and `y()` on the dialog, so any Qt or FDCAD code that asked the dialog for its font or position got a field widget and would fail. This was a real bug risk. The fields are now `font_box`, `x_box` and `y_box`, like the existing `height_box` and `width_box`. Test: `test_dialog_fields_do_not_hide_widget_methods` (fails before the fix).
Status: Default
Reason: Widget attributes must never share a name with a Qt method.

D481: Hole Tool form visibility loop (round 8r). `HoleForm.update_visibility` reused the name `widget` (a row widget from the loop just above) for the attribute names "table", "remove_point" and "hint". Each loop assigns the name before using it, so behaviour was right; only the type was mixed. The loop variable is now `attr`. Test: `test_own_position_widgets_follow_the_sketch_choice` checks the table, Remove Point and hint show for own positions and hide for an existing sketch.
Status: Default
Reason: One name per type keeps the loop readable and type checked.

D482: Spec form choice rows (round 8r). `SpecForm._make` reused `value` (a float in the number branch) and `label` (the row label) as the loop names for each choice's value and label text. The branches never run together and `label` is set again before the row is added, so behaviour was right. The loop names are now `choice_value` and `choice_label`, and the row label is `row_label`. Test: `test_spec_form_choices_and_row_labels` checks each choice box lists its choices and each row shows its field label.
Status: Default
Reason: Same as D481.

D483: Snap popup settings (round 8r). `SnapOptions._set` wrote `replace(options, **{key: on})`. Any key was accepted, so a wrong key such as `over_define` would store a bool where an `OverDefine` value is expected and break the over define prompt later. Only the three snap keys are passed today, so no wrong value was ever stored. The new `with_snap` sets `snapping`, `model_snaps` or `auto_relations` by name and raises `ValueError` for any other key. Test: `test_snap_popup_only_sets_the_three_switches`.
Status: Default
Reason: A bad key now fails at once instead of storing a value of the wrong type.

D484: Sketch mode job list (round 8r). `SketchMode._jobs` was typed as a list of `_OutlineJob`, but the model snap job (`_ModelJob`) is kept in it too. The list only keeps running jobs alive and is trimmed to the last four; nothing reads outline only attributes from it, so behaviour was right. It is now typed as a list of `QRunnable`. Test: `test_sketch_mode_keeps_outline_and_model_jobs` checks both kinds are kept when a sketch opens.
Status: Default
Reason: The type now says what the list holds.

D485: Pick list reorder (round 8r, found by the cleanup). `PickList.move(step)` in the property panel replaced `QWidget.move`, so `move(QPoint)` on a pick list failed. This was a real bug risk like D480. The reorder step is now `move_item(step)`; the up and down buttons call it. Test: `test_pick_list_keeps_widget_move` (fails before the fix).
Status: Default
Reason: Same as D480.

D486: Other type fixes (round 8r). No change in behaviour, UI text or file formats. (1) `MainWindow` declares the attributes the install modules add (`import_flow`, `curvature_graph`, `print_orientation`, `build_volume`, `overhang_analysis`, `wall_thickness`, `print_estimate`, `geometry_check`) as class annotations with no value, imported for type checking only. They are still set by `imports.py` and `print_tools`, so `getattr` and `hasattr` checks work as before and startup loads nothing new. `body_display` and `PropertyPanel.body_form` get their real types. (2) None checks where Qt can return None (`parentWidget`, `child`, `widget`) and where `window.panel` or `sketch_mode` can be None. In the app these values are never None at those points; before, a None would have raised, now the step is skipped. (3) `view_commands` loops test `isinstance(tab, DocumentTab)` instead of `hasattr`; only `DocumentTab` has those attributes. (4) Lambdas mypy could not type (`_by`, `_about`, node editor and face menu commands) became small functions or `functools.partial`. (5) Two `type: ignore` comments mypy reported as unused were removed and one in the samples became an `isinstance` check. (6) The roll previous step accepts a stored id or None, the two values `_rollback` stores. Note: cached `uv run mypy` runs showed 105 errors before the cleanup, a run without the cache 88; both are zero now.
Status: Default
Reason: Real annotations and checks over `type: ignore`, as the round brief asks.

D438: Scope opened after Phase 7 (owner approval 2026-10-30, changes D48). With every PLAN phase built, the owner approved four work streams: (1) a bug hunt across the whole app (PLAN Phase 6 "fix all bugs labelled for v1.0"); (2) the items the specs mark [Later] in docs/TOOL_SPEC.md and docs/PHASE2_SPEC.md to docs/PHASE5_SPEC.md, including the sheet metal tools of PHASE5_SPEC P5.6; (3) the three items in IDEAS.md; (4) release preparation for v1.0. Where a [Later] item names a tool without describing its behaviour, the implementer designs the behaviour from general engineering practice and FDCAD's existing tools, records it in DECISIONS, and never looks anything up (CLAUDE.md 10). Each stream is built by a cloud session with its own DECISIONS number block; release preparation runs last.
Status: Locked
Reason: owner request "give the next phases to cloud" and choice of all four streams.

D510: Round 9t scope: deferred tool options and ideas 1 to 3 (D438 streams 2 and 3, sheet metal excluded). (1) Already built by earlier rounds and only marked done in the specs: Extrude Up to Next, Up to Vertex, Up to Face, Offset from Face, Up to Body and Draft (TOOL_SPEC T5.1.3: D210, D217, D460, D461), extrude Thin Feature (T5.1.7: D211), Revolve Up to Vertex, Up to Face and Offset from Face (T6.1.5: D462 to D464). (2) Curve driven pattern (PHASE3_SPEC P3.2 item 6) is covered by Array along curve (D292), as the spec itself says; no second command is added, the tag is replaced by this decision. (3) Not built because they need surface bodies, which are not in PLAN.md: the Delete option of Delete Face (PHASE3_SPEC P3.1.2, stays greyed with its tooltip). Sheet metal (PHASE5_SPEC) belongs to another session. (4) Every other [Later] item is designed from general engineering practice and FDCAD's existing tools, never from outside material (CLAUDE.md 10), and recorded in D511 to D528 before it is built; items found too large are listed as left out in D529. (5) Order of work, by value to a 3D printing user: ideas 1 to 3, Hole Tool slots, revolve Thin Feature, sketch shapes and dimensions, fillet and chamfer options, draft options, extrude drag interactions, reference plane options, then the rest. (6) The work ran as parallel groups on separate worktrees, each writing its design note under `docs/plans/round9t/` before code; the notes were then copied into this file.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner approved every [Later] item (D438); marking built items avoids duplicate work, and surface bodies are a scope change only the owner can make.

D511: 3 point rectangles and parallelogram (TOOL_SPEC T2.3 item 4). (1) Three new sketch tools, each a command in the Sketch tab rectangle dropdown with Corner Rectangle and Center Rectangle: 3 Point Corner Rectangle (`sketch.three_point_corner_rectangle`), 3 Point Center Rectangle (`sketch.three_point_center_rectangle`) and Parallelogram (`sketch.parallelogram`). No default keys. (2) 3 Point Corner Rectangle: click the first corner, click the second corner (this sets the first side's length and angle, at any angle), then the third click sets the other side: the third corner is the cursor moved square onto the line through the second corner, so only its distance from the first side counts. The four lines get Perpendicular between the first two sides and Parallel on each pair of opposite sides, never Horizontal or Vertical, so the rectangle can turn. (3) 3 Point Center Rectangle: click the centre, click the midpoint of one side (this sets half the width and the angle), then the third click sets half the height (its distance from the line through the centre and that midpoint). Like Center Rectangle it gets two construction diagonals that meet in a construction centre point (Midpoint of both), plus Perpendicular between two adjacent sides; the diagonals already make opposite sides parallel. When the second click lands on an existing point, that point gets Midpoint to the side through it. (4) Parallelogram: click corner 1, corner 2, then the third click is corner 3 anywhere (the adjacent side at any angle); corner 4 completes it. Only Parallel on opposite sides. (5) Shift while placing the third point makes the two 3 point rectangles a square (both sides the length of the first) and adds Equal between two adjacent sides, as D159. (6) Corners snap and take the snap's relations as the other rectangles do; a third corner moved off its snap by the square rule is placed free. Click drag (D155) works: a press and drag gives the second point, a click the third. (7) Typed sizes (D443): after the first click a typed number sets the width (the first side's full length; for the centre tool the box asks for the full width and the side midpoint goes half of it from the centre); after the second click a typed number sets the height (the second side's length: square distance for the rectangles, along the cursor direction for the parallelogram). Each locked size adds a Distance dimension to the first or second side in the same undo step. (8) The shape values group (D157) shows Width and Height of the first two sides for all three tools, typed through the solver. (9) A shape whose three points are in a line, or with a zero side, is not made. (10) Icons are drawn in the house style. Nothing is stored in a new file key: the shapes are plain lines and relations.
Status: Default
Reason: These are the usual three point inputs; Perpendicular and Parallel keep a turned rectangle a rectangle without tying it to the sketch axes.

D512: Perimeter circle (TOOL_SPEC T2.4 item 2). (1) A new tool Perimeter Circle (`sketch.perimeter_circle`) in the Circle dropdown with Circle. Click three points on the circle. After one click a line follows the cursor; after two the circle through both clicks and the cursor follows it. (2) The third click makes a normal circle (centre point and radius) through the three points. Three points in a line give no circle: the clicks are dropped and the status bar says "The three points are in a line, so no circle goes through them. Click a point off the line." (3) Snaps: a click on an existing point (end point, centre, origin) puts that point on the circle (Coincident between the point and the circle). A click that snapped to anything else with relations (a point on a curve, a midpoint, an intersection, a part edge or vertex) places a construction point there with the snap's relations and puts it on the circle. A free click adds nothing. With automatic relations off no snap relation is added. (4) No typed size: the circle has no single size to type while its three points are picked.
Status: Default
Reason: A circle stored as centre and radius works with every existing tool, dimension and file; the snap relations keep the circle through what it was drawn through.

D513: On screen value input while drawing (TOOL_SPEC T11 item 6). (1) A new switch on Preferences > Sketch, "On screen value input while drawing", off by default, stored as `sketch/value_input` with the other sketch switches (QSettings, not in `.fdef`). (2) When on, as soon as a tool that takes typed sizes (D443: Line, Centerline, Corner and Center Rectangle, Circle, Centerpoint Arc, straight slots; and the D511 tools) is ready for a size, the D443 value box opens at the cursor by itself, empty, without a digit typed first. A line chain opens it again for each segment; a rectangle asks for the height after the width. (3) The box never blocks drawing: while it is empty it follows the cursor, and a click in the sketch closes it without locking a size and places the point as usual. Enter in the empty box just closes it. Once the user types into it, it works exactly as D443: Enter locks, a click applies the typed value as before, Escape closes it. The box has keyboard focus while open, so letter shortcuts wait until it is closed. Tools with value labels (Polygon, patterns and so on) keep their labels and do not open the box by itself. (4) Everything else is the D443 machinery (typed_size and the value box); nothing new is saved in files.
Status: Default
Reason: Reusing the D443 box keeps one way to type sizes; an empty box that gives way to clicks keeps mouse drawing unchanged.

D514: Dynamic mirror and spline curvature combs (PHASE2_SPEC P2.8 items 4 and 10). (1) Dynamic Mirror (`sketch.dynamic_mirror`) is a checkable command in the Sketch tab Mirror dropdown. Turning it on with one sketch line or centerline selected uses that line as the mirror line; otherwise the status bar asks "Dynamic mirror: click a line or centerline to mirror about. Escape cancels." and the next click on a line picks it (Escape cancels and turns it off). With no sketch open the command stays off and the status bar says to open a sketch first. (2) While it is on, each shape a drawing tool makes is mirrored about the line at once with the core mirror operation (`core/sketch/ops/mirror.py`): the copies get Symmetric relations to the originals, in the same undo step as the shape. Points, lines, circles and arcs are mirrored, each end point with its own Symmetric relation, so the copy is fully set by the original and adds no degrees of freedom; splines and ellipses are not (the core mirror does not handle them) and the status bar says "Dynamic mirror skips splines and ellipses. Use Mirror for other shapes." Fixed reference copies of part geometry are not mirrored. A pick tool (Trim, Offset, patterns and so on) is not mirrored: only shapes made by the drawing tools' clicks are. The mirror line is kept on the open sketch (`SketchEdit.mirror_axis`). (3) It stays on until the command is used again, the mirror line is deleted, or the sketch closes. The sketch status bar adds "Dynamic mirror on." while it is on. Nothing is saved in files. (4) Show curvature: a "Show curvature" tick box in the sketch panel, shown while the Spline tool is active or a spline is selected, and the matching View > Hide or Show item "Curvature Combs" (`view.curvature_combs`). When on, every spline in the sketch canvas draws its curvature comb: at 60 samples per spline the curve normal scaled by the curvature, with the tips joined. The scale makes the longest tooth a fixed share (one fifth) of the spline's size. The samples, tangents and curvature are computed with numpy from the Bezier pieces (`core/sketch/freeform.curvature_comb`). (5) The combs are view state only (not saved), kept for the session like the relation tags.
Status: Default
Reason: Mirroring each new shape with the existing mirror operation gives the same relations as the Mirror tool; combs as view state need no file change.

D515: Arc length dimension (TOOL_SPEC T4.1, "an arc, then its two end points"). (1) In Smart Dimension, an arc and both of its end points, picked in any order (arc first, end points first, or an end point, the arc and the other end point), give an arc length dimension; the next click places it, as for other dimensions. A third pick is taken only when it completes such a set, so two end points alone still give a distance as before. (2) It is stored as a new sketch dimension type `arc_length` whose `entities` holds only the arc id: the end points are the arc's own, so naming them again adds nothing and the dimension can never disagree with them. (3) Solver: the planegcs arc length constraint on the arc with a fixed value; measure: radius times the counter clockwise sweep (`solver.arc_length`). Driving and reference both work; a driving one that conflicts goes through the same over define prompt or setting as other dimensions. Construction arcs take it too. (4) Display: the dimension line is an arc concentric with the measured arc, 24 pixels outside it when placed automatically or through the dragged text, with extension lines from the arc's end points; the value is plain (no prefix). The value box, the cursor preview, label drag (`label` offset from the point halfway along the arc), the Dimension panel ("Arc Length") and equations names (`d4@Sketch 1`) work as for every other dimension. (5) File: `arc_length` is an optional new value in the existing list of dimension types (FDEF_SPEC 6 item 5), an addition to schema 1; files without it open and save unchanged. Unknown dimension types are read and written back unchanged by every FDCAD version, and the solver stops at them with "Unknown dimension type", so an older FDCAD shows a sketch error on such a sketch but loses nothing on save.
Status: Default
Reason: Holding only the arc keeps the file small and needs no new key, and the solver already has an exact arc length constraint.

D516: Shift click picks Nearest or Farthest (TOOL_SPEC T4.3 item 3). (1) In Smart Dimension, a circle or arc clicked with Shift held is measured to its near or far side instead of its centre. The side is read from the click when the dimension is placed: Nearest when the click point is closer to the other picked item than the circle's centre is, Farthest otherwise. The other item is measured square to it for a line, or from its centre for another circle or arc. (2) The circle may be picked first or second; the click point is kept with the pick. Two Shift clicked circles each decide against the other's centre. The preview that follows the cursor already shows the chosen side. (3) As T4.3.2 and D123 say, there is no side with a point, so Shift does nothing there; it also does nothing when two circles are placed as a horizontal or vertical distance, which always run between centres. (4) Without Shift nothing changes: the centre is used, and the Dimension panel's Measure to choice still changes the side afterwards. The side is stored in the existing `measure_to` key (no new key).
Status: Default
Reason: Comparing the click with the centre against the other item gives the side the user clicked on without any extra prompt.

D517: Convert curve features into a sketch (IDEAS.md item 2, D438, D292 item 5). (1) Convert Entities also takes curve features: every feature whose result carries a curve (contour curves, projected curves, composite curves, helices and spirals, and the other curve features of PHASE3_SPEC P3.6 and P3.7). While the tool is active, clicking a curve feature in the feature tree converts it, and the curve features are drawn as faint dotted reference curves in the sketch view, where hovering one highlights the whole feature and a click converts it (a part outline edge under the cursor comes first). Only curve features above the sketch in the tree and not suppressed are offered (for a new sketch, all of them), so a sketch never copies a later feature. (2) When the sketch opens, every edge of those curves is projected onto the sketch plane along the sketch normal in a background job (CLAUDE.md rule 2; `core/sketch/curve_projection.py`). A straight edge becomes a line; a round edge whose axis is along the sketch normal becomes an arc or a full circle; an edge whose projection is straight (a circle seen edge on, worked out exactly from the circle) becomes a line; every other edge becomes a spline (the D278 entity) through 8 to 64 points spread evenly along its parameter, as many as the kernel needs to keep within 0.01 mm, with smooth default handles (a closed curve also stays smooth where it closes). Neighbouring pieces share exact end coordinates, so the copy of a closed loop is a closed contour that makes a profile. (3) Edges that project to a point or to less than 0.0001 mm are skipped, and the status bar says so: "Converted Contour 1: 6 curves. 6 edges were skipped because they project to a point." A piece that already has a fixed curve on it is not copied again, so contour loops stacked on top of each other (seen along the contour direction) are copied once; a curve already fully in the sketch gives "Contour 1 is already in the sketch.", and a tree pick of another feature says it is not a curve feature above this sketch. (4) The copies are fixed, like converted part edges (D275), and For construction makes construction curves. They are not linked to the curve feature: the existing link (FDEF_SPEC 6 item 9, D250) names a part edge or corner of the solid body and is checked against the body's projected edges in the sketch rebuild; curve features are not part of the body, and splines have no link target, so a link would need a new source kind, a new matcher and a new file key. A copy that never moves silently is the safe default (rule 12). (5) The whole conversion of one feature is one sketch undo step. No file key is added. The pure part (pieces, adding them to the sketch, the duplicate check) is `core/sketch/curve_convert.py`, with no kernel import so the sketch tools stay light.
Status: Default
Reason: Reusing Convert Entities, the fixed copy rule and the spline entity turns contour curves into sketch geometry with no new command and no file change.

D518: Face fillet and full round fillet (PHASE2_SPEC P2.4 item 1). (1) Two new `fillet_type` values, `"face"` and `"full_round"`. Old files keep `"constant"` and `"variable"` and open and save unchanged. (2) Face fillet: two face sets in `refs.faces1` and `refs.faces2` and the `radius`. Every edge shared by a face of set 1 and a face of set 2 is rounded with the radius by the same kernel fillet as a constant fillet, so new faces are named `fillet/<edge name>` and failing edges are pinpointed (D213 item 4) with the "Reduce the radius" fix only ("Fillet the rest" is not offered, as the edges are not picks). Sets that share no edge fail with "Fillet 3: the two face sets do not meet at an edge. Pick faces that touch each other." (3) Full round: three face sets, `refs.faces1` (side 1), `refs.centre` (centre faces) and `refs.faces2` (side 2). Each set must be flat faces on one plane, and the two side planes must be parallel and apart. The centre faces are replaced by a round of radius half the distance between the sides, tangent to both sides and touching the centre plane (the centre face may slope across the rib). It is built exactly: a prism whose cross section is the region between the two side planes above the round's arc is cut away. The prism runs along the round's axis (the side normal crossed with the centre normal) over the length of the centre faces. The round face is named `full_round/<first centre face name>`. The radius is computed, so the panel hides the radius; the stored `radius` is written as before but not used. A rib of width w and length L loses exactly L (w w / 2 less pi w w / 8). (4) Full round errors, each with what to do: a set is empty; a set is not flat or not on one plane; the sides are not parallel ("a full round needs two parallel side faces") or on one plane; the centre face is parallel to the sides; the centre faces do not lie between the sides; a side ends before the round's axis ("the first side is shorter than half the width (2 mm), so the round does not fit"); the cut does not give one valid body. (5) Panel: a Face Sets group with one pick list per set and a "Pick into" list; after each pick the next set is chosen, so one click per set is enough, and clicking a list makes it the target. Face sets are named Face Set 1 and 2, or Side Face Set 1, Centre Face Set and Side Face Set 2 for the full round. Items to Fillet is hidden for these types, and the whole Fillet Parameters group for the full round. (6) Left out: face sets that do not meet (for example two walls with a gap). The kernel's fillet maker only rounds existing edges, and a rolling ball blend between faces that do not touch needs a surface builder the kernel does not offer reliably.
Status: Default
Reason: Rounding the shared edges reuses the tested fillet path, and the prism cut gives an exact, valid single solid for the full round.

D519: Fillet assistant, partial edges, cross sections and setback (P2.4 items 1, 3 and 6). (1) Fillet assistant: in Items to Fillet, a scope list (Whole Part or an earlier solid feature) and two buttons, Add Convex Edges and Add Concave Edges. Each click adds one item to the list ("Concave edges of the part", "Convex edges of Extrude 2"), stored in `refs.auto_edges` as `{"convexity": "convex"}` or `{"convexity": "concave", "feature": "f6"}`. The edges are found when the feature rebuilds with the kernel's edge analysis (smooth edges and edges of one face are skipped), so the item follows later changes to the part and no kernel work runs on the UI thread. A scope feature with no faces left fails naming it. Works with Constant Size and Variable Size (these edges use the main radius). (2) Partial edges (Constant Size only): a checkable Partial Edges group with Distance or Percent, a start and an end, and Flip. Keys: `partial` (`"distance"` or `"percent"`), `start_distance` and `end_distance` (lengths) or `start_percent` and `end_percent` (numbers), and `partial_flip`. The range is measured along each item edge from its first end (the other end with Flip). The kernel cannot round part of an edge (a radius law may not reach zero), so each edge is done in steps: the part is split by the planes square to the edge at the start and the end, the piece of the edge in the middle piece is rounded, and the pieces are fused and their split faces merged again. The round ends square at the start and end planes. Faces that were only split get their names back; the new face is `fillet/<edge name>`. A range that is empty, reversed or longer than the edge fails with "the partial range on edge X must start before it ends and stay on the edge (0 to 50 mm long)". A kernel failure names the edge and suggests a smaller radius or moving the ends away from corners. Partial edges need a part with one body. The fillet is done edge by edge, so several partial edges cost several kernel steps. (3) Left out: start and end "by reference" (a picked point or plane), because distance and percent cover the common cases and a reference needs its own pick list. (4) Cross sections, left out: the kernel's fillet maker offers three section shapes (rational, quasi angular and polynomial), but all three are ways to build a circular arc. None makes a conic or a curvature continuous section. (5) Setback at a corner vertex, left out: the kernel builds corner blends itself and has no setting for how far they are set back.
Status: Default
Reason: Stored convexity items keep the rounding in step with the part, and splitting the part gives exact partial rounds with the kernel's own fillet.

D520: Offset face chamfer and face to face chamfer (P2.5 item 1). (1) Two new `chamfer_type` values, `"offset_face"` and `"face_face"`. (2) Offset face: picked edges and faces as for Distance Distance, `method` symmetric or asymmetric, `distance` and `distance2`, and `flip`. Each distance is an offset measured square to a face: `distance` from the reference face (D216 item 2), `distance2` from the other face. The chamfer runs along the lines where each face, moved inward by its offset, meets the other face. With phi the angle between the faces across the chamfered corner (pi less the angle between the outward normals), the distance along the reference face is `distance2 / sin(phi)` and along the other face `distance / sin(phi)`; these feed the kernel's two distance chamfer. At 90 degrees this equals Distance Distance with the two distances on swapped faces. The angle must be the same along the whole edge (checked at both ends and the middle), so straight edges between flat faces and round edges of holes and bosses work; others fail with "the angle between the faces changes along edge X. Use Distance Distance for this edge." Faces that meet smoothly fail too. (3) Face to face: two face sets, `refs.faces1` and `refs.faces2`; the edges where they meet are chamfered. `method`: `"symmetric"` (`distance` along both faces), `"asymmetric"` (`distance` along the set 1 face, `distance2` along the set 2 face) or `"width"`, with the new optional `width` length: the width of the chamfer face, so the distance along each face is `width / (2 sin(phi / 2))`. The `distance` key is still written with Width (hidden in the panel) so files keep the required key. Flip is hidden (set 1 decides). Sets that share no edge fail like the face fillet. Failing edges are pinpointed with the "Reduce the distance" or "Reduce the width" fix ("Chamfer the rest" is not offered). (4) The method list shows Width only for Face to Face (the item is disabled for other types and the choice falls back to Symmetric). New faces are named `chamfer/<edge name>` as before. (5) Left out: face sets that do not meet, for the reason in D518 item 6.
Status: Default
Reason: Turning the offsets and the width into along face distances reuses the kernel's exact two distance chamfer.

D521: Parting line draft and step draft (PHASE2_SPEC P2.7 item 4). (1) Draft gets an optional `draft_type`: `"neutral_plane"` (default, not written), `"parting_line"` or `"step"`. Parting line and step drafts use `refs.neutral` as the direction of pull (a plane or a flat face, Reverse flips it, as for the neutral plane method) and a new `refs.parting_lines` (edge references). `refs.faces` and `propagation` are not used by them and are not written. (2) Faces to draft are found from the edges: every face next to a parting edge is on the pull side of the edge (its centre lies further along the pull) or on the other side. Faces lying in the parting plane (square to the pull) are skipped. By default the faces on the pull side are drafted; `other_side` (optional boolean) drafts the faces on the other side instead; `both_sides` (optional boolean) drafts both, the other side by `angle2` (optional angle, the main angle when it is not written). Each side tilts away from the parting line: pull side faces lean in going along the pull, other side faces lean in going against it, so the parting line stays the widest section and stays where it is. (3) Every parting edge must lie in a plane square to the pull (straight or curved edges, checked at several points to 0.001 mm); an edge that does not is an error naming it. Parting line draft needs all edges in one such plane; edges at several heights fail with a message that points to Step Draft. (4) Method (`core/features/draft_parting.py`): the kernel's draft always carries a tilt on to faces joined smoothly, so a face split by a split line would drag its other half with it. The part is therefore cut by the parting plane into the piece on each side (a common with a box far larger than the part), the faces of each piece are drafted about the parting plane, the pieces are joined again and the faces the cut divided are merged back: only across edges in the parting plane whose two faces carry the name of one face; every other edge and vertex is kept, so the part's own split faces never merge. When the parting plane is the top or bottom of the part, the empty piece is skipped. Inside a piece the kernel still carries the tilt on to faces joined smoothly on the same side (the rest of a side face above a lower split line). When a drafted piece comes back slightly out of tolerance (split faces next to a tilted face), the kernel's shape fixer mends it, keeping the face names. Drafted faces keep their names; the feature adds no face roles. (5) Step draft: the parting edges may lie at several heights, each in a plane square to the pull (a stepped parting line). Faces are grouped by the height of their parting edges and each group is drafted about its own plane in turn, from the lowest along the pull; a face next to edges at two heights is an error naming it. The connecting faces between the levels keep their position, so the drafted faces at each level meet them in a step. (6) Errors: no direction of pull, no parting lines, a lost edge (named), a face the kernel cannot tilt (named), and a cut or join that fails ("Use a smaller angle or fewer parting lines"). (7) Panel: Type of Draft at the top (Neutral Plane, Parting Line, Step Draft; remembered for the next draft like the angle). For the two new types the Neutral Plane group is titled Direction of Pull, its button Pick Direction Face, and the Faces to Draft group is replaced by Parting Lines: a list of edges picked in the view, Other side (hidden while Draft both sides is ticked), Draft both sides and Other angle (shown only with Draft both sides, starting at the draft angle). The first flat face clicked while Pick Direction Face is on sets the direction; edges clicked go to the list; other faces are refused with "Pick edges for the parting lines, or a flat face for the direction." Show changed faces moved to the Draft Angle group so it is there for every type. (8) Where parting edges come from: FDCAD merges faces that lie on one surface when features join, so split side faces come from imported parts (STEP); in parts modelled in FDCAD the parting edges are usually where a boss meets a face (a round boss gives a curved parting line and its side becomes a cone) or an outer edge of the part. (9) Left out: parting edges on a slope (not in a plane square to the pull). The kernel's draft tilts a face about one straight line in its neutral plane and makes no new faces, so along a sloped edge the drafted face and the face across the edge no longer meet on the edge; a step face would have to be built by hand for every case, which is not reliable.
Status: Default
Reason: Cutting the part at the parting plane keeps the kernel's own reliable neutral plane draft while stopping it from carrying the tilt across the split line.

D522: Draft analysis and the draft assistant (PHASE2_SPEC P2.7 item 4). (1) Evaluate, Draft Analysis is an on and off overlay like Overhang Analysis (D354): a kernel job after every rebuild, display only, nothing saved. While it is on a small tool window shows Direction of Pull (the planes of the part, Top Plane first by default, or a flat face picked with Use Selected Face), Reverse, Minimum Angle (degrees, default 1) and a legend with the colour and face count of each group. (2) Maths (`fdcad/core/draft_analysis.py`, no Qt): the part is triangulated as for the overhang analysis and every triangle is tested in one numpy pass. A triangle's draft is the angle between its surface and the pull direction, positive when its outward normal leans toward the pull: sin(draft) = n . d. Area shares per face are summed with `numpy.bincount`. (3) A face is Straddle (blue) when at least 2 percent of its area has positive draft and at least 2 percent negative draft of at least the minimum angle; otherwise it takes the group with the largest share of its area: Positive draft (green, at least the minimum angle), Negative draft (red, at least the minimum angle) or Needs draft (yellow, draft smaller than the minimum angle either way). Faces square to the pull count as positive or negative (draft 90 degrees). (4) Draft assistant: the Faces to Draft group (neutral plane method) has Add Faces That Need Draft. It runs the same maths in a kernel job (`assistant_faces` in `core/draft_analysis.py`) on the part before the draft, with the neutral plane's normal as the pull and the draft angle as the minimum, and adds every flat, cylindrical or conical face whose group is Needs draft and that is not already in the list (the kernel can only tilt those kinds). A face square to the pull, such as a flat neutral face, is never in Needs draft. A line under the button says how many faces were added ("Added 3 faces that need draft.", "No other face needs draft from this neutral plane.") or what is missing. It only fills the list: Cancel drops it like any other pick. (5) The command sits in the Evaluate tab's Check group under Geometry Check, with its own icon and no shortcut. The tool window is a Qt tool window like the curvature graph's; the window and the colours go away when the command is turned off.
Status: Default
Reason: One set of maths serves the analysis and the assistant, and the triangle pass is the same fast numpy method the other analyses use.

D523: Thin Feature for Revolve and Revolved Cut (TOOL_SPEC T6.1 item 5). (1) Revolve takes the extrude Thin Feature keys unchanged (D211): `thin_type` (`"one_direction"`, `"mid_plane"`, `"two_direction"`), `thin_thickness`, `thin_thickness2`, `thin_reverse`, `thin_cap` and `thin_cap_thickness`, all optional and written only when Thin Feature is on, so older files save byte for byte the same. (2) The wall is made exactly as for the extrude (`extrude_thin.thin_sketch`): the region between the curves offset to the two sides in the sketch plane, One Direction inside a closed profile and on the offset side of an open one, Reverse swaps the sides, Mid Plane splits the thickness, Two Direction takes the first thickness outside and the second inside. Open profiles (one chain without branches) are allowed only with Thin Feature on. A sketch line used as the axis is left out of the chain. A wall from a single straight line is offset in the sketch plane by the code (the kernel finds no plane for a lone line, so before this both Extrude and Revolve failed with "the open profile could not be offset"); One Direction puts it to the right of the line's direction seen from the sketch normal, Reverse to the left.
