(3) The wall is then turned with the revolve's own angles and end conditions (Blind, Mid Plane, Direction 2, Through All, Up to Vertex, Up to Face, Offset from Face), boss or cut, Merge Result and Cut Outside as before. Selected Regions are not used while Thin Feature is on, as for the extrude. (4) The wall must stay on one side of the axis (it may touch it): otherwise "Revolve 1 failed: the thin wall crosses the axis. Make the wall thinner, put it on the other side with Reverse, or move the profile away from the axis." (5) Face names follow D211: `side/<entity>/outer`, `side/<entity>/inner`, the end walls of an open profile `side/<entity>/start` and `side/<entity>/end`, and the angular ends `cap/start` and `cap/end` as before. A full turn of a thin wall revolves a copy of the profile (`solids.revolve(copy=True)`): only then does the kernel report the faces made by edges square to the axis, which would otherwise be left as `face#k`. Plain revolves keep the old call so old files keep their face names (see d). (6) Cap ends: closed profiles only, and only for a revolve of less than a full turn whose ends are given by angles (Blind, Mid Plane, Direction 2, Up to Vertex, or a face plane that holds the axis). Each end gets a flat lid of the cap thickness: the region inside the wall's outer side (as for the extrude) made into a slab from the end face into the revolve, and clipped to that region turned through the whole angle, so it never pokes out near the axis or past the outer wall. The lids' outer faces join `cap/start` and `cap/end`, their inner faces are `thin_cap/start` and `thin_cap/end`, their other faces `lid_side/...` and `lid_clip/...`. Otherwise "Revolve 1: Cap ends needs a revolve of less than 360 degrees with angle ends. Turn it off." (7) This replaces the last sentence of D211 ("Thin Feature is not offered for revolve, since P2.1 names only the extrude"). (8) The panel shows the Thin Feature group for Revolve and Revolved Cut, the same group the extrude uses (`ThinControls`). (9) The build123d script export writes "Not exported: revolve Thin Feature." for a thin revolve.
Status: Default
Reason: Reusing the extrude wall keeps one set of rules and keys; a lid clipped to the turned region is the closest match to the extrude's Cap ends.

D524: Hole Tool slots (PHASE4_SPEC P4.1 item 2). (1) Simple, Counterbore and Countersink holes get a Slot tick box: optional key `slot` (true, written only when ticked) with `slot_span` (length), `slot_span_mode` (`"overall"`, written only then; centre to centre by default) and `slot_angle` (angle in the face plane from the position sketch's X axis, written only when not zero). The length key is not `slot_length` because the nut slot already uses that name for a different length. A boolean on the three hole types fits the existing layout better than three new types: the standard tables, sizes, fits and type groups stay as they are. (2) Centre to centre: the distance between the two end centres, greater than zero. Overall: end to end over the round ends, greater than the hole diameter; the centre distance is the overall length less the diameter. Errors: "Hole 1: the slot length must be greater than zero. Enter a longer slot." and "Hole 1: the overall slot length must be greater than the hole diameter. Enter a longer slot or measure it centre to centre." (3) Each position point is the slot centre. The slot runs along the position sketch's X axis turned by `slot_angle`, laid flat on the plane square to the hole axis. (4) Shape: the hole's own section (head, counterbore, countersink, wall, flat or drill point bottom, head clearance, far side countersink) is swept straight along the centre line between the two end centres, and each end is the same section turned half a turn, so every level of the hole is a stadium (two half circles joined by straight sides). The pieces are fused and merged into one tool per position, and all positions are still cut in one boolean (D313 item 5). (5) Depths (Through All, Up to Next, Up to Vertex, Up to Face) are found along the axis at the slot centre, as for a round hole at that point. (6) Fit presets and the printer tolerance widen the slot like a round hole: the diameters grow by the fit; the centre distance stays, so an overall length also grows by the fit. (7) Face names: the straight sides are `hole/<p>/<role>/side1` and `side2`, the round ends `hole/<p>/<role>/end1` and `end2` (roles as for round holes: `wall`, `cbore_wall`, `csk`, `far_csk`, `tip`, `head_wall`); flat faces across the slot keep the round hole's names (`hole/<p>/bottom`, `cbore_floor`, `head`). (8) Slots are not offered for tapped holes, heat set inserts, nut traps or nut slots; the core ignores `slot` on those types. Cosmetic and modelled threads do not apply.
Status: Default
Reason: Slots let a printed mount slide to adjust; building them from the round hole's own section keeps every hole option working on slots.

D525: Extrude drag interactions: Alt drag snap and drag a sketch without the panel (TOOL_SPEC T5.2 item 4, T5.4). (1) Alt snap: while an extrude depth arrow (`depth` of Extrude or Extruded Cut with Blind or Mid Plane, and `depth2`) is dragged with Alt held, the 3D view looks under the cursor with its normal detection (the AIS context `MoveTo`, on the UI thread, picking only, no kernel builds) for a vertex or face of the shown part. A vertex wins over a face and gives its point. A flat face parallel to the sketch plane gives its plane, so the depth is exactly its distance; any other face gives the point under the cursor. The new travel is the distance from the arrow's start along its direction to that point; on Mid Plane the total depth is twice it, so the end lands on the point. Behind the start a Direction 1 arrow that flips (D147) flips; other arrows stop at their smallest value. A small marker (a ringed plus in the accent colour) sits on the snapped point and the value beside the arrow gets "to vertex" or "to face". Without Alt, or over nothing, the drag works as before (ruler and free value). The arrows that snap carry a new `PreviewHandle.snaps` flag, set only by Extrude, so the Offset from Face arrow, revolve arrows, move face and every other handle are unchanged. Alt and left click (select the next item) still works: it happens only on a click without a drag on the part, while a press on an arrow starts a handle drag and never selects, so the two never clash. (2) Drag a sketch: with nothing open for editing (no feature panel, sketch or reference panel), a plain left click (no Ctrl, Shift, Alt or Meta) in the 3D view casts the view ray onto the plane of every finished sketch shown there. Hits behind the part point under the cursor (more than 0.01 mm) are left out, so a sketch hidden by the part is not clicked. A worker finds the first hit that lies inside one of that sketch's regions (D193 regions, the cached `SketchOutput.regions()`) and probes the part 0.01 mm on each side of the plane with the solid classifier. Material on one side makes it start as a cut going into the part; material on neither side makes it a boss along the sketch normal (and a boss always goes away from material). The new feature is an ordinary Extrude: Blind, `refs.regions` holding the clicked region, the default name ("Extrude 1" or "Cut 1"), and a first depth of one ruler step (D146) of the region's size. The normal feature preview shows it with its arrow, ruler, flip past the start and Alt snap; dragging sets the depth. After release a small bar near the cursor offers Boss, Cut, OK, Cancel and Edit in Panel. Boss and Cut swap the operation, the name and the direction (into or away from the part). OK (or Enter) adds the feature with the normal undoable Add Feature command and selects it in the tree. Edit in Panel opens the full Extrude panel on the same feature, nothing added until its OK. Escape (in the view or on the bar), Cancel, a click elsewhere, a changed document, opening a panel or sketch, or a tab change drop the arrow and preview without changing the document; the feature id taken for it is given back. Nothing new is stored in files.
Status: Default
Reason: Both reuse the existing drag handles, preview, regions and new feature command, so the result is an ordinary feature and nothing new is saved.

D526: Reference plane Project and Parallel to screen (PHASE2_SPEC P2.10 item 1). (1) Method `project`: first pick a point (vertex, sketch point or reference point), second pick a face (any face; a curved face is the usual case). By default the point goes to the nearest point of the face (shortest distance), and the plane passes through it, normal to the face there, pointing out of the part. With `along_normal` (Along Sketch Normal tick box, only for a sketch point) the point moves along its sketch's normal, either way, to the nearest place where that line meets the face. Errors: "Plane 1: only a sketch point can be projected along the sketch normal. Pick a sketch point or turn off Along Sketch Normal." and "Plane 1: the point does not reach the face along the sketch normal. Turn off Along Sketch Normal or pick another face." A point picked with a face, cylinder or cone face (in either order) is guessed as `project`; a point and a flat face stay Parallel through a point. (2) Method `screen` (Parallel to screen): one pick, a point. The plane passes through it, normal to the view direction, pointing toward the viewer. The direction is taken from the 3D view when the method is chosen and stored as the plain numbers `normal_x`, `normal_y` and `normal_z` (a unit vector, rounded to 12 places), so rebuilds never depend on the camera; core reads only the stored vector. A Use Current View button, shown only for this method, takes the view direction again. Without a stored direction the panel says "Press Use Current View to take the view direction." and the feature error says "Plane 1: the view direction is missing. Press Use Current View to take it." Both methods take `flip_normal`. The keys are optional and written only for these methods, so older files are unchanged (FDEF_SPEC 5.3.20). (3) A sketch point pick now also carries its sketch normal (`Geo.normal`); no other method reads it.
Status: Default
Reason: These were the last two plane constraints in P2.10; storing the captured normal keeps rebuilds stable and keeps the camera out of core.

D527: Keep separate body in the file, and formulas follow a feature rename (IDEAS.md items 1 and 3, approved in D438; changes D76 and D390 item 7). (1) The optional common feature key `keep_separate_body: true` (FDEF_SPEC 5.1 item 9, section 15 item 6) records that the user kept the separate body a feature made. It is written only when true, so it is an optional addition to schema 1: older files open and save byte for byte the same, and older readers keep it as an unknown key (FDEF_SPEC 14 item 4). Fixture `tests/fixtures/schema1/keep_separate_body.fdef` covers it. (2) The fix button "Keep separate body" in the Errors tab now sets the key with one undoable command (`SetKeepSeparateBody`, undo text "Keep Separate Body: <feature>") instead of hiding the warning for the session only. While the key is set the rebuild drops that feature's `separate_body` warning (after the cache, in the rebuild engine), so the Errors tab and the feature tree no longer show it in warning colour. The key is left out of the rebuild cache key, so setting or clearing it rebuilds no feature. (3) The feature's right click menu shows "Warn About Separate Bodies" while the key is set; it clears the key with one undoable command and the warning comes back. (4) Renaming a feature or sketch (tree rename, one undoable `RenameFeature`) also rewrites every formula that names it: quoted names `"<value>@<old name>"` become `"<value>@<new name>"` in feature values, sketch dimensions, global variables, suppression formulas, configuration overrides, design table cells and graph node formulas (value parameters and the Formula node's `formula` setting). Only whole names match: the text after the last `@`, without surrounding spaces, must equal the old name exactly, so renaming "Extrude 1" never touches "Extrude 10", and the id form `"depth@f6"` is left alone. The parser has no unquoted form for these names (`@` and spaces are not name characters), so only quoted names are rewritten; plain values (no `=`) are never touched. Comments are keyed by the value name without the feature name, so they need no change. (5) A formula the tokenizer cannot read (for example a missing closing quote) is left as typed; a new name holding a double quote cannot be quoted, so formulas are then left as typed. (6) The rewrite is pure Python in `core/equations/rename.py` (`rename_rewrite` returns edited copies; the part is not changed). The command stores the old and new copies of only what changed, so undo restores the old name and every rewritten formula, and redo puts them back.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner approved both ideas (D438); an optional key keeps old files unchanged, and rewriting quoted names only touches exact matches.

D528: Split saves bodies to separate files, and Wrap gets the Spline surface method (PHASE3_SPEC P3.4 item 3, PHASE4_SPEC P4.7 item 2). (1) Split: after Cut, each row of the body list can be renamed with a double click; the row text is the file name. A row left as "Body k" saves as "<part> body k" (the part's file name, or "Part" before it is saved). Below the list a format box (FDCAD Part, STEP, STL, 3MF) and a "Save Bodies" button (enabled after Cut) write each ticked body to its own file in a folder the user picks. FDCAD Part writes a new `.fdef` part whose only feature is an Imported STEP body (D290) holding that body, so it opens and can be edited directly; STEP, STL and 3MF use the export writers with default mesh settings. Characters not allowed in file names become `_`, names used twice get " 2", " 3", and files of the same name are replaced. The pieces are made again and written on a worker thread (`core/io/save_bodies.py`); the part is not changed, no undo step is added and nothing is stored in the file (renaming a row does not change the feature either). The result shows under the buttons: "Saved 2 files to <folder>." or the error, which names the body that failed. (2) Wrap: optional key `method: "spline"` (default `"analytical"`, not written; FDEF_SPEC 5.3.31 item 4). The Spline surface method works on any single face and the sketch plane need not touch it: the sketch origin is projected onto the nearest point of the face (on its boundary when that is nearest) to get (u0, v0); the sketch's x and y directions are turned into the face's tangent plane there (lengths kept, the side that keeps the sketch readable) and written in the tangent directions dS/du and dS/dv (least squares). That gives one fixed affine map from sketch coordinates to face parameters, so lengths along the face match the sketch near that point and follow the face's parameters further away; it is exact on flat faces and cylinders. Each sketch curve is made a B-spline in the sketch plane and its poles are moved by the map (exact, also for rational splines), giving curves on the face; holes are kept. Emboss and deboss make the wrapped faces thick along the face normal: a prism on flat faces, the kernel's simple thicken on curved faces with the side picked from where the result's centre lies against the face's outward normal. Scribe splits the faces as before. Reverse is hidden and not used with this method. (3) Messages: a sketch that leaves the face (checked at 24 points along each curve, with periodic faces taken round) or would wrap all the way round a closed face: "Wrap 1: the sketch runs off the face. Move it or make it smaller."; a point where the face has no tangent plane: "Wrap 1: the sketch origin does not project onto the face. Move the sketch."; a sketch plane square to the face: "Wrap 1: the sketch plane is seen edge on from the face. Sketch on a plane that faces it.". (4) The panel's Method box (Analytical, Spline Surface) sits above the face pick. Left out: the optional pull direction for emboss and deboss (as D322).
Status: Default
Reason: Writing pieces through the existing STEP import and export code adds no new file format, and an affine map into the face parameters is exact on planes and cylinders and kernel friendly elsewhere.

D529: Round 9t items left out, and test notes. (1) Left out because the kernel cannot do them reliably: face fillet and face to face chamfer between face sets that do not touch (D518, D520), conic and curvature continuous fillet sections and setback at a corner vertex (D519), parting edges on a slope (D521). (2) Left out as too large for this round: partial edge fillet ends set by a reference (D519; ends by distance and percent are built). (3) Left out by design: a link from converted curve copies back to their curve feature (D517), mirroring splines and ellipses while Dynamic Mirror is on (D514), a typed size for Perimeter Circle (D512), a depth field on the drag a sketch bar and revolve drags without the panel (D525), the Wrap pull direction (D322, D528), storing Split file names (D528), slot drag handles (D524). (4) Not built because they need surface bodies: the Delete option of Delete Face (D510). (5) Found and left for the bug hunt (outside this round's tools): model snapping draws helix shaped part edges as a straight chord because `core/sketch/projection.py` samples them with only their end points; a plain full turn Revolve leaves the faces made by profile edges square to the axis unnamed (`<fid>/face#k`), and fixing it renames faces in old files. (6) Fixed on the way: a Thin Feature wall from a single straight line failed in Extrude ("the open profile could not be offset"); test `test_thin_single_straight_line`. (7) Timing budget tests (`test_startup_and_empty_part_memory`, the mesh measure and generated part rebuild budgets) failed in the cloud container while seven groups ran tests at once; the memory test also fails on phase1 in this container (723 MB against 400 MB), so it is an environment limit and not a regression.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for every [Later] item that fits, with the rest listed and explained.

D490: App sweep for the Phase 6 bug hunt (round 9s, D438 stream 1). `tests/ui/test_app_sweep.py` drives the main window on the offscreen platform: every command id with no selection, a face, an edge, a vertex, a sketch and a body; every view and tree right click menu item; each sketch command on a fresh sketch; every preference page; Save As each type and reopen; every command tab button and dropdown entry. Modal dialogs are replaced (`tests/ui/sweep_support.py`): they cancel or accept with their defaults, so no step waits for a person. Each step must not raise, must finish within 30 s, and Undo then Redo must give back the same `.fdef` text. The text comparison leaves out `next_id`: feature ids are never reused, so opening a panel or undoing an Add may move the counter on without an undo step. Reusing ids after Undo could tie old view state (dismissed warnings, picks) to a new feature, so this is kept on purpose. The quick tests (one sample part, OK with no selection, plus menus, sketch tools, preferences, files and tabs) run by default in about 75 s; the full sweep over every sample and graph sample with every selection kind, Cancel and OK is marked slow. Failures and fixes are logged in `docs/BUG_HUNT.md`.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for the bug hunt without a human tester; a repeatable sweep keeps the found bugs fixed.

D491: Startup memory budget on Linux (round 9s). Peak resident memory counts mapped library files. On Linux the kernel library alone maps about 245 MB of them, so the startup budget test failed at 449 MB though the app itself allocates about 160 MB. Linux is not a target platform (CLAUDE.md 9), so on Linux the test checks the memory the app allocates (`sysinfo.private_memory`, from `RssAnon`) against the same 400 MB. macOS and Windows keep the peak resident check.
Status: Default
Reason: The budget must catch app growth, not differences in how one non target platform maps a library.

D492: Cancel on the first sheet values (bug hunt B2). Starting Base Flange in a part with no Sheet Metal folder adds the folder and opens its panel first (D330). Cancel there used to keep the folder and still open the Base Flange panel. The property panel now records whether the last edit closed with OK (`PropertyPanel.accepted`); on Cancel the flow undoes the folder it added and stops. OK behaves as before.
Status: Default
Reason: Cancel must leave the part as it was.

D493: Plane picks and tree refreshes (bug hunt B3). While a plane pick is armed (Edit Sketch Plane, a new sketch or a feature that waits for a plane), the pick listens to the tree's current row. A tree refresh (after any rebuild, roll back or suppress) clears and refills the rows, and each row change reached the pick: the part row raised KeyError, and the restored row could replace the user's chosen plane. Doing so during the clear could also start a sketch while the rows were being deleted, which crashed the process in the sweep. The pick now ignores row changes while `FeatureTree.filling` is true and ignores rows that are not features.
Status: Default
Reason: Only the user's own clicks choose a plane.

D494: Next steps in error messages (bug hunt B5, CLAUDE.md 8.4). The audit found no dashes in user text, but about 280 messages that say what failed without saying what to do. The most visible ones now end with a next step: export and flat export failures, the five print checks, preview, regions, measure, reference geometry kernel failures, Combine with one body, Select Other with nothing under the cursor, and unreadable or damaged part files. The remaining ones, mostly value checks in feature builds ("the depth must be greater than zero") whose fix is implied, are listed in `docs/BUG_HUNT.md` as open and left for the release preparation round, to keep this round's changes local while other sessions edit the same feature modules.
Status: Default
Reason: Fix the messages users meet most first, without broad edits that clash with parallel work.

D530: Hem (PHASE5_SPEC P5.6, D438). Type `hem`. Pick one or more straight outside edges of flat walls, as for Edge Flange; each gets a fold back over the face the edge lies on (Reverse folds under). Four kinds: closed (bend of 180 degrees with inside radius 0, the hem lies flat on the sheet), open (180 degrees, inside radius half the typed `gap`), teardrop (inside radius `radius` and a typed `angle` between 180 and 350 degrees, so the hem leans back toward the sheet) and rolled (inside radius `radius` and an `angle` between 90 and 350 degrees, with no straight wall after the bend). `length` is the hem length seen from outside: from the outer face of the fold to the end of the hem, so the straight wall is `length` less (inside radius + thickness); rolled hems have no length. Position: material inside (default: the outer face of the fold lies on the picked edge, the wall is trimmed back by inside radius + thickness) or material outside (the fold starts at the edge, the part grows). Every hem covers its whole edge; where two picked edges share a corner, each hem is shortened there by the other hem's length plus `corner_gap` (default 0.5 mm in the panel) so their folds do not meet, and with material inside the usual relief (D336) is cut at that end. A hem whose fold or wall would cut into the sheet (a long teardrop or a big roll) is an error that says to shorten it or reduce the angle. The bend allowance comes from the part's method with the hem's radius and angle, so the flat length is exact (a bend table needs a row for the hem angle).
Status: Default
Reason: The spec only names the tool; these are the four common hem shapes, built from the existing bend model so they flatten exactly.

D531: Miter Flange (P5.6, D438). Type `miter_flange`. Refs: `edges` (straight edges on one face, top or bottom, of one wall, joined end to end into a chain with convex corners) and `sketch` (an open chain of lines on a plane square to an end edge of the chain, starting at that edge's end point). The sketch lines are the continuation of the picked face: the material lies on the side of the lines away from that face, so a line that turns toward the picked face has that face inside its bend (setback R x tan(A / 2)) and one that turns away has it outside (setback (R + T) x tan(A / 2)). The first line must turn away from the sheet's plane (it becomes a bend of the default radius at the edge); later corners become bends too. Every edge of the chain gets the same walls and bends. At each corner of the chain the walls are cut on the vertical plane that halves the corner, each side kept `gap` / 2 from it (default 1 mm in the panel), and the bends end where their nearest point reaches that plane, so a small open notch is left at each mitred bend (a corner relief). The sheet is trimmed back from every picked edge to the bend tangent line, the corner included. Lines only (no arcs) in the profile; edges on several walls are an error. Faces: `e<k>/wall<m>/<role>`, `e<k>/bend<m>/<role>`, `trim<k>/<role>`.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec names the tool; a chain on one wall with mitred walls keeps the corners exact in the flat pattern while the bend model stays a straight strip.

D532: Jog (P5.6, D438). Type `jog`. A sketched line on a flat face, as Sketched Bend (D338, same fixed side rules and `flip_fixed`), gives two bends of the same angle in opposite directions so the moved side ends parallel to the fixed side, offset along the face normal (Reverse: the other way). `offset` is measured by `offset_from`: "same_face" (default; the shift of a face), "inner_faces" (between the facing faces: shift = offset + T) or "outer_faces" (overall: shift = offset - T). With R, T and angle A the straight middle wall is m = (shift - (2R + T) x (1 - cos A)) / sin A; m below zero is an error asking for a larger offset, a smaller radius or a smaller angle, and m of zero leaves out the middle wall. `position` places the first bend on the line as Sketched Bend does. The wall is cut into the fixed side, the middle wall and the moved side out of the original wall, so the flat pattern keeps the wall's flat size exactly. Flanges already on the moved side move with it; a line through another bend, or a flange on the middle wall, is an error. Faces: `bend1/<role>`, `bend2/<role>`, `middle/<old name>`, `moved/<old name>`.
Status: Default
Reason: The two bend jog is the usual offset form; cutting the pieces from the original wall makes the flat size exact by construction.

D533: Closed Corner (P5.6, D438). Type `closed_corner`. Refs `faces`: end faces (the narrow faces across a wall's length) of flange walls. For each picked face the partner is the nearest end of another wall (within 4 x (R + T) + gap). Both walls are lengthened at those ends by a tab in their own frame and then cut on a plane, so they close the corner whatever the angles: `corner_type` "overlap" (default; the picked wall reaches the partner's outer face, the partner stops `gap` short of the picked wall's inner face), "underlap" (the reverse) or "butt" (both stop `gap` / 2 from the plane that halves the angle between their outer faces). `gap` defaults to 0.1 mm in the panel. The bends are left as they are, so the relief at the bend corner stays open. The tabs are part of the walls, so the flat pattern shows them exactly. A face that is not a wall end, or with no partner close enough, is an error.
Status: Default
Reason: Cutting a lengthened wall on a plane closes corners of any angle with exact flat tabs and no change to the bends.

D534: Break Corner (P5.6, D438). Type `break_corner`. Refs `edges`: the short edges through the thickness at outside corners of walls. `break_type` "chamfer" (default; `distance` along both outline edges) or "fillet" (`radius`, an arc tangent to both outline edges). The cut is a prism through the wall in the wall's own frame, so the flat pattern has the same chamfer or round. A corner on a bend line, a corner that is not convex, or a size larger than either outline edge is an error.
Status: Default
Reason: Corner breaks of the flat outline are the shop meaning of the tool; a cut in the wall frame flattens exactly.

D535: Rip (P5.6, D438). Type `rip`. Two ways, either or both in one feature: (1) sketched rips: `refs.sketch` with lines on flat faces of the sheet; each line cuts a slit of width `gap` (default 0.1 mm in the panel) centred on the line, through the wall, only as long as the line; (2) edge rips: `refs.edges`, each an edge where two walls touch without a bend (after Closed Corner with no gap, or Convert to Sheet Metal); one wall is cut back from the other by `gap` (it loses the material within `gap` of the other wall's plate). By default the wall that loses less material is cut; `flip` cuts the other. Rips are cuts in the wall frames, so the flat pattern is exact.
Status: Default
Reason: A rip is a narrow cut that lets the sheet unfold; walls in this model only meet by bends, so edge rips are for walls that touch.

D536: Tab and Slot (P5.6, D438). Type `tab_slot`. Refs `edge` (a straight outside edge of the tab wall) and `face` (a flat face of the slot wall). `tab_count` tabs (default 2) of `tab_length` along the edge are spread evenly, centred, with `spacing` between them measured from tab centre to tab centre (0, the default, spreads them over the edge with equal end distances). Each tab sticks out of the edge by `depth` (default the sheet thickness) in the tab wall's plane. The slot in the other wall is the tab grown by `clearance` (default 0.1 mm) on every side across the tab, cut through the slot wall. Tabs that miss the slot wall are an error. Both are part of their walls' flat outlines, so the flat pattern is exact.
Status: Default
Reason: A tab on one wall's edge passing through a slot in the other is the usual self locating joint; the slot copied from the tab keeps them matched.

D537: Convert to Sheet Metal (P5.6, D438). Type `convert_sheet`. Refs `face` (a flat face of the solid that stays fixed) and `bends` (straight edges between flat faces). Thickness, radius and allowance come from the Sheet Metal folder (D330; the command adds the folder first, as Base Flange does). The faces reached from the fixed face across bend edges become walls; the solid's faces are the outer faces of the sheet and the material goes inward by the thickness. Each bend edge is the outer virtual sharp of a bend of the bend angle (180 degrees less the angle inside the solid); convex and concave edges both work. Bends that share a corner are each shortened by the other's setback plus `gap` (default 0.1 mm), and the walls are trimmed to the bend tangent lines along the whole edge. Edges between two kept faces that are not bend edges become rips: the wall found later from the fixed face is cut back to `gap` from the other wall's inner face. Faces not reached through bend edges are left out (so a box with its four lower edges as bends becomes an open box with ripped corners). Bend edges that close a loop, curved faces among the kept faces and a concave rip edge are errors. The result is an ordinary sheet model, so the flat pattern is exact.
Status: Default
Reason: The solid's faces keep the outside sizes, which is how such parts are usually drawn; the bend model already flattens exactly.

D538: Insert Bends (P5.6, D438). Type `insert_bends`. For a thin solid of even thickness (a shelled or thin walled part). Refs `face`: a flat face on the outside of the thin part. The thickness is measured from that face to the parallel face behind it and must match the Sheet Metal folder (an error says which value to set). The outside faces are the faces reached from the picked face across edges whose neighbour is not a thickness side face (a face square to the sheet and as wide as the thickness). Every edge between two outside faces becomes a bend, taken in the order found from the picked face; an edge that would close a loop becomes a rip. Then the part is built as Convert to Sheet Metal (D537) with the picked face fixed.
Status: Default
Reason: Insert Bends is Convert to Sheet Metal with the choices found from the part, so both share one tested builder.

D539: Cross Break (P5.6, D438). Type `cross_break`. Refs `face`: a flat face of a wall. Two cosmetic lines join the opposite corners of the wall's outline box on that face; no geometry changes. They are drawn in the view folded and flat (with the bend lines) and written to the flat pattern DXF and SVG on a `CROSS_BREAKS` layer. `reverse` only changes the "up" or "down" title in the SVG.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec says cosmetic lines only; the X across the panel is the usual mark.

D540: Corner relief options (P5.1 item 3, D438). The Sheet Metal folder and Edge Flange (own relief) gain `corner_relief`: "rectangular" (default, the existing clearing down to the tangent lines, D336) or "circular", with `corner_relief_size` (the circle's diameter, default 2 x thickness). Where two bends of one Edge Flange share a corner, a circular relief is a round hole through the sheet centred where the two bend tangent lines meet. Where the circle would reach a bend, that bend and its flange wall are shortened at that end so they stop at the circle. It is a cut in the wall frame, so the flat pattern is exact.
Status: Default
Reason: A round hole at the bend corner is the usual relief against tearing; stopping the bends at the circle keeps every piece a plain strip that flattens exactly.

D541: Unfold and Fold (P5.5 item 6, D438). Types `unfold` and `fold`. Unfold: `refs.bends` (faces of bends) or `all_bends`; those bends are shown flat, the wall nearer the first wall staying fixed. Features after it may be cuts (Extruded Cut and other features that only remove material); they are taken in by the Fold. Fold (no settings besides `refs.unfold`, the Unfold it closes) works out the removed material (the Unfold's part less the current part), cuts it from every wall in the wall's frame and, where it crosses an unfolded bend strip, stores the cut's outline on the bend. A folded bend with cuts is built by wrapping each outline onto the bend: across the strip, a distance y becomes the angle y / BA x A, so the cut lands where it would after bending the flat sheet. Cuts across a bend must go through the sheet; arcs wrap exactly, other curves as short lines within 0.01 mm. A feature between Unfold and Fold that adds material is an error. The flat pattern uses the cut strips, so it stays exact.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks for cuts across a bend; taking the cut from the ordinary Extruded Cut keeps one cutting tool, and wrapping the outline is exact for the bend allowance.

D542: Gauge tables (P5.1 item 4, D438). Folder top level key `gauge_table`: CSV text, one row per gauge: name, thickness (mm), then one or more inside radii (mm); an optional header row. Folder param `gauge` (the row name, stored only while a gauge is in use): the thickness comes from the row and the radius must be one of the row's radii (an error lists them). Load Gauge Table on the Sheet Metal tab reads a CSV file, checks it, stores it in the folder and asks which gauge to use (setting the thickness and the first radius); one undoable step. The bend allowance method is unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: Plain data in the file as for bend tables (D332); the typed thickness and radius stay so turning a gauge off is lossless.

D543: Swept Flange (P5.6, D438). Left out. Swept along a path with arcs, the walls would be curved in two directions, which the flat wall model (D333) cannot hold or flatten exactly; along a chain of straight edges it is the same result as Miter Flange (D531). Recorded in IDEAS.md for a later model.
Status: Default
Reason: The brief allows leaving out what is too large; no exact flat pattern is possible with flat walls.

D544: Lofted Bend (P5.6, D438). Left out. A transition between two profiles needs a developable surface, which the flat wall model can only fake with many thin facets and no exact flat length. Recorded in IDEAS.md.
Status: Default
Reason: The brief asks for exact flat lengths or a clear message; this one needs a new model.

D545: Forming tools (P5.6, D438). Type `form_tool`. A built in set made by parameters, never from imported parts: `tool` "dimple" (round, `diameter`, `height`), "louvre" (`length`, `width`, `height`: a strip lanced along one long side and raised as a sloped hood with closed sides) and "rib" (embossed rib with round ends, `length` from the sketch line, `width`, `height`). Placement: `refs.sketch` on a flat face of a wall; every sketch line places one form centred on its midpoint and turned along it (a rib runs from end to end of the line). The form rises from the sketched face; Reverse presses it the other way. The formed shape is a hollow pressing of the sheet thickness with sloped sides (45 degrees). It is only in the folded part: the flat pattern keeps the flat outline, and a louvre's lance is a 0.02 mm slit in it. A form that runs off its wall or within the thickness of a bend is an error.
Status: Default
Reason: Forming does not change the outline the blank is cut from; parameter made shapes keep the file free of embedded parts.

D546: Sheet model additions for D530 to D545. (1) `Wall.folded_cuts` and `Wall.adds`: solids cut and then added in the folded part only (forming tools); `Wall.plate` may be a fused shape (tabs, closed corner extensions). (2) `Bend.cuts`: cut outlines on a bend strip, in the strip's flat frame (Fold). (3) `SheetModel.unfolded`: bends shown flat by an Unfold. (4) `SheetModel.marks`: cosmetic lines on wall faces (Cross Break). (5) A bend whose child wall does not exist (rolled hem, jog with no middle wall) is allowed. (6) Every new type returns a `SheetResult`, so it counts as a sheet metal feature for the Flat Pattern limit (P5.5 item 7); any other feature after the last one still blocks flattening by name.
Status: Default
Reason: Small additive fields keep the existing features and files unchanged.

D547: Sheet Metal tab for D530 to D545. A second row of commands: Flanges group adds Miter Flange, Hem and Jog; a Corners group has Closed Corner, Break Corner, Corner Relief is a folder setting; a Cuts group has Rip, Tab and Slot, Cross Break; a Convert group has Convert to Sheet Metal and Insert Bends; a Forms group has Forming Tool; the Flat Pattern group adds Unfold and Fold; the Sheet Metal group adds Load Gauge Table. Command ids `feature.<type>` and `feature.gauge_table`, no default keys, shortcut editor group Sheet Metal. Panels use the shared form tables as D341. Fold starts with the newest Unfold that has no Fold. Convert to Sheet Metal and Insert Bends add the folder first when the part has none, as Base Flange does.
Status: Default
Reason: Same layout rules and shared forms as D341, so the shared registries change only by additions.

D550: Next steps in every message (bug hunt O1 and O2, CLAUDE.md 8.4, round 9v). Every text of an FDCAD exception shown to the user is a complete message: one or more sentences, each ending with a full stop, one of them a next step. A wrapper that shows such a reason puts it last and adds nothing after it ("Could not open {name}: {reason}", "Variables: {reason}", "Import failed: {error}", "Export failed: {reason}" for an `ExportError`). Reasons from outside FDCAD (operating system errors, file decoding, the CSV reader, unexpected exceptions in background jobs) go through `strings.clause()`, which uses the system's short error text and drops a final full stop; a separate template then adds a fixed next step after the clause ("Could not open {name}: {reason}. Check that the file exists and that you can read it."). So no message ends with "..", and none ends with a reason that has no step. `DeformError` text stays a lower case clause, because the deformation features always wrap it in a message with a step. About 300 messages were rewritten at their sources: feature value checks keep their rule and add a step ("Depth must be greater than zero. Enter a positive depth."), sketch solver relation messages say what to select and to add the relation again, and values from a newer or damaged file say to choose another value in the property panel. The print orientation message no longer repeats its prefix.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for every message to say what to do next; fixing reasons at their sources is the only way to avoid double full stops and steps that do not fit the reason.

D551: Help, Open User Guide (round 9v). The guide is the Markdown in `docs/user_guide`, shown inside FDCAD in a text browser window with Back, Forward and Contents. Links between guide pages work; links with a web address are not followed (CLAUDE.md rule 8) and the browser's tooltip shows the address instead. The build bundles every `.md` file under `docs/user_guide` at the same path (`packaging/fdcad.spec`), and `ui/help/paths.py` finds it under `sys._MEIPASS` in a build or from the repository root in the source tree. A missing guide gives a message that says to reinstall. Reading the guide in the app was chosen over opening the `.md` files with the system, which on most systems opens a text editor showing raw Markdown.
Status: Default
Reason: The guide must work offline in both installers; Qt reads Markdown without a new dependency.

D552: First run welcome (round 9v). A non modal window, shown once after the main window is up on the first start: how to start a sketch, the command tabs, the left panel icons, where Preferences and the themes are, and the user guide, with Open User Guide and Start Modeling buttons. Closing it in any way sets the preference `help/welcome_seen`, so it never shows by itself again; Help, Welcome opens it again. It is skipped when the startup budget report runs (`FDCAD_STARTUP_REPORT`). It is not modal so it never blocks a file opened at start, and it is shown from `app.main`, not from the main window, so tests that build a window never see it.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for a short dismissable welcome; non modal keeps startup and tests unaffected.

D553: About box (round 9v). Help, About FDCAD is a dialog with an About tab (version, a one line summary, the GPL v3 or later license and the not affiliated sentence) and a Licenses tab that shows the FDCAD license, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the LGPL 2.1 and LGPL 3 texts from `packaging/licenses` (bundled as `licenses/` in a build). The not affiliated sentence is the README sentence word for word (`strings_help.NOT_AFFILIATED`, checked by a test): the owner asked for it in the About box, so it is the one place in the UI that names those trademarks, as CLAUDE.md 7.5 allows for that one sentence. The old `ABOUT_TEXT` message box is gone.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner listed the About box contents; one shared constant keeps the trademark sentence in one place.

D554: Help, Keyboard Shortcuts (round 9v). A modal list of every command in `input/commands.py` with its group and current keys (the user's changes included, Mac keys on a Mac), sorted by group, with a filter box that matches the command, group or key text, and a Change Shortcuts button that opens Preferences. The Help menu items are plain menu actions, not commands with keys, so the shortcut editor, the sweep's command list and the guide's command check are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: The list reuses the shortcut map, so it can never disagree with the keys in use.

D555: Message scan test (round 9v). `tests/core/test_message_next_steps.py` reads the source with `ast` and checks every message written as text: the first argument of every raised user facing exception (`FeatureError`, `SketchSolveError`, `NodeError` and the others listed in the test), every message of `Issue`, `SketchIssue` and `GeometryIssue`, and the error and warning constants of the UI strings modules, with a short documented exemption list for texts that are not problems. A message passes when one of its sentences, after an optional "Name:" prefix, starts with a word from the test's list of next step verbs, or when it ends with a wrapped reason (checked where that reason is raised). Messages built in variables cannot be read and are not checked. `tests/ui/test_error_message_steps.py` checks that wrappers never give "..".
Status: Default
Reason: A source scan catches new messages without a step the moment they are written, which a list of examples cannot.

D556: Version 1.0.0 preparation (round 9v). The version stays `1.0.0.dev0` until the owner tags the release. It lives in `pyproject.toml` and `fdcad.__version__`: the `uv_build` backend cannot read one from the other, so `tools/set_version.py VERSION` writes both, followed by `uv lock`, and a test checks they match. The release workflow refuses a `v*` tag that does not equal `__version__`, so a release can never ship with a development version. The Mac bundle version uses the numeric part only ("1.0.0"), as macOS expects. Files record the version that saved them (`app_version`); tests save with the fixtures' version 0.1.0 (autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py`, marker `real_version` to opt out) so the byte for byte save checks test the schema, not the version stamp, and do not all change with each release.
Status: Default
Reason: One command sets the version, a test catches drift, and the workflow catches a tag made before the bump.

D557: App icon (round 9v). FDCAD had no app icon. A new one, drawn for FDCAD: a white isometric block with a drilled hole on a rounded blue tile (`src/fdcad/ui/app_icon.svg`). `tools/make_app_icon.py` renders it with Qt to PNGs at 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1024 px, `packaging/icons/fdcad.ico` (16 to 256 px, PNG entries) and `packaging/icons/fdcad.icns` (16 to 1024 px including the Retina entries), written by the script without a new dependency. The spec uses the `.ico` for the Windows executable and the `.icns` for the Mac bundle and its `.fdef` document type; the installer uses it for the setup program; `app.main` sets the SVG as the window icon. A test checks every size in each file.
Status: Default
Reason: Both installers need an icon at every size; generating them from one SVG keeps them the same.

D558: Installer review for v1.0 (round 9v). The Windows script already had the uninstaller, Start menu entries, publisher, x64 mode and the `.fdef` association. Added: the setup icon, the uninstall display name, `CloseApplications`, a copyright line, an `OpenWithProgids` entry, and removal of the association's content type value on uninstall. The Mac spec gained the bundle icon, the document type icon, a numeric bundle version and a copyright line; `make_dmg.sh` already signs ad hoc and verifies. Both installers now ship the user guide. Tests check the installer script and the spec for each of these items.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for a check of both installers before 1.0.

D559: Release documents for v1.0 (round 9v). `CHANGELOG.md` [Unreleased] became `## [1.0.0] - TBD`, its Added list grouped by area (sketching, features, holes and fastening, curves and bodies, reference geometry, sheet metal, 3D printing and evaluate, import and export, equations and the node editor, interface, samples and tests); the release workflow still finds the section by its version. `docs/RELEASE_NOTES_1.0.md` sums up 1.0 in plain words by area, with getting started and known limits. `docs/OWNER_REVIEW_1.0.md` fills in PLAN 13 for v1.0, ordered by risk: install and start, older files, crash safety, upstream edits, save and export, the speed and memory budgets on the baseline machines, this round's changes, then the release steps. The owner sets the date in both documents when tagging.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN 12 and 13 ask for release notes and an owner checklist with each release.

D570: Owner notes from the v1.0 review (2026-10-30). Clicking the part name in the tree crashed the plane highlight: `FeatureTree.selected_id` now skips the part row as it skips the rollback bar. Opening a feature turns the view to 3D and framed only the flat sketch, so the preview grew off screen: the view frames the first preview after that turn (`fit_next_preview`). A finished feature no longer leaves its dimensions on the part: feature dimensions show only for a feature the user clicks in the tree; the Measure tool reads sizes off the part.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for the part to stay centred and for a clean part after its values are given.

D571: Plane outlines and names (2026-10-30). Each theme's plane outline, which is also the name colour, now reads at 4.5:1 or more on both ends of the view gradient (Light Gray #3E4550, Beige #55493A, Dark Grey #E1E5EA, Stealth #C3C8CF). They are sent to the 3D view as sRGB, as the background is, instead of as linear values that paled them; the outline is 1.5 px and names 12 px. The fill stays light and mostly see through. A test checks the ratio for every theme.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for more contrast on plane outlines and names, keeping the planes transparent.

D572: Shell falls back to round joins (2026-10-30). The kernel's sharp offset joins can fail, or return broken geometry, on parts such as a filleted bore. Shell now checks the sharp result for validity and, when it fails, tries round joins before reporting the error. Sharp joins stay first, so existing shells keep their exact walls. Found by an original multi feature test part (plate, tower, through bore, ribs with mirror and pattern, corner holes, fillet, chamfer, shell). Known limit: shelling from a face where chamfered holes break through still fails with a clear message.
Status: Default
Reason: Shell is common on real parts and the round join result is valid.

D573: Patterns copy Hole Tool holes (2026-10-30). A linear or circular pattern, or a mirror, of a Hole Tool feature failed because the hole has no operation setting. Feature types can now declare a fixed `pattern_operation`; the Hole Tool declares "cut", so a bolt circle of holes copies the hole feature. Curve Array used "boss" for a seed without an operation and would have added holes as solid pins; it now uses the same declaration. A hole with modelled threads still asks for Geometry pattern, since the feature copy leaves the threads out. Found by `tests/core/features/test_complex_parts.py`, three original parts (turned shaft, swept elbow, drafted housing) that chain revolve, revolved cut, chamfer, modelled and cosmetic threads, tapped holes, bolt circles, sweeps, loft, draft, shell, rib, mounting boss and dome.
Status: Default
Reason: Patterning holes round a bolt circle is one of the most common modelling steps.

D574: Command search box (2026-10-30). A search box sits at the top left, before the command tabs (Ctrl+K). It matches command names and search words like the shortcut bar, lists up to 12 matches with their icon and shortcut, and Enter or a click runs one. Ctrl+Q was taken by Force Rebuild.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for a search bar at the top left for tools and features.

D575: Part files are saved as `.fdprt` (2026-10-30). Save, Save As, Save Bodies, autosave and the samples write `.fdprt`. The content is unchanged (the `format` key stays "fdef", FDEF_SPEC 1). Open, double click, the command line, recovery and Open Sample accept both `.fdprt` and the older `.fdef`; saving a part opened from a `.fdef` file keeps that file until Save As picks a new name. The Windows installer and the Mac bundle register both extensions. Test fixtures keep `.fdef` so the older name stays covered.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for part files to save as .fdprt.

D576: Property panel check text fits the panel (2026-10-30). The pre check message in a feature panel (for example a failed Fillet) cut off its text and fix buttons on the right and showed a sideways scroll bar, because long edge names such as `edge(f6/cap/end|f8/side/e4)` have no break points and the buttons grew to their full text. The message now gets zero width break points after `/`, `|`, `(` and `,`, its width no longer sets the panel width, and fix buttons shorten their text in the middle to fit, with the full text in the tooltip. The panel never scrolls sideways. A check of the display mesh of a cylinder with a through cut whose corners touch the rim found it correct (triangle area equals face area), so the mesher was left alone.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner reported the first installed build looked wrong in the view; the clipped panel was a real bug.

D577: Command search box moves to the top right (2026-10-30). The search box from D574 now sits in the right corner of the command tab row, and its result list lines up with the box's right edge so it never runs off the window. Ctrl+K and the matching rules are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for the search at the top right instead of the top left.

D578: Showcase part (2026-10-30). `showcase/everything_part.fdprt` is one single body that chains extrude, revolve, shell, hole, patterns, fillet, chamfer, sweep, loft, mounting boss, dome, both thread types and draft, built to try the installed app. It is not under `samples/` because every sample needs a golden entry. The Rib is left out: it reported "does not meet the part all round" at every sketch position tried.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for one complex part with every feature, saved.

D579: Straight arrows and the section drag arrow (2026-10-30). Length handles on feature previews (Extrude, Cut and the rest) are now an arrow: a cone head at the tip with a thin shaft behind it, instead of a bare cone. Angle handles keep their curved arrow. Section 1 gets a drag arrow in the 3D view: it stands on the section plane, points along its normal, and dragging it types the new Offset into the panel. The arrow is a handle only preview (no solid), made on the kernel worker like other arrows. Its value is the offset plus 10000 mm, so a drag can go below zero while handle values stay positive; the label and the panel take the 10000 off again. No arrow shows when the section turns about an axis. Not checked by hand: dragging the arrow with the mouse (the tests cover the handle, the arrow shape and the panel link).
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for arrows instead of cones, and a drag arrow for the section view.

D580: Section view starts mid part, edges pick within 6 pixels, Appearance easy to reach (2026-10-30). (1) A new section cut through Front at offset 0, which is the bottom face of parts built on Front: the part vanished and the cap fought with that face in stripes. A new section now starts with each plane through the middle of the part's bounding box; picking Front, Top or Right keeps it centred until the user types an offset. Reopening the panel keeps the offset, Reverse and rotations it was left with (they reset to 0 before). (2) The 3D view picks edges and vertices within 6 logical pixels (scaled by the screen's pixel ratio) instead of the kernel's 2 device pixels, so Fillet and Chamfer edges are easier to hit. (3) Appearance (D254) was only in the Edit menu. It is now also a button in the view toolbar, an item in the right click menu of a face and of empty space (the part), and in the tree menu of the part and of every feature that makes solid faces.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner reported that fillet edges do not snap easily, that the section view looks wrong, and asked to colour the part, faces and features.


D581: New app icon "Ember" (2026-11-01). The owner asked for a cooler logo and picked this one from three new drawings. It replaces the white block of D557 and D672: a chamfered amber block with a drilled hole on a midnight blue tile. The two big side faces carry F and D, and the narrow chamfer face between them carries CAD stacked top to bottom, all drawn in the plane of each face. The letters are original blocky shapes made of paths, not a font, so the icon looks the same on every machine. The 16 to 32 px drawing (`app_icon_small.svg`) is the same block larger on a full tile and leaves out the CAD letters, which cannot be read at that size. `tools/make_app_icon.py` regenerated every PNG, the `.ico` and the `.icns`.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request; the icon must stay original work (CLAUDE.md section 7).

D582: Command tabs can be moved and hidden from a button (2026-11-01, owner request). Holding the mouse on a tab for 400 ms turns on dragging with a grab cursor, and the tab then follows the mouse along the row. A quick click only switches tabs, so a shaky click never moves one. The order is saved (`appearance/command_tab_order`) and applied at start; tabs missing from the saved order, such as a tab a newer version adds, come after the saved ones. A small arrow button at the left end of the tab row opens the same list as a right click on the row: one tick box per tab, then Show All Tabs and Reset Tab Order. All tabs are shown by default, and the last visible tab cannot be hidden. Closing a sketch goes back to the Features tab by name, not by position.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request; people arrange the tabs they use most first.

D583: Clean preview for Fillet, Chamfer, Shell and Draft (2026-11-01, owner request). The preview laid see-through copies of every changed face over the part. The copy and the part were meshed differently, so curved faces showed diagonal stripes, and the copied faces drew blue outlines. These features now show the finished part instead: opaque, in the part's colour, without edge lines, with only the faces the feature made (the faces named after its id, for example the round faces of a fillet) in the accent colour. The part stays in the view but is drawn fully see-through and without edges, so its edges can still be hovered and clicked to add them. It comes back as before when the panel closes. The tinted faces are mapped through the private copy the preview meshes. Other features keep the see-through solid of D109.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request: no stripes, no lines, a clean preview.

D584: Colours in use can be changed and removed (2026-11-01, owner request). The Appearance panel's list of colours in use and the Appearances rows of the feature tree show one row per item with a colour: the part, each body, each feature, and the coloured faces of each feature together. Double click a row to change its colour. Select it and press Delete (or Backspace in the panel) to remove it. Right click for Change Color and Remove Color. Removing the part colour puts the default back, so Remove is off while the part has the default colour. Each change is one undoable step. In the tree, Delete on a colour row only removes the colour; it never deletes a feature.
Status: Default
Reason: The rows only showed text, so a colour could not be removed without selecting its faces again.

D585: Partial preview draws the outline (2026-11-01, owner request). The Fillet and Chamfer preview choices are Full, Partial and None. Full shows the finished part with the new faces tinted (D583). Partial leaves the part as it is and draws only the edges of the faces the feature will make, as thick lines in the preview colour, for every picked item. None shows nothing. Partial used to show one item at a time with a Next Item button; that button is gone. The view gets the request through the key `preview_outline` in the previewed copy's `data`, which is never saved.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner found Partial and Full looked the same; Partial should only show where the round or chamfer goes.

D586: Section view arrow (2026-11-01, owner request). The drag arrow of the section view is a flat arrow, one thin face with a head and a shaft, built facing the viewer when the section is shown. Handle arrows of every preview are drawn with an empty set of clipping planes that overrides the view's planes, so the section cut never cuts them.
Status: Default
Reason: The section cut sliced the arrow, and the owner wants a flat arrow.

D587: Readable CAD on the app icon (2026-11-01, owner request). The block on the app icon is taller and its middle (chamfer) face is as wide as half the block, so CAD can be large. CAD is drawn as thick round strokes with space between the letters. F, CAD and D read down to 64 px, and CAD still shows at 48 px. The 32 px and smaller icons use the small drawing (a larger block, same letters), where only the shape can be made out.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner could not read CAD between the F and the D.

D588: Installer pictures (2026-11-01, owner request). The Windows installer shows the app icon and the name FDCAD on its welcome and finish pages, and the icon at the top right of the other pages, instead of Inno Setup's default pictures. `tools/make_installer_images.py` draws them from `app_icon.svg` as BMP files at every size Inno Setup picks from for the screen scale, into `packaging/windows/images`.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner did not see the new icon in the installer.

D589: Corrections from the 2026-11-01 test plan run (docs/TEST_RUN_2026-11-01.md). (1) Scale per axis transforms a copy of the bodies without the display mesh, which made the live preview fail. (2) Linear Pattern's count is optional, since Up to reference works it out and the panel leaves it out. (3) Cosmetic and Modeled Thread pick the standard size that fits a picked round edge: the major diameter for a shaft, the tap drill for a hole, within 0.15 mm, metric first. A Modeled Thread whose size is far from the face says so with both sizes. (4) Messages name values in words (`value_label`: "count 1", "end condition") instead of quoting parameter keys, and sheet metal edge errors give the edge's place in the list instead of its internal name. (5) Print Estimate measures volume to a relative error of 1e-6 (`precise_volume`); the quick `volume_of` stays for internal checks.
Status: Default
Reason: Found by the automated run of docs/TEST_PLAN.md.

D590: Save while a sketch is open (2026-10-31, bug hunt round 10a). Save and autosave wrote the part without the open sketch's edits, and a new sketch was missing from the file, while the title showed no star. Save, Save As and Save As with the FDCAD part type now close an open sketch of that part as OK does before writing, as closing the part already did. If the sketch cannot close (a value box holds a bad value), nothing is saved. Autosave never closes the sketch: it writes a copy of the part that holds the sketch as it stands, inserted where OK would put it.
Status: Default
Reason: Found by the round 10a file hunt (open item O1 of its report). Data loss.

D591: Feature tree and rollback rules (2026-10-31, bug hunt round 10a). (1) Feature names must not hold `"` or `@` and must not equal another feature's name or id, because formulas find features by name or id; the check is exact, so names that differ only in case are allowed. The tree refuses such a name with a message and puts the old name back (`fdcad/core/document/names.py`). (2) The rollback bar is stored as the feature it sits after. When that feature is deleted or dragged, the bar moves to the feature before it, so no other feature changes its rolled back state; Undo puts it back. (3) The rebuild leaves out every feature in `rolled_back(doc)`; before, it stopped at the bar's feature, which a suppressed feature skipped. (4) The tree refills one event loop turn after every undo stack change, as well as after the rebuild, and its row handlers ignore rows whose feature is gone. (5) Undo and Redo are off while a feature panel is open, as in sketch mode. (6) A double click on a row only opens the feature; rename is F2 or the menu. (7) A refused drag says why in the status bar.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10a tree hunt, bugs R10a T1 to T12.

D592: Switching parts with a bad sketch value (2026-10-31). Changing the part tab closes an open sketch of the part being left, as OK does. When that fails because a value box holds a bad value, the tab goes back to the sketch's part and the sketch stays open, as Edit Sketch on another sketch already does.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10a sketch hunt, open item 2.

D593: The sketch Dimension panel's value field applies on Enter and when it loses focus (2026-10-31). Text that equals the dimension's current value changes nothing, so leaving the field adds no empty undo step.
Status: Default
Reason: Tab away from the field dropped the typed value.

D594: Feature tree rows show the full feature name as a tip, followed by the feature's messages when it has any (2026-10-31).
Status: Default
Reason: Long names are cut off in a narrow tree.

D595: Extrude and Revolve details (2026-10-31, bug hunt round 10a). (1) Mid Plane with a draft uses Direction 1's angle and Draft outward on both halves (D212 only allowed the pair). (2) A drafted Through All cut ends 1 mm past the far side of the part instead of using the long tool length, which an inward draft closed up; without a draft Through All is unchanged. (3) In an inch part the From offset and Offset from Face start at 0.5 in, and the thin wall and caps at 0.05 in, like the inch depth and shell defaults. (4) Revolve Offset from Face larger than the turn to a face of the part is an error that says the end is behind the start; on a plane that holds the axis, the other half of the plane is still used. (5) A new Revolved Cut on a face no longer starts with Reverse pressed: pointing into the part applies to Extruded Cut only. (6) Switching between Up to Face and Offset from Face keeps the face just picked.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10a Extrude and Revolve hunt, bugs R10a E1 to E8.

D596: Sketch rules (2026-10-31, bug hunt round 10a). (1) A sketch the solver cannot solve reports Over defined, so it is red and its message shows (TOOL_SPEC T1.4.1); the rebuild already treated it the same way. (2) Angle dimensions accept only values above 0 and below 180 degrees. (3) This extends D273(3): with Copy off, Mirror's copies keep the relations among the picks that a mirror keeps true (Coincident, Collinear, Concentric, Coradial, Equal, Intersection, Midpoint, Parallel, Perpendicular, Tangent); Horizontal, Vertical, Fix, Symmetric and dimensions still go with the originals. (4) Delete never removes the sketch origin or its Fix. (5) Trim and Extend drop the arc length dimension of an arc whose ends change.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10a sketch hunt, bugs R10a S1 to S11.

D597: File handling (2026-10-31, bug hunt round 10a). (1) Save As adds the type's suffix to the full typed name instead of replacing its last dotted part ("rev 1.2" becomes "rev 1.2.fdprt"); an older `.fdef` name still becomes `.fdprt` (D575). When that final name is a different file that already exists, Save As asks before replacing it. (2) A recent file that fails to open because it is missing is taken off the recent list; `&` in a path is shown as written. (3) Each autosave is held by a `QLockFile` (`<id>.lock`) while its FDCAD runs. The lock is stale only when its process is gone, never by age, so a second FDCAD leaves a running one's autosaves alone. (4) Atomic saves create their temporary file with normal permissions (the umask applies) and copy the mode of the file they replace; the private disk cache keeps `mkstemp`. (5) A recovered part keeps the file it came from and stays unsaved. (6) Open stores the full path, and a file that is already open is not opened again. (7) Save As and Export start in the part's own folder.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10a file hunt, bugs R10a F1 to F13.

D598: The pick tolerance test needs a display (2026-10-31). `test_edges_pick_within_a_few_pixels` builds a real 3D view, which on Linux needs an X server. It skips when the kernel cannot connect to a display, so it still runs on the macOS and Windows CI runners.
Status: Default
Reason: The full suite failed in the Linux cloud container.

D599: Dialogs opened with `exec()` and parented to the main window are deleted after they close (2026-10-31). Preferences kept each closed dialog (about 300 widgets) as a hidden child of the window, so every later theme change restyled more widgets; after a few hundred opens in the slow app sweep, Preferences OK took 80 s. The window now calls `deleteLater()` on the Preferences dialog after `exec()`. The Equations and Design Table dialogs and the section view panel leave fewer widgets behind and are listed as open in docs/BUG_HUNT.md. The slow sweep itself never returned to the main event loop, so no `deleteLater` ever ran there and closed panels piled up to over 12000 widgets; `sweep_support.settle` now delivers pending deletes as the running app does.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10a slow sweep: `test_every_command_on_every_sample[plate_with_holes]` failed on the base commit and on this branch with Preferences OK over the 30 s step limit.
D600: Lost picks name the feature that caused them (2026-10-31). When a feature's picked faces or edges are lost because an earlier feature that made them failed or is suppressed, the message names that feature ("Linear Pattern 1 has an error. Fix Linear Pattern 1 first." or "... is suppressed. Unsuppress ... or pick again.") instead of only asking the user to pick again. Fillet, Chamfer, Shell and Draft picks build the message in `modify.lost_message`; for every other feature the rebuild engine adds the same sentence to an error whose highlighted names come from such a feature. The owner of a name is the feature id before the first `/` of each face name in it.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b bug hunt: after a pattern count was raised so a copy fell off, a fillet on another copy said its edges were lost and asked for a new pick, which could not help.

D601: A test that builds the 3D view skips when there is no display (2026-10-31). `test_edges_pick_within_a_few_pixels` creates the 3D view on its own. On Linux with the offscreen platform the graphics driver cannot connect to a display server and the test failed. It now skips there, as the main window already shows no 3D view on that platform (`viewport_supported`). CI on macOS and Windows still runs it.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b: the full suite failed in a Linux container for this reason only.

D602: Pattern direction 2 checks (2026-10-31). A circular pattern's direction 2 angle must be greater than zero, as direction 1's already was; zero put every copy on the seed and failed with a misleading "would not touch the part". A linear pattern whose direction 2 is parallel to direction 1 now fails ("copies would land on each other. Pick another direction 2."), matching Mirror's check for parallel planes.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b bug hunt.

D603: What to change when pattern copies fall off (2026-10-31). The message for copies that miss the part ends with a step that fits the feature: "pick another mirror plane" for Mirror, "change the angle or the axis" for Circular Pattern, "move the sketch points" for Sketch Pattern, and "change the spacing" for Linear Pattern. Mirror has no spacing, so the old text could not be followed.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b bug hunt.

D604: Geometry pattern of a pattern copies its seed too (2026-10-31). A pattern or mirror's own faces are only its copies, so a Geometry pattern of Linear Pattern 1 copied the copies and left out the seed they came from (five holes instead of six). The seed features of any pattern, mirror or curve array among the picked features are now copied as well, followed down through patterns of patterns. Copying a pattern as a feature (Geometry pattern off) still says to turn on Geometry pattern.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b: the error message told the user to turn on Geometry pattern, which then gave the wrong number of copies.

D605: Points that shape a curve are not hole or pattern points (2026-10-31). `hole.point_kinds` gives a new kind, `helper`, to the axis ends of an ellipse or ellipse arc and to the inner through points and tangent handles of a spline. Helper points never get a hole and never get a Sketch Pattern copy. Ellipse centres count as centres, ellipse arc ends and spline ends as ends, like those of arcs and lines. Sketch Pattern now uses the same rule (only free points), so its instance numbers can change for sketches that hold ellipses or splines.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b: a sketch with one point, an ellipse and a spline made seven pattern copies and eight holes instead of one.

D606: Edges in several pieces (2026-10-31). An edge is named by its two faces (FDEF_SPEC 8.3), so two faces that meet along several edges (a notch across an edge) give several edges the same name. (1) `resolve_edge` now looks at every edge with the name: the one whose snapshot still matches is used; otherwise the one nearest to where it was picked, with a warning. Before, it always took the first, so picking the second piece rounded the first. (2) Fillet and Chamfer resolve a pick with `resolve_edge_pieces`: when no piece matches the snapshot and two or more pieces lie inside the edge as it was picked (same curve kind and direction, no longer than it, midpoint within half its length), the edge was split by an earlier edit and every piece is rounded. Pieces are named `<edge name>#1`, `#2`, so their fillet faces are `<fid>/fillet/<edge name>#k`; they share the edge's own radius. The "Fillet the rest" fix removes the pick a failing piece came from.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b bug hunt (topological naming): a fillet picked on the right piece rounded the wrong one, and a notch added before a fillet left half the edge sharp, both with no message.

D607: Result checks for features the kernel gets wrong quietly (2026-10-31). (1) Shell with removed faces fails when the removed faces are still there or no material went ("the wall is as thick as the part"). (2) Loft fails when its solid has no volume (profiles on one plane), when a closed loft has fewer than three profiles, and names a missing profile instead of failing in the kernel. (3) Modelled thread: an inside out swept thread is turned the right way, and a thread cut fails clearly when it removed less than 1% of the thread's volume or differs by more than 1% from what the thread overlaps ("the kernel could not cut the thread cleanly. Change the length slightly, or end the thread before the far end of the face."). Threads that run out of the far end of a face, including a tapped hole whose thread is deeper than a through hole, now fail with that message; making them cut is left open (BUG_HUNT Round 10b).
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b: each of these reported OK with wrong geometry.

D608: Reference geometry values follow variables (2026-10-31). The equations engine refreshes only parameters whose spec has a kind. Reference planes (`distance`, `angle`), points (`x`, `y`, `z`, `distance`, `percent`) and coordinate systems (`x`, `y`, `z`, `rx`, `ry`, `rz`) now declare theirs, so formulas, variables and design tables drive them. The panel already typed angles in degrees; a test helper that typed radian text was changed to match.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b: a plane offset typed as a variable kept its old value after the variable changed.

D609: Small fixes from round 10b (2026-10-31). (1) A saved three distance vertex chamfer has no `equal` key; the panel reopened it with Equal ticked and OK made it equal. Equal is now ticked only when stored, or when there is no second distance. (2) "Fillet the rest" removes the per edge values of the edges it drops (`radius_k`, `vr_k_*`) and moves later ones up, in the core fix and in the panel's rows, so each edge keeps its radius. (3) A partial fillet over the whole edge (0 to 100 percent) skips the split instead of failing. (4) Mounting Boss messages start with the feature name. (5) An edge dome that adds nothing (a face that is not convex) fails with "Tick Continuous dome." (6) The thread panels keep a size that is not in the table (shown as itself, or "Custom size" when empty) instead of switching to the first table size.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10b bug hunt.
D610: Body tool ticks that are on by default (2026-10-31). The generic body tool panel removed an unticked flag from the feature, and the core reads a missing flag as on, so Merge result (Intersect), Uniform (Scale) and Equal spacing (Circular Pattern) could not be turned off. `form_widget.apply` now writes `false` for an unticked flag whose form default is true. Files saved before keep their meaning, since a missing flag still reads as on.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; the option did nothing when unticked.

D611: Move Face and Delete Face edit only the picked bodies (2026-10-31). Offset, move, copy, patch and fill ran on every body of a multibody part at once, so Up to Body and offsets toward another body failed and overlapping bodies gave a false zero thickness warning. `bodies.on_own_bodies()` now runs the edit on the bodies that hold the picked faces and puts the others back unchanged, in the same body order. Moving a face into another body leaves two separate bodies that overlap; a direct edit never joins bodies (use Combine). The per face fallback of "Keep the faces that worked" still runs on the whole part (BUG_HUNT round 10c, open).
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; multibody direct edits gave wrong results.

D612: Intersect and Split region lists (2026-10-31). Intersect fills its region list by itself, on a worker thread, whenever the bodies, planes or region kind change, and lists only regions of the chosen kind (ticking the other kind would change nothing). Ticks the user changed are kept and a late result from an older count is dropped. Split clears its numbered list and ticks when the tools or bodies change, keeps every body and shows the Press Cut hint again; this also drops the stored `keep` of a saved Split whose tools are edited, because the old numbers would point at bodies numbered anew. In a pick box that takes bodies, picks are labelled and compared by body number, so another face of a picked body removes it.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; the Intersect list never filled and a stale Split list could keep the wrong bodies.

D613: File names for export, Save As and Save Bodies (2026-10-31). Export always adds the format's suffix to a typed name. Only known suffixes (.fdprt, .fdef, .step, .stp, .stl, .3mf) are replaced; any other dotted text is part of the name, so "v1.2 bracket" stays whole. A typed `.stp` is kept for STEP. Save Bodies adds "_" after a body name that Windows reserves for devices (CON, NUL, AUX, PRN, COM1 to COM9, LPT1 to LPT9), before the first dot.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; names were cut at a dot, saved without a suffix, or could not be written on Windows.

D614: Deform panels refit to the axis and bodies (2026-10-31). Changing Axis in Bend, Twist, Taper, Stretch or Flow refits Start and End to the bodies' extent along the new axis, about the triad where it is. Bodies picked on a new feature move the triad to their centre; editing a saved feature never moves it. The refit is a bounding box query on the UI thread, like the start defaults (D75). In an inch part the deform defaults are 0.0004 in (tolerance), 0.4 in (stretch distance) and 2 in (bend radius) instead of millimetre text read as inches. Other body tool forms still copy millimetre default text in inch parts (open).
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; a Twist about X used planes fitted to Z and turned the bar about 9 degrees instead of 90.

D615: Bend and Flow refuse folds through the body (2026-10-31). A Bend whose radius is smaller than the bodies' reach toward the bend centre, measured in the triad's frame, is an error: "would fold through themselves.
