Enter a smaller angle, a larger radius or move the triad." Flow compares the curvature along the used part of the curve with the bodies' box across the curve. Both use box corners, so they err on the safe side: a round rod on a curve whose radius is between r and 1.41 r can be refused when the bend direction is diagonal to the triad axes.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; these cases built self crossing solids that passed as valid.

D616: Mesh import tolerance (2026-10-31). OBJ files with Windows (CRLF) or old Mac (CR) line endings are read. A binary STL with extra bytes after the last triangle is accepted when the text "vertex" does not follow the header. Corners that are not numbers, damaged 3MF transforms and NaN or infinite corners raise a mesh import error with a next step instead of a kernel error or a silent hole.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; common files from Windows programs imported with "no triangles".

D617: STEP export always writes thread notes and units (2026-10-31). The coloured STEP writer, used by File, Export, dropped the cosmetic thread notes (P4.2, D314). Both writers now add them, and the coloured path sets the unit to millimetres explicitly.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; thread notes were lost on every export from the window.

D618: View tools follow the shown part, one side panel at a time (2026-10-31). When the user switches part tabs, Appearance closes, an open section panel closes as OK (the old part keeps its section), the Measure box stays open with its options and history and switches to the shown part's picks, units and planes, and Print Estimate refreshes. Closing a part forgets its section state. Appearance and the section panel are never open together: showing another side panel closes Appearance and closes the section panel as OK. A new section starts through the middle of the shown bodies, leaving out hidden bodies and bodies outside isolate (refines D580). The section drag arrow label uses the part's units.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; tools kept changing the part the user had switched away from, and two side panels broke each other.

D619: Appearance, Measure and isolate details (2026-10-31). Copy Appearance of a face takes the colour it is drawn in (face, then feature, then body, then part). Colours in use list face colours by the feature that made them with a count ("2 faces of Bracket"), not by internal face names; a colour on a deleted feature still shows its id. Measure leaves seam and degenerated edges out of a perimeter, and changing units, decimals or Show dX dY dZ redraws the result without adding to the history. Isolate leaves hidden bodies out of the picks; with none left it asks for a pick that is not hidden. Show All with one hidden body says "Showing the hidden body."
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10c bug hunt; wrong colours copied, internal names shown and wrong perimeters.

D620: Pieces of a split stay apart and do not warn as edge contacts (2026-10-31). Split and Split for Print leave pieces that share their cut face. (1) A boss feature fused with the whole part, and a fuse joins every body that touches another, so a boss on one piece joined the pieces back into one body. `combine` now fuses a boss only with the bodies it meets (box test, then a distance of at most 0.1 micrometre) when it meets some but not all bodies; bodies keep their order in the part. A part with one body, a boss that meets every body and a boss that meets none (a new separate body) work as before. (2) The zero thickness check flagged every edge and corner of the shared cut face, so every later solid feature warned that bodies touch only along an edge. Edges and corners that lie on an area where two bodies meet face to face (planar or cylindrical faces on the same surface whose common area is above zero) are no longer flagged. Two bodies that meet only along an edge are still flagged, also next to a face contact elsewhere. Found in round 10d (known issue).
Status: Default
Reason: The warning came on every feature after a split, and a boss on one piece silently undid the split.

D621: Split for Print picks the bodies to cut (2026-10-31). Split for Print cut every body its planes crossed. It now takes optional `refs.bodies` (a face of each body, like Split). The panel shows Bodies to Cut, a group with a tick box, when the part has more than one body; while it is ticked, faces clicked in the view pick bodies, else they are cut planes (planes mode). Ticked with no body picked, OK is refused with a message. Without picks every body is cut, as before. Each body is now cut on its own, as Split does, so overlapping bodies never cut each other, and auto planes come from the picked bodies' box. An edge click now says "Click faces: flat faces to cut at, or a face of each body to cut." instead of a message meant for projected curves.
Status: Default
Reason: Known issue: Split has a body picker and Split for Print had none.

D622: Printing tools treat split pieces as separate bodies (2026-10-31). (1) Lip and Groove: the grown rim outline came out inside out on the cut face of a split, so every lip or groove built there was invalid; the face is now rebuilt from the reversed wire when its area is negative. A rim face shared by two bodies (the cut face after Split for Print) gets the lip on the body it faces out of and the groove in the other body, so a lip and a groove picked on the same shared rim fit together; each lip and groove now fuses or cuts only the body of its rim. There is no control yet to swap which piece gets the lip (IDEAS.md). (2) Snap Hook and Mounting Boss join only the body of the face they stand on, so a tall hook or boss next to a wall no longer joins the pieces. (3) The build volume check measures each body on its own when the part has more than one (the pieces of Split for Print print separately); the message counts the bodies that fit or are too large. Lay Face Flat still turns all bodies together.
Status: Default
Reason: The normal print flow (shell, Split for Print, lip and groove, hooks, build volume check) failed or gave wrong messages.

D626: Configured values follow variable renames and deletes (2026-10-31). Renaming a global variable in the equations manager or the Variables tab moves its `var.<name>` overrides in every configuration, and its design table column, to the new name in the same undo step; deleting the variable drops them. Rows remember the name they had when the table or manager was filled, so swapping two names works. Formulas that use the old name are not rewritten (IDEAS.md). Overrides of a deleted feature stay in memory so undo restores them, but they are left out of the saved file and the configured value count (`configurations.owner_exists`, `kept_paths`), so the part saves as schema 1 again when nothing else is configured. Renaming a row in the design table renames that configuration in place. The equations manager's OK refuses a variable name that breaks the variable name rule; value errors are still applied (D390). The Variables tab solves with the whole part (core equations engine), so it accepts feature value names and keeps comments.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10d bug hunt: renames lost per configuration values, and the Variables tab blocked edits and dropped comments.

D627: Node editor and design table fixes (2026-10-31). (1) Unwired typed node inputs whose text is a formula are worked out again with the part's current variables on every run, as the Value node already did; when a node has a formula, the variable values are part of its result key. A formula that can no longer be solved is an error on the node. (2) Pasting an Add as Feature node adds its own graph body feature, and deleting the node deletes its graph body, each in one undo step (completes D378 item 3). (3) New graph body names skip names already in the tree. (4) Graph errors name nodes by their title, not their type name. (5) The search and settings column beside the canvas keeps at least 230 logical pixels. (6) Design table CSV import uses a semicolon or tab separator when the header row has no comma.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10d bug hunt: formula inputs gave stale geometry, pasted outputs did nothing, deleted outputs left broken features, settings were cut off.

D628: Array Along Curve fuses copies as separate tools and warns about skip numbers that do nothing (2026-10-31). (1) The copies of one operation still go into one boolean (PLAN 11.3 item 4), but each copy is passed to the kernel as its own tool through `combine(..., pieces=True)`, because the kernel never intersects the pieces of one compound argument with each other. Other callers of `combine` are unchanged; with several bodies the copies also go through the D620 rule (fuse only with the bodies they meet). (2) Instance 1 (the original), numbers above the count and skipping every copy each give a warning that says how to fix it. (3) Face picks for bodies to copy, and Projected Curve faces, pass on the "found by its position" warning like other features. Linear and circular patterns were not checked for the same overlap problem (BUG_HUNT round 10d, open).
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10d bug hunt: overlapping copies made wrong geometry, and skip numbers that do nothing were ignored silently.

D629: Curve directions from planes and axes, contours as paths (2026-10-31). (1) Contour Curves and Projected Curve take a plane, reference plane or reference axis feature as the direction, as well as a flat face or straight edge (PHASE3_SPEC P3.6 item 2). An axis gives its direction, and a contour counts its levels from the axis origin. (2) Both panels use the same direction list: planes and axes above the edited feature, never below it, plus a face or edge clicked in the view. The empty list prompt is "Plane, axis, flat face or edge", short enough not to widen the panel. (3) Contour curves are offered wherever curves are: the sweep path list and the composite curve items. (4) Each feature list in the curve panels shows its own prompt while empty.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10d bug hunt: an axis direction failed, the Projected Curve panel could not take a plane or axis, and the panel lists were inconsistent.

D623: Flat Pattern takes in cuts on flat walls (2026-10-31). A feature that is not sheet metal after the last sheet metal feature blocks flattening only when it changes the part in a way the flat pattern cannot show. Features that add no solid (planes, axes, points, sketches, curves) never block. When the part only lost material (Extruded Cut, Hole Tool, fillets and chamfers on walls), the removed material is cut from each wall in its own frame, as Fold does (D541), and the result is used only if the folded sheet model then has the same volume as the part. Added material blocks with the old message. A removal that reaches a bend or a form blocks with a message that says to cut across bends between an Unfold and a Fold. Other sheet metal features after such a cut still need to be moved above it.
Status: Default
Reason: Known issue: the Flat Pattern warned too often. The volume check proves the flat pattern matches the part.

D624: Panel tick boxes keep what the feature builds with (2026-10-31). In the shared form panels (`body_tools/form_widget.py`), a flag whose new feature default is on stores false when unticked, instead of being removed. When a saved feature has no value for a flag, the panel shows the feature type's own default, not the new feature default. A group tick that only the panel stores (sheet metal Own bend, Own relief, Base Flange Direction 2) starts ticked when the feature has values for any of the group's fields.
Status: Default
Reason: Opening a panel and pressing OK could change the part, and unticking Merge or Uniform did nothing.

D625: Sheet metal lengths in parts in inches, and a second sheet start (2026-10-31). A new Sheet Metal folder in a part in inches types its defaults as "1 mm"; a loaded gauge types its thickness and radius with " mm". Base Flange, Convert to Sheet Metal and Insert Bends refuse to start on a part that already has an active sheet start, with a status message. Flatten does nothing, with a message, when the Flat Pattern is suppressed or below the rollback bar. Edge Flange and Hem corner reliefs also clear the square between two reliefs when it would otherwise be a loose piece.
Status: Default
Reason: Gauge and default values are in mm, and typed text is read in the part's units on every rebuild. The other changes stop commands that could only fail or that would leave a loose body.
D630: Kernel view tests on Linux without a display (2026-10-31, round 10e). `test_edges_pick_within_a_few_pixels` builds the real kernel viewport. On Linux with no X display the kernel cannot open its display connection and the test failed in cloud containers. It now skips when `Aspect_DisplayConnection()` cannot be made. Windows and macOS need no display connection, so CI on both target platforms still runs it.
Status: Default
Reason: CLAUDE.md 9.8 says CI must never depend on a GPU or display; Linux is not a target platform but the suite runs there in cloud sessions.

D631: The UI thread gets a turn during long rebuilds (2026-10-31, round 10e). The kernel bindings keep Python's GIL for the whole of each kernel call, so while a rebuild runs every Qt call made from Python on the UI thread waits for the next kernel call to end. Opening `generated_200.fdprt` froze the window for 1.2 s to 3.3 s, mostly in the first paint of the new tab. `fdcad/ui/ui_turns.py` adds a heartbeat: while a rebuild is queued or running, a 15 ms timer on the UI thread records a beat. Between features the rebuild job checks it; when the last beat is older than 50 ms (and younger than 0.5 s, which means the UI thread is blocked rather than busy) the job sleeps in 2 ms steps for at most 0.1 s. `DocumentSession.wait` holds the heartbeat so a UI thread that waits on purpose never slows the rebuild. Worst gap is now about 0.2 s and the rebuild takes the same time. The kernel lock rules (D400) are unchanged: the job still runs under `@kernel_job`.
Status: Default
Reason: The window must stay responsive while a long rebuild runs (CLAUDE.md 5.2, round 10e brief). A single long kernel call (one boolean) still holds the GIL; that cannot be split from Python.

D632: Command tabs scroll sideways; compact labels and panel colour (2026-10-31, round 10e). (1) Each command tab's groups sit in a frameless `QScrollArea` inside `RibbonPanel`. When they do not fit, a thin scroll bar (one spacing step high, kept free under the captions on every tab so the height never changes) and the mouse wheel scroll the tab sideways. A scroll bar that comes and goes cannot change the height: the command tabs sit in a `QToolBar`, which does not lay out again when its widget's height hint grows. The main window's smallest width was 1330 px because of the Features and Sketch tabs, wider than a 1280 px screen (a 1920 px laptop at 150 percent), so the right side of the window was off screen. It is now about 490 px. `RibbonPanel` stays the tab widget, so code that looks up panels by object name is unchanged. (2) Compact buttons fixed their smallest width when made, before the style sheet's padding was applied, so a narrow window cut "Swept Boss" to "Sw...ss". `CompactButton.minimumSizeHint` now measures the longest tool of the group with the current padding each time. (3) The style sheet gave the panel colour only to the Features, Sketch and Evaluate tabs; every `RibbonPanel` now carries a `ribbon` property that the style sheet selects, so all seven tabs match.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10e bug hunt: the window must fit common laptop screens and labels must not be cut off.

D633: Closed parts and finished background jobs are freed (2026-10-31, round 10e). (1) Eleven kinds of background job (rebuild, feature preview, regions, sketch outlines and drag, measure, reference geometry preview, body tool counts and helpers, print tools) were started with `setAutoDelete(False)` and `pool.start(job)`. PySide then hands the Python job to Qt and never frees it, so every rebuild and every preview kept its document copy and the results it was given (with their shapes) until the app quit: about 0.5 MB per rebuild of `generated_200.fdprt`. `fdcad/ui/background.start_job` starts `job.run` instead; the pool frees its own task when `run` returns, and each caller still keeps the job until its result signal arrives. Jobs left on Qt's default auto delete were already freed and are unchanged. (2) Every `DocumentSession` is a child of the main window, and closing a tab never freed it: its undo history, last rebuild report with every shape, and the closed tab (held by the window's slots on the session's signals) stayed alive, about 8 MB per open and close of the 200 feature part. `DocumentSession.close()` now clears the undo stack, cache and report, disconnects the session's signals and drops the window's ownership; `close_tab` calls it. The session object is not deleted outright, because several panels keep a reference to the current session for a moment after its tab closes. (3) Print tool jobs connect closures that hold the job; their signal object is deleted when the job reports, which frees both.
Status: Default
Reason: CLAUDE.md 5A.3: never hold shapes or data longer than needed. Found while checking memory in round 10e.

D634: Damaged values never stop a part from opening silently (2026-10-31, round 10e). Changing one value at a time in sample files and opening them in the app found three escapes: (1) a configuration entry of the wrong type raised `TypeError` inside `fdef.load`; `from_json_data` now turns any `KeyError`, `IndexError`, `TypeError`, `AttributeError` or `ValueError` while reading into the usual "The file is damaged" message with its next step. (2) `appearance`, `print_setup` or `embedded` that is not an object loaded and then broke the feature tree; reading now rejects it as damaged. (3) A sketch dimension whose value is not a number raised in the quick value refresh that `DocumentSession.request_rebuild` runs on the UI thread, after the tab was added, so the part never rebuilt and no message showed. `_sketch_param` now skips such a value (the sketch reports its own error), and the quick refresh can no longer stop the rebuild from starting: the engine solves again in the background and reports any problem. After the fix, 770 damaged files opened from six samples gave no uncaught error.
Status: Default
Reason: The app must never crash or fail silently because a file is damaged (CLAUDE.md 5.7, 8.4).

D635: The first window size fits the screen (2026-10-31, round 10e). The main window always opened at 1400 x 900, so on a 1280 x 720 screen (a 1920 x 1080 laptop at 150 percent) it opened partly off screen. `start_size` keeps 1400 x 900 when the primary screen has room, and otherwise uses 95 percent of the available width and 90 percent of the available height. The window still does not remember its size between starts; that would be new behaviour and is not in the plan.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10e bug hunt: a new user on a small laptop screen must see the whole window.

D636: The installed app ships the node editor samples (2026-10-31, round 10e). The user guide (Node editor, Sample graphs) and the attractor plate tutorial tell the user to open samples from the `graphs` folder inside the samples folder, but `packaging/fdcad.spec` only shipped `samples/*.fdprt`, so the installed app had no such folder. The spec now ships `samples/graphs/*.fdprt` too, and the bundle check that the release workflow runs on the built app reports a missing graphs folder. File, Open Sample still lists only the top level samples, as before. The Windows installer and Mac bundle settings were checked and both register `.fdprt` and `.fdef`; no change was needed there.
Status: Default
Reason: Round 10e packaging review.

D637: Closed dialogs are freed (2026-10-31, round 10e). Preferences, New Part, About, Shortcuts, the Text dialog, the insert table, the configuration chooser and two question boxes were made with a parent and never deleted, so each use left its widgets alive. Preferences OK restyles every widget, so it slowed down the longer FDCAD ran: the slow app sweep (`test_every_command_on_every_sample[bracket]`) failed with Preferences OK taking 70 s after about 2,400 steps. Each now calls `deleteLater()` after its result has been read. `WA_DeleteOnClose` was not used, because several callers read the dialog's values after `exec()` returns. The Equations manager is freed when it closes; the Design Table, shortcut bar, view selector and snap popup free the previous one when a new one opens, so at most one of each stays (the window keeps the last one for code that looks at it).
Status: Default
Reason: Found by the round 10e slow test run.

D638: The app sweep frees closed widgets like the app does; Preferences OK restyles only on a theme change (2026-10-31, round 10e). The slow sweep `test_every_command_on_every_sample[bracket]` failed with Preferences OK taking 70 s. The sweep's `pump()` called only `processEvents()`, which never runs `deleteLater()` when no event loop is running, so every closed property panel, form and dialog stayed: about 25,000 widgets after 800 steps, and restyling them took 20 s or more. The app's own event loop does run those deletes, so the app was not affected by that part. `pump()` now also sends the deferred delete events, which keeps the sweep at about 1,200 widgets and makes it much faster. Separately, Preferences OK called `apply_theme` every time, which repolishes every widget twice (style, then style sheet); it now does so only when the theme changed.
Status: Default
Reason: Fix the failing slow test at its cause and remove a needless restyle.

D639: Python's garbage collector runs on the UI thread only (2026-10-31, round 10e). The slow right click sweep crashed with a segmentation fault: Python started a cyclic collection inside the background rebuild thread (it collects in whichever thread allocates) and destroyed Qt objects there while the UI thread was deleting widgets. Destroying Qt objects off their own thread is not safe, and the round 10e memory fixes (D633, D637) make more Qt objects freeable. `fdcad/ui/gc_guard.install()`, called when the main window is made, turns automatic collection off and runs `gc.collect` from a 500 ms UI timer whenever the generation counts pass Python's own thresholds. Objects without cycles are still freed at once by reference counting; only cycles wait up to half a second.
Status: Default
Reason: The app must never crash (CLAUDE.md 5.7). This is the usual remedy for Qt bindings, where only the UI thread may destroy widgets.
D640: Features tab order (RIBBON_SPEC R2, 2026-10-31). The Features tab has six groups: Sketch; Add Material; Remove Material (Extruded Cut, the Hole Tool dropdown with Thread and Cosmetic Thread, Revolved Cut, then Swept Cut and Lofted Cut stacked); Modify (Fillet dropdown with Chamfer, Pattern dropdown, a column Rib, Draft, Shell and a column Dome, Wrap, Mirror); Reference and Curves; Direct Editing (Move Face, Offset Face, Delete Face stacked). The Fasten and Pattern groups are gone. The Pattern dropdown holds Linear, Circular and Sketch Driven Pattern: FDCAD has no separate curve pattern command (Array Along Curve is in the Curves dropdown, as R2.5 says), and scope is frozen (D48), so none was added. The group title is "Reference and Curves", short enough not to make the group wider than its two buttons. The unused Phase 4 Features layout in `command_tabs/phase4_groups.py` is removed; it put the Hole Tool in one dropdown with the print features.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked why Draft hides under Shell; RIBBON_SPEC R1 and R2.

D641: R1 on the other tabs (2026-10-31). Bodies tab: Combine and Intersect share a dropdown (both join or overlap bodies); Move and Copy Body and Transform Handles are large; Split, Scale and Delete and Keep Body are a stacked column. Split and Scale were in dropdowns with tools that are not variants of them. 3D Print tab: Split for Printing and Mounting Boss are large; Snap Hook and Snap Hook Groove share a dropdown (a hook and its mating groove); Lip and Groove and Vent have their own buttons. Sketch tab dropdowns stay: each holds variants of one tool (lines, rectangles, circles, arcs, trim and extend, mirror, fillet and chamfer, sketch patterns), and Spline with Ellipse and Partial Ellipse counts as the curve kinds R1.2 allows. Sheet Metal, Evaluate and Graph have no dropdown that breaks R1; their layout data lives outside `command_tabs` and is unchanged, they only get the new drawing (D642).
Status: Default
Reason: RIBBON_SPEC says to apply R1 and R3 to every tab.

D642: How ribbon buttons are drawn (RIBBON_SPEC R3, 2026-10-31). Large and small buttons paint their own icon, label and dropdown arrow; the style draws only the background and frame, so the arrow no longer sits in the style's corner. Large button: icon, then a label area of two lines, then an arrow row of three spacing units that every large button keeps, so labels share one baseline and all arrows line up. The arrow is a small filled triangle centred under the label. Width is the icon or the longest label line of the group, plus one spacing unit and one pixel on each side, and the horizontal size policy is fixed. Small button: icon, label, then for a dropdown the arrow one spacing unit after the label, centred on it; all buttons in a column share the column's width and left edge. Text widths are measured with `QFontMetricsF` and rounded up, so labels are no longer cut off by rounding. Each group row has a stretch at both ends, so buttons keep their own width and stay centred under a wider title.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner said the dropdown buttons look uneven.

D643: Which part of a dropdown opens the list (RIBBON_SPEC R1.3, R3.1, 2026-10-31). On a large dropdown the strip from just above the label to the bottom (label and arrow) opens the list; the icon part runs the tool shown. On a small dropdown the area from just before the arrow to the right end opens the list; the icon and label run the tool. The button skips the style's own menu area so only these areas open the list. While the pointer is over the list area it gets a light tint in the highlight colour, so the two parts can be told apart.
Status: Default
Reason: R3.1 says the whole strip under the icon opens the list.

D644: Marking the shown tool in a dropdown list (RIBBON_SPEC R3.6, 2026-10-31). The list holds the window's own commands, so their icons, names and shortcuts show as in the menus. The tool the button shows gets a short rounded bar in the highlight colour at the left of its row. A check mark was not used because it would make the shared commands checkable, which would change them in the menus too.
Status: Default
Reason: R3.6 asks for the shown tool to be marked.
D650: One contrast helper and a list of pairs (2026-10-31, UI_POLISH_SPEC U1.7). `fdcad/ui/themes/contrast.py` has `ratio` (WCAG 2), `hue_gap`, `lightness` (CIE L*) and `pairs`, which lists every text, input and view colour pair of a theme with its lowest ratio: body text 7:1 on plain backgrounds, all other text 4.5:1 (including hover, selected and pressed fills), input outlines and view marks 3:1. `test_theme_contrast.py` fails if any pair of any theme is below its limit. New tokens: `Chrome.input_border` (inputs, spin boxes, check boxes and slider grooves; `border` stays for dividers) and in `Palette`: `preselection`, `face`, `silhouette`, `sketch_reference`, `handle_idle`, `view_text`, `mesh_reference`, `axis_x`, `axis_y`, `axis_z`, relation tag and label plate colours, and the view toolbar plate. The accent darkens to #1A63C2 in the light themes and lightens to #6EA8FF in the dark ones (also in `icons.ACCENT`), so accent text passes 4.5:1. Light and Beige view gradients end a little lighter, and the light state colours are a little darker, so they pass 3:1 on the view.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec listed measured misses in every theme; one helper keeps them fixed.

D651: Selection and pre-selection colours (2026-10-31, U1.4). Selection is burnt orange (#AD4200) in the light themes and amber (#FFD060) in the dark ones; pre-selection is deep teal (#00705F) and light mint (#7FF0D0). Both read at 3:1 on both ends of the view gradient. Against FDCAD's grey part (#B4BCC4) they reach 3:1 in the light themes; in the dark themes no colour can be 3:1 against both a dark background and a light grey face, so there the limit is 1.3:1 with the highlight lighter than the face, and highlighted edges are drawn thicker (pre-selection 2.5 px, selection 3 px) so selection does not rely on colour alone. Highlighted faces are filled with 15 percent transparency. The sketch tool preview, the box selection band and the filter cursor funnel use the selection colour.
Status: Default
Reason: The old orange was 1.67:1 on the Light view bottom, and the default kernel highlight was a pale grey outline.

D652: Fixed data colours live in the theme module (2026-10-31, U1.6). Colours that mean the same in every theme (draft, overhang, wall thickness and build volume maps; node editor category bands and port types; the cursor arrow) are `theme.DATA`, `theme.NODE_CATEGORIES` and `theme.NODE_PORTS`. A test fails on any hex colour or numeric `QColor` in a UI file except the theme module, the icon palette, the appearance swatches (user data) and the bundle check.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec asks that every colour comes from a theme token.

D653: How the 3D view draws (2026-10-31, U6). `fdcad/ui/viewport/look.py` holds the numbers: 4 sample MSAA (the kernel falls back quietly), smooth lines, per pixel shading, a key light (0.72), a fill (0.26) and ambient (0.30) that follow the camera so top, front and side of a box always get three clear shades, a 2 px outline (the kernel's silhouette option) and 1 px edges, both scaled with the screen's pixel ratio. The axis triad uses theme axis and text colours at 7 percent of the view height, and fits leave a 16 percent margin so it stays clear of the part. Standard views and Normal To turn the camera in 250 ms with ease in and out (`ViewportWidget.turn_ms`, set from the Animations preference, 0 turns at once). A mouse press or wheel ends a turn at once. The view redraws as soon as it starts, so there is no black first frame.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for a 3D view that looks like a top product.

D654: Edges and outline are two colours (2026-10-31, U1.3). `edge` is the colour of edges drawn on the faces and reads at 3:1 on the grey part in every theme (dark grey). `silhouette` is the outline around the part and reads at 3:1 on both ends of the view gradient (dark in the light themes, light grey in the dark ones). The spec asked for edges lighter than the faces in the dark themes; tried on screen, light edges disappeared into the lit faces, so the outline carries the contrast to the background and the edges keep the contrast to the faces.
Status: Default
Reason: Black edges vanished on the dark backgrounds, light ones vanished on the faces.

D655: Select Shapes highlights only the picked face or edge (2026-10-31). `ViewportWidget.select_shapes` made owners that were not marked as coming from a decomposition, so the kernel highlighted the whole part. They are now marked, like the owners made by a click.
Status: Default
Reason: Found while checking the new selection colours on screen.
D660: One type scale (2026-10-31). `ui/themes/typography.py` holds the four sizes of UI_POLISH_SPEC U2.1: captions and units 11 px, body 13 px, panel and group titles 13 px semibold, dialog titles 15 px semibold, all from the system UI font. The app font is set to the body size when a theme is applied. Sizes are stored as point sizes (pixels times 72 over the screen's logical dots per inch: 9.75 pt on Windows, 13 pt on macOS) so code that scales `pointSizeF()` keeps working. Widgets ask `type_font(role)` instead of picking a size; the sketch labels, gesture guide, node editor, About heading and panel titles now do. A test fails on any other font size in `src/fdcad/ui`, except the command tab caption (RIBBON_SPEC, another round), which scales the body size by 0.85 to the 11 px caption. Value fields, the sketch value box and the status bar coordinates use tabular figures (U2.4).
Status: Default
Reason: The owner asked for a product team finish; one scale is the base of it.

D661: FDCAD's own Qt style (2026-10-31). The app uses `ui/themes/app_style.AppStyle`, a proxy style on Fusion, instead of plain Fusion. It does what a style sheet cannot: it paints menu rows (D668), sets the layout gaps (D667), gives small tool buttons a 24 by 24 px hit area, tracks the mouse over scroll bars, names icon buttons (D665) and skips Fusion's dotted focus box where the style sheet draws a ring. It is installed once per app (`app.style()` returns Qt's style sheet wrapper, so the app carries a flag) and put back to plain Fusion when Python exits, because Qt can still call the style while widgets are destroyed after PySide has shut down.
Status: Default
Reason: Style sheets cannot colour the menu shortcut column, react to hovering a whole scroll bar or change layout metrics.

D662: Keyboard focus ring (2026-10-31). Every control shows a 2 px accent ring inside its corner radius when it has keyboard focus (U4.1). `FocusRing` listens to the app's focus changes and sets a `keyfocus` property on the new focus widget when the window has Qt's keyboard focus flag (set by Tab, Backtab and shortcuts) and no mouse button is down; a click on the widget or focus moving away clears it. Style sheet rules match `[keyfocus="true"]`, and drop the padding by 1 px so nothing moves. Text fields and spin boxes show the ring on any focus, since typing goes there. Item views ring their current row. The 3D view and the sketch editor draw over everything inside them, so their stack sits in a `view_focus` frame with a 2 px border that turns accent. Command tab buttons keep their own look (RIBBON_SPEC); their ID rules outrank the ring.
Status: Default
Reason: Focus must be visible for keyboard users without a ring after every mouse click.

D663: Control states and sizes (2026-10-31). `ui/themes/states.py` adds the U3 rules after the base style sheet, so they win where both set a property and the base rules stay as they were. Each control has normal, hover (a little fill), pressed (more fill), checked (the accent or the selected fill with an accent border), keyboard focus and disabled (muted text, 3:1 or more) looks: push buttons, tool buttons, check boxes, radio buttons (new), sliders (new), spin boxes (new, with chevron arrows), fields, tabs and rows. Corners are 4 px on buttons and fields and 6 px on menus, popups, tooltips and panels. Buttons, fields, check boxes and rows are at least 24 px tall; main buttons (the default button, dialog button boxes and the property panel header) are 28 px and filled with the accent. The hover and pressed fills of an accent button move toward the text colour, which always raises the contrast of the button text. Input outlines use an `input_border` token when the theme has one (round 11a adds it), else `border_strong`. The document tab close button is 24 by 24 px.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U3.1 to U3.3.

D664: Reduce motion (2026-10-31). Preferences, General has a Reduce motion box in place of Animate view changes. It is the same stored switch (`appearance/animations`), inverted, so code that reads `settings.animations` keeps working. `ui/themes/motion.py` holds the lengths (150 ms for panels and menus, 250 ms for the camera, ease in and out with no overshoot) and `duration(ms)`, which gives 0 while Reduce motion is on or while a rebuild has run longer than 300 ms. With Reduce motion on, Qt's menu, combo box, tooltip and tool box effects are turned off; turning it off puts back what the system had. The sketch turn asks `duration`. FDCAD has no other animations today.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U4.5 and U7; one switch must stop every animation.

D665: Accessible names (2026-10-31). A button without visible text (icon only tool buttons, arrow buttons) and a field without its own name get the first line of their tooltip, as plain text, as accessible name. The name follows later tooltip changes; a name set on purpose is never replaced. Fields in a form keep Qt's name from their label. The feature tree, property panel, side panel, variables, errors, document tabs, 3D view, sketch editor, view tools, status bar, quick actions bar and command search have names from `ui/strings_a11y.py`.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U4.3.

D666: States not by colour alone (2026-10-31). Tree marks now differ in shape: a triangle for a warning and a disc for an error, both with an upright bar, outlined in the panel colour so they stand off the row icon. Rows in the errors list show the warning or error icon beside the coloured text.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U4.4; the old marks were two dots of different colour.

D667: Spacing on the 4 px grid (2026-10-31). The style gives every layout that does not set its own numbers 16 px margins round a window, 12 px margins inside a panel and 8 px between items (Fusion gave 6 and 9 px). The property panel uses 12 px padding, 16 px between groups and 8 px between rows; the sketch panel header uses 12 px.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U2.2; setting it in the style fixes every dialog at once.

D668: Menu rows (2026-10-31). Every menu row is 28 px tall. A 16 px icon column is always kept, so labels line up with or without an icon; a checked row with no icon shows a tick there, and one with an icon gets an accent box round it. Shortcuts sit right aligned in the muted colour, and a submenu arrow column is kept in every row. The hover fill is the theme's hover colour with 4 px corners. Separators stay in the style sheet.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U3.4.
D670: Icon rules and the pixel grid (2026-10-31). `fdcad/ui/icons/audit.py` holds the icon rules of UI_POLISH_SPEC U5.1 and a test runs it on all 268 icons; `tools/icon_sheet.py --audit` prints the same report. Rules: a 24 by 24 frame with one root group (no fill, `currentColor` stroke, 1.5 wide, round caps and joins); every stroke 1.5 wide; shapes inside 2 to 22; only the theme placeholders; solid fills only for dots up to 5 units, larger areas a tint of 0.35 or less; secondary lines at least half opacity; dashes `1.5 3` (or `4 3 0.5 3` for centre lines); the accent never paints the whole icon. Pixel grid: a 1.5 unit stroke cannot be sharp at both 16 and 24 px, so horizontal and vertical lines sit on 0.75 + 1.5 k. That is one whole pixel at 16 px, two whole pixels at 32 px and three at 48 px, and at 24 px one edge is sharp instead of both being soft. Lines on the centre line 12 stay, so symmetric icons stay symmetric. Existing icons were moved onto the grid by a one off script that picks, per icon, the grid positions that keep the distances between lines and the symmetry about 12; 33 icons got small hand fixes (dots drawn as filled circles, heavy and hairline strokes made 1.5, shapes pulled inside 2 to 22, solid areas made tints, a few small icons drawn larger).
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U5.1 and U5.2; the old 16 px icons drew most lines as two grey half pixels.

D671: Icon colours come from the theme tokens (2026-10-31). `icon()` now fills `currentColor` with the theme's `text`, `#ACCENT` with `accent`, `#DANGER` with `danger` and the new `#WARNING` with the view palette's `state_warning`, for the theme in use, so Beige and Stealth icons match their themes instead of borrowing Light or Dark colours. The warning mark is drawn in the warning colour instead of the accent. Disabled icons are the whole drawing in the theme's disabled colour (a `disabled` chrome token when one exists, else `muted`) instead of the normal drawing at 40 percent opacity, so a disabled accent never shows as faded blue.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U5.4 and U1.8.

D672: A bolder app icon drawing for 16 to 32 px (2026-10-31). `app_icon_small.svg` is the same block with a drilled hole, drawn about a fifth larger on a full bleed tile with a larger hole. `tools/make_app_icon.py` uses it for the 16, 24 and 32 px images in the PNGs, `fdcad.ico` and `fdcad.icns`, and the window icon is built from pixmaps per size (Qt's SVG icon engine keeps only one drawing per icon). A test checks the committed installer icons match what the tool draws now.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U5.5: at 16 px the padded tile left the block about 9 pixels wide.

D673: Feedback and messages (2026-10-31). (1) Error boxes are one `ErrorMessage` (a message box): the plain message from the existing strings, OK as the default and Escape button, Show Details with the technical text (version, OS, what was being done, the trace) and a Copy Details button that copies it without closing the box. Open, Save and import read failures use it. (2) Rebuild and export progress shows in the status bar only when the work still runs after 300 ms, so quick rebuilds never flicker; rebuilds get a Cancel button that stops at the next feature. (3) Saved, exported and copied confirmations show in the status bar and go back to "Ready" after 5 seconds unless something newer was shown. (4) Empty places: a part with only its planes and origin shows a muted hint under the tree rows ("Start a sketch on a plane..."); an empty Recent Files menu shows a disabled "No recent files"; a command search with no match says so in its list (the row does not run). The Errors tab draws its warning mark plain while there are no problems and in the warning colour when there are. (5) Safe defaults: closing an unsaved part says the changes are lost and defaults to Save, which never loses work; deleting a feature that others use, deleting a rolled back feature with its dependents and discarding sketch changes default to No. Strings are in `strings_feedback.py`.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U8.

D674: Window memory and title (2026-10-31). The main window stores its geometry, its dock state (the left panel width) and whether it was maximised under `window/` in the preferences when it closes. At start the size and place are restored before the window shows; the panel width is restored in the same step that builds the panels, so nothing jumps. If no 100 by 20 pixel piece of the title bar would be on any screen (a monitor was unplugged), the window opens centred on the primary screen, shrunk to fit. The title is the file name with its extension, Qt's unsaved mark and the app name, for example "bracket.fdprt* Â· FDCAD" (macOS shows the mark as the dot in the close button); before any part opens it stays "FDCAD" and the version.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U9.1 and U9.3.

D675: Dark title bar on Windows (2026-10-31). In Dark and Stealth (and System when it is dark) FDCAD asks Windows for the dark title bar with `DwmSetWindowAttribute`, attribute 20, falling back to 19 for Windows 10 builds before 2004. It is set before the window first shows, so it never flashes light, and again after the theme changes in Preferences. macOS and Linux keep their native title bars, which follow the system.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U9.5.

D676: One handler for uncaught errors (2026-10-31). `ErrorHandler` replaces `sys.excepthook` and `threading.excepthook` at start (after the log file is set up). It writes the full trace to the log, then shows the plain message with Copy Details. The box opens window modal without a nested event loop, so the app keeps running; while it is open, further errors only go to the log. Errors on worker threads are logged at once and shown on the UI thread. The log only setup hook stays as the fallback before the UI starts.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U10.1.

D677: Qt messages, diagnostics and the About box (2026-10-31). (1) At start, Qt's messages go to the log through `qInstallMessageHandler`, under the `fdcad.qt` logger (debug messages are below the log level). A test builds the main window, opens every left panel tab and the Preferences, About, Keyboard Shortcuts, Welcome and user guide windows, and fails on any Qt warning, except the offscreen test platform's own "This plugin does not support ..." notices. (2) Help > Diagnostics has Copy System Info (version, build, OS, Python, Qt, PySide6, OCP, the Qt platform, OpenGL version, GPU and vendor from a small offscreen context, every screen with its scaling, the theme and the log folder) and Open Log Folder. (3) The About box shows the build date, the log folder and an Open Log Folder button. The build date is the date of the app file in an installed build (installers keep file dates); from source it says "Running from source". No build step had to change.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U10.2, U10.3 and U9.4.

D678: Developer overlay (2026-10-31). Preferences, General has "Show frame and rebuild times in the view (for developers)", off by default (`developer/overlay`). When on, each part shows a small label at the lower left of its 3D view with the last frame time and the last rebuild time, refreshed twice a second. The frame time is how long the view took to handle its last paint event from Qt; redraws the view does itself during a drag are not timed, so it reads low while rotating. It uses only theme tokens, the caption size and tabular figures.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U10.4.

D679: Clean start (2026-10-31). The start already shows the empty, themed window first and builds the heavy panels in one step after it (PLAN 11.3), so no half built panel is ever painted. This round adds the restored size, place and panel width (D674) and the Windows title bar colour (D675) before the window shows, so the first frame is already right. No splash screen was added: the window itself appears well within the 1 second the spec allows, and a splash would only add a second window that flashes.
Status: Default
Reason: UI_POLISH_SPEC U9.2.

D680: File types for assemblies and drawings (2026-11-01). Owner decision: assemblies are saved as `.fdasm` and drawings as `.fddrw`, next to parts in `.fdprt`. Assemblies and drawings are still out of scope (D48); this only fixes their names so every future spec and the installer's file associations use them. Both will be text files in the same family as `.fdprt` (FDEF_SPEC), with their own schema version.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner request while planning the post 1.0 phases (assemblies, drawings).

D681: Rounds and chamfers that run into each other (2026-11-02, owner report). Two rounds on the edges of a face narrower than their radii are each valid, but together the solid crosses itself; the old local check (D77) only looked at the new faces and edges, so a broken sliver was shown with no error. Fillet and Chamfer now also run the whole shape check (`breaks_solid`, a few milliseconds at 200 faces) and treat a result that fails it as a failure, but only when the part passed it before, so an already invalid part is not blamed on them. The usual pinpointing then keeps the edges that fit and offers the fixes. Their messages now name edges by their place ("edge 2"), not by stored names, like D589 item 4.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner part: a 20 mm tube, its end chamfered down to a 1 mm ring, the ring filleted at R2.

D682: What standard views and Zoom to Fit frame (2026-11-02, owner report). With a part shown they fit the part, the shown sketches and the preview, and leave out planes, axes, labels and the origin, which are helpers drawn around the part and made a small part sit small and off centre. An empty part still frames everything shown. A Shift and arrow quarter turn also moves the view so the middle of the part is in the middle, keeping the zoom; plain 15 degree arrow turns and Ctrl panning stay as they were.
Status: Default
Reason: A 20 mm tube was small and off centre after Isometric and after Shift and arrow turns.

D683: Tutorial review items approved (2026-11-02, owner). The owner approved every item in docs/TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC.md (TR1 to TR34), including the three marked for an owner decision (TR7 3D sketch, TR31 IGES import and healing, TR34 sketch blocks). They are now PLAN.md Phase 7A (v1.2), built in priority order. This widens scope as D48 allows only with owner approval; surface building tools stay out of scope, so TR31 joins and heals imported surfaces but does not add surface features. TR22 keys: Ctrl+Tab goes to the next open part tab (Control+Tab on Mac); going to the previous one has no default key, because Ctrl+Shift+Tab already shows all hidden bodies and Ctrl+Page Up and Down change command tabs; it can be set in the shortcut editor. The items are built by implementer sessions that never read reference/ (CLAUDE.md section 10); the manager session that wrote the spec does not build them.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner reply "accept all things you found" after the tutorial review.

D684: Move, Copy, Rotate, Scale and Stretch Entities (2026-11-02, TR1). Choices the spec left open: (1) One flow for all five: click entities (or start with them selected), then click the base point (Rotate: the center); with picks, a click on a point snap or on empty space sets the base point and a click on a curve adds or removes it. The base and target use the usual snaps. There is no From and To or Delta switch: Delta X and Y (Rotate: the angle) follow the cursor from the base point, so the value labels show them live; a typed value holds while the cursor moves, and Enter applies it without a click. Rotate and Scale also have Center X and Y (Base X and Y) fields, so a typed center works. (2) Rotate measures the angle from the X direction through the center. Scale has a Scale factor field (default 2) and applies on a click or Enter once the base point is set. Rotate has no Copy option; Copy Entities and Scale with Copy do. (3) Stretch picks only with a crossing box (drag, or click two corners); a selection made before it starts is ignored, because a box is what says which points move. (4) Relations and dimensions are sorted by the points they use: all still, kept; all moving, kept, except that a turn drops Horizontal, Vertical and horizontal or vertical distances (a quarter turn swaps them) and a scale scales length dimensions and offset values; some moving and some still, removed and named in the status bar. Dimensions follow the same rule as relations. Stretch keeps a relation or dimension on a curve that crosses the box when it still holds afterwards (axis, parallel, perpendicular, collinear and coincident relations are checked; dimensions are measured), so a stretched rectangle stays a rectangle and only the changed size dimension goes. (5) A scaled dimension's typed text becomes its new value in millimetres; an equation in it is not kept. (6) After each change the tool keeps its picks and asks for a new base point, so the same entities can be moved again; Escape steps back from the base point to the picks to the end of the tool. (7) The five commands share one dropdown in the Sketch tab's Modify group, in Convert Entities' old place; Convert Entities moved beside Sketch Picture so the tab keeps its width. No default keys. (8) Tool panels got a plain number field kind (`number`) for the scale factor.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR1.

D685: Copy and paste of sketch entities, sketches and features (2026-11-02, TR3 and TR9). Choices the spec left open: (1) Keys: Edit, Copy (Ctrl+C) and Edit, Paste (Ctrl+V) are window commands. An open sketch with focus takes the keys for its own entities; the node editor with focus gets them through the same commands, so Copy Nodes and Paste Nodes lost their own default keys (two commands may not share a key). (2) In a sketch the copy is placed by the middle of its extent at the cursor; the click that places it ends the paste and selects the copy. The clipboard holds plain sketch data in FDCAD's own format and is read as data only, so copies also go between parts. (3) A copied sketch keeps its entity ids, so a pasted feature's references into its sketch (a revolve axis, hole points) still work; the feature's other references (faces, edges, end conditions) are kept as they are and show the usual errors if they do not fit. (4) Part links: entities that copy part geometry (they carry a `source`) cannot carry over. A pasted sketch (TR3.2) drops the construction copies with every relation and dimension that names them and takes the Fix off drawn curves copied from the part; the status bar gives the count. For a pasted feature (TR9.2) FDCAD asks: Keep leaves the copies as fixed geometry where they are, without their link, so the sketch keeps its shape and place; Remove drops them as above. (5) Placement: a pasted sketch keeps its coordinates (origin on the new plane's origin, as TR3.2 says). A pasted feature on a face, with Remove, is centered on the face (its stored middle, or the drop point for Ctrl and drag), and relations and dimensions to the sketch origin are removed so they do not pull it back; with Keep or on a plane it keeps its coordinates. Without this the copy often landed off the new face. (6) Paste onto the selected plane or flat face, else the plane picker asks for one. Only sketches and features made from a sketch (a `sketch` reference) can be copied in the part; anything else gets a status note. (7) The sketch and its feature are added as one undo step, at the insert point (above the rollback bar when rolled back).
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR3 and TR9.

D686: Hidden Lines Visible (2026-11-02, TR13). The style uses the same hidden line computation as Hidden Lines Removed, with the kernel's hidden line drawing turned on: hidden edges are dashed, 1 px wide (scaled for high DPI), in the theme's edge colour faded 40 percent toward the view background, so they read lighter in every theme. Default key Shift+H (free; H alone hides bodies). It sits between Hidden Lines Removed and Wireframe in the View menu, the view toolbar's style list and the right click Display Style menu.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR13.

D687: Next and previous part (2026-11-02, TR22). Commands Next Part (Ctrl+Tab, Control+Tab on Mac, keys set in D683) and Previous Part (no default key) step through the open part tabs and wrap round. Their keys work while focus is in the document area (3D view, sketch canvas) or the feature tree, so text fields and the node editor keep Ctrl+Tab for their own use. With one part open they do nothing. No icons: they are keyboard commands, like the command tab steps.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR22.

D688: Midpoint Line (2026-11-02, TR4). The middle is a construction point placed with the first click's snap relations (so a click on the origin ties it there), with a Midpoint relation to the line. The clicked end takes its snap relations; the mirrored end is free. The end gets the Line tool's direction snaps (horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular) and their relation. A typed length is the whole length, so the end goes half of it from the middle, and it adds the usual length dimension. The tool sits in the Line dropdown after Centerline, with no default key; it draws one line per pair of clicks, no chain.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR4.

D689: Save Image (2026-11-02, TR24). File, Save Image (no default key) asks for the size (the view's size in device pixels, or a typed width and height from 1 to 8000) and whether to include the background, then for a PNG file name. The kernel draws the view off screen at that size, so a chosen size needs no window resize and keeps the camera's framing (the aspect is adjusted, not stretched). Without the background the view is drawn twice, on solid black and on solid white, and each pixel's opacity is taken from the difference (whole array numpy), so smooth edges keep a soft outline; the axis triad is left out of such images. Selection and pre-selection highlights are drawn as on screen.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR24.

D690: Dimetric, Trimetric and saved views (2026-11-02, TR14). (1) Dimetric looks from (1, 0.5, 1): the front and side are seen alike and the top smaller. Trimetric looks from (0.56, 0.42, 0.72), the same direction feature panels already turn to (new_feature.TRIMETRIC), so the two match. Y up, fitted like the other standard views; no default keys; they are in the View menu, the view toolbar list, the right click View Orientation menu, the command list and as two buttons in the view selector. (2) Saved views store the full camera (target, direction, up, eye distance and scale) in the part file's optional `views` key (FDEF_SPEC 2 item 14). Names are unique ignoring case, up to 60 characters; Save View suggests "View 1", "View 2" and so on. Going to a saved view puts the camera back exactly (no fit), so a zoomed in detail view stays zoomed. (3) Saving, updating, renaming and deleting are undo steps that mark the part modified but do not rebuild. (4) Saved views are listed after the standard views in the View menu (a Saved Views submenu with Manage Saved Views), the view toolbar's views list and View Orientation; the manage dialog has Go To, Update, Rename and Delete.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR14.

D691: Split Entities (2026-11-02, TR2). (1) The two pieces share one sketch point (the same point id at the end of one and the start of the other), so it can be dimensioned and dragged as one point; the solver handles shared points (checked with an ellipse split into two partial ellipses). Two lines get Collinear; two arcs share their centre point, which keeps them on one circle without an Equal relation (that would be redundant); two partial ellipses share the centre and axis points. (2) The original keeps its id and its relations, except those that held its size (length dimensions, Equal, Midpoint, Symmetric, Fix), which go and are named in the status bar, as Trim does. (3) Circles and ellipses take two clicks on the same curve. (4) Splines are split at the nearest through point between their ends, which the pieces share with its tangent handle, so the shape does not change; splitting between through points would change the curve, so it is not offered. (5) Deleting a split point joins the pieces back when exactly two curves of the same kind meet there end to end, they continue each other (collinear lines, arcs on one centre, partial ellipses of one ellipse, splines sharing the point and handle) and no relation or dimension names the point; two arcs or partial ellipses that meet at both ends join back into the full circle or ellipse. Otherwise Delete works as before. (6) The tool is in the Trim and Extend dropdown, no default key.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR2.

D692: Tree folders and feature comments (2026-11-02, TR23). (1) Both live in the part file's optional `tree` key (FDEF_SPEC 2 item 15), not in the features, so adding or editing them never makes the part rebuild. (2) A folder stores its member ids; the tree shows a member in the folder only while it sits next to the others among the top level rows (from the first member to the first gap), so a moved feature simply leaves it. Deleted features' ids stay in the data harmlessly (ids are never reused) and drop out when the folders next change. (3) To pick neighbours the tree now takes Ctrl and Shift click (extended selection); everything else still acts on the current row. Add to New Folder refuses rows that are not next to each other with a message. New folders are named Folder 1, Folder 2 and so on; names are unique ignoring case. A feature put in a new folder leaves its old one. (4) Folder rows open and close (kept while FDCAD runs, not saved), rename in place (F2 or double click), and right click offers Rename and Remove Folder; Delete on a folder row removes the folder and keeps its features. A folder never crosses the rollback bar or a node graph row: members after one start a new row with the same name. (5) A comment is plain text up to 2000 characters, edited with Comment... in the right click menu; the row's icon gets a small accent dot (left off when an error or warning mark is shown) and the text joins the row's tooltip. (6) Each change is one undo step that marks the part modified.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR23.

D693: Temporary axes (2026-11-02, TR17). (1) View, Temporary Axes (a toggle for all open parts, not saved, no default key) draws one dash and dot line per axis of the part's cylindrical and conical faces, in the edge colour on the top layer, so the part does not hide it. Faces on the same axis (split half cylinders, a counterbore and its hole) share one line, which runs over their length and 15 percent (at least 5 mm) past each end. The lines are recomputed when the part is shown after a rebuild. (2) Clicking a line selects its round face, so every panel that takes an axis from a cylinder or cone face (circular pattern, reference axis and plane through an axis) works unchanged. Revolve and Revolved Cut now also take a round face as the axis, when its axis lies in the sketch plane; otherwise the error says to pick an axis in the sketch plane or a sketch line. (3) In a sketch opened while they are on, each axis seen on the sketch plane (not square to it) is added to the part geometry the sketch snaps to and draws; a snap to one ties to a fixed copy that is not linked to the part, since an axis is not an edge with a name.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR17.

D694: Replace From File (2026-11-02, TR11). The import feature keeps its id, name, tree place and options; only its `source` points at a new embedded block (a new block id, never reusing the old one). The old block is removed when no other feature reads it, and comes back on undo, so the file never keeps an unused copy. A STEP import takes .step or .stp, a mesh import .stl, .3mf or .obj; changing the kind would change the feature type, so it is refused with a message. The file is read on the UI thread as bytes only; reading the geometry stays in the rebuild (rule 2), and the import report shows in the status bar after it, as for a new import. Lost references on later features are the usual D116 errors.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR11.

D695: Insert DXF (2026-11-02, TR5). (1) No new dependency: a small DXF reader of FDCAD's own (`core/sketch/dxf_import.py`) reads ASCII DXF group codes, the ENTITIES section and `$INSUNITS`; binary DXF is refused with a message. It reads LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, LWPOLYLINE and POLYLINE (with bulges, as arcs), ELLIPSE (full or partial) and SPLINE; splines pass through the file's fit points, or its control points when it has none, so a spline drawn only from control points comes out close to, not exactly, the original. Blocks (INSERT), text, dimensions, hatches and 3D entities are skipped and counted. Arcs with a downward extrusion are mirrored. (2) Units: the file's unit when it gives one (the first choice), else the user chooses (mm first). The scale multiplies on top. (3) The geometry is placed with the paste tool of D685: it follows the cursor, held by the base point (the drawing's origin or the middle of its extent), and a click adds it as one undo step. Ends closer than 0.000001 mm are joined with Coincident; nothing is fixed or dimensioned. (4) A file with nothing to insert, or that is not DXF, says so in the status bar. The command sits in the Sketch Tools group under Sketch Picture, no default key.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR5.

D696: Sheet metal small options (2026-11-02, TR30). (1) Link to thickness is an optional `link_thickness` flag of Extrude (cuts and bosses alike in the core; the panel shows it for cuts in parts that have sheet metal features). With Blind, the depth used is the thickness of the last good sheet before the feature; the typed depth stays stored and comes back when the flag is turned off. Without a sheet above it the feature errors with what to do. (2) Edge Flange position `offset` with `offset_distance` (default 5 mm, zero or more) and `offset_rule` (material inside, material outside or bend outside): the bend's setback is the rule's setback at the edge plus the distance, so the whole flange moves that far in. (3) Miter Flange `propagate`: the picked edges plus every edge joined smoothly to them, walking only through straight edges (the existing tangent chain with a straight only mode), so it stops at a corner that is not tangent, at a cut and at a curved edge, which a miter flange cannot follow. The added edges must still form one chain on one face, with the usual messages if not.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR30.

D697: Bodies a feature acts on (2026-11-02, TR33). (1) `bodies_scope` ("all", the default and the old behaviour, or "selected") with `refs.bodies`, one face reference per body (D233 item 1). With Selected bodies the picked bodies are combined with the tool on their own and the rest of the part is added back unchanged, so a cut through two bodies cuts only the picked one, and a boss joins only the picked bodies even where it touches others. Picking every body is the same as All bodies. Selected with no picks is an error. A boss with Merge result off keeps its own body as before and ignores the box. (2) Extrude, Revolve, Sweep, Loft (cuts and bosses) and the Hole Tool support it in the core. (3) The panel shows the box only when the part has two or more bodies before the feature (or the feature already uses Selected bodies). While Selected bodies is chosen, clicks in the view go to the box; any face of a body adds that body once, listed as Body 1, Body 2 and so on.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR33.

D698: Named dimensions and Show All Dimensions (2026-11-02, TR32). (1) A sketch dimension keeps its name in an optional `name` key of the dimension (FDEF_SPEC 6); a feature value in the feature's optional `value_names` key (value to name). Both are left out when unused, so older files save unchanged. Names follow the variable name rule (a letter, then letters, digits or underscores) and must not clash with another value or name of the same feature. (2) Formulas name a named value `"wall@Shell 1"`; the automatic name (`"thickness@Shell 1"`, `"d1@Sketch 1"`) and the id forms keep working as aliases, so naming never breaks an older formula. The equations manager lists the name; design table headers show "name (feature)" with the column path as tooltip (columns are still stored by path). (3) Renaming a named value rewrites every quoted use of the old name in formulas (variables, feature values, sketch dimensions, suppression, configuration overrides and design table cells), in the same undo step: the general Edit (replace feature) command looks for renamed values, so it works for sketch edits and panel OK alike. Going from the automatic name to a new one needs no rewrite. (4) The names are set in the sketch Dimension panel's Name field (a sketch undo step) and with Name This Value... on the right click menu of a feature panel's value fields (stored on OK). (5) Show All Dimensions (View menu and the part row's right click menu, a toggle kept while FDCAD runs) shows the values of every built feature at once, each once, with the usual double click editing; a named value's label reads "wall = 2.00".
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR32.

D699: Split View (2026-11-02, TR16). (1) The extra views are panes with their own kernel view on the main 3D view's viewer and interactive context, so they show the same part, previews and highlights, and a pick in any pane is the one shared selection (sent to the window as a pick in the main view). (2) The main view is the top left cell of a grid it sits in from the start, so a split never moves its native window; panes are added and removed around it. Layouts: one view, two side by side, two stacked, four. Four views start as Front (the main view), Top, Right and Isometric; two views keep the main camera and start the second as Isometric. The layout is per part tab and not saved. (3) The view clicked last is the active view. It takes the standard views, Normal To, Zoom to Fit and Redraw; other view commands (zoom to area, previous view, section, display style, which applies to the whole part) and the arrow key turns act on the main view, which owns the drag handles, value labels and Select Other. Panes navigate with the middle button (Ctrl pans, Shift zooms) and the wheel, and pick with a left click (Ctrl adds). (4) Commands One View, Two Views Side by Side, Two Views Stacked and Four Views in View, Split View; no default keys. Without a 3D view (the test platform) the status bar says so.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR16.

D700: Gusset and normal cut (2026-11-02, TR12). (1) Gusset (`gusset`, refs `walls`: one face on each wall the bend joins) works in the bend's cross section: the rib fills the inside corner between the inner bend surface and either a straight line (Flat) or the circle that touches both walls (Round), meeting each wall `depth` from the bend's tangent line; it runs `width` along the bend, centred `rib_position` from the bend's middle (0 by default; past either end is an error). The outside gets the same shape pressed in, moved out of the corner by the sheet thickness along the line that halves the bend, so the sheet keeps its thickness at the rib's middle and is only close to it elsewhere. The press is cut from the whole folded part and the rib then added (new part level lists in the sheet model, folded only). The outline uses true arcs, so the round faces are smooth. (2) The flat pattern skips the gusset unless Cut out in the flat pattern is ticked; then a slot of the rib's width across the bend strip and `depth` onto each wall is cut from the flat pattern only (a flat only cut list in the sheet model). (3) Normal cut (`normal_cut`, true by default, stored only when false): an Extruded Cut in a sheet metal part, while the sheet model is current (no plain feature since the last sheet metal feature), meets the cut tool with each wall's middle plane and cuts that outline straight through the wall, as a wall cut in the sheet model, so later sheet metal features and the flat pattern include it. A cut that reaches a bend, or is made while bends are unfolded, keeps the plain cut, which the flat pattern already takes in exactly by wrapping it round the bend (D541). Cut Outside and Selected bodies keep the plain cut. Off gives the plain cut. Cuts in parts that are not sheet metal are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: TUTORIAL_REVIEW_SPEC TR12.

D701: Phase 7B Stage 1 comes before the rest of Phase 7A (2026-11-02, owner). The audit defects in PLAN.md Phase 7B Stage 1 are built before the Phase 7A items still open (TR6, TR7, TR8, TR10, TR15, TR18 to TR21, TR25 to TR29, TR31, TR34), because several of them give wrong results with no warning: a face reference that silently moves to another face, a unit change that rescales the model, a twisted sweep with the wrong volume, splines dropped from paths. Stage 1 follows the order in docs/PHASE7B_BRIEF.md; item 1 (topological naming) goes to an Opus subagent (CLAUDE.md section 1A). The open Phase 7A items follow Stage 1 and are then built together with Phase 7B Stage 2. Audit items that turn out wrong when checked are recorded here and skipped (brief rule 3).
Status: Default
Reason: Owner instruction on 2026-11-02 to fix silent wrong results first.

D702: A unit change keeps every value (2026-11-02, audit D3 item 1, PLAN.md section 7 item 1). Of the two fixes the brief offers, Change Units rewrites the texts instead of storing a unit per value, so the file format does not change and files saved before the fix open with the same geometry. Before the unit switches, every length whose value depends on the part unit is rewritten in the same undoable command (`core/equations/unit_change.py`): a bare number gets the old unit ("25" becomes "25mm", "2" in an inch part becomes "2in"); a formula whose result is a plain number is multiplied by one old unit ("=Count*5" becomes "=(Count*5)*1mm"); any other text that mixes bare numbers and units outside a formula ("1/4in + 2") becomes its value in the old unit. A rewrite is checked by evaluating it again in the new unit; if it does not give the same value, the value itself is written with the old unit. Texts that already carry a unit, angles, plain numbers and texts with errors are left as typed. Places covered: feature values, sketch dimensions, global variables, configuration overrides, design table cells and graph node formulas (graph inputs typed without a formula keep their stored value already). New bare numbers typed after the switch use the new unit (D66).
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D3 item 1; keeps the FDEF format unchanged.

D703: Twisted sweep (2026-11-02, spec 2 section 19 item 1, audit E item 1; amends D219 item 2). The auxiliary spine is now used in the kernel's plane mode (each section lies in the plane square to the path, turned toward where that plane meets the spine) instead of the curvilinear mode, which in this kernel version distorts the sweep: +0.16 percent at 20 mm, -5 percent at 70 mm and failure at 100 mm, all reported OK. With the plane mode the volume matches area times length to about 1.5e-5 at 90 degrees and better at larger turns, on straight and bent paths. The spine is sampled evenly by length (49 points), kept square to the path, and placed at half the tightest bend radius of the path (at most the path length), so each section plane meets it once; before, a spine one path length away failed on a bend at 720 degrees. Its fit tolerance is 1e-7 mm. A guard test keeps the plane mode. New golden sample `twisted_sweep`: a 4 by 8 mm bar swept 60 mm with a 90 degree twist, exact volume 1920 mm3. The old 1 percent sweep test is now 1e-4.
Status: Default
Reason: Spec 2 section 19 item 1; the kernel fix is not released yet.

D704: Face merge fallback (2026-11-02, spec 2 section 19 item 2, audit E item 2). Every face merge after a boolean goes through `core/unify.py`: when the kernel's merge raises, gives nothing, or makes a face or edge that fails the kernel check, the unmerged shape is kept (valid, with extra seams) and names are not carried. Only the faces and edges the merge made are checked, so large parts stay fast. Sites: the shared boolean merge, sheet metal, mesh import, node editor booleans, hole slots, partial fillet corners and the draft parting line. Two stacked ruled cones of the same taper reproduce a merge that raises. The fallback also changed one golden result: the node editor `lattice_block` sample merged into an invalid solid whose volume was 0.8 percent low (4770.36 instead of 4809.71 mm3, both by the precise volume); the golden file now holds the valid unmerged body (193 faces instead of 167).
Status: Default
Reason: Spec 2 section 19 item 2.

D705: Volume check after booleans, and the fillet crash guard (2026-11-02, spec 2 section 19 items 3 and 4). (1) After each boss or cut in the shared boolean, the result's volume must lie between the larger input and the sum (boss) or between the body less the tools and the body (cut), with a margin of 1 percent of the total because the quick volume can be that far off on B-spline faces. Outside it the feature fails with "the kernel gave a result of the wrong size". Inputs that are inside out are not judged. The volume of the last result is kept, so the next feature does not measure its body again. Bodies with more than 100 faces skip the check, because measuring a large body after every feature put the 200 feature sample over the rebuild budget (PLAN.md section 11, about 0.6 s on 1.8 s); a check over only the changed faces was tried and dropped, because the kernel's volume of open faces is zero for single flat faces and wrong for some curved ones. Whole body validity after fillets and chamfers was already checked; booleans keep the new face and edge check of D77. (2) A guarded worker process for fillets is not built: every fillet would copy the whole body to another process, and the loft corner case has no reproduction in FDCAD yet. It is recorded in IDEAS.md for when a reproduction exists. A guard test keeps fillet radii on point tables and the two radius form, never kernel law functions (item 5).
Status: Default
Reason: Spec 2 section 19 items 3 to 5, inside the rebuild budget.

D706: Splines and ellipses in paths and sketch tools (2026-11-02, spec 2 section 20 item 2, audit D2 items 1 to 4, audit A item 8). (1) Path chains (sweep, pipe, thin feature, rib) are built from the same exact edges as profiles, so lines, arcs, partial ellipses and open splines join end to end, and a circle, full ellipse or closed spline is a chain on its own. A spline only path failed with an index error before. (2) The shared sketch curve helper (composite and projected curves, flow, array along curve, contour, node editor model references) raises a feature error naming a curve it cannot turn into an edge, instead of leaving it out. (3) A sketch with crossing curves is split into the groups of joined curves that take part in a crossing and the rest. The rest (splines and ellipses included) is built as a sketch without crossings and added to the regions of the crossing part. When the two overlap, the sketch fails with the existing advice to trim the crossing curves, because joining region faces with freeform loops would need exact crossing formulas for splines (D278). Region picking with freeform curves in the crossing part stays refused. (4) Offset, Mirror, Trim, Extend, the sketch patterns, Sketch Fillet and Sketch Chamfer still work on lines, circles and arcs only (TR42 and TR48 in Phase 7B add more): a click on a curve they cannot use now says "<tool> works on <kinds> only, so it cannot use that curve. Pick <one> instead." Offset's Select Chain says when the chain goes on into a spline or partial ellipse.
Status: Default
Reason: Spec 2 section 20 item 2; refuse with a message where support is a later item.

D707: Flat sweep paths keep the section square to their plane (2026-11-02, amends D219 item 2). Twist None used the kernel's Frenet frame, which turns the section over where a flat spline changes the way it bends: a 2 mm round section swept along such a spline gave 72.1 mm3 instead of 80.4 mm3, reported OK. For a curved path that lies in a plane, None now holds the section's up direction to that plane's normal (the kernel's fixed binormal mode), which is the same solid as before for paths that bend one way only. Straight paths and 3D paths keep the Frenet frame.
Status: Default
Reason: Found while testing spline paths for D706.

D708: Pasting into another part (2026-11-02, audit D3 item 3, E item 7.8; amends D685). The clipboard records which open part a copy came from (process and document, so a copy from another run of FDCAD counts as another part). Pasting into a different part: (1) every reference other than the feature's own sketch is cleared, because face and edge names are per part, and the status bar names the cleared keys and says to edit the feature and pick them again; a feature that needs them then fails with its own "pick" message instead of using an unrelated face; (2) every formula of the feature and its sketch (values, dimensions, the suppression rule) becomes its value with a unit, because names such as "d1@Sketch 1" or a variable may mean something else there; (3) ties to part edges are removed without asking.
