In the same part, picks and formulas are kept as before. In both cases references into the copied sketch (a revolve axis line, hole points) now follow the pasted sketch instead of the original. Remapping faces by geometry was not chosen: the target part has no record of where the source faces were, so any match would be a guess (PLAN.md section 6 item 6). The note is kept through the rebuild that follows, which used to replace it at once.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D3 item 3; never guess a reference silently.

D709: Limits for damaged and hostile files (2026-11-02, audit D12 items 1 to 8, D item 3). (1) 3MF tags are matched in one pass with possessive repeats and the attributes in any order, so a damaged tag cannot make the pattern backtrack: a sample the old patterns took 42 s on reads at once; no XML parser is added. (2) A 3MF package may hold at most 10000 files and its model may unpack to at most 1 GB, by the size the zip states (Python's zip reader never reads past it). (3) Embedded blocks unpack in steps to at most 1 GB and sketch pictures to at most 256 MB; the picture path now has the base64 check and says to insert the image again. (4) ASCII STL with a word longer than 64 characters is refused before the token array is made. (5) DXF end points join through a grid of cells one join tolerance wide (6000 lines in well under 3 s), and one insert takes at most 50000 entities of the chosen layers. (6) DXF values that are not finite numbers are a DXF error naming the value. (7) Part files over 2 GB are refused before reading; JSON nested too deeply for the reader, numbers with thousands of digits and values of the wrong form are reported as a damaged file, and the recovery scan skips such files and damaged notes. (8) Formulas may nest at most 100 levels of brackets and signs; deeper ones give a normal formula error. The mesh is still read on each rebuild of an import: with (1) that is quick, and a cache would hold the mesh longer than needed (CLAUDE.md section 5A item 3).
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D12; every limit is far above real files and gives a message saying what to do.

D710: Quitting, stopped rebuilds and partial exports (2026-11-02, audit D3 items 4 and 12, E item 12). (1) Quit asks Save, Discard or Cancel for every unsaved part, last tab first as before, and closes nothing until every part has an answer; Cancel, or a Save that is cancelled or fails, keeps every part open with its changes. A single summary dialog listing all parts was not built: the per part question already exists and is tested, and the order fix alone removes the data loss. (2) A rebuild that was stopped shows "Rebuild stopped: the part shows only the features built so far. Press Ctrl+B to rebuild it." instead of "Rebuilt in N s". (3) Export refuses while a rebuild runs (the body shown may be older than the part) and after a stopped rebuild, saying what to do. Export of a part with failed features or with the rollback bar up still runs, because that can be what the user wants, and the confirmation says which features the file leaves out.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D3 items 4 and 12; never lose changes or write a partial body silently.

D711: Sheet metal features in mirrors and patterns (2026-11-02, audit E item 7.7, spec 2 section 20 item 7). Mirroring or patterning sheet metal features (any type in the sheet metal package: flanges, hems, jogs, tabs, forms) is refused, picked as a feature or by its faces, with one message: the copies would not be part of the sheet, so they would not unfold; add the flanges with Edge Flange, or mirror the whole body if no flat pattern is needed. Before, the feature pick said to pick the faces and the face pick said to pick the feature. Cuts and holes in a sheet metal part are not sheet metal types, so patterns of them still work and flatten. Building real copies in the sheet model (mirrored walls and bends) was not done: no Phase 7B item asks for it, and it needs mirrored bend placement in the sheet model. A body mirror still blocks Flatten with the existing message that names it.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit E item 7.7; consistent advice.

D712: Hole seeds, axes from reference geometry, and round faces as revolve axes (2026-11-02, spec 2 section 20 items 1, 3 and 4). (1) The Items to Copy list offers exactly what the core copies: bosses, cuts and types with a fixed pattern operation (the Hole Tool hole). Rib, Dome, Wrap, Mounting Boss and thread features stay out of the list: the core cannot copy them as features and says so, and they can be copied by their faces or with Geometry pattern. (2) A reference axis feature, and the origin's axes through a new reference form `{"feature": <origin id>, "axis": "x" | "y" | "z"}`, resolve as a line wherever an axis or direction is asked for (circular pattern, Move Face rotate, Move and Copy Body rotate, revolve). A plane is still not an axis, and its message now also offers a reference axis. The axis pick boxes list the reference axes above the feature and "X Axis (origin)", "Y Axis (origin)" and "Z Axis (origin)"; the revolve Axis list has them too. FDEF_SPEC section 7 gains the origin axis form (listed in the pull request, as FDEF_SPEC is an owner file); older readers that do not know the `axis` key would read it as the origin feature and fail with "not a plane", never silently. (3) Clicking a cylinder or cone face while a revolve takes its axis uses the face's axis (the core accepted it since TR17); the "made by itself or a later feature" message now names edges and faces.
Status: Default
Reason: Spec 2 section 20 items 1, 3 and 4.

D713: Smaller sweep, loft and polygon fixes (2026-11-02, spec 2 section 20 items 5, 6 and 8). (1) Sweep and Loft keep choosing finished sketches in their panel; the guide's "every tool on this page starts the same way" now names Extrude and Revolve only and says Sweep and Loft need their sketches drawn first. Starting a sketch from Sweep is not added: it needs two or more sketches, so one automatic sketch would not finish the feature. (2) A circular profile sweep with Thin Feature on fails with "Thin Feature does not work with a circular profile. Turn off Thin Feature, or use Pipe for a tube." (3) The Polygon option is renamed "Corners on the circle (off: sides touch the circle)"; the behaviour and the default (corners on the circle) are unchanged, and it is a tool setting, so no file changes. The guide says to turn it off to draw a nut by its size across the flats.
Status: Default
Reason: Spec 2 section 20 items 5, 6 and 8; say what happens rather than change saved geometry.

D714: Printing workflow fixes (2026-11-02, spec 2 section 20 items 11 to 19). (1) Item 11: names in 3MF are XML escaped, and characters XML cannot hold are dropped. (2) Item 12: Export 3MF and Open in Slicer move the face colours with the laid flat copy through the transform's history, so both keep colours; Save Bodies uses the part colour instead of the default grey. Split pieces in Save Bodies keep only the part colour: their faces are new, so face colours would need the split's history, which the body Split panel does not keep. (3) Item 13: new command File, Export, Bodies (no default key, D750 item 4) writes each body to its own file in a picked folder, as STL, 3MF, STEP or FDCAD Part; STL and 3MF follow Lay Face Flat with one placement for the whole part, so the bodies keep their layout, as Export STL does. It refuses while a rebuild runs or after a stopped one. (4) Item 14, one orientation per body, is TR383 (per body print settings, approved) and is built there. Item 15, thread clearance, is TR178. Item 19, Mounting Boss height up to a face, is TR146 item 1. They are not built twice. (5) Item 17: a new Split for Printing takes its build size (bed X, bed Y, height) and clearance from the active printer profile; saved splits keep their values. (6) Item 18: the meanings are written in the guide (Lip and Groove spacing is the whole gap; profile fit, Hole Tool Print Fit and Split clearance are per side), and a Print Fit on a heat set insert gives a warning. The Hole Tool's Print Fit stays None by default: a fit changes a standard hole size, so it must be chosen.
Status: Default
Reason: Spec 2 section 20; build each behaviour once, in the item that owns it.

D715: Mesh units, 3MF components and silent drops in Scale and flat export (2026-11-02, spec 2 section 20 items 20 and 21, audit D items 7 and 9). (1) Import Mesh has an optional `file_unit` (mm, the default when missing, cm, m or in) that scales an STL or OBJ mesh to millimetres; 3MF ignores it, as it carries its own unit. File, Open of an STL still reads millimetres without asking (the guide says so), and the unit is changed afterwards in the Mesh feature's panel, so opening a file never stops on a dialog. (2) 3MF objects that list components are read with each component's transform, nested up to 16 levels (deeper, or a loop, is a damaged file); a build item or component whose transform mirrors flips its triangles so the mesh stays outside out. (3) Scale scales solid bodies only; when the part has unconverted reference meshes it now warns and says to tick Convert to Solid. (4) DXF and SVG export of a sketch count the items they leave out (sketch text and curves that cannot be made) and say so in the status bar. Joining splines and ellipses into closed polylines and writing layers stay with audit D item 12 (Medium, export layers and colours) in the later audit sections.
Status: Default
Reason: Spec 2 section 20 items 20 and 21; nothing is dropped silently.

D716: Construction geometry and silent Combine results (2026-11-02, audit A item 6, B items 15 and 16, E items 7.1, 7.4, 7.5). (1) Hole positions and sketch pattern points leave out construction points and every point of a construction curve (centre, ends, axis points, spline points), unless a drawn curve also uses the point. Two round 10b tests that built their ellipse and spline as construction curves now expect only the free point. (2) Combine Add warns ("combine_apart") when the result has more than one body; Subtract warns ("combine_missed") when the main body's volume did not change, since the tool bodies are used up. Both stay warnings, not errors, because the result is what was asked for. (3) Split with a sketch cuts with the drawn curves only, through the shared sketch curve helper (D706), so construction lines and text outlines neither cut nor imprint seams.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit A6, B15, B16.

D717: Linear Pattern Up to reference, and Propagate Colours (2026-11-02, audit B items 1 and 2, E items 7.2 and 7.3). (1) Up to reference measures how far the reference lies from the seed centre along the direction: a plane or flat face where the direction line meets it (so a face at an angle works, and one parallel to the direction says so), a vertex at its point, and an edge or curved face at its centre of mass. Before, only vertices worked fully, flat faces only when square to the direction, and edges and cylinders always failed. (2) Copies made by a pattern or mirror with Propagate Colours on take the colour of the seed face they came from: a copy's face name `<pattern>/instance<i>.<j>/<seed face>` (or `mirror<k>`) is looked up as the seed face too, following copies of copies back, in the view, the appearance panel and exports. A colour set on the copy itself still wins.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit B1 and B2.

D718: Sketch geometry in reference tools, and user planes in plane lists (2026-11-02, audit B items 3 and 4). (1) Each reference box's menu has a submenu per earlier sketch listing its points, lines, arcs and circles; choosing one stores `{"feature": <sketch>, "sketch_entity": <id>}`, which the core already read for points and lines. Arcs and circles now resolve as their axis (through the centre, square to the sketch). Sketch splines stay out: no method takes a free curve yet. Picking sketch items by clicking them in the 3D view was not added, because the 3D view does not pick sketch entities; the menu covers the same choices. (2) The Up to Face, Offset from Face and From Surface lists, the Draft neutral plane, the Loft end directions, the Sweep twist direction and the print form plane lists offer reference planes as well as the three default planes (their results already carry a plane).
Status: Default
Reason: Audit B3 and B4.

D719: Toolbars, filters and view commands (2026-11-02, audit C item 8, D11 items 1 to 7, E items 10.1, 12.1 to 12.3). (1) The stray block that added the last relation button twice is gone. (2) The Solid Bodies filter lets face clicks through, since a body is picked by one of its faces; Planes, Axes and Sketches are greyed in the filter bar with a tooltip saying to choose them in the feature tree, because the 3D view does not pick them; making datums pickable in the view was not done in this defect pass. (3) Esc in the 3D view leaves Isolate when no feature is open (T12.4). (4) The graph body of Add as Feature and the automatic Flat Pattern are added with the normal insert rule, just above a rollback bar (T14.5.1). (5) Temporary axes are drawn in the theme accent, which a new test checks at 3:1 on both ends of every theme's view gradient (the edge colour is meant for edges on faces). (6) The tree toolbar offers Edit Feature, Edit Sketch (when there is one), Hide or Show of the sketch, and Delete for every feature type except the origin, not only extrude and revolve. (7) Normal To while a sketch is open fits the sketch in the view and says the sketch already faces you; it is also in the empty space sketch menu (T9.2). Zoom to Selection in a sketch with nothing picked gives its message.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D11 and C8.

D722: Data exchange fixes (2026-11-02, audit D items 1, 2, 4 to 6, 8 and 15). (1) DXF: a closed polyline of two vertices gets its closing segment, so the usual two bulge DXF circle is two arcs. (2) DXF entities with extrusion -Z: circles and polylines are in a frame whose X runs the other way (the arbitrary axis rule gives X = -world X for -Z), so their X is negated and polyline bulges change sign; ellipse points are world points, but their minor axis points the other way, so the arc runs from the end parameter to the start. Other tilted extrusions are still read as if flat (Z values are flattened, audit D item 11). (3) DXF blocks: the BLOCKS section is read, and each INSERT adds its block's entities moved, turned and scaled, nested up to 8 deep. An INSERT that mirrors or scales X and Y differently is skipped and counted, because circles and arcs would not stay round; array inserts (rows and columns) place one copy. (4) DXF paper space (group 67 = 1), invisible entities (group 60 = 1) and entities on frozen layers or layers that are off (negative colour) are skipped and counted, as they are not shown in model space. (5) OBJ negative corners count back from the vertices read before that face; files that use them are read line by line, others keep the whole array path. (6) STEP import adds a report line counting the loose faces, curves and points that are not part of a solid and were left out. Names, layers and invisibility of STEP items stay as noted in audit D item 13 (Medium) for later. (7) STEP colour matching uses a face map instead of nested searches (audit D item 15).
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D High items.

D723: Saving and opening safely (2026-11-02, audit D3 items 2, 7 and 13 to 15, D5 item 4, spec 2 section 21 item 10). (1) Save writes the part file on the UI thread as before (it is quick text), and the shape cache in a background thread; a second Save waits for the first cache write, and closing a part waits up to 10 s. The cache store looks faces up through a face map, so it no longer grows with the square of the face count. (2) Save flushes and syncs the temporary file, reads it back and compares it, and only then replaces the old file; any failure leaves the old file and removes the temporary one. (3) Save As refuses a path that another open tab uses, saying to close that tab or pick another name. (4) On open, a feature id used twice makes the file damaged; a next id at or below the highest used id is raised, and a rollback bar naming no feature is cleared, so later ids never repeat. (5) A formula whose result is infinite or not a number, or a function that overflows, gives a formula error at once instead of failing at save.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D3; never lose or overwrite a part silently.

D724: Recovery and design table safety (2026-11-02, audit D3 items 9 and 11). (1) The recovery question has Yes (open the copies), Discard (delete them) and Cancel (keep them for the next start); before, No deleted every copy with no second chance. (2) An autosave that cannot be read is renamed with `.damaged` added, so it is not tried at every start and is still there to look at. (3) When the part's own file was changed after the autosave, the recovered copy opens without a file name and the status bar says to use Save As, so Save cannot overwrite the newer file. (4) Design table OK lists the configurations it would delete (those with no row) and asks first. CSV export writes UTF-8 with a byte order mark; import already accepted one.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D3 items 9 and 11.

D725: Autosave in the background (2026-11-02, audit D3 item 10). The timed autosave makes the part text on the UI thread (embedded blocks are already encoded text, so this is quick) and writes it in a background thread through the same atomic, verified write as Save (D723); a write still running is waited for before the next one and before the copy is discarded. The autosave with a sketch open still writes at once, as it reads the sketch editor. When a write fails, the status bar says "Autosave failed" with the reason once per part. Compressing an imported file into the part is not moved: it runs once per import, inside the import flow, and is noted as a Low performance item.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D3 item 10.

D726: Newer files open and keep their data (2026-11-02, audit D5 items 1 to 3, E item 7.10). (1) A parameter object with `expr` and `value` plus other keys reads as its value (the other keys are dropped, since a Param holds only those two); a parameter that is a list or another object is kept as it is and written back, so a file from a newer FDCAD opens instead of being "damaged". `ParamValue` gains list and object for this. (2) Unknown keys are kept on graph nodes and in their `ui` object, on saved views, on tree folders and at the top of the tree object (FDEF_SPEC 14.4). Wires and groups still keep only known keys; they have no room for extra data yet. (3) FDEF_SPEC 9.2 says configuration paths that name nothing are kept, while the writer drops them. The writer is kept: such a path can never apply again, and keeping it would hold schema 2 for nothing. FDEF_SPEC is an owner file, so the wording change is proposed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit D5.

D727: Sheet metal and curve fixes (2026-11-02, audit A items 1 to 5 and 7). (1) The Sheet Metal folder reads a loaded bend table with any method; with K-factor or bend allowance a table that cannot be read is ignored, since the folder does not use it, and a flange whose own values choose the table gets it. (2) Flatten always works out the flat size for the panel; Show bounding box only draws and exports the box. (3) Choosing a gauge stores the typed thickness and radius in the folder (`before_gauge`), and No gauge puts them back. (4) Cross Break lines are clipped to the wall at mid thickness, so a notch splits a line into the pieces on the sheet. (5) Array Along Curve with both picked bodies and ticked features copies the bodies, as before, and warns that the features are not copied. (6) Forming Tool still places a form on each sketch line and now warns how many other curves it left out.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit A.

D728: Mounting boss fins and inch clearance holes (2026-11-02, audit E item 9.1, D13 item 1). (1) A mounting boss with fins but no stored fin length, width or height uses the panel's defaults (3, 1.2 and 6 mm), so raising the fin count from 0 by a formula, configuration or design table builds instead of failing. (2) The audit found the inch clearance values smaller than the ASME B18.2.8 data it compared against, matching common close and free fit drill sizes. The implementer cannot check the standard (clean room), so the values stay and the file header and guide now say what they are; whether to switch to the standard's values is listed in the pull request for the owner.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit E9.1 and D13.1.

D729: Boss and cut, pattern and panel fixes (2026-11-02, audit B items 5 to 7, 9, 11 and 13). (1) Item 5 was checked and is not a defect (brief rule 3): Up to Body for a boss clips the long prism with the picked body, so each part of the end stops where it meets the body's surface and fuses with it, which is "up to and into" the body; the guide now says so in those words, and TOOL_SPEC T16.1 needs no change. (2) A revolve with no axis chosen says "the sketch has no centerline" when its sketch has no line, and the old "pick the axis" message otherwise. (3) Cap Ends is hidden, and never written, for Sweep and Loft thin features, which do not read it (Extrude and Revolve keep it). (4) The guide is corrected where the code is right: Partial preview outlines the new faces; the seed is copy 1, so "3" is the second copy, and 1 or a number past the count is ignored; a copy that falls off the part fails the pattern until Skip copies that failed is clicked.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit B Medium items.

D730: Curve inputs (2026-11-02, audit B items 17 and 18). (1) Body tool pick boxes gain a "curve" kind listing curve features (helix, projected, composite and contour curves, as in the Sweep and Pipe panels); the Flow Along Curve path takes sketches and curve features, which the core already read. (2) A node editor curve input that holds several wires (a sketch with several curves through a model reference) is joined into one wire when the pieces meet end to end; otherwise the node fails saying how many separate curves it got. Before, the first wire was used silently.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit B17 and B18.

D731: End conditions follow Selected bodies (2026-11-02, audit B item 12). D720: Weak names are checked against the stored snapshot (2026-11-02, Phase 7B Stage 1 item 1, audit E item 13). (1) A name is weak when it holds a number given by position or by file order: a `#k` suffix (split pieces, position ordered caps, sides and fallback names such as the `<feature>/face#k` rings a revolve makes from profile lines square to its axis) or an imported face index `/face/<k>`. Edge and vertex names are weak when one of their faces is. Every other name resolves by name alone, as before. (2) Its family is every face (edge, vertex) whose name is the same with the numbers taken out (`f6/cap/end#3` and `f6/cap/end#1#2` are both `f6/cap/end`; every face of an import is `<feature>/face/*`). Renumbering only moves a number inside a family. (3) The face the name gives is kept silently when it still matches the snapshot exactly (the old rule: centre within 0.001 mm, area within 0.01 percent, same normal), or when it is the clearly nearest family member to the stored centre (every other compatible member at least 4/3 as far) and its centre has moved less than half its size (square root of the stored area; length for straight edges, radius for round ones). Compatible means the same surface or curve type and, for flat faces, normals within 45 degrees; for straight edges and round faces and edges, directions within 45 degrees either way. (4) Otherwise, in order: one exact snapshot match in the family, else anywhere in the body, is used with the existing warning (several equal matches are a lost reference, never a pick); one compatible family member whose centre has not moved (the rings of a revolve share their axis, so their centres tell them apart) is used with the warning; the named face, when it is still the clearly nearest but has moved far, is kept with a warning that it is far from where it was picked; else the reference is lost and the message says the name now belongs to another face and asks to reselect it. (5) Choices: the centre distance is used instead of a point inside the face, because the centre of a ring lies on its axis outside the face, and a point inside fails when a dimension edit moves the slot over the old centre. The size guard is needed because a profile edit can remove the picked corner while the name passes to the next corner along, which is then the nearest; that case now warns or is lost instead of filleting the other corner silently. A family member that matches the snapshot is preferred over one found elsewhere in the body. The snapshot is never rewritten during a rebuild (that would change the document outside an undoable command), so a face that has moved more than half its size since it was picked warns until it is reselected. (6) Edge families are named in one pass over the body, and edges are compared without the neighbour face normals (`select.curve_snapshot`), so checking an imported body with many edges stays quick; the check only runs when the named face or edge no longer matches its snapshot exactly. (7) Unchanged: names that fail resolve by the exact snapshot as before; an edge name that gives several pieces still uses D606. The revolve rings keep their position fallback names: naming them after their profile line would change the names in saved files. Tests: `tests/core/naming/test_weak_names.py`, each hard case failing before the change, plus plain dimension edits on split pieces that must give no warning.
Status: Default
Reason: PLAN.md section 6 item 6 (never guess silently) and the audit's 17 silent wrong references, while keeping ordinary dimension edits free of warnings (audit: 1108 edits lost nothing).

D721: The outward normal of a flat face reads the handedness of its plane (2026-11-02, audit E item 13.5). A mirror copy turns every plane's frame left handed, and on a left handed frame the surface normal is the opposite of the frame's main direction. FDCAD read only the main direction and the face orientation, so the top face of a mirrored boss reported a downward normal, a sketch on it faced into the part and a boss on that sketch grew down. `fdcad/core/plane_normal.py` (`plane_normal`, `plane_frame`) now gives the normal out of the material for any frame, and the snapshot, sketch on a face, reference geometry, Move Face and other direct edits, draft, Up To Face and Offset From Surface ends, Start From Surface, helper face picks, Split for Print face sides, Measure, node editor face planes and flat DXF export use it. The radius a round face gets from an offset (`direct.radius_after`) reads the handedness the same way, so offsetting a mirrored cylinder grows it instead of shrinking it. The kernel's mirrored geometry is left as it is: left handed frames are valid geometry, can also come from imported files, and reading the handedness fixes every reader in one place. Sketches already placed on mirrored faces now face out of the part, as they should; snapshots stored on mirrored faces before this change have the opposite normal, so such a reference only differs when its name fails and the snapshot is used.
Status: Default
Reason: Audit E item 13.5: the mirrored boss top reported a downward normal.

It is a view setting: not saved in the part and not an undo step. (2) Only the kernel camera's projection changes, with the kernel's default field of view; zoom, pan, rotate, standard views, Zoom to Fit and saved views work as before, since saved views and turns store the eye, centre, up and scale, not the projection. Previous View restores an earlier camera but keeps the projection the user chose. (3) Measure, dimensions and value labels read the model, so they show true values in either projection. (4) The icon is a box drawn in perspective with an accent vanishing point.
Status: Default
Reason: TR15; one toggle like the other view switches.

D748: Measure in two units (2026-11-03, TR26, Phase 7A). The Measure box options get Second unit: None (the default), mm or in. When set, each length, area, volume and point result shows the value in the box's unit, then in the second unit in brackets, with the same number of decimals, for example "25.40 mm (1.00 in)". Angles and counts have no unit and show once; a second unit equal to the first is not repeated. The copy button copies the first value only, so it can be pasted into a value field; the history keeps both. Like the box's other options it is not saved and is not an undo step.
Status: Default
Reason: TR26; a pasted value must read as one number with one unit.

D749: Equations to and from a text file (2026-11-03, TR25, Phase 7A). (1) The file is UTF-8 text in FDCAD's own simple form (`core/equations/text_file.py`): a `# FDCAD equations` line, then `[variables]`, `[suppression]` and `[equations]` sections matching the manager's three sections, one row per line as a quoted name, ` = `, the value exactly as typed in the manager and an optional comment after `//` (a `//` inside quotes is part of a name). Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are skipped, a byte order mark is accepted, and rows before any section are variables. A line that is not a row is refused with its line number and the form to use. Files over 1 MB or 10,000 rows are refused (hostile file limits, audit D12). Reading the file never runs code. (2) The equations manager gets Export..., Import..., Link... and Remove Link. Export writes the rows as they are in the manager. Import merges the file into the manager's rows: a row with the same name in the same section is replaced (a variable keeps its kind), new rows are added, rows the file does not name stay, and equations or suppression formulas for values or features the part does not have are left out and named in the message. Nothing changes until OK, which applies it as one undo step. (3) Link... imports the file and stores its full path in the part as the new top-level key `equations_file` (written only when set, so other parts save unchanged; a value that is not text makes the file damaged). The linked file is read again when the part opens, with the values put in directly (opening is not an undo step and the part does not show as changed), and on Rebuild (Ctrl+B), as one undo step, "Read Equations File". When the stored path is gone, a file of the same name next to the part is used, so a folder of parts and their shared file can move together. A linked file that cannot be read leaves the values as they are and says so in the status bar. Remove Link stops reading the file and keeps the values. (4) FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `equations_file` added to the top-level keys; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR25; one file drives several parts without code in the file.

D752: Offset plane by Ctrl and drag (2026-11-03, TR10, Phase 7A). (1) Holding Ctrl and pressing within 6 pixels of the border of a shown plane (a main plane or a reference plane shown in the view) grabs it; the border is the plane's rectangle seen on screen, found in `ui/viewport/plane_drag.py`, so the inside of the plane still picks what is behind it. While the mouse moves, an accent copy of the plane shows where the new plane will be: the offset is the point of the line along the plane's normal through the grab point that is closest to the cursor ray, so it reads true in any view. (2) On release, the reference plane panel opens with Offset distance, the grabbed plane as the reference, the distance rounded to 0.5 mm (0.01 in for inch parts) and Flip side ticked when the drag went to the back of the plane. The value can be typed over; OK adds the plane as usual, Cancel adds nothing. A drag that rounds to 0 opens nothing. (3) A Ctrl press on a border with no drag is an ordinary Ctrl click, so adding to the selection works as before. Ctrl with the left button had no other use in the view. (4) The plane's corners come from the kernel edge by edge, not round the face, so they are put in order round their middle before the border is measured (plane faces are rectangles).
Status: Default
Reason: TR10; the panel keeps the usual OK and Cancel so a drag never adds a plane by itself.

D753: See through for one body (2026-11-03, TR21, Phase 7A). (1) A body row in the Solid Bodies folder gets Make Body See Through, which turns into Make Body Solid once it is on; hidden bodies do not offer it. The body is drawn with the same see through amount as Toggle Transparency, and the other bodies stay solid. Toggle Transparency (Shift+T) stays the switch for the whole part. (2) Like hiding (D410), it is saved in the part as face name marks, in `appearance.see_through_bodies`, so it survives rebuilds that renumber the bodies, and each change is one undo step that needs no rebuild. It changes only what is drawn: picking, measuring, features and exports are unchanged. (3) TR21 also names a display column on feature rows. FDCAD's feature tree has one column, and a feature does not always make one body, so only the body rows get the command; a display column for feature rows is left for the tree work in Phase 7B. (4) FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new appearance key; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR21; stored like hidden bodies so the two behave the same.

D754: Zebra stripes (2026-11-03, TR18, Phase 7A). (1) Evaluate, Zebra Stripes (no default key, D683) is a toggle on the Evaluate tab, beside Curvature Graph. While on, the current part reflects black and white stripes and a small window sets the number of stripes (4 to 48, 12 to start) and their direction (up and down, or side to side). Turning it off, or switching to another part tab, puts the normal shading back on the parts it no longer shows. (2) The stripes are the kernel view's environment texture, a 256 by 256 striped image built once per setting, so they follow the view as it turns with no work in Python per frame and no mesh of our own; a probe on a sphere showed crisp stripes with the shaded styles. (3) Display only: the part does not change, nothing is saved and nothing goes on the undo list. Planes shown in the view are shaded too, so they also show stripes; that is accepted.
Status: Default
Reason: TR18; the kernel's own reflection mapping is exact and costs nothing per frame.

D755: Lasso selection (2026-11-03, TR19, Phase 7A). (1) Selection, Lasso Selection (no default key, D683) is a toggle for every open part, like Perspective; a part opened while it is on uses it too. While on, a left drag in the 3D view draws a free loop instead of a box. Zoom to Area still draws a box. (2) The loop's direction on screen sets the rule, matching the box (TOOL_SPEC T14.3.3): drawn clockwise it selects items fully inside; counter clockwise it also selects items it crosses. The direction is the sign of the loop's area (`selection_rules.lasso_is_crossing`); points closer than 2 pixels are left out. Shift adds, Ctrl toggles, and with neither the loop replaces the selection. It selects the same types as the box: edges, or the types the filters allow. (3) The kernel does the selection (`SelectPolygon`, with overlap detection for crossing) and the outline is the same dashed band as the box, drawn as a closed polygon. (4) The sketch editor keeps the box; TR19 names the 3D view.
Status: Default
Reason: TR19; the direction rule mirrors the left to right and right to left box rule.

D756: Selection breadcrumbs (2026-11-03, TR20, Phase 7A). (1) When a face, edge or vertex is picked in the 3D view, the left end of the strip above the view shows its chain: the part's name, its body (only in parts with more than one body), the feature that made it and that feature's sketch, as flat buttons separated by a small angle mark. With nothing picked the row is hidden. The strip is used because Qt cannot draw a see through widget on the kernel's native window on every platform (the reason the view toolbar sits there too). (2) The feature is the one the face's name starts with (`f6/cap/end` comes from `f6`); an edge or vertex takes the feature of the first named face it touches (`core/breadcrumbs.py`). So a face a fillet made shows the fillet, and a face an extrude made and a later cut trimmed still shows the extrude. With several picks, the chain is for the last one. (3) Clicking a crumb selects that row in the feature tree (the part row, the body row in Solid Bodies, the feature or the sketch); right clicking shows the tree's own menu for that row, so every command there works from the view.
Status: Default
Reason: TR20; the face names already carry the feature that made each face.

D757: Conic and equation curves (2026-11-03, TR28, Phase 7A). (1) Both sketch tools (Conic and Equation Curve, on the Sketch tab beside Spline, no default keys) add an ordinary sketch spline, so every tool, relation, profile, the solver and the kernel already handle them, and the file format does not change. A new curve type would have touched 17 modules (solver, regions, trim, offset, drawing, the kernel edges and the file format) for a Low item. (2) Conic: click the start, the end, then the top point where the end tangents meet; Shape (rho) in the tool panel, 0.01 to 0.99, 0.5 to start. The exact curve is the rational quadratic with weight rho / (1 - rho) on the top point (0.5 a parabola, less part of an ellipse, more a hyperbola). It is halved at its shoulder two times (three above rho 0.8), and each piece becomes one cubic spline piece whose ends, end tangents and middle match the exact curve; the halves of a piece have equal weights, so every join is smooth. Measured on a 40 mm span: a parabola is exact, the gap is under 0.0002 mm up to rho 0.8 and under 0.00003 mm at 0.99. A top point on the line between the ends is refused with a note, and the ends stay so only the top is picked again. The curve is then a spline: moving its points later reshapes it as a spline, not as a conic. (3) Equation Curve: x(t) and y(t), t from and to, and the number of points (3 to 200, 25 to start) in the tool panel, then Add Curve, as one undo step. Expressions go through the safe parser with t as a plain number (CLAUDE.md 5.10); a leading = is added when it is left out, since functions need it, and plain numbers are in the part's unit. The spline passes through the evenly spaced samples with tangents from the expressions (a third of the step's travel, from a small central difference), so a half circle of radius 10 with 13 points stays within 0.001 mm. An expression error, a value that is not a number, equal start and end or all points in one place are refused with the t value and what to change. (4) The tool panel gets a `text` option kind for the expression fields.
Status: Default
Reason: TR28; splines keep every existing tool working, and the measured error is far below drawing tolerance.

D758: Compare two bodies (2026-11-03, TR27, Phase 7A). (1) Evaluate, Compare Bodies (no default key, D683) is a toggle on the Evaluate tab, under Measure. Its window picks a First body of the part and a Second: another body of the part, or STEP file... which asks for a file. Compare runs in a kernel job (CLAUDE.md 5.2); a newer compare, a part tab change or turning it off drops an older result. (2) `core/compare.py` cuts each body from the other; the volume left of each is what only that body has, and differences under 1e-6 mm3 count as none. A face of the first body differs when a face of either leftover piece lies on it (within 1e-4 mm, from a point inside each leftover face), so a face that only partly changed counts too, which a test at the face's middle missed. (3) The faces that differ are painted red, the volume only the first has is a see through red overlay and the volume only the second has a see through blue one, with the draft analysis colours. The window and the status bar give the face count and both volumes in the part's unit, or "The bodies are the same." A kernel failure gives a message, never a crash (CLAUDE.md 5.7). (4) Display only: nothing in the part changes and nothing is saved. Turning it off gives the part its own colours back.
Status: Default
Reason: TR27; two cuts give the volumes exactly and show where the change is.

D759: Intersection curves and silhouette (2026-11-03, TR6, Phase 7A). (1) Two sketch tools beside Convert Entities, no default keys: Intersection Curves (where the sketch plane cuts the part) and Silhouette (the outline of the part seen square to the sketch plane). When a sketch opens, both are worked out in one kernel job with the part as last rebuilt, like the reference outline (D72); each tool previews its curves and Add Curves copies them, one undo step. (2) `core/sketch/model_curves.py`. Intersection: the kernel's section of the part with the plane, made into exact lines, arcs and splines by the curve projection Convert uses for curve features (D517). Silhouette: the kernel's hidden line removal looking along the plane normal gives every visible sharp and outline edge; an edge is kept only when a line square to the plane just beside it meets the part on one side and not on the other, so edges inside the outline (a step, a hole seen from above has none) are left out. A test on an L shape keeps exactly the 80 mm outline; a cylinder seen from the side gives its two ends and two outline lines. (3) TR6 asks for the whole body or picked faces, and for curves linked to the model like Convert Entities. A sketch cannot pick part faces, and the link check (D250) follows named edges and vertices, which section and outline curves do not have. So both tools take the whole part and copy fixed curves, as Convert does for curve features (D517); after a part change, Add Curves again on the new curves (the copies already there are not repeated). (4) A kernel failure gives no curves and the tool says there are none, never an error.
Status: Default
Reason: TR6; fixed copies reuse the Convert path, and the outline test needs no 2D union of faces.

D760: IGES import and Heal (2026-11-03, TR31, Phase 7A, owner approved in D683). (1) IGES files (`.igs`, `.iges`) open and insert like STEP files: File, Open, Import STEP Body (its file dialog now lists both) and Replace From File, which swaps STEP and IGES both ways. No new feature type: the file is stored in the part as a `step` block with `format: "iges"` (as mesh blocks carry their format), and the STEP import feature reads such a block with `core/io/iges_import.py`. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs that block format and the new parameter below; they are listed in the pull request. (2) An IGES file usually holds loose surfaces. They are healed and sewn with the same code as STEP (`step_import.heal`), so surfaces that close a volume become a solid and the report says so. When they do not, the import is an error that says how many gaps are left and where the first three are (the middle of each open edge loop after sewing), and what to do: close them in the program that made the file, or Heal with a larger gap. Text that is not IGES reads as an empty file, so both give one message. (3) Heal... on the tree menu of a STEP or IGES import asks for the largest gap to close (0.001 to 1 mm; it starts at ten times the last value, or 0.1 mm) and sets the import's new optional `heal_gap` length, as one undo step; the import is read again with that sewing tolerance, and the report ends with "Healed with a gap of N mm." A box whose top face sits 0.05 mm too high stays open by default and closes at 0.1 mm. More than 1 mm is refused, since it would join faces meant to be apart. (4) TR31 also asks Heal to list the faces it could not fix, each with Zoom to Selection. The kernel's check reports a shape as invalid, not which faces, so the report keeps the existing note to find them with Geometry Check, which lists faces with Zoom to Selection. Building new surfaces stays out of scope (PLAN.md), so surfaces that will not close stay an error.
Status: Default
Reason: TR31; one feature type for both formats keeps Replace, naming and colours unchanged.

D761: Order of the last Phase 7A items within Stage 2 (2026-11-03; follows D701). D701 has the open Phase 7A items built together with Phase 7B Stage 2. Twelve of them are built (D747 to D760) and TR8 was already done (D751). The three left wait as follows. (1) TR29 Face fillet with a hold line is built with TR60 Split Line (Stage 3). A hold line is an edge inside the face being rounded, and the only way to put one there is a split line; picking an existing face boundary instead makes the fillet eat the whole face, which the kernel's fillet cannot do. The kernel side is known to work: a variable radius fillet whose radius at each point is the setback to the hold line times the tangent of half the angle between the faces (the setback itself at a square corner). (2) TR7 3D sketch and TR34 sketch blocks, both Low items that the spec marks large, are built after the Stage 2 High items, so the High items users meet first in the tutorials come sooner. PLAN.md keeps all three unticked.
Status: Default
Reason: High items first; TR29 needs TR60 to be usable.

D762: Fully Define Sketch (2026-11-03, TR35, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) A sketch tool beside Relations (no default key, D750 item 4). Its panel: Use (the whole sketch, or the entities selected when it started), Add relations, Add dimensions, the dimension scheme (Baseline, Chain or Datum Pairs) and the datum, which is the sketch origin until a point is clicked while the tool is active. Calculate lists what would be added; Apply adds it as one undo step. (2) `core/sketch/fully_define.py` tries candidates in a fixed order on a copy of the sketch and keeps each one only when it takes freedom away with no conflict or redundant item, and stops once nothing is free, so it never adds an extra relation or dimension: first relations that already hold (Horizontal and Vertical lines, Coincident points in the same place), then sizes (circle diameters, arc radii, line lengths), then positions. Baseline gives every point its horizontal and vertical distance from the datum, all horizontal ones first; Datum Pairs gives the same distances point by point; Chain gives each point its distance from the one before it along each axis, sorted, starting at the datum. A point level with the datum gets a Horizontal or Vertical relation to it instead of a zero distance while relations are on. Construction points come after curve points, so handles and tool centres are placed last. Candidates are capped at 2000 so a very large sketch does not stall. (3) Every new dimension takes the current size and a horizontal or vertical distance keeps its side, so nothing moves; the tests check that no point moves more than 1e-6 mm. Entities already fully defined (solver check, D72) are skipped. A sketch with a conflict or a redundant item is refused with a message and nothing is added. (4) The datum is a point only; TR35's separate horizontal and vertical datums (for example two lines) and the extra in section 22 item 1 (several candidate sets with a preview) are not built: one greedy set shown as a list. Datum lines can follow with TR45's baseline and ordinate dimensions.
Status: Default
Reason: TR35; a greedy set checked by the solver can never over define the sketch.

D763: Check Sketch for Feature, and Use Only Fully Defined Sketches (2026-11-03, TR36, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) A sketch tool beside Relations (no default key). The tool panel picks the feature: Boss, Cut, Revolve, Sweep profile, Sweep path, Loft profile, Rib, Thin feature, Wrap, Split or Flange. Check lists what that kind cannot accept, or says "No problems found for ...". Nothing in the sketch changes. (2) `core/sketch/feature_check.py` uses the checks features run (`topology.check`: duplicates and overlaps, three or more curves at a point, open ends) and adds what they do not say: each open end with its distance to the nearest other open end; two ends closer than 0.05 mm that are not joined, as a near miss reported once per pair; and the number of open and closed contours the kind takes (one open, one closed, several closed, one of either for a flange, or any mix for wrap and split). Crossing curves are not a problem (D116 item 1) and construction geometry is ignored. Contours are counted from the joined end points, so a circle is one closed contour and an open chain is never counted as a loop. (3) The tool panel holds fixed fields, so instead of a Zoom button on each row, the panel lists the problems in order and Zoom to Next Problem centres the sketch on the next one (at least 8 pixels per mm) and selects its curves; it goes round to the first after the last. (4) Item 6: Preferences, Sketch, Use only fully defined sketches (off by default, saved with the other preferences). While on, a feature built from a sketch that is not fully defined is an error naming the sketch and saying to use Fully Define Sketch or turn the preference off; the sketch itself still solves and shows. The check is in the rebuild engine before the result cache, so switching the preference rebuilds the open parts and takes effect at once. Only the sketch a feature is built from (its `sketch` reference) counts; sketches used as paths or guides follow when those features gain the check.
Status: Default
Reason: TR36; the same checks the features run, shown before the feature is made.

D764: Mass Properties (2026-11-03, TR79, Phase 7B Stage 2; D750 item 2 approved widening D6 and D29). (1) Evaluate, Mass Properties (no default key) is a toggle on the Evaluate tab beside Measure. Its window: Bodies (the whole part or the picked bodies), Include hidden bodies, Material, Density and Inertia about (the centre of mass, the part origin or any coordinate system of the part). It calculates when it opens and on Calculate, in a kernel job; Copy puts every row on the clipboard as label, tab, value. Nothing in the part changes. (2) `core/mass.py`: the kernel's global properties give the volume, the centre of mass and the inertia about the centre for unit density, summed over the bodies; the density scales them; the principal moments and axes come from the symmetric tensor's eigen decomposition (smallest first); the inertia about a coordinate system uses the parallel axis rule and turns the tensor into that frame's axes. A 20 by 10 by 4 mm steel block matches the textbook formulas for every moment and product of inertia, about its centre and about a corner. (3) Units follow the part: mm, g and g mm2, or in, lb and lb in2; density is always g/cm3, as in Print Estimate. (4) TR78 part material is a Stage 3 item, so the Material list is Print Estimate's materials from the preferences (D351), starting on the one picked last there, plus Typed density; typing a density picks Typed density. When TR78 is built, the part's material becomes the default.
Status: Default
Reason: TR79; every value is the kernel's, checked against closed forms.

D765: Drop files on the window (2026-11-03, TR377, Phase 7B Stage 2). Dropping files that File, Open accepts (`.fdprt`, `.fdef`, STEP, IGES, STL, 3MF and OBJ) anywhere on the main window opens each of them through the same path as File, Open: a part opens in its own tab, or its tab comes forward when it is open already, and an import file becomes a new unsaved part. An event filter (`ui/main_window/file_drop.py`) is installed on the window, on every 3D view and on the feature tree, because those take drops for their own drags (moving tree rows, Ctrl and drag onto a face, D684 and TR9.3) and would otherwise swallow a file; drags that carry no files go on to them unchanged. While dragging, the cursor shows a drop is possible only when at least one file can be opened. Files that cannot be opened are skipped and the status bar names the first one and how many were skipped. Inserting a dropped STEP or mesh file into the open part, instead of opening it as a new part, is not done: Import STEP Body and Import Mesh do that.
Status: Default
Reason: TR377; one path for File, Open, the Dock, double clicks and drops.

D766: Mac menu roles, Window menu and title bar file (2026-11-03, TR376, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Help, About already had the About role; Tools, Preferences now has the Preferences role and File, Quit the Quit role, so on a Mac all three always sit in the application menu instead of depending on Qt guessing from their text. On other platforms the roles change nothing. (2) On a Mac only, a Window menu between Tools and Help holds Minimize (Command+M), Zoom (maximise or back), Bring All to Front and one ticked item per open part, filled each time the menu opens; choosing a part shows its tab. Windows and Linux menus are unchanged. (3) The window's file path is the active part's file, set together with the title, so the Mac title bar shows the file icon with its path menu; an unsaved part has none. The Mac pieces are checked only through CI (CLAUDE.md 9.6); the tests build the Window menu on any platform.
Status: Default
Reason: TR376; Mac conventions without changing Windows menus.

D767: Mac Redo key (2026-11-03, TR375, Phase 7B Stage 2; the owner approved the change in D750 item 2, amending D19 for the Mac). On a Mac, Redo takes Command+Shift+Z, the key every Mac app uses, and keeps Command+Y; Previous View moves from Command+Shift+Z to Control+Shift+Z, so it keeps a default key. Windows and Linux keep Ctrl+Y for Redo and Ctrl+Shift+Z for Previous View. No two commands share a default key on a Mac (a test checks every command). In an open sketch both platforms already took Ctrl+Shift+Z as redo (D741). SHORTCUTS.md (an owner file) needs the Mac keys for Redo and Previous View; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR375 as approved; Mac users get the standard Redo key.

D768: Windows contrast themes (2026-11-03, TR378, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) When a Windows contrast theme is on, FDCAD draws with the system's own colours whatever theme is chosen in Preferences, since the user asked the whole system for them. `ui/themes/system_contrast.py` asks Windows through ctypes (`SystemParametersInfo` for the contrast setting, `GetSysColor` for the window, text, highlight, highlighted text, button, button text, disabled text and link colours), and gives nothing on other platforms or when it is off; a failing call never stops the app. It is read each time the theme is applied (start up and Preferences). (2) Every FDCAD colour, chrome and view, comes from one of those system colours. Where one would not meet FDCAD's contrast limits on its background (the same `contrast.pairs` the four themes pass), the next system colour in a fixed list is used, then the text colour, then black or white. Rows, buttons and fields use the window colour when the button colour does not leave the text readable; the view has one flat colour, the part faces are in the window colour and the edges and outline in the text colour. (3) The colours are a fifth internal theme, Theme.CONTRAST, kept out of the table of the four chosen themes and out of Preferences; `scheme_for` gives any theme's colours, and the icon colours now use it, which the screenshot run showed was needed (the icons looked the theme up in that table, so the app would not have started under a contrast theme). (4) Four contrast colour sets, FDCAD's own samples (light on black, black on white, yellow on dark and dark on cream), are in the contrast tests, where every pair passes, and `tools/screenshot_tabs.py --contrast` shoots every tab and panel with each of them. The Mac's Increase Contrast setting is not read; Qt's system palette there already follows it in light and dark.
Status: Default
Reason: TR378; the user's system colours win, within FDCAD's contrast rules.

D769: Status without colour alone (2026-11-03, TR292, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Sketch status now also shows by line and point shape: under defined is a thin solid line with hollow points, fully defined a heavier solid line with filled points, over defined a heavy dotted line with square points; construction keeps its dash and dot line (`ui/sketch_tools/status_style.py`). Feature tree rows already had a different mark shape for errors and warnings, and the status bar names the sketch state in words. (2) Preferences, General, Colour vision safe colours (off by default) swaps the green and red status colours for blue and orange in sketches and feature states, in each of the four themes, keeping every contrast pair (the dark themes needed lighter values). It does not apply while a Windows contrast theme is on. (3) Sketch hover used a lighter accent, which fell below 3:1 on the light themes; it now uses the theme's pre-selection colour, as the 3D view does. A test checks selection, pre-selection, the accent (the focus ring) and the three sketch line colours at 3:1 on the view, and the focus ring at 3:1 on every chrome background, in all four themes with and without the colour safe set.
Status: Default
Reason: TR292; shape and line weight carry status for anyone who cannot tell the colours apart.

D770: Signed horizontal and vertical distances (2026-11-03, TR337 with TR111 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 2). A horizontal or vertical distance now keeps the side its second item lies on, along the axis from the first item: the dimension stores `side` (+1 or -1), taken from the geometry the first time it is solved and kept afterwards, so a later edit or drag can never land the point on the mirror solution. The solver sets the side times the typed value, so a negative value puts the point on the other side on purpose (the one meaning of a negative value, spec section 27 item 7); a zero value is allowed as before. Plain and aligned distances are unchanged: they have no side. The side is saved with the dimension only once set, so sketches saved before this read as before and pick their side from their geometry at the first solve; a side that is not 1 or -1 makes the file damaged. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the optional `side` key on sketch dimensions; it is listed in the pull request. The measured value shown stays positive.
Status: Default
Reason: TR337; a fully defined sketch must not flip to its mirror when values change.

D771: Interference and gap check (2026-11-03, TR150, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Evaluate, Interference Check (no default key) is a toggle on the Evaluate tab beside Compare Bodies. Its window: Report gaps under (0.3 mm to start), Count touching bodies, a tick per body to leave bodies out, Check, the list of pairs, and Ignore Pair, which takes the selected pair out of the list while the part is open (kept per open part, not saved). (2) `core/interference.py` checks every pair: pairs whose bounding boxes are further apart than the gap are skipped at once; otherwise the boolean common of the two gives an overlap with its volume (above 1e-6 mm3), and the smallest distance gives a touch (1e-4 mm or less) or a gap under the chosen size with its two closest points. The smallest distance is reported, not only an overlap volume (spec section 22 item 38). A pair the kernel cannot check is listed as such with what to do. The work runs in a kernel job. (3) Clicking a row shows that pair: an overlap as a red see through volume, a gap as a line between the closest points. Showing the other bodies see through (TR150 item 1) is left to the body's own Make Body See Through (D753), and comparing gaps with the printer profile's clearance and cutting the overlap from a body (section 22 item 23) are not built. Section 27 notes that the owner may want to confirm this is in scope (it acts on the bodies of one part, not an assembly); it was approved with Phase 7B in D750. Display only: nothing in the part changes.
Status: Default
Reason: TR150; booleans and distances from the kernel, nothing guessed.

D772: Enclosed cavities (2026-11-03, TR284, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Evaluate, Enclosed Cavities (no default key) is a toggle in the 3D Print tab's Check group, beside Draft Analysis, since trapped resin and powder are a printing problem. Opening it looks for voids at once, in a kernel job. (2) `core/cavities.py`: a closed void is a shell of a solid other than its outer shell, listed with its volume and middle (voids under 0.001 mm3 are kernel noise). A space that reaches the outside is not a closed void, so it is not listed; spaces with only a tiny opening are not judged. (3) Add Drain Hole is the fix button: it adds an ordinary undoable Hole feature, never by itself (CLAUDE.md 5.12): a 3 mm simple hole from the named outer flat face nearest the void's middle (with the point straight across from it inside that face), square to the face, ending Up to Next, so it stops where it meets the void. A test drains a hollow cube and finds no void after the rebuild. When no outer flat face lies straight across, the message says to place a hole with the Hole Tool. (4) Cup Volume (item 2): the picked faces' bounding box, padded by 1 mm, is cut by the opening plane and by the body; the pieces that stay clear of the padded box's sides are what the faces hold. The opening is the top of the picked faces level with the Top Plane (model +Y), or any plane of the part. The space shows see through in the view. Display only, apart from the drain hole.
Status: Default
Reason: TR284; voids from the solid's own shells, and the fix is a normal feature.

D773: Show the cause of an error (2026-11-03, TR288, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) After every rebuild, each missing reference error (`core/rebuild/causes.py`) gets the earlier feature that took the face away: the face's name starts with the feature that made it (`f6/cap/end` from `f6`); walking the built features in tree order, the cause is the first feature after the last body that still had that name. When the making feature failed or is suppressed, or no longer makes the face at all (its sketch or values changed, or a replaced import has fewer faces), the making feature is the cause. (2) The error then ends with "It was lost at <feature>." (left out when the message already names that feature, as "X has an error. Fix X first." does) and gets a Show Cause: <feature> button, which selects that feature in the tree and changes nothing. (3) The errors list puts errors first as before, and among them those with a known cause first, in the cause's tree order, so fixing the first row often fixes the rows after it. It works from the rebuild's own results, with no kernel calls. Only face names are traced; a lost edge or vertex keeps its message as before.
Status: Default
Reason: TR288; the face names already record who made each face.

D774: Change test (2026-11-03, TR287, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Evaluate, Change Test (no default key) is a toggle in the Evaluate tab's Rebuild group. Its window: Step (10 percent to start), Steps each way (2), Run, Stop, and the result list. (2) `core/change_test.py` works on a deep copy: every value typed as a plain number (feature values and driving sketch dimensions above 0, and global variables that are not 0) is stepped up and down one at a time by the step times 1, 2 and so on, and the copy is rebuilt with a fresh engine each time. The typed text keeps its unit (the number in "20mm" is scaled). Values set by a formula are not stepped, since they follow the values they read. A step that makes any feature fail, or changes the part's face count, ends that direction; the result gives the steps each way that still rebuilt with the same faces and the first problem in words. A part that does not rebuild now is refused before testing. (3) The list shows the values that break the part first, each with its safe range; clicking a row selects its feature in the tree. Stop ends the test after the rebuild that is running and keeps what was found. It runs in a kernel job, and nothing in the part changes.
Status: Default
Reason: TR287; real rebuilds of a copy, so the safe ranges are what the kernel does.

D775: Model health report (2026-11-03, TR286, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Evaluate, Model Health (no default key) is a toggle in the Evaluate tab's Rebuild group. Opening it checks the part as last rebuilt, in a kernel job (the cut check reads volumes); Check runs it again. Clicking a row selects its feature in the tree (Zoom to Item). The only fix is Move to End for an early fillet or chamfer, an ordinary undoable move the user clicks (CLAUDE.md 5.12). (2) `core/health.py` checks, all advice: a sketch with curves and no relation, dimension or fixed point tying it to the sketch origin or part geometry; in a fully defined sketch, lines that are exactly level with no Horizontal or Vertical relation; a feature (sketches included) whose references name a face or edge a fillet or chamfer made; a fillet or chamfer with solid features after it; a cut or hole whose rebuild left the volume unchanged (within a millionth); a blind hole with no bottom or tip face of its own; features still called by their default name (one row for all of them, naming the first four); three or more sketches each holding one circle of the same radius. (3) Item text is FDCAD's own and each row says what to do. Thresholds for "many single shape sketches" (three) and "unchanged" (a millionth) are FDCAD's own choices (spec section 27 leaves them to the implementer).
Status: Default
Reason: TR286; advice only, from the document and the rebuild's own results.

D776: Mesh export options (2026-11-03, TR182, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) File, Export of STL and 3MF opens an options window after the file name is chosen: Quality (Coarse 0.1 mm and 34 degrees, Standard 0.01 mm and 29 degrees as before, Fine 0.002 mm and 11 degrees, or Custom with a typed chord deviation and angle; typing a value picks Custom), Format for STL (Binary as before, or Text), Unit (mm, or in: the file's numbers are inches, the 3MF says so in its unit, and the chord deviation stays the same real size), and Bodies (all, the shown ones, or the picked ones, by the picks' bodies). The triangle count and the file size (exact for STL, about for 3MF) are worked out in a kernel job as values change; a count for a closed window is dropped. (2) The choice is kept in the part's `print_setup.mesh_export` (deviation, angle, text, unit) through one undo step, only when it changed, and the next export starts from it; bad saved values fall back to the defaults. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs that key; it is listed in the pull request. Export with a given file name (tests, Export Bodies) uses the kept options without asking. Open in Slicer uses the kept quality, always in millimetres. (3) STEP export is unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: TR182; the core already took mesh settings, so the work is the panel and keeping the choice.

D777: 3MF that slicers understand, items 1 to 4 (2026-11-03, TR381, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Each body gets a colour group from the 3MF materials extension with one colour, its most used face colour (else the part colour), set as the body object's own colour, so slicers that map object colours to filaments give one filament per body; per face colours stay as base materials per triangle for viewers. (2) The bodies are written as mesh objects that are components of one assembly object named after the part, and the build has one item for it, so a slicer keeps them together as parts of one object. (3) The print orientation (Lay Face Flat) is the build item's transform (the 3 by 4 matrix, translation in the file's unit) instead of moved vertices, so the model keeps its own coordinates and its face colours; File, Export and Open in Slicer both do this. (4) A 256 pixel PNG of the 3D view is the package thumbnail (Metadata/thumbnail.png, with its relationship and content type), when the window has a 3D view. (5) Item 5, checking every export against the public 3MF schema and the consortium's conformance files in CI, is not built: those files are not in the repository and cannot be fetched here; a later session adds them with their BSD licence noted (CLAUDE.md 6.6). PLAN.md keeps TR381 unticked until then. The tests check the structure directly: colour groups, the assembly, the transform values and the thumbnail.
Status: Default
Reason: TR381; the open 3MF core and materials forms, no slicer specific keys.

D778: Body roles for printing wait for the slicers' key names (2026-11-03, TR382, Phase 7B Stage 2). TR382 asks for Modifier, Negative Volume, Support Blocker and Support Enforcer bodies written "in the forms the main slicers read (one family through metadata keys on the object, another through its model settings file)". The spec does not give those keys or the settings file layout, and the clean room rule (CLAUDE.md section 10) keeps implementers from looking them up in other tools' files or documentation. Guessing them would write files the slicers ignore. So TR382 is not built: the manager session adds the key names and file forms to the spec from public material, and the item is built from that. PLAN.md keeps it unticked.
Status: Default
Reason: CLAUDE.md section 10; the spec lacks the slicer forms the item needs.

D779: Bed edge chamfer (2026-11-03, TR177, Phase 7B Stage 2). 3D Print, Bed Edge Chamfer (no default key), beside Lay Face Flat, adds one ordinary Chamfer feature (symmetric distance) on every edge of the face on the bed, so hole edges on that face are included: the chamfer's existing "every edge of each face" picks. The face is the print orientation's face, or else the one picked flat face; with neither, the status bar says to lay a face flat or pick the bottom face. The size is asked once, 0.4 mm to start (0.05 to 5 mm), typed in the part's unit in the feature. The feature is named Bed Chamfer N, is one undo step and is edited like any chamfer; a later change of the bed face does not move it, since it names the face it was made on.
Status: Default
Reason: TR177; an ordinary chamfer keeps it editable and needs no new feature type.

D780: Support free hole tops, Hole Tool part (2026-11-03, TR175, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) The Hole Tool gets Print Top: Round (as before), Teardrop or Flat Bridge (the optional parameter `print_top`), for every type except slots. A teardrop adds, along the hole's main bore and its head clearance, the triangle between the circle's tangents at 45 degrees either side of up: exactly r squared times (1 minus pi over 4) more area, checked against the kernel's volume. A flat bridge cuts that triangle off level with the top of the circle. The extra faces are named `hole/<p>/top/<k>`. (2) Up is the printer's up: the model's +Z (a part with no print orientation prints as modelled, D353), or straight off the bed face when a face is laid flat. A hole whose axis is within about 6 degrees of up stays round, since its top does not overhang. (3) TR175 also asks for the option on Extruded Cut; that is not built yet, so PLAN.md keeps TR175 unticked. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new hole parameter; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR175; a fixed 45 degree point is the shape printers bridge without support.

D781: Bridging under counterbores (2026-11-03, TR176, Phase 7B Stage 2). The Hole Tool gets Head Down Bridge for counterbores and countersinks (optional `print_bridge`: none, `sacrificial` or `stepped`) and Layer Height (`bridge_layer`, 0.2 mm to start: the printer profile's layer height is typed by the user, as the profile's fit tolerance is for Print Fit). Sacrificial leaves one layer over the small bore just past the head's floor, to drill out after printing. Stepped leaves two layers: the first is cut as a slot as wide as the bore across the whole head, the second as a square as wide as the bore, so each layer prints as bridges across the one before (the slot along the hole's sketch X direction). The volumes are checked against the exact areas. A small bore too short for the layers is an error saying to make the hole deeper or the layers thinner. The new faces are named `hole/<p>/bridge_slot/<k>` and `bridge_square/<k>`. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the two parameters; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR176; the usual two layer trick, sized from one layer height.

D782: Printable thread profile and fit (2026-11-03, TR178, Phase 7B Stage 2). Thread (modelled) gets a Printing group. (1) Profile (`form`): `iso` (the 60 degree V, as before), `printable` (a 90 degree V: flanks at 45 degrees from the axis, so a thread printed standing up needs no supports; the same fractions of the triangle as ISO, so the depth is 0.3125 pitch and the hole for it is the thread diameter minus 0.625 pitch) and `round` (a half circle of radius a quarter pitch, half the pitch wide, for caps and jars with any pitch). (2) Clearance per side: typed as `clearance`, else from Print Fit and Fit Tolerance as for the Hole Tool (half its diameter change, so Clearance gives one tolerance per side). The thread's surface moves into the material by it, radially: a hole's thread grows, a shaft's shrinks; a groove that would get wider than the pitch is trimmed square at 95 percent of it, so turns never touch. Clearance must be under half the pitch. (3) Lead In (`lead_in`): a 45 degree cone at the start, on a shaft down to the root and in a hole out to the major diameter, so the thread does not start as a thin edge. The cone is cut before the thread: the other order leaves invalid faces in the kernel. The panel shows Print Fit; the typed `clearance` parameter is for files and the API. Tapped holes with Modelled Thread keep the standard profile. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `form`, `clearance`, `print_fit`, `fit_tolerance` and `lead_in` on the thread; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR178; 45 degree flanks are the usual unsupported print limit.

D783: Sketch tab Tools group kept narrow (2026-11-03, Phase 7B Stage 2). The full test run found the window's minimum width over 1024 px once a theme was applied before the window was built (as the app starts): Fully Define Sketch and Check Sketch for Feature (D762, D763) made the Relations column the width of their long labels, and a ribbon tab is never narrower than its widest group (D632). So: (1) Check Sketch for Feature is labelled Check Sketch (the tool, command and tooltip keep its meaning; the spec name stays in the decisions); (2) Fully Define Sketch sits under Construction Geometry, the widest column already, and Check Sketch under Relations. The window's minimum is about 930 px again. Two other failures from the same run are fixed with it: the theme colour check now allows `themes/system_contrast.py`, whose sample colours are system data (D768), and a body tool's count that arrives after its panel closed is skipped instead of touching a deleted list.
Status: Default
Reason: D632's 1024 px minimum.

D784: Support free hole tops, Extruded Cut part (2026-11-03, TR175, Phase 7B Stage 2). Extruded Cut gets Print Top (optional `print_top`: none, `teardrop`, `flat`), the same choice as the Hole Tool (D780), shown for extruded cuts only. Every whole round face of the cut's tool (a full cylinder, so circles in the profile, not arcs of a slot) gets the same prism as a hole, over the face's own length along its axis, toward the printer's up (D780 item 2). The prisms are cut after the main cut, in one boolean. Cut Outside cuts and sheet metal normal cuts (D700) are left as they were. The hole and the cut share `hole.top_prism`. The volume check is exact: r squared times (1 minus pi over 4) per unit length. With this TR175 is done. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `print_top` on extrude; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR175 item 1 names both the Hole Tool and Extruded Cut.

D785: Machining corner relief (2026-11-03, TR244, Phase 7B Stage 2). A new feature type, Corner Relief (`corner_relief`, Features tab, Remove Material group, under Lofted Cut, no default key). (1) Relief types: Dogbone, a cylinder of the relief radius centred that far from the corner along the diagonal into the pocket (the sum of the two walls' outward normals), so it reaches the corner and cuts into both walls; T-Bone, centred on one wall's plane so it cuts a half round into the other wall only (`flip` picks the other wall; the first wall is the face whose name sorts first); Corner Fillet, the corner rounded to the relief radius with the kernel's fillet, which adds material instead. (2) The relief radius is half the tool diameter plus the clearance; Tool Diameter is an ordinary length, so it can be a variable. (3) Picks: `edges`, or `feature` (an extrude), which takes every edge shared by two of that feature's side faces that is an inside corner: straight, between two flat, non parallel faces, with the material wrapping round it (a point stepped off the edge along one wall's normal and back along the other's is inside the solid). Each cylinder runs exactly the edge's length; all are cut in one boolean. A picked edge that is not an inside corner is an error saying so. Faces are named `relief/<k>`. The volumes are checked exactly for T-bone and fillet and against a numeric area for the dogbone. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR244; reuses the cut and fillet kernels with no new geometry types.

D786: More screw heads, thread series and drill names (2026-11-03, TR253, Phase 7B Stage 2). Compiled from the published standards (CLAUDE.md 7.6), listed in `core/features/hole_heads.py`. (1) Counterbore heads (the optional hole parameter `cbore_head`): socket (as before), button, low head socket, pan, cheese, and washer, a washer seat: a socket head on a plain washer, so the bore is the washer's diameter plus the usual clearance and as deep as the head plus the washer. Metric from ISO 7380-1, DIN 7984, ISO 7045, ISO 1207 and ISO 7089; inch from ASME B18.3, B18.6.3 (fillister for cheese) and B18.21.1 narrow washers. A head with no size for the chosen thread fills nothing, so the typed values stay. (2) Countersunk heads (`csk_head`): flat (the socket form, as before) and recessed, the cross recessed form of ISO 7046-1 (theoretical head diameter, 90 degrees), metric only; inch keeps its one 82 degree form, so the choice is hidden for inch. (3) Sizes: ISO fine pitches M3x0.35 to M36x3 (holes, heads and nuts of the coarse size; tap drill is size minus pitch), the larger coarse sizes M30, M36, M42 and M48 (ISO 273, 4762, 4032; their countersunk head is twice the size, since ISO 10642 stops at M20), and the inch gauge sizes #0, #1, #3 and #5 with the rest of the UNF and UNEF series from ASME B1.1 with 75 percent thread tap drills. Each list is sorted by diameter, coarsest thread first, so the first inch size is now #0-80. (4) Drill names: number drills #1 to #80, letter drills A to Z and fractions in 1/64 inch steps up to 2 inches; the panel shows "Drill: #7" under the size when the hole diameter is within 0.0003 inch of a named drill (a letter that is also a fraction shows both). A test checks that every inch tap and clearance drill in the tables has a name, which catches mistyped values. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the two head parameters; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR253; nominal values from the standards named above.

D787: Merge faces and a touching tolerance (2026-11-03, TR261, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) A new feature type, Merge Faces (`merge_faces`, Features tab Direct Edit group and the body tools panel, no default key). Picks: faces, or edges (both faces of each edge).
