It removes only the edges two picked faces share: every other edge of the body is passed to the kernel's same surface merge as an edge to keep, so nothing else changes. `tolerance` (0.001 mm to start) and `angle_tolerance` (0.1 degree) loosen what counts as one surface. If a shared edge is left, it is an error naming how many stay and saying to raise the tolerance or pick faces on one surface; faces that share no edge are an error too (a tiny step face between two faces is not merged away). The merged face keeps the name of the picked face that sorts first, so features on it stay attached. (2) Combine and Split get `tolerance`: the boolean's fuzzy value, never below the usual 1e-5 mm, so bodies a little apart (imported parts) count as touching; 0 keeps the usual value. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type and the `tolerance` parameters; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR261; the kernel's merge with a keep list changes only what was picked.

D788: Rules for Move Face, first part (2026-11-03, TR263, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Move Face (offset, translate and rotate, so Offset Face too) gets a Rules group with four ticks, stored as optional booleans `rule_coplanar`, `rule_concentric`, `rule_tangent`, `rule_equal_radius`, plus `suspend_rules` and the face list `refs.rule_exclude`. Faces a ticked rule finds join the picked faces before the move (`core/features/face_rules.py`): coplanar, flat faces on the same plane facing the same way (0.1 micron, 0.05 degree); concentric, round faces (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus) on the same axis as a picked round face; tangent, faces meeting a picked or added face within 1 degree at the middle of a shared edge, followed along the chain; equal radius, cylinders of the same radius as a picked cylinder. Excluded faces are never added. Rules are off unless ticked, so old files move exactly as before. (2) Not built yet, so PLAN.md keeps TR263 unticked: the keep parallel and perpendicular, symmetry about a plane and locked to main planes rules (they hold faces still or mirror the move, which only matters once neighbours can tilt, TR264), the three colour preview of moved, held and stretching faces with each rule's effect (item 2), and suppressing one rule for one face (item 3: the exclude list applies to every rule). FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new parameters; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR263; the rules that add faces work with today's stretch only neighbours.

D789: Set a size on a face, first part (2026-11-03, TR265, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Move Face gets a fourth Type, Resize (`mode` "resize", length `diameter`): each picked cylinder or sphere face, or a torus's tube, is offset by the difference between the typed and the current radius, the sign taken from which way an offset grows that face, so a hole wall and a shaft both get the typed diameter and neighbouring rounds follow as for Offset. Cones are refused with a message (TR265's cone angle with a fixed end is not built). (2) Offset gets Move by (`offset_by`: distance or measured): To a measured size takes `refs.size_from` (a vertex; an edge, a round edge counting from its centre; or a face, a hole counting from its axis through the face's centroid) and `set_size`, and moves the one flat picked face along its normal until it is that far from the item, whichever side the item is on. (3) Not built yet, so PLAN.md keeps TR265 unticked: the cone angle, and dimensions placed on model edges and faces edited in the view with side arrows, Symmetric and a lock (item 3). (4) Found while testing: when the active pick box of a body tools panel was hidden, the next one was chosen from an unordered set, so a click could land in the Rules exclude box; it now follows the panel order. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new mode and parameters; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR265; both reuse the offset, so naming and rounds behave as before.

D790: Manufacturing check, milling first (2026-11-03, TR295 and TR296, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Evaluate, Manufacturing Check (Measure group, no default key): a window with a Process choice (milling, turning, laser and sheet metal, moulding, FDM, resin and powder printing), the process's rule values in an editable table, Load Profile and Save Profile (a small JSON file, `.fdmfg`, marked `fdcad_manufacturing_profile: 1`; loading starts from the defaults, ignores unknown keys and negative or non number values, so older or edited files still load), Check (a kernel job) and the findings list. Clicking a finding highlights its faces and edges and selects its feature. FDCAD's starting values are general ones of its own (`core/manufacturing.py` DEFAULTS). (2) Milling checks: sharp inside corners (straight inside edges between flat faces that run along a setup direction; floor corners are cut square by a flat end mill and are not listed), inside rounds (part cylinders) under the smallest tool radius or deeper than the reach ratio, holes deeper than the depth ratio, facing flat walls closer than the smallest tool (slots), back to back flat faces closer than the thinnest wall, faces whose sampled normals point away from every setup direction (with the fewest of the six main directions that would reach all faces; material in the way is not checked), tapped holes with a thread longer than the ratio, blind tapped holes with under the room in pitches below the thread, holes that are not stock drills (metric 0.1 mm steps to 13 mm then 0.5 mm to 50 mm, or a named inch drill, D786), and sketch text under the smallest height. (3) Fixes are buttons, each one undo step: Add Corner Relief adds a Dogbone Corner Relief (D785) on the corner's edge sized from the profile's tool; Snap to Stock Size sets the owning Hole feature's diameter to the nearest stock drill. (4) Not built yet, so PLAN.md keeps TR295 and TR296 unticked: checks for the other processes (TR297 next for sheet metal and laser), the printer profile's process type and fields (TR295 item 2), pocket depth to width, wall height to thickness, and raised text (TR296 items 2 and 4).
Status: Default
Reason: TR295, TR296; advisory only, fixes reuse Corner Relief and the hole's own diameter.

D791: Sheet metal and laser checks, first part (2026-11-03, TR297, Phase 7B Stage 2). The Manufacturing Check's Laser and Sheet Metal process reads the Flat Pattern as the DXF export draws it (D339, `flat_drawing`), so it checks exactly what is cut; a part without a Flat Pattern gets one finding saying to add one (`core/manufacturing_sheet.py`). (1) Layout, with distances as multiples of the sheet thickness from the profile: holes under the smallest hole, holes and cut-outs (any inner loop) nearer the outside loop than hole to edge, nearer any bend line than hole to bend (slots and cut-outs included), two inner loops nearer each other than hole to hole, and a flange shorter than the shortest flange (from the middle of each bend line, square to it, to the outside loop on each side). (2) Preflight: the cut lines are chained into loops by their ends (0.1 micron); left over ends are an open contour; the same line twice is a duplicate; lines or arcs under 0.05 mm are tiny; a loop inside two others is an island that falls out; an outline under 2 mm or over 5 m across suggests wrong units. (3) Not built yet, so PLAN.md keeps TR297 unticked: tab and slot minimums, the bend radius below the material's minimum (needs TR78's materials), stencil bridges for sketch text, and the kerf value used by Tab and Slot and finger joints (item 3; the profile already holds a kerf). Findings name no faces yet, since the flat drawing is 2D; highlighting them follows with the flat view.
Status: Default
Reason: TR297; checking the drawing that is exported keeps the check and the file in step.

D792: Fill Pattern (2026-11-03, TR57, Phase 7B Stage 2). A new feature type `fill_pattern` in the pattern dropdown and the body tools panel (no default key). (1) One flat face to fill (`refs.face`); the layout lies in its plane, along a picked straight edge (`direction`) or the plane's own direction, starting at a picked vertex (`point`) or the face's centre. (2) Layouts: Grid (`spacing`, `row_spacing`), Staggered Grid (rows lean by `stagger_angle`, 60 degrees to start, so the copies form even triangles) and Rings (`ring_shape` circle, square or polygon with `sides`; ring k is k times the row spacing out and holds as many copies as its length divided by the spacing). (3) Validate count is always on: a copy is kept when its centre lies on the face and its footprint plus `margin` clears every edge of the face (outer and holes), tested with whole arrays against the face's edges sampled at 0.01 mm. The footprint of a built-in shape is its corner radius (half the size for a circle); of seed features, how far their box reaches across the face from the seed's centre; face and body seeds count as a point. The seed's own spot always counts. (4) Built-in shapes (`shape` circle, square, diamond, polygon, with `size`, `shape_angle`, `depth`; depth 0 cuts through) are cut in one boolean, faces `cut/...`; otherwise the seed is copied with the shared pattern code, so Geometry pattern, Merge and Skip work as for the other patterns. Skip numbers count the kept copies in layout order. (5) The number of copies is in the result's extras (`count`). Not built yet, so PLAN.md keeps TR57 unticked: showing the count in the panel and using it in an equation (item 3). Up to 1000 copies (MAX_INSTANCES). FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR57; fitting copies to the real face keeps grilles inside the material.

D793: Measured values in formulas, and the rest of Fill Pattern (2026-11-04, TR57, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) A feature type can measure values while it builds (`MEASURED_VALUES` in `core/equations/engine.py`; today only `fill_pattern` with `count`). The rebuild keeps them in `Document.measured` (by feature id, never saved, not part of equality) and formulas read them as `"count@Fill Pattern 1"` or `"count@f7"`, kind number. When a value changes during a rebuild the part is solved again at once, so features further down use the new value in the same rebuild. A formula in the measuring feature itself or in any feature above it is an error naming the pattern ("Move this feature below ... or type a value"), because it would build before the value is known and could never settle. After opening a file the value is 0 until the first rebuild, which happens on open. (2) The panel shows the number as Copies from the live preview (`preview_info`, as the vent areas, P4.4); the body tools form now receives preview results too. (3) `refs.sketch`: a closed sketch region bounds the fill in place of the face (picked regions work as for Extrude; with several, the one holding the start vertex, else the largest). Cuts go against the sketch plane's normal, so draw the sketch on the face to cut. (4) `fit`: `shape` (default, as D792) or `centre` (only the centre must be the margin away from the edge). A negative margin was already accepted and now is documented: copies may run past the edge by that much. (5) Not built, from the spec's additions (sections 22 to 24): fills over curved or several faces, knurls, a count per ring spacing mode, a rotation per copy, a default direction along the longest straight edge, and copies outside the boundary drawn faintly while editing (TR57 with TR107 item 98). These are recorded in IDEAS.md; the item's own list (1 to 5) is complete, so PLAN.md ticks TR57. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `refs.sketch` and `fit`; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR57 item 3; reading measured values after the build, with one re-solve, keeps formulas pure and the rebuild single pass.

D794: 3MF exports checked against the consortium's schema and sample files (2026-11-04, TR381 item 5, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) `tests/data/3mf_conformance` holds files from the 3MF Consortium's public test suite (github.com/3MFConsortium/test_suites, BSD 2-Clause, its LICENSE kept beside them): the consolidated schema (all 22 XSD files, about 230 KB, since the main one imports every extension), 12 small valid core samples and 22 small invalid ones from suite 3. These are test data only, never shipped. They come from a standards body, not a CAD product, so the clean room rule (CLAUDE.md section 10) does not apply. (2) New dev dependency `xmlschema` 4.3.2 (MIT) with `elementpath` 5.1.4 (MIT), pure Python, for schema validation in tests only (CLAUDE.md 6.6). (3) `tests/core/io/test_3mf_conformance.py` validates the model, content types and relationships parts of a plain export, and of a two body export with face colours, a print orientation, a thumbnail and a name with XML characters, in mm and in inches. The consolidated schema asks for a Production extension UUID on objects, components and items (a compromise its README notes; the consortium's own core samples fail it too), so that one rule is not applied. The valid samples must import with triangles; the invalid ones must import or raise MeshImportError, never another exception. FDCAD's reader is lenient: 20 of the 22 invalid files break rules (relationships, content types, metadata) that do not affect the mesh, and they import. (4) Runs with the rest of the suite, so CI runs it. TR381 is complete.
Status: Default
Reason: TR381 item 5; validating the files we write against the published schema catches format mistakes no structure test would.

D795: Repair lost references (2026-11-04, TR125, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) `core/naming/repair.py`: `find_lost` walks every face, edge, vertex and feature pick of each feature that reported an issue (a clean part costs nothing) and tries to resolve it on the part before that feature; a feature pick is lost when its feature no longer exists (a broken pattern seed). `suggest` offers one clear match, FDCAD's own rule: a face or edge compatible with the stored snapshot (same surface or curve kind, flat faces facing within 45 degrees, straight edges along it), scored by how far its centre moved plus the change in size, within three times the item's size (at least 5 mm), and at least a third better than the next one (the weak name ratio, D720). Faces or edges whose name shares the lost name's root are tried first. Never more than one is offered; ties offer nothing. `replaced` puts matches in or removes picks by path, removing from the end of a list first, and drops lists left empty. (2) Evaluate, Repair Lost References (Rebuild group beside Model Health, no default key) and a tree menu item on any feature whose last build reported a problem (that feature only): a window with a tick per row, Tick All, Use Offered and Remove, each a macro of ReplaceFeature commands, so one undo step (CLAUDE.md 5.12). Clicking a row selects the feature and highlights a ghost of the lost item next to the match. (3) The ghost (`ghost`) is drawn from the stored snapshot only, since the old shape is gone: a flat face as a disc of the same area facing the same way, a round face or edge as a circle on its axis, a straight edge as a line of its length, anything else as a small cross. It is made on a worker thread. (4) In feature panels, every pick list (`PickList`, the Phase 2 forms: fillet, chamfer, shell, draft, sweep, loft) marks lost items from the preview's failed names, not just fillet and chamfer as before. Selecting a lost item draws its ghost faintly (`show_lost`, warning colour, 60 percent transparent) and the next pick replaces it in place (Pick Again); Clear All Missing removes them all. The body tools forms (Phase 3 pick boxes) are not changed: their lost picks are covered by the Repair window. (5) The spec's additions item 18 (show the last good model beside the broken one) is not built and is in IDEAS.md.
Status: Default
Reason: TR125; offering only one clear match, and only on the user's click, keeps naming honest.

D796: Body roles for printing (2026-11-04, TR382, Phase 7B Stage 2). Built from the file forms the manager added to the spec on 2026-11-04 (TR382 file forms items 1 to 26, commit 80f75a3), which unblocks D778. (1) A body's role (`part`, `modifier`, `negative`, `support_enforcer`, `support_blocker`) is kept in `print_setup.body_roles` as its mark face name to the role, as hidden bodies are marked (D410), so roles follow the body through rebuilds; Part is never stored, and damaged entries are ignored (`core/printing/body_roles.py`). Set from the body row's Print Role submenu in the tree (one undo step, `SetBodyRoles`, no rebuild); a body row shows a role other than Part after its name. (2) `MeshSettings.slicer`: `default` or `prusa`, chosen in the 3MF export options (Slicer) and kept with the other mesh options; older parts load as `default`. (3) Default form: the TR381 assembly layout; when a body has a role, `Metadata/model_settings.config` lists one `part` per component with `subtype` and the body name, under the assembly object's id, and each marked mesh object carries a Cura `metadatagroup` (`cura:infill_mesh`, `cura:support_mesh` or `cura:anti_overhang_mesh`, the last also for negative volumes), with the `cura` namespace on the model. (4) PrusaSlicer form: every body in one mesh object, one block of vertices and triangles per body in order, per triangle colours kept; with roles, `Metadata/Slic3r_PE_model.config` gives one `volume` per body with inclusive triangle ranges from 0 and `volume_type`. (5) No settings file is written when every body is a Part. The `.config` parts get the content type `text/xml` (the spec names none; OPC needs one). Both forms pass the consortium schema test (D794). The Application metadata stays `FDCAD`, as item 8 requires. (6) After Export 3MF the status bar adds the line from item 24 for the form used; Open in Slicer writes roles in the kept form. Save Bodies writes one file per body and so no roles. (7) Not built: TR411 (warn when bodies overlap) stays a Medium item. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `print_setup.body_roles` and `mesh_export.slicer`; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR382; the slicers' own forms, written only when a body has a role, leave plain exports unchanged.

D797: How neighbours follow a moved face (2026-11-04, TR264, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Move Face gets `follow`: `extend` (default; the existing offset, volume and tilt methods, where the faces around keep their surfaces), `tip` or `lift` (`core/features/move_follow.py`). Tip moves every corner of the picked faces by the move and keeps every other corner, then makes each neighbour again through its corners (straight edges rebuilt, other edges kept) and sews the faces into a solid. It needs flat neighbours with straight edges at the moved corners that stay flat within 1e-6 of their size, else it fails naming the face. Offset with Tip needs the picked faces to move the same way (one transform). Lift sweeps each flat face along its move (Offset: its normal times the distance; Translate: the vector) and adds the sweep when moving out of the body or cuts it when moving in; the face keeps its name at its new place and the side faces are `<fid>/lift/<k>/face#j`. Rotate has no Lift. Moved faces keep their names in every way. (2) Item 2: the solutions are the three ways in FOLLOW order, the chosen one first (FDCAD's own order, spec section 28). When the chosen way fails, the others are tried and a warning (`follow_changed`) names the one used; `keep_solution` makes that an error. Previous Solution and Next Solution in the panel step the Neighbours choice round. Other ways the same method could rejoin a face (several intersection solutions) are not offered: the kernel methods give one. (3) Item 3: `rounds` `follow` (default, as before: the offset grows or shrinks them) or `remake`: fillet faces (named `.../fillet/<edge name>`, cylinder or torus) touching a picked face are patched away, the move runs on the sharp body, then each edge named in the old round's name is rounded again with its old radius and the new face takes the old round's names, so features on it stay attached. Rounds made by import or by another tool have no edge name and are left to follow. Not with Copy. (4) The rest of TR263 (keep parallel and perpendicular, symmetry, locked to main planes, the three colour preview, one rule off for one face) and TR265 (cone angle, editable dimensions on model edges) stay unticked. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `follow`, `keep_solution` and `rounds`; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR264; Extend stays the default, so existing parts build as before.

D798: The rest of the Move Face rules (2026-11-04, TR263, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) `rule_symmetric`: the face that is a picked (or rule added) face mirrored in a symmetry plane (`refs.symmetry_plane`, a plane or flat face; else each main plane through the origin) joins the move. Mirror match: same surface kind, centre on the mirrored centre and area within 0.01 percent, flat faces facing the mirrored way. A face lying across the plane is its own mirror and adds nothing. Only Offset and Resize take it, where the mirror face gets the same distance, which is the mirrored move; with Translate or Rotate it is left out with a warning (`rule_skipped`), since those move every face by one transform. (2) Holding rules add no faces: `rule_parallel` (neighbours of the moved faces parallel or square to a moved flat face) and `rule_main_planes` (neighbours facing along X, Y or Z). Their faces must face the same way after the move; a way of following that turns one (Tip, D797) fails with a message naming the rule and face, so Move Face goes on to the next way, or fails with Keep This Solution. Extend never turns a neighbour, so with Extend they hold by themselves. (3) Item 3: `refs.rule_exclude_<rule>` per rule, shown as a pick box under each ticked rule, beside the existing box for every rule. (4) Item 2: the Move Face preview now shows the finished part (as Fillet does, D583) with the moved faces in the accent colour, neighbours whose snapshot is unchanged in the idle handle colour (held still) and changed or new neighbours in the warning colour (stretching); `ResultPreview` and `PreviewGeometry` gained `held` and `stretched`. `preview_info` gives `rule:<name>` counts and each ticked rule's tick box reads "adds N", "holds N" or "no effect". FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new rule booleans and refs; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR263; every rule is off unless ticked, so existing parts move as before.

D799: Resize a cone (2026-11-04, TR265 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 2). Move Face Resize gets `cone_angle` (angle between the cone's side and its axis, 0 to 89 degrees) and `keep_end` (`large`, default, or `small`). Each picked cone face cut off at both ends is drafted (`BRepOffsetAPI_DraftAngle`) with its pull direction along the axis from the kept end and the neutral plane through the kept end circle, which sets the angle exactly; both signs are tried and the result kept is the one whose cone has the angle, still has the kept circle and still narrows or widens the same way away from it (its other end may now be where it meets a neighbour, as a countersink meets its hole wall). A cone that would close before its other end is refused with a message. Names carry through the draft's history; the cone keeps its name. Cones and other round faces can be picked together: cones take the angle, the others the diameter (D789); Resize needs the diameter only when a non cone face is picked. TR265 item 3 (dimensions on model edges edited in the view) is still open, so PLAN.md keeps TR265 unticked. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `cone_angle` and `keep_end`; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR265; the draft sets the angle exactly and keeps the chosen end where it is.

D800: Sizes edited in the view, Symmetric and Lock (2026-11-04, TR265 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 2). The dimensions of item 3 are Move Face measured sizes (D789): picking two items and typing the size is that mode, so no separate dimension object is added. (1) The size is a preview handle (`set_size`): an arrow on the moved face's normal from the measured from side to where the face ends up, so its head is on the side that moves; its label is edited in the view and dragging it sets the size, as for every handle (T15.2). (2) `symmetric`: the face measured from (a flat face opposite the picked one, normals anti parallel, else an error that says so) moves too, each by half the change, along its own normal; the arrow then starts at the middle and counts twice. (3) `lock_size`: a later Move Face (any mode) that picks one face of a locked size, and not the other, takes the other face along: Translate and Rotate move it rigidly, Offset moves it by the distance times the dot of the two normals, so the gap stays. Only flat parallel pairs measured face to face are locked. An unlocked size is re measured on every rebuild as before. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `symmetric` and `lock_size`; they are listed in the pull request. TR265 is complete.
Status: Default
Reason: TR265 item 3; reusing the measured size keeps one way to set a size, with its naming and undo.

D801: Turning checks, more milling checks, and the printer's process (2026-11-04, TR295, TR296, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Turning (`manufacturing.turning`): the turning axis is the axis of the biggest cylinder; faces neither round about it (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus on that axis) nor flat and square to it are one `not_turned` finding; flat faces square to the axis that overlap radially give `narrow_groove` (facing, under `min_groove`) and `thin_wall` (back to back, under `min_wall`); this pairing reads ring faces by their edges' distance from the axis, since a ring's centre is not on the ring. A part with no cylinder gives `no_axis`. (2) Milling (TR296 items 2 and 4): `deep_pocket` when two facing walls are deeper (their extent along the first setup direction) than `pocket_depth_ratio` (4) times the gap; `tall_wall` when a wall is taller than `wall_height_ratio` (10) times its thickness; `raised_text` when a boss extrude uses a sketch with text. 0 turns a ratio off. (3) TR295 item 2: printer profiles get `process` (`fdm`, `resin`, `powder`), `layer_height`, `min_hole` (smallest round hole) and `max_bridge`, edited in Preferences, Printing; old preferences load with the defaults. The Manufacturing Check's profile for the active printer's process starts from that printer's values (`manufacturing_values`: `min_wall`, `nozzle`, `layer_height`, `min_round_hole`, `max_bridge`); the print profiles gained those keys. The print process checks themselves are TR299 and the moulding checks TR298 (Medium items, spec section 13): with this, TR295 and TR296 are complete.
Status: Default
Reason: TR295, TR296; advisory checks from FDCAD's own general values, as D790.

D802: Stencil text, kerf and tab minimums (2026-11-04, TR297 items 1 and 3, Phase 7B Stage 2). (1) Sketch text gets `stencil` and `bridge` (mm, 0 for 12 percent of the height; saved only when set). Each glyph is bridged before it is placed: for every inner loop (a counter) an upright strip `bridge` wide (never wider than the counter) through the counter's middle, from below to above the glyph, is cut out of the glyph, which splits the ring so the island stays joined to the sheet. Upright is in the glyph's own frame, so the bridges stand square to the base line, also on a curve. (2) The Sheet Metal feature gets `kerf` (optional length, default 0). Tab and Slot draws each slot narrower by the kerf on each side in the sheet's plane (the cut widens a slot and thins a tab by about a kerf each), so after cutting the fit is the typed clearance; the slot's depth through the wall keeps the clearance. Finger joints (TR246) will use the same value. The manufacturing profile's own kerf stays the shop's value for its checks. (3) The sheet metal check adds `short_tab` (tab length under `min_tab`, 2, times the thickness) and `shallow_tab` (depth under the thickness). (4) Still open in TR297: a bend radius below the material's minimum, which needs part materials (TR78); PLAN.md keeps TR297 unticked until then. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the text keys and `kerf`; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR297; compensating the kerf in the model is the usual way laser cut parts are drawn, and stencil bridges only change text that asks for them.

D803: Part material (2026-11-04, TR78, owner decision approved in D750, widening D29; TR297's last rule). (1) `core/materials.py`: a `Material` is a name, a density in g/cm3, an optional colour and an optional smallest bend ratio (inside radius over thickness) for sheet metal. The library is FDCAD's own general values (printing plastics, acrylic, plywood, aluminium, mild and stainless steel, copper, brass) with the densities the user sets in Preferences, Printing laid over it, and the user's own named densities after it: the existing density table is the user's material list, so no second table is added. (2) The part's material is `Document.material`, saved as a top level `material` key only when set (older parts save unchanged; a damaged entry is dropped on open, so the part still opens). (3) Tools, Material (no default key) and the new Material row of the tree (under Appearances; double click or right click) open a dialog: material, density (g/cm3, with lb/in3 beside it), and Use its colour for the part; OK is one undo step (`SetMaterial`, no rebuild). (4) Mass Properties and Print Estimate list the part's material and start from it; choosing another there does not change the part. (5) The sheet metal check adds `tight_bend` when a bend's inside radius is under the material's bend ratio times the thickness; parts without a material, or materials with no bend value, are not checked. With this, TR297 is complete. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the `material` key; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR78; one material per part, kept in the file, used where density matters.

D804: Guide curves for Sweep and Loft, and a loft centerline (2026-11-04, TR55, owner approved in D750; amends D219 item 4 and D220 item 6). Item 5 asked for a kernel test first: the kernel's own guide mode keeps the section rigid (D219) and the probes in spec section 19 failed, so FDCAD builds both from sections of its own and the kernel's smooth surface through sections (ThruSections), which is reliable. The probes recorded in the tests: a circle with one straight guide gives the exact cone (1e-9), a rectangle with two guides the exact pyramid frustum, a bent path with a parallel guide the bent tube to 1e-3, a loft between two squares with a straight guide the exact box. (1) Sweep (`refs.guides`, one or two sketches, curves or edges; `sweep_guides.py`): 41 stations spaced evenly by length; the profile is carried along the path with the least turning (double reflection, as D703) and then, in the plane square to the path, turned and scaled so the points where it touched the guides land on them: one guide turns and scales about the path point, two guides fix a similarity (turn, scale and a move in the plane). Each guide must touch the profile's outline (within 0.001 mm) and not start on the path. The sweep stops where the shortest guide ends, with a warning (`guide_short`). Holes in the profile follow too and are cut. Faces keep the sweep's names (`side/<entity>`, `cap/start`, `cap/end`). Orientation and Twist are ignored with guides. (2) Loft (`refs.guides`, any number; `loft_guides.py`): 8 sections are added in each span by blending the two profiles edge by edge (corners stay corners), so every profile needs the same number of edges (the next profile's edges are turned round to line up with the first's); each section is pushed by how far each guide leaves the straight line between its touching points, weighted by closeness along the outline to where that guide touches (one guide moves the whole section). Each guide must touch every profile; errors name the guide and the profile. (3) Loft `refs.centerline` and `sections` (1 to 50, default 4): the added sections are turned square to the centerline and centred on it. Guides or a centerline need an open, solid loft (not closed, not thin), and the kernel's own alignment and end constraints are not used then. (4) Panels: a Guide Curves group in Sweep and Loft (a list; Add takes the chosen sketch or curve; Pick edges as guides takes edges from the view), and Centerline and Number of Sections in Loft. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `guides`, `centerline` and `sections`; they are listed in the pull request. Stage 2 of Phase 7B is complete.
Status: Default
Reason: TR55; sections FDCAD computes, joined by the kernel's surface through sections, give exact results where the kernel's guide mode does not.

D805: Printing and moulding checks (2026-11-04, TR298 item 1, TR299, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/manufacturing_print.py`, FDCAD's own general values. Printing (FDM, resin, powder share the rules; their profiles get `pin_ratio` 8, `text_nozzles` 8, `thread_layers` 4 beside the printer values of D801): `slender_pin` (a whole outside cylinder taller than pin_ratio times its diameter), `thin_wall` (back to back walls under min_wall plus 0.2 percent of the part's largest size), `small_hole` (under min_round_hole), `long_bridge` (a flat face looking down, above the lowest point, narrower side over max_bridge), `small_text` (sketch text under text_nozzles times the nozzle) and `fine_thread` (a modelled thread with a pitch under thread_layers layers). Moulding (profile gets `wall_change` 2 and `rib_ratio` 0.6): `thick_wall`, `thin_wall`, `wall_change` (thickest over wall_change times thinnest), `rib_thick` (a narrower wall thicker than rib_ratio of the thickest), `sharp_inside` (inside corners between flat faces, one finding) and `no_draft` (flat faces along Z, the pull direction). Boss wall and height, corner radius against wall and draft by height (TR298 item 1's last parts) are read as the inside corner and no draft findings; TR298 item 2 (Rib and Mounting Boss sized from a wall) is not built and is in IDEAS.md. Every process now has checks.
Status: Default
Reason: TR298, TR299; advisory checks that read the geometry, like D790.

D806: Save a Copy and the tree filter (2026-11-04, TR97, TR95, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) File, Save a Copy and Save a Copy and Open (no default keys): the document is written with `fdef.save` to the chosen file (offered as "<name> copy.fdprt" beside it); the session keeps its path, title and unsaved state, and no undo step is made. A copy onto the part's own file or a file open in another tab is refused, as Save As does (D723). An open sketch is finished first, as for Save As. (2) The tree tab holds a filter box and a state choice (All, Errors and Warnings, Suppressed, With Comments) above the tree (`ui/tree/tree_filter.py`); rows whose text holds the typed text (any case) show with every row above them, and are opened; the filter is applied again after each refresh (`FeatureTree.refreshed`). The filter only hides rows; it changes nothing in the part.
Status: Default
Reason: TR97, TR95.

D807: Undo To and delete with dependents (2026-11-04, TR208, TR201, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Edit, Undo To: a submenu filled when opened with the active part's last 25 steps by their undo text, newest first; choosing one sets the undo stack's index to that step, which undoes it and every later step (each still on Redo). No toolbar drop down is added, since FDCAD has no Undo button outside the Edit menu. (2) Delete of a feature that other features use opens a list (`ui/tree/delete_dialog.py`) of every feature and sketch that depends on it directly or through another (`rollback.dependents`), each ticked: Delete removes the feature and the ticked ones in reverse tree order as one undo step (the basic choice is to delete them all; unticking is the advanced choice). The feature's own sketch keeps its separate question (T9.10). Graphs that read it are named, not deleted. Cancel is the default button. (3) The Delete key in the 3D view with faces picked opens a menu: Delete Feature (the feature that made the first face, through the same dependents list) and Delete Face (the Delete Face feature on the picked faces).
Status: Default
Reason: TR208, TR201.

D808: The tree follows the selection (2026-11-04, TR200, Phase 7B Stage 3). `ui/main_window/tree_follow.py`. (1) A pick in the view (the last picked shape) opens the tree's folders above the feature that made it and scrolls it into sight, without changing the tree's selection (selecting would start the tree's own behaviours such as dimensions on the model); the first scroll position is kept and an empty pick scrolls back to it. Preference "Tree opens to the feature of a picked face or edge", on by default. (2) Go To Feature on the right click menu of a face or edge shows the tree tab and selects the feature. (3) Hovering a feature row draws that feature's own faces (names starting with its id) with the view's highlight after 120 ms; leaving the tree clears it. Preference "Hovering a tree row shows its feature in the view", on by default.
Status: Default
Reason: TR200.

D809: Bounding Box (2026-11-04, TR69, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `bounding_box` (`core/features/bounding_box.py`; Evaluate tab, Measure group dropdown; no default key). `box_shape` box or cylinder; `orient` axes (the part's axes: the box never turns), best_fit (the kernel's oriented bounding box, optimal mode; a cylinder's axis is the longest of its directions) or frame (`refs.frame`: a plane feature or coordinate system, by its datum, else a plane or flat face); `make_solid` adds the box as a separate body, else it is drawn as an edge outline (`extras.reference`) and the part is unchanged. The box is the optimal axis aligned box of the part in the frame; the cylinder's centre is the middle of that box across its axis and its radius the furthest mesh point (whole arrays, 0.01 mm chord), so it can be a little larger than the smallest possible cylinder. Measured values (D793): `length`, `width`, `height` (frame X, Y, Z; a cylinder's diameter twice) and `volume`, read in formulas as numbers (mm, mm3). The parameter is `box_shape`, not `shape`, because panel labels are shared by name and `shape` is the Fill Pattern's cut shape. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR69.

D810: Custom properties (2026-11-04, TR82, owner decision approved in D750). (1) `Document.properties`: rows of name (letters, digits, spaces, underscores), kind (`text`, `number`, `date`, `yes_no`), value text and optional `configs` (configuration name to value text), saved as a top level `properties` list only when there are rows; damaged rows are dropped on open (`core/properties.py`). (2) A value starting with "=" is a formula worked out after the equations: it can use variables, feature values, measured values and, for properties only, the part's `volume@Part`, `area@Part` and `mass@Part` (the finished part, worked out at the end of each rebuild when the part has properties; mass from the part's Material, D803). Plain number rows (not formulas) are equation names `"<name>@Properties"`; formula rows cannot be used by equations, which keeps solving free of loops. (3) Tools, Custom Properties (also on the part's right click menu; no default key): a table with Name, Kind, Value, a column for the active configuration's own value, and the worked out Result; Add, Remove, Work Out; OK is one undo step (`SetProperties`). (4) 3MF export (File, Export and Open in Slicer) writes the rows that work out as `fdcad:<name>` metadata (spaces become underscores) in the namespace `https://fdcad.org/3mf/properties/2026`; the file stays valid against the consortium schema. Not built: STEP export of properties (needs the STEP writer's product data, recorded in IDEAS.md) and sketch text from properties (TR54 is a separate item). FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the `properties` key; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR82.

D811: Symmetric linear pattern (2026-11-04, TR140, Phase 7B Stage 3). `symmetric1` and `symmetric2` (optional booleans, with spacing fill only): the copies at steps -1 to -(count - 1) are added in that direction. Instance numbers stay as before on the near side (1 to count); the far side's copies are numbered count + 1 onward, so existing Skip lists keep meaning the same copies. With two directions the grid covers every combination. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the two keys; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR140.

D812: The printer's fit values in equations (2026-11-04, TR180, Phase 7B Stage 3). The app keeps the printer in use's fit tolerance in `Document.measured["__printer__"]` (never saved): set when a part opens and again after Preferences change, when parts whose value changed rebuild. `printer_names` adds the length names `"fit_tolerance@Printer"` (the gap per side) and `"clearance_fit@Printer"`, `"slip_fit@Printer"`, `"press_fit@Printer"` (the diameter change of each preset, as the Hole Tool's fit adds, D311) to every solve. Without an app (scripts, tests) FDCAD's default tolerance (0.2 mm) is used, so formulas always have a value. A part opened on a computer with another printer takes that printer's values, which is the point of the item.
Status: Default
Reason: TR180.

D813: Primitive solids (2026-11-04, TR127, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `primitive` (`core/features/primitive.py`; Features tab, in the Lofted Boss dropdown; no default key). `kind` box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, wedge, prism or tube; `operation` boss or cut with Merge as other bosses; sizes `length`, `width`, `height`, `top` (wedge: height at the far end, 0 for a sharp edge), `diameter`, `diameter2` (cone top), `inner` (tube), `ring` and `tube` (torus), `sides` (prism, 3 to 64); `centred`. Each solid is made standing on its own XY plane at the origin with Z up (centred moves its middle to the origin) and placed on `refs.frame` (a plane or coordinate system by its datum, a plane or flat face through its point; for a face, the face's middle, which Bounding Box now uses too) or the part's axes. Faces are named by position (`<fid>/face#k`), which the weak name checks cover (D720); primitives have no sketch entities to name faces after. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR127.

D814: Esc stops a rebuild or a slow preview (2026-11-04, TR126, Phase 7B Stage 3). Esc in the 3D view, or in a feature panel, first checks for running work: a rebuild of the active part, or (with a feature panel open) a preview being worked out. Then it asks (Yes is the default, since the user pressed Esc on purpose) and stops it: the rebuild through the session's cancel (the cancelled rebuild keeps the last finished features and says so, audit D3 item 12), the preview through its cancel event, keeping the last finished preview and the open panel. With nothing running, Esc does what it did before (cancel the panel, leave Isolate). Slow work with its own Cancel button (Manufacturing Check, mass properties) is unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: TR126.

D815: Extrude along a picked direction (2026-11-04, TR239, Phase 7B Stage 3). Extrude gets `refs.direction` (a plane feature's normal, a reference axis, a sketch line or a model edge, resolved as a direction) and `depth_along` (`direction`, the default, or `normal`). The direction is turned to leave the sketch on the side of its normal, then Reverse flips it as before; within about 1 degree of the sketch plane it is refused. With `normal` the direction is scaled so its normal part is 1, so every distance (blind, mid plane, the up to conditions and Through All reach) is measured square to the sketch. The panel's Direction 1 group gets Along (Square to the sketch, the planes and axes before the feature, or an edge picked in the view) and Depth measured (shown only with a direction). A typed vector is not offered: an axis or sketch line gives any direction. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `refs.direction` and `depth_along`; they are listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR239.

D816: Extrude twist and scale, sweep scale (2026-11-04, TR240, TR241, Phase 7B Stage 3). Both use the section method of D804 (`core/features/law_sections.py`): 25 copies of the profile, each moved, turned and scaled, joined by the kernel's surface through sections, with the extrude's or sweep's face names. (1) Extrude `end_twist` (angle) and `end_scale` (factor): the profile turns about the line through its centre along the extrusion and scales about that centre, both evenly from nothing to the end value. Only a Blind extrusion in one direction from the sketch plane, without draft or Thin Feature; anything else is refused with what to change. The panel writes them only when they are not 0 and 1, so other extrudes save unchanged. One scale for both X and Y: a separate X and Y factor needs a non uniform transform the section method does not take, and is in IDEAS.md. (2) Sweep `scale_start`, `scale_end` and `scale_law` (`linear`, or `smooth`: a half cosine): the profile is carried with the least turning (as D703 and D804) and scaled about the path's start point. A twist angle with a scale is refused, as the spec says. Exact: a 2 by 4 profile scaled 1 to 2 along 20 mm gives the frustum's volume to 1e-4.
Status: Default
Reason: TR240, TR241.

D817: Curve through points (2026-11-04, TR61, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `point_curve` (`core/features/point_curve.py`), a curve feature (D291): the kernel's interpolated curve through the points in order (closed: periodic). Points come from `refs.points` (vertices, sketch points or reference points, which win when present) or `data.points` (mm, in `refs.frame` when set: a plane, coordinate system or flat face, whose face frame starts at the face's middle). A text file is read only by the panel (Load File and Reload: three numbers a line, any of space, comma, tab or semicolon; other lines skipped; at most 5000 points) and its points are stored, with `data.file` kept as a note, so opening a part never reads a file (CLAUDE.md 5.10). Two points in a row at one place, or fewer than two, are errors. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; it is listed in the pull request.
Status: Default

D818: Measured values and saved measurements (2026-11-04, TR190, TR191, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `measurement` (`core/features/measurement.py`): `refs.items` (one or two faces, edges or vertices, resolved with the usual naming rules every rebuild; none measures the whole part's volume and area) measured with the Measure tool's own code. Its values are measured values (D793): `distance`, `length`, `diameter`, `radius`, `area`, `angle` (in degrees, as the user reads it), `dx`, `dy`, `dz` and `volume`, 0 when the items have none; features below it can use them in formulas and update in the same rebuild, features above get the ordering error of D793. The view shows a label "<name>: <main value>" at the items (the Show All Dimensions labels, always on for measurements) and a line between two items' nearest points. Measure gets Keep, which adds the feature (one undo step). X, Y and Z parts are the dx, dy, dz values. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; it is listed in the pull request.

Hide All Types remembers each tick, turns all off, and a second time restores them. Sketch dimension tags in the 3D view are Show All Dimensions; there is no separate kind. Rows keep their index in the panel's own order, so `select(n)` and the fix buttons work after sorting. Highlighting, fixes and Open Feature are unchanged.

D821: Table Driven Pattern (2026-11-04, TR58, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `table_pattern` (`core/features/table_pattern.py`), built on the shared pattern code like the sketch driven pattern. Rows are stored in the part as `data.rows` (`[x, y]`, or `[x, y, false]` for a row ticked off), so a loaded file is a one time read. `refs.frame` (coordinate system, plane or flat face, read with `frame_from_ref`) gives the origin and the X and Y axes, else the part's; `refs.point` is the seed's reference point, else its centre. A copy moves the reference point to origin + x X + y Y, keeping the seed's height along the frame normal, so a table typed for a plane works on parallel faces. A row at the reference point is the seed and makes no copy. Row k is instance k, so the usual skip list and the Skip copies fix apply. Paste and files read two numbers a line split by spaces, tabs, commas or semicolons; other lines (headers) are skipped. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; it is listed in the pull request.

D822: Sketch Merge (2026-11-04, TR40, Phase 7B Stage 3). Merge is listed with the relations for two picked points, but it is an edit, not a stored relation: `core/sketch/ops/merge.py` replaces the second point by the first in every curve, relation and dimension (and `measure_to`), removes relations and dimensions left between the point and itself, and deletes the second point; one sketch undo step. The first picked point stays where it is (a point copied from part geometry is kept over a plain one); the solver moves the rest. Two ends or points of one curve cannot merge (that would collapse the curve), so Merge is not offered for them. A real point merged with a construction point stays real. Saved files gain no new relation type.

Reason: TR40.

D823: Select Loop and Select Tangent (2026-11-04, TR92, Phase 7B Stage 3). Topology lives in `core/naming/loops.py`. A loop is the wire of a face that holds the edge, in wire order. The flip handle is the menu item itself: Select Loop again on the same edge turns to the next face of that edge (cheaper than a view handle, same result). The inner loop (spec item 2) comes from a picked face: with a face in the selection that holds the edge, its wire through that edge is used, so a hole edge gives the inner loop; Ctrl click is left as it is. Partial loop: Start Partial Loop remembers the first edge, End Partial Loop Here on another edge selects the run between them along a loop holding both, the shorter way by edge count. Select Tangent: faces across edges where both normals agree at the edge middle within 1e-3 rad, repeated; edges by the existing tangent chain walk.
Status: Default
Reason: TR92.

D824: Thin feature auto fillet (2026-11-04, TR65, Phase 7B Stage 3). Extrude params `thin_fillet` (flag) and `thin_fillet_radius` (the inside radius). The wall face of an open sketch is built as before, then its bend corners are rounded in 2D (`BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet2d`) before it is extruded: a corner whose bisector points into the face is an outside corner and gets radius + wall, the other side gets the radius, so the wall stays even. Corners on the two end edges stay square, and smooth joins are left alone. The round faces are named `side/<e1>+<e2>/round_outer` and `/round_inner` (the two sketch entities sorted), so references stay stable when other corners change. Closed profiles have no open corners and ignore it. Revolve has no thin option yet and Sweep's thin wall is built another way, so only Extrude (and Loft, which shares the thin profile code but does not offer the setting) get it; the setting sits next to Cap ends, which is also Extrude only. A radius too big for the lines gives an error naming the fix. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the two params; listed in the pull request.

D825: Offset Body and Shell corners (2026-11-04, TR129, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `offset_body` (`core/features/offset_body.py`): params `distance`, `inward`, `corners` ("sharp", default, or "rounded"); `refs.bodies` (a face of the body, first one used) is needed only with several bodies. It runs the kernel's offset of the whole solid (the same call Shell uses for a closed hollow) with intersection joins for Sharp and arc joins for Rounded, and checks the result is a valid solid. Each face's moved face keeps the original face name, so later features keep their references; new round faces are `<fid>/round`. A shrink past the thinnest part, or a sharp join the kernel cannot make, gives an error with the fix. Shell gets an optional `corners` param: without it, the old behaviour (sharp, then rounded when sharp fails); with it, only that join. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type and the Shell param; listed in the pull request.

A loft profile ref that is a vertex, a sketch point (`sketch_entity` naming a Point) or a reference point feature becomes a point section, allowed only first or last; it goes to the kernel loft as an end vertex. A point end has no constraint of its own: a start or end constraint other than Default or None at a point end is an error naming the fix (the spec's "the end constraint applies at the point" would need the kernel to bend the loft's tip, which the end vertex loft does not offer; recorded here for a later look). Close Loft, Thin Feature and guides are refused with a point end. Face names are as before, taken from the first profile that is not a point; the pointed end has no cap face. D827: Export each configuration (2026-11-04, TR196, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/io/export_configs.py`: for each chosen configuration a deep copy of the part is switched to it and rebuilt from scratch with its own engine, then written as STEP (plain, no colours), STL or 3MF (the part's saved mesh settings, no print orientation), or saved as a part file with that configuration active. Files are "<part> <configuration>.<ext>" with characters not allowed in file names replaced by "_". Failures (unknown names, no solid, kernel errors) are caught per configuration; features with errors are left out and noted. `Export log.txt` lists every configuration's outcome. The UI copies the document before starting the background job, so the open part is never touched off the UI thread. Picked configurations, the file kind and the folder come from one dialog under File, Export.

D828: Scale to fit the printer (2026-11-04, TR185, Phase 7B Stage 3). `orientation.fit_to_volume` lays the part flat as set, then tries turns about the build direction every 5 degrees from 0 to 175: the first turn that fits wins with no scale; otherwise the turn that needs the least shrinking, with factor min(volume / size) over X, Y and Z (a hair under, so it fits within tolerance). The part is never enlarged. The fit (factor, degrees) is kept on the tab only (view state, not saved, like D353's preview but unlike the saved lay flat face), and `placement`, `print_shape`, `print_shape_faces`, `check_fit` and `volume_shapes` take it, so STL, 3MF (as the build item transform), Open in Slicer and the build volume all agree. Save Print Scale as Feature adds a uniform Scale feature about the origin with the factor (one undo step) and keeps only the turn on the tab. Commands sit in the Lay Face Flat dropdown.
Status: Default
Reason: TR185.

D829: Turn a relation or dimension off (2026-11-04, TR109, Phase 7B Stage 3). Relation and Dimension get `off` (saved as `"off": true` only when set, so older sketches save unchanged). The solver skips off relations when building (keeping relation indexes, so conflict marks still point at the right items), skips off dimensions like driven ones, and leaves off coincident relations out of point grouping and fully defined checks. Off items are drawn in the reference colour with a dashed line; a dimension's text ends with "(off)". Sketch right click on relation tags or a dimension offers Turn Off, or Turn On when all picked items are off; one sketch undo step. Copies and patterns of sketch items keep the flag. Configurations: paths `<sketch id>.r<index>:off` and `<sketch id>.d<n>:off` read and write the flag, so a configuration can hold its own state (spec item 2); there is no separate menu item for "off in this configuration only": the configuration table holds it like any other value.
Status: Default
Reason: TR109.

D830: Equation editor comfort (2026-11-04, TR194, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type ahead: the value column uses a line edit whose completer matches the word before the cursor (a quoted name or a plain word) against every name the part's formulas can use (quoted) and the function names, case insensitive and matching anywhere; picking replaces that word. Filter hides rows whose name, value and comment do not hold the text; Sort orders each section by name with the Add row last (no column sort, which would mix the sections). Several rows can be selected and deleted together. Disable (equations only): the row's formula is kept in the feature's `data.off_equations` (value name to formula) and the value keeps its current number as plain text, so the rebuild ignores it; enabling restores the formula; deleting a disabled row drops it. Replace Name finds the first name the current row uses (its target or a name in its formula) that no longer exists and replaces every use with a picked name. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the `off_equations` data key; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR194.

D831: Right click to move on (2026-11-04, TR207, Phase 7B Stage 3). With a feature panel open, a right click in the 3D view first asks the panel's form for its next pick box (`next_pick`, in panel order among the shown boxes); if there is one it becomes active, the status bar names it and no menu opens. On the last box (or a form without pick boxes) the existing menu with OK and Cancel opens (T9.4), so "ready" means "no box after this one" rather than a check of every required pick, which the panel already does on OK. The body tool forms (patterns, direct edit, bodies, deform) implement it; the older feature forms (fillet, shell, sweep and so on) route picks by their own rules and keep the OK and Cancel menu.

Reason: TR207.

D832: Rotate about a picked item (2026-11-04, TR209, Phase 7B Stage 3). A middle button press and release that moves no more than the drag threshold sets the turning centre to the part point under the cursor (off the part: cleared); the status bar says which. While a centre is set, or Keep the model upright is on, a middle drag turns the camera itself from where the drag started: sideways about the view's up direction (or the model Z axis when upright is kept) and up and down about the view's right direction, both through the centre, pi/400 radians a pixel. Otherwise the kernel's own turning is used as before. The centre is view state of each part's view and is not saved. Keep the model upright while turning is a General preference (`view/lock_up`, default off).
Status: Default
Reason: TR209.

D833: Part templates (2026-11-04, TR217, Phase 7B Stage 3). A template is an ordinary part file with the default features only, saved to `<data folder>/templates/<name>.fdprt` by File, Save as Template (`core/templates.py`). It keeps the units, global variables, the part colour (face, feature and body colours name items of the old part, so they are left out), print setup without the laid flat face, material and custom properties, and the active printer profile's name in `extra.template_printer`. New Part lists the templates; choosing one disables the unit choice (the template has its own), opens a new unsaved part from it, and makes its printer the active profile when one with that name exists. Grid, decimals and display settings in the spec are app preferences in FDCAD, not part settings, so a template does not carry them. A template file that still has features (a part saved into the folder by hand) starts empty all the same.
Status: Default
Reason: TR217.

D834: Round All Corners (2026-11-04, TR227, Phase 7B Stage 3). Corners are points where exactly two of the selected lines meet end to end (`corners_of`, in line order, numbered from 1 in the dialog); points with three or more lines are not profile corners and are left alone. Each corner uses the existing sketch fillet (constrained corners kept as a corner point, as Sketch Fillet does). The first rounded corner carries the one radius dimension and the others get Equal to it (the shared dimension of spec item and TR48 item 3); corners with their own radius get their own dimension. Corners that cannot take the radius are skipped and listed; if none can, nothing changes. The work is tried on a copy first, so a refusal never leaves half a change, and the real change is one sketch undo step. Lines only for now: arcs, ellipses and splines are corners of TR48, still open. The command sits in the sketch right click menu when two or more lines are selected.
Status: Default
Reason: TR227.

D835: Pause rebuilds and checkpoints (2026-11-04, TR276, Phase 7B Stage 3). Pause is per part (session state, not saved). While paused, a rebuild request only marks the part out of date (status bar); undo commands work as usual. Rebuild leaves the pause and rebuilds; Rebuild and Stay Paused rebuilds and moves the discard point to now; Discard Paused Edits sets the undo stack back to the discard point (so it is itself undoable with Redo) and leaves the pause. A checkpoint is `data.checkpoint: true` on a feature, set from the tree menu as one undo step and saved with the part. Each rebuild builds a copy of the part with its rollback bar at the first checkpoint (a checkpoint below the bar, on the last feature or suppressed does nothing), so later features show as rolled back and the status bar names the checkpoint; Continue Rebuild rebuilds once past every checkpoint. "Asks to stop or go on" is the status bar message and the Continue Rebuild command rather than a dialog in the middle of the background rebuild. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the `checkpoint` data key; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR276.

D836: Lock a body (2026-11-04, TR269, Phase 7B Stage 3). Locked bodies are marked like hidden and see through bodies: face names in `appearance.locked_bodies`, saved with the part, set with an undoable command from the body row menu (Lock Body or Unlock Body; a locked body offers no Transform Handles). The view draws a locked body in the reference colour and unselects any face, edge or vertex of it right after every pick, box or lasso, so no tool or panel receives it ("cannot be changed" follows from "cannot be picked": every edit in FDCAD starts from picks or the tree). Hover highlighting is kept, which is what "can be snapped to" needs in the 3D view. Features that already reference the body keep rebuilding.
Status: Default
Reason: TR269.

D837: Tick boxes as formulas (2026-11-04, TR275, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature's tick box (a parameter whose spec is a plain on or off value) can carry a formula in `data.flag_rules` (name to formula). The equations engine solves them with the suppression formulas (`flag:<fid>:<name>` cells, which may use `true` and `false` as well as `suppressed` and `unsuppressed`), and the values step before each rebuild sets the parameter to the answer (nonzero is on). They are edited in the equations manager's Feature Values section as `<tick box>@<feature>`, with comments like the other rows; a name that is not a tick box of that feature is refused with the usual message. The panel's tick shows the current value and is overridden at the next rebuild while a formula exists (the panel does not grey it, to keep both form systems unchanged). FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the `flag_rules` data key; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR275.

D838: Replace a reference everywhere (2026-11-04, TR277, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/naming/replace.py` walks every feature's refs (nested dicts and lists) and swaps references equal to the old one: by feature id for sketches, planes and features (refs without a face or sketch item name), by name and kind for faces, edges and vertices. A feature is never pointed at an item below it. The UI offers it for features in the tree (Replace Everywhere) with candidates of the same kind (planes for planes) above the first user, and Delete the old one; all edits and the delete are one undo macro. The Delete dialog's Replace Instead button runs the same with Delete the old one ticked. Faces, edges and vertices are supported by the core walk; picking a face pair in the view for it is left to the repair tools (TR125), which already re-pick lost faces.
Status: Default
Reason: TR277.

D839: Airfoil profile (2026-11-04, TR257, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/sketch/airfoil.py` uses the published series equations: the four digit thickness with the closed trailing edge coefficient (so the base section is sharp), the four digit camber line, and the five digit standard camber lines 210 to 250 (and the same with a higher first digit for more lift, scaled from the design lift of 0.3). Reflexed five digit codes (third digit 1) are refused with a message. A point file's lines of two numbers are read in order and scaled to a unit chord from the smallest x, then thinned to 17 points keeping the nose. Points use cosine spacing, 9 per surface sharing the nose, for one sketch spline with the usual default handles. Trailing edge thickness is added as a straight taper on both surfaces (half each), so the nose is unchanged. The angle turns the profile about its nose; the nose goes at the sketch origin. Close the trailing edge adds a line across a thick edge, or Coincident at a sharp one. The command is in the sketch's empty space right click menu; one sketch undo step.
Status: Default
Reason: TR257.

D840: Self tapping holes (2026-11-04, TR255, Phase 7B Stage 3). Hole type `self_tapping`. Sizes come from FDCAD's own rule (the spec asks for that, not a standard): hole 0.8 of the nominal size, depth 2.5 sizes, for M2 to M6 and #2 to #10; the table is edited with the insert table's dialog and kept in the preferences (`holes/self_tapping`). The entry bevel is the near side countersink: on unless `near_csk` is False, 90 degrees, to 1.25 times the hole (the nominal size) unless its own diameter and angle are stored; the panel fills them from the table. Everything else (end conditions, positions, print fit) works as for a simple hole. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new hole type value; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR255.

D841: Shaft and bore shapes (2026-11-04, TR247, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `shaft_shape` on a picked cylindrical face; a face whose outward normal points away from its axis is a shaft, else a bore. Sizes are FDCAD rules from the diameter D (the spec gives no standard for these): hex with its corners on the round (across flats D sqrt(3)/2), flats 0.1 D deep, keyway D/4 wide and D/8 deep. A shaft is cut by (a large sleeve minus the shape) over the length; a bore is filled by (its round minus the shape) and cut by the shape, with the shape grown by `clearance` (default 0.1 mm) on every side, so the whole hole grows by the clearance and a shaft of the same D fits. Length (default the face's whole length along the axis) is measured from the face's start or end; `angle` turns the shape about the axis from the face's own x direction. New faces are `<fid>/shape`; the old faces keep their names through the boolean history. The param is `shaft_form` (not `kind`, whose label belongs to Primitive Solid). Keyways to a key standard are TR248, still open. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR247.

D842: A depth per region (2026-11-04, TR242, Phase 7B Stage 3). Each Selected Regions pick may carry its own `depth` ({expr, value}, typed in the part's units) inside the pick in `refs.regions`, so a removed region drops its depth with it and a new region uses the feature's depth (the spec's "new regions at zero depth with a warning" is replaced by "at the feature's depth": a zero depth cannot build, and nothing needs fixing first). With any own depth, the extrude builds one Blind extrusion per region and joins them, then combines as usual; other end conditions, Direction 2, Thin Feature and Cut Outside are refused with a message. Faces of region k > 1 are named `<fid>/r<k>/...`; the first region keeps the plain names. A region that the sketch split is still resolved by the existing region rules (D194): it follows the wider region with a warning rather than becoming two rows. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the per pick `depth` key; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR242.

D843: Pierce (2026-11-04, TR101, Phase 7B Stage 3). Not a solver relation: the sketch feature's `refs.pierce` lists `{point, curve}` pairs (a curve feature or another sketch by id, or a part edge reference), kept in refs so the rebuild knows the sketch depends on the curve. Before the sketch is solved on each rebuild, the point is moved to the crossing of the curve's edges with the sketch plane nearest to where it is, and a Fixed relation holds it there (the relation is added in the sketch when it is pierced, so dragging in the sketch does not fight it). No crossing: a warning, and the point stays. In the sketch, Pierce (right click one point) lists the curve features and sketches above this sketch (spec item 3's "picking a curve feature must work" is met by the list, without picking curves in the 3D view while sketching); Remove Pierce drops the pair and its Fixed relation. A deleted point drops its pierce at the next rebuild. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the `pierce` refs key; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR101.

D844: Cut away the model in front of the sketch plane (2026-11-04, TR113, Phase 7B Stage 3). FDCAD sketches in a 2D editor that shows the part as projected edges, an outline seen square to the plane and snap targets (D72, D250, TR6). Cut Away trims the part to the half behind the sketch plane (the side away from its normal, which faces the viewer) before those projections, in the background jobs, so the projected edges, outline and snaps leave out everything in front; the section at the plane is unchanged. It is display only and kept per sketch as `data.cut_away` (saved with the part, so it is "a tick per sketch"). The command Cut Away in Front sits in the empty space right click menu and can be given a key in the shortcut editor; there is no default key (D750 item 4). FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the `cut_away` sketch data key; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR113.

D845: Derived sketch (2026-11-04, TR49, Phase 7B Stage 3). A derived sketch is a sketch feature with `refs.derived_from` (the source sketch) and `data.derived_place` (dx, dy in mm, angle in radians). On every rebuild its geometry is the source's solved geometry turned about the sketch origin and moved, every point held by a Fixed relation (no other relations or dimensions), on its own plane; so it follows the original and cannot change shape. Opening it in the sketch editor is refused with a message; Edit Placement (typed X, Y and angle, one undo step) moves it; dragging it in the view is left out (typed values cover spec item 2). Relations to the original cannot be added because it has none of its own. Break Link writes the current copy into the sketch as ordinary geometry without the Fixed relations and drops the link. Sketch text items are not copied. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `derived_from` and `derived_place`; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR49.

D846: Replace Entity (2026-11-04, TR104, Phase 7B Stage 3). The new curve takes the old curve's entity id (its own id goes), which keeps the profile edge and face names (they are built from entity ids) and so keeps the features that use them. Relations and dimensions on the old curve stay on that id unless they cannot fit the new curve's kind (line only relations on a non line, round only relations and radius or diameter on a non round); those, and any that would join a point to itself, are removed and listed. Each end or centre point of the old curve hands its relations and dimensions to the nearest point of the new curve. The old curve is deleted with its unused points, or kept as a construction copy under a new id. The op is tried on a copy first and applied as one sketch undo step; selection order decides which curve is replaced (first picked).
Status: Default
Reason: TR104.

D847: Segment a curve (2026-11-05, TR103, Phase 7B Stage 3). Lines and arcs only (ellipses and splines have no equal length relation in the solver). Segment splits with the existing split op, piece by piece; line pieces get Equal relations so they stay equal, arc pieces start equal (Equal on arcs means equal radius, so no relation keeps their lengths equal). Equally Spaced Points splits a construction copy of the curve that shares its end points, so the curve itself stays one entity and the copy's inner points are spaced evenly. The count is asked for (2 to 100); editing it later is done by undoing and segmenting again rather than by a stored count, since the sketch has no feature that remembers it (spec item "the count can be edited later" is met only that way). One sketch undo step.
Status: Default
Reason: TR103.

D848: Corner point at rounded corners (2026-11-05, TR105, Phase 7B Stage 3). Already built (D-era P2.8 items 6 and 7): Sketch Fillet and Chamfer with Keep constrained corners (on by default) move the corner's relations and dimensions to a construction point held by an Intersection relation with the two lines, so they keep working when the fillet is added or changed. New: such a point (a construction point that is the first item of an Intersection relation) is drawn as a small x, so it reads as a corner and not as a loose point. No change to saved data.
Status: Default
Reason: TR105.

D850: Surface modelling approved (2026-11-04, owner). (1) The owner approved adding surface modelling to FDCAD. This reverses the PLAN.md section 2 out of scope item "Surface modeling tools" and amends D6 and the D750 note that surface building tools stay out of scope. The TR31 note in PLAN.md Phase 7A ("no surface building tools") is history and is left as written. (2) Scope: surface bodies (SURFACE_SPEC SF0) and seventeen tools: Extruded Surface, Revolved Surface, Swept Surface, Lofted Surface, Boundary Surface, Filled Surface, Planar Surface, Ruled Surface, Offset Surface, Extend Surface, Trim Surface, Restore Surface Edges, Join Surfaces, Delete Surface, Thicken, Thicken and Subtract, Cut by Surface (SF1 to SF17). Network surfaces, two rail sweeps, blend surfaces and free form control point editing stay out of scope. (3) The work is PLAN.md Phase 8, Surfacing (v1.4), one checklist line per SF section, built in the spec's order (SF18). (4) The Delete option of Delete Face, greyed by D510 and D529 item 4 because FDCAD had no surface bodies, is enabled by SF0.7 and SF14. (5) FDEF_SPEC.md stays an owner file: SF0.8 lists the changes it needs, and the implementer drafts them in `docs/plans/surfacing/FDEF_CHANGES.md` for the owner. (6) The spec was written by the manager session from a research round logged in docs/CLEAN_ROOM.md (2026-11-04). The kernel is OpenCascade 8.0.1 (D53); kernel notes in the spec were probed against it. (7) Implementers record their choices from D860 upward unless the manager gives another block; D790 to D849 are left for Phase 7B.
Status: Locked
Reason: Owner approval relayed by the coding session on 2026-11-04; the spec turns it into a phase.

D849: Select regions and chains in a sketch (2026-11-05, TR39, Phase 7B Stage 3). A click in empty sketch space (no tool, no drag) picks the smallest closed region under it from the region split the Selected Regions code uses, selects every curve of its outer loop and holes, and shades it; a click while something is selected only clears, as before, so the old "empty space clears" behaviour is kept. An outline with a gap makes no region, so it never shades (spec item 2: the missing shade is the cue). Dragging a curve that is part of a multi selection moves every selected curve's points together, and the solver keeps the relations. Select Chain adds to the selection while Ctrl is held. Display and selection only; nothing is saved.
Status: Default
Reason: TR39.

D860: Snap to grid, length and angle steps, snap filter (2026-11-05, TR102, Phase 7B Stage 3; D850 to D859 are taken by the surfacing spec). Grid spacing per part: `extra.sketch_grid` {major mm, minor count}, set from the sketch's empty space menu as one undo step; 0 keeps the automatic grid; minor lines thin out (doubling) below 6 px. Snap to Grid is a Sketch preference (off, while the grid shows, always) and applies only when the cursor does not snap to sketch or part geometry. Length and angle steps (preferences, default 1 mm and 15 degrees) apply while Alt is held during drawing, measured from the tool's last click; Alt was free while drawing, Shift and Ctrl are not. Snap Next Click To is a submenu of the drawing right click menu (end point, midpoint, centre, nearest); for one click only that kind counts, anything else becomes a free point. Tangent is left out of the filter: FDCAD adds tangency as an inferred relation, not as a snap kind. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `extra.sketch_grid`; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR102.

D861: Property panel behaviour (2026-11-05, TR206, Phase 7B Stage 3). Pin is a checkable header button; OK on a new feature while pinned runs Repeat Last Command, which starts the same command again (so it works for every command that can repeat). It stays out of the Tab chain so Tab still runs through the fields in reading order (Qt's own Tab, Space and arrow handling covers spec item 2's keys). Plain groups remember being folded by title for the session (checkable groups keep following their tick). Pick boxes of both form systems get a right click menu with Delete and Clear Selections; body tool pick boxes that take several picks grow from 4 to 10 rows with their contents. The active pick box was already highlighted (body tools, D831's next box).
Status: Default
Reason: TR206.

D862: Dimension preview on selection (2026-11-05, TR110, Phase 7B Stage 3). With one or two sketch items selected (and nothing else, no tool), the Smart Dimension preview of those picks follows the cursor while it is in empty space within 40 px of one of them; a click there starts Smart Dimension with the picks and places the dimension, so the usual value box opens. Further away the click clears the selection as before (keeping D849's clear-then-region behaviour). The kind of dimension follows the placement, as Smart Dimension already does (distance or angle for two lines, length or radius for one curve); the spec's "small choice of likely dimensions" for several items is served by that placement choice rather than a separate list. Also fixed: the TR102 change had dropped the Tangent relation name.
Status: Default
Reason: TR110.

D863: Insert SVG (2026-11-05, TR117, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/sketch/svg_import.py` reads the SVG with the standard library XML parser into the DXF drawing structure (all on one layer, units mm), so Insert SVG reuses Insert DXF's dialog, preview and placement. Files that declare their own XML entities are refused (no entity expansion), and the DXF size guard applies. Elements: line, rect (sharp corners), circle, ellipse, polyline, polygon, path (M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, A, Z, absolute and relative), with group and element transforms (matrix, translate, scale, rotate). Straight pieces become lines; circles stay circles unless a transform squashes them; Bezier pieces and elliptical arcs become splines through 7 points per piece (arcs: one point per 22.5 degrees); this keeps the spline count low while following the curve closely.
