Sizes: the root width in a physical unit over the view box width gives mm per user unit; otherwise 96 user units per inch. Y is turned upward. Text, images, styles and clip paths are counted as left out and named in the status bar.
Status: Default
Reason: TR117.

D864: Undercut analysis (2026-11-05, TR83, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/undercut.py` tries up to nine points inside each face (a 3 by 3 grid of its UV range, kept when inside the face). A point whose face turns toward the pull (or against it) is seen from that side when a ray from just off the point along that side hits nothing of the part. A face is above or below when all its tried points are seen from that side, straddle when some are and some are not, undercut when none are, and a side wall when every point is square to the pull (within 1e-3 of the cosine). The pull is a plane's normal, as in Draft Analysis, with Reverse; "rotate it live" is changing the plane or Reverse, which redraws at once. The tool window counts each group and Zoom selects and zooms to its faces. Runs in the kernel worker; display only.
Status: Default
Reason: TR83.

D865: Combine options (2026-11-05, TR128, Phase 7B Stage 3). Operation `exclusive`: picked bodies are folded pairwise as (A minus B) beside (B minus A), which leaves what lies inside an odd number of them. `keep_tools` keeps the tool bodies in the part: for subtract the picked tools, for add, common and exclusive every picked body after the first (the first is the one the result replaces). `keep_largest` keeps the largest solid of the result when it has several (by volume). Split keeps its own piece list (D-era P3.4), where any piece can already be kept or left out, so Keep Largest is offered on Combine only. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new operation value and the two flags; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR128.

D866: Gear profiles (2026-11-05, TR161, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch tool (not a curve feature), so the outline can be edited and dimensioned like any sketch geometry. `core/sketch/gear.py` uses the published involute geometry: pitch radius m z / 2, base radius r cos(alpha), addendum m (1 + x), dedendum m (1.25 - x), tooth thickness m (pi / 2 + 2 x tan alpha) on the pitch circle; each flank is one spline through 6 points of its involute (radial below the base circle), tips and roots are arcs. Rounded roots: a short spline into the root arc of about 0.38 m (an approximation of the cutter's trochoid, good enough for printing and laser cutting); internal gears have sharp roots. Diametral pitch converts to module as 25.4 / P. Sprockets: pitch diameter p / sin(180 / z), roller seats of radius 0.505 d1 + 0.069 d1^(1/3) over a 140 - 90 / z degree seat angle, straight flanks to the tip circle D + 1.25 p - d1; chain pitch and roller sizes for ANSI 25 to 60 and ISO 04B to 10B. Everything is centred on the sketch origin and joined end to end, one sketch undo step.
Status: Default
Reason: TR161.

D867: Multi colour inlays (2026-11-05, TR184, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `inlay` (`core/features/inlay.py`): the sketch (with its Selected Regions) is extruded as a Blind cut of `depth`, into the material whichever way that is; the material it removes (the common of tool and part) becomes a separate body named `<fid>/inlay/...`, and the part is cut by it, so the two fit exactly with no gap (the slicer's own settings handle overlap). 3MF export already writes each body as its own component of one object (D777), which is what a slicer needs to give the inlay another filament; the body names in the file follow the part's body order. A sketch that does not reach into the part is an error naming the fix. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR184.

D868: Linked child configurations (2026-11-05, TR195, Phase 7B Stage 3). A configuration item may carry `parent` (a configuration name) and `own` (the paths it sets itself). Every sync of the active configuration marks as own the paths whose value differs from the parent's, and drops paths that equal it again; then every child takes its parent's value for each path that is not its own, parents first, so chains work. Add Linked creates a child of the active configuration. A feature added while a linked child is active gets `<fid>.suppressed` true in every other configuration and false in the child (own in each child), inside the Add Feature undo step. Renaming a parent renames the link; deleting it unlinks its children. Marking in the list is the "linked to X, n own values" label. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs `parent` and `own` on configuration items; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR195.

D869: Magnet pockets (2026-11-05, TR179, Phase 7B Stage 3). Hole type `magnet`: `diameter` is the magnet's diameter or a block's width, `depth` its thickness, `magnet_length` a block's length (0 is round), so the existing hole parameters, fit presets and end conditions keep working. A round pocket is the ordinary revolved hole; a block is a box prism aligned with the sketch X axis (length along X). `magnet_relief` adds three 0.8 mm slots running 0.8 mm past a round pocket at 0, 120 and 240 degrees, or 0.8 mm squares centred on a block's corners. `magnet_skin` (blind only) starts the pocket that far under the face (the profile's top moves down, the depth grows by the skin), so the cut leaves a closed void to print the magnet into. The size list is common nominal neodymium sizes (names say round or block); Print Fit adds its offset to the diameter and length like other holes. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the type and its three parameters; listed in the pull request. Also reworded the Inlay error so it starts with a next step.
Status: Default
Reason: TR179.

D870: Ratio and difference relations (2026-11-05, TR226, Phase 7B Stage 3). Four relation types: `length_ratio` and `length_difference` keep their number in `Relation.value` (the field Offset already uses), so they are relations as the spec names them, not dimensions: a ratio has no unit, and dimensions are lengths or angles. The solver gives each line or arc a free length parameter (point to point distance for a line, arc length for an arc) and holds A = value x B, or A - B = value, with planegcs' parameter constraints. `equal_angle` (four lines) shares one free angle parameter between the two pairs; `equal_distance` (point, line, line) shares one free distance. Adding a ratio or difference from the menu asks for the value, starting at today's; added any other way it holds today's value. The relations are offered in Add Relation for fitting selections. Editing the value later means deleting and adding the relation again for now. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the four types; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR226.

D871: Standard keyways and keyseats (2026-11-05, TR248, Phase 7B Stage 3). Added to Shaft Shape's keyway as `key_standard` (`rule` default, so D841 parts rebuild the same; `metric`, `inch`, `woodruff`) rather than a new feature: the face pick, length, end, turn and bore clearance already fit. Tables in `core/features/keys.py`, compiled from the published standards: metric parallel keys by shaft range with width, shaft depth t1 and hub depth t2 (ISO/R 773, DIN 6885 A); inch square keys by shaft range (ANSI B17.1), half the key in each part; half moon keys by key number with width, key diameter and height (ANSI B17.2). The standards do not tie half moon keys to one shaft size, so FDCAD picks the widest key no wider than D / 4, then the largest key diameter no larger than D. The half moon seat is a disc of the key's diameter, its lowest point at the seat depth (height minus half the width), centred along the length; the hub keyway is half the width deep. Depths are measured from the round's top line, a simplification of the standards' chord based depths. Bores take the hub depth plus the clearance.
Status: Default
Reason: TR248.

D872: Dowel holes (2026-11-05, TR252, Phase 7B Stage 3). Hole type `dowel`, sized by the Standard choice: metric parallel pin diameters (ISO 2338 and ISO 8734 nominal sizes, 1 to 16 mm) or inch dowel pin diameters (1/16 to 3/4 in). The "fit helper" is the Pin fit choice in the panel: Press makes the hole the nominal size (pins are ground over size, so this is the usual interference with a reamed hole); Slip adds 0.02 mm, FDCAD's own rule for a sliding fit on machined parts. The depth starts at 1.5 x the diameter. The panel fills the diameter and depth from the size and fit; the feature itself stores only the diameter and depth like other holes, so nothing new reaches the file except the type name and the panel's `dowel_fit` memory. Dowel holes can have a near side countersink as a lead in.
Status: Default
Reason: TR252.

D873: Bearing seats (2026-11-05, TR251, Phase 7B Stage 3). Hole type `bearing`, built as a counterbore: `cbore_diameter` is the bearing's outside diameter (plus 0.02 mm for a slip fit), `cbore_depth` its width, and `diameter` the shoulder hole, half way between bore and outside diameter (FDCAD's rule: it clears the inner ring and keeps a shoulder under the outer one), 1 mm or a quarter of the width deep below the seat. Designations are common deep groove ball bearings (miniature 62x/69x/68x and 60xx/62xx series) with ISO 15 boundary dimensions. `bearing_groove` adds an internal retaining ring groove above the bearing: about 4.5 percent over the seat diameter and 1.1 to 1.85 mm wide by size band, FDCAD's rule close to the published ring tables; the seat and the hole both get deeper by the groove plus a 0.5 mm land so the bearing still sits its full `bearing_width` below the ring. Groove faces are named `.../groove/top|wall|bottom`. The panel reuses the counterbore rows (the head choice hides) and the dowel Pin fit choice. Linear bearings and motor face patterns are left for TR72 library content.
Status: Default
Reason: TR251.

D874: Retaining ring grooves (2026-11-05, TR249, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type `ring_groove` (one feature type per module) rather than another Shaft Shape option: it places a narrow groove at a position, not a shape over a length. It reuses Shaft Shape's round face pick, which also tells a shaft from a bore. Params: `ring_type` (`ring` or `e_clip`), `position`, `from_end`. Tables in the module, compiled from the published standards: external rings by shaft diameter (DIN 471) and internal rings by bore diameter (DIN 472), each giving groove diameter and width, matched within 0.3 mm of a listed size; E clips (DIN 6799) by shaft range, taking the largest groove the range allows. The groove is a ring cut from the groove diameter to 1 mm past the round. A round with no listed ring is an error naming the two nearest sizes. The table rows are the common sizes; more rows can be added as needed. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR249.

D875: Pattern counts of zero and one (2026-11-05, TR345, Phase 7B Stage 3). `count_of` accepts 0. A pattern with no instances to place (a count of 1 places only the seed, which is never copied; a count of 0 places nothing) returns the part unchanged; only a 0 count adds a warning (code `no_copies`) so the tree says why nothing happened, while a count of 1 stays quiet because it is a normal family member. Suppressed seed features are skipped; when every seed is suppressed (and no faces or bodies are picked) the pattern returns the part unchanged with the same warning. A warning rather than a new info level, since the tree has only OK, warning and error.
Status: Default
Reason: TR345.

D876: Thickness at a point (2026-11-05, TR349, Phase 7B Stage 3). Measure remembers the model point under the cursor (the 3D view's existing `cursor_point` signal, from the hover pick) at the moment a new item is picked. When exactly one face is picked, `Options.at` and the part's solid go to the worker, and `core/measure.thickness_at` projects the point onto the face, takes the inward normal (the outward normal reversed, by face orientation) and finds the nearest point where a line that way meets the solid again (`IntCurvesFace_ShapeIntersector`); the distance is the "Thickness here" row. No row when the line meets nothing (an open or odd face). The other parts of the item were already there: Measure pushes no undo step, the box has its own units list, and its frame list measures from the origin by default.
Status: Default
Reason: TR349.

D877: Two point and tangent circles (2026-11-05, TR317, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two more tools in the Circle drop down rather than modes of Circle, matching how Perimeter Circle was added (D512). 2 Point Circle reuses Perimeter Circle's point ties for snapped ends. Tangent Circle asks for three clicks; the first two must land on a line, arc or circle. Three curves: the circle starts at the middle of the three clicks with the mean distance to the curves as its radius; two curves and a spot: it starts at the spot, and a driving radius dimension holds that size so the user can type the radius. The tool solves a copy of the sketch first (circle plus Tangent relations) and adds nothing if that fails, so a bad pick never leaves a broken sketch; then it adds the circle at the solved place with the same relations. Several tangent circles exist for most picks, so the click positions choose which one.
Status: Default
Reason: TR317.

D878: Result line after each command (2026-11-05, TR290, Phase 7B Stage 3). The rebuild worker (off the UI thread) runs `core/rebuild/change_line.describe` when a rebuild reused earlier results: the first rebuilt feature that makes or changes the solid is the one just added or edited, and its body is compared with the body before it. The line gives the net volume change (two volume calls; booleans for added and removed separately would slow every rebuild) and the change in face count, in cm3 or in3 by the part's units. A full build (opening a file) keeps "Rebuilt in". The status label sends an accessibility name change event so screen readers read it.
Status: Default
Reason: TR290.

D879: Cable tie channels (2026-11-05, TR363, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `cable_tie`: sketch points (and line ends, as the Hole Tool reads them, reusing its placement code) on a face. Each point gets a loop: two entry slots from the face down to the tunnel floor, `span` apart along the sketch X axis turned by `angle`, and a tunnel under the face `cover` deep joining them; slots and tunnel are the strap's `tie_width` and `tie_thickness` plus `clearance` on every side (0.2 mm by default). "Through or under a wall" is the same loop on a wall's face. Support free top: the tunnel's section has a 45 degree point toward the face, rising half the tunnel width; when that would leave less than half the cover, the top is flat at half the cover instead (a short bridge). All loops are cut in one boolean. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR363.

D880: Profile offset on Extruded Boss and Cut (2026-11-05, TR344, Phase 7B Stage 3). `profile_offset` (a signed length, stored only when not zero, like End twist) offsets every profile face in its plane before the extrude, after picked regions or thin walls: `BRepOffsetAPI_MakeOffset` with arc joins, so outside corners round over and inside corners stay sharp, which is how a printed or cut part behaves. The offset edges carry their original sketch entity, so side faces keep their usual names. An offset that collapses the profile is a feature error asking for a smaller value. Revolve is left out: the spec names boss and cut only.
Status: Default
Reason: TR344.

D881: Mark results that did not rebuild (2026-11-05, TR352, Phase 7B Stage 3). The engine keeps building after a failed feature, as before (later features build on the last good part, so the user still sees something), but after the loop it marks every later solid feature with a warning (code `not_rebuilt`) naming the failed feature, and sets `RebuildReport.failed_at`. Marking is redone on each rebuild and never stored in the cache, so fixing the failure clears it. Measure shows an out of date note under its results and Mass Properties puts it above its values while `failed_at` is set. Non solid features (sketches, planes) are not marked. Also updated the robustness test for TR345: a count of 0 is now a warning, not an error.
Status: Default
Reason: TR352.

D882: Half lap joints (2026-11-05, TR364, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `half_lap` on two picked bodies. A plate's thickness direction is the normal of its largest flat face; the joint's height direction is the cross product of the two normals (parallel plates are an error). The crossing (common of the two plates) is measured along that direction and split at `depth_percent` (default 50): the first plate loses the other plate, grown, on one side of the split, the second plate the first one, grown, on the other side. Growth is clearance / 2 minus kerf / 2 on every side (an offset shape), so the slot is the other plate's thickness plus clearance minus kerf. Which side is "top" follows the sign of the cross product; either way the plates slot together. Mortise and tenon and snap joints are left for later, as the spec allows. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR364.

D883: Finger joints (2026-11-05, TR246, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `finger_joint` on two picked bodies. Plates must overlap at the corner (the usual way to model a box: each plate drawn to the outside), and that overlap block is what gets shared: it is split along the edge direction (the cross product of the two plates' thickness normals) into `finger_count` equal fingers (or as many as fit `finger_width`; 5 by default). Even fingers stay with the first plate and odd ones with the second; each plate loses the other's fingers. Each removed finger is lengthened along the edge by clearance / 2 minus kerf / 2 at both ends, so gaps open by the clearance and close by the kerf. Plates that only touch, with no overlap, are an error asking to extend one plate. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR246.

D884: Blend curve (2026-11-05, TR318, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch tool that adds an ordinary two point Spline (so it can be edited and dimensioned like any spline) using the picked curves' own end points, so it stays joined. Each handle starts along the curve's direction at that end, a third of the gap long (weight 1); dragging a handle is the weight. A line's handle also gets a coincident relation to the line, which keeps the blend tangent when the line moves; arcs and splines get no relation yet because the solver has no point on tangent relation, so their blends keep the shape they were made with. Curvature matched ends need a third control point per end, which the sketch spline does not have; left for a later change and noted in IDEAS. Clicks on curves near their ends; a click on an end point picks the curve that ends there.
Status: Default
Reason: TR318.

D885: Detach linked geometry (2026-11-05, TR340, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/sketch/links.detach` works on the picked entities that follow the model: those with a `source` (on the entity or its points) and curves held by a Fixed relation (how converted and projected curves are kept in place). It clears `source` on them and their points and removes the Fixed relations that touch them, so they become free geometry of the same shape; dimensions and other relations stay. One sketch undo step from the right click menu, shown only when the selection has such geometry. A detached curve may be under defined afterwards, which the sketch status shows as usual. Also reworded a Half Lap message so it starts with the next step.
Status: Default
Reason: TR340.

D886: O ring grooves (2026-11-05, TR250, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `oring_groove` with `cross_section` (the cord, a length) and `use` (`static`, `moving`, `face`). A picked round face makes a radial groove: on a shaft it is cut into the shaft (piston seal), in a bore it is cut out of the wall (rod seal), at `position` from an end, reusing Shaft Shape's face pick. A picked sketch makes a face seal: the sketch's closed profile is offset by half the groove width each way (TR344's offset) and the band is cut `depth` into the face the sketch is on. Groove sizes are FDCAD's rule from the common design guidance rather than one standard's table: depth 0.80 / 0.85 / 0.75 of the cord (about 20 / 15 / 25 percent squeeze) and width 1.4 / 1.3 / 1.5 of the cord. The feature computes squeeze and fill, puts them in `extras["oring"]`, and warns outside 10 to 30 percent squeeze or above 85 percent fill. Dash numbers are not a list in the panel yet; the cords of the five inch series and common metric cords are named in the tooltip and in `CORDS`. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR250.

D887: Pattern at model points (2026-11-05, TR365, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `point_pattern`, using the shared pattern code (seed, skip, merge, geometry options) like Sketch Pattern. Targets: `refs.targets` (vertices; round edges give their circle centre and axis; cylinder faces give their axis) and `refs.hole_faces` (flat faces: the centre and axis of each inner loop that is a circle). Copies are translations from the seed's reference point (`refs.point`; else, for feature seeds, the centre of the seed features' own solids, because the faces they leave can include a whole face they touched and pull the face centre away; else the seed's face centre). For targets with an axis the move along that axis is dropped, so copies keep the seed's height. Copies are not turned to match a target's normal: every target in the spec's examples (holes of a face, vertices of a plate) shares the seed's direction; turning can follow if needed. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR365.

D888: Turned outline (2026-11-05, TR319, Phase 7B Stage 3). The axis is the sketch's X axis through its origin, so no extra pick is needed (put the sketch on a plane through the axis). Worked out with the other model curves in the sketch's background job (`core/sketch/turned.py`): the part is meshed (0.1 percent of its size, at least 0.02 mm), and at 400 stations along the axis the largest distance from the axis is taken from mesh vertices and from where mesh edges cross each station; the distance from a line is convex, so a triangle's largest value in a slice lies on its edges, and everything runs in numpy (CLAUDE.md 5A.2). Points on a straight run are dropped (5 micron tolerance), and the profile is closed down to the axis at both ends and along the axis, as lines, added fixed like Silhouette. Shoulders come out as near vertical lines one station wide; exact arcs are not fitted.
Status: Default
Reason: TR319.

D889: Expected value checks (2026-11-05, TR359, Phase 7B Stage 3). Stored in `Document.extra["checks"]` (a list of kind, value, tolerance, and feature and key for a measurement), so files keep them with no schema change; `core/checks.py` reads them. The rebuild worker evaluates them after each rebuild when there are any (volume, optimal bounding box sizes, face count, hole count, or a Measurement feature's stored value), so the kernel work stays off the UI thread, and the report carries the results. Hole count: cylinder faces whose surface faces their own axis, counted once per axis. The status bar appends "Checks: n of m pass."; Tools > Expected Values edits them as one undoable step that rebuilds, and shows actual values and pass or fail. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) should mention `extra.checks`; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR359.

D890: Switch boss and cut (2026-11-05, TR387, Phase 7B Stage 3). Tree right click items on extrude, revolve, sweep and loft: the feature is replaced by a copy with `operation` flipped (one Replace Feature undo step; sketch, end conditions and refs untouched). Make Thin adds `thin_type` one direction and a 1 mm `thin_thickness`; Make Solid removes every `thin_` value. A name still in FDCAD's default form for the old operation takes the next default name for the new one; any other name stays.
Status: Default
Reason: TR387.

D891: Crush ribs (2026-11-05, TR403, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `crush_ribs` on a picked round face (Shaft Shape's pick tells a hole from a pin). `rib_count` ribs, evenly spaced, each a wedge section `rib_width` wide at the wall standing `rib_height` off it (into a hole, out from a pin), with a flat tip `rib_tip` wide in place of the spec's tip round (a flat prints the same at these sizes and keeps the section simple), sunk 0.05 mm into the wall so it fuses. They run `rib_length` (default the whole face) from `from_end`, and the first `rib_height` of each rib is cut back at 45 degrees as a lead in. Parameter names carry `rib_` so their panel labels do not clash with other features. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the new type; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR403.

D892: Hole size carry over setting (2026-11-05, TR66, Phase 7B Stage 3). A preference (`holes/carry_size`, on by default, so nothing changes for current users) shown as a tick box in the Hole panel's type group, where its effect is seen, rather than on a preferences page. The panel remembers the last size per hole type (`holes/last_sizes`) whenever the size settles; with the tick off, changing the type picks that type's remembered size (or keeps the current one when the type has none yet).
Status: Default
Reason: TR66.

D893: Trim keeps pieces as construction (2026-11-05, TR47, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Trim tool option (off by default). Rather than change each of the five trim modes, the tool copies the sketch before a trim and `core/sketch/ops/trim_keep.keep_trimmed` compares it with the result: for every old normal line, arc and circle, the parts no longer covered by a curve on the same line or circle are added as construction lines or arcs, in the same undo step. Other curve types (ellipses, splines) are trimmed as before without kept pieces. The spec's second item (dragging back over a trim to undo it) is left out: Undo already does that and a reverse drag would conflict with drag trim's own path.
Status: Default
Reason: TR47.

D894: Select bodies by size (2026-11-05, TR70, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Tools command opening a small dialog. Body volumes and a face reference per body are worked out in a background job (`core/body_sizes.sizes`), never on the UI thread. The limit is a percent of the largest body's volume (slider 1 to 100) with a smaller or larger choice. Select sets the view selection; Delete and Keep Only These add one Delete Body feature (option delete or keep) with the picked bodies' references, so the step is undoable and editable like any Delete Body. Also: a click in empty space now decides whether it places the selection's dimension (D862) from where the click is, not from the last hover.
Status: Default
Reason: TR70.

D895: Modify Sketch (2026-11-05, TR50, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch right click item opening a dialog (typed values with units and formulas) rather than a drag tool, since Move, Rotate and Scale Entities already cover dragging. It applies Move Entities' steps (TR1) to every entity not held to the part (no Fixed relation, no `source`, none of their points held), in a fixed order: scale, turn, flip, then move, all about the sketch origin. Flip mirrors point coordinates and swaps the ends of arcs and partial ellipses after a single mirror so they stay counter clockwise. Length dimensions scale with the scale (Move Entities' rule). The spec's base point and dragged values are left to the existing entity tools.
Status: Default
Reason: TR50.

D896: Add relations to existing geometry (2026-11-05, TR416, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/sketch/find_relations.suggest` checks, within 1 degree and 0.05 mm: horizontal and vertical lines; parallel and perpendicular pairs, skipped when both lines already follow an axis (that would only repeat what Horizontal and Vertical give); separate end points that nearly meet (Coincident); a line sharing an end with an arc and leaving along its tangent; arcs and circles of nearly equal radius (Equal). Existing relations are not offered again. The sketch's right click menu opens a tick list, all ticked, and the ticked ones are added in one sketch undo step; the solver then pulls the geometry onto them. Symmetric and equal line lengths are left out: they match by chance too often to tick by default.
Status: Default
Reason: TR416.

D897: Text linked to a value (2026-11-05, TR54, Phase 7B Stage 3). Fields are `{name}` or `{name:format}` inside the text; the stored text keeps the field, and the sketch feature replaces it while building (`core/sketch/text_fields.py`) from the document's global variables, the sketch's own dimensions (by `d<n>` or their name) and custom properties. Lengths are shown in the part's units and angles in degrees; numbers default to six significant figures; the format part is passed to Python's number format, which cannot run code. Unknown names stay as typed so mistakes show. The sketch's cache key includes the expanded text (`key_data`), so a changed value rebuilds the text. The sketch editor shows the text with its fields as typed.
Status: Default
Reason: TR54.

D898: Sketch from a picked edge (2026-11-05, TR51, Phase 7B Stage 3). An edge right click item that adds an ordinary Reference Plane (method normal_to_curve, the edge and its end vertex nearer the click as references) and opens a sketch on it once the plane is built. A real plane feature rather than a hidden one, so the sketch stays tied to the edge and the plane can be edited; it is two undo steps (the plane, then the sketch) like doing it by hand. The click's 3D point comes from the view's last hover pick; without it the edge's first end is used.
Status: Default
Reason: TR51.

D899: Mirror Part to a new file (2026-11-05, TR73, Phase 7B Stage 3). The finished body is mirrored about the Right plane (YZ through the origin, `gp_Trsf.SetMirror`, which keeps solids valid) and written as a new part holding it as one embedded STEP import (`part_from_step`), saved where the user picks and then opened. It runs as a background job. The new part does not follow the original: a live link needs Insert Part (TR71), which is not built yet; the user guide says so. The original document is never touched.
Status: Default
Reason: TR73.

D900: Spline analysis aids (2026-11-05, TR44, Phase 7B Stage 3). Shown together with the curvature combs (the same tick box) rather than with new switches: they answer the same question. `core/sketch/curvature.spline_aids` uses the comb's own samples at four times the density: inflections where the signed curvature changes sign (placed by linear interpolation between samples), the tightest point at the largest curvature with radius 1 / k, and the control polygon as the spline's Bezier poles. Display only, never saved.
Status: Default
Reason: TR44.

D901: Dimension tolerance and display (2026-11-05, TR46, Phase 7B Stage 3). An optional `display` dict on a sketch dimension (saved only when set, so older sketches save unchanged): `tolerance` (none, bilateral, limit, symmetric) with `plus` and `minus` in mm or radians, `decimals`, and `show` (radius or diameter) for round dimensions. `core/sketch/dimension_display.label` builds the label; the value, what it drives and formulas are untouched. Linear diameter as a separate style is not added: the existing diameter and doubled distance dimensions already give it. The inner angle or its supplement is already chosen by where an angle dimension is placed (`supplement`, T4.1), so no new setting. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) should list the dimension `display` key; noted for the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR46.

D902: Parabola and Jog Line (2026-11-05, TR52, Phase 7B Stage 3). Parabola reuses the Conic tool's exact rational construction: a conic with shape 0.5 is a parabola, so from the focus and apex FDCAD works out the two ends on the curve (by their distance across the axis from the clicks) and where the end tangents meet, and draws `conic_spline(start, top, end, 0.5)`; the result is a spline, as conics are (D753), rather than a new curve type with focus and apex points. Jog Line keeps the original line as the first piece (its relations at the start stay), adds the step and a second piece shifted by the signed distance of the second click, shares their end points and adds Parallel between the pieces; the step's width starts equal to the depth. A step that does not fit inside the line is refused with a message.
Status: Default
Reason: TR52.

D903: More plane methods (2026-11-05, TR74, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two Reference Plane methods. `tangent`: a cylinder face plus a plane or a point; the touching side is the plane's normal (or the direction to the point) with any part along the axis removed, and the plane sits one radius out from the axis, its X along the axis. With a point it is placed level with the point along the axis. Cones are refused for now (a cone's tangent plane also tilts; not asked for in the spec's examples). `line_point`: normal = line direction x (point - line point), X along the line. The pick guesser picks `tangent` for a cylinder with a plane; a cylinder with a point still guesses Project as before.
Status: Default
Reason: TR74.

D904: Batch export over variable values (2026-11-05, TR368, Phase 7B Stage 3). Built beside Export Configurations (TR196) and reusing its file kinds, log and outcome records. Values per variable are a comma list or a range `a..b step s`; the combinations are the full product (first variable slowest), at most 500. Each combination sets the variables' expressions on a copy of the part and rebuilds it with one shared rebuild engine, so features that do not depend on the changed values are reused from its cache between files. File names come from a template with `{part}` and `{variable}` fields (Python format fields over plain strings, so nothing runs), default "{part} width{width} ...". A combination whose values break the equations or leave no solid is logged and skipped. TR273's goal seek is a separate item.
Status: Default
Reason: TR368.

D905: Find typed values that should be linked (2026-11-05, TR351, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Model Health check (`unlinked_value`): feature values and sketch dimensions whose text is a plain number (with an optional unit) equal to a global variable's value, matched by kind when the parameter declares one; zero is skipped (too many false matches). The fix replaces the text with the variable's name as one Replace Feature undo step, from a Link to Variable button beside Move to End; geometry does not change because the value is the same. Pattern counts beside a count variable are covered by the same rule (a count is a number value). It is advice only, like the rest of the report.
Status: Default
Reason: TR351.

D906: Variables with allowed values (2026-11-05, TR274, Phase 7B Stage 3). `Variable.allowed` holds `{"choices": [...]}` or `{"min", "max"}` in mm or radians, saved only when set. It survives equations edits (apply_rows keeps it by name). The rebuild lists every variable outside its allowed values (`report.variable_warnings`) and the status bar shows the first, naming the variable and what to type; the value is never changed. Set from the equations manager's Allowed Values button, typed as a list or `low..high`. The spec's choice box in fields that use the variable is not built: those fields hold formulas, so the warning covers every place the variable is used; a choice box can follow. FDEF_SPEC.md (an owner file) needs the variable `allowed` key; listed in the pull request.
Status: Default
Reason: TR274.

D907: Overlapping bodies on export (2026-11-05, TR411, Phase 7B Stage 3). STL and 3MF export check the exported bodies for overlaps with the interference check (TR150) in the export job. A new mesh export setting `overlaps` (saved with the part's other mesh settings, only when not the default): `warn` adds a sentence naming the pairs and volumes to the export message; `join` fuses each group of overlapping bodies; `first` cuts each body by the earlier bodies it overlaps, so the earlier one keeps the shared volume (the spec's "which body wins", ordered by the tree). Only the file changes, never the part. When bodies are joined or cut, 3MF body roles (TR382) are left out, since the body list no longer matches. STEP export is unchanged: CAD readers expect the bodies as modelled.
Status: Default
Reason: TR411.

D908: Living hinge patterns (2026-11-05, TR402, Phase 7B Stage 3). Type `living_hinge` on a sketch whose closed profile outlines the bending area. Rows run along the sketch X axis from half a row spacing inside the outline's box; each row repeats slit then bridge, and every other row starts half a pitch earlier, so bridges stagger. The slit prisms (at most 4000) are clipped to the outline extruded through the part, then cut through it in one boolean. The spec's printed form (a V groove leaving a thin skin) is not built here: it is a different shape (a groove, not slits) and is left for later; the laser form covers the main use.
Status: Default
Reason: TR402.

D909: Fix overhangs from the analysis (2026-11-05, TR410, Phase 7B Stage 3). A 3D Print command rather than a button inside the analysis colours, since the analysis is a view toggle with no panel. In a background job it finds flat faces facing straight down (within about 1 degree) in the print orientation's build direction, except those at the part's lowest height (the bed); then it asks a size and adds one Chamfer feature (distance and distance, symmetric, so 45 degrees, which needs no support) on the edges of those faces, as one undoable feature (the user's click is the confirmation, CLAUDE.md 5.12). The spec's "typed angle" is the 45 degree chamfer: other angles need an angle and distance chamfer whose reference face differs per edge, left for later. Overhang Analysis now adds a note counting overhanging faces made by a fillet.
Status: Default
Reason: TR410.

D910: Mid plane between faces that are not parallel (2026-11-05, TR360, Phase 7B Stage 3). Instead of the old error, the plane goes through the line where the two planes meet and halves the angle between them. Two planes do that; the one with the two picked faces' points on opposite sides is used (the plane that runs between the faces, which is what a user picking two faces of a wedge means), and the existing Flip side tick, now shown for Mid plane, takes the other. Its X direction is along the shared line. For parallel faces nothing changes and Flip side has no effect.

D911: Mean Dimensions (2026-11-05, TR306, Phase 7B Stage 3). A right click item in empty sketch space, shown only when a driving dimension has a bilateral or limit tolerance with different plus and minus (symmetric ones are already at the mean). It is per sketch rather than per part, because tolerances are on sketch dimensions and the sketch editor is where its undo lives (one sketch undo step). Each changed dimension takes the mean value, its tolerance becomes the same half band both ways so the label still names the same largest and smallest sizes, and the typed expression, value and tolerance are kept in the dimension's display settings under mean_of. Typed Dimensions puts them back. A meaned value is a plain number, so a formula in the dimension is replaced until it is put back. FDEF_SPEC: the display object gains the mean_of key; listed for the owner in the PR.

D912: Convex Hull in sketches (2026-11-05, TR229, Phase 7B Stage 3). A right click item for two or more picked sketch items. The hull is found from points along the picked curves (720 per circle), each point tagged with the circle or arc it came from; runs of hull points on one circle become one item, and the outline between items is the exact outer tangent line, so circles give exact arcs joined by tangent lines (tangent relations added) and lines and points give corners. If a tangent point would fall past an arc's end, the arcs are followed by points instead. Ellipses and splines give short lines through 48 points each, since an exact tangent to them needs a solve. The picked curves are kept. The part half of TR229 (a smooth solid bridge around bodies) is not built: the kernel has no hull of curved faces, so it went to IDEAS.md.

D913: Bolt circle shorthand (2026-11-05, TR407, Phase 7B Stage 3). In the Hole Tool's Positions tab, a Bolt Circle box takes "count x diameter" (x, X, * or the times sign; the diameter is any length text, so units and formulas work) and an optional start angle. The last clicked point is the centre and is replaced by the holes, since a click is how the Hole Tool picks the face and plane, and the centre of a bolt circle rarely gets a hole. The holes are plain own points, so each can still be moved or removed. The sketch Circular Pattern does not get it: it already has an instance count and a centre, and its radius is set by where the picked curves are, so the shorthand adds nothing there.

D914: Hose barbs and luer fittings (2026-11-05, TR406, Phase 7B Stage 3). One feature type, hose_fitting, with a fitting choice (barb, luer_male, luer_female), so the panel, the placement and the bore are shared. It stands on a picked face at a vertex or round edge centre (the Mounting Boss placement helpers), or in the middle of the face when no point is picked, since the body tool panel has no click to place. Its refs are base_face and base_point, not face and position, because those names already mean a round face and a groove position in the shared label table. A barb is a stem of the hose's inside diameter with barbs that step out sharply on the side facing the part and taper back toward the tip (barb diameter defaults to 1.15 times the hose). Luer sizes are from ISO 80369-7: 6 percent taper, 7.5 mm long, male tip 3.925 mm, female opening 4.27 mm. The luer lock thread is not modelled. On a curved face the base reaches down to meet it, as the boss does. The command shares a ribbon drop down with Cable Tie so the 3D Print tab keeps its width. FDEF_SPEC: the new hose_fitting type and its params need adding; listed for the owner in the PR.

D915: Select Previous and Invert Selection (2026-11-05, TR93, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two Selection menu commands with no default keys (SHORTCUTS.md is the owner's file). Each 3D view remembers its last non empty selection and keeps it as the previous one when the selection becomes empty; a rebuild forgets it, because the kernel makes new faces and edges and old picks no longer match, and mapping them through names is more than the request needs. Invert takes every face, edge or vertex of the part not picked now: of the kinds the selection filter allows when it is on, else of the kinds picked now, else faces. Both are 3D view commands; the sketch editor already has its own selection tools.

D916: Menu access keys (2026-11-05, TR205, Phase 7B Stage 3). The menu titles already had access letters (Alt+F and so on). For the entries, instead of an ampersand in every command name, an event filter on each menu bar menu and its submenus (watched again each time a menu opens, so rebuilt lists such as Open Recent are covered) handles a plain letter key: one entry starting with it runs, or opens its submenu; several are stepped through, and Enter runs the chosen one. This is the usual first letter behaviour of Windows menus. Ampersands were not added because the same actions show on command tab buttons, in the shortcut editor and in command search, where they would show or need stripping, and fixed letters would clash as commands are added. An entry that does have its own access letter is left to Qt. Context menus are not changed.

D917: Pick distance (2026-11-05, TR313, Phase 7B Stage 3). One choice in Preferences, General with four steps (Small 0.6, Normal 1, Large 1.5, Extra large 2 times) scales both the 3D view's kernel pick distance (6 pixels at Normal, times the screen scale) and the sketch editor's (10 pixels). One setting rather than separate point, edge and vertex values: the kernel takes a single pixel distance for all kinds, and a few named steps are easier to choose than pixel counts. The scale is a module value set at start and on OK, so views read it without touching the settings store on every mouse move; open views take it at once.

D918: Recent sketch tools (2026-11-05, TR204, Phase 7B Stage 3). The sketch editor keeps its own list of the last eight tools started (newest first, each once), separate from the part's Recent Commands, and shows it as a Recent Sketch Tools submenu in the empty space right click menu once two tools are in it (with one, the existing Last Tool item already covers it). The list lasts for the session and covers every sketch, since the same tools are used across sketches.

D919: Reserved variable names (2026-11-05, TR310, Phase 7B Stage 3). A name equal to a length or angle unit (mm, cm, m, in, ft, deg, rad), a formula function or pi is refused where a name is made: the equations manager's OK, a new variable typed as ="name" in a value box, a dimension name and a feature value name. Names are compared exactly (case sensitive, as variable names are), so Mm or mm2 are allowed. Variables with such names already in a part are kept and still solve, so older parts open and rebuild as before; only new names are refused.

D920: Explain a relation (2026-11-05, TR237, Phase 7B Stage 3). A right click item on one relation tag. The words come from a core table with one sentence per relation type, naming each linked item by its kind and id (line e3), the same ids the Relations panel lists. A relation whose item is gone or that is switched off says so and what to do. The text goes to the status bar and the canvas tooltip rather than a dialog, so it does not interrupt sketching.

D921: Show formulas on dimensions (2026-11-05, TR235, Phase 7B Stage 3). A checkable item in the empty sketch space right click menu. While on, a dimension whose value is a formula shows it beside the value in one line ("width/2 = 20.00") rather than above it, so label boxes, picking and placement stay as they are. It applies to every sketch for the session, like the other sketch display toggles, and is not saved in the part. The dimension comment on hover was left out: it needs a new saved field on dimensions, which is the owner's file format decision, so it went to IDEAS.md.

D922: Step a dimension through a range (2026-11-05, TR236, Phase 7B Stage 3). A right click item on a driving dimension that is on. It asks From, To (50 and 150 percent of the value by default) and Steps (2 to 100, default 10), then sets each value on a timer (450 ms apart) and solves, so the canvas redraws at each. A checkpoint is taken first and rolled back at the end, so the sketch, its undo list and the part are exactly as before. Values that do not solve are counted and reported; the stepping does not stop at them, since seeing where it breaks is the point.

D923: Save Increment (2026-11-05, TR305, Phase 7B Stage 3). A File command with no default key. It saves to the next numbered name beside the current file and the open tab moves to that file (like Save As), so each increment is a step the user can go back to. The number is found from the end of the name: a trailing number goes up by one with the same width and separator; otherwise " 01" is added. A name made only of digits gets " 01" too, so a part called 2024 is not taken for a counter. Existing files are skipped, never overwritten. A part with no file yet asks for a name as Save As does.

D924: Hole and thread list (2026-11-05, TR316, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Hole feature now keeps where each of its holes starts in its rebuild result (extras holes, display data, not saved), so the table needs no second rebuild. The table is built in core from the last rebuild: one row per hole, tagged with a letter per feature and a number per hole, and one row per thread mark of other features (cosmetic or modelled threads, which already report their marks). Depth is the typed depth for Blind, Through for Through All, and empty for the Up To end conditions, whose depth differs per hole. Copy gives tab separated text for spreadsheets and Save CSV gives comma separated values with the unit in the header. Positions are in model coordinates; a table relative to a chosen origin is left for later.

D925: Measure free points (2026-11-05, TR192, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Points on faces tick in the Measure box. While on, a click adds the model point under the cursor (the same hover point the thickness reading uses) instead of the face, edge or vertex. The points are turned into vertices inside the background measure job, so the existing one item (position) and two item (distance, dX dY dZ) results apply unchanged and no kernel call runs on the UI thread. Keep is refused for free points, because a Measurement feature needs part items it can find again after a rebuild.

D926: Mirror image display (2026-11-05, TR309, Phase 7B Stage 3). A checkable View menu command. The image is a second display object of the same part shape with a mirror display transform, so no kernel work runs and nothing is copied; it is drawn see through in the reference colour, is never picked, and is redrawn after each rebuild. The plane is the plane feature (or a feature with a plane result) picked in the tree when the command is turned on, else the Right plane, since most parts are drawn symmetric about it; the status bar names the plane. It is per view and not saved.

D927: Preset sketch shapes (2026-11-05, TR228, Phase 7B Stage 3). One Shapes dialog from the empty sketch space right click menu, like Gear and Airfoil, rather than a drawing tool per shape: each is placed centred on the sketch origin and then moved or dimensioned, which keeps the tool list short. Triangles are solved from the typed sides or angles (the law of cosines and sines) and refuse sizes that cannot close. The trapezoid is isosceles. The keyhole, constant width triangle are exact lines and arcs; the egg (two half ellipses of different heights joined at the widest point) and the superellipse are four splines through points, one per quarter, joined end to end. No dimensions or relations are added: the user picks which values to drive. TR114's rectangle and polygon presets stay with that item.

D928: Colour per sketch (2026-11-05, TR233, Phase 7B Stage 3). Kept in the part's appearance block as an optional sketches map (sketch feature id to #RRGGBB), beside features and bodies, left out of the file while empty, so parts without sketch colours save byte for byte as before. It is set from the sketch's tree menu with the colour dialog (Usual Sketch Colour removes it) through the existing undoable appearance command, which only redraws. Only finished sketches in the 3D view use it; the sketch editor keeps its status colours (TR38). FDEF_SPEC 10: the appearance block gains the sketches key; listed for the owner in the PR.

D929: Edge Angle Analysis (2026-11-05, TR420 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). An Evaluate toggle built like the other analysis overlays (worked out again in the background after each rebuild). The angle across an edge is the angle between its two faces' outward normals at the edge's middle, so 0 is smooth and 90 degrees is a square corner; edges with one face or a seam of one face are skipped. Below half a degree counts as smooth and is not drawn; the user's limit (asked each time it is turned on, default 10 degrees) splits nearly smooth (yellow) from sharp (red). One sample per edge is enough to find the problem edges; an edge whose angle changes along it shows its middle value. The second half of TR420 needed no new command: every plane is already drawn sized to the part (0.6 of the part's extent, at least 50 mm, refreshed on each rebuild, D75) with its tree name as a label in the view (T13), so all planes size to the model together without a separate step.

D930: Copy configuration inputs (2026-11-05, TR304, Phase 7B Stage 3). Copy Table and Paste Table buttons in the Design Table dialog, using the same table format as Import and Export CSV, so one path handles parts and spreadsheets: copy writes tab separated text (what spreadsheets paste into cells), and paste accepts tab separated or comma separated text and shows it in the dialog, applied only on OK with the same checks and the delete confirmation as an import. Copying one part's configuration inputs into another is this same copy and paste between their Design Tables; columns name values by feature id and variable, so they match between parts that share features (for example a part saved from another).

D931: Part notes (2026-11-05, TR392, Phase 7B Stage 3). Plain text in the part file's top level notes key (kept in Document.extra like the expected value checks, D889, so older FDCAD versions keep it untouched), left out while empty. A plain text editor rather than rich text: the spec asks for plain text only, and headings, lists and tables written as text need no format. Editing is one undoable command that does not rebuild. Nothing is parsed or run, and links are not made clickable, so there is no network access (CLAUDE.md section 5 items 8 and 10). FDEF_SPEC: the top level notes key is listed for the owner in the PR.

D932: Hide construction geometry (2026-11-05, TR419 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A checkable Sketch command with no default key (keys are the owner's file, SHORTCUTS.md), per open sketch and not saved. While on, construction curves are not drawn and cannot be picked, and any picked ones are let go; construction points stay, and snaps still find hidden curves so layout geometry keeps guiding new lines. Item 2 of TR419 (groups of sketch items) is not built yet, so the item stays open.

D933: Sketch points from a text file (2026-11-05, TR415 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A right click item in empty sketch space. The reader takes the first two numbers of each line, split by commas, white space or semicolons (CSV, XYZ and plain columns all work), in the part's units, skips lines that are not two numbers (a header) and lines starting with #, and caps a file at 10,000 points. The points are plain and free, so the user can dimension them or draw through them; curves through them stay with TR61. Item 1 of TR415 (a turn style choice: free, turntable, arcball) is not built yet; Keep the model upright (TR209) already gives turntable turning, so the item stays open for the arcball choice.

D934: Select All (2026-11-05, TR380 item 3 and TR224 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). One Selection command serves both items: in the 3D view it picks every item of the kinds already picked (one edge picked gives every edge, as TR224 asks), or of the kinds the selection filter allows, or every face when nothing is picked; in an open sketch it picks every sketch item that is not hidden. It has no default key: Ctrl+A is listed as not mapped in SHORTCUTS.md, the owner's file, so the PR asks to map Ctrl+A to it. The other items of TR380 and TR224 stay open.

D935: Heat set insert entry chamfer and depth margin (2026-11-05, TR189 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). The entry chamfer already exists: heat set insert holes take the Near Side Countersink, so nothing new was added for it and the guide points to it. The depth margin is one preference beside the insert table (Edit Insert Table, 0 to 20 mm, default 0 so existing parts and tables give the same holes), added to the table depth when the Hole Tool fills a heat set insert hole's depth. One margin for all sizes rather than a column per row: the room needed depends on the printer and material, not the insert size. Items 1 to 3 of TR189 (polygon holes, corner ears, drain holes) stay open.

D936: Geodesic sphere and dome (2026-11-05, TR371 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two more kinds of the Primitive Solid feature rather than a new feature, so the frame, Centred, Add or Cut and merge options apply as for the other shapes. The sphere is an icosahedron (a vertex straight up) with each face split frequency times along each side into frequency squared triangles, every point pushed onto the sphere, sewn into one solid of flat faces; frequency is 1 to 8 (up to 1280 faces) to keep rebuilds quick. The dome is the sphere's top half, cut flat at its middle and moved to stand on the frame, since a clean equator of whole triangles only exists for some frequencies. Items 1 to 3 of TR371 stay open. FDEF_SPEC: the primitive kinds and the frequency param are listed for the owner in the PR.

D937: More formula functions (2026-11-05, TR89 with its section 22 addition, Phase 7B Stage 3). Added exp, ln, log10, sign, trunc and mod (item 1) and pow, random and sinh, cosh, tanh (addition 14) to the safe parser's function table; nothing else in the parser changed. mod is the floored remainder (sign of the second value) and keeps the unit; trunc keeps the unit like floor and ceil. pow takes a plain power; a length or angle base needs a whole power and the result's unit is the base unit to that power. FDCAD has no `^` operator, so item 2's note on `-3^2` is documented as `-pow(3, 2)` instead of adding an operator. random(seed) and random(seed, low, high) are seeded from the seed's text with Python's string seeding, which is fixed across versions, so a rebuild always gives the same value and no hidden state is stored in the file. Older documents with variables named like a new function keep working because a name is a function only when `(` follows it; the reserved name check (D919) blocks only new names. typing-values.md now documents if, the comparisons, the minus sign and the tolerance test for computed lengths.

D938: Keep proportions on the first dimension (2026-11-05, TR119, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Sketch preferences switch, off by default, stored with the other sketch switches. It acts when a typed value is applied to a driving length dimension (distance, horizontal or vertical distance, radius, diameter, doubled distance, arc length) that is the only driving dimension, in a sketch with no geometry taken from the model and no Fix other than the origin's: those already size the sketch, so scaling would fight them. Angles never scale the sketch. The sketch scales about its origin (points, circle radii, offset and length difference values, reference dimensions and label places) by new value over the measured value, then the dimension takes the typed text, so it is one undo step with the value change. Relations are all kept, since a uniform scale about the origin keeps every one of them true. The core code is core/sketch/proportions.py.

D939: Isolate display choices (2026-11-05, TR99, Phase 7B Stage 3). FDCAD's Isolate is a key toggle with a status line, not a panel, so the choice is a General preference, Other bodies while isolating: Hidden (the default, as before), Transparent or Wireframe. It is read when Isolate starts. The isolated bodies stay the part shape, so picking, measuring and the section view work on them only, as before; the others are drawn as one extra viewer object that is never picked (see through at 0.8, or edges in the reference grey). Leaving Isolate (I again, Esc or Show All) removes that object, which is the spec's "returns the bodies to normal when closed". A view state, never saved or undone, like Isolate itself (D410).

D940: Deleting a feature and its equations (2026-11-05, TR91 with its section 23 addition, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature's own equations (its formula values and dimensions) always go with it, so the list is of global variables: those that a formula or a sketch text field of the deleted features uses, and that no kept feature, kept text field or kept variable uses, followed through variables (a variable used only by such a variable is listed too). A variable no formula used before is not listed, since this delete did not leave it behind. The list is in the TR201 Delete dialog (the addition), below the dependents, every row unticked so nothing is deleted without a click; the dialog now also opens for a feature with no dependents when such variables exist. Ticked variables are removed with their configuration overrides and design table columns (configurations.follow_variables) in the same undo macro as the features. The code is core/equations/orphans.py.

D941: Leaving a sketch (2026-11-05, TR120, Phase 7B Stage 3). Exit Without Saving is a new command (sketch.discard, no default key) that runs the confirmation corner's Cancel: it asks only when the sketch changed, and the safe button is No. It sits under Exit Sketch in the Sketch group. Two Sketch preferences switches, both off by default so nobody leaves a sketch by surprise: a double click where nothing is picked, with no tool and no dimension tool active, exits (a double click on a dimension still edits it); and Esc exits only when it has nothing else to do, so it still stops a tool, closes a value box and clears the picks first. Both exits save, like Exit Sketch, and run after the event that asked for them, because leaving deletes the canvas.

D942: Parent and child arrows (2026-11-05, TR96, Phase 7B Stage 3). Item 2: the tree menu entry did exist, but showed a text box; it is now a dialog (ui/tree/relatives_dialog.py) with a Uses list and a Used by list from core dependencies.parents_of and children_of; a double click shows that feature's own lists and selects it in the tree. Item 1: a checkable Parent and Child Arrows entry on the part row's menu, off by default and not saved (a view state like the closed folders). The tree paints the arrows over its rows: from the hovered row, or the picked one when the mouse is outside, along the left margin to each parent in the accent colour and each child in the selection colour, with heads at the target. A target inside a closed folder or feature row points at the highest closed row that holds it.

D943: Select Similar (2026-11-05, TR303, Phase 7B Stage 3). Three face rules in core/select_similar.py: same kind and size (surface type and radii, relative 1e-4; covers hole walls of one size and rounds of one radius, since those are cylinders and tori), parallel (plane normals and the axes of round faces, either way round) and same area (within 5%). Rules combine in a small dialog: each rule is Not used, Must match or Except, and the Must match rules need all or any to match (and, or, except). The first picked face is the reference and is always kept. Finding the faces measures areas, so it runs in a background kernel job; a rebuild meanwhile drops the result. Item 2 is three commands, Select Their Edges, Faces and Bodies, which convert picks (faces to their edges, edges and vertices to their faces, any pick to every face of its body; the view picks faces, edges and vertices only, so a body is picked as its faces). They only walk the topology, like Select All (D934), so they run at once. No default keys. TR94's saved and rule based selection sets stay with TR94.

D944: Selection sets (2026-11-05, TR94 with its section 22 and 24 additions, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sets are kept in the part as `Document.extra["selection_sets"]`, a list of `{name, items | rule | combine}` (FDEF_SPEC owner file: listed in the PR). `items` holds stable names (face names, `edge(...)`, `vertex(...)`), so a saved set follows rebuilds like feature references do, and names that no longer resolve are skipped and counted. A rule set runs again each time it is used (the additions): faces of a feature (by its face name prefix), faces of a colour (the part colour means every face in no other colour) and edges at least a length long. The concave edge rule named in addition 25 is left out, since the edge angle check (D929) has no sign. Sets combine two at a time by union, subtract or intersect; a set that uses itself, directly or through others, is an error, and a set another set uses cannot be deleted. Saving, combining and deleting are undo steps that do not rebuild. Resolving runs in a background kernel job, and the result is dropped if the part rebuilt meanwhile. Commands: Save Selection Set and Selection Sets, in the Selection menu, no default keys.

D945: Offset corner style (2026-11-05, TR391, Phase 7B Stage 3). Offset gets Outside corners, Sharp (today's behaviour, the default) or Round, for every chain, open or closed: a corner is outside when the offset side is opposite the way the chain turns there, so the offset curves leave a gap. Inside corners still meet by extending or trimming. A round corner is an arc that shares the end points of the two copies, which the offset relation holds square across from the source corner, so the arc follows the source; its centre is its own construction point (it lands on the source corner) and one Tangent to the earlier copy fixes it. Centring the arc on the source corner point, or adding a second Tangent, over defines the sketch, and joining the arc by Coincident instead of shared points puts a point where a circle touches a line, which the solver cannot hold. The new arcs count as offset copies for the result. Fix found on the way: drag() refused a move whenever the solver reported any redundancy, including its own helper rules (an arc end on its circle beside a pinned offset end), while solve() counts only redundancy in the user's relations; drag now filters the same way.

D946: Slot along picked curves (2026-11-05, TR225, Phase 7B Stage 3). A right click entry on picked lines and arcs, Slot Along Curves, that asks for the width, rather than a fifth kind in the click based Slot tool, since it works on picks, like Convex Hull (D912). It is built from Offset (core/sketch/slot_along.py): both directions at half the width with one shared distance, round caps at the open ends, and the picked curves made construction, so joins along a chain are trimmed the way Offset joins them and the slot follows its centre line. The offset's own distance is freed and one distance dimension across the slot (between the two copies of the first line) drives both sides, so the width is one dimension; when the first picked curve is an arc the offset distance stays and no width dimension is added. Ellipses and splines are refused with a message, because Offset cannot follow them, and so is a closed loop, which has no ends.

D947: Presets for any panel (2026-11-05, TR326, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Phase 4 Favourites box (presets in the spec) is added to every property panel whose form does not already have one, as the last group, stored per feature type in the preferences as before. Added: Rename (the default choice follows the rename) and New ones start with: Factory settings (the default, so nothing changes until chosen), Last used (the settings of the last feature of that type made, remembered on OK) or a favourite. The start settings apply only when a command starts the feature (new feature commands, the body tools and the sheet metal flow), never when a drag or an edit opens the panel, and they never change the operation (Boss or Cut) the command chose; a missing favourite falls back to the factory settings. Sort is the name order the list already uses; no manual order is kept. Tests now give the panel preferences a store of their own (conftest), so a preset chosen in FDCAD never reaches a test.

D948: Recent files in the system and one running FDCAD (2026-11-06, TR379, Phase 7B Stage 3). ui/system_integration.py, turned on by the app at start only (never in tests, the bundle check or the startup report). Windows: every path that goes on FDCAD's own recent list is also sent to the shell with SHAddToRecentDocs, which feeds the taskbar jump list and Start for the registered .fdprt type; the native file dialog already adds files it opens there, so this covers parts opened from the recent list, by drag or by double click, and saves. Mac: a Dock menu (QMenu.setAsDockMenu) with New Part and the ten newest recent parts, filled each time it opens. A second launch with part files connects to a per user QLocalServer (FDCAD-<user>) and hands the paths over as one JSON line; the running FDCAD opens them, comes to the front, and the new launch quits. A launch without part files, or when no FDCAD runs, starts as before; a socket left by a crash is removed and listened on again. Not done: the Windows jump list New Part task, which needs the shell's custom destination list COM interface; ctypes could reach it but the code would be large for one entry, so it is left open in the plan.

D949: Number display (2026-11-06, TR350, Phase 7B Stage 3). core/units/number_display.py holds one shown number style for the app (set at start and after Preferences, reset by the test conftest): a rounding rule (half away from zero, the default; half to even; truncate), a decimal separator (point or comma; the Preferences choice Follow the system asks QLocale) and an inch fraction step (off, the default, or 1/2 to 1/64). Rounding works on the number as Python prints it (Decimal of repr), so 2.675 rounds to 2.68 under half away, not to 2.67 from its binary tail, and a shown zero never has a minus sign. A fraction is shown only when the value is within half of the last decimal place of a step, else the decimals stay, so a fraction never hides a difference. The style reaches the shown values only: property panel values, sketch dimension labels and the cursor readout, and Measure results; text that goes into a value field (the Dimension panel's reference value, typed_length) keeps a point and decimals, because the parser reads a point. Measure points join with a semicolon when the separator is a comma. Angles and millimetres never show fractions.

D950: Swap axis relations (2026-11-06, TR124, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch right click entry, Swap Axis Relations, shown when a picked line has a Horizontal or Vertical relation of its own (core/sketch/swap_axis.py). The first picked line with one is the reference: every other picked line along the same axis becomes Parallel to it and every line along the other axis Perpendicular to it, and all those Horizontal and Vertical relations are removed, the reference's too, so the shape gains exactly one freedom, the turn. Relations switched off (TR109), relations between two points and a line with both Horizontal and Vertical (already a conflict) are left alone. One sketch undo step; when nothing can be swapped a message says what to pick and no step is left.

D951: Diameter mode stays on (2026-11-06, TR361, Phase 7B Stage 3). After Smart Dimension places a doubled distance (a diameter past a centerline), the canvas keeps that centerline as the diameter axis. While it is set, one picked line that is not construction, is parallel to the axis and is not on it gives a doubled distance to the axis wherever the text goes, in the preview and on the click; anything else picks as before. The axis is cleared by Esc (which ends the dimension tool when no item is picked, as before) or by any other tool, so a later Smart Dimension starts without it. A status message says the mode is on and how to end it.

D952: Shade closed regions and show sketch points (2026-11-06, TR335, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two checkable entries in the sketch right click menu, kept on the canvas class for the whole session like Show Formulas (D921) and reset by the test conftest. Shade Closed Regions fills every region the region finder (TR39) returns with the selection colour at a low alpha, under the picked region shading; the regions are cached against the sketch data and found again only when it changes, and a sketch that cannot be split shades nothing. Show Sketch Points, on by default, hides every point when turned off; picked and hovered points still show, as with the existing centre and end point options (T11.2, T11.3), which stay as they are.

D953: Dimension to midpoints (2026-11-06, TR418, Phase 7B Stage 3). In Smart Dimension, a click where the midpoint snap shows on a sketch line or arc, or on a part edge line, picks a construction point held at the middle by a midpoint relation (for a part edge, on its fixed construction copy, D113). The dimension then measures to that point like any point, so distance and angle placement and the solver are unchanged. A curve that already has a point held at its middle reuses it, so repeated dimensions add no points. Three Sketch preferences: end point picks and centre picks (on, the behaviour before) and midpoint picks (off by default, because the usual way to dimension a line is a click on it, often near its middle, which a midpoint pick would take over; a test sweep of the existing Smart Dimension tests showed this). With end or centre picks off, a click on such a point falls back to the curve under the cursor. Part edge arcs are not offered, because their fixed copy is a full circle with no midpoint.

D954: Repeat with the same tool (2026-11-06, TR314, Phase 7B Stage 3). Shift and Enter in a property panel accepts it like Enter and, for a new feature, emits the same again signal the pin uses (TR206, D861), so the command that opened the panel starts again empty; editing an existing feature just accepts. The panel title takes the theme's error colour, with a tooltip saying what to do, whenever the latest finished preview has no shape (the feature cannot be built with the picks and values so far), and goes back when a preview builds or the panel closes. The preview's own messages are unchanged.

D955: The part's own views (2026-11-06, TR333, Phase 7B Stage 3). Three View menu commands with no default keys: Home, Set Current View As (a list: Front, Back, Left, Right, Top, Bottom, Home) and Reset Standard Views. Setting a standard view stores one rotation in the part, extra["view_frame"]["frame"] (FDEF owner item), the rotation that takes that standard view's direction and up to the current camera's, with up made square to the eye; every standard view command then looks along the turned direction, so Front, Top and the rest stay square to each other. Setting Home stores the camera's eye and up under extra["view_frame"]["home"]; Home without one is the isometric view, turned with the frame. The geometry, planes and saved views do not move, and the view cube, Normal To and the triad keep the model axes (the frame only names views). Each change is an undoable document command that rebuilds nothing; Reset removes the key. A part without the key uses the standard views exactly as before.

D956: Purge Unused and Delete Below Rollback Bar (2026-11-06, TR159, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two feature tree commands with no default keys (core/document/purge.py, ui/tree/purge.py). Purge Unused (Edit menu) lists sketches that no feature and no graph uses, suppressed features, and global variables that no formula, feature value, configuration cell or sketch text field uses, also through other used variables; every row starts ticked and OK deletes the ticked ones. A layout sketch counts as unused, so it is listed and the user unticks it to keep it. Deleting a suppressed feature also deletes the features built on it, so no feature is left with a missing parent; the dialog says so. Delete Below Rollback Bar (Rollback menu) lists the rolled back features in a Yes or No question with No as the default, then deletes them. Each command is one undo macro of the existing Delete Feature commands and the TR91 variable delete; with nothing to delete a status message says so and no dialog opens.

D957: Copy Values and Edit by Rule (2026-11-06, TR160, Phase 7B Stage 3). core/copy_values.py, ui/tree/copy_values.py. Copy Values to Others is on a feature's right click menu when another feature of the same type exists: a list of those features, all unticked, and OK copies every value of the source (Param and plain values) except the ones that say how the feature joins the part (operation, merge, body choices, keep separate, feature scope); picks (refs), names, suppression and the feature's own data stay. Values only the target has stay too. Edit by Rule (Edit menu, no default key) picks a feature type present in the part, one of its number values, a test (<, <=, =, >=, >, equal within 1e-6) and a typed limit read in the part's units and variables; the list shows the matches live and OK sets the typed value, kept with its text, on all of them. Both go through DocumentChange, so each is one undo step that rebuilds. Configured values (configurations) are not changed: the base values are, as an edit in the property panel does for the base.

D958: Group identical bodies (2026-11-06, TR308, Phase 7B Stage 3). The rebuild (and a part read from the disk cache) measures each body of a multibody part in the worker (core/body_groups.py): face, edge and vertex counts, volume, surface area and the three principal moments of inertia, compared within 1e-6 relative. Bodies that match are one group, stored in RebuildReport.body_groups as Solid Bodies indexes. These measures do not change when a body moves or turns, so pattern copies group; a mirrored copy measures the same too and groups with its original, which is wanted for a printing count. Parts with one body, or more than 500, are not measured. The feature tree puts each group of two or more in an Identical Bodies (n) folder inside Solid Bodies, at the place of its first body; the body rows, their numbers and picking are unchanged.

D959: Message bars and hidden messages (2026-11-06, TR203, Phase 7B Stage 3). Each part tab has a strip of bars between the view tools and the view (ui/main_window/message_bars.py). A bar has a key, a level (information or warning, shown by its edge colour), its text, Don't Show Again and Close; showing a key that already shows updates its text instead of adding a bar, and the code that showed it can take it away. Close only closes it this time; Don't Show Again adds the key to the preference messages/hidden and closes it, and a hidden key is never shown. The Preferences dialog lists the hidden messages by name with Show Again (the picked ones, or all when none is picked), applied on OK. The first message on a bar is Rebuilds are paused (TR276), which shows while rebuilds are paused and goes when they run again; the status bar text stays as before. Other messages can move to bars later through the same call.

D960: Standard 3MF metadata (2026-11-06, TR183 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). 3MF export writes the core specification's metadata names next to Application: Title (a custom property named Title, else the part name), Designer (Designer, Author or Drawn By), Description, Copyright, LicenseTerms (Licence or License, with or without Terms) and CreationDate (Created, Creation Date or Date Created), each only when the part has that custom property with a value (names compared without case), and ModificationDate as the export date. The custom properties are still written as fdcad: items as before (D810), so a part number keeps its own item; the 3MF core has no part number name. The bodies keep their counter names: a body's own name needs lasting body names (D254), so that part of item 1 stays open. Item 2, the package thumbnail, was already written by 3MF export (TR381), so nothing was added for it.

D961: File commands and older copies (2026-11-06, TR218 items 1 and 3, Phase 7B Stage 3).
