File menu commands with no default keys: Save All (saves each part with unsaved changes in tab order, stopping at the first cancelled or failed save), Close All (asks about every unsaved part before closing any, as quitting does, D710) and Revert to Saved (a Yes or No question with No as the default; the tab closes without asking and the saved file opens again in the same tab place; a part never saved or without changes gets a status message). On quit the paths of the saved open parts are stored; with the preference Open the parts from last time at start (off by default) a start without files to open opens the ones still on disk. Older copies (core/io/backups.py): with Older copies to keep above 0 (0, the default, keeps none; at most 20) each save first copies the file it writes over to name.backup1.ext in a Backups folder beside the part or in the typed folder, moving older copies up one number and deleting the one past the count; a failed copy never stops the save. The command sweep skips Close All and Revert to Saved, which close the part being swept. Item 2, the start page with thumbnails, is not done.

D962: Pattern by total length and the large count question (2026-11-06, TR142 items 3 and 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). Linear Pattern's Fill gets a third choice, Total length and instances (fill1 or fill2 "total", FDEF owner item with the new total1 and total2 lengths): count copies spread evenly from the seed to total, so the spacing is total / (count - 1); the Spacing field is hidden and Symmetric is not offered with it, since a total measured one way only would be ambiguous both ways. A total of zero or less is a feature error with a next step. Before a new or edited linear or circular pattern is built, the property panel works out its copies from the typed counts (both directions, symmetric sides counted) and above 200 asks Yes or No with No as the default; No keeps the panel open to change the count. Up to fills are not counted, since their count is found while building; the hard limit of 1000 copies stays. Items 1, 2 and 5 (patterns of reference geometry, Edit Seed and a reference point for sketch and table patterns) are not done.

D963: Recently Edited and naming new features (2026-11-06, TR221 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). The property panel emits applied(feature id, was new) after OK; the window keeps the ten newest ids per open part (view state, not saved) and the feature tree's right click menus (on a feature and on empty space) get a Recently Edited submenu, newest first, whose entries open the feature for editing. The preference Name new features as they are made (off by default) starts typing the name of a new feature in the tree once the rebuild after OK has filled the tree again. Item 1's Collapse All key needs the owner's choice of key (Shift+C is taken), so it is not added. Item 2, a description apart from the name, is the feature comment that TR23 added (shown on hover), so nothing new was added. Item 3, the hovered edge's length or radius in the status bar, would measure in the kernel on every hover on the UI thread, which the kernel rules forbid; it is left for a worker based design.

D964: Open end marks and Show in Sketch (2026-11-06, TR341 items 1 and 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). core/sketch/open_ends.py finds the end points that only one non construction curve uses (coincident and overlapping points count as one node, as Check Sketch does); the canvas rings them in the warning colour while the sketch is open, caching the result against the sketch data. A Show in Sketch submenu in the sketch's right click menu holds session wide switches kept on the canvas class (like Show Formulas, D921, reset by the test conftest): Open Ends (on), Driving Dimensions and Reference Dimensions (on; a hidden dimension is not drawn and so cannot be picked), one entry per relation kind present in the sketch to hide its tags, and Normal or Large tags (the caption or the body size of the type scale, apart from the dimension label size; sizes come from the type scale only, U2.1, so there is no smaller one). Items 2, 3 and 5 (direction arrows, extension lines of point on line relations, and a line weight setting) are not done.

D965: Reference dimensions in bulk (2026-11-06, TR111 item 5, Phase 7B Stage 3). With two or more dimensions picked and nothing else, the sketch right click menu offers Make Reference when any is driving (all become reference) or Make Driving when all are reference (each takes its measured size, as the single toggle does, and one that would over define the sketch stays reference through SketchEdit.set_driving); it is one sketch undo step and the status bar says how many changed. New Dimensions Are Reference is a checkable entry in the empty space menu, kept on the canvas class for the session like the other sketch switches: while on, Smart Dimension places reference dimensions, with the same message as the over define preference's reference choice, and opens no value box. Items 1 to 4 (locking the type with a right click, angles to imaginary lines, per arc end choices, and negative values) are not done.

D966: Design table column numbers (2026-11-06, TR198 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). core/table_summary.py reads one design table column the way applying the table does (parse_cell with the part's units and variables) and gives the count, sum, average, smallest and largest of the cells that hold a value; empty cells (the configuration keeps its value) and cells that do not read are left out, and tick box, suppression and text columns have none. The design table editor shows them for the column of the current cell in a line under the table, in the part's units through the property panel's value format (so the number display choices of D949 apply), and updates as cells change. They are shown, not stored: no formula can use them yet. Item 2, a variable read from a CSV file by row, would read a file during evaluation, which needs a design for where the file lives and when it is read again, so it is left open.

D967: Ellipse construction axes (2026-11-06, TR114 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Ellipse tool gets a tool panel option Construction axes, on by default: with it, both axes are added as construction lines through the centre, each from the mirror of its axis point to that point, ending coincident with the axis point and with the centre as its midpoint, so they add no freedom to the sketch. They give lines to dimension (axis lengths, an angle to the ellipse) since relations on ellipses are limited (Coincident and Fixed). Partial Ellipse is unchanged. Dynamic mirror (D514) skips an ellipse with a note, and now skips the helpers tied to it too, so the axes are not mirrored without their ellipse. Items 1 and 2 (rectangle centrelines, rounded corners and inner frame, and editing a polygon after drawing) are not done.

D968: Low disk and memory warnings (2026-11-06, TR220, Phase 7B Stage 3). core/resources.py reads free disk space with shutil.disk_usage (for a file not yet written, its nearest existing folder) and, on Windows, free physical memory with GlobalMemoryStatusEx through ctypes; on other systems memory is not read, so no memory warning shows there rather than a guess (no new dependency). The window checks once a minute: the disks of the recovery folder and of every open saved part (each disk once), warning below 500 MB, and memory below 300 MB. A shortage shows a warning message bar (TR203, D959) on the current part's view with a Save All button (bars can now carry one action button) and Don't Show Again; the bar closes by itself when there is room again. Saving is never blocked.

D969: Add Values to a design table (2026-11-06, TR90 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). The design table editor gets Add Values...: a list of every value that is not a column yet (the same choices as Add Column, shown by their names), each with a tick box; global variables and feature values or sketch dimensions whose text is a formula start ticked, since those are the parameters and equations a table usually drives. OK adds a column for each ticked value with each configuration's current value, as Add Column does, and says how many were added. Item 1 (description, colour and custom property columns, and a configuration made from a parent) is not done.

D970: Shake test for sketches (2026-11-06, TR372, Phase 7B Stage 3). Shake Sketch (sketch right click menu, empty space) works on a deep copy (core/sketch/shake.py): every point the solver does not fully define is given a random push of up to 3 percent of the sketch's size (a fixed seed, so a shake repeats), all at once through the solver's drag, or one point at a time when all at once conflicts; the entities whose points moved, and circles and arcs whose size is still free (a size is not a point, so it cannot be pushed), are picked in the sketch and counted in the status bar. The sketch itself is never changed and no undo step is made. Lock All Points is a checkable entry for the open sketch: while on, pressing on a sketch item does not start a drag and the status bar says why; it is not saved and adds no relations, so it is a comparison aid, not a Fix relation.

D971: Open for Viewing (2026-11-06, TR356, Phase 7B Stage 3). File, Open for Viewing (no default key) opens a part as Open does and marks its session view only; a part that is open already is left as it is. Every document change in FDCAD goes through the part's undo stack (CLAUDE.md 5 item 3), so the stack is now a small QUndoStack subclass that, while view only, drops each pushed command (and macro brackets) and emits blocked, which the window turns into a status bar message saying how to edit. Viewing, measuring, picking and view commands do not push commands and work as usual; a sketch or a property panel can still be opened, but OK is refused the same way, which the message explains. The tab title adds (view only) and an information bar (TR203) offers Edit, which turns the guard off for the rest of the session. View only is not saved in the file.

D972: Feature History of a body (2026-11-06, TR153 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A body row's right click menu gets Feature History. Off the UI thread (core/body_history.py), the body's faces are found in the part's lasting face names; every feature id that appears in a name of one of its faces counts (a pattern copy names the pattern and the feature it copies), with the sketches those features use, listed in tree order. The list opens in a small window that is not modal; clicking a feature selects it in the tree. A feature that left no face on the body (one whose faces a later feature removed) is not listed, since the names are the record. Item 1 (folders inside Solid Bodies) is not done.

D973: Group drag of picked points and circles (2026-11-06, TR53, Phase 7B Stage 3). Dragging a picked curve already moved every picked curve (TR39). Now, when two or more sketch items are picked and the dragged one is among them, a point or a circle moves the whole picked group by the same offset too, instead of snapping alone (a point) or changing its radius (a circle edge); a lone point or circle drags as before. Points in the group move with it. The rigid drag on a held key (no new relations, keeping the shape) is not added: Shift already adds to the selection, and the spec leaves the key to be chosen in the shortcut editor, which needs the owner's choice of default.

D974: Sketch on a picked face with a tool active (2026-11-06, TR123, Phase 7B Stage 3). Most of this was already there: a sketch tool command with no sketch open starts a new sketch with that tool waiting (then_tool), on the picked flat face or plane, or else through the plane picker, which shows the planes and highlights the plane or face under the cursor; the pick opens the sketch with the tool active. What changed: the picker's status text names the tool (Select a plane or flat face to draw a Line on), and a test covers the whole flow. The click that picks the face is not also taken as the first point of the shape, so a stray first point never lands on an unseen spot of the new sketch plane; the next click starts drawing.

D975: Reduce Motion follows the system (2026-11-06, TR294 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Until the user sets Reduce motion in Preferences (the stored appearance/animations key is missing), FDCAD reads the system: on Windows SystemParametersInfo SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION (window animations off means reduce motion), on a Mac the Accessibility Reduce motion setting through defaults read com.apple.universalaccess reduceMotion; anything else, or a failed read, counts as not reduced. Once set in Preferences the choice wins. The test conftest replaces the reader so tests never depend on the machine. Items 2 (screen reader roles and Describe Part) and 3 (Large Controls, which would change the theme's control heights on the spacing scale) are not done.

D976: Text along circles and splines (2026-11-06, TR230, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sketch text's Along list now offers circles and splines besides lines and arcs. A full circle is followed clockwise starting at the bottom, so the letters stand outward and a Centre aligned text sits on top (the usual badge layout); Left starts at the bottom. A spline is sampled into 400 points (core freeform sample) and the text is placed by length along them, each letter turned to the local direction; past either end the end piece goes on straight. A new Start Offset (mm, the text item's offset key, an FDEF owner item, stored only when not zero) moves the text along the curve after the alignment, for lines and arcs too. Ellipses are still refused, with a message naming what can be followed.

D977: See-through colour for sketch pictures (2026-11-06, TR116 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). The image's own alpha was already drawn (Qt keeps it when a PNG is read), so that part needed nothing. New: a picture can name one colour (clear_colour, #RRGGBB, and clear_tolerance, 0 to 1 of the largest RGB distance, default 0.1; FDEF owner item, stored only when a colour is set) whose pixels are drawn fully clear, for example a scan's white paper. The tool panel takes the colour as typed text (a wrong one is refused with a message) and the tolerance in percent. The mask is worked out with numpy over the whole image (core/sketch/picture.py clear_mask) and the cleared image is cached per picture, colour and tolerance, so painting stays fast; the stored image is not changed. Item 2, Trace, is not done.

D978: Linked values (2026-11-06, TR193, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two or more picked dimensions of one sketch can be linked under a shared name (sketch right click Link Values, which suggests Link1, Link2 and so on): each gets the dimension key link (an FDEF owner item, stored only when set) and the first picked dimension's value and text. SketchEdit.set_dimension then gives every dimension with the same link the new value, whichever was changed, so any of them drives the others without an equation and without a global variable. Only one kind links (lengths with lengths, angles with angles); a bad name or mixed kinds are refused with a message and no undo step. Labels show the name before the value. Unlink Values keeps the values. Links stay inside one sketch; across sketches a global variable is the way, as before.

D979: Array Along Curve offsets (2026-11-06, TR373, Phase 7B Stage 3). Array Along Curve gets Start offset and End offset lengths (start_offset and end_offset, FDEF owner items, stored only when not zero). The copies are spread as before but over the curve between the offsets: with Count, instance k (k of 2 or more) sits at start + (k - 1) x (length - start - end) / (count - 1) along the curve, so with no offsets nothing changes; with Spacing, the spacing must fit between the offsets. The seed stays where it is. Offsets that add up to more than the curve, or a negative offset, are feature errors with a next step. The orientation choice of the item (follow the curve, keep, or stay square to a picked face) is not done beyond the existing Orient to Curve tick: square to a face needs a face pick in this panel.

D980: Extra offset for reference geometry (2026-11-06, TR149, Phase 7B Stage 3). Every method of Plane, Axis and Coordinate System gets six more values and a tick at the end of its panel: Extra offset X, Y and Z, Extra turn about X, Y and Z, and Flip after the extra offset (params extra_dx to extra_rz and extra_flip, FDEF owner items, stored only when not zero or ticked). They apply after the method in the reference's own axes (core/features/extra_placement.py): Z is the plane normal, the axis direction or the frame's Z, X the plane's or frame's X (for an axis, a fixed direction square to it), Y = Z x X; first the offset, then the turns about X, the turned Y and the turned Z, then the flip. With none set the placement is exactly as before. Formulas can drive them (length and angle kinds are declared).

D981: Linear Pattern spacing laws (2026-11-06, TR366 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Each Linear Pattern direction gets Spacing law (law1, law2: even, the default and the old behaviour; growing; random; FDEF owner items with ratio, jitter and seed values). Growing: the first gap is the spacing and each next gap is the ratio times the one before (ratio above zero, 1.2 by default). Random: each copy moves along the direction by a uniform amount up to the percent of the spacing given (at most 49 percent, so copies never swap places), from a seeded generator, so a rebuild gives the same layout. The symmetric side mirrors the positions. Total length and Up to fills keep even spacing in their counts; the law then moves the copies. Not done: a list of fractions (the panel has no text field of this kind yet), per copy angles, and laws for curve and circular patterns.

D982: Sketch layers (2026-11-06, TR389, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch keeps a list of layers (name, colour as #RRGGBB or none, style solid or dashed, visible) and a map from curve id to layer name, saved as the sketch keys layers and layer_of (FDEF owner items, written only when the sketch has layers; deleted curves drop out on save). Points are not put on layers; they follow their curves. The canvas draws a layer's curves in its colour and style unless they are picked, hovered or in conflict (those states still win), and treats a hidden layer like hidden construction (TR419): not drawn, not picked. Layers are display only: the solver and profiles see every curve, so hiding a layer never changes the shape. The Layers submenu (sketch right click; with curves picked it also offers New Layer with them, Put on and Take Off Layer) makes each change one sketch undo step. Layers also serve as the groups of TR419 item 2 (no block needed): Pick selects all of a layer's curves (so a drag moves them together, TR39 and D973), Show hides them together, and Lock (the layer key locked) refuses drags of its curves and of their points with a status message. With this, TR419 is complete (item 1 was D932).

D983: Remove History (2026-11-06, TR158, Phase 7B Stage 3). Edit, Remove History (no default key) asks Yes or No (No is the default), then writes the built shape as STEP data off the UI thread (save_bodies.step_bytes) and, as one undo macro, rolls the bar to the end, deletes every feature after the origin and the three planes (last first) and adds one Imported STEP feature named Body holding the data as an embedded block (AddImport, so undo removes the block too). The whole part is turned, not one body of a multibody part: a STEP of several solids imports as several bodies again, so the bodies stay apart. Variables, configurations, appearance by face and custom properties stay, but values that drove the deleted features have nothing to drive; face colours that the STEP writer does not carry are lost. Embedded files of deleted import features stay in the part until Purge Unused gains them.

D984: Point where a line meets a curved face (2026-11-06, TR353, Phase 7B Stage 3). Reference point Intersection now finds every crossing of its two picks, not only the first: an axis or other endless line is followed 100 m both ways as an edge, an edge or a face is used as it is, and the kernel's distance solutions at zero gap are the crossings, without repeats, ordered along the first line or edge. A new value Crossing number (the param crossing, an FDEF owner item, 1 by default) picks one, since a reference point is one point; a number past the crossings is a feature error that says how many there are. Two lines and a line with a plane are solved as before.

D985: Partial hyperbola (2026-11-06, TR374 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch tool Partial Hyperbola (in the Spline list, no default key): click the centre, the vertex and one end; the branch runs from that end through the vertex to its mirror across the axis. It is drawn exactly as the conic through the two ends whose end tangents meet on the axis at a / c (a the vertex distance, c the end's distance along the axis over a), with shape value c / (c + 1), which is above 0.5 as a hyperbola needs, then stored as a spline like Conic and Parabola (D902). An end not beyond the vertex, or on the axis, is refused with a message. The 3D curve from x, y and z expressions is not done.

D986: Merge Into Sketch (2026-11-06, TR122 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch row's right click menu offers Merge Into Sketch when another sketch (not a derived one) has the very same plane or face reference, so the sketch coordinates match. core/sketch/merge.py copies everything of the merged sketch into the kept one with new ids at the same coordinates: points, curves, relations, dimensions (a name the kept sketch already uses is dropped), pictures and texts (new ids) and layers; the merged sketch's fixed origin maps onto the kept one's, so relations to the origin hold and only one origin fix remains. One undo macro updates the kept sketch (DocumentChange) and deletes the merged one. A sketch that any feature uses is refused with a message, since its features would lose their sketch; merging the other way works. Item 2 (linked copies) is not done.

D987: Crossing and fork marks (2026-11-06, TR238 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). core/sketch/crossing_marks.py finds the points where two non construction curves cross away from an end they share (the same test Check Sketch uses for crossings, D116) and the end points where three or more curves meet. The open sketch draws an X at each crossing and a square at each fork in the warning colour, next to the open end rings (D964), cached against the sketch data. A Crossings and Forks switch in Show in Sketch (on by default, every sketch for the session) turns them off. Not done from this item: keeping changed dimensions locked while dragging, and a polar grid.

D988: Print Estimate with infill and walls (2026-11-06, TR187 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). The estimate job now also measures the surface area. The window gets Infill (percent, 100 by default, which is the solid estimate as before) and Walls (1 to 20, 2 by default). Below 100 percent the weight counts a solid shell of area x walls x line width (the active printer profile's nozzle size, else 0.4 mm), at most the whole volume, plus the infill percent of the rest; the top and bottom layers are treated as walls too. It stays an estimate: slicers vary in how they print thin areas and overlaps. Item 1 (a check for heights and walls that are not whole layers or line widths) is not done.

D989: More export formats (2026-11-06, TR369 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). File, Save As offers IGES (the kernel's IGES writer, millimetres, solids as BRep), OpenCascade BREP (BRepTools, the exact kernel shape), PLY (binary little endian, millimetres) and glTF as one binary .glb file (glTF 2.0 with one mesh of positions and indices, written by FDCAD itself from the same triangles as STL, in metres since glTF has no unit). The meshes use the part's kept mesh settings without the STL and 3MF options window; colours are not written to PLY or glTF yet. Each writer goes through a temporary file in the target folder, and runs in the export job off the UI thread. The 3D DXF wireframe of edges is not done.

D990: Fill holes by size and voids (2026-11-06, TR388, Phase 7B Stage 3). Delete Face, which already filled picked hole, pocket and boss faces, gets Holes up to (hole_size, a diameter; 0, the default, is off) and Fill voids (voids). core/features/simplify.py finds round holes as cylinder faces whose outward side faces their own axis (so a pin or boss is never taken) with a diameter up to the size, and fills voids by keeping each solid's outer shell only (BRepClass3d outer shell), keeping the face names. The holes found join the picked faces and are healed with the chosen option (patch or fill); with either new value the picks may be empty. Nothing to fill is a feature error with a next step. Holes are found by their cylinder walls: a blind hole's flat bottom is patched with it by the kernel's defeaturing; other small features (bosses, ribs) still need picking.

D991: Standard profiles (2026-11-06, TR367, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sketch, Shapes (TR228) gets six more kinds, centred on the sketch origin (core/sketch/std_profiles.py): angle (two legs and a thickness), channel (height, flange depth, thickness), I beam (height, width, web and flange thickness; the dialog now has four value boxes), rectangular tube and round tube (an outside and an inside outline, added as two closed loops in one undo step, the circles as two half arcs each) and the top hat DIN rail (EN 60715 TS 35 x 7.5: 35 mm over the flanges, a 27 mm hat, sheet 1 mm by default). Sizes are typed, so any catalogue size can be used; the defaults are common ones (a 100 mm I beam has a 55 mm flange, 4.1 mm web and 5.7 mm flanges). Corner radii of rolled sections are not drawn: add Sketch Fillet where needed. T slot and V slot extrusion profiles are not included: their outlines differ by maker, so a picked catalogue file (Insert DXF or SVG) fits them better.

D992: Printer limits (2026-11-06, TR413, Phase 7B Stage 3). A printer profile gets keep out zones, the spec's no print zones (rectangles x0 y0 x1 y1 in mm from the bed's front left corner, typed in Preferences, Printing as numbers separated by semicolons; a zone that does not read keeps the old zones) and a head clearance (the height under the gantry for printing one part at a time; 0, the default, is not set). Build Volume, which places the part in the middle of the bed as drawn, now also counts bodies whose footprint reaches into a zone and, with a clearance set and more than one body, bodies taller than it when more than one is (one tall body can print last), and adds a warning for each to its message; the part still counts as fitting. FDCAD has no arrange on the bed command yet (TR301 is open), so the zones are checked where Build Volume places the part; TR301 is to avoid them when it is built.

D993: Layer Preview (2026-11-06, TR315, Phase 7B Stage 3). An on and off analysis overlay like Overhang Analysis (ToggleOverlay, worked out again after each rebuild): the part is cut off the UI thread with planes across the build direction of the print orientation (Lay Face Flat, else the part's Z), one per layer height of the active printer profile from the lowest point up (core/printing/layer_lines.py), and the cut edges are drawn as thin lines. Above 400 layers every n-th layer is drawn (n the smallest that keeps it at 400 or fewer) and the status bar says which; the layer count is always the full one. It sits in the Evaluate tab's drop down with Enclosed Cavities and Edge Angle Analysis, with no default key.

D994: Change a fillet to a chamfer and back (2026-11-06, TR134, Phase 7B Stage 3). A constant size fillet's right click menu offers Change to Chamfer and an equal distance chamfer's offers Change to Fillet (core/fillet_chamfer.py). The feature keeps its id, its edge picks (edges, faces of edges and features) and its size as typed (the radius becomes the distance and back); options only one kind has are dropped, and a default name follows the kind (Fillet 2 becomes Chamfer 2). It is one undo step (ReplaceFeature). Variable, multiple radius and face fillets, and angle, vertex, offset and face to face chamfers are not offered. Its new faces have the other kind's names, so features after it that picked its faces may need their picks again; the status bar says so when such features exist.

D995: OBJ export (2026-11-06, TR336 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Save As writes Wavefront OBJ (.obj): one object of shared vertices and triangle faces in millimetres, from the same triangles as STL and PLY (the part's kept mesh settings), through a temporary file, in the export job. No normals or materials are written; slicers and viewers work them out. The mesh preview before saving and refining by largest edge length and aspect ratio are not done: the kernel's mesher has no edge length limit, so it needs its own design.

D996: Deviation along an edge (2026-11-06, TR199 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). With one edge picked, Measure now also gives the angle between the two faces that meet there, at 21 points spread along the edge (its ends included): largest, smallest and average (core/edge_deviation.py, the same outward normal reading as Edge Angle Analysis, D929). 0 means the faces meet smoothly at that point, so a blend that is tangent only in places shows a smallest of 0 and a larger largest. A free edge or a seam (not two faces) gives no rows. Item 1, curvature colours on faces with a readout, is not done.

D997: Omit attach edges (2026-11-06, TR64 item 6, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Fillet that picks whole features (refs.features) can tick Omit attach edges (param omit_attach, an FDEF owner item, written only with feature picks): of the picked feature's face edges, only those whose faces were all made by that feature are rounded, so the edges where it meets the earlier body stay sharp. Picked edges and faces are not filtered. Chamfer has no feature picks, so it has no such option. Items 1 to 5 (keep features, round corners, overflow, select through faces, partial chamfer edges) are not done.

D998: Shell Check Walls (2026-11-06, TR147 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Shell panel gets Check Walls: off the UI thread it samples the bend of every face of the part before the shell (the same grid as the shell's own pre check, PLAN 5A item 4; faces bulging out limit an inward wall, faces curving in an outward one) and says which faces bend tighter than the typed wall, tightest first (up to three named), with the smallest radius, or that every face fits and how tight the tightest bend is. It only reads the part: nothing is built or changed. Items 1 and 3 (draft and dome options) are not done.

D999: Fragments and Inside at least (2026-11-06, TR371 items 1 and 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two more Combine operations rather than new commands, since they take the same body picks: Fragments cuts the picked bodies at every crossing and keeps every piece as its own body; Inside at least keeps only the volume inside at least Number of bodies (min_bodies, 2 by default, an FDEF owner item) of the picked bodies, joined. Both build the same cells (core/features/combine.py fragments): each new body splits every cell into the part inside it and the part outside it, and adds what lies outside all earlier bodies, counting how many bodies cover each cell; the booleans carry face names as the other Combine operations do. No volume inside enough bodies is a feature error with a next step. Item 3, Shear, is not done.

D1000: Shear in Scale (2026-11-06, TR371 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Shear is part of Scale rather than its own command, since it is the same general transform about the same centre and body picks: Shear angle (shear_angle, under 80 degrees), Shear along and Shear by height along (shear_along, shear_from: x, y or z, different) add tan(angle) times the distance along the second axis to the first, after the scale factors. A shear keeps the volume. Any shear uses the general transform, so circles become ellipses and those faces general surfaces, as with a per axis scale. FDEF owner item: the three params.

D1001: Turn style (2026-11-06, TR415 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Preferences, General gets Turn style (view/turn_style): Free (the kernel's own turning, the default), Turntable (Z stays up) and Arcball. Turntable is the old Keep the model upright checkbox (TR209, D832), which the choice replaces; a stored view/lock_up of true reads as Turntable, so nobody loses the setting. Arcball (ui/viewport/arcball.py, plain maths) maps the drag's start and the pointer to a ball filling the smaller side of the view and turns the camera the other way by the angle between them, about the picked turning centre or the view's centre, always from the camera at the press so the turn does not drift; a drag outside the ball slides on its rim and rolls the view about the line of sight. Trackpad scrolling and arrow keys turn as before.

D1002: Help for This Tool (2026-11-06, TR380 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Help gets Help for This Tool (command help.tool, so it can take a key in the shortcut editor). It looks up, in order, the open panel's feature, the sketch tool in use and the last command run, and opens the local guide at the first match (ui/help/topics.py, no Qt): a heading equal to the name, then a heading containing it, then a page naming it in bold; with no match it opens the contents. The default key (F1, and Command and question mark on Mac) is an owner item for SHORTCUTS.md, so it ships with no key. Items 1, 4 and 5 are not done.

D1003: Default keys and the Windows rules (2026-11-06, TR380 item 5, Phase 7B Stage 3). ui/input/key_rules.py checks key strings, and tests/ui/test_key_rules.py runs it on every default key for Windows: no Ctrl and Alt together (AltGr), no Windows key, no Alt and a letter that opens a top menu, and no key on two commands. Today's defaults pass; the one Alt key, Alt+C (Centerline), clashes with no menu letter (F, E, V, I, T, H). Quit and Force Rebuild: Quit uses the platform's standard key, which Qt leaves empty on Windows, and on Mac it is Command+Q while Force Rebuild's Ctrl+Q becomes Control+Q, so the two never share a key; the test checks both platforms. A change of default keys stays an owner item for SHORTCUTS.md, so a future clash makes this test fail rather than moving a key.

D1004: Box drag from the model (2026-11-06, TR224 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Already true in the 3D view: a left press anywhere, on the part or not, becomes a box (or a lasso, TR19) once the pointer moves past the drag distance, and only a press that does not move picks the item under it. So no key is needed and none was added; handles, value labels and Ctrl on a plane still take a press first. tests/ui/test_box_on_model.py drags from the middle of a box part (it needs a display, like the other kernel view tests). Item 1 (pick through see through faces with Shift for the face itself) is not done: Shift already adds to the selection and Alt already picks the next item under the pointer, so it needs an owner choice of key. Item 4 (a before and after slider in a preview) is not done.

D1005: Corner Ears (2026-11-06, TR189 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Print feature (core/features/corner_ears.py, beside Crush Ribs in the command tabs). Pick the flat face on the bed; a disc Ear diameter across (10 mm) and Ear thickness thick (0.4 mm) is centred on each outer corner of that face whose inside angle is at most Corners up to (120 degrees), lying on the face's plane and growing into the part, fused. Corners come from the face's outer wire walked in order: the turn between the end tangent of one edge and the start tangent of the next gives the angle, and its sign against the outline's winding tells outer from inside corners, so it works on curved outlines and whichever way the wire runs. Holes in the face get no ears. No corner sharp enough is a feature error with a next step. FDEF owner item: the new type and its params.

D1006: Drain Holes (2026-11-06, TR189 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Print feature with no picks: for every closed void of the part (core/cavities.py enclosed_voids, as the TR284 drain fix uses) it cuts one round hole, Hole diameter across (3 mm), from the void's lowest point straight down along Z (Drain toward Bottom) or from its highest point straight up (Top), running past the part so it always opens. The lowest point is the void's nearest point to a plane below it; when that is on a level flat floor the hole starts at the middle of the largest such face, away from the walls. Z is the drain direction rather than a picked one, since the slicer's up is the part's Z. The TR284 fix button stays: it drills from the nearest outer flat face to one void as a Hole feature. A part with no void is a feature error with a next step. FDEF owner item: the new type and its params. Item 1 (polygon holes) is not done.

D1007: Polygon Holes (2026-11-06, TR189 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Print feature: pick the round faces of holes; each is cut out to a polygon prism along its axis over the face's length whose flats touch the hole's circle (corner radius r / cos(pi / n)), so material is only removed and the flats sit at the nominal size. Sides is a count from 3 to 64; empty gives twice the diameter in mm (a common rule for printed holes), at least 3. One flat lies across the polygon's first side at an angle of pi / n from the hole's own frame; the turn is not a setting. A picked pin is a feature error with a next step. FDEF owner item: the new type and its param (sides).

D1008: Tool pocket with a clearance and a finger notch (2026-11-06, TR408 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). Met by existing tools rather than a new feature: one sketch holds the picked or traced outline and a circle over its edge for the notch, and Extruded Cut with Profile offset (TR344, D880) grows the joined outline by the clearance. A separate command would ask for the same outline, depth and clearance, plus a notch position that a sketched circle gives more freely. tests/core/features/test_tool_pocket.py builds one and the guide gives the steps under Profile offset. Items 1 to 3 (transition spiral, stone seat, sprue tree) are not done.

D1009: Base Pad (2026-11-06, TR414 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Print feature: pick the flat bed face; a pad Pad thickness thick (0.6 mm) is added as a separate body, its outline the face's outline grown by Margin (3 mm, the same rounded offset as Profile offset, D880, holes in the face stay holes) and moved Air gap (0.2 mm) away from the face along its outward normal. It is never fused, even with no gap, so the slicer gets two bodies and the pad can be given its own settings (TR383 when it lands). A face whose outline cannot grow by the margin is a feature error with a next step. FDEF owner item: the new type and its params. Item 1 (material interlock teeth) is not done.

D1010: 3D DXF wireframe (2026-11-06, TR369, Phase 7B Stage 3). File, Save As gets 3D DXF wireframe (.dxf): an R12 ASCII DXF in millimetres ($INSUNITS 4) with every edge of the part once, straight edges as LINE and others as 3D POLYLINE (flag 8, vertices flag 32) through points that keep within 0.01 mm of the curve; degenerate edges are left out. R12 entities, as the flat DXF export uses, so every reader takes it. Only Save As offers it, and a .dxf name in Save As means this wireframe: the flat face and flat pattern DXF keeps its own Export command. No mesh settings are asked.

D1011: 3D curve from expressions (2026-11-06, TR374, Phase 7B Stage 3). Part of Curve Through Points rather than a new feature: the panel gets X(t), Y(t), Z(t) (formulas in t with the safe expression parser, plain numbers in the part's unit, variables and functions as in any value field), t from, to and a number of points (2 to 5000), and Fill Points, which replaces the table with the evaluated points (core/features/point_curve.py expression_points). The curve is then the smooth curve through those points, as for typed points, so sweeps and lofts use it unchanged. The expressions and range are kept in data.equation only so the panel shows them again; the rebuild uses the stored points, so changing a variable later does not move the curve until Fill Points is clicked again. FDEF owner item: data.equation.

D1012: Partial edges for Chamfer (2026-11-06, TR64 item 5, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Chamfer panel gets the Partial Edges group of Fillet (D519): Distance or Percent, start and end, and the flip button, with the same params (partial, start_distance, end_distance, start_percent, end_percent, partial_flip). It shows only for a symmetric Distance Distance chamfer, since the bevel is made with one distance on the split piece; a file with partial on another chamfer type is a feature error with a next step. The routine is the partial fillet's (core/features/fillet_partial.py): split the part square to the edge at the ends of the range, bevel that piece of the edge, fuse and merge faces back, carrying names; the bevel face is chamfer/<edge name>. An end set by a picked vertex or reference (the rest of item 5) is not done. FDEF owner item: the partial params on chamfer.

D1013: Sketch line weight (2026-11-06, TR341 item 5, Phase 7B Stage 3). Show in Sketch gets Thin, Normal, Bold and Extra Bold Lines (0.75, 1, 1.5 and 2 times), which scale the pen of every sketch curve and the size of point marks, for every sketch until FDCAD closes like the other Show in Sketch choices (a class setting, D964). The display scale part is already met: the sketch draws in Qt's device independent pixels, so lines and marks grow with the screen's scaling on both platforms; the choice is for screens or projectors where that is still thin. Dimension text has its own size (Large Tags and the typography roles), so this choice leaves text alone. Items 2 and 3 (direction arrows, line extensions) are not done.

D1014: Polar sketch grid (2026-11-06, TR238 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Preferences, Sketch gets Grid (Square or Polar, sketch/grid_kind) and Polar grid angle (1 to 90 degrees, 15 by default, sketch/polar_angle). The polar grid draws rings round the sketch origin at the same spacing the square grid uses (the part's grid spacing, TR102, or the zoom's step) and spokes every angle step, only the rings that cross the view. Snap to grid on a polar grid rounds the radius to the ring spacing and the direction to the angle step (ui/sketch_tools/polar_grid.py, no Qt). The centre is the sketch origin; a picked centre is not a setting. Locking changed dimensions while dragging is not done.

D1015: Pattern reference point (2026-11-06, TR142 item 5, Phase 7B Stage 3). Already met: Sketch Driven and Table Driven Pattern take an optional Reference point (refs.point, a vertex or a sketch point, resolved like any placement) and use the seed's centre without one (D234, the table pattern's own decision); the guide describes both. Nothing was added; PLAN records it. Items 1 and 2 (patterns of reference geometry, Edit Seed from a copy) are open.

D1016: Edit Seed (2026-11-06, TR142 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). The 3D view's right click menu on a face of a pattern or mirror copy gets Edit Seed, which opens the first seed feature in the property panel. The copy is found from the face's name, <fid>/instance<i>.<j>/ or <fid>/mirror<k>/ (core/features/seed_of.py, no Qt), and the seed from that pattern's refs.features. Copies of faces or bodies have no seed feature, so they get no Edit Seed; their pattern is still in the feature submenu. A pattern of a pattern opens the inner pattern, which is the seed it copies.

D1017: Square to face (2026-11-06, TR373, Phase 7B Stage 3). Array Along Curve gets Square to face (refs.square_face, one face, an FDEF owner item): each copy's frame has Z along the face's normal at the point of the face nearest the curve (projected onto the face's surface) and X along the curve with its part along the normal taken out; the motion takes the frame at the curve's start to the frame at the copy's place, so the seed's relation to the face is kept. It wins over Orient to curve, which is greyed while it is ticked. With the tick on, a face clicked in the view becomes this face rather than a body to copy. A curve that runs along the normal or a face with no normal there is a feature error with a next step.

D1018: List of fractions (2026-11-06, TR366 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Linear Pattern's Spacing law gets List of fractions (law1 or law2 "fractions", with fractions1 or fractions2, a text param such as "0.1, 0.3, 1", FDEF owner items): copy k + 1 sits at the k-th number times the run from the seed to the last copy as even spacing would place it (Spacing times the copies), so 1 is the last even place and numbers past 1 or below 0 reach beyond. One number per copy, split by commas, semicolons or spaces; a wrong count or a word is a feature error with a next step. The symmetric side mirrors it, as for the other laws. Body tool panels get a plain text field kind for it (kept in params, left out when empty). Per copy angles and laws for curve patterns are not done.

D1500: Per copy angles and curve spacing laws (2026-11-07, TR366, Phase 7B Stage 3). Circular Pattern gets law1 and law2, "even" (default) or "angles", with angles1 or angles2, a text list of degrees (FDEF owner items): copy k + 1 turns by the k-th number from the seed, so the copies can sit at any angles; one number per copy, Reverse turns them the other way, and a symmetric direction 2 reuses direction 1's angles. The list is parsed like Linear Pattern's fractions (D1018). Array Along Curve gets law, ratio, jitter, seed and fractions (FDEF owner items), the same laws as Linear Pattern (D981, D1018) through the shared law_positions with an empty suffix. The step is the curve's even step (the spacing, or the room between the offsets divided by the gaps), and the law measures from the start offset. On an open curve a copy past the end offset or before the start is a feature error with a next step; on a closed curve positions wrap round. With this, TR366 is done.

D1501: Seed cell and grid rotation (2026-11-07, TR270 item 2 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Linear Pattern gets seed_cell1 and seed_cell2 (numbers, 1 to the count, FDEF owner items): the seed sits in that cell, so the steps along the direction run from 1 - cell to count - cell and earlier cells are copies the other way. Instance numbers stay the cell numbers (cell 1 is always the first, so the seed's own number is its cell), which keeps Skip lists readable. It is refused with Symmetric, which already centres the seed. rotate (an angle, FDEF owner item, shown with direction 2) turns both directions about their common normal, so the grid turns in its plane while copies still only move. Seed only (direction 2) now leaves out every cell off both axes (i and j not 0) instead of only positive ones, which a seed cell needs; with Symmetric on direction 1 it now also drops the far side cells off the axes, as its name says. Hiding instances in the view only, explode (item 1) and box skip (item 3) are not done.

D1502: Spacing and overall size (2026-11-07, TR398 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Linear Pattern's fill1 or fill2 gets "fit" (an FDEF owner item): the count is the whole number of spacings that fit in the overall size plus one (the seed), floor(size / spacing) + 1. The overall size reuses total1 or total2, the Total length field, so no new param is needed; Symmetric is hidden for it as for Up to reference. More than the instance limit is a feature error with a next step.

D1503: Suppress Region (2026-11-07, TR398 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Every pattern built by the shared engine (Linear, Circular, Sketch, Table, Point and Fill Pattern, and Mirror) takes refs.region, faces and sketches, and region_mode, "inside" (default) or "outside" (FDEF owner items). A copy is skipped when the seed's centre (seed_centre, the area centre of its faces) moved by the copy's motion projects onto a region face inside its boundary (or onto none, for outside). Sketches give their closed profile faces; a sketch with no closed shape is a feature error. Skipped copies join the typed skip list for that build only, so their numbers stay. The fields sit in the Instances to Skip group. Box skip by dragging (TR270 item 3) is separate and not done.

D1504: Sweep turns and Follow Curvature (2026-11-07, TR56 items 3 and 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep's twist gets "turns" with twist_turns (a number, FDEF owner items): the twist angle is the turns times 360 degrees and uses the same least turning spine as the angle twist (D703). On a closed path (the path wire is closed) an angle or turns twist that is not a whole number of turns is a feature error with a next step, since the ends would not meet. Orientation gets "curvature" (FDEF owner item): the kernel's Frenet frame on every path, even a flat one where Follow Path keeps the section to the path's plane (D707), so the section turns with the path's bend as along a helix. It sets the turning itself, so any twist but None is a feature error. A scaled sweep refuses turns as it refuses an angle. Start and end tangency (item 1) and merging tangent side faces (item 2) are not done.

D1505: Hole taper and depth to the tip (2026-11-07, TR144 item 3 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Hole Tool gets taper (boolean) with taper_angle, and point_in_depth (boolean), FDEF owner items. Taper narrows the plain wall from where it starts (under a counterbore or countersink) to the bottom by the angle from the axis, so the wall face is a cone but keeps its wall role; it is for simple, counterbore, countersink and tapped holes, below 45 degrees, and is refused with a slot or a far side countersink (those build their own sections). A taper that closes the hole before its bottom is a feature error with a next step. Point_in_depth puts the drill point's tip at the depth, so the wall stops one tip length higher (with a taper, the shorter tip of the narrower end, solved in closed form). A start plane other than the clicked face is not done.

D1506: Counterdrill (2026-11-07, TR144 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new hole_type "counterdrill" (an FDEF owner item) with cbore_diameter, cbore_depth and cdrill_angle (the included angle, 118 degrees, a twist drill's point, when left out). The section runs down the counterbore wall to its depth, then a cone (role cdrill) to the hole diameter, then the hole wall, so the depth of the counterbore is to where the cone starts. Sizes come from the counterbore table for the head form, as for Counterbore, and the hole list calls it Counterdrill. It has no slot, bridge or near side countersink options. Hole element stacks (item 1) and user hole standards (item 4) are not done.

D1507: Thread classes (2026-11-07, TR393, Phase 7B Stage 3). Tapped holes and Thread (modelled) get thread_class (an FDEF owner item): "none" (default) or a class from core/features/thread_class.py, metric ISO 965-1 6H, 4H, 5H, 7H, 6G, 7G (internal) and 6g, 4h, 6h, 8g, 6f, 6e (external), inch ASME B1.1 1B to 3B and 1A to 3A. The allowance comes from the published formulas: metric fundamental deviations e, f, g and G of 50, 30, 15 and 15 micrometres plus 11 times the pitch in mm, H and h none; inch 1A and 2A 0.3 times the class 2A pitch diameter tolerance 0.0015 D^(1/3) + 0.0015 sqrt(9P) + 0.015 P^(2/3) inches, 3A and the B classes none. A modelled thread adds half the diameter allowance to its clearance per side (on top of the print fit) unless a clearance is typed, so the class sets the thread's allowance; a tapped hole's modelled thread does the same. A shaft class on a hole thread or a hole class on a shaft thread is a feature error naming the kind to choose. The Hole Table's thread column shows it after the size ("M5 6H"). The hole panel offers the internal classes; the Thread panel offers every class since the edge decides the kind.

D1508: Hole values in formulas (2026-11-07, TR397 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). The table values a Hole feature uses (diameter, depth, head and thread sizes) are its own stored params, so they already are named values such as "cbore_diameter@Hole 1" (D310 stores the filled values, not the table). What was missing is the count: the Hole result's extras get "count" (the number of position points that made a hole) and MEASURED_VALUES lists it for hole, so "count@Hole 1" and "count@<id>" work as for Fill Pattern (TR57), with the same rule that a formula above the hole is an error. Radial placement (item 1) is not done.

D1509: Where a sweep crosses itself (2026-11-07, TR139 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). When the swept solid is not valid (the kernel check that finds self crossing, D218), the message comes from core/features/sweep_errors.py: the path's curvature is sampled (24 points per edge, in wire order, reversed edges measured backwards) and the tightest bend is named by its distance along the path, its share of the length and its radius; when the profile reaches further from the path's start than that radius (the farthest corner of its bounding box) the message says so. The next steps are the spec's three: a larger bend radius, a smaller profile, or splitting the path there. A straight path (no bend) keeps the old message. Guided and scaled sweeps keep theirs. Show Sections (item 2) is not done.

D1510: Flat sided thread forms (2026-11-07, TR254 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Thread's form gets "trapezoidal", "acme", "square", "buttress" and "pipe" (FDEF owner items), built by one section maker from (leading flank angle, trailing flank angle, depth) taken from the published basic profiles: metric trapezoidal ISO 2904 15 and 15 degrees, 0.5P; ACME ASME B1.5 14.5 and 14.5, 0.5P; square 0 and 0, 0.5P; buttress ASME B1.9 7 (load) and 45 (back), 0.6P; pipe ISO 228 and ISO 7 (Whitworth) 27.5 and 27.5, 0.640327P. The crest and root flats are equal and take the rest of the pitch, so the Whitworth form's round crests and roots become flats at the same depth. All four kinds (cut or extruded, shaft or hole) work, and clearance and thread classes apply as for the V forms. The size list still holds the 60 degree sizes, so these take a typed diameter and pitch. A user profile from a sketch and the end finishes (fade out, chamfer, square) are not done.

D1511: Tapered pipe tapped holes (2026-11-07, TR145 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new hole_type "pipe_tapped" (an FDEF owner item) takes the tapped hole's thread values and always tapers the wall 1 in 16 on the diameter (half angle atan(1/32)), using the taper of D1505. Sizes: ANSI gives NPT 1/16 to 2 from ASME B1.20.1 (outside diameter and threads per inch, effective thread length L2 = (0.80 D + 6.8) p), ISO gives Rc 1/8 to 2 from ISO 7-1 (gauge plane major diameter, threads per inch, gauge length as the thread length); the drills are the usual tap drills. The filled diameter is the drill plus the thread length over 16, so the hole narrows from the face to the drill size at the thread depth, which is also the hole depth. The cosmetic thread mark and the Hole Table name the size ("1/2 NPT"); thread classes and a modelled thread are not offered for it. A tapered modelled thread for Thread is not done, so TR145 stays open.

D1512: Patterns of patterns (2026-11-07, TR141 item 2 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Linear, Circular, Sketch or Table Pattern whose seed is features can itself be a seed feature of a later pattern or mirror (patterns.NESTED_TYPES). Its tools are each inner seed feature's solid together with that solid moved to every inner copy that is not skipped (typed skips and Suppress Region, D1503), built against the part before the inner pattern, so one boolean per seed still adds or cuts them all; it nests to any depth. Face names gain both roles, <outer>/instance<i>.<j>/<inner>/instance<k>.<l>/<face>. The seed list in the panels offers such patterns; a pattern of faces or bodies is refused with a next step (Geometry pattern already copied those, D604). Body seeds already took a pattern's bodies by their faces. Pattern chains with reorderable steps (item 1) are not done.

D1513: Varying instances (2026-11-07, TR59 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Linear Pattern's law1 and law2 get "increment" with increment1 or increment2 (lengths), and Circular Pattern's get "increment" with increment1 or increment2 (angles), FDEF owner items: each gap is the one before plus the increment, the first being the spacing or step; a negative increment closes the gaps up and can bring copies back. Every pattern of features gets vary (an FDEF owner item), text such as "depth 2; draft_angle 1": the copied feature's named values grow by the step (mm, or degrees for angles, by the seed type's kind_of) times the copy's steps from the seed, (i - 1) + (j - 1) by instance number. Each varied copy's solid is built again from a copy of the seed feature with the grown values against the part before the seed, so it is slower; a seed without that value, a copy that fails with its values, Geometry pattern and face or body seeds are feature errors with a next step. Seeds inside a pattern used as a seed (D1512) are not varied. Values of a seed's sketch dimensions are not varied, and per instance overrides by clicking markers (item 3) and Vary Sketch (item 4) are not done.

D1514: Sweep by a face or a second path (2026-11-07, TR396 item 2 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep's orientation gets "face" with refs.orient_face (one face) and "second_path" with refs.x_path (a sketch or curve, as the path box takes), FDEF owner items. They map to the pipe shell's own modes: the face is the spine support whose normal sets the section's binormal, and the second path is an auxiliary spine reached by equal arc length share with no contact, which points the section's X axis at it. Either sets the turning, so any twist but None is a feature error, as is a missing face or second path; the panel shows the face pick or the path list for its choice, and a face clicked in the view with Normal to Face fills it. "Normal to a projection direction" is the existing Specify Direction Vector twist (it fixes the binormal), so nothing new is added for it. Profile dimensions as formulas of the position along the path (item 1) are not done.

D1515: Sweep corners (2026-11-07, TR137 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep gets corners (an FDEF owner item): "smooth" (default, the old behaviour, the kernel's transformed mode turns the section), "mitre" (the kernel's right corner mode: the two runs meet in a sharp edge on the corner's bisector plane, which is the spec's keep the sharp corner and mitre in one, since a swept section can only stay sharp by meeting on the bisector) or "round" (the round corner mode, rounded about the corner point). Guided and scaled sweeps build their own way and ignore it. A profile part way along the path and several profiles (items 1 and 2) are not done.

D1516: Sweep a model face (2026-11-07, TR138 item 1 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep's profile_type gets "face" with refs.profile_face (one flat face, FDEF owner items): the face (outline and holes) is the profile, its plane (normal turned to the face's outside) is the profile plane the path must start on, the plane's X axis is the section's up hint, and side faces are named side/edge<k> by the face's edges in explorer order, since there are no sketch entities. A curved face or a missing pick is a feature error with a next step, and Thin Feature is refused (it offsets sketch curves). The path plane check is now shared by the sketch and face profiles. Loops of model edges as loft profiles, the group picker for chains (item 2) and the tool body sweep (item 3) are not done.

D1517: Mounting Boss from the mating part (2026-11-07, TR146 item 1 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Mounting Boss gets refs.height_face (one face) with height_clearance, and refs.pin_edge (one round edge) with pin_clearance (FDEF owner items). With a height face, the height is where the boss axis first meets that face above the base, less the gap, in place of boss_height (still kept for the panel and validation); a face the axis misses, or a gap as large as the distance, is a feature error with a next step. With a pin edge (pin types only), the pin diameter is the edge circle's diameter less twice the clearance for a pin, plus twice for a pin hole; a straight edge is refused. Fin direction from picked faces or edges already existed (refs.fin_direction). A step on the boss, and the Lip and Groove and Vent extras (items 2 and 3), are not done.

D1518: Size gradient fill (2026-11-07, TR324, Phase 7B Stage 3). TR324 is built on Fill Pattern (TR57), which already fills a face or sketch region with circles, squares, diamonds or polygons (hexagons) in grid, staggered (hexagon) and ring layouts with a clear border (the margin). It gets gradient (boolean), size_end (length) and refs.gradient_from (a vertex, point or edge), FDEF owner items: each cut shape's size runs from size at the gradient origin to size_end at the copy farthest from it, in proportion to the distance in the face plane (to a point, or to the edge sampled as segments); with no origin the layout's start point is used. Copies are first laid out with the smaller size's footprint, then each must fit with its own size and the margin (unless Fit is Centre Only), so big copies near the border drop out. Seed copies (features, faces, bodies) do not grow; use Vary values (D1513) on other patterns for that. A custom sketch shape and a radial layout are not offered; the spec's circular layout is the ring layout. With this, TR324 is done.

D1519: Pattern check level (2026-11-07, TR399 item 3 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Every pattern built by the shared engine gets check (an FDEF owner item): "full" (the default, as before: each copy of a feature must touch the part, or overlap it for a cut, and each copy of faces must too, else the error names the copies with the Skip fix) or "fast" (those per copy distance and boolean tests are skipped; the one boolean of all copies and the split body check still run). The spec's automatic choice is not made: no cheap test proves a copy safe, and a wrong guess would hide copies that fell off, so Full stays the default and Fast is the user's choice. Add to Pattern and following a pattern (items 1 and 2) are not done.

D1520: Skip a hole by clicking (2026-11-07, TR143 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A hole with an existing sketch (refs.sketch) keeps data.skip_points (an FDEF owner item), the ids of that sketch's points that get no hole; position_points leaves them out, so the count, the holes and the Hole Table follow. On the Positions tab a click on the model while an existing sketch is chosen goes to the nearest sketch point within the larger of the hole diameter and 2 mm, in the sketch plane, and toggles it in the list. The hole's own position sketch is unchanged (its points are removed from the table instead). Positions by distances from two edges or concentric with a round edge (item 1) are not done.

D1019: Section properties (2026-11-07, TR81, Phase 7B Stage 3). Built into the Mass Properties window as a third Bodies choice, "Section of the picked face or sketch", rather than a new command: the same Calculate and Copy, no new key or ribbon button. It measures the picked faces when any are picked (all must be flat and in one plane, using the first face's plane axes), otherwise the default profile (closed outlines with holes) of a sketch selected in the tree, using the sketch's X axis and normal. core/section_props.py takes the kernel's surface properties (area, centroid, inertia tensor about the centroid for unit density) and turns the tensor to the plane's axes: for points in the plane its in-plane terms are the second moments of area, so Ixx is the sum of y squared, Iyy the sum of x squared, Ixy the sum of x times y, J = Ixx + Iyy. Principal moments come from the 2 by 2 matrix [[Ixx, -Ixy], [-Ixy, Iyy]]; the first (smaller) axis is signed so its angle from X lies in (-90, 90] degrees and the second is the normal crossed with it. Values show in mm or inches (area squared, moments to the fourth). A curved face, faces in different planes or an empty pick is a message with a next step. The centre of mass point and mass overrides (TR80) are separate.

D1020: Goal Seek and Sweep (2026-11-07, TR273, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Tools menu window (command tools.goal_seek, no default key, own icon). Targets: volume@Part, area@Part and mass@Part, then every value a measuring feature stores (Measurement, Bounding Box, Fill Pattern count), named as formulas name them. Each trial (core/goal_seek.py, Trials) deep copies the document, sets the variable's text to the value with an explicit unit (mm or deg, so the part unit cannot change it) and rebuilds with one RebuildEngine kept for the whole run, so features the variable does not reach come from its cache. The part values are stored for each trial even when the part has no custom properties (the rebuild stores them only for property formulas). A trial with a failed feature, a variable error or no value is a row with the reason, never a crash. Goal Seek first tries the range ends and seven values between, stopping at the first sign change, then refines with Illinois false position (bisection when a step leaves the bracket or a trial fails) until the result is within a millionth of the target (at least 1e-9) or the bracket closes, at most 40 trials. No sign change is a message giving the nearest result and saying to widen the range. Range values show in the part unit (degrees for angles); measured values stay in mm, mm^2, mm^3 and g, as formulas see them, and the window says so. Nothing in the part changes until Use Value, which sets the variable in one SetVariables undo step. Runs in a background job with a Stop flag checked between trials and passed to each rebuild.

D1021: Centre of mass point and mass overrides (2026-11-07, TR80, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) The point is a new Reference Point method, centre_of_mass, with no picks, rather than a separate feature type or a view only mark: it can be picked by later features like any point, follows the model because it is rebuilt in tree order (the volume centre of the solids built above it, uniform density), and shows and hides like other reference points; that is the view toggle. With no solid above it, it is a feature error saying to move it below a feature that makes a body. (2) Override Mass Properties is a button in the Mass Properties window. It stores Document.mass_override (FDEF owner item: top level key mass_override with mass in g, optional centre [x, y, z] in mm and optional inertia, a symmetric 3 by 3 tensor about the centre in model axes in g mm2), written only when set, so other parts save unchanged; a damaged value is dropped on open. The typed values apply when Bodies is The whole part (picked bodies stay measured): mass and centre replace the measured ones, the inertia is the typed tensor or the measured one scaled by the mass ratio, principal values are recomputed, volume and area stay measured and the shown density is mass over volume. A first row, Typed values (Override), is the mark. The dialog works in the part unit (g and mm, or lb and in) and refuses a tensor that is not symmetric, has a negative principal moment or breaks the triangle rule (one principal moment larger than the other two together). Setting or clearing it is one undo step that rebuilds, since Centre of mass points use the typed centre when there is one.

D1022: Sensor (2026-11-07, TR86, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature type, sensor (FDEF owner item: params source volume, area, mass or formula, default volume; value, low and high as number params, all optional), on the Evaluate tab's Measure group in a column of its own, with no default key. A feature rather than a separate list so it sits in the tree, saves with the part and uses the existing warning mark and hover text. It passes the part through. Volume, area and mass are measured on the bodies built above it (mass needs the part material; without one it is a feature error saying to choose one), because the part's own values reach formulas only after the rebuild; a formula source is resolved like any number param, so it can read variables, dimensions, equations and measured values of features above it. Out of limits is a warning, not an error: it names the value with its unit, the limit it passed, and says to change the model or the limit. No limit, or a low limit above the high one, is a warning with a next step. The value is a measured value (MEASURED_VALUES sensor: value), so formulas below can read value@Sensor 1.

D1023: Extruded Cut from an open sketch (2026-11-07, TR157, Phase 7B Stage 3). Used automatically when an extrude's operation is cut, Thin Feature is off and the sketch has curves but no closed region (before, that was an error), so no saved part changes. The open chain (sketch_chain, so lines, arcs, partial ellipses and splines) is closed into one profile face (core/features/extrude_open.py): each end is carried on straight along its end tangent by twice the size of the part and chain plus 10 mm, and the far ends are joined by three edges on one side: the side to the left of the chord from the far start to the far end, looking down the sketch normal, or the right with flip_side (a new extrude param, FDEF owner item, written only when true). Carrying on along the tangent rather than stopping at the part keeps a line that ends inside the part a clean split. Faces the chain makes are named after its curves as for any cut (side/<entity>); the carried on parts are <entity>/extend_start and /extend_end. A chain that closes on itself, crosses itself or is crossed by its carried on ends gives a feature error that suggests Thin Feature. Boss features with open sketches keep the old message. The cut panel gets a Flip side tick (not on revolved cuts).

D1024: Twist Lock (2026-11-07, TR357, Phase 7B Stage 3). Feature type twist_lock (FDEF owner item: refs.face, a cylinder face; params lug_count, lug_width, lug_height, lug_depth, lock_depth, twist, lock_clearance, other_end, clockwise; the names are its own so the shared panel labels of count, depth and clearance do not change), on the 3D Print tab in a dropdown with Half Lap. One pick: the plug's outer round face; a bore (the classifier finds the picked solid just outside the face) is refused. The plug is the solid of the face; the socket is every other solid the slot shape reaches, so no second pick is needed and a box built from several bodies works. Lugs and slots are annular sectors about the face's axis: lugs from half the lug depth inside the face (so they fuse) out to the lug depth; each slot is an entry sector from the lug ring out past the open end, plus a ring sector turning by Twist, both widened by Clearance round the lug (in angle as clearance over the radius). The open end is the face's end along its axis parameter, or the other with other_end; anticlockwise seen from the open end unless clockwise. Checks with next steps: 1 to 12 lugs, sizes above 0, slots that would overlap, lugs that do not fit on the face at that depth, and no body round the plug. New faces <fid>/lug/<k> and <fid>/slot/<k>.

D1025: Thin Feature Merge Ends (2026-11-07, TR272, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new extrude param thin_merge_ends (FDEF owner item, written only when true), a tick in the Thin Feature group of Extrude only (hidden where Cap ends is hidden), used for open walls on a boss. The chain's ends are carried on straight along their end tangents by twice the part's size plus 10 mm before the wall is offset and extruded; then the material already there is cut from that long wall, the one piece that overlaps most with the wall as drawn is kept (so a wall drawn through a wall loses what sticks out the far side, and a wall that crosses a wall partway keeps the larger side only), and any carried on stub that does not touch the part is cut off again, so an end with nothing to meet stays as drawn. The result is fused as usual. Face names come through the cut from the wall's own names.

D1026: Indent (2026-11-07, TR68, Phase 7B Stage 3). Feature type indent (FDEF owner item: refs.bodies, target then tool; params indent_mode indent or cut, indent_thickness, indent_clearance), in the 3D Print tab's Half Lap dropdown. The tool body is kept. Cut mode takes the tool grown by the clearance (kernel offset by join) out of the target. Indent mode first adds the shell between the tool grown by clearance plus thickness and the tool grown by the clearance, limited to the target grown by the thickness, then cuts the same hollow: so the wall follows the target where the tool meets it instead of wrapping the whole tool. The spec's Keep or Remove picked side is not a separate pick: the wall's extent is set by that one thickness band round the target, and Cut mode gives the no wall case. A tool that does not reach the target within clearance plus thickness, a failed offset, a negative clearance or a zero thickness are feature errors with next steps. New faces <fid>/indent/<k> (pocket) and <fid>/indent/w<k> (wall).
D1600: Corner triad clicks (2026-11-07, TR210 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). The kernel draws the corner triad at a fixed size in device pixels whatever the view size; measured from its drawing, its centre sits 34.5 px from the left and 35.5 px from the bottom and each arrow is 26 px long (viewport/triad.py). A left press within 7 px of an arrow (projected with the current camera; an arrow pointing at the screen is picked at the centre) is a triad click, checked before handles, values and picks. A click looks along the axis from its positive end (view_for_normal keeps the up square); when the view already looks from there it turns to the negative end. Shift and click turns the eye and up a quarter turn about the axis (right hand rule). Item 3 (Normal To with two faces: the first faces the screen, the second sets up) was already met by view_commands.target and two_face_view.

D1601: Orientation popup without a key (2026-11-07, TR210 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new command view.orientation (View > Orientation, no default key: the spec leaves the key to the owner, since Space is free but Ctrl+Space is the view selector) opens a menu at the cursor: the nine standard views, the saved views (without Manage), the four split layouts and New View..., which is Save View. Owner item: choose its default key in SHORTCUTS.md.

D1602: Edge display options (2026-11-07, TR212, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new Preferences page, View (preferences/view_page.py, values in preferences/view_options.py under view/ in the same store, so the shared Settings class is not touched), holds the round 12 view options. Smooth edges (view/smooth_edges: shown, dashed, removed; default shown): the smooth edges are the TR420 edge angles below 0.5 degrees (core/edge_display.py), marked G1 on their two faces with BRep_Builder.Continuity, and the part's face boundaries get upper continuity C0 so the kernel leaves them out; Dashed draws them again as a thin dotted overlay in the edge colour, never picked. The choice applies to Shaded with Edges only: wireframe and the hidden line styles draw every edge, since the kernel's wire and hidden line drawings have no continuity filter. The edges are found once per shown part, only when the choice is not Shown. Hidden edges (view/hidden_edges: dashed, solid) set the line type of Hidden Lines Visible. Feature edges (view/feature_edges, default off): when a feature row becomes current in the tree, every edge of the faces named after that feature is drawn on top in the selection colour and width; another row or the option off clears it.

D1603: Section zones and see through bodies (2026-11-07, TR355, Phase 7B Stage 3). With two or three planes the Section View panel lists every zone (2 to the number of planes; named "In front of 1, behind 2" and so on) with a tick box (section/zones.py). Each ticked zone is one clipping chain whose planes are turned round where the zone is behind them, and the viewer cuts away what any chain cuts, so separate zones go at once (SectionState.zones, cut_zones, section_view.clip_chains). With none ticked, or one plane, the old rule stays: only the zone in front of every plane goes. See Through Bodies lists the part's bodies (Solid Bodies order) with tick boxes and a slider from 10 to 90 percent (60 by default); while the section is on the ticked bodies get that transparency on the part's drawing (set_section_see_through), and turning the section off puts them back, keeping the bodies' own See Through (TR21). Like the rest of the section these are view state only and never saved (saving is TR213).

D1604: Saved sections (2026-11-07, TR213 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Section View panel gets Save with the part: on OK the section (planes with reference vectors, source, reverse, offset, rotations and colours, the axis, cap, zones and see through bodies; core/section_store.py) is stored in appearance.section of the part file as one undo step (Save Section, or Remove Saved Section when unticked), view state like hidden bodies, so no rebuild. FDEF owner item: appearance.section. When a part opens with one, its section is turned on. Turning the section off does not change the file. Save View and Update while a section is on store it in that view under a section key (owner item: views[].section); Go To on such a view shows that section, and a view without one leaves the section as it is. Damaged section data is ignored, so the part still opens. Left for later: choosing which bodies are cut (the part is one drawing, so clipping per body needs one drawing per body), the section planes as a tree folder with a drag handle and rotation rings, and Measure on the cut faces.

D1605: Display quality (2026-11-07, TR214, Phase 7B Stage 3). A per part value from 1 to 10 in appearance.display_quality (FDEF owner item; 5, the old fineness, is not stored). The display mesh's chord deviation is the old one (0.0005 of the box diagonal, at least 0.001 mm) times 2 to the power (5 - quality) / 1.5, so 10 is about ten times finer and 1 about six times coarser; the angle scales the same way within 0.05 to 0.6 radians. View > Display Quality (view.display_quality, no key) opens a slider dialog that shows the deviation for this part in its unit; OK pushes one undo step that rebuilds, and the rebuild thread meshes at the new quality (cleaning the old meshes first when the quality went down, since the mesher keeps finer meshes). Lower quality while turning: when the part has more than 1500 faces, a middle button turn switches multisampling and line smoothing off until the button is released.

D1606: Display mode per body (2026-11-07, TR216, Phase 7B Stage 3). FDCAD has no F8 display column yet (SHORTCUTS.md item 17 lists the key, nothing was built), so the per body choices sit on each body row's right click menu in Solid Bodies, beside See Through: Display Mode (As the View, Shaded With Edges, Shaded, Wireframe) and Transparency... (0 to 90 percent). They are saved in appearance.body_display as {mark: {"mode", "transparency"}} using the same body marks as hidden bodies (core/body_modes.py; FDEF owner item), each change one undo step with no rebuild. Shaded and Shaded With Edges set the body's own face boundary drawing on the part's coloured drawing; Wireframe hides the body there and draws its edges on a separate drawing in the edge colour that is never picked; transparency is the body's custom transparency. Hidden lines per body is left out: hidden line removal is a whole view mode in the kernel, so one body cannot have it alone.
