D1608: Display states (2026-11-07, TR88, Phase 7B Stage 3; the file key was approved with the item in D750). appearance.display_states holds {"states": [{"name", "values"}], "links": {configuration: state}} (core/display_states.py; FDEF owner item). A state's values are copies of the appearance keys hidden_bodies, see_through_bodies, bodies (body colours) and body_display (TR216); applying a state replaces exactly those keys, so locked bodies, feature and face colours stay. View > Display States (view.display_states, no key) lists them with Save Current... (asks a name; the same name updates it), Apply, Delete (also drops its links), Link to Active Configuration and Unlink; each is one undo step that replaces the appearance block and redraws with no rebuild. Activating a linked configuration from the configurations panel applies its state in the same undo step (a macro of the switch and the appearance change). Links are by configuration name, so renaming a configuration drops its link.

D1607: Zoom keys and mouse settings (2026-11-07, TR211, Phase 7B Stage 3). Zoom Out (view.zoom_out, View menu) zooms one step out about the view centre, the inverse of Zoom In; it has no default key (D750 item 4; Z stays Repeat Last Command). A double middle click zooms to fit. Preferences, View gets: Reverse the mouse wheel zoom (view/wheel_reverse, off), Zoom about the pointer or the view centre (view/zoom_about_cursor, pointer), Arrow key turn 1 to 90 degrees (view/arrow_step, 15; Shift and arrow stays a quarter turn), Mouse turn speed 0.25 to 4 times (view/turn_speed, 1; the drag's move from the press is scaled before every turn style uses it), and Zoom to fit when a standard view is chosen (view/fit_on_view, on; off keeps the zoom and centre when a standard view is chosen from the View menu, a key, the view toolbar or the orientation popup; the view selector, Normal To and the triad still fit).

D1609: Mouse presets (2026-11-07, TR312, Phase 7B Stage 3). Preferences, View, Middle button (view/mouse_preset) picks what a middle drag does, named by behaviour: "turn" (alone turns, Shift zooms, Ctrl pans: FDCAD's default and the old behaviour), "turn_shift_pan" (alone turns, Shift pans, Ctrl zooms) and "pan" (alone pans, Shift turns, Ctrl zooms). Alt and middle drag rolls in all three, the left button keeps picking and the right button keeps gestures and the menu, so no preset takes a button another tool needs; the trackpad setting is unchanged. A middle click without a drag still sets the turn centre whatever the preset (keynav.MOUSE_PRESETS, middle_drag).

D1610: Pick through see through bodies and the before and after slider (2026-11-07, TR224 items 1 and 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). A left click whose top item lies on a body drawn see through (TR21 See Through, a body transparency above 0 from TR216, or the section's See Through Bodies, TR355) picks the first item under the pointer that is not on such a body, replacing or adding as usual; when nothing lies behind, or with Shift held, the see through item itself is picked (Shift still adds). Toggle Transparency makes the whole part see through, so it does not pick through. When a preview replaces the part (Fillet, Chamfer, Shell, Draft, D583), a small frameless After and Before slider floats over the lower right of the view (a tool window, since child widgets of the kernel's native view are covered by its drawing); 0 shows the new part as before, moving right fades the result out and the part before the feature in, and it hides with the preview.

D1611: Collapse All and hover information (2026-11-07, TR221, Phase 7B Stage 3). Collapse All (tree.collapse_all, View menu, no default key as D750 item 4 says) closes every item of the feature tree. Item 3: after each hover the status bar's coordinates gain the edge under the pointer's length, and its radius for a circle or arc, or, when one flat face is picked and the pointer is over another flat face, the angle between their planes from 0 to 90 degrees (core/hover_info.py), in the part's units. Item 2 (a description apart from the name) is the TR23 feature comment, already done.

D1612: Trackpad gestures (2026-11-07, TR380 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). The 3D view handles the platform's native gestures beside pinch: rotate rolls the view by the gesture's angle (turning the fingers clockwise rolls the part clockwise), smart zoom (a two finger double tap on a Mac) is Zoom to Fit, and a swipe pointing left (an angle between 90 and 270 degrees) is Previous View while other swipes go forward again: Previous View now keeps the cameras it leaves on a forward list that any new view change clears. Windows precision touchpads send these gestures rarely, so this is mainly for the Mac. Item 4 (taskbar and Dock progress) is left: Qt 6 has no taskbar progress class, so it needs platform code on each system.
D1100: Sheet metal Tab (2026-11-07, TR165, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sheet metal feature, type sheet_tab (core/features/sheetmetal/tab.py, Flanges group beside Jog). Refs: sketch and sheet_metal, no params. The sketch's closed regions are extruded three thicknesses through the sketch plane and cut to the slab z = 0 to thickness of the first wall whose face (z = 0 or z = thickness, within 1e-5 mm) holds the sketch plane and that the tab touches; the result is joined to that wall with add_material, as Tab and Slot does, so it folds with the wall and is in the flat pattern without any flatten change. Each closed region is one tab: a sketch pattern makes a row of tabs, which is how "it can be patterned" is met, since a pattern feature after a sheet metal feature adds material outside the sheet model and would block the flat pattern. A sketch on a face square to the sheet is not taken: a closed outline there is not a wall piece of the sheet thickness, so it is an error that says to draw on a wall face. A tab that does not touch the wall or adds no volume is an error. Extruded Boss in a part with sheet metal now shows Link to thickness too (the core already used the sheet thickness for any Blind first direction, D696).

D1101: Edge Flange profile sketch (2026-11-07, TR166 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Edit Flange Profile is an optional Edge Flange ref, profile_sketch (an FDEF owner item), picked in the Flange Length group as Flange profile (Blind only), with one picked edge. The sketch's closed outline is read in the sketch's own coordinates rather than placed on the flange face: X along the edge from the start of the bend, Y up the flange measured as Length is (Length's Measure from offset is taken off), because a sketch drawn on the flange's own face would depend on the feature it shapes (a loop in the rebuild). Any sketch plane may hold it. The outline above Y = 0 becomes the wall in the child frame (core/features/sheetmetal/flange_profile.py); its extent along a 0.001 mm strip at Y = 0 sets the bend's start and width, so the flange can be narrower, wider than the edge, notched or shaped; Length still types the handle but the outline sets the wall. A bend narrower than the edge gets a rectangular notch of the flange's relief width and depth at each end inside the edge (no corner clearing, unlike a trimmed side bend). An outline that does not reach Y = 0 is an error. The form's sketch field now stores its pick under its own name (body_tools/form_widget.py), so a second sketch pick is possible; every earlier sketch field is named sketch, so nothing else changes. Item 2 is not built: flanges on curved edges need walls that are not flat plates, which the sheet model (D333) does not have; Up to Vertex already ends a flange at a picked point (length), and Length 2 to Length 8 already change several flanges in one feature (D337).

D1102: Edit Bends (2026-11-07, TR167, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sheet metal feature, type edit_bends (core/features/sheetmetal/edit_bends.py, Sheet Metal group beside Load Gauge Table), placed in the tree like any other so it is undoable, suppressible and rebuilds with the part. Params all_bends, radius, method, k_factor, allowance; refs bends (a face of each bend, found by its name as Unfold does, D541). Each chosen bend's rule is the Sheet Metal folder's rule with the bend's own radius, then this feature's typed values (rule_from); its radius and allowance are replaced and nothing else: the bend keeps p0, the line where it starts on its parent wall, so the walls after it move with the new radius and the flat pattern grows or shrinks by the change in allowance. Keeping the outer virtual sharp fixed instead was left out, because converted and Insert Bends parts have no typed flange length to hold. Bends of converted and Insert Bends parts are in the same sheet model, so they change the same way. A picked face not on a bend is an error.

D1103: Sheet metal Corner Relief (2026-11-07, TR168, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sheet metal feature, type sheet_corner_relief (core/features/sheetmetal/corner_relief.py, Corners group), because corner_relief is already the machining relief of TR244. A corner is a pair of bends on the same parent wall whose tangent lines (p0 lines) cross within 3 x (thickness + radius) + 2 mm of an end of each; three bends round a corner give pairs. Collect all corners (all_corners, on by default) takes them all; off, the corners between the picked bends (refs bends, faces of bends). Types: rectangular (a square, sides along the two bends), circular, tear (a circle on the corner point), obround (a slot along the diagonal, twice the size long) and constant_width (a slot of the size across from the corner point to the far corner of the two bend strips). Size by ratio (ratio x thickness, 2 by default) or value (size). Placement bend_lines centres the relief where the two bend centre lines cross; tangent sets it so it touches both tangent lines on the wall (tear and constant width ignore placement). corner_types, an optional text param, gives one type per corner in corner order (bends sorted by id), a blank keeping relief_type; an unknown word is an error. The relief is drawn through the sheet in the wall's flat frame and cut from the wall, from each bend strip (as a strip cut, wrapped when folded, D541) and from each flange wall in its flat frame, only where it meets them, so folded part and flat pattern agree. Params all_corners, relief_type, corner_types, size_by, ratio, size and placement are FDEF owner items. The edge flange's own corner relief (D540) stays as it is. The form's text field now shows its Field default as its placeholder (body_tools/form_widget.py).

D1104: Bend notches (2026-11-07, TR169, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two Flat Pattern params, bend_notches ("none" by default, "triangle", "circle", "rectangle") and notch_size (a length, the sheet thickness when missing), both FDEF owner items. At each end of every bend centre line (SheetModel.bend_lines) a notch is cut through the flat solid only, in the first wall's frame: it reaches notch_size into the sheet along the bend line and is notch_size wide where the bend line ends (a triangle with its point inside, a half disc of that diameter, or a rectangle), and reaches as far outside so it always opens on the edge. Because the flat outline comes from the flat solid's top face, the notches are in the view, the DXF and SVG OUTLINE layer and the STEP flat export with no export change. A bend that ends at a relief or inside the sheet gets its notch there too. The folded part never has them. bend_notches is left out of the file when None (form OMIT_NONE).

D1105: Flat pattern options (2026-11-07, TR76, Phase 7B Stage 3). Item 2: the Flat Pattern gets merge_faces (true when missing; false builds the flat with the walls' and bends' faces kept apart, model.build(merge=False), so the bend regions show), corner_trim (cuts, from the flat only, the parallelogram from a corner's tangent line crossing to the far corner of its two bend strips, for every corner found as in D1103) and refs leave_out (faces; the wall holding each, found by name or by its flat face, is dropped from the flat with its bend and every wall bent from it; the first wall cannot be left out). These three are FDEF owner items. Simplify Bends is not a setting: the flat bend regions are always exact straight strips with their cut outlines mapped exactly (D541), so there is nothing to simplify. Item 1, No Bends, is met by Unfold with All bends, cuts, then Fold (D541), which works on converted and Insert Bends parts as on flanged ones (spec merge note 13); a test covers the Insert Bends case. Item 3 was already met: Base Flange's Start list (D334) starts at a parallel face or plane, a vertex or an offset; a test covers a reference plane. Item 4: Flatten and Export Flat Pattern are unchanged when no option is set (the model is used as it was).

D1106: Flat pattern data for quoting (2026-11-07, TR172, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Flat Pattern works out, from the top face (z = thickness in the first wall's frame) of the merged flat part with its notches: blank_area (square mm), outer_cut_length (the outer wires), inner_cut_length (every inner wire), cut_outs (the number of inner wires), bends (bends in the sheet model) and flat_length and flat_width (the flat size along the grain). They go in the result's extras and in MEASURED_VALUES["flatten"] (core/equations/engine.py, a shared file), so equations read them as blank_area@Flat Pattern and so on, like the Bounding Box values (D809). The Flat Pattern panel lists the first five under the flat size, and Export Flat Pattern gets "Quote data CSV (*.csv)": name,value rows (core/features/sheetmetal/quote.py). With Merge faces off the values come from a merged build, so they do not change.

D1107: Sheet metal small options (2026-11-07, TR174 items 1, 2 in part, 3, 5, 6 and 7, Phase 7B Stage 3). Hem: length2 to length8 give the 2nd to 8th picked edges their own hem length (as Edge Flange, D337), and method, k_factor, allowance in an Own Bend Values group give the hem its own allowance (own relief was already there). Closed Corner: overlap_ratio (0 to 1, 1 when missing) moves the covering wall's cut plane in by (1 - ratio) x thickness, so an overlap or underlap reaches that share across the other wall; several end faces already closed several corners. The open or closed bend region choice is not built: the bends of the sheet model have no corner region of their own to close. Cross Break: break_angle and break_radius are written into each line's title ("Cross break up 3 degrees, radius 50 mm"), which the SVG titles and the flat drawing carry; they stay cosmetic, as D539. Break Corner: collect_all takes every corner of every wall's flat outline between two straight edges and off the bend lines, and corner_kind ("outside" default, "inside") says which; an inside corner is filled with the chamfer or round (the shape is added to the wall instead of cut), for picked corners too. Tab and Slot: edge_offset spreads the tabs between equal offsets from both ends (with a spacing the row was already centred), and skip_tabs, a text list such as "2, 4", leaves tabs and their slots out; use inside patterns and mirrors is not built, as a pattern after a sheet metal feature is outside the sheet model. Flat Pattern: sheet_length and sheet_width (2500 x 1250 mm for new ones) give a warning, code flat_too_large, when the flat size does not fit the sheet either way round. Item 4 (rip on hollow cylinders and cones) is not built: the sheet model has flat walls only. All new params are FDEF owner items.

D1108: Flat pattern DXF and SVG output options (2026-11-07, TR173, Phase 7B Stage 3). Export Flat Pattern, when the path is picked in the file dialog and the file is DXF or SVG, opens the Flat Pattern Output dialog (ui/sheet_metal/flat_output_dialog.py): Outline, Bend lines, Cross break and form marks and Bounding box ticks, Origin (Part origin, Lower left corner, Centre of the outline), Rotate (degrees), Flip X and Flip Y, the DXF colour numbers of up and down bends (1 red and 5 blue), and a list of every bend line and mark with a tick each, the preview where single items are left out. Cancel writes nothing. core/features/sheetmetal/flat_output.py (FlatOutput, apply_output) turns the drawing: items kept, then turned, mirrored (arc angles reflected) and moved. With colours, the DXF puts bends on BEND_UP and BEND_DOWN layers instead of BEND_LINES; without the dialog (a path given in code) the file is as before. Sketches are not an item: the flat drawing has no sketch geometry, only marks; one file per body waits for several sheet metal bodies (TR281), so a part writes one file. The list is the preview rather than a drawing, to keep the dialog small.

D1109: Sheet metal small additions (2026-11-07, TR370, Phase 7B Stage 3). Extend Wall (type extend_wall, Flanges group): pick an edge face of a wall (a face square to the wall, through its thickness, found by its normal lying in the wall's plane and the wall's material just inside it); the face is pushed out along its normal by distance (end_condition blind) or up to a plane or flat face (end_condition up_to, refs limit; the distance is measured from the face's centre along its normal), and the prism is joined to the wall with add_material, so it folds and flattens with it. Perforated Fold Line (type perforation, Cuts and Marks group): every non construction line of a sketch on a wall face gets slots slot_length long (5 mm), slot_width wide (0.5 mm) and bridge apart (2 mm), as many as fit, the row centred on the line, cut from that wall only where they meet it. Both keep the sheet model, so the flat pattern shows them.

D1110: Bend Table and bend order (2026-11-07, TR282, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Sheet Metal command, Bend Table (feature.bend_list, Flat Pattern group), opens a window listing the bends of the Flat Pattern's sheet model (core/features/sheetmetal/bend_list.py), numbered from 1 in the order they were made: number, feature, direction, angle, radius, allowance and step. Picking a row highlights the bend's inner and outer faces. Radius, allowance and step can be typed; OK adds one Edit Bends feature (D1102) per changed bend just above the Flat Pattern (named Edit Bend n, picking the bend's inner face; a changed allowance is stored as method bend_allowance) and writes the steps as the Flat Pattern's bend_order text param (bend numbers in bending order, such as "2, 1", an FDEF owner item; left out when it is the plain order), all in one undo macro, so the table never edits the features that made the bends. Bends a bend_order leaves out follow in their own order; a number twice or out of range is an error. The DXF writes each step as TEXT at the middle of its bend line on a BEND_ORDER layer, the SVG adds ", step n" to the bend title. Not built: rips in the table and turning a bend into a rip and back, because rips are cuts, not entities of the sheet model, and a bend turned into a rip would leave its child wall unconnected in the model; listed in the report.

D1111: Sheet metal rule library (2026-11-07, TR332, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Sheet Metal command, Sheet Metal Rules (feature.sheet_rules), opens a window over a JSON library file (core/features/sheetmetal/rules.py): {"format": 1, "rules": {name: values}}, lengths and numbers as {"text", "value"} in mm, choices as strings, sorted by name so a shared file diffs cleanly. A rule holds the Sheet Metal folder's thickness, radius, method, k_factor, allowance, relief, relief_by, relief_ratio, relief_width, relief_depth, corner_relief, corner_relief_size and kerf, and the material it is for as a note (FDCAD has no sheet material on the folder; the part material is TR78's). Save Current, Delete and Library File (the path is kept in the settings key sheet_metal/rule_library; by default sheet_metal_rules.json in the app data folder) edit the library; Apply copies the values into the folder with ReplaceFeature (one undo step), sets the new folder param rule_name (an FDEF owner item) and drops a gauge, since the rule sets its own thickness and radius. A part never reads the library when it opens. The per feature override tick is the existing Own Bend Values and Own Relief groups. A library file that is not JSON or has no rules list shows a message in the window, never an exception.

D1112: Fold progress and flat marks (2026-11-07, TR283 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Fold Progress is a Flat Pattern param, fold_percent (0 to 100, 100 when missing, an FDEF owner item): while Flattened is off the Flat Pattern shows a copy of the sheet with every bend angle scaled by the percent (0 shows the flat part), without gusset shapes, which fit only the full bend; the model kept for later features and exports is unchanged, so it is a view setting, not a new state. Mapping sketch points and curves onto the flat pattern is a new sheet metal feature, Flat Marks (type flat_marks, Cuts and Marks group; refs sketch, param title): every non construction line, arc and circle of a sketch on a wall face becomes cosmetic marks on that wall (arcs and circles as chords about 1 mm long), stored like Cross Break lines (D539), so they show folded and flat and are written on the CROSS_BREAKS layer of the DXF and SVG. Sketch points alone are not marked: a point has no line to draw. Item 1 (dimple, drawn cut out and bead as sketch driven features with several profiles and bead end shapes) is not built in this round.

D1113: Partial miter flange (2026-11-07, TR170 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Miter Flange gets offset_start and offset_end (lengths, FDEF owner items; named so their labels differ from Base Flange's start_offset): the walls, bends and parent trim stop that far short of the chain's free start and free end (a mitred end is not changed). The chain's start is the free end the chain ordering already uses, the one with the smallest X, then Y, in the wall's frame. Offsets that leave nothing of an edge are an error. The edge beyond an offset keeps its material; with Material inside there is no relief cut there, because the bend lies above the wall and does not overlap it. Not built: trim side bends, the miter flange's own relief and allowance beyond its Own Bend Values, and arcs in the profile (the profile is still lines only, D531).
D1300: Repair Sketch (2026-11-07, TR37, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) A sketch tool under Check Sketch (no default key). Its panel: Tolerance (a length, 0.05 mm by default, the near miss of D763), Find, Zoom to Next Fault, Fix and Fix All. The tool panel holds fixed fields, so as in D763 the faults are listed in the prompt and Fix repairs the fault last zoomed to (the first one before any zoom) instead of a Fix button on each row. (2) `core/sketch/repair.py` finds, in this order: relations and dimensions that name a missing entity or that the solver refuses for their entity kinds (driven dimensions are checked as if driving), zero length lines (1e-6 mm or less), zero radius circles and arcs, lines and arcs shorter than the tolerance, curves on top of each other, overlapping collinear lines, two point ids at one place that no relation or curve ties (a point on the sketch origin is not counted), and gaps: two open ends (coincident and overlapping points count as one, as in topology) of different curves closer than the tolerance, each end paired with its nearest. Construction geometry is checked too, since it can carry the same faults. Splines, ellipses and partial ellipses are not measured for tiny length. (3) Fixes: a broken relation or dimension is deleted; a gap moves both ends, and every point joined to them, to their middle and merges them into one point (TR40 merge), so the move is half the gap; a duplicate point is merged into the other (no move); a tiny or zero length line or arc is removed and its ends joined at their middle; a zero radius circle is removed; a duplicate curve is removed; overlapping lines become one line from the outermost end to the outermost end, reusing those end points so their connections stay, and nothing moves. A point that nothing uses afterwards is removed; the sketch origin is never moved or removed. (4) Each Fix is one undo step and Fix All is one undo step; Fix All finds the faults again after each fix (one fix can change another) and skips a fault whose fix fails. Messages give the largest move in mm. Nothing changes without a press (CLAUDE.md section 5 item 12).
Status: Default
Reason: TR37; small, exact fixes that each say what they move.

D1301: Sketch problem list (2026-11-07, TR38, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) States: the core `SketchStatus` (under, full, over) is unchanged, since features, the tree and the rebuild use it. The sketch editor adds display states from `core/sketch/problems.py` (`Status.display`): Dangling (a relation or dimension names an entity that is not in the sketch), Invalid (a line of zero length, a circle or arc of zero radius, a spline whose sampled outline crosses itself) and No solution (the solver fails with nothing conflicting or redundant), in that order of precedence, then under, full or over. Dangling shows in the theme's warning colour, Invalid and No solution in the over defined colour. (2) `solve_around` solves the sketch with dangling relations switched off (their indexes stay) and dangling dimensions left out, then puts them back, so the rest of the sketch still solves; before, one dangling item stopped the whole solve. A saved sketch with a dangling item still fails as a feature (unchanged), since the list repairs it in the editor. (3) The list opens by clicking the sketch status in the status bar. It does not block the sketch (it is not modal), so Pick New Item takes the one item selected in the sketch. Rows: dangling items, invalid curves, conflict sets (conflicting items that share an entity form one set), redundant items (listed apart, "harmless"), and no solution. Clicking a row selects its items. Buttons: Zoom to Item, Pick New Item, Delete, Repair All Dangling, Diagnose with Apply Way Out, Select Under Defined. (4) Repair All Dangling: the single clear match for an item with one missing name is the one entity (trying up to 400) that, put in its place, makes the item fit and already hold where the sketch stands: it solves with nothing conflicting or redundant and no point moves more than 1e-6 mm. With none or more than one, the item is left for Pick New Item or Delete. The user confirms each replacement; the accepted ones are one undo step. (5) Diagnose tries each item of the set on a copy: a dimension made reference, a relation deleted; it keeps the ones after which the sketch solves with no conflict, and shows each with the largest point move in mm, a duplicate dimension (same type and entities as an earlier one) first, then the smallest move. The preview is the selection of the item and the move amount; a ghost of the moved geometry is not drawn. (6) Not built: the faint image of the item a dangling item lost (TR38 item 2), since a sketch does not keep deleted geometry; the list names the missing id instead.
Status: Default
Reason: TR38; repairs in the editor where the user can see them, without changing what features accept.

D1302: Solution jumps and Keep This Side (2026-11-07, TR338, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) `core/sketch/sides.py` records the side of each corner (two lines whose ends are joined, by shared point, coincident relation or place: the sign of the turn from the older line to the newer, each pointing away from the corner) and each arc (less or more than half a turn). Corners within a sine of 0.02 of straight and arcs within 0.02 rad of a half turn have no side, so they never count; nodes where more than six line ends meet are skipped. (2) A jump is an item whose side differs between the geometry before a solve and after it (so the user's own edit is never a jump, only what the solver did), and, for drags, between before and after each drag step for corners and arcs that do not use a dragged point. The status bar then says "The sketch jumped to another solution at ..." and offers Undo and Keep This Side. (3) The solver has no inequalities, so a lock is checked after each solve instead: Keep This Side (right click in empty space, while a jump is pending) undoes the change and stores the sides the items had before it in the sketch (`keep_sides`, an optional sketch key mapping `corner:<id>:<id>` or `arc:<id>` to +1 or -1, an FDEF owner item), as its own undo step. A later change that flips a locked item is undone at once with a message naming it. Remove Side Locks removes them all. Locks on deleted entities are ignored. (4) Only corners and arcs are watched: circles, ellipses and splines have no side here, and a point flipping across a line with no corner is not caught.
Status: Default
Reason: TR338; a check after the solve needs no solver change.

D1303: Relation groups and Equal Length (2026-11-07, TR108, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Parallel, Equal, Collinear and Coradial already stored any number of entities in one relation. Adding one of these to a pick where an item already has a switched on relation of the same type now joins that relation instead of adding a new one: the entities of every such relation and the new picks become one relation at the place of the first, and the others are removed. The joined relation is first tried on the solver's geometry; if it does not fit (for example Equal on lines meeting Equal on circles), a separate relation is added as before. (2) A group of three or more entities shows its tag at every member, with a number counted per relation type in sketch order (for example the tags of the second parallel group read with a 2). Pairs keep their one tag. No file change: the number is worked out when drawing. (3) Equal on lines and arcs together makes their lengths equal (the solver's line length and arc length held by one shared value, D870's length parameters); the relation list offers Equal for any mix of lines and arcs. Ellipse arcs and splines are not solver curves with a length (D278: splines are points and handles only), so Equal Length on them is not built; TR41 records what curves the solver can relate.
Status: Default
Reason: TR108; one relation per group keeps the relation list short and the solver's work the same.

D1304: Relations on ellipses and splines (2026-11-07, TR41, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Through the solver's ellipse (D278): Tangent between a line and an ellipse or partial ellipse uses the solver's line to ellipse tangency; between an ellipse and a circle, arc or another ellipse it adds a helper point on both curves, started where they come closest, with the angle between them there held at 0 or 180 degrees (whichever is nearer), as the solver joins curves with no shared point. Curves that share an end point use the angle at that point, as D277 does for arcs. Concentric takes ellipses and partial ellipses with circles, arcs, other ellipses or one point (their centres coincide). Equal between ellipses holds the same major and minor axes. Midpoint of a partial ellipse puts the point on the ellipse and on the perpendicular bisector of its chord, so it is as far from both ends: on a partial ellipse that is not symmetric this is not the halfway parameter, which the solver has no relation for. (2) Splines stay points and handles (D278). Tangent between a spline and a line, circle, arc or ellipse acts on one end: the end the other curve uses or a coincident relation ties to it, else the end nearer the other curve when solved. The line through that end point and its handle is held parallel to the line, or tangent to the circle, arc or ellipse. The relation stores the two entities only, so no file change. (3) Equal Curvature at a spline end is not built: the solver has no curvature of a spline, and a handle length rule (curvature from the handle and the next handle) would only match the kernel's curve for some splines. TR43's handle dimensions let the user set the handle by hand meanwhile. (4) The relation list offers these only for picks they fit.
Status: Default
Reason: TR41; the solver's own ellipse relations, and handles as the spline's tangent.

D1305: Spline handles (2026-11-07, TR43, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Handles were already construction points (D278), so they drag and take point dimensions. The editor now draws each handle of a selected spline (or of a spline whose through point or handle is selected) as a dashed line from the through point to a small square at the handle, filled when pinned. (2) Pin Handle (right click a through point or a handle end) adds a Fixed relation on the handle point, so it stays where it is while other points move; Reset Handle removes every Fixed relation on that handle. No new relation type or file key. (3) Add Handle Line adds a construction line from the through point to the handle that shares both points, so the handle's angle and length take the usual angle and length dimensions and line relations (Parallel, Collinear, Perpendicular, Tangent to an arc), and equations through them. A handle line already there is reused. (4) Each command is one sketch undo step.
Status: Default
Reason: TR43; handles stay points, so everything that works on points and lines works on them.

D1306: Spline edit tools (2026-11-07, TR42, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Insert Spline Point (a click tool in the spline dropdown) finds the nearest spot on the clicked spline and adds a through point there with its handle along the curve's direction. A spline's handles are mirrored at each point (D278), so a cubic piece cannot be split exactly unless the split is in its middle; the handle length is chosen from 100 trial lengths as the one that keeps the two new pieces closest to the old piece. A neighbouring handle shared with another piece stays as it was; the handle of the spline's first or last point belongs to this piece only, so it takes its exact split value (de Casteljau). The tests check the curve moves less than 0.02 mm when the clicked piece is the whole spline and less than 0.15 mm (1.5 percent of its width) on a 10 mm wide wave of two pieces. A click within the first or last 2 percent of a piece is refused as "a point is already there". (2) Fit Spline (tool panel: Tolerance, Keep originals as construction, Fit) takes the curves selected before the tool or clicked with it (a second click drops one). They must be lines, arcs, partial ellipses or splines that join end to end into one open chain (coincident and overlapping ends join, as in topology); a branch, a gap or a closed chain is refused with a message. Closed chains are left out because a spline here has two distinct end points. The fit resamples the chain evenly, starts with its two ends and adds the sample furthest from the curve until every sample is within the tolerance both ways (chain to spline and spline to chain) or 200 points are used. Each handle follows the chain's direction at its point, a third of the shorter neighbouring chord long. The new spline reuses the chain's two end point ids, so joins to the rest of the sketch stay; the originals are removed with their relations and dimensions, or turned into construction geometry. (3) Simplify Spline (Tolerance, Preview, Apply) refits the picked spline the same way from its own samples, shows how many of its points are left and the new curve, and Apply replaces its points and handles while keeping its id and end points. A result with no fewer points is refused. (4) Each change is one sketch undo step.
Status: Default
Reason: TR42; one adaptive fit serves Fit Spline and Simplify Spline, measured both ways against the target.

D1307: Baseline, ordinate, chamfer and path length dimensions (2026-11-07, TR45, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Path Length is a new dimension type `path_length` (an FDEF owner item) whose entities are the lines and arcs of a chain; the solver holds a running sum of their lengths (one shared length value per curve, D870) equal to the value, so it drives and can be solved for like any dimension. Offered in the right click menu when two or more lines and arcs that join end to end (open or closed) are selected; its text sits on a leader from the middle of the chain's middle curve. (2) Baseline Dimension and Ordinate Dimension are tools in Smart Dimension's dropdown. Baseline: a base point or line, then each point or line; each click adds a distance (horizontal or vertical from a base point, chosen in the tool panel; square to a line when either item is a line) and stacks its text one row further out than the one before (rows 8 pick distances apart, so the spacing follows the zoom). Ordinate: a zero point, then points; each adds a horizontal or vertical distance from the zero point with `display` style `ordinate` and a group name (zero point id and axis), drawn as a leader from the point with its number. The texts of a group share one row: moving one moves them all. The `display` dict already exists (D901); the style and group keys are FDEF owner items. (3) Chamfer Dimension (right click a line with a line joined at each end): Length and Angle adds the chamfer's length and its angle to the line at its first end; Two Lengths adds a construction point held at the intersection of the two neighbouring lines (Intersection relation) and its distances to the chamfer's two ends. (4) All are ordinary driving dimensions; a new one that would over define the sketch becomes a reference dimension with a note, as Smart Dimension does.
Status: Default
Reason: TR45; one new dimension type for the sum, everything else from the dimensions the solver already has.

D1308: Sketch pattern options (2026-11-07, TR107, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) The instance count shown in the sketch and edited there is already built: every number field of a tool panel is a label in the sketch that opens a value box when clicked (D513), and the pattern counts are such fields. The pattern is not kept as an object after Make Pattern (the copies are geometry with relations and dimensions), so the count is edited while the tool is open, as before. (2) Pick Direction 1 of Linear Sketch Pattern also takes a straight part edge projected onto the sketch (within the pick distance). With Fix direction on, Make Pattern adds a fixed construction copy of the edge (the copy Smart Dimension uses, D116 item 3) and holds the pattern direction to it; with it off only the angle is taken. (3) Circular Sketch Pattern gets Radius and Angle from center: the distance and direction from the centre to the picks' first point. They follow the centre and the picks; typing either moves the centre so the picks sit at that radius and angle, which lets go of a picked centre point, as typing Center X or Y does. A radius of zero or less is refused. The arc angle is the existing Total angle. Both show as labels in the sketch like the other fields.
Status: Default
Reason: TR107; the count label was already there, the rest are two small panel additions.

D1309: Control of relations offered while drawing (2026-11-07, TR231, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Item 2: Preferences, Sketch gets a switch per kind of automatic relation (Horizontal, Vertical, Parallel, Perpendicular, Tangent, Equal, Midpoint, Coincident), all on by default, below Automatic relations, which still turns them all off. A kind switched off is not added where a click lands on a snap or a line snaps to a direction; snaps still place the point. Coincident covers ties to fixed copies of part points and edges. Joins that are part of a shape (the next segment of a line chain, rectangle corners, a fixed orientation picked in the Line panel) always stay, as with Automatic relations off (T1.3.3). Stored with the other sketch switches (`sketch/auto_<kind>`). (2) Item 1: while a drawing tool is active, Tab skips the automatic relations of the next click (the status bar says so) and pressing it again keeps them; a click that makes geometry clears it. Tab is a key of the sketch canvas only while a tool is active (the canvas keeps the focus), like Esc; SHORTCUTS.md is an owner file, so the key is listed in the round report for the owner to add. "Lock" is what an offered relation does already (it is added and holds), and "turn off for this entity" is the skip. Cycling through several offered relations with Tab is not built: the snap rules pick one target (T1.2.3 order), so only one relation set is offered at a time. (3) Item 3: tags already stack side by side where they would overlap (each further tag at one point moves one tag width right), so they never hide each other; right click cycling is not needed and not built.
Status: Default
Reason: TR231; per kind switches in the existing preferences page, and one key for the common case of a relation the user does not want.

D1310: Weak automatic relations (2026-11-07, TR362, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) A relation added automatically while drawing (a snap's relation, or a line's Horizontal, Vertical, Parallel or Perpendicular) is stored with `weak: true` (an optional relation key, written only when set: an FDEF owner item). Joins that are part of a shape stay ordinary relations, and so do ties to fixed copies of part geometry. Weak tags are drawn dotted. (2) After every change in the sketch editor, if the solve finds conflicting items and some of them are weak relations, those weak relations are removed and the sketch solved again, with a status note naming each one and saying Undo brings it back (it is the same undo step as the change). So a conflicting relation or dimension the user adds replaces the automatic one instead of over defining the sketch; this also covers a new automatic relation that conflicts with another automatic one. Conflicts among ordinary relations behave as before. The solver wrapper is unchanged: the editor removes items, as a user would. (3) Keep Relation (right click a weak relation's tag) makes it an ordinary relation (the "convert" of TR231 and TR362 in section 22 item 79). Relations in files saved before this are ordinary.
Status: Default
Reason: TR362; the solver's conflict report already names the items, so weak ones can give way without solver changes.

D1311: Limit dimensions and Point on Segment (2026-11-07, TR342, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) The solver has no inequalities, so `solve` works with an active set: limit dimensions and segment ends are left out at first; after a successful solve every limit the geometry passes (by more than 1e-7) is held as an exact dimension at its value, and the sketch is solved again from there, up to 8 rounds. Each new solve starts with none held, so a limit lets go when the geometry moves back inside. A drag does the same after its own solve. A held limit takes freedom away only while held, so a sketch whose last freedom is a limit shows as under defined. (2) A dimension's limit is stored as `limit: "min"` or `"max"` (optional key, written only when set: an FDEF owner item); the right click menu on a driving dimension has Limit with Exact Value, Minimum and Maximum (one undo step). (3) Point on Segment is a new relation type `on_segment` (point, then line; an FDEF owner item): the point lies on the line, and when it would pass an end it is held at that end (coincident) by the same active set. Its tag reads S. Offered for a point and a line.
Status: Default
Reason: TR342; an active set on top of the solver keeps the solver wrapper's rules and needs no new solver code.

D1312: Negative distances and angles to an axis (2026-11-07, TR111 items 2 and 4 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Item 4: a horizontal or vertical distance typed as zero is accepted (the two items line up), and a negative value flips the side the distance keeps (TR337's `side`) and stores the size: "-6" is kept as "6", other negative text as "-(text)", so the stored text and value agree. One undo step. Other dimensions still refuse zero or less with the old message, since a distance, radius or angle has no direction to flip. (2) Item 2 in part: Angle to Horizontal and Angle to Vertical (right click a line) add a construction line through the line's first end, coincident with it and held horizontal or vertical, and an angle dimension between them (reference when it would over define), one undo step. Not built from item 2: the symmetric angle about a centerline. Items 1 (locking the type by right click while placing) and 3 (minimum, centre or maximum per arc end, two points on one arc, arrow flip, hiding lines) are left for a later round; Shift click already gives nearest or farthest (T4.3.3).
Status: Default
Reason: TR111 in part; the parts that fit the existing dimension model.

D1313: Rectangle extras (2026-11-07, TR114 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Corner Rectangle and Center Rectangle get three tool panel fields: Construction lines (None, Corner to corner, Midpoint to midpoint), Corner radius and Inner frame offset (lengths, 0 for none). They are made in the rectangle's own undo step after its sides: the construction lines first (diagonals coincident with the corners; midlines held at the midpoints of opposite sides), then the inner frame with the Offset tool's code toward the centre with its offset dimension, then the four outer corners rounded with Round All Corners (one radius dimension, Equal on the others, D834). A Center Rectangle already has its diagonals, so Corner to corner adds nothing more there. If the frame or the radius cannot be made (too large for the rectangle) the rectangle is not made and the status bar says why. The fields keep their values for the next rectangle while the tool stays active. Not built: item 2 (editing a polygon's sides and size later; Polygon with 3 sides is the triangle).
Status: Default
Reason: TR114 item 1; reuses Offset and Round All Corners so the extras behave like those tools.

D1314: Line click buffer and Relax Spline (2026-11-07, TR115 items 3 and 4 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Item 3: with the Line and Centerline tools a second click within the pick distance of the first (the snap distance at the current zoom) is ignored, unless a size was typed; the segment waits for a click further away. (2) Item 4 in part: Relax Spline (right click a spline) gives every inner through point the handle a new spline through the same points would have (`freeform.default_handles`), keeping the points, both end handles and pinned handles (TR43), one undo step. Converting a line and arc chain to a spline is Fit Spline (D1306). Not built: raising or lowering the degree and weights (FDCAD splines are cubic pieces with handles, D278, so there is no degree or weight to change), a spline length dimension (splines are not solver curves), item 1 (infinite construction line) and item 2 (flipping a tangent arc at a junction).
Status: Default
Reason: TR115 in part; the small options that fit the sketch model.

D1315: Linked copies (2026-11-07, TR122 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Copy Entities gets a Linked tick (off by default). With it and Keep relations on, each driving dimension copied with the entities shares a value link (TR193, D978) with its original: the original's link name when it has one, otherwise a new name `copy_<dimension id>` (with a number added if taken) given to both. A value link is the sketch's existing "same value by formula" mechanism, so changing the original, or any copy, changes them all, and Unlink Values breaks it. Reference dimensions are copied unlinked. TR122 is now done (item 1: D986).
Status: Default
Reason: TR122 item 2; value links already do what "follow by formula" asks.

D1316: Line extension under an on-line snap (2026-11-07, TR341 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). While the cursor shows an on curve snap whose target is a sketch line, the canvas draws that line carried on across the view, dashed in the preview colour at about a third of its strength, since the coincident relation the snap adds holds the point on the line's infinite extension. Display only, never saved. Tangent snaps are not a snap kind of their own (a tangent arc follows from the Line tool's end), so only the point on line case is drawn. Item 2 (direction arrows on lines and chains) is left open.
Status: Default
Reason: TR341 item 3; a drawing aid on the existing snap.

D1317: Sketch Fillet on arcs (2026-11-07, TR48 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Sketch Fillet picks lines and arcs. A corner where an arc meets a line or another arc end to end (shared point, coincident relation or the same place) is rounded by `core/sketch/ops/curve_fillet.py`: the fillet centre is where the two curves' offsets by the radius cross (a line's two parallels; an arc's circles of radius R + r and, when R > r, R - r); among centres whose touching points lie on both curves (not at the corner itself), the one nearest the corner is used. Each curve's corner end moves to its own new point at the touching point, the coincident join between the old ends is removed, and an arc on a new centre joins them with Tangent to both (the solver's tangency at a shared end, D277) and a radius dimension, or Equal to the run's first fillet when Dimension each fillet is off (item 3, as for lines). (2) A corner whose point carries other relations or dimensions is refused with a message to delete them first: Keep constrained corners holds a corner with an Intersection relation, which the solver has for two lines only. A radius that does not fit says so. (3) Not built: fillets with splines (the solver has no spline curve, D278), chamfers on arcs, and sizing by dragging the preview arc (item 3).
Status: Default
Reason: TR48 in part; offset crossings give the exact centre for lines and arcs, and the solver keeps it tangent.
D1400: Tangent propagation off (2026-11-07, TR131, Phase 7B Stage 3). The kernel test (D750) found that the fillet and chamfer makers always walk a whole smooth chain and cannot end a round at a smooth join. So Fillet (Constant and Variable Size) and Chamfer (symmetric Distance Distance) get a Tangent propagation tick, on by default, written only when off as tangent_propagation false (an FDEF owner item), built with the partial edge routine (D519, core/features/fillet_tangent.py): for each picked edge with a smooth neighbour, the part is split square to the edge at each smooth end only, the edge is rounded in its own piece (with its radius law for a variable fillet), and the pieces are fused and merged back, carrying names; the round ends square at the join. Picked edges with no smooth neighbour are rounded together afterwards in one kernel call, found again by their middle point. One body only; an asymmetric, angle or offset chamfer with the tick off is a feature error with a next step. Partial Edges takes priority when both are set. Face and Full Round fillets have no tick.

D1401: Partial edge ends by picks (2026-11-07, TR64 item 5, Phase 7B Stage 3). Partial Edges on Fillet (Constant Size) and Chamfer (symmetric Distance Distance) get a third kind, Reference (partial "reference", an FDEF owner item), with refs.partial_ends: exactly two picks, the start then the end (core/features/partial_refs.py). Each pick resolves like a reference geometry pick (datum resolve_pick): a vertex or reference point sets the end at the nearest point of each edge (projection onto the edge curve), a reference plane or flat face at the first point where the edge crosses it. The two points are turned into distances along each edge (smaller first), and the partial routine (D519, D1012) runs as for typed distances; Flip does not apply. Errors with next steps: not two picks, a line or round face picked, a plane that misses the edge, two ends at one point. In the panel, vertices clicked in the view go to the Start and End list while the kind is Reference; a Pick Ends toggle sends flat faces there too, so a face can set an end without becoming an item. Reference planes from the tree are not routed to form picks today, so in the panel a plane end is a flat face; the file accepts a plane feature.

D1402: Fillet methods and profiles (2026-11-07, TR62, Phase 7B Stage 3). Constant size fillets get method ("radius" default, "asymmetric", "chord") and profile ("circular" default, "conic", "curvature", "elliptic"), with distance2, rho (conic shape) and reverse; all written only when not the default (FDEF owner items). The kernel fillet makes only circular sections of one radius, so: Circular with Radius is the kernel as before; Chord Width is the kernel with each edge's radius r = chord / (2 cos(a/2)), a the angle between the faces at the edge middle; every other choice is built in core/features/fillet_profile.py for straight edges between two flat faces: the cross section (corner point, the two tangent points d1 and d2 along the faces, the profile curve) is extruded along the edge and cut from a convex edge or fused to a concave one, all edges in one boolean each. Curves: circular and elliptic are the rational quadratic Bezier through corner and tangent points with middle weight sin(a/2) (exactly the circle when d1 = d2, its affine ellipse otherwise, so Circular on Asymmetric is the ellipse); conic uses weight rho/(1 - rho), rho from 0.05 to 0.95 (0.5 a parabola); curvature continuous is the quartic Bezier p0, p0 + (c - p0)/2, c, p2 + (c - p2)/2, p2, whose curvature is zero at both ends. With Radius on a non circular profile the tangent points are where the circle of that radius would touch; with Chord they are chord / (2 sin(a/2)) from the corner. The prism ends square at the edge ends, so corners between several such edges meet as mitres, not corner blends. Errors name the edges that are not straight between flat faces (spec item 3). Multiple radius or Tangent propagation off with a built profile is a feature error with a next step. A shaped fillet cannot Change to Chamfer.

D1403: Variable fillet point positions (2026-11-07, TR133, Phase 7B Stage 3). A variable fillet's control point j can have vp_j, its position in percent of each edge (a number, an FDEF owner item; the same for every edge, like the point count). Without it the point is evenly spaced as before, so old files rebuild unchanged. Positions must be strictly between 0 and 100 and differ; the radius law is sorted by position, so points may be typed in any order. The panel shows a Point j at (%) row per point; Add Point raises the count and puts the new point in the middle of the widest gap between 0, the points and 100; Delete Point removes point j and moves the positions and radii of the later points up one place. The count stays at most 5.

D1404: Change existing fillets and drafts (2026-11-07, TR132, Phase 7B Stage 3). Pure edits in core/fillet_edit.py, each pushed as ReplaceFeature (several in one undo macro). (1) The view menu on a face named <fid>/fillet/<edge> of a constant fillet whose edge is in refs.edges offers Change Fillet Edge: OK gives that edge its own radius (multiple_radius with radius_k), Remove from Fillet drops it from refs.edges and moves the later radius_k and vr_k_* values up one place; the only edge of a fillet cannot be removed (delete the feature). Edges that came from picked faces, features or the assistant have no menu item, since they have no per edge value. (2) Change Fillets, from the tree menu on any fillet, lists the part's constant fillets (name, radius text, picked edge count) inside a typed radius range and sets one new main radius on all listed fillets (per edge radii stay). (3) Change Drafts, from the tree menu on a draft, lists every draft feature sorted by pull direction (the neutral plane or face name, and reversed) then angle; Set Angle writes the typed angle (0 to 90 degrees) on the selected drafts, Remove Selected deletes them. Drafts on extrudes are not listed: they belong to their extrude. The view menu change is in main_window/context_menu.py (shared file), the tree items in tree/feature_tree.py.

D1405: Fillet failure help (2026-11-07, TR346, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) When a fillet of picked edges (Constant or Variable, no Partial Edges, Tangent propagation on, 2 to 12 edges, none from faces or features) fails, pinpointing (D213) also tries other ways as chains of separate fillets built one after the other on the result (core/features/fillet_help.py): each chain (edges sharing an end point), smaller groups (greedy: as many edges as build together, then the next group on that result), larger radius first (Multiple radius: one fillet per radius, largest first) and one fillet per edge. Edges are found again on each intermediate body by their middle point. Only ways that build are offered, as fixes with action split_fillet and data groups (picked edge names); an identical grouping is offered once. Applying one (main window apply_fix, shared file) is one undo macro: the feature keeps the first group, each other group becomes a new fillet right after it with the next free Fillet name, and radius_k and vr_k_* follow their edges. The panel cannot add features, so it hides split fixes and says to click OK and use the errors panel. The rounds made one after the other meet differently at shared corners than one kernel call would. (2) Fillet and Chamfer already name failing edges and the cause (D213, D216); Shell names the tight face (D998 pre check), and TR278 names the face the kernel cannot treat; Offset Body now runs the same bend check on failure and names the tightest face and its radius, or says the likely cause (the wall may be too thin, sharp corners may not meet).

D1406: Skip one face as a fix (2026-11-07, TR278, Phase 7B Stage 3). When Shell's offset fails and the bend pre check found no tight face, it tries leaving out one face at a time (as an extra opening), tightest bend first, at most 25 faces and only on bodies of up to 150 faces (each try is a whole shell). The first face that lets the shell build is named in the error and highlighted, with the fix "Skip face X (leave it open)": a new fix action add_refs (core/features/fixes.py and the main window's fix list, shared file) that adds the face to refs.skipped_faces (an FDEF owner item). Skipped faces are opened like removed faces but kept in their own list, so Reset Skipped Faces in the tree menu (shown only when the list is not empty) removes them in one undo step; the geometry never changes without the click (CLAUDE.md 5.12). Offset Body has no skip: leaving a face out of an offset body would not give a closed solid; its failure names the tight face instead (D1405).

D1407: Edges to keep and limiting plane (2026-11-07, TR271 items 2 and 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Constant size fillets get refs.keep_edges and refs.limit_plane with param limit_flip (FDEF owner items; core/features/fillet_limits.py). (2) The kernel cannot route a round around an edge, so Edges to Keep protect by checking: after the round, each kept edge must still be found by its middle point; if not, the fillet fails naming the swallowed edges (highlighted) and, for one main radius, offers "Reduce the radius to X mm", X the largest radius (eight halvings, rounded down as in D213) whose round keeps them all. (3) The limiting plane (a reference plane or flat face, resolved like a datum pick) is applied with the partial edge routine (D519): each edge keeps its part behind the plane (against its normal, or in front with limit_flip) up to its first crossing, rounded with a square end at the plane; an edge with no crossing is rounded whole when its middle is behind and skipped when in front; all edges in front is an error. A limiting plane with Partial Edges is an error. Item 1 (limit failing areas: round what works and leave the failing stretches of an edge sharp) is not done: finding the failing stretch of one edge needs many partial trials per edge, and Fillet the rest (D213) and the split ways (D1405) already cover failing whole edges. The panel's Limits group has Pick Kept Edges and Pick Limit toggles that route view picks.

D1408: Fillet rules (2026-11-07, TR320, Phase 7B Stage 3). refs.auto_edges items may be rules (key rule, an FDEF owner item) beside the assistant items (convexity, D519): attach (edges of feature F's faces where a face of another feature meets it), free (edges whose faces are all F's), feature (every edge of F's faces) and parallel (straight edges parallel to axis x, y or z, of F or of the whole part). A face belongs to F by its primary name, so a face merged with a coplanar face of an earlier feature belongs to the earlier one. Smooth edges are never found (only convex or concave edges, as the assistant). exclude lists edge names a rule leaves out; radius names a length param rule_radius_<n> (n never reused in the feature) with the rule's own radius, used unless Multiple radius gives a picked edge its own. Picked edges win over rules for the same edge. In the panel a rule list, Add Rule (with the assistant's scope), Own radius and a Pick Exclusions toggle that adds clicked edges to the rule selected in the items list; labels show the rule and how many edges it leaves out.

D1409: Face fillet with a hold line (2026-11-07, TR29, Phase 7B Stage 3). Face fillets get method "hold_line" (the method param, otherwise used by constant fillets, D1402) with refs.hold_lines, edges on one face set (FDEF owner items). A hold line round uses up the face between the hold line and the other set, and the kernel fillet cannot end a round exactly on a face's far edge (a test failed at the exact radius), so it is built in core/features/fillet_hold.py for straight edges between two flat faces: at each end of an edge the gap d to the hold line is measured, and a circular cross section touching both faces at distance d (the rational conic of D1402) is made there; a ruled solid through the two sections (a prism when the gaps match) is cut from a convex edge or fused to a concave one, and the boolean removes the used up face. A linear change of gap gives a ruled round whose middle sections are close to circular. A hold line that touches the edge is an error; other edges are named as for the shaped profiles. The panel's face fillet gets Method (Radius, Hold Line), a hold line list and a Pick Hold Lines toggle.

D1410: Remove Fillets (2026-11-07, TR260, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type remove_fillets (FDEF owner item) with optional min_radius, max_radius, new_radius, the panel ticks use_range and resize, and optional refs.faces (core/features/remove_fillets.py, registered from fillet.py so the shared features package is not edited). A round is a cylinder (not a whole turn), torus (tube radius) or sphere face with at least two smooth edges, so holes and shafts are never found. Rounds are removed smallest first in batches of four with the Delete Face patch (BRepAlgoAPI_Defeaturing, D232); a failing batch is retried one face at a time; faces that still fail stay and are named in a warning, and no face removed is an error. With new_radius the edges between the faces each removed round joined smoothly are rounded again in one kernel call, named fillet/<edge name>. It is added from Change Fillets (D1404), which counts the rounds in the typed range on the built part and adds the feature with that range and the new radius; its panel (a declarative form) edits picks, range and resize. No command or ribbon button was added, to stay out of the shared command files.

D1411: Shell Both Sides (2026-11-07, TR322 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Shell gets both_sides (an FDEF owner item): the shell is made twice at half the thickness (and half of each face thickness), inward and outward, with the same removed and skipped faces, and the two are fused (they meet on the part's old surface, which goes). The outer half's wall faces are renamed outer/<face name> so names stay unique; inner walls keep shell/<face name>. One body only (an error with a next step otherwise); Shell outward is ignored and greyed out while Both sides is ticked. The approximate Never Thinner or Never Thicker mode is not done: the kernel offsets exactly along each face normal, and the thickness only differs at sharp corners where the joins decide it (an inward offset always meets convex corners sharp), so neither promise can be kept for every corner without new corner geometry.

D1412: Replace Face (2026-11-07, TR130, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type replace_face (FDEF owner item) with refs.faces and refs.target (a reference plane or flat face; a dict, or a list of one as the panel stores it). The spec left the extent to the owner; D683 approved the spec as written, and only flat targets are built, as solid work: a curved target is an error with a next step. For each picked face, with n the target normal turned the way the face looks, the face swept along n is cut to the slab short of the plane and fused (extend), and the face swept against n is cut to the slab past the plane and cut away (trim), so only the picked faces' own column changes. Tool faces on the plane are named replaced, kept faces keep their names, and coplanar faces merge. Side faces are extended along n, which matches neighbours square to the target (the common flatten case); other neighbours meet the new walls at an edge. The panel is a declarative form (the first picks are faces to replace, then the target, unless a list is clicked), opened from the view menu on a face (main_window/context_menu.py, shared); no ribbon command was added.

D1413: Push Pull (2026-11-07, TR267, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type push_pull (FDEF owner item): signed distance, optional symmetric, refs.faces (flat faces) or refs.sketch (a closed sketch on a face), optional refs.to_face. Faces move as Move Face Offset (direct.offset_faces): along their outward normal, so positive adds and negative cuts; every picked face takes the same distance (spec item 3: in the panel, clicking more faces gives them the same distance, instead of a double click in the view). A sketch builds the equivalent Extrude (boss for positive, a reversed cut for negative, Mid Plane when symmetric). to_face (a list of one from the panel, or a dict) is a flat face parallel to the first picked face; the distance is then the signed distance to it, so it follows later edits. Item 2's Tab while dragging is the panel's Next Parallel Face button: it steps through the parallel faces nearest first, sets to_face and shows the distance; switching between one side and symmetric is the Symmetric tick (regions only, since a face has only one side). Opened from the view menu on a face (context_menu.py, shared); no ribbon command.

D1414: Split Line (2026-11-07, TR60 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type split_line (FDEF owner item) with method "projection" (refs.sketch projected onto refs.faces along refs.direction or the sketch normal, with reverse and both, reusing Projected Curve's projection, D291) or "intersection" (refs.plane, a reference plane or flat face, a dict or a list of one; BRepAlgoAPI_Section of each picked face with the plane). The edges that lie on a picked face are added to that face with BRepFeat_SplitShape, so only picked faces split and the volume is unchanged; pieces take <face name>#k by position through the maker history (PLAN section 6), and deleting the feature joins the faces again. Not built: Silhouette (the outline along a pull direction needs a curve where the surface normal turns square to the pull on every face kind, which OCC has no direct tool for) and intersection with another body (a later step with BRepAlgoAPI_Section against the body). The panel is a declarative form opened from the view menu on a face (context_menu.py, shared).

D1415: Parting Line (2026-11-07, TR84 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new curve feature type parting_line (FDEF owner item) with refs.direction (a plane or axis feature, flat face or straight edge, as Projected Curve's direction; the panel stores one reference) and reverse. Each face's draft sign is the area weighted sine between its outward normal and the pull over the draft analysis triangles (D522, one numpy pass); faces with no draft count as positive, so an undrafted box's line runs round the bottom of its walls (reverse moves it to the top). Parting edges are the edges between a positive and a negative face, kept as the feature's curve (curve_result). Free ends (end points used by an odd number of edges) mean a broken line: a warning gives their count and the gaps, pairing nearest ends first; faces with more than 2 percent of their area on each side are straddle faces, named in the messages. No edge found is an error with a next step. The tick box that splits straddle faces at the line (spec item 1) is not built: it needs the silhouette curve on each straddle face (Split Line Silhouette, D1414). Opened from the view menu on a face (context_menu.py, shared).

D1416: More Geometry Check classes, fixes and Symmetry Check (2026-11-07, TR87 items 1 and 3, TR262 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). core/geometry_check.check takes optional Limits: curvature (faces whose smallest bend radius, inside or outside, from the shell sampler, is under it; off unless ticked), knife (edges whose faces meet at a wedge angle under it, default 5 degrees), near_smooth (edges less than it short of smooth, more than 1e-6 rad, default 2 degrees), duplicates (faces whose position snapshots match) and inexact (edges without same parameter or with a tolerance over 1e-4 mm, when not already a gap). Edges with gaps were already found (D356); short edges under a typed length are the existing Tiny edge limit. The window (print_tools/geometry_check.py) adds the limits, Next and Back (zoom to each finding; the clip sphere is not done), Ignore (hidden by kind and message for the session) and Fix: a sliver or duplicate face is removed by a new Delete Face (patch) feature, one undo step, only on click. Fixes for gaps, nearly smooth edges and nearly square faces are not done: each needs new healing geometry beyond Delete Face. Symmetry Check (TR87 item 3) mirrors the part about the selected flat face's plane off the UI thread; it is symmetric when every face's mirror image matches a face of the part, and the faces that do not are listed for highlighting. TR87 item 2 (wall thickness target and hover reading) is not done.

D1417: Detailed preview (2026-11-07, TR164 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature copy sent to the preview with data preview_detailed (set by the panel on the preview copy only, never saved, like the outline preview of D585) is built in full in the preview builder (core/features/preview.detailed_view): the whole result replaces the part, faces whose names are all new are tinted in the preview colour (accent: what the feature adds) and new faces that carry a name from before go in the second colour (stretched, the Move Face colour of D798: what it changes); when the result has more bodies than before, only the new bodies show. The Draft panel gets a Detailed preview tick, kept for the session; it takes priority over Show changed faces. The same flag works for Extrude and Rib, but their panels (property_panel/panel.py and the shape forms) are shared files and their ticks are not added in this round.

D1418: Allow reduced angle (2026-11-07, TR147 item 1 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Parting line and step drafts get allow_reduced (an FDEF owner item). When the kernel cannot tilt the faces at the full angle, the draft looks for the largest share of both angles (the angle and the other side's angle together) that builds, in seven halving steps, uses it and adds a warning (code reduced_angle) with the angle used; without the tick the failure stays an error as before. A failure that names a face (a face that cannot be drafted at any angle) is not retried. Not done: tapered or square steps for Step Draft (the step faces between levels are the part's own faces and are not tilted; tapering them needs a choice of which faces are steps), and TR147 item 3 (a dome direction vector and constraint sketch).

D1419: More draft options (2026-11-07, TR323 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Neutral plane drafts get neutral_split with angle2 and angle_mode (FDEF owner items). With neutral_split the part is cut at the neutral plane and each half is drafted about the plane with the same pull (the parting draft's half routine, D521): faces above tilt by angle, faces below by angle2, so equal angles give the one plane draft; the halves are joined and the split faces merged. angle_mode "relative" adds the angle to the lean a flat face already has (asin of its normal along the pull; curved faces have no lean), so a face drafted 3 degrees and drafted again by 2 relative ends at 5 degrees; it also lets a flat face that already leans (up to 89 degrees) be picked, which the default "absolute" mode still refuses as before. The panel's Neutral Plane group gets the angle list, the tick and the angle below (written as angle2). The Fixed Edge type (keep one edge and add faces where needed) is not done: it needs new side faces built along the kept edge.

D1420: Reapply Fillets (2026-11-07, TR259 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Move Face and Delete Face get reapply_fillets (an FDEF owner item; a tick in their forms). The round faces that share an edge with a picked face (the Remove Fillets test for a round, D1410) are removed with the Delete Face patch, the feature's own change runs on that sharp body (the picked faces are found again by name, since the patch carries names), and the edges between the faces each round joined smoothly are rounded again at that round's radius in one kernel call (core/features/reapply_fillets.py). The new rounds are named fillet/<edge name> after the editing feature, so references to the old round faces become lost references with the usual message. Rounds that cannot be removed, or cannot be made again, are a feature error naming them, with turning off the tick as the next step. Draft and Combine are not done in this round: Draft's faces go through the parting and split routines, and Combine works on bodies rather than picked faces.

D1421: Corner Chamfer recorded as met (2026-11-07, TR394 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Picking one vertex and typing a distance along each of its three edges is the existing Chamfer type Vertex (D216: distance, distance2 and distance3 along the three edges, ordered by edge name, or Equal distance), so nothing new is built. Items 1 (list fillet pieces as included, excluded or edited, and drag a piece end) and 2 (choose the transition where fillets meet: stop at a reference, continue past a sharp edge, sharp, corner sphere or patch) are not done: the kernel makes the pieces and the corner patches itself and has no setting for the transition kind; item 1's drag needs viewport handles.

D1200: Mesh preview and largest edge length (2026-11-07, TR336, Phase 7B Stage 3). The STL and 3MF options get **Largest edge** (0, shown as No limit, by default) and **Show the mesh in the view**, and show the longest edge, the worst aspect ratio (the longest edge squared over four times the area, times the square root of 3, so an equilateral triangle is 1) and the count of triangles above 20 beside the triangle count. The kernel's mesher has no edge length limit, so the export triangles are split afterwards in numpy (`core/io/mesh_refine.py`) by longest edge bisection: each round marks the edges above the limit, a triangle with a marked edge also has its longest edge marked and is halved across it first, so triangles never get thinner and every split edge is split on both sides, keeping the mesh closed; new points are edge middles, inside the chord deviation already met. Splitting stops at 16 rounds or about 4 million triangles. Coloured 3MF refines each body as one mesh, so colour seams stay closed. The limit is kept in the part's print setup (`mesh_export.max_edge`, written only when set) and also applies to PLY, OBJ and glTF. Refining by aspect ratio was tried and left out: bisection and flipping flat neighbours keep the shapes of thin triangles from long faces, so a ratio limit could not be met without a remesher that moves points; the preview reports the ratio instead. The preview is a shaded overlay with triangle edges, cleared when the window closes.

D1201: Lasting body names (2026-11-07, TR183 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A body row's menu gets **Rename Body...**: the name is kept in the part's print setup under `body_titles`, a face name of the body (its mark, the same as hidden bodies, D410, and print roles, D796) to the name, so it follows the body through rebuilds that renumber bodies. One undo step (a general `SetPrintSetupKey` command, which later print setup keys also use). Names lose control characters, have their spaces joined and are cut at 120 characters; an empty name takes it off. The tree shows the name instead of Body N, and 3MF export names that body's object (and its Bambu and Prusa settings entries) by it, escaped; bodies without one keep "title body N". This finishes TR183: item 1's metadata and part number are D960, item 2 is the thumbnail of TR381. FDEF owner item: the new `print_setup.body_titles` key.

D1202: STEP export options (2026-11-07, TR302 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). STEP export asks, after the file name, for **Unit** (millimetres, inches or metres; the kernel's writer converts the lengths and writes the unit, and readers convert back), **Y up** (a quarter turn about X, Z up to Y up, as a moved copy; face colours move with it), **Body names** (on by default: each body is its own named product, its Rename Body name or Body N, or the part name for a one body part), **One file per body** (`<name>_<body>.step` beside the chosen name, characters a file name cannot hold made underscores, a number added when two names match) and **Include hidden bodies** (off: hidden bodies are left out, an all hidden part is an export error with a next step). The choice is kept in the part's print setup under `step_export` and used without asking by Save As and other exports that pass a file name. The STEP controller is now set up before the schema and unit settings are written: before, the first STEP export of a session silently kept the default settings. Batch export, export bodies and configurations keep plain millimetre STEP. FDEF owner item: the new `print_setup.step_export` key.

D1203: Pick the bodies of a STEP import (2026-11-07, TR302 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). The STEP and IGES import feature gets an optional text param `keep_bodies`: the numbers of the bodies that come in, from 1 in the healed shape's order ("1, 3"), empty or missing for all. Faces keep the names they have in the whole file, so references on a kept body do not move when another body is ticked or unticked. A pick that is not whole numbers, or that keeps no body of the file (for example after Replace From File with a smaller file), is a feature error with a next step. **Pick Bodies...** on the import's tree menu reads the file in a background job and shows a tick list, one row per body with its volume and size; the ticked bodies are drawn in the 3D view as a shaded overlay while the window is open, and OK needs at least one tick. Insert, STEP opens the same list after the import's first build when the file holds more than one body; Open of a STEP file as a new part does not ask. The tick list shows numbers, not the names in the file: names are lost when healing makes new solids. One undo step. TR302 is done with D1202. FDEF owner item: the new `import_step` param `keep_bodies`.

D1204: Section and outline export (2026-11-07, TR300, Phase 7B Stage 3). File, Export, **Export Section and Outline** asks for the source (Section at a plane, or Outline seen along the axis), the plane (Top, Front or Right; the drawing's X is the model's X, or Y for Right), the section offset along the plane's normal, a kerf or tool offset, a scale, and a use per body (Cut, Engrave or Ignore), then a .dxf or .svg file. A section is the common of each body with a large face in the plane.
