An outline is the body's shadow: its sharp, smooth and silhouette edges, seen and hidden, are projected with the kernel's hidden line algorithm, split where they cross, and the regions they bound are kept when a line along the normal through a point inside meets the body, then joined, so through holes stay holes. The kerf grows each face by its value in the drawing's millimetres (negative shrinks, round corners as Profile offset, D880), so it is not scaled. Each use is a layer: DXF layer names CUT and ENGRAVE on the R12 entities, SVG groups with those ids stroked red and blue as laser programs map them; one file holds every body. Nothing to draw (the plane misses every body, or all are ignored) is an export error with a next step. The choice is not kept in the part.

D1205: Read slicer 3MF files (2026-11-07, TR386, Phase 7B Stage 3). `mesh_import.read_3mf_parts` reads a 3MF as parts: one per mesh object placed in the build (through components, as D715), or one per volume of PrusaSlicer's one object layout (`Metadata/Slic3r_PE_model.config` triangle ranges), each with a name and a print role. Names come from the Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer settings (`Metadata/model_settings.config` parts by object id), the Prusa volume names, or the object's name attribute, else "Object N"; roles from the Bambu part subtype, the Prusa volume type, or Cura's `cura:` mesh settings (infill mesh to Modifier, support mesh to Support Enforcer, anti overhang mesh to Support Blocker, cutting mesh to Negative Volume). Settings parts above 16 MB are skipped, tags are found with linear patterns and paired in one pass (no lazy search to a closing tag, D709), out of range triangle ranges fall back to the whole object, and names are unescaped and cleaned as body names (D1201). The Import Mesh feature gets two optional booleans for a converted 3MF: `parts` (One body per part) and `keep_roles` (Keep slicer roles; off leaves modifier, negative and support parts out). Part faces are `part<k>/face/<j>`; the feature's result gives each part's first face its name and role (`extras["body_titles"]`, `extras["body_roles"]`), which the tree, Rename Body, Print Role and export use where the user set none; setting such a body back to Part stores "part", so the file's role does not come back. FDEF owner items: the `import_mesh` params `parts` and `keep_roles`, and a stored `print_setup.body_roles` value may now be "part".

D1206: Slicer targets (2026-11-07, TR385, Phase 7B Stage 3). The 3MF options' **Slicer** choice, which Open in Slicer also uses, becomes a target with four values: Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer or Cura (the default form B with Cura marks, D796), PrusaSlicer (form P), **Cura only** (the assembly layout with the `cura:` marks and no `model_settings.config`) and **Plain 3MF** (core 3MF with bodies, colours, names and metadata only: no roles, no slicer settings, for any program). Under the choice a line says what the target keeps, including the per body settings and settings by height of TR383 and TR384; the status line after export says what was dropped. The kept value is `mesh_export.slicer` as before; older files load unchanged. Each target's slicer files are written from the file form facts in the spec, and the spec says they need a test with the real slicer program before a release (spec section 21 item 7): that stays a manual release check, since CI cannot run the slicers. FDEF owner item: `print_setup.mesh_export.slicer` may also be `cura` or `plain`.

D1207: Per body print settings (2026-11-07, TR383, Phase 7B Stage 3). A body row's menu gets **Print Settings...**: a tick box per setting, layer height (0.01 to 2 mm), wall count (0 to 50), infill density (0 to 100 percent), infill pattern (Grid, Gyroid, Cubic, Lines, Honeycomb), supports on or off, and extruder (1 to 16); only ticked settings are kept, under `print_setup.body_settings` by the body's mark (as roles, D796), one undo step. 3MF export writes them per body in each family's keys: Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer as `<metadata key value>` in the body's `<part>` of `model_settings.config` (`layer_height`, `wall_loops`, `sparse_infill_density` as "35%", `sparse_infill_pattern`, `enable_support` 1 or 0, `extruder`), which amends the D796 rule of no other keys in that file, since these keys are print settings on purpose; PrusaSlicer as volume metadata in `Slic3r_PE_model.config` (`layer_height`, `perimeters`, `fill_density`, `fill_pattern`, `support_material`, `extruder`); Cura as `cura:` metadata on the body's mesh object (`wall_line_count`, `infill_sparse_density`, `infill_pattern` with Honeycomb as triangles, `support_enable`, `extruder_nr` counted from 0; Cura has no layer height per model, so that one is not written). Plain 3MF writes none. Lines is `line` for Bambu and Prusa. The panel says FDCAD does not also change the geometry for what slicers compensate (hole shrink, first layer spread), so effects never double. The key names need the release check with the real slicers (D1206). FDEF owner item: the new `print_setup.body_settings` key.

D1208: Settings by height (2026-11-07, TR384, Phase 7B Stage 3). Print, **Settings by Height** keeps a part level list under `print_setup.height_changes`: entries with `z` (mm above the print bed, after Lay Face Flat), `kind` `pause`, `colour` or `setting` (with `key` layer height, infill or walls and a `value` that holds from that height up to the next change of the same key), and an optional note; at most 200, sorted, damaged entries dropped. One undo step. 3MF export and Open in Slicer write them for two targets: Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer in `Metadata/custom_gcode_per_layer.xml` (`<layer top_z type>`: 1 a pause with `M400 U1`, 0 a colour change with `M600`) and `Metadata/layer_config_ranges.xml` (`<range min_z max_z>` with `<option opt_key>` for `layer_height`, `sparse_infill_density`, `wall_loops`), and PrusaSlicer in `Metadata/Prusa_Slicer_custom_gcode_per_print_z.xml` (`<code print_z type>`, pause `M601`) and `Metadata/Prusa_Slicer_layer_config_ranges.xml` (`fill_density`, `perimeters`), each range on the build item's object, the last up to the part's height on the bed. Cura and plain 3MF have no place for them, and the panel says so. The `.xml` parts get a content type. These forms need the release check with the real slicers (D1206). The warning for an insert pocket that a roof closes below its pause height (spec addition 94) is not done. FDEF owner item: the new `print_setup.height_changes` key.

D1209: Layer Fit Check (2026-11-07, TR187 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Evaluate, **Layer Fit Check** runs in a job on the part as it lies on the bed (Lay Face Flat and Scale to Fit), with the active printer profile's layer height and its nozzle size as the line width (as D988). Heights are the levels of flat faces facing straight up or down, measured from the lowest point; walls are pairs of flat side faces facing away from each other with material at the middle point between them (a solid classifier test), up to 8 line widths thick (thicker is solid infill). A size more than a tenth of a layer or line from a whole number is listed with its count and the nearest whole size; sizes under half a layer or line are left out. At most 1500 flat faces are looked at. The list (25 lines, then a count) shows in a message box and the status bar gives the count; nothing found is a status line. The check never changes the part. TR187 is done with D988.

D1210: Suggest Orientation and Arrange on Bed (2026-11-07, TR301, Phase 7B Stage 3). Print, **Suggest Orientation** tries the six largest flat face directions (outward normals of flat faces grouped within 1e-6, by total area; each with its largest face) as the face down direction, since only a flat face can be applied with Lay Face Flat, and ranks them: fitting the build volume first (height and footprint against the active profile, either way round), then by overhang area (triangles steeper than the profile's overhang angle and not on the bed, as the Overhang Analysis, D354), then by height. A list shows each with its overhang, height and fit; Apply lays the chosen face flat as one undo step. A part with no flat face says so. **Arrange on Bed** asks for a spacing (5 mm by default), takes each body's footprint after the print orientation's turn, and places the deepest first in rows from the bed's front left corner, trying the corners next to what is already placed, with the spacing between bodies and around no print zones (TR413); because print placement centres the whole layout on the bed, the zones are packed around a second time where they fall once the layout is centred. The moves become one Move and Copy Body feature per moved body (translate by delta, in model coordinates), all one undo step, so the layout is part of the model and every export and Open in Slicer follows it. Bodies that do not fit are a status message with a next step.

D1211: Split for Printing magnets, screws and a glue gap (2026-11-07, TR181 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Two connector kinds join pins and dovetail keys, placed at the same spots: **Magnet Pockets** (`magnet_diameter`, `magnet_depth`: a round pocket `magnet_depth` plus clearance deep into each piece, no body added; a spot whose pocket would break out of the part is left out with the existing warning) and **Screws and Nuts** (`screw_diameter`: a hole clearance wider right through the part along the cut normal; `nut_size` across flats and `nut_height`: a hexagon pocket, clearance larger, in from where that line last leaves the part on the normal's side, found with a line and surface intersection, fused with the hole into one tool since overlapping tools in one compound were cut once only). An optional `glue_gap` (any connector) trims the pieces on each cut's normal side back by the gap with a slab cut, before connectors, so the part gets that much shorter; zero is not written. Face names carry through the cuts. Draft on keys and the stepped or shaped cut from a sketch path (item 2) are not done: a drafted dovetail needs a tapered key and pocket pair, and a sketch path cut needs its own splitter design. FDEF owner items: `split_for_print` connector values `magnets` and `screws`, and the params `magnet_diameter`, `magnet_depth`, `screw_diameter`, `nut_size`, `nut_height`, `glue_gap`.

D1212: Mesh repair and reduce (2026-11-07, TR186, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/mesh_repair.py`, all numpy. **Repair** drops repeated triangles (the same three corners in any order), keeps only the first two triangles on an edge that more than two share, drops loose pieces with less than 1 percent of the largest piece's area (pieces found by spreading the smallest vertex label along triangle edges with pointer jumping), then fills each hole: every open edge gets a triangle, turned the other way, to the middle of its rim (rims found the same way), so the mesh closes without ordering the rim. A twisted or very bent hole fills with a fan that may cross itself. **Reduce** clusters vertices on a grid whose cell is found by halving search so the count meets a target (Keep percent, 1 to 99, or Keep count, at least 4); each cell's vertices merge to their mean, collapsed and repeated triangles go, a largest move caps the cell at that move divided by the square root of 3, which may leave more triangles than asked, and Keep open edges keeps rim vertices in cells of their own. The Import Mesh feature gets the optional params `repair` (boolean), `reduce_percent` or `reduce_target` (whole numbers), `reduce_error` (length) and `keep_boundary` (boolean), applied after reading and before showing or converting; what was done goes into the import report on the status bar. One body per part (D1205) reads the parts again from the file and is not repaired. FDEF owner items: those five `import_mesh` params.

D1213: Suction cups and floating islands (2026-11-07, TR409, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/printing/islands.py` looks at the part as placed on the bed (Lay Face Flat and Scale to Fit) from below on a grid of 160 cells along the longer side: the downward facing triangles of a coarse mesh are sampled densely (about three samples per cell width, made for all triangles at once) and the lowest sample wins in each cell. Cups: turned upside down, the bottom surface is filled like a landscape with water, each cell rising to the lowest rim it can spill over while cells with nothing over them and the border drain (whole grid passes until nothing changes); cells that rise more than 0.5 mm are grouped into cups, with the deepest. Islands: groups of cells of one height that are more than 0.05 mm off the bed with no lower cell next to them. Evaluate, **Suction Cups and Islands** runs it in a job, marks the middle of each cup and island in the view as points, and offers **Add Drain Holes** (cups only, the TR189 feature) or **Suggest Orientation**. Suggest Orientation (D1210) now ranks fit, then overhang, then the island count (an 80 cell grid per direction), then height. Grid cells limit what is seen: holes narrower than a cell can be missed.

D1214: Coating allowance (2026-11-07, TR307, Phase 7B Stage 3). Print, **Coating Allowance** keeps a thickness (0 to 5 mm) in `print_setup.coating`, one undo step; 0 takes it off. STL and 3MF export and Open in Slicer move every face of every body inward by it, in the export job, with the kernel's offset (sharp corners, as Offset Body, D825), and move face colours onto the new faces through the offset's history; the status line says it was applied. A body thinner than twice the coating is an export error with a next step. STEP export, Save As to other formats and the model are never changed, since STEP goes to CAD programs that should get the nominal shape. As a feature, Offset Body inward with the coating thickness already does the same; no separate feature type was added. FDEF owner item: the new `print_setup.coating` key.

D1215: Code tags (2026-11-07, TR311, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/printing/qr_code.py` is FDCAD's own QR code encoder written from the public standard (ISO/IEC 18004): byte mode with UTF-8 text, error correction level M (about 15 percent of the code may be damaged), versions 1 to 10 (21 to 57 modules, up to 213 bytes), Reed-Solomon codewords over GF(256), block interleaving, the finder, timing and alignment patterns, format and version information, and the mask with the lowest penalty. The output was checked once by decoding rendered codes for versions 1 to 10 with an open source reader in a scratch environment (not a project dependency); the tests check the fixed patterns, the codeword syndromes and the outline area. `core/sketch/code_tag.py` draws the dark modules as one region of sketch lines with shared end points: outlines are walked with the dark side on the left, straight runs merged, and where two modules touch only at a corner each outline cuts that corner back by 0.04 of a module, since a sketch needs every point to join exactly two curves. Sketch, right click, **Code Tag** asks for the text and the module size (at least 0.4 mm) and shows the tag's size; one sketch change.

D1216: Material interlock teeth (2026-11-07, TR414 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A Print feature, type `interlock`: pick a flat face of one body where it lies against another body (found by a point a quarter tooth past the face's middle being inside it); the face's plane is covered by a checkerboard of `tooth_size` squares (3 mm to start) from the corner of the face's extent in its own frame, and each square becomes a tooth `tooth_depth` deep (1.5 mm), clipped to the face's outline: on squares of one colour the picked body grows into the other, on the other colour the other body grows back, so material is traded, not lost. Teeth are made as two compounds and joined with one boolean per body side (CLAUDE.md 5A rule 5); more than 2500 teeth, a face with no body against it, or teeth that break a body apart are feature errors with a next step. Both bodies stay separate; face names carry through, new tooth faces are `<fid>/teeth/face#k`. TR414 is done with D1009. FDEF owner item: the new type `interlock` and its params.

D1217: Printing sample parts (2026-11-07, TR188, Phase 7B Stage 3). Three samples with tutorials (`samples/parts_print.py`, golden results like the others): **fit_test_plate** (a 70 x 30 x 4 plate with five pins of diameter `Pin` and five through holes `Pin + 2k Step` wide for k from 1 to 5, so the gap per side steps by `Step`, 0.1 mm), **living_hinge_strip** (an 80 x 20 x 1.2 strip with a 24 mm Living Hinge band, D908) and **storage_bin** (a bin `Grid * Wide` by `Grid * Deep` on a 42 mm grid, `Height` tall with `Wall` sides and a `Floor`, using number variables for the grid counts). The new sample files carry the fixture app version like the others; the existing sample files were left unchanged. Not done: the nut and bolt on the fit plate (a hexagon needs a sketch outline the sample builder does not draw yet), the print in place hinge, and the base grid under the bin (the bin is sized on the grid, but the grid plate itself is not modelled).

D2000: Guided fit calibration (2026-11-07, TR358, Phase 7B Stage 3). Print, **Fit Calibration** asks for the first gap per side (0 to 1 mm, default 0.1), the step (0.01 to 0.5 mm, default 0.05) and the number of holes (2 to 10, default 6), then opens a new part from `core/printing/calibration.py`: a 3 mm plate with one 5 mm pin (8 mm tall) and a row of holes at 12 mm pitch, each sized `=Pin + 2 * Gapk` and labelled with its gap in 4 mm text cut 0.4 mm deep. The spec asks for one configuration per step; one plate with a variable per hole (Pin, Gap1, Gap2 ...) was chosen instead, so a single print tests every step and the labels still follow the values. **Keep Measured Fit** asks for the gap that fitted and stores it as the active printer profile's fit tolerance (TR180, D812), then rebuilds parts that read `fit_tolerance@Printer`. The spec's shrink compensation note is not built: FDCAD has no shrink compensation to keep away from fit features. Continues the round 12 work in progress that was to be D1218.

D2001: Refining export meshes by aspect ratio (2026-11-07, TR336, Phase 7B Stage 3). The STL and 3MF options get **Largest aspect ratio** (0, shown as No limit, by default; limits below 2 count as 2), kept as `mesh_export.max_aspect` in the print setup (written only when set) and used by every mesh export that refines (STL, 3MF, PLY, OBJ, glTF and the preview). D1200 found that longest edge bisection cannot meet a ratio: it keeps thin triangles similar. `core/io/mesh_refine.py` now does three things per round instead, all in numpy: (1) flips edges between two triangles in one plane (normals within 1e-6 rad, same colour group) where the other diagonal lowers the worse aspect ratio of the two (not the Delaunay test, which every set of points on one circle passes; each flip lowers the sorted ratio list, so flipping ends; independent flips per pass, largest gain first); (2) marks, in triangles still thinner than the limit, the edges longer than 1.5 times the shortest edge of the input triangle they came from that a flip cannot mend (sharp edges, colour seams, open borders); long edges inside a flat region are left to the flips, since splitting them at the middle leaves two needles; (3) splits exactly the marked edges at their middles with no longest edge rule (one, two or three split edges give two, three or four triangles), so a strip is cut across rather than halved both ways. Up to 40 rounds and the 4 million triangle cap. A 100 x 1 x 1 box goes from a ratio of 87 to under 3 with 260 triangles; a cylinder's side meets the limit, while caps of three neighbouring points on an end circle stay (about 39 on a 5 mm radius at standard quality), because mending those needs points inside the face; the preview reports the worst ratio left.

D2002: Split for Printing along a sketch, and drafted keys (2026-11-07, TR181, Phase 7B Stage 3). A third cut mode `mode: "sketch"` (shown as **Along Sketch**) cuts along the drawn curves of the sketch in `refs.path` (`[{"feature": id}]`), swept both ways through the part along the sketch normal with the same tool Split uses (D233, construction lines left out), so a seam can step or follow a curve. New faces are named `cut1#k`. Connectors are placed on the flat faces of that cut: each distinct plane among them becomes a cut plane for the existing connector code, so pins, keys, magnets and screws work as before on every straight step. A glue gap is refused in this mode (its slab trim needs an endless plane): an error asks for 0 or At Planes. `key_draft` (optional angle, 0 to 10 degrees, written only when above zero, shown for Dovetail Keys) tapers both the key and its pocket along the slide direction: the bowtie section is full size 1 mm before the part on the slide's negative side and scaled down toward the far side so each side face narrows by the draft (a ruled loft between the two hexagon sections); a draft that would shrink the section below a fifth across the part is an error. Keys slide in from the wide end and wedge. FDEF owner items: `split_for_print` mode value `sketch`, ref `path`, param `key_draft`.

D2003: Nut and bolt, print in place hinge and bin base grid samples (2026-11-07, TR188, Phase 7B Stage 3). Three more samples in `samples/parts_print.py` with tutorials and golden results. **nut_and_bolt**: an M8 x 1.25 bolt (13 mm hexagon head `Flats`, 5.5 mm `Head`, 20 mm shaft with 18 mm of thread) and a separate nut body (`NutHeight` 6.5 mm, hole 7.25 mm) beside it, both threads Thread (modelled) with 0.1 mm clearance in the default ISO form (the `form` param of D782 is not in FDEF_SPEC yet, so a sample may not write it; the tutorial shows switching to Printable). They are a sample of their own rather than bodies on the fit test plate, so the plate's golden result and tutorial stay as they were; the tutorial says to print them as the thread check. The nut hole is 7.25 mm so that it also suits the printable form, whose internal cut needs the hole at least at its crest (major minus 5/4 of the form's depth). STEP reimport of helical faces is a few millionths smaller in volume, so the sample has a golden volume tolerance of 1e-5 (as D394 does for deformed samples). **print_in_place_hinge**: two 35 mm leaves and three 10 mm `Knuckle`s round a 5 mm pin, leaf A holding the outer knuckles and the pin, leaf B a ring with a `Gap` (0.4 mm) all round, kept a separate body with Merge result off; the room, the pin and leaf B are sketched on reference planes offset from Front, since samples must not use the newer extrude start keys (test_old_files). **bin_base_grid**: a 3 by 2 plate of 42 mm `Grid` cells, 5 mm `Base`, each cell a 3 mm pocket `Lip` (1.2 mm) in from its sides. `SketchBuilder` gets `hexagon` (the Polygon tool's six sides on a construction circle sized across the flats, centre placed, one side horizontal, fully defined) and the builder `edge_ref` (the reference of the one edge passing a test). Existing sample files were left unchanged.

D2004: Lattice Fill (2026-11-07, TR390, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `lattice_fill` (3D Print tab, Lattice Fill; body tools form) with params `lattice` (`gyroid` default, `diamond`, `honeycomb`), `cell`, `wall` and optional `skin`, and optional `refs.bodies`. With a skin the body is shrunk by the skin with a joined offset, the lattice is cut to the shrunk body, and the skin (body less shrunk body) is fused back, so the fill is closed; without one the lattice is cut to the body. Gyroid and diamond (Schwarz D) are sheets: `core/lattice_field.py` samples the distance to the periodic surface (its value over its gradient length) less half the wall, joined with the box's distance, on a grid of 8 samples per cell, and finds the zero set by marching tetrahedra (six per cube along the main diagonal, so neighbouring cubes share face diagonals; points shared by grid edge key; triangles faced from the inside corners to the outside ones), all in numpy. The mesh is sewn into faceted solids (one face per triangle; no face merging, which took minutes). This is heavy (a 20 mm cube with 10 mm cells is about 19,000 faces and 8 s of sewing), so the grid is capped at 400,000 cubes and a finer request is an error asking for a larger cell. Honeycomb is exact: a plate with hexagonal holes (flats `cell - wall`, rows offset by half a cell) extruded along Z through the body. The node editor's strut lattice stays as it was. Lattice faces are `<fid>/lattice#k`. FDEF owner items: feature type `lattice_fill` and its params.

D2005: The orientation popup does not block (2026-11-07, Phase 7B Stage 3). With PySide6 6.12, replacing `QMenu.exec` on the class no longer reaches instance calls, so the app sweep's menu stand in did not apply and the view orientation popup (D1601) waited forever on the offscreen screen, hanging `test_every_command_on_a_part`. The popup now opens with `popup()` and deletes itself on close, which behaves the same for the user. Other context menus are opened from mouse events the sweep does not send, so they were left as they are.

D2006: Mark (2026-11-07, TR330, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `mark` (3D Print tab, Mark; body tools form) with `refs.sketch` and an optional `depth` (0 to 5 mm). The marks are the sketch's drawn curves plus the outlines of its text, kept as 3D edges in `extras["marks"]` and drawn in the view as a reference. Depth 0 (the default) leaves the part untouched, so it never blocks sheet metal work (D1100's blocker test sees the same body). Depth above 0 cuts the sketch's closed profile (letters and closed shapes) that deep from the sketch plane along its normal, on whichever side removes material; open lines with a depth are an error asking for 0 or closed shapes. The sheet metal Flat Pattern collects the marks of earlier Mark features whose edges lie on the fixed wall (its top or bottom face in the sheet frame, the wall that stays put when flattened) into `extras["engraving"]`; the flat drawing samples them into segments on a MARKS layer (DXF colour 6, a purple SVG group), kept with the outline in the output options. Marks on bent walls are left out: carrying them would need the unfold transform per wall. FDEF owner items: feature type `mark` with `depth` and `refs.sketch`.

D2007: Timing pulleys and the gear root fillet (2026-11-07, TR348, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sketch, Gear gets the kind **Timing pulley** (`core/sketch/gear.py` `pulley_outline`, 8 to 300 teeth) with a **Belt** choice: GT2, GT3, HTD 3M, HTD 5M (curved teeth) and MXL, XL, T2.5, T5 (trapezoid teeth). The outside diameter is z p / pi less twice the pitch line offset (0.254 for GT2, MXL and XL, 0.381 for the 3 mm belts, 0.5715 for HTD 5M, 0.3 for T2.5, 0.5 for T5); between round lands on it each groove is one arc through both groove edges and the groove bottom for curved tooth belts, or straight flanks (40 degrees included, 50 for XL) to a flat floor for trapezoid belts. Groove depths and widths are the belt tooth sizes of the published belt standards plus about 0.1 mm for printing, written as FDCAD's own table; they suit printed and cut pulleys, and are not gauge profiles. **Root fillet radius** (0 shown as Automatic, enabled with Rounded roots for spur gears) makes a true round root when set: a radial piece from the flank's foot, an arc of that radius tangent to the radial line and the root circle (centre at root radius plus fillet radius, turned asin(r / (root + r)) from the foot), the root arc and the mirror pair; a fillet too wide for the tooth gap is an error. Automatic keeps D866's spline rounding, so existing outlines do not change. `Piece` gets `clockwise` for arcs traversed against the sketch arc direction.

D2008: Hinge (2026-11-07, TR404, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `hinge` (3D Print tab, Hinge; body tools form): pick a straight edge where two bodies meet (`refs.edge`); the axis runs along it. The edge's body (the solid within 1e-6 of the edge) takes knuckles 1, 3, 5 ..., the first other solid within 1e-3 takes 2, 4 .... Params: `knuckles` (2 to 15, default 3), `knuckle_diameter`, `clearance` (default 0.3, the axial gap between knuckles and the radial room round the other body's knuckles), `form` (`pin` or `print_in_place`), `pin_diameter` (pin: one hole right through, smaller than the knuckle less 1 mm), `pin_cone_angle` (print in place: cones of base radius 0.55 of the knuckle radius on the first body's knuckle ends, sides at this angle from the axis, 20 to 70 degrees, default 45; matching sockets 1.5 clearances larger cut into the other body's knuckles) and `detents` (a 0.6 mm bump on each knuckle end of the first body clicking into a dimple half a clearance larger). The spec asks the cone angle to follow the printer's overhang limit: the core cannot read the printer profile, so the form defaults to 45 degrees and the tip says to use the printer's limit. Each body is built by a chain of booleans; tools that touch or overlap each other are given in separate steps, because the kernel joins tools only to the body, not to each other (a cone and a bump in one fuse stayed separate solids). Knuckle faces are `<fid>/knuckle#k`. FDEF owner items: feature type `hinge` and its params.
D2100: Design table description, colour and property columns (2026-11-07, TR90 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Three new kinds of design table column. `config.description` is stored as an optional `description` text in the configuration's entry (kept on save like any other extra key of an entry) and shows as the tooltip of the configuration in the configurations panel. `part.color` is a configured path like a feature value: its live value is `appearance.part_color`, so switching configurations, Change in This Configuration, the design table and saving all work unchanged; cells must be # and six (or eight) hex digits and are stored in capitals; the path is never treated as a deleted owner. `prop.<name>` is a custom property (TR82): its cell is the property text in that configuration, written to the row's per configuration values (`configs`) and dropped there when it equals the shared value. Description and property columns are not configured values, so they never enter `overrides`; an empty cell keeps the text as it is. The design table's undo step now also keeps the part's appearance and custom properties. The last part of item 1, a configuration made from a parent so it starts with the parent's values, is already there: Add Configuration copies the active configuration and Add Linked Configuration (TR195, D868) follows it. Owner note: `description` in a configuration entry and the `part.color` and `prop.` column paths are new FDEF additions for FDEF_SPEC section 9.

D2101: More values per configuration (2026-11-07, TR197, Phase 7B Stage 3). Three new configured paths in `core/configurations.py`. `<sketch id>.plane` reads and writes the sketch's `refs.plane` (only when the sketch has no parameter of that name); in the design table its cell is the name of a plane feature, matched without regard to case, and a face reference shows as "(face)", which applying leaves as it is. `<sketch id>.<dimension id>:driving` reads and writes the dimension's `driving` flag (true or false in the table; `:off` paths now read as tick box columns too). `part.colors` holds the face, feature and body colour maps of `appearance` as one value (`part_color` stays its own path, D2100); it is not a table column, since a face name map is not typed text. It is turned on and off with Colours by Configuration in the configurations panel (`core/config_preview.set_colours_vary`, one undo step): on gives every configuration the current colours, and from then on switching stores the live colours in the configuration being left, so colours picked while a configuration is shown stay with it; off makes them shared again with the colours shown. Item 2: Preview in the configurations panel builds the selected configuration on a deep copy in the background (`core/config_preview.build`, the same way Export Configurations does) and shows it in a small non modal window with its own 3D view and the configuration's part colour, with the number of failed features; the part and its active configuration do not change. Owner note: the three paths are FDEF additions for FDEF_SPEC section 9 item 2.

D2102: Variables read from a CSV table (2026-11-07, TR198 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). D966 left open where the file lives and when it is read. Answer: the same as a linked equations file (TR25, D749). A variable gets an optional `lookup = {file, row, column}` (saved in the variable only when set). The file is read when Read from CSV... sets it, when the part opens and on Rebuild (`DocumentSession.read_linked_equations` now also calls `read_csv_lookups`, so the window needed no change); evaluation never reads a file, and the value read last is the variable's typed value, saved in the part, so the part opens and rebuilds without the file. The path is resolved like the equations link: the stored path, or a file of the same name next to the part. The row is a label in the first column (ignoring case) or, when no label matches and the text is a whole number, its position from 1 under the header; the column is a header (ignoring case). The cell is worked out as a typed value of the variable's kind, so `10mm` or `0.5in` work. CSV reading follows the design table's rules (comma, or semicolon or tab when the header has no comma, an optional byte order mark) and refuses files over 5 MB. A file that cannot be read leaves the variable's last value and the status line names it. Changed values are one undo step (Read CSV Values). Typing another value for the variable in the manager drops the lookup. Variable rename and unit change now copy variables with `dataclasses.replace`, so `allowed` (TR274) and `lookup` are no longer dropped there. Owner note: `lookup` in a variable is an FDEF addition for FDEF_SPEC section 4.

D2103: Configuration rules, themes and trial values (2026-11-07, TR331, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/config_rules.py`. Rules are stored in the configurations block as `rules`, in order: `{if, test, value, then, choices, off}`, where `if` and `then` are configured value paths (D391), `test` is one of > >= < <= = !=, `value` and each choice are typed table text (parsed like design table cells, so units, S or U and plane names work). A rule holds when the `if` value passes the test; it is met when the `then` value equals a choice (numbers within a relative 1e-9, text ignoring case). Applying sets an unmet value to the first choice; rules run top to bottom on the live values, so later rules see earlier changes; `off` rules are skipped. "Apply wherever the value is edited" is met this way: every rebuild lists unmet rules after the allowed value warnings (TR274, `allowed.problems`), so an edit anywhere is checked and the status line names the rule; values change only when the user applies the design table (rules run in every configuration after the cells are set) or clicks Apply Rules (one undo step), since CLAUDE.md 5.12 forbids changing the part without the user's action and a hidden change after each edit would also break undo and redo. Item 2: themes are stored as `themes` (name to {path: typed text}); the design table gets a `config.theme` column kept in each configuration entry's `theme`; on apply a row's empty cells are filled from its theme (name matched ignoring case), cells typed in the row win, and a column is added to the table for every value a used theme sets, so the table shows what the theme did. Item 3: Try Row puts the current row's cells (theme filled, rules run) into a deep copy and builds it in the TR197 preview window; nothing is added to the part. Rules and themes are edited in Rules and Themes..., one undo step, with each rule and theme value checked before it is stored. Owner note: `rules` and `themes` in the configurations block and `theme` in a configuration entry are FDEF additions for FDEF_SPEC section 9.

D2104: Text and yes or no variables, and groups (2026-11-07, TR417, Phase 7B Stage 3). `Variable` gets `type` ("" for a number as before, "text" or "yes_no") and `group`, both saved only when set (`core/equations/variable_types.py`). No new unit kind was added, so every formula, unit and number display path stays as it was. A yes or no variable has kind Number and value 1 or 0: its typed value is yes, no, true, false (any case, also y, n, on, off), which the solver reads as 1 or 0, or a formula (a comparison gives 1 or 0); formulas and tick box formulas (TR275) use it as a number. A new manager row typed as such a word becomes yes or no by itself; other types are chosen with Type... (Number, Text, Yes or No). A text variable keeps its text in `expr`, is left out of the solved cells, so it is not a formula name and never shows an error, and its value stays 0. Sketch text fields (TR54) show a text variable's text and Yes or No for a yes or no variable. Configured values: `var.<name>` of a text variable is a text design table column and of a yes or no variable a tick box column; writing a boolean stores yes or no. The note per variable already exists (the manager's Comment). Groups: Group... sets the group of the chosen variables; the manager lists a group's variables together, ungrouped first, shows the group in the name's tooltip, and its filter matches group names; the order of the saved list does not change. Not built: a text variable used inside a configuration name (configuration names are typed names, D391, and a name that changes with a value would break design table rows and links). Owner note: variable `type` and `group` are FDEF additions for FDEF_SPEC section 4.

D2105: Named faces and edges (2026-11-07, TR152, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/named_items.py`. Names live in the part's tree block (`tree.named_items`, a list of `{name, kind, ref}`), which already keeps unknown keys, so no new top level key; `ref` is the lasting reference features store (`naming.select.reference_for`), so a name follows its face or edge through rebuilds the way a feature's picks do. Faces and edges only: bodies already have names (TR183, D1201), and the list shows them too. Names follow the custom property rule (a letter, then letters, digits, spaces and underscores), are unique ignoring case, and naming an item that has a name renames it. Changes are one undo step (SetTreeInfo) and ask for a rebuild. After each rebuild, when the part has custom properties, the named items are measured into `Document.measured` (`__named__`, never saved): `area@<name>` (mm2) for a face and `length@<name>` (mm) for an edge; custom property formulas read them like `volume@Part`. Feature formulas cannot, since the values come from the finished part and would loop (the same reason as D810); a Measurement feature (D818) remains the way to drive features from geometry. Node editor: Use Selection on a named face or edge stores `{"named": name}` in the Model Reference, and the graph environment carries the named references (`GraphEnv.named`), so the node follows the name. Tools, Named Items is a non modal list; clicking a name picks the item in the 3D view; Rename and Remove Name. Owner note: `named_items` in the tree block is an FDEF addition for FDEF_SPEC section 2 item 15; the node editor `ref` may now be `{"named": name}` (section 12A).

D2106: Body folders (2026-11-07, TR153 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/body_folders.py`. A body's folder is kept in the print setup under `body_folders`: a face name of the body (its mark) to the folder name, the same lasting way as body names (D1201) and hidden bodies (D410), so a body stays in its folder when bodies are numbered again; a body is in at most one folder and a folder exists while it holds a body (no empty folders are kept). In the tree a folder row sits inside Solid Bodies and takes its bodies before the Identical Bodies grouping (TR308) applies. Body row: Move to Folder... (a new or existing name; empty takes the body out). Folder row: Hide Bodies and Show Bodies (one hidden bodies step), Colour... (the body colours of all its bodies, one appearance step), Delete Bodies (adds one Delete Body feature, D233, with one face reference per body, so the bodies come back by Undo or by deleting the feature; nothing is removed without a feature), Rename Folder... and Remove Folder (bodies go back to Solid Bodies). Owner note: `body_folders` in the print setup is an FDEF addition next to `body_titles`.

D2107: Move a feature to another body (2026-11-07, TR155, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/move_to_body.py`. Moving uses the Bodies box of TR33 (D697) instead of a new mechanism: the feature's `bodies_scope` becomes "selected" and `refs.bodies` one face reference of the chosen body, taken from the part just before the feature, so the feature cuts or joins that body only and the others are added back unchanged. Offered on the feature row's right click menu (Move to Body..., a list of the bodies by their names, D1201) for the types that have the Bodies box (extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, hole) when the part has two or more bodies before the feature; one undo step (ReplaceFeature). The feature's sketch is not changed: it stays on its plane and keeps its shape, so "with its sketch" means the sketch goes on driving the moved feature; a sketch drawn on a face of the old body keeps that face, and Edit Sketch Plane moves it when the user wants. The feature's place in the tree does not change, since the bodies it may act on are those that exist above it. No new keys.

D2108: Seed and boundary pick (2026-11-07, TR328, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/seed_pick.faces_between`. The picks already made are the boundary, faces or edges; the face right clicked is the seed (the menu item Select Faces Between shows on a face when something else is picked). From the seed the pick spreads across shared edges to every face it reaches, never across a boundary edge and never into a boundary face; boundary faces are not picked. It is a topology walk on the last rebuilt shape (no geometry), like Select Tangent (TR92), and the result replaces the selection, so Fillet, Delete Face and the other tools use it as it stands. When the boundary does not close the region the walk reaches the rest of the part, which the count in the status line shows. No new keys.

D2109: Partial success for tools with many picks (2026-11-07, TR400, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/features/partial.py`. Delete Face already tries each face when several fail together and offers Keep the faces that worked (drop_refs). Move Face now does the same: when the whole move fails without a fix of its own, each picked face is moved alone (2 to 12 faces; each try is a whole build) and, when some but not all fail, the error names and highlights them with the same drop_refs fix. Hole: when cutting all holes in one boolean fails and the holes come from an existing sketch, each hole is cut alone and the error says how many fail, with Cut the holes that work (skip N), a new fix action skip_points that adds those points to the hole's skipped points (TR143, D1520), so clicking a skipped point in the panel brings it back; holes on the hole's own points have no skip list, so they get the old error. Nothing changes until the user clicks a fix, as with Fillet's skip button (CLAUDE.md 5.12). No new keys.

D2110: Extrude picks the operation (2026-11-07, TR334, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/features/extrude_auto.py`. New extrude params `auto_operation` and `auto_alternate` (booleans, saved only when ticked). With Pick operation from where it sits, every rebuild first builds the extrusion as a boss and measures it against the part: more than half of its volume inside the part is a cut; any part of it inside, or touching within 1e-4 mm, is a boss joined to the part; apart from the part (or with no part yet) is a new body (a boss with Merge result off). Alternate solution takes the second choice: cut to boss, boss to cut, new body to cut. The choice is made at build time, so it follows changes above, and the stored `operation` stays what the user last chose, so the tree icon, Switch to Cut (TR387) and names do not change behind the user's back; the result carries `extras.operation` and the panel shows "Chosen: Cut". The probe build costs one extra extrusion only while the option is on. Revolve does not get it (the spec names Extrude). Owner note: `auto_operation` and `auto_alternate` are FDEF additions for the extrude section.

D2111: Mould Cavity (2026-11-07, TR85, Phase 7B Stage 3). Feature type `mould_cavity` (`core/features/mould_cavity.py`): refs `main` (the block, a face reference of the body) and `part` (the part body), optional `coord_system` (`{"feature": id}`); params `uniform` with `factor` or `fx`, `fy`, `fz` (numbers, 0.5 to 2, default 1.02 in the panel), `about` ("centroid" of the part, "origin" or "coord_system", its origin) and `keep_part` (default true). The part is copied, scaled with one general transform about the centre (uniform or per axis, as Scale does, D235) and cut from the block with the named boolean, so the cavity faces carry the part's face names; the other bodies stay. Item 2, a tooling split with a flat parting plane, is left to Split (D233), which already splits a body with a plane; the guide says so. Owner note: the `mould_cavity` feature type is an FDEF addition.

D2112: Rib draft at the wall and Wrap pull direction (2026-11-07, TR75 items 1 and 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Rib gets `draft_at` ("sketch", the default and left out of the file, or "wall"). With "wall" the draft's neutral plane is moved from the sketch plane to where the rib's middle first meets the part (a line from the middle of the sketch line along the growth direction), so the rib is the typed thickness there and thicker toward the sketch; the prism is cut where an inward draft would close past the wall, and the 'draft closes before the part' check does not apply. The spec's Next Reference, which side the draft starts from, is this choice. (2) Wrap gets `refs.pull`: a line, edge or plane (resolved like Extrude's direction, TR239). On a flat face the wrapped face is swept along it until it is the thickness away from the face, so the volume stays the same and the walls lean. On a cylinder the face is swept along it a short way (at most 0.9 of the radius plus the thickness, so it never reaches the far side) and cut to the shell between the cylinder and the cylinder grown or shrunk by the thickness. A direction along the face is refused. Not with Scribe or the Spline method. Item 3 (a single line font) is not done: FDCAD has no stroke font of its own yet and drawing one is a separate piece of work. Owner note: rib `draft_at` and wrap `refs.pull` are FDEF additions.

D2113: Project a sketch onto any face (2026-11-07, TR156, Phase 7B Stage 3). A third Wrap method, `method` "project" (`core/features/wrap_project.py`), rather than a new feature type, since Wrap already has the sketch, face, emboss and deboss and the pull direction (D2112). The sketch regions are swept along the pull direction, or the sketch plane's normal without one, right through the part; the picked face is made into a slab of the height (a simple thick solid of the face, on the outside for emboss and the inside for deboss, chosen by which side its centre falls), and the sweeps are cut to the slab, then joined to or cut from the part. So the shape follows any face, the sketch need not touch it, and the walls run along the direction; lengths are not kept on curved faces (it is a shadow), which the guide says. Scribe is refused with this method. Owner note: the method value "project" is an FDEF addition for the wrap section.

D2114: Rib network (2026-11-07, TR285, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/features/rib_network.py`. Rib's sketch may now hold several open chains: curves that join end to end form a chain, and a group whose curves branch (three or more ends at one point) is split into its single curves, so a T or a star makes one wall per line. Each chain is built as a rib with the feature's own settings (each grows to the part on its own) and the walls are joined with one another and then with the part, so crossing and touching walls become one network. A sketch with one chain builds exactly as before. Draft still needs one straight line per wall. No new keys.

D2115: Library feature files (2026-11-07, TR72 item 1 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). `core/io/library.py`. A library feature file (`.fdlib`, JSON: format, version 1, name, feature, sketch) holds exactly what Copy puts on the clipboard (TR9, D685): a sketch, or one feature made from a sketch with its sketch. Save as Library Feature... on the tree row writes it; Tools, Insert Library Feature reads it as data only (size limited, features checked like a part file) and pastes it through the Copy and Paste path as from another part (D708): onto the selected plane or flat face or one picked, centred on a face, with face picks cleared and formulas made plain values, as one undo step. Not done yet: one file holding several features, asking for each face the saved feature was attached to, hiding internal dimensions, and item 3 (a link to the library file, or dissolving it); they need a placement model beyond paste. Owner note: the `.fdlib` file format is new (FDEF_SPEC has no section for it yet).

D2009: Face Seats (2026-11-07, TR405, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `face_seats` (3D Print tab, Face Seats; body tools form) with `refs.on_face` (the face to cover) and `refs.seed` (a face of a separate seed body, modelled at the origin with +Z out of the face it sits on), and params `count_u`, `count_v` (1 to 100 each), optional `sink` and `operation` (`boss` or `cut`). The spots are the middles of a count_u by count_v grid over the face's parameter range, kept where the face classifier says the spot is on the face (so trimmed faces and spheres' poles work). At each spot the seed's origin goes to the point moved `sink` inward, +Z to the outward normal (the surface normal, reversed on reversed faces) and +X to the face's first direction made square to the normal. The seed body is used up; all copies are joined or cut in one boolean (they do not overlap each other when the grid is coarser than the seed). The spec says it extends TR398 (pattern suppress regions): a picked region is not taken here; the counts and the face's own extent bound the copies. Cut faces are `<fid>/seat#k`. FDEF owner items: feature type `face_seats` and its params and refs.

D2010: Transition spiral (2026-11-07, TR408 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A curve feature `transition_spiral` (Reference Curves group; body tools form) with `refs.sketch` (a sketch with exactly one drawn line), `spiral_length`, `end_radius` and `hand` (`left` default, `right`). It is a clothoid: curvature s / (R L), heading s^2 / (2 R L); the points come from summing the heading's cosine and sine over 4000 steps with numpy, and a C2 spline (GeomAPI_PointsToBSpline, 1e-6) goes through 41 of them. It starts at the line's second point along the line, in the sketch plane, and is kept in `extras["curve"]` like the other curves, so Sweep can use it. A length over four times the radius (a turn past two right angles) is refused. Items 2 (stone seats and prongs) and 3 (sprue trees and kit frames) are not built in this round. FDEF owner items: feature type `transition_spiral` and its params.

D2011: Edge Profile (2026-11-07, TR243, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `edge_profile` (3D Print tab, Edge Profile; body tools form) with `refs.loop_face` (a flat face: its outer wire is the path) or `refs.edges` (a chain joined into one wire), and params `router_profile` (`round_over` default, `cove`, `rabbet`, `chamfer_flat`, `ogee`), `profile_size` and optional `profile_depth` (rabbet and chamfer with flat; the size when left out). The section is drawn at the path's start (the first edge of the wire in order and its oriented start vertex) in the corner between the face and the side face: u into the material away from the side, v into it away from the face, both from the faces' normals, reaching 0.05 mm past both faces so the cut is clean; arcs are exact (round over: the square less a quarter circle about the far corner; cove: a quarter circle about the edge; ogee: a hollow then a round of half the size each). It is swept with a pipe shell that keeps the face normal as binormal and round corner transitions, made solid and cut in one boolean. The start must be between flat faces; picked edges use the first edge's first face as the face. Presets only: any closed sketch as a profile, and the addition mode, are not built (a sketch profile needs placing rules the spec leaves open). Faces of the cut are `<fid>/profile#k`. FDEF owner items: feature type `edge_profile` and its params and refs.

D2012: Lightening Pockets (2026-11-07, TR245, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `lightening_pockets` (3D Print tab; body tools form) with `refs.plate_face` (a flat face) and params `border`, `web`, `cell`, optional `corner_radius` and `pocket_depth` (0 or left out: through). The face is offset inward by the border with a 2D face offset (round joins), which also grows its holes by the border, so one width keeps both the edge and rings round holes. Rib strips `web` wide cross it in three directions 60 degrees apart at a row pitch of cell times sqrt(3) / 2 through the face's centre, giving equilateral triangle pockets of side about `cell`; the pockets are the offset face less the ribs. A corner radius shrinks each pocket by the radius and grows it back (round joins), which rounds convex corners and drops pockets too small for it; pockets under web squared in area are dropped. The pockets are pushed along the inward normal by the depth (or through) from 0.01 mm above the face and cut in one boolean. Keep regions drawn by the user and free shaped pockets (the spec's "free shapes") are not built: the border and hole rings are the keep regions. Pocket faces are `<fid>/pocket#k`. FDEF owner items: feature type `lightening_pockets` and its params.

D2013: Landing Pad (2026-11-07, TR325, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `landing_pad` (3D Print tab; body tools form) with `refs.wall_face` and `refs.sketch` (a closed outline; its plane is the pad's flat face, normal out of the wall), and params `pad_mode` (`raise` default or `press`) and optional `cup_wall`. Raise: the outline is pushed from its plane into the part, the part is taken away from it, and the pieces of what is left that reach the sketch plane and touch the wall are joined on: that is the space between the wall and the flat, and never the inside of a hollow housing or the far side. Press: the outline pushed outward from its plane is cut away; with a cup wall, first the outline grown by the wall (2D offset, round joins) is pushed from one wall behind the plane outward, the outside air pieces of it (those reaching its far end) are taken off, and the rest (the cup inside the wall and the cavity) is joined, so a thin wall stays closed round the sunk pad. Sweeping the wall face itself to find the space beside it was tried and dropped: a closed curved face swept along a direction folds over itself. The spec's own clearance, draft and extent to a face are not built: the sketch plane sets the extent, and a draft would need a drafted prism of any outline. New faces are `<fid>/pad#k`. FDEF owner items: feature type `landing_pad` and its params and refs.

D2014: Joint helpers (2026-11-07, TR401, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `joint_helper` (3D Print tab, Joint; body tools form) with `refs.bodies` (exactly two: the body cut into first, then the body that goes in) and params `joint` (`groove` default, `rabbet`, `mortise`, `dowels`), `depth`, optional `joint_clearance` (default 0.2), `shoulder` (mortise) and `dowel_diameter` (dowels). The contact is the largest common patch of two flat faces, one of each body, with opposite normals in one plane; the direction into the first body is the second body's face normal. Groove and rabbet are the same cut (the second body's whole contact patch pushed the depth into the first, which gets a pocket the clearance larger all round and deeper); a rabbet is what that gives when the patch reaches the first body's edge. Mortise: the patch shrunk by the shoulder (2D offset) is the tenon, the mortise is the tenon grown by the clearance. Dowels: two holes the clearance larger, the depth into each body, at a quarter of the patch's length from its centre along its long axis (refused when shorter than three diameters). The lower priority kinds (biscuit, pocket hole, mitre spline, scarf) are not built. New faces are `<fid>/joint#k`. FDEF owner items: feature type `joint_helper` and its params.

D2015: Knurl (2026-11-07, TR163 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A feature `knurl` (3D Print tab; body tools form) with `refs.round_face` (a cylindrical face) and params `knurl_pattern` (`straight` default or `diamond`), `knurl_pitch` and `knurl_depth` (under half the radius). The groove count is the circumference over the pitch, rounded, 3 to 180. Straight: V grooves along the axis, each a triangle (the pitch's angle wide at 0.2 mm outside the face, the depth inside it) pushed past both ends of the face. Diamond: two sets of V grooves on 30 degree helices, right and left hand, swept with the modelled thread's helical sweep (D315); each groove's section in the axial plane is as wide as the axial spacing of one set, so neighbouring grooves meet and leave full pyramids. Each set is cut in its own boolean, since crossing tools in one compound are not all cut. A diamond knurl on a 16 mm cylinder at 2 mm pitch takes some seconds. Item 2 (texture from an image) is not built: the spec leaves whether it fits to the owner. Groove faces are `<fid>/knurl#k`. FDEF owner items: feature type `knurl` and its params.

D2016: Safe graphics (2026-11-07, TR219, Phase 7B Stage 3). `ui/safe_graphics.py` decides before the QApplication exists whether to draw in software: the `--safe-graphics` argument, `FDCAD_SAFE_GRAPHICS=1`, the Preferences tick **Safe graphics (draw in software)** (General page, QSettings `view/safe_graphics`, from the next start), or a start marker (`starting.marker` in the data folder, written before Qt starts and removed once the window shows) left by a start that never showed its window. Software drawing sets Qt's AA_UseSoftwareOpenGL and QT_OPENGL=software (Qt's bundled software OpenGL on Windows) and asks Mesa for llvmpipe (LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE, GALLIUM_DRIVER) where Mesa is the driver. The status bar says why it is on. The internal error message ends with how to turn it on, which is the spec's link from the crash message. Whether VTK's own window follows Qt's software OpenGL on Windows is not verified here (no Windows in this session): the owner should try it on a machine without a working driver.

D2017: Describe Part and Large controls (2026-11-07, TR294 items 2 and 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). The main widgets already carry accessible names (strings_a11y, earlier rounds). View, **Describe Part** (`view.describe_part`, no default key) shows a message box, which screen readers read, with the part's name, the number of bodies, the overall size from the exact bounding box, and the features after the origin and default planes in order, each with ", suppressed" or its state when not OK (`ui/accessibility.py`, no kernel work beyond a bounding box of the current result). **Large controls** (Preferences, General; QSettings `view/large_controls`) scales the command tab button icon sizes by 1.5 (`ribbon.set_scale`, read when buttons are made and applied to existing ones when the preference changes) and the tree row icons, which sets the row height. Live screen reader change events from the 3D view and sketch editor (the spec's "report state and changes") are not added: Qt only sends them for its own item views, and the view's picks would need a custom accessible interface.

D2018: Hints, panel help and What's New (2026-11-07, TR291 items 1 and 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Every property panel header gets a **?** button that opens the guide at the tool's section (the existing Help for This Tool lookup, D1002). The first time each feature type's panel opens, a one line hint (the command's tooltip text) shows above its groups with a **Show Me** link (the same guide lookup) and **Turn off hints**; seen types and the switch are QSettings `help/hints_seen` and `help/hints_off` (`ui/help/hints.py`, with a reset helper for a later Preferences button). Help, **What's New** shows the first two version sections of CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased and the last release) in a text browser; the installer now ships CHANGELOG.md beside the license files. Item 2, first run lessons that check the result step by step, is not built in this round: it needs a lesson format and checks per step.

D2019: Before and After (2026-11-07, TR289, Phase 7B Stage 3). The session keeps the report before the last rebuild (`previous_report`, dropped when the part closes). This holds one more set of feature results; it is the price of showing the old shape, and is released at the next rebuild. View, **Before and After** (`view.before_after`, no default key) opens a non modal window listing, in tree order, the features whose part volume changed (`core/rebuild_compare.py`): only results that are new objects are measured, since the rebuild cache hands back the same object for features it did not rebuild, and changes under 1e-6 relative are left out. Clicking a row draws that feature's part from before the change as a faint shaded overlay layer (`before_after`); closing the window clears it. The spec says the list shows after a value change; it opens on the command instead, so it does not cover the view after every edit.

D2020: Shortcuts by key position and through input methods (2026-11-07, TR354, Phase 7B Stage 3). An app event filter (`ui/input/key_position.py`) looks at key presses without modifiers outside text boxes whose text is a non Latin letter: the Latin letter on the same key comes from the layout independent key code (Windows virtual key codes A to Z, Apple's ANSI key codes from Events.h, X11 key codes of a US layout) and that letter's shortcut runs (`CommandActions.trigger_key`). Input method events outside text boxes whose commit or composition text is one Latin letter, full width forms included (NFKC), run that letter's shortcut; any other composition shows "single letter shortcuts are paused" in the status bar. Shortcuts stay stored as letters; binding a shortcut to a key position in the shortcut editor (rather than this automatic fallback) is not added, since the fallback covers the same need without a new key format. Not tried here with a real input method (no desktop in this session).

D1900: Values of one copy (2026-11-07, TR59 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Every pattern of features gets instance_values (an FDEF owner item), text such as "3: depth 8; 2.2: depth 4, draft_angle 2": an instance number (i or i.j, as in Skip), a colon and value names of the seed feature with the value that copy uses (mm, or degrees for angles by the seed type's kind_of). The value replaces the seed's value and any Vary step for that copy only; the copy is built again from a copy of the seed like a varied copy (D1513). Instance 1 is the seed and is refused with a next step, as are unreadable text, a value the seed does not have, and Geometry pattern or face and body seeds. The values are typed in Copy values next to Vary values, because the view has no instance markers to click yet; clicking a marker to fill the field is not done. A negative increment (D1513) and a negative Vary step already run the other way (gaps close up, values shrink), which a test now covers. Vary Sketch (item 4, low priority: copies re-solving their sketch against the faces they land on) is not done: it needs the sketch solver run per copy against moved geometry, which the pattern engine does not do.

D1901: Pattern Chain (2026-11-07, TR141 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type pattern_chain (an FDEF owner item, with its params steps, spacing, instances, reverse, turns, angle, reverse_turn, scales, factor and refs direction, axis, plane, centre) runs pattern steps in the order of the text steps, such as "mirror, linear, circular, scale": each step's copies feed the next, so the copies are every combination of one move from each step, the later steps applied after the earlier ones. The order is changed by retyping the list, a plain text field like Vary, because the panel has no reorderable list widget; each kind of step is used at most once, so its fields need no step number, and the panel shows only the fields of the steps listed. Linear moves by a spacing along a direction; Circular turns by a total angle shared by its instances (360 degrees or more spreads them evenly round, so no instance lands on the seed); Mirror adds the mirror image; Scale makes each copy factor times the size of the one before about a point (the origin when none is picked), a gp_Trsf scale moved like any other copy. Instances are numbered (n, 1) with the first step counting fastest, so Skip, Copy values (D1900) and Vary work as in a Linear Pattern. Every copy goes through the shared engine (apply_pattern, one boolean per seed), so feature, face and body seeds, Suppress Region, Check and Geometry pattern all work, and a chain can be the seed of a later pattern (NESTED_TYPES, D1512). More than 1000 instances is a feature error with a next step.

D1902: Explode Pattern (2026-11-07, TR270 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). The feature tree menu of a Linear, Circular, Sketch, Table or Point Pattern or a Pattern Chain gets Explode Pattern (core/features/pattern_explode.py, no Qt): the pattern is replaced, in one undo step, by one feature per copy it makes now (skipped and Suppress Region copies left out), each a copy of the pattern with the new key only (an [i, j] pair, an FDEF owner item) and the name '<pattern> copy <i>'. A pattern with only builds just that instance, so each copy can be edited, suppressed or deleted alone and given its own values with Copy values (D1900); the seed feature stays as it was. The first copy keeps the pattern's id, so features that use faces of that copy keep them; faces of the other copies get the new ids, so features on those faces need their picks redone. If later values no longer make the kept instance, the copy warns and leaves the part unchanged. A copy itself cannot be exploded again. Mirror and Fill Pattern are not offered: their copies are not numbered instances of one placement list in the same way. Hiding copies in the view only (item 2 rest) and skipping by a box over instance markers (item 3) are not done: the view has no instance markers, and the copies of one pattern are faces of one solid, which the viewport draws as one shape.

D1903: Fill Pattern on a cylinder face (2026-11-07, TR398 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Fill Pattern takes a cylinder face as well as a flat one, with surface_spacing (an FDEF owner item): "mapped" (default) lays the layout out on the face unrolled, so the spacing round the face is measured along the surface, and "projected" lays it out in the plane touching the face at the start point, so the spacing is as seen from straight on (copies thin out toward the sides, and none go past the outline). The layout's v runs along the axis and u round it from the start point (the picked point, else the middle of the face's parameter range); the Direction pick is not used on a round face. Copies are rigid turns about the axis plus slides along it, so copied features and cut shapes stay square to the surface; cut shapes are built once at the start and turned into place, cut from outside in to the axis (an outside face, so a tube is cut through one wall only) or from the axis plane outward (an inside face, a bore). Fit tests reuse the flat code on the unrolled boundary; a whole cylinder's seam counts on both sides. Only cylinders are taken: other curved faces (cones, spheres, free form) are a feature error with a next step, since they cannot be unrolled exactly, and Curve and Point Patterns already follow their curve or points, so the item's option applies to Fill Pattern only.

D1904: Add to Pattern and Follow Pattern (2026-11-07, TR399 items 1 and 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type follow_pattern (an FDEF owner item, with refs.pattern, the seed refs and the key on, the [i, j] copy its seed was built on) repeats its seed at every copy of an earlier Linear, Circular, Sketch, Table or Point Pattern or Pattern Chain. Each rebuild reads that pattern's copies (its skips, Suppress Region and an exploded copy's only, D1902, included), so a change of count or layout carries over (item 2). The seed may sit on any copy: each copy m gets the move T_m T_on^-1, the original counting as T = identity, and the copy the seed sits on is left out; if the pattern no longer makes that copy, it is a feature error with a next step. The feature tree menu of a feature built on a pattern copy (a face, edge or vertex of <pattern>/instance<i>.<j>/ in its refs or its sketch's refs) or on a pattern's seed gets Add to Pattern (item 1), which adds a Follow Pattern just below it in one undo step, with Geometry pattern on when the seed neither adds nor cuts (a chamfer or fillet, whose faces are copied). The followed pattern is set by the command and not shown in the panel, which edits the seed, skips and options like the other patterns. A Follow Pattern can itself be the seed of a later pattern (NESTED_TYPES). Following is offered, not automatic: a feature built on a copy stays a single feature until the user picks Add to Pattern, so nothing changes geometry unasked.

D1905: Sweep start tangency and merged side faces (2026-11-07, TR56 items 1 and 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep gets start_tangency (an FDEF owner item): "none" (default, as before: the profile is swept as drawn, so a path leaving the sketch plane at a slant gives a slanted, smaller section) or "path_tangent" (the kernel's section correction turns the profile square to the path's start tangent, so the section is the full profile all along and the end cap is square to the path too, which is why there is no separate end choice). Tangent to Adjacent Faces is not built: the pipe shell has no mode that blends a section into neighbouring faces, and faking it with a fillet would change geometry the user did not pick. merge_faces (an FDEF owner item, Merge tangent faces) sweeps a path of several pieces whose joints all turn by less than 0.001 rad as one spline (the pieces converted and joined end to end), so each profile edge makes one side face, named side/<entity> with no #k; a path with a sharp corner or a single piece keeps its faces and warns with a next step. Guided and scaled sweeps build their own way and ignore both.

D1906: Profile part way along a sweep path (2026-11-07, TR137 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch or face profile no longer needs the path to start on its plane: when neither end is there, the path is cut where it first crosses the plane (each edge intersected with the plane, the crossing edge split in two), and sweep_direction (an FDEF owner item) picks "forward" (default, the part after the crossing, along the path), "backward" (the part before it, run away from the plane) or "both". Both sweeps each part from the profile and fuses them into one solid; the backward side's faces are named back/side/<entity> and back/cap/end, and twist_angle2 or twist_turns2 (FDEF owner items) give it its own twist, else it takes the first side's. A profile at an end of the path sweeps along it as before, whatever the direction. Both ways is refused with guides or scales (they build their own way along one run), and a path that never meets the plane is a feature error with a next step. Several profiles along one path (item 2) is not done.

D1907: Sweep through several profiles (2026-11-07, TR137 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep gets refs.profiles (an FDEF owner item), later sketches along the path, each with one closed region whose plane the path passes through (sampled at 65 points along the path, the nearest within one sample step or 1 mm). Their outlines are sorted by where they sit along the path and added to the same pipe shell as the first profile, which blends the section smoothly from one to the next and through to the last. The first profile must be one closed region without holes (a pipe shell blends single outlines), the extra profiles are not used by guided or scaled sweeps, and a both ways sweep (D1906) refuses them. Side faces keep the first profile's entity names. The panel gets a More Profiles group: a list, a sketch chooser and Add.

D1908: Loft profiles from model edges (2026-11-07, TR138 item 1 rest, Phase 7B Stage 3). A loft profile can be {"kind": "loop", "edges": [edge references]} (an FDEF owner item): the edges are joined end to end into one wire that must be closed and lie flat (its plane, found by the kernel, gives the profile normal for Normal constraints). In the Loft panel, edges picked together in the view (Pick Edges as Guides off) become one loop profile, listed as Edge loop of <feature>, in the order picked among the other profiles. Side faces are named from the first sketch profile's curves as before; a loop has no sketch entities. The group picker that joins pieces of several sketches and edges with trim and extend (item 2) and a cut by a solid tool body moved along a path (item 3) are not done: the first needs a new chain editing widget, and the kernel has no sweep of a solid, so a tool body would have to be approximated by many copies, which leaves scallops in the cut.

D1909: Show Sections (2026-11-07, TR139 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep and Loft get show_section (a whole number, an FDEF owner item; 0 or absent shows none): section k of 11, evenly spaced from the start (1) to the end (11), is drawn as reference geometry (extras reference) with a report line such as "Section 4 of 11, 30% along the path." A sweep's section is its profile's outlines carried along the path with the least turning (the guided sweep's stations and double reflection frames), worked out without the kernel's sweep, so it shows even when the sweep fails: then the result keeps the error and the part before it, with the section. Twist and the other orientations are not applied to the shown section, which is the path's own frame. A loft's section is a slice of the built loft by the plane square to the line from its first profile's centre to its last, at that share of the way; a failed loft shows none. The panel gets a Show section field in the options of both; it is stored only when above 0. Stepping is done by typing the next number; a slider was not added.

D1910: Section sizes along a sweep (2026-11-07, TR396 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep gets section_values (an FDEF owner item), text such as "d1 = 10 + 10 * t; d2 = 4": a dimension of the profile sketch, by its id (d1) or the user's name, and a formula of t, which runs from 0 at the start of the path to 1 at its end, read by the safe expression parser (part variables may be used too; mm or degrees by the dimension's kind). The profile sketch is copied and solved again at 9 evenly spaced stations along the path with those values, each outline is carried to its station with the least turning (the guided sweep's frames, D804), and a smooth loft joins the sections; side faces keep the profile's entity names and the caps cap/start and cap/end. It needs a sketch profile of one region without holes, one direction, and no Thin Feature; a missing dimension, a bad formula or a profile that cannot be solved at some station is a feature error with a next step. Twist, the other orientations and the corner modes are not applied (the least turning frame is used), as for a scaled sweep (D816), which this extends from scaling the whole profile to changing chosen dimensions. The panel gets a Section values line in the options.

D1911: Hole placement with no sketch (2026-11-07, TR143 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Hole Tool's Positions tab gets Place by (place_by, an FDEF owner item stored for the panel; the refs decide the build): Points (as before), Distances from Two Edges (refs.place_edges, two straight edges, with place_distance1 and place_distance2, FDEF owner items) or Concentric (refs.concentric, a round edge or a cylinder or cone face, whose axis meets the face). Either places one hole on the face picked in the Face box, which also becomes refs.plane, so the hole's own position sketch is not needed (core/features/hole_place.py builds a one point sketch at build time). Distances are measured in the face's plane, each from its edge toward the face's centre, so the hole lands on the face; parallel edges, curved edges and an axis along the face are feature errors with a next step. Concentric covers counterbores over an existing hole and holes on bosses. The values are typed in the panel's length fields; on screen dimension editing in the view is not done (the view has no dimension widgets for features), and clicks on the model go to the pick lists while placing by edges.

D1912: Custom hole stack (2026-11-07, TR144 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new hole_type "custom" (Custom Stack, an FDEF owner item) with stack (an FDEF owner item), text such as "counterbore 10 3; countersink 8 90; straight 5 12": from the face inward, each element is a kind (straight, counterbore, tapped, countersink), a diameter and a length, or for a countersink its included angle, the cone running down to the next element's diameter. The order is the text's order, so elements are reordered by editing the line (the panel has no reorderable list for this). The revolve section is built from the stack (hole_stack.py), with roles head, step<k>, step<k>_floor, wall for the last bore and bottom or tip; the depth is the sum of the elements, so only Blind is allowed, and the drill point, head clearance and print fit apply as for the other types. The diameter param became optional in the type (the other types still require it in their own check). Far side elements and cosmetic thread marks on tapped elements are not built: tapped is a plain bore at the typed diameter.

D1913: Hole start plane (2026-11-07, TR144 item 3 rest, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Hole Tool gets refs.start_plane (an FDEF owner item; a flat face in the panel, or a plane feature): every hole is moved along its own axis to start where the axis meets that plane, instead of on the face it was placed on, so holes can start below a curved or stepped top. A plane along the hole axis is a feature error with a next step.

D1914: User hole sizes (2026-11-07, TR144 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). The hole standards get "user" (User Sizes): a comma separated file with a header row (name and diameter needed; pitch, tap_drill, three clearances, head diameter and height, countersink diameter, nut flats and height optional, in mm, missing values following common proportions of the diameter) is loaded with Load User Sizes... on the hole panel's Type tab. The text is kept in the preferences (holes/user_sizes), so the sizes come back next time; reading it is plain CSV and never runs code. Holes store their own values, so a part opens the same without the file; the file only fills the size list. A bad file is refused with the row that is wrong. Head types beyond the existing counterbore and countersink forms are not added.

D1915: Radial hole placement and slanted holes (2026-11-07, TR397 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3).
