Place by (D1911) gets Distance and Angle from an Axis (refs.radial, a round or straight edge or an axis, with radial_distance and radial_angle, FDEF owner items): the hole sits that far from where the axis meets the face's plane, at that angle from the plane's X direction; and On a Point (refs.at_point, a vertex, sketch point or reference point, seen straight onto the face). Both make one hole with no sketch, like D1911. Any hole can run along refs.hole_axis (an FDEF owner item, a straight edge, sketch line or axis): each hole keeps its start point and turns to that direction, the way that goes into the part, so holes need not be square to the face; an axis along the face is a feature error with a next step. A slanted hole's head starts square to its own axis at the start point, so part of a counterbore's rim can sit above a flat face; use a start plane (D1913) or head clearance when that matters.

D1916: Mounting Boss step and fin direction from a face (2026-11-07, TR146 item 1 rest, Phase 7B Stage 3). Mounting Boss gets step_height and step_diameter (FDEF owner items): a narrower collar on top of the boss (roles step/side and step/top), for example to locate it in the mating part's hole; the hole, head bore, pin or pin hole then starts on top of the collar. 0 makes none. The step must be smaller than the boss and larger than its hole, head bore or pin, else a feature error with a next step. The fin direction pick takes a face as well as an edge (the face's normal, which the core already read), so item 1 is done. Lip and Groove (item 2: jumping gaps where ribs meet the wall, keeping the wall's draft, picking the rim by edges; lip only or groove only already works) and Vent (item 3: fillet, draft and offset per element group) are not done.

D1917: Tapered modelled thread (2026-11-07, TR145 rest, Phase 7B Stage 3). Thread gets taper_angle (an optional half angle, an FDEF owner item, below 10 degrees; 1.79 degrees, 1 in 16 on the diameter, for NPT and Rc as in ASME B1.20.1 and ISO 7-1, D1511): the helix runs on a cone (the kernel's conical surface, its side parameter advanced by the lead over the cosine of the angle per turn) instead of a cylinder, and the profile moves with it, so the thread's depth stays the same while its diameter changes along the axis. A hole's thread narrows going in and a shaft's widens away from the picked end, as pipe threads do. The cut's run in before the start follows the cone. Sizes still come from the typed diameter and pitch (the pipe sizes are in the Hole Tool's Tapered Pipe Tapped type, D1511), and a tapered modelled thread in tapped holes is not offered. TR145 is done.

D1918: Thread profile from a sketch and end finishes (2026-11-07, TR254 rest, Phase 7B Stage 3). Thread's form gets "sketch" (From a Sketch, an FDEF owner item) with refs.profile_sketch (an FDEF owner item): a sketch with one closed region, drawn anywhere; its X runs along the thread axis and its Y is the depth into the material for a cut (the height off the face for an extruded thread), measured from the region's lowest point, which sits on the face; points on that line reach a little past the face so the cut opens cleanly, and the region is centred along the axis. The outline is sampled (0.005 mm deflection) into the swept section, so arcs work. Thread also gets end_finish (an FDEF owner item): square (default, as before), chamfer (the last part of the thread runs out of the material at 45 degrees, over its own depth) or fade (it runs out over the last pitch). The run out is a second helical solid that continues the thread on a cone leading the section out of the material, joined to the shortened main thread at the same section, because the kernel's common of a helical solid with a solid of revolution came back empty or whole at some positions. With a run out, the thread cut check compares only the removed volume (the kernel measures the common of two touching helical solids loosely). A tapered thread (D1917) ignores the end finish. TR254 is done.

D1919: Fit values by hole size and direction (2026-11-07, TR412, Phase 7B Stage 3). A printer fit table (core/printing/fit_table.py, no Qt) refines the single fit tolerance (D311, TR180): one row per line, "<hole|outside> <flat|upright|any> <up to diameter> <gap per side> [nozzle]", kept in the preferences (printing/fit_table, plain text, never run). The lookup takes the rows of the right kind, direction (or any) and nozzle (or none named), and picks the smallest band that holds the diameter, rows naming the exact direction and the nozzle first; with no row the printer's fit tolerance is used. The Hole Tool's options get Fit Table... (edit the rows) and Fit from Table, which sets this hole's Fit Tolerance from the table for its diameter and its direction (upright when its face is flat across the model's Z, the printer's up; a curved face counts as lying down) and the active printer's nozzle, with a note that says the gap is applied in the model so the slicer's own hole compensation should be off, or this set to 0 (the which side applies it part; FDCAD does not read slicer settings). The value is still stored in the hole as fit_tolerance, so parts rebuild the same without the table. Outside sizes have rows in the table for later use; no feature reads them yet, since FDCAD has no outside size fit besides Split for Printing's clearance. The table is per app, not per printer profile, to keep the printer profile format (an owner file area) unchanged.

D1920: User thread tables (2026-11-07, TR327, Phase 7B Stage 3). The user size file of D1914 is the thread table too: its rows (name, diameter, pitch, tap_drill and the rest) gain an optional class column (the thread class, such as 6g), kept in ScrewSize.thread_class. Thread and Cosmetic Thread get Load User Sizes... (one loader shared with the Hole Tool, so all three read one file kept in the preferences), and their size lists add the user's sizes; choosing one fills the diameter and pitch, and the thread class when the panel has one and the class is known. The Hole Tool already offers them under User Sizes (tap drills included). Thread already remembers its last size (remembered_keys) and Repeat Last Command (Enter or Z) opens Thread again with it, so applying the same thread to another cylinder is that: Repeat, then click the round edge; nothing new was needed there. Types beyond the size's own name are not kept: a row is one size of one thread type.

D1921: Simplify threads while editing (2026-11-07, TR347, Phase 7B Stage 3). A preference (Simplify threads while editing, rebuild/simplify_threads, off) and a part setting (extra simplify_threads in the part file, an FDEF owner item, true or false, which wins when present) make Thread features and tapped holes with a modelled thread build as cosmetic threads: the part is left as it is and a thread mark is drawn (BuildContext.simplify_threads, set by the rebuild engine per feature, with its own cache key so switching does not reuse the wrong result). The report lists them (RebuildReport.simplified). Force Rebuild makes every thread real for that one rebuild (engine.real_once), and every export names the simplification in its note (export_warning) with Force Rebuild as the next step, so a part is never exported without its threads silently. The 3MF and STL exports for printing go through the same export and note. The part setting has no panel yet: it is set in the file (a document command for it is left for the part properties work).

D1922: Thread relief and end chamfer (2026-11-07, TR256, Phase 7B Stage 3). Thread gets relief and the Hole Tool's tapped holes get thread_relief and thread_chamfer (FDEF owner items, booleans). The relief is a run out groove (undercut) at the thread's end, sized from the pitch after DIN 76-1 form A, normal undercuts, rounded to rules of the pitch P (thread_relief.py): on a shaft d - 1.6 P across and 3 P long, in a hole d + 0.3 mm across and 4 P long; its far side is where the thread ends, so the thread runs out into it, and a groove as long as the thread is a feature error with a next step. A tapped hole's entry chamfer is a 90 degree countersink to 1.05 d (DIN 76-1's countersink for internal threads, the smaller end of its range), set in place of a near countersink. Thread's end chamfer is its existing Lead In (a 45 degree cone to the root at the start, D782), which the panel names as such. Both grooves are revolved rings cut in one boolean per feature, their seam turned off the thread's start section (the kernel failed booleans where the seams met, D1918). Fine and coarse rows of the DIN tables (short and long forms) are not offered.

D1923: Closed spring ends on a helix (2026-11-07, TR162 item 2 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Helix gets ends (open by default, or closed) with end_pitch (FDEF owner items): a constant pitch helix becomes a variable pitch one through four rows, the end pitch at turns 0 and N and the pitch at turns 1 and N - 1, so each end coil tightens to about the wire's diameter over its first and last turn, as a closed spring end. It needs 2.5 turns or more and an end pitch below the pitch, and no taper; the panel's Closed Ends tick shows the End Pitch. Ground flat ends (the flat cut at each end) are not built into the curve: a helix is a curve, and the flat belongs to the swept spring, so it is made with an Extruded Cut through the spring's ends after the Sweep. The bolt, nut and washer samples (item 1) are not done.

D1924: Loft Tangent and Curvature to adjacent faces (2026-11-07, TR136 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Loft's start and end constraints get "tangent" (Tangent to Faces) and "curvature" (Curvature to Faces), FDEF owner items, for an end profile that is a face of the part: the direction is found from the faces next to it, at each edge of the profile face the direction in the neighbouring face square to the edge and away from it, averaged (so a box's top face with upright sides gives straight up), and then used like Direction Vector with the tangent length (one guiding copy of the profile a quarter of the length out, D220). Curvature adds a second copy twice as far along the same line, so the loft leaves straight along the faces, matching flat neighbours' zero curvature; it is the closest the section loft (ThruSections, no tangency control) gets, not true curvature continuity with curved neighbours. A sketch or point end refuses both with a next step, as do neighbours that cancel out. Connectors several per profile with dragging (item 1) and Add Loft Section (item 3) are not done.

D1925: Several planes or points in one command (2026-11-07, TR148, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new Plane with Offset distance or At angle, and a new Point along a curve, get How many (1 to 50) in the panel; with more than one, OK adds them all in one undo step (core/features/datum_series.py). Each extra one is its own reference feature, so sketches and features can use any of them, and its distance, angle or percent is a formula of the first one's ("distance@Plane 1" times k), so editing the first respaces them all; the names follow on (Plane 2, Plane 3). Points have three spacings: by the distance, by the percent, or spread evenly over the curve (0 to 100 percent, typed numbers, so they do not follow the first). The spec's "from one feature" is kept in the sense of one command: one feature holding several datums would need every reference pick and display in the app to learn a datum number, so separate features linked by formulas were chosen. Editing a plane later shows no count (it is one plane); delete or add planes to change how many.
D1800: Select through faces (2026-11-07, TR64 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Fillet and Chamfer panels get a Select through faces tick in their items group (property_panel/forms/pick_through_box.py). It is view state only, kept for the session and never written to the file. While it is ticked the view's `pick_through` flag is on: a click looks through everything the view lists under the cursor, nearest first, and takes the first edge (ui/viewport/through_edges.py), so an edge behind a face is picked without turning the part. With edges filtered out the flag does nothing. The flag is turned off when the panel's form is deleted. Hover still highlights the front item, since the hover highlight is the kernel context's own. Shared file changed: ui/viewport/widget.py (one flag and one call before the see through pick of TR224).

D1801: Round corners recorded as met (2026-11-07, TR64 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Where three rounded edges meet at a vertex the kernel already makes a corner blend face (named corner/face#k, D213) that meets each round with tangent continuity, so nothing new is built; a test checks the eight corners of a fully rounded plate are blends with no crease. Items 1 (Keep features: a large round passing over bosses and cuts rounds around them) and 3 (Overflow: Keep edge or Keep surface) are not built: the kernel's fillet maker has no setting for either; it always rebuilds the faces it overflows onto, and a boss or cut a round passes over makes the round fail rather than wrap around it. Keeping features would need the features removed, the round made and the features rebuilt, which is a new rebuild path for one option. TR64 has items 2, 4, 5 and 6 done; 1 and 3 are left for a kernel with those settings.

D1802: Limit failing areas (2026-11-07, TR271 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). When a constant size fillet fails on some picked edges (the pinpoint of D213), each failing edge (up to four) is searched for the longest stretch that rounds alone with the partial edge routine (D519): stretches of 95, 90, 80, 70, 60, 50, 35 and 20 percent that keep the start, keep the end or sit in the middle, in that order (core/features/fillet_limit_areas.py). When every failing edge has one, the fix "Limit failing areas (round N edges in part)" is offered (action limit_failing, data parts: [edge name, start percent, end percent]). It runs from the errors panel like the split fixes (D1405): the fillet keeps its other edges and each failing edge becomes a Partial Edges fillet (partial percent) right after it, one undo step, so the stretch stays editable. It is offered only for fillets the partial routine can make: Constant Size, Radius method, circular profile, whole edges, tangent propagation on, no limiting plane, picked edges (not edges from faces or features), one body. Shared file changed: main_window/window.py (one fix action branch).

D1803: Shell wall rule (2026-11-07, TR322, Phase 7B Stage 3). Shell gets wall_rule, "never_thinner" or "never_thicker" (an FDEF owner item; the panel's Wall list: Exact, Never thinner, Never thicker). The wall is measured as the distance from a point of the new wall to the nearest kept face of the part. The kernel offsets each face exactly, so only corners and joins differ: sharp joins reach past the thickness where offset faces open apart (1.41 times at an edge, 1.73 at a box corner), round joins keep the thickness. Never thicker therefore uses rounded corners only (with Corners Sharp it is an error with a next step); Never thinner keeps the corner setting (sharp, or rounded where sharp fails, both at least the thickness). After the build the wall's vertices and edge middles are measured (up to 400 points; rim faces on the plane of a removed face are left out) and a warning (code wall_rule) gives the thinnest or thickest value when the rule is missed by more than 2 percent. This replaces the D1411 note that the mode could not be kept: D1411 reasoned about the distance across a corner, while this rule measures the nearest distance. Not checked: Both sides and Multi Thickness shells, where the wall is not one thickness (core/features/shell_wall_rule.py).

D1804: Fixed Edge draft (2026-11-07, TR323, Phase 7B Stage 3). Draft gets draft_type "fixed_edge" with refs.fixed_edges (FDEF owner items; core/features/draft_fixed_edge.py). The neutral pick gives only the direction of pull. Each face to draft uses the picked fixed edge that lies on it and turns about it: the face gets its own neutral plane through that edge, square to the pull, and the kernel tilts all faces in one call, so the fixed edge stays where it is and the neighbours are extended or trimmed by the kernel as for any draft. The edge must be straight and square to the pull (otherwise the face cannot turn about it); a face with no fixed edge, a curved edge or a leaning edge is an error naming it. "Adds faces where needed" is met as far as the kernel's draft goes: the kernel does not build new side faces, so where neighbours cannot follow the draft fails with the usual message. In the panel the type adds a Fixed edges list in the Faces group; edges clicked in the view go there. With this TR323 is done (D1419 and D1804).

D1805: Dome direction vector (2026-11-07, TR147 item 3 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Dome gets an optional refs.direction (an FDEF owner item; the panel's Direction pick takes a straight edge, flat face or plane). The dome is made as before and then sheared (core/features/dome_direction.py): a point at height h over the face moves sideways by h along the lean, so the base stays on the face and the top follows the direction; a shear keeps the volume. The direction is turned to leave the face, and one closer than 5 degrees to the face is an error. The kernel's general transform turns the dome's surfaces into spline surfaces (the volume stays within 0.1 percent); a direction along the face normal changes nothing. Not done: the constraint sketch that sets the dome's profile (TR147 item 3 rest), and tapered or square steps for Step Draft (TR147 item 1 rest, see D1418).

D1806: Reapply Fillets on Draft (2026-11-07, TR259 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Draft gets reapply_fillets (an FDEF owner item) for Neutral Plane and Fixed Edge drafts with Propagation None or Along tangent and no Other angle below: the rounds next to the picked faces are removed, the draft runs on the sharp body and the rounds are made again (core/features/reapply_fillets.around, D1420). The tick sits in the Faces group. Parting Line, Step and split drafts go through the cut and join routines of D521, whose faces are new, so they are left out; propagation All, Inner or Outer finds its faces only on the body. Combine is not done: it works on whole bodies, the rounds next to the change are not on picked faces, and the new edges where two bodies meet had no round before, so there is no radius to make again.

D1807: Heal Edges, the gap fix (2026-11-07, TR262 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). New feature type heal_edges (an FDEF owner item, core/features/heal_edges.py) with an optional tolerance (length, default 0.01 mm). On each solid of the part it runs the kernel's shape fixer (precision 1e-7, largest tolerance the typed one), then measures every edge's tolerance again from its curves (forced same parameter) and updates vertex tolerances, so a loose tolerance no real gap needs is cut back and outline gaps up to the tolerance are closed. No face moves; face names are carried through the fixer's replacements. A gap still wider than the tolerance gives a warning (code gap_left) with its size. Geometry Check's Fix on a gap or inexact edge (not an open edge) adds this feature, one undo step, with the tolerance a little over that edge's gap (1.1 times, rounded up to two digits, at least the default). Not done: making a nearly smooth edge exactly smooth and squaring up a nearly square face (both need the faces themselves rebuilt, which no kernel call does without moving geometry the user did not pick), and the clip sphere of the tour (viewport clipping is shared view code). The feature has no panel of its own; it edits through the generic parameter panel.

D1808: Wall thickness target and hover reading (2026-11-07, TR87 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Preferences, Printing gets Wall analysis target (setting printing/wall_target, mm; 0, shown as "Minimum wall", uses the active profile's minimum wall as before). It is one value for the app, not per profile, so it can be set for one check and put back. While Wall Thickness Analysis is on, the view's cursor point (the model point the status bar already shows, D114) is measured in a kernel job, one at a time (a reading still running drops new cursor moves, so hovering never queues kernel work): the point goes onto the nearest face within 0.5 mm, a ray goes into the material against the outward normal, and the wall is the distance to where it leaves (core/printing/wall_point.py, the same measure as the analysis, D414). The status bar shows "Wall here: X mm (target T mm)". With this TR87 is done (D1416, D1808).

D1809: Detailed preview on Extrude and Rib (2026-11-07, TR164, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Extrude panel (Direction 1 group, not Revolve) and the Rib panel get the Detailed preview tick of D1417, each kept for the session. The flag preview_detailed goes only on the copy sent to the preview, never on the feature that OK writes: Extrude has no form, so the panel's change handler copies the feature when the tick is on; Rib's form returns the copy from for_preview. Shared file changed: property_panel/panel.py (the tick, one class flag and the copy in _changed). With this TR164 is done.

D1810: Split Line Silhouette and intersection with a body (2026-11-07, TR60, Phase 7B Stage 3). Split Line gets method "silhouette" with refs.direction (a plane, flat face or straight edge, resolved as a direction) and, for Intersection, refs.tool_body (a face of another body of the part, used instead of refs.plane; both FDEF owner items). The silhouette is where a face's normal turns square to the pull. On the faces parts are mostly made of it lies in a plane (core/features/silhouette.py): a cylinder's outline is the section with the plane through its axis square to the pull's part across the axis, a sphere's the plane through its centre square to the pull, and a cone whose axis is square to the pull the plane through its axis square to the pull. So the face is cut with that plane's section, as Intersection does. Flat faces have no outline and are left as they are; a cylinder pulled along its axis, a cone leaning to the pull, a torus or a spline face is an error naming the face, with Projection as the next step (their outlines are curves no kernel call returns as edges, which D1414 noted). Intersection with a body sections each picked face with the tool solid; the tool must be another body of the part. The split itself moved to split_line.split_with, shared with Parting Line. With this TR60 is done.

D1811: Parting Line splits straddle faces (2026-11-07, TR84, Phase 7B Stage 3). Parting Line gets split_faces (an FDEF owner item; the panel tick Split faces at the line). When straddle faces are found, those that are cylinders, cones or spheres are split along their silhouette for the pull (D1810) and the parting edges are found again on the split part, so the line runs across them; the feature's result then carries the split part, so later features see the split faces (named <face name>#k). Straddle faces of other kinds stay whole and are named in a warning with a Split Line as the next step. Without the tick the part is unchanged, as before. With this TR84 is done.

D1812: Chamfer corners (2026-11-07, TR321 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Chamfer gets corner, "patch" (the default, not written) or "mitre" (an FDEF owner item; the panel's Corners list, not for the Vertex type). Patch is the kernel's corner: a small flat triangle where three bevels meet. Mitre (core/features/chamfer_corners.py) takes each corner face that is a triangle between three flat bevel faces of this chamfer, finds the point where the three bevel planes meet (a 3 by 3 solve), adds the tetrahedron between the triangle and that point (or cuts it when the point lies inside the part) and merges the faces that then share a plane, so the bevels meet in three mitre lines and keep their names. Other corners (four sided, curved bevels) stay patches with a warning (code corner_left). Not built: a blend corner and a setback (the kernel's chamfer maker has neither setting; see D1814).

D1813: Rip on tubes and cones (2026-11-07, TR174 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). Rip gets refs.tube_faces with tube_angle and tube_offset (FDEF owner items). Each picked cylinder or cone face is cut by a slab of the rip's gap that holds the face's axis and points out at the angle (measured about the axis from the surface's own X direction, the only fixed start a round face has), moved sideways by the offset, and long enough to pass the face on every side, so the slit runs along the whole wall (core/features/sheetmetal/tube_rip.py). It works on a plain solid, as the step before treating a rolled tube as sheet: the result is an ordinary body, not a sheet model. A flat face, or a slit that cuts nothing, is an error with a next step. The panel shows the three fields in the Rip group with 0 defaults.

D1814: Setback fillets and fillet transitions not built (2026-11-07, TR63, TR394 items 1 and 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A kernel check of the fillet maker (BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet: Add, SetRadius, SetLaw, SetParams, SetContinuity, SetFilletShape and the contour queries) shows no setting for a setback distance at a vertex, for the kind of transition where rounds meet, or for listing and trimming the pieces of a chain: the maker builds corner patches itself. Building them would need an own corner surface builder (a new blending engine), which is Opus work beyond this round. The rounds already meet in a smooth corner blend (D1801), and Vertex chamfers and the mitre corner (D216, D1812) cover the chamfer cases.

D1815: Orient Body by frames (2026-11-07, TR268 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Move and Copy Body gets mode "frame" with refs.from_frame and refs.to_frame (FDEF owner items; core/features/orient_body.py). Each frame is up to three picks in order: the origin (a vertex, or a round edge or cylinder, whose axis point is used), the Z direction (a flat face's outward normal, a straight edge or an axis) and an optional X direction (made square to Z; without it the kernel's default X for that Z is used). The body moves with the displacement that takes the first frame onto the second, so frames line up exactly (Z along Z); reverse turns the target Z round, which sets a face down on a face. Copies repeat the move as for the other modes. The panel adds Frame to frame to the Mode list with the two pick lists. Not built: item 1 (several mate like relations solved together; it needs a small assembly solver) and item 3 (pivot and axis choices of the transform handles, which are viewport code shared with other sessions).

D1700: Sketch Fillet with splines (2026-11-07, TR48, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sketch Fillet picks splines (`core/sketch/ops/spline_corner.py`). A corner where a spline meets a line or an arc end to end is rounded: the spline is sampled with numpy (96 samples per cubic piece), the centre candidates are the spline points moved by the radius along each normal, and where their distance to the other curve's full line or circle crosses the radius the place is refined by bisection. Of the centres whose touching point lies on the other curve, the one nearest the corner is used (as D1317). The spline is cut there by splitting its cubic piece (de Casteljau): the new end and its direction are exact, and when the cut piece is the only piece kept next to the cut, the whole piece is exact. When more pieces are kept, the through point next to the cut keeps its handle (it also shapes the next piece), so the cut piece bends a little between its ends. The fillet arc shares the spline's new end and gets Tangent to both curves (the solver's spline end tangency); two splines together are refused.
Status: Default
Reason: TR48; the solver has no spline curve, so the fillet is placed by numbers and held by the spline end tangency the solver has.

D1701: Sketch Chamfer on arcs and splines (2026-11-07, TR48, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sketch Chamfer picks lines, arcs and splines (`core/sketch/ops/curve_chamfer.py`). On a corner with an arc or a spline, Distance and distance is the straight distance from the corner to each chamfer end (for an arc found exactly from the chord, for a spline by bisection along samples). The curves are cut back there, a line joins the new ends, a construction point stays at the corner with Coincident to each line or arc that met there, and two distance dimensions run from it. Angle and distance needs two lines and says so.
Status: Default
Reason: TR48; the straight distance needs no arc length and dimensions the same way the line case does.

D1702: Sizing a sketch fillet by dragging (2026-11-07, TR48 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Pressing on a corner point in Sketch Fillet rounds it at once with the panel radius as before; while the button is still down the tool stays busy, and each cursor move makes the fillet again from the state before it with the radius equal to the distance from the corner to the cursor (the panel Radius follows). A radius that does not fit keeps the last one that did, with the message in the status bar. Release ends sizing; it is one undo step. A sized fillet gets its own radius dimension even when Dimension each fillet is off. A drag from the first picked curve to a second still picks the second where the button is released.
Status: Default
Reason: TR48 item 3; remaking the fillet gives the true result live, without a separate preview shape.

D1703: Construction geometry after the sketch is closed (2026-11-07, TR339, Phase 7B Stage 3). A tick per sketch, Show Construction in Part, stored in the sketch data as `show_construction: true` (left out when off; an FDEF owner item), set from the open sketch's Sketch command `sketch.show_construction` or from the sketch's feature tree menu (one undo step, ReplaceFeature). The tick is off by default, and while it is off the 3D view now leaves a closed sketch's construction curves out (before, every curve was drawn). With it on, the construction curves and free construction points (not line ends, centres or spline handles) are drawn, the rebuild keeps a compound of them in `RebuildReport.construction_edges`, later sketches get it as a Convert Entities source under the sketch's own id and name (D517: click the sketch in the tree while Convert is active), and Up to Vertex and Start from Vertex offer the sketch's construction points (`core/sketch/construction_refs.py`). Revolve axes and the reference geometry pick lists already offered construction lines and points and are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: TR339; construction geometry is layout help, so it stays out of the way unless the sketch asks to share it.

D1704: Close Sketch to Model (2026-11-07, TR106, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch tool, Close Sketch to Model (`sketch.close_to_model`, Sketch tab with Convert Entities; `core/sketch/close_to_model.py`, `ui/sketch_tools/close_model_tool.py`). It uses the part's intersection curves in the sketch plane that the sketch already works out when it opens (D759), and the silhouette when those do not hold the ends. The sketch must have exactly one open profile with two open ends (D964), each within 0.001 mm of a part edge. The edge pieces holding the ends are cut there (a circle becomes two arcs) and the loop is walked both ways from one end to the other; a branch or a dead end drops that way. The two ways each close the profile into a shape. The prompt is the tool itself, not a dialog: moving the cursor inside a shape previews its edges, and a click inside one copies its edge pieces into the sketch as fixed curves (as Convert Entities, D517), with Coincident between the profile's ends and the copies' ends, one undo step; the tool then ends.
Status: Default
Reason: TR106; picking by clicking inside the shape shows both choices in place, with no dialog to read.

D1705: Direction arrows (2026-11-07, TR341 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Tool previews get `Preview.arrows` (a tail point and a direction in sketch millimetres), drawn by the canvas in the preview colour at a fixed 22 pixel length with a 7 pixel head, so they read the same at any zoom. Shown where the direction changes the result: Offset draws one arrow per chain, from the chain's nearest point to the first offset piece's start (so it points to the offset side, and to both with Both directions); Linear Sketch Pattern draws arrows from the original toward the first copy of Direction 1 and, with more than one row, of Direction 2 (Reverse turns them); Circular Sketch Pattern draws one from the original toward the next copy, which shows the turning direction. Chain order is not shown on its own: no sketch tool's result depends on it apart from the offset side. Display only, never saved.
Status: Default
Reason: TR341 item 2; one arrow kind in the preview covers the cases where direction matters.

D1706: Lock changed dimensions while dragging (2026-11-07, TR238, Phase 7B Stage 3). Driving dimensions already hold their values during a drag (TOOL_SPEC T2), so the lock is about place: Preferences, Sketch gets Lock changed dimensions while dragging (`sketch/lock_changed_dimensions`, off by default). The open sketch remembers each dimension whose value is set (`SketchEdit.set_dimension`) until it closes; with the preference on, a drag pins every point of those dimensions' entities (a curve's own points, or the points themselves) where they are, with `solver.drag(..., hold=...)`, in both drag passes, so the drag moves the rest. A dragged point itself is never held. The list is not saved.
Status: Default
Reason: TR238; what the user has just sized is what they least want a drag to shift.

D1707: Lock the dimension type while placing (2026-11-07, TR111 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). While Smart Dimension's preview follows the cursor, a right click (no drag) locks the type it shows when that is a point to point distance (aligned, horizontal or vertical: the types the cursor position switches between, `edit.LOCKABLE`); the preview and the placed dimension then keep it wherever the label goes. A second right click unlocks. The lock goes when the dimension is placed or Smart Dimension ends. The right click is taken before the sketch right click menu only while a preview shows; otherwise the menu opens as before. The status bar says locked or unlocked.
Status: Default
Reason: TR111 item 1; the other dimension kinds have one type each, so nothing to lock.

D1708: Hide extension and dimension lines (2026-11-07, TR111 item 3 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Dimension Display (D901) gets Hide extension lines and Hide dimension line, for linear distances only, stored in the dimension's display settings as `hide_extension: true` and `hide_line: true` (left out when off; FDEF owner items). The canvas leaves those lines out; the label and its value are unchanged. Already there from item 3: nearest, centre or farthest per circle or arc of a distance (the Dimension panel, T4.3.2) and two points of one arc (a point to point distance). Not built: arrow flip, since sketch dimensions draw no arrowheads; and from item 2 the symmetric angle about a centerline, which needs a new dimension type in the solver.
Status: Default
Reason: TR111 item 3; display settings already hold per dimension look.

D1709: Edit a polygon later (2026-11-07, TR114 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Nothing new is saved: a polygon is found again from what the Polygon tool made (`core/sketch/polygon_edit.py`): three or more lines joined in one Equal relation that close a loop, and a construction circle that every corner is Coincident with (corners on the circle) or every side is Tangent to (sides touch). Right clicking such a side offers Edit Polygon (a dialog: Sides, Corners on the circle, Circle diameter, Angle of the first corner or of the first side's middle). The polygon is made again about the same centre point with the Polygon tool's code; the new circle takes the old circle's id, so relations and dimensions on the centre and the circle stay, a diameter or radius dimension on the circle takes the new size, and those on the old sides and corners go. Lines that were construction stay construction. One sketch undo step. The Polygon tool gets a Triangle button that sets three sides.
Status: Default
Reason: TR114 item 2; finding the polygon from its relations needs no new FDEF data.

D1710: Infinite construction line and flipped tangent arcs (2026-11-07, TR115 items 1 and 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Infinite Construction Line (`sketch.infinite_line`, Line dropdown; `ui/sketch_tools/infinite_line.py`): the sketch and the solver have no endless curve, so it is a construction line reaching 1000 mm each way from the first click, through the second; both clicks become construction points Coincident with it, and a direction snap adds its relation. Trim cuts it to size later. (2) Tangent Arc gets a Flip direction tick: the arc leaves the end backward along the curve (the end direction reversed), so it turns back over the curve; the Tangent relation holds it, since the solver's tangency at a shared end takes either sense. Item 4's degree and weights do not apply (cubic pieces with handles, D278, D1314) and a spline length dimension needs a solver spline curve; left open.
Status: Default
Reason: TR115; a long line is what trimming needs, without a new curve kind in the file.

D1711: Trace a sketch picture (2026-11-07, TR116 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Sketch Picture tool gets Trace Colour Region and Trace Box buttons and a Trace colour tolerance (20 percent by default). The canvas hands the tool the picture's pixels (decoded by Qt, as for the see-through colour, D977); `core/sketch/trace.py` works on them with numpy: the image is first reduced by a whole step so its longer side is at most 400 pixels; a colour region is the pixels joined by sides to the clicked one within the tolerance of its colour (grown by whole array dilation); a box region is the pixels inside the box that differ from the colour at its first corner. The outline is walked along pixel sides into closed loops (loops under 4 pixel sides are specks and dropped), simplified with Douglas and Peucker at one reduced pixel (starting from an extreme corner, and dropping points the outline runs straight through), mapped through the picture's size, flips and turn, and added as closed loops of plain lines with shared end points, one undo step. Curves are not fitted: lines are what the user edits and what Fit Spline (D1306) can turn into a spline.
Status: Default
Reason: TR116 item 2; a bounded pixel grid keeps the outline walk small, and plain lines stay editable.

D1712: Convert Entities on a face (2026-11-07, TR118, Phase 7B Stage 3). The sketch has the part outline on its plane as edge polylines, not faces, so a face is found from them (`ops/convert.face_loops`): edges joined end to end that close make loops; a click inside a loop and not on an edge picks the face whose outer loop is the smallest loop round the click, and its inner loops are the loops inside that one which do not hold the click and are not inside another of them. Convert Entities copies the outer loop and, with the new Inner loops tick on (default), the inner loops, as fixed curves in one undo step; hovering previews them. Holding Ctrl and clicking an edge copies only that edge's loop (its chain, as Select chain). Ctrl and a click inside a face takes nothing, so a Ctrl click near an edge never grabs a whole face. The canvas now hands Ctrl to tools with a `ctrl` attribute (a small shared canvas change).
Status: Default
Reason: TR118; the outline polylines already hold every face boundary in the sketch plane.

D1713: Explode Text (2026-11-07, TR121 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Right click empty sketch space, Explode Text (shown while the sketch has text). The glyph outlines are laid out by the text code (`text.layout`) in a kernel job off the UI thread; each glyph edge becomes a curve piece (`core/sketch/text_explode.py`): straight edges lines, round edges arcs, other edges splines through 9 points along them. When the job ends, every text item is replaced by its curves in one sketch undo step (if the sketch's text items are still there). The curves are free (no Fix), and ends that meet within 0.0001 mm get Coincident, so each letter outline stays closed while it is edited. A text the kernel cannot lay out stays as it is and the status bar says so. Items 2 (bold, italic and rotation per character) and 3 (a number that counts up across pattern copies) are not built: both need new text fields in the file and item 3 a pattern link, so they are left for the owner's next round.
Status: Default
Reason: TR121 item 1; plain curves are what the sketch edits best, and the kernel work stays off the UI thread.

D1714: Temporary guide lines (2026-11-07, TR232, Phase 7B Stage 3). While a drawing tool is active, the cursor resting 0.6 s on a sketch point (a point snap) marks it as a guide start (a ring); resting on a second point draws a dashed guide between the two (`ui/sketch_tools/guides.py`). The guide's ends, middle, thirds and quarters snap as a new snap kind, Guide, which is a free point with no relations, and only where no stronger sketch snap is (it ranks with free, aligned and on curve snaps). Guides are display only, never saved, and are cleared when the tool changes or ends. The rest timer is a child of the canvas so it never fires after the canvas is gone. The spec's other way in, dragging from a point with a key held, is not built: the drag keys are an owner choice (TR53).
Status: Default
Reason: TR232; resting needs no key, and a segment between two points gives the ends and fractions the spec asks for.

D1715: Sketch on a face without splitting it (2026-11-07, TR234, Phase 7B Stage 3). Already met by design, so no tick was added: a finished sketch is shown in the 3D view as display only lines that are deactivated for picking (C1, `show_sketches`), so a sketch on a part face never splits that face for picking, and the face is still picked whole. Sketch regions are drawn over a face only while a feature panel's Selected Regions box takes picks (T5.3.2, D194), which is the one time picking a region instead of the face is wanted. A per sketch tick would change nothing, so none is stored. The user guide says so.
Status: Default
Reason: TR234; the behaviour the tick would give is the only behaviour FDCAD has.

D1716: Drag without solving (2026-11-07, TR112, Phase 7B Stage 3; owner approved TR112 as written, D750). `core/sketch/free_drag.py`. (1) Drag Without Solving, a checkable item in the sketch's empty space menu, per open sketch (`SketchEdit.free_drag`, not saved): drags set point positions (or a circle's radius) with no solve and add no drop relations. On release, each relation (but Fix and switched off ones) is solved alone on a copy, and it no longer holds when that moves a point by more than 0.000001 mm; each driving dimension no longer holds when its measured value differs. A question (Yes or No, `canvas.ask_delete_unmet`) asks whether to delete them; No keeps them, and the status bar says what to do. (2) Preferences, Sketch, Dragging changes dimensions (`sketch/drag_changes_dimensions`, off by default, so TOOL_SPEC T2 stays the default): the driving dimensions whose entities use a dragged point are let go for the drag (made driven), and after it take their measured values (text like "26mm" or "30deg") and drive again. (3) Detach Segment on Drag, a checkable item in the same menu, per open sketch: when a drag starts on an end point shared by curves, the picked curve that uses it (else the first user) keeps the point and moves; every other curve gets its own new point at the corner, and Coincident relations from the point to other points go.
Status: Default
Reason: TR112; each part is a small switch on the existing drag, off unless asked for.

D1717: Sketch blocks (2026-11-07, TR34, Phase 7B Stage 3; owner approved, D683). `core/sketch/blocks.py`. A block is stored in its sketch as `blocks` (written only when there is one; an FDEF owner item): each `{id, name, sketch, copies}`, where `sketch` is the block's own geometry as sketch data in its own axes (its origin at the lower left of the curves it was made from) with the relations and dimensions among them (Fix left out), and each copy is a `map` from the block's entity ids to the sketch's. Copies are ordinary sketch geometry, so profiles, the solver and every tool work on them unchanged. Where a copy sits (origin and turn) is read back from two of its points far apart, so Move and Rotate Entities and drags move a copy with no extra state. Right click: Make Block (loose picked curves), and on a curve of a copy Insert Copy (placed 10 mm right and down of that copy at its turn, picked), Select Block Copy, Update Block from This Copy (that copy's shape becomes the block's; every other copy is deleted and made again at its own place and turn, so relations from outside to those copies are lost and the guide says so), and Explode Block Copy (the copy stops following; a block with no copies goes). Deleting every curve of a copy drops it. Each command is one sketch undo step. Mirrored copies are not offered: the frame is a turn and a move only.
Status: Default
Reason: TR34; copies as plain geometry keep every existing tool working, and an explicit update avoids live links the solver cannot hold.

D1718: Slice Body (2026-11-07, TR151 item 1 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Tools, Slice Body (`tools.slice`; `core/slices.py`, `ui/main_window/slices.py`): a dialog takes a base plane (any plane feature), the number of slices (1 to 200), the spacing and a start offset. The cuts are made off the UI thread with the Intersection Curves code (D759) on the last rebuilt body, each plane being the base moved along its normal with the same axes. For each plane that meets the part the command adds a reference plane (method offset from the base, `flip` for a negative distance, named Slice Plane n) and a sketch on it (Slice n) with the cut as fixed curves and the usual fixed origin point; all go at the end of the tree in one new folder, Slices (Slices 2 and so on when taken), in one undo step. The slices are copies and do not follow later part changes. Not built: planes round an axis (they need reference planes at an angle through an axis, which the slice plan does not have yet) and item 2, turning the current section view into a cut body feature (a section can combine up to three turned planes, which no single body feature takes).
Status: Default
Reason: TR151 item 1; plain offset planes and fixed sketches use only features FDCAD already has.

D1719: 3D sketch, first form (2026-11-07, TR7 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3; owner approved, D683). A new feature type `sketch3d` (`core/features/sketch3d.py`, panel `forms/sketch3d_form.py`, command `feature.sketch3d` beside Curve Through Points), a curve feature like the others (D291), so sweeps, pipes, lofts and Convert Entities use it. Its data (FDEF owner items) holds `parts`, each `{name, plane, sketch}`: a plane reference as a sketch's `refs.plane` and ordinary 2D sketch data, solved and placed on that plane at rebuild (construction curves left out), and `lines`, each `{kind: line | spline, points: [[x, y, z], ...]}` in mm: straight segments through the points or one interpolated curve through them. All edges make one wire when they join end to end, else a compound; the report gives the curve count and the true 3D length. Plane parts are made by drawing a normal 2D sketch on any plane and pressing Add Part, which copies its plane and data (a copy, so the 3D sketch does not follow later edits of the source). Not built: drawing inside the 3D sketch with Tab switching the working plane, relations between parts on different planes, Along X, Y and Z relations, and 3D dimensions; these need a 3D solver (planegcs is 2D only), so they are left for a later round.
Status: Default
Reason: TR7 first step; planes plus typed space curves give real 3D paths with the solver FDCAD has.
D1816: Sheet metal Stamp (2026-11-07, TR77 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new sheet metal feature type stamp (an FDEF owner item; core/features/sheetmetal/stamp.py; command feature.stamp in the Forms group, no key) with refs.sketch (one closed outline of lines and arcs on a flat face of a wall), depth, draft (0 to under 60 degrees) and reverse. The outline is joined into one closed wire; its top is the outline moved depth out of the face and shrunk by depth times tan(draft) with a planar offset; the shell between them is lofted, and the hollow under it is the same loft one thickness lower, as the Forming Tool presses dimples and ribs (D545), so the sheet keeps its thickness along the press. Like the forming tools it changes the folded part only (wall adds and folded cuts); the flat pattern keeps the blank and gets the outline as marks titled "Stamp outline" (the Flat Marks list, D1112), so DXF and SVG show it. The foot must lie on one wall (a box check, as for the forming tools). Not built: punch, die and corner radii (rounding the stamp's edges would need fillets on the loft and its hollow kept one thickness apart, which the kernel's fillet does not promise), so the stamp's edges are sharp. FDCAD icon feature.stamp is new and original.

D1027: Round 13 merge fixes (2026-11-07, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) The 3D Print tab's Print group grew to five columns in round 13 and set the window's minimum width (1379 px on the test platform, above the 1024 px small screen check, D632), since a group never scrolls inside itself. Its six analysis tools (Overhang Analysis, Wall Thickness Analysis, Print Estimate, Settings by Height, Layer Fit Check, Suction Cups and Islands) move to a new Print Analysis group beside it. (2) The nut and bolt sample (D2003) used an 18 mm modelled thread that the kernel on Windows could not cut (17.9 to 18.1 mm fail, 17.5 mm and below build), so the sample and its tutorial use 17 mm. (3) The panel help button (D2018) gets the 24 px minimum size (U3.3). (4) The living_hinge_strip sample waits for the owner's FDEF_SPEC section for `living_hinge` (D908: `slit_length`, `slit_width`, `bridge`, `row_spacing`, `refs.sketch`); its two spec key tests are strict expected failures until then.

D2200: Symmetric angle about a centerline (2026-11-08, TR111 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). An angle dimension between a line and a centerline (a construction line) that cross gets a `symmetric` flag: its value is the full angle, twice the line's smaller angle to the centerline, which is the angle between the line and its mirror image. Smart Dimension picks it by where the text goes, as the doubled distance does (D123): text on the line's side gives the plain angle (the half angle), text across the centerline gives the full angle, with entities stored as [line, centerline]. The solver holds the line at half the value to the centerline (the angle nearest the current one, so the line does not flip side). Values must be above 0 and below 180 degrees. Stored as `"symmetric": true` on the dimension, left out when off (FDEF owner item). The canvas draws a third leader to the line's mirror image. It stays an `angle` dimension, so units, display, reference mode and the value box treat it as any angle. Arrow flip (the rest of item 3) is not built: sketch dimensions draw no arrowheads (D1708), so there is nothing to flip; TR111 stays unticked with that note.

D2201: Spline length dimension (2026-11-08, TR115 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). The solver has no spline curve (D278), but a spline's cubic pieces can be built from solver points: every point de Casteljau's split at t = 1/2 makes is a midpoint, and the solver's `symmetric_point` holds a helper point at the midpoint of two others; the mirrored in handle is held the same way. Each piece is halved three times (`freeform.LENGTH_DEPTH`) and its length taken as the sum over the eight parts of half the chord plus half the control polygon (Gravesen's estimate; about 1e-4 of the length off the true length on strongly curved pieces, far closer on gentle ones), each a distance parameter, summed with running parameters as Path Length does (D1307). `freeform.spline_length` uses the same split, so a held length reads back as typed. The helper points add no degrees of freedom. The dimension is a `path_length` whose entities may now include splines, so no new type or FDEF key: Spline Length (right click one spline) adds it on that spline, and Length Ratio and Length Difference accept a spline too. Raising or lowering the degree and control point weights do not apply (cubic pieces with handles, D278, D1314), so TR115 is ticked.

D2202: Bold, italic and turn per character (2026-11-08, TR121 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A sketch text item gets `styles`: runs, each with `start` and `end` (character positions, end not included) and any of `bold`, `italic` (over the whole text's setting) and `angle` (radians, added to the text's character turn); a later run wins where runs overlap. Stored only when there are runs (an FDEF owner item under the text keys). Layout picks the font face per character (one font object per bold and italic pair used), so advances and glyphs follow each character's face. Runs keep character positions and are not moved when the text is retyped; a run past the end does nothing. The Text dialog gets a Selected characters row: Bold and Italic switch the style of the selected characters (from the first one's current style), Turn turns them by the angle beside it, Clear Styles removes the runs. Positions instead of rich text keep the file plain and the text box a plain line edit.

D2203: Text that counts pattern copies (2026-11-08, TR121 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). A text field `{copy}` (beside the value fields of D897) shows the pattern copy number: 1 outside patterns and for the seed. A pattern of features (not Geometry pattern) whose seed uses a sketch with `{copy}` text builds each copy again, as varied values do (D1513): the sketch is built once more per copy with the copy number in the build context (`BuildContext.copy_number`) and the seed's tool reads that sketch result. Copies count along the first direction, then row by row: number = i + (j - 1) times count1 (`patterns.copy_number`). A format after a colon works for the number, such as `{copy:03d}`. A variable, dimension or property named copy wins over the field. No new FDEF key. This touches `core/features/patterns.py` (shared with patterns work): a small hook beside the vary code.

D2204: Slices round an axis (2026-11-08, TR151 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Slice Body dialog gets Around axis (None, or any reference axis of the part), Angle step and Start angle; with an axis, Spacing and Start offset are greyed and the angle boxes used. `SlicePlan.axis` holds the axis feature id, and `start` and `spacing` are then radians. Each plane is made as an angle reference plane does it (`slices.axis_plane`: the base normal turned about the axis direction, through the axis point, X along the axis), so the cut curves lie in the sketch plane the saved feature rebuilds; each slice becomes a reference plane with method angle (refs first the base plane, second the axis; the angle stored as its size) and its sketch, in the Slices folder as before. The axis must lie in or parallel to the base plane, as for angle planes; the dialog says so otherwise. A whole plane through the axis cuts both sides of it.

D2205: Section view kept as a cut feature (2026-11-08, TR151 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type `section_cut` (Section Cut; `core/features/section_cut.py`; an FDEF owner item) with no refs and no params; data key `zones` holds the zones the section view cut away when it was made (`SectionState.cut_zones`, D1603), each a list of one to three planes as `origin` and unit `normal` in part space. Building it removes, for each zone, the material in front of every plane of the zone: a box on the front side of each plane (a square face on the plane, pushed along the normal past the part), the boxes of one zone intersected, and all zones cut from the part in one boolean (CLAUDE.md 5A.5). Cut faces are named `<fid>/zone<z>.plane<p>`. This takes the up to three turned planes and the zones of a section, which no existing body feature does (D1718). The planes are a copy, as the section view's own planes are only display settings; they do not follow later reference plane changes. The section panel gets Save as Cut Feature: it adds the feature at the end (AddFeature, one undo step, rolled back parts as usual), turns the section view off and says so. A section that removes the whole part gives a feature error saying to move the planes. FDCAD icon feature.section_cut is new and original. Shared files touched: `ui/section/panel.py` and `ui/section/tool.py` (one button and one method).

D2206: 3D relations and dimensions for 3D lines (2026-11-08, TR7 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). planegcs is 2D only, so a small 3D solver is written for the free 3D lines (`core/sketch/solve3d.py`, numpy only, no new dependency): unknowns are the 3D line points; each relation gives residual rows with exact derivatives; a least squares step of smallest size (`numpy.linalg.lstsq`) is repeated until every residual is under 1e-9 mm (60 steps at most), so points move as little as they can from where they are stored. A conflict (residuals above 1e-6 mm after the steps) is a feature error that says to delete a relation or change a length. The 3D sketch data gets `relations` (an FDEF owner item): each `{type, points, value?, at?}` with type along_x, along_y, along_z, coincident, fixed (`at`, the place in mm) or length (`value` in mm: the 3D dimension); points are `"k.i"` (point i of 3D line k, from 1) or `"Pk:eN"` (point eN of plane sketch part k, placed in space and held, so a 3D line can be tied to a sketch on any plane). The solve runs at every rebuild from the stored points (deterministic; the stored points are not rewritten), and the report adds the free movements left (3 times the point count less the rank). The 3D Sketch panel gets a 3D Relations group (type, two point lists, a length, Add Relation and Remove); removing a line or part removes its relations and renumbers the rest. Not built: drawing points in the 3D view with Tab switching the working plane (a new view tool), and relations between two plane sketch parts (each part is solved on its own plane); TR7 stays unticked with that note.

D2207: A depth arrow snapped to a vertex follows it (2026-11-08, TR395 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Alt snap of D525 already sets a depth from a part vertex or face while dragging; what was missing is that the value follows the point. When an extrude depth arrow (`depth` or `depth2`) is let go while Alt snapped it to a part vertex, the 3D view sends `handle_snapped` with the vertex; the feature preview turns it into a stored vertex reference (`naming.select.reference_for` on the part shown) and the panel (`PropertyPanel.link_end`) sets that direction to Up to Vertex on it, so every rebuild measures the depth to the vertex where it is then. Only a Blind direction is linked (Mid Plane and the other end conditions keep the snapped number), and a vertex with no stable name keeps the number. A face snap keeps the number as before. Not built: the same for fillet radius, chamfer distance and hole position handles: those values have no end condition or reference that could follow a point (a fillet radius set "to a vertex" has no meaning once the part changes), so TR395 stays unticked with that note. Shared files touched: `ui/viewport/widget.py` (one signal), `ui/viewport/preview.py`, `ui/property_panel/panel.py`.

D2208: More pick tools (2026-11-08, TR329 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Pick in Volume (Selection menu, `select.in_volume`; `core/pick_volume.py`, `ui/main_window/pick_volume.py`): a dialog takes a box, cylinder (radius, length and an X, Y or Z axis) or sphere, its centre and sizes (starting from the box round the part), what to pick (faces, edges, vertices) and how (inside, outside, touching). A job off the UI thread samples each item (a vertex its point, an edge 9 points, a face the points of its edges and its centre) and tests all samples with numpy at once: inside when every sample is in the volume, outside when none is, touching when some are. The picks replace the selection (`select_shapes`) unless the part rebuilt meanwhile. (2) Paint Selection (`select.paint`, checkable, every open part, like Lasso, D755): a left drag picks every face under the cursor as it passes (faces only while painting, then the filters come back). (3) Pick Bodies Only, Pick Faces Only, Pick Edges Only (`select.only_bodies`, `select.only_faces`, `select.only_edges`): the selection filter takes that one type and turns on (`SelectionFilter.only`); the same command again clears it. No default keys (SHORTCUTS.md is the owner's), so they can be bound in Preferences. Five new original icons. Not built: sizing the volume with handles in the 3D view (typed sizes instead), so TR329 stays unticked with that note.

D2209: Work without dragging (2026-11-08, TR293 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). (1) Handles: a press and release on a handle arrow without moving (within the drag distance) no longer ends the drag: the arrow follows the cursor (the same drag code, Alt snap included) until the next left click sets it. While it follows, Up and Right raise the value by the ruler step (1 mm or 1 degree when the handle has no ruler; Shift a tenth), Down and Left lower it (never under the smallest value), Enter keeps it and Escape puts back the value it had at the click (`ViewportWidget.handle_key`, `finish_click_handle`). Typing a value was already there (the value box, T5.2.3, T15.4). (2) Sketch: with no tool active, the arrow keys move the picked points and curves by `SketchCanvas.nudge_step` (1 mm; Shift 0.1 mm) along the sketch axes through the drag solver (`drag_to`), so relations hold, one sketch undo step per press; with a point picked, Tab picks the next point in drawing order, wrapping round (Tab stays in the sketch then; otherwise it moves focus as before). No owner key is used: arrows and Tab are free in the sketch with no tool (SHORTCUTS.md). (3) Tree: Move Up and Move Down (right click a feature) move it one place through the same check and command as a drop (`FeatureTree.step_feature`). The rollback bar already has Roll Back to Here, and Alt click and Select Other step through the items under the cursor. Not built: placing a sketch dimension label by click then click (its label still drags), so TR293 stays unticked.
D2300: Keep features and Overflow stay unbuilt (2026-11-08, TR64 items 1 and 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). A second check of the kernel's fillet maker (BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet and its ChFi3d builder: Add, SetRadius, SetLaw, SetParams, SetContinuity, SetFilletShape, the contour and fault queries) finds no setting for keeping a boss or cut a round passes over, and none for choosing Keep Edge or Keep Surface where a round overflows onto another face: the builder picks the overflow itself. Both items stay open with a "not built" note on the PLAN.md line, for a kernel with those settings.
D2301: Dome profile sketch; step draft steps not built (2026-11-08, TR147 items 1 and 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Dome gets an optional refs.profile_sketch (an FDEF owner item; the panel's Profile sketch box, empty by default). The sketch's closed outline is read in the sketch's own coordinates, as the flange profile is (D1101): X is the distance out from the middle of the face, Y the height above it, so any sketch plane may hold it and the dome does not depend on a sketch drawn on its own face. The outline is turned a full turn about the sketch's Y axis, the solid is placed with that axis through the face's middle (the disc centre for a round face, else the face's centroid) along the face normal, and it is kept inside the face pushed up past the outline's top (core/features/dome_profile.py), so a round face gets exactly the drawn section and other faces the section cut by their edges. With a profile the Distance, Elliptical and Continuous are not used; Reverse and Direction still work. An outline that crosses X = 0 or dips below Y = 0 is an error. Tapered or square steps for Step Draft (TR147 item 1 rest) are not built: FDCAD's Step Draft drafts each parting level separately and refuses a face that meets parting lines at two heights (D521), so a parting line with steps in it, whose step segments the option would taper, cannot be picked at all; building it needs the parting surface itself split along the stepped line, a new draft method.
D2302: Reapply Fillets on Combine (2026-11-08, TR259, Phase 7B Stage 3). Combine gets reapply_fillets (an FDEF owner item; a tick in the Combine panel, shown for Add, Subtract and Common). The rounds next to the change are the round faces (Remove Fillets' finder, D1410) of a picked body that touch or lie inside another picked body (kernel distance under 1e-4 mm; for Subtract only the main body's rounds, since the tools are used up). They are removed with Delete Face (patch), the combine runs on the sharp bodies, and the edges between the faces each round joined are rounded again with its radius (reapply_fillets.redo, shared with D1420 and D1806). A boolean splits faces into name#k pieces, so the edges are found between the pieces of the two faces as well as between the faces themselves; this answers D1806's point that the new edges where two bodies meet had no round: they stay sharp, and only the rounds that were there are made again. Exclusive, Fragments and Inside at least keep pieces of several bodies apart and are left out.
D2303: Geometry Check smooth and square up fixes and the clip box (2026-11-08, TR262, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new finding kind not_square lists edges between two flat faces whose wedge angle is less than Limits.near_square (default 1 degree, a typed box "Nearly square within") off 90 degrees and more than 1e-6 rad. For a nearly smooth edge (D1416) or a nearly square edge between two flat faces the check (in the background) also works out a turn: the face to turn and the signed angle about the edge's curve direction that makes the faces' normals equal (smooth) or square. The face leaning further off the X, Y and Z axes turns, as the other is most likely the one drawn square; when both lean alike the smaller face turns. Fix adds a Move Face (mode rotate, about the edge, that angle) on that face, one undo step, only on click (CLAUDE.md 5.12), so the geometry moves only where the user asked and Undo takes it back. Curved faces get no turn and no fix: D1807's point stands for them. Square up for a nearly square hole is not built (a hole's axis would have to turn, which Move Face does not do for a cylinder about an outside axis without moving its ends). The clip sphere of the tour is a clip box: the viewer clips only with planes (Graphic3d_ClipPlane, at most 8 per view), so Clip around each finding sets six single plane chains (one per side, so everything outside any side is cut away, D1603) round the finding's box padded by half its size and at least 2 mm, display only. The view's own section is kept and put back when the tick is turned off or the window is closed.
D2304: Chamfer blend corner (2026-11-08, TR321, Phase 7B Stage 3). Chamfer corner gets "blend" (an FDEF owner value of the corner param; the panel's Corners list). Each corner triangle of the kernel's chamfer whose three neighbours are bevel faces of this chamfer is replaced by a face from the kernel's filling (BRepOffsetAPI_MakeFilling, default settings) bounded by the triangle's three edges with a G1 (tangent) constraint to each bevel, put in with a reshape and the shape fixer; the face keeps its corner name. Along the middle of each edge it meets the bevel tangent; at the triangle's three points the two bevels there are not one plane, so no face can be tangent to both and a slight crease stays (the filling's reported G1 error is about 15 degrees at those points on a 2 mm cube corner). Higher filling settings were tried and took far over a minute for one corner, so the defaults are used. The blend bulges out of the flat triangle toward the mitre point, so the volume lies between Patch and Mitre. A corner the filling cannot make, or whose result is not a valid solid, stays a patch with the corner_left warning. Setback stays not built (D1814): the kernel's chamfer maker has no setback setting.
D2305: Edge flanges on curved edges stay unbuilt (2026-11-08, TR166 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Rechecked against the sheet model: a wall is a flat plate in its own frame and a bend a cylinder between two such plates (D333), so a flange along a curved or tangent edge chain, whose wall would be a ruled or conical surface, has no place in the model; building it needs a new wall kind with its own unfolding. The other two parts of item 2 are already met: Up to Vertex ends a flange at a picked point (D1101) and Length 2 to Length 8 change several flanges in one feature (D337). The PLAN.md line stays open with a "not built" note.
D2306: Miter flange arcs and own relief (2026-11-08, TR170, Phase 7B Stage 3). Arcs in the profile: an arc between two lines and tangent to both (within 1e-5 of its radius) is replaced by the sharp corner where the two lines cross, and the bend made there takes the arc as its own radius: the sketch lies on the picked face's side, so for a turn toward that side the arc is the bend's inside (inner radius = arc radius) and for a turn away it is the outside (inner radius = arc radius minus the thickness, an error when that is not above 0). The setback on the sketch line is then exactly the arc's tangent length, so the walls follow the drawn profile, and the bend's allowance is worked out with its own radius. The profile must start and end with a line (an arc at the start would have to be tangent to the sheet, which a profile square to the edge rarely is) and two arcs need a line between them. Own relief: relief, relief_by, relief_ratio, relief_width and relief_depth (FDEF owner items, read only when relief is set, so earlier miter flanges are unchanged; the panel's Own Relief group, as Hem's) cut a rectangular, obround or tear notch into the parent wall at each offset end (D1113), against the end of the bend and reaching the relief depth past its tangent line. The miter flange's own allowance is the Own Bend Values group, already there. Not built: trim side bends. A miter flange's walls start at a free end of the chain, and the side bends a trim would cut belong to earlier flanges on the next edge, which the miter flange does not read; trimming them needs the Edge Flange's neighbour search (D336) rebuilt for a chain whose ends may be mitred, so it is left.
D2307: Convert to Sheet Metal keeps the body and gets rip types (2026-11-08, TR171 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). keep_body (an FDEF owner item; Keep the solid in the panel) keeps the converted solid as its own body beside the sheet: the sheet model gets a kept list of solids that the folded build puts beside the sheet without a boolean (core/features/sheetmetal/model.py), so every later sheet metal feature carries it on, and the flat pattern never holds it. The kept solid overlaps the sheet, as the sheet is its own skin. rip_type (an FDEF owner item; "overlap" when missing, so earlier files build as before) sets how two walls meet at a rip edge: overlap (the wall nearer the fixed face covers the corner, D537), underlap (the later wall covers it), open (both stop the gap short of the other's inside face, so the corner square is empty) or butt (both stop half the gap short of the plane that halves the corner; the cut is a half space box on the far side of that plane in each wall's frame). The type is one for the whole feature. Not built: rip sketches to choose the rips, a type, gap and overlap ratio per rip (rips are found as every edge between walls that is not a bend, with no pick or number the user could tie a value to), and rounded edges of the solid becoming bends with their radius (a converted wall is a flat face; a cylinder face between two flat faces would have to be taken as the bend's own outside, which the converter's setbacks, worked out from sharp corners, do not handle). Converting the kept solid a second time needs a part with several sheet metal bodies (TR281), so Convert still refuses a part that is already sheet metal.
D2308: Closed Corner bend region (2026-11-08, TR174 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Closed Corner gets bend_region ("open" when missing, or "closed"; an FDEF owner item; the panel's Bend region list). D1107 left it because the sheet model's bends have no corner region of their own. A closed region is now made without one: each of the two flanges' bends is run on past both its ends (a copy of the bend, longer by twice the radii, thickness and both lengths), and the common of the two longer bends, the piece of sheet where the two bent surfaces cross (a vault at a square corner of two 90 degree bends), is added to the folded part as a part add of their parent wall (D700), so it is in the folded part only and the flat pattern keeps its corner, as for a gusset. Where the bends already reach into it the fuse merges them. It needs both flanges bent from the same wall; otherwise, or when the two bends do not cross, the region stays open with a warning (code region_open). With this TR174 is complete: every item is built or covered (items 1 to 7: D1107, D1813, D2308).
D2309: Stamp punch, die and corner radii (2026-11-08, TR77, Phase 7B Stage 3). Stamp gets punch_radius, die_radius and corner_radius (optional lengths, 0 when missing; FDEF owner items; three fields in the Stamp panel). Corner radius rounds the outline in plan before the loft: a planar offset in and out by the radius rounds the outward corners, out and in the inward ones (arc joins). Punch radius rounds the top edges with the kernel's fillet: the press solid by the punch radius plus the thickness, the hollow one thickness lower by the punch radius, so the inside of the stamp has the punch radius. Die radius: the press solid is fused with a slab below its foot, the concave edge where the two meet is filleted, and the part below the foot is cut off again, which leaves a flare of that radius where the stamp leaves the wall; the hollow gets the die radius plus the thickness at the wall's other face. D1816 doubted the fillets would keep the two solids one thickness apart; they do for the drafted stamps the tests use (along the press, as before), and a round that does not fit gives an error asking for smaller radii or a larger depth. The flat pattern is unchanged (the blank with the outline marks).
D2310: Rips in the Bend Table (2026-11-08, TR282 item 1 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). The Bend Table window gets a second table of the Rip features above the Flat Pattern that are not suppressed (core/features/sheetmetal/bend_list.rip_rows): R1, R2 and so on, the feature, the kind (sketched, edge, both, or tube, from its refs) and the gap. Picking a row highlights the faces the rip cut (its slit and edge roles). The gap can be typed; OK replaces each changed Rip feature with the new gap, in the same undo macro as the Edit Bends features and the bend order (D1110). A gap of zero or less keeps the window open with a message. Not built, as D1110 found: turning a bend into a rip and back. A bend joins a child wall to its parent in the sheet model's tree; as a rip the child would hang free, and a rip made into a bend has no bend values or child to fold, so the switch would need the model to hold walls joined by rips, which it does not.
D2311: Sketch driven dimples, drawn cut outs and beads (2026-11-08, TR283 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Rather than three new feature types, the sketch driven forms are built from the two that exist. Stamp (D1816) is already a sketch driven dimple; it now takes several closed outlines in one sketch (edges are grouped by shared end points, each group joined into its own wire and pressed as its own stamp, face roles <fid>/stamp, <fid>/stamp2 and so on; earlier stamps keep their names), so several profiles go in one feature. A new Stamp tick, drawn_cut (an FDEF owner item), cuts the stamp's top away along its top outline down past the inside of the cap, which gives the drawn cut out: a hole with a drawn collar. The Forming Tool's rib is already a bead pressed along each sketch line from end to end; rib_ends (an FDEF owner item, "round" when missing, or "square") gives it square ends, a rectangle foot instead of the slot. The flat pattern is unchanged for all of them (the blank, and the stamp outline marks). A bead along a curved path is not built: the rib follows straight lines only, as before (D545).
D2312: Several sheet metal bodies (2026-11-08, TR281, Phase 7B Stage 3; approved by the owner in D750). A part may hold several sheet metal bodies, each with its own Sheet Metal folder (thickness, bend values, relief) and its own Flat Pattern, mixed with solid bodies. This amends D330 (one folder per part) and the Base Flange first solid rule. How: every sheet model records its folder (SheetModel.folder, set from the feature's refs.sheet_metal); latest_sheet and so require_sheet take the last good sheet of the feature's own folder (a model or feature without a folder still goes with any, so one sheet parts and older files build as before). Each sheet metal feature builds only its own sheet; the rebuild engine then puts the part's other bodies back beside it without a boolean (common.with_other_bodies): for a Base Flange every solid of the part so far, for Convert and Insert Bends every solid but the one holding the picked face, and for the others every solid that is not this sheet's own solid from its last feature (SheetResult.own). When a cut changed the sheet's own solid (Fold and the Flat Pattern take such cuts in), solids touching the old sheet count as the sheet, not as other bodies. A non sheet feature after a sheet blocks it only when it changed that sheet's own solid; adding or changing another body does not. Sheet metal features and Flat Patterns of another folder never block. The flat only rule below an unflattened Flat Pattern (D339) holds per folder: features of another folder below it are built as usual (a feature or Flat Pattern without a folder keeps the old rule). A Base Flange is an error only when its own folder already has a sheet; the message says to add a Sheet Metal folder. UI: starting Base Flange, Convert or Insert Bends in a part whose folders all have a sheet adds a new folder after the others and opens its panel first (Cancel takes it back); other tools take the folder of the sheet picked in the view (from the name of the picked face or edge), else the newest sheet's; each folder with a sheet gets a Flat Pattern with refs.sheet_metal naming it (a new FDEF owner key on flatten). Not built: Bend Table and Export Flat Pattern work on the first Flat Pattern only, and one file per body for the flat export (TR173, D1108) stays open.
D2313: Own forming tools from a body (2026-11-08, TR279 in part, Phase 7B Stage 3). Forming Tool gets tool "custom" (Own tool (a body)) with refs.tool_face (the stop face: a flat face of a solid body of the part, the whole tool on one side of it), optional refs.remove_faces (flat faces that leave holes), optional refs.insert (a vertex, the insert point; the stop face's centroid when missing), tool_angle and mirror (all FDEF owner items; named tool_face so the ref does not clash with the tool choice in the panel). The tool body is moved into the form frame: insert point at the origin, stop face on the wall, the tool rising away from it, X along the world X (or Y) laid in the stop face, then mirrored across the line and turned by the angle.
