On each sketch line, as for the built in forms (D545), it is placed on the line's middle along the line, so several lines pattern it. The press is the tool solid less itself one thickness lower (thickness along the press, D545, D1816), so straight sided tools give no side wall, which the guide says. Each removed face cuts a block through the pressing under it along the face's normal. The tool body leaves the part: the rebuild leaves the solid holding the stop face out of the other bodies it carries beside the sheet (D2312). Not built: saving tools to a library and placing them from it. A tool would have to live in another file that the rebuild reads, and a forming tool needs only the solid, so modelling the tool body in the part is the way for now; a library needs an owner choice on where tool files live.
D2400: Pattern instance markers (2026-11-08, TR59, Phase 7B Stage 3). While a Linear, Circular, Sketch, Table or Point Pattern or a Pattern Chain is open in the property panel, PreviewGeometry gets markers (core/features/pattern_markers.py, no Qt): each copy's instance number (as typed in Skip: 3 or 2.2) and a point, the middle of the bounding box of the seed (the faces its seed features made in the part before the pattern, the picked seed faces, or the picked bodies) moved by that copy's transform. Skipped copies keep their marker, so a copy can be given values before it is brought back; an exploded copy (only) and patterns of more than 200 copies show none, and a pattern whose placements fail shows none. The view draws them as value labels with the text '#3' and the param 'instance:3' (the same label layer, colour and spreading as T15.2 value labels), so no new view code was needed; clicking one goes through value_clicked to FeaturePreview.edit_value, which starts that copy's entry in Copy values with add_instance_values (D1900) and puts the cursor after it, instead of opening a value box. Vary Sketch (item 4) is not built: copies are moved copies of the seed's solid, and re-solving the seed's sketch against the faces each copy lands on would need a sketch solve and a feature build per copy against moved geometry, which the pattern engine does not do; the PLAN line stays open with a note.

D2401: Box skip over instance markers (2026-11-08, TR270 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). A box dragged in the view while a pattern panel shows instance markers (D2400) and at least one marker lies inside the box skips those copies instead of box selecting: the view emits markers_boxed with the marker labels (ViewportWidget.markers_in, screen positions of the labels inside the box rectangle), and FeaturePreview.skip_boxed adds them to the panel's Instances to Skip field in the order boxed, keeping entries already there. Ctrl while dragging toggles: boxed copies already skipped are brought back. Skipped copies keep their markers so they can be boxed again. A box with no marker inside selects as before. Hiding copies in the view only (item 2 rest) is not built: the copies of one pattern are faces of the one result solid, which the view draws as one shape, so hiding some would need a second display shape built per pattern; the existing Preview Partial setting already keeps live previews of big patterns fast.

D2402: Patterns of reference geometry (2026-11-08, TR142 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). The small form: Linear Pattern and Circular Pattern accept one reference feature (plane, ref_plane, ref_axis, ref_point or coord_system) as their only refs.features seed (core/features/pattern_datums.py, no Qt; no new FDEF keys). The pattern then copies that datum to every placement (skipped copies left out) and leaves the part as it is: its result keeps the body, has no datum of its own and lists the copies in extras datums as (instance label, Datum) pairs, which the view draws (a square outline for planes, the datum's own lines for the others; MainWindow.datum_shapes). A reference feature mixed with other seeds, faces or bodies is a feature error with a next step. To use a copy as a reference, Explode Pattern (D1902) turns each copy into its own feature (only key) whose result carries that copy as its datum, and as its plane for a plane, so sketches, ref features (datum picks read result.datum or result.plane) and plane picks in the view (plane_faces and plane_names now include such copies) use it like any reference feature. A copy inside an unexploded pattern cannot be picked on its own, since a FeatureResult holds one datum and references name a feature; that kept the change small. Sketch, Table, Point Pattern and Pattern Chain do not copy reference geometry.

D2403: Several loft connectors per profile (2026-11-08, TR136 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Loft gets match_<k> (text, FDEF owner item): more connectors for profile k as vertex numbers such as "3, 6", counted like connect_<k> (vertex n starts edge n, before the connection point turns the wire). Each connector is kept as its point, so it survives the connection point and the profile being turned to face along the loft. Every profile with a wire must list the same number. At build time (core/features/loft_connectors.py) each wire is cut at its connectors into stretches, found in the order they come along the final wire, and every stretch is given as many edges as the same stretch has on the profile with the most, by halving the longest edge at its middle parameter until the counts match (at most 64), then the wires go to ThruSections with its own alignment off, so the kernel pairs edges one to one and stretch i of every profile meets stretch i of the others. Split pieces of the first profile keep their sketch line's side/<entity> face name (the unsplit edge under the piece's middle). Connectors are refused on closed lofts and with guides or a centerline. The panel's Profiles group gets a Connectors text field for the selected profile next to the connection point, and Reset clears every connection point and connector. Dragging connectors in the view is not built: the view has no vertex handles on sketch profiles (D220 item 6), and typed vertex numbers do the same job.

D2404: Add Loft Section (2026-11-08, TR136 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). The feature tree menu of a loft gets Add Loft Section, which asks for a position as one number (1.5 is halfway between profiles 1 and 2) rather than a pick in the view, since a click on the loft's side face gives no profile order. Both neighbours must be sketches on parallel planes (core/features/loft_section.py, no Qt). It adds, in one undo step and just before the loft, a ref_plane (method offset from the first neighbour sketch's plane reference, by the fraction of the gap, flipped when the gap runs against the plane's normal) and a sketch on it holding the loft's cross section there, made with BRepAlgoAPI_Section of the loft's own solid: straight edges (or curves within 0.0001 mm of their chord) become lines, full circles circles, other curves 12 lines through points on them, with shared end points so the sketch is one closed region. The sketch becomes the loft's profile after the first neighbour, connect_ and match_ numbers of later profiles move up by one, and the sketch opens for editing. Curved sections drawn as short lines facet the loft slightly there until the user edits them.

D2405: Swept Cut with a tool body (2026-11-08, TR138 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep's profile_type gets "body" with refs.tool_body (one face reference of the body, FDEF owner items), offered in the panel for Swept Cut only; a boss with it is a feature error with a next step. The body moves along the path without turning (a milling cutter path), from the path end nearer its bounding box centre, by the path point less that end. The kernel has no sweep of a solid, so core/features/sweep_body.py follows the path as straight moves (line pieces as they are, curves by GCPnts_TangentialDeflection within 0.05 mm and 0.2 radians, at most 200 moves) and builds each move's swept space exactly: the tool is split in two by the plane through its middle square to the move (where the outline of a body of revolution about an axis square to or along the move lies), every face of each half is pushed along the move with BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism (faces along the move give no volume and are left out), and the tool is added at the far end; all pieces go into one general fuse, then UnifySameDomain. A half with a face whose normals point both ways along the move (not a round or flat sided tool) is refused with a next step. Copies of the tool spaced along the path were tried first and were far too slow (over two minutes for a 30 mm slot). The cut uses combine_or_keep like any sweep; the tool body lies inside the swept space, so it is removed with the material, which is what a cutter body is for. Faces are named tool/face<k> in explorer order. Item 2, a group picker joining pieces of several sketches and edges into one chain with trim and extend, is not built: it needs a new chain editing widget, and paths of model edges (path_edges) and sketch chains already cover most uses.

D2406: Vent draft and fillet per element group (2026-11-08, TR146 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Vent gets rib_draft, spar_draft and fill_draft (angles) and rib_fillet, spar_fillet and fill_fillet (lengths), FDEF owner items, in a new Draft and Fillet group of the panel; the offset per group already existed (rib_offset, spar_offset, fill_offset). The draft leans the walls of a group's bars (core/features/vent_shape.py, BRepOffsetAPI_DraftAngle through fastening.draft_sides) so they get narrower going into the wall, the neutral plane being the bars' outer face at the group's offset; the bar ends that sit on the opening's wall are left upright, so the bars stay joined to the part. The fillet rounds the edges of the bars' outer face except those on the opening's outline. Negative values, and a draft or fillet the kernel cannot make, are feature errors with a next step. 0 changes nothing, so older files build as before.

D2407: Lip and Groove rim by edges, jump gaps and wall draft (2026-11-08, TR146 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Lip and Groove gets refs.lip_edges and refs.groove_edges (edges round the opening; the flat face next to each edge that has an opening is used as the rim, added to the rim faces without repeats), jump_gaps (a length) and follow_wall (a boolean), FDEF owner items. Jump Gaps closes notches in the opening narrower than the value before the band is made, by growing the opening outline by half the value and shrinking it back (a morphological closing with BRepOffsetAPI_MakeOffset), so the band crosses rib tops flush with the rim instead of going round them; the closed notch corners round off slightly. Follow Wall Draft reads the lean of the part's wall at the first edge of the opening (the wall face's normal there, turned to point into the opening; its part along the rim normal is the sine of the lean) and leans both walls of the band by it, outward going up for a lip and the matching way down into the wall for a groove, on top of any Lip Draft or Groove Draft taper. Lip only or groove only on a body already worked (D318).

D2408: Ground spring ends (2026-11-08, TR162 item 2 rest, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sweep gets ground_ends (a boolean, FDEF owner item; the Ground ends tick in the sweep's options): after the sweep is built (and before it is combined), the solid is cut by two half spaces through the path's start and end points, square to the spring's axis, keeping the side between them (core/features/sweep_ground.py). The axis is the helix's own axis, the normal of its circle sketch turned to run from the path's start to its end, when the path is a Helix feature; for any other path it is the line from start to end, and a closed path is refused with a next step. The new flat faces are named ground/start and ground/end. D1923 had said the flat belongs to the swept spring rather than the curve; it is now an option of the sweep, so it follows the helix.

D2409: Hex fasteners sample (2026-11-08, TR162 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new sample hex_fasteners (src/fdcad/samples/parts_print.py, tutorial hex-fasteners.md) builds an ISO M6 hexagon head bolt, hexagon nut and plain washer as three bodies, with every size read from FDCAD's own tables when the sample is built: hole_data.find('iso', 'M6') for the thread, the nut's flats and height and the tap drill, and hole_heads.washer('M6') for the washer (12 mm, 1.6 mm), with the close clearance (6.4 mm, the ISO 7089 hole) for its hole. The hexagon head height (ISO 4017, 4 mm for M6) is not in the screw table, which holds socket heads, so the sample states it as a constant. Threads are cosmetic, so the golden result is quick and exact; the nut_and_bolt sample (D2003) already shows modelled threads. A node graph that builds fasteners from a size was not made: the node editor has no nodes that read the screw tables. A ground spring sample was built too but is left out: the helix's ends and end_pitch (D1923) and Sweep's ground_ends (D2408) are not in FDEF_SPEC.md yet, and samples may only write keys the spec lists (tests/core/io/test_schema_keys.py), so it waits for the owner's spec update; the guide describes the steps instead. The sample is saved with app_version 0.1.0 like the others, and only its entry was added to the golden results. Its nut and washer sit on offset planes centred on their sketch origins, because a hexagon sketched off its origin was solved back 1.2e-6 mm from its saved points, which the sketches solve in place test refuses.

D2410: Stone Setting (2026-11-08, TR408 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type stone_setting (core/features/stone_setting.py; command feature.stone_setting in the 3D Print tab's dropdown with Face Seats, no key; a body tools form), FDEF owner items: refs.seat_face (one flat face) and refs.seat_point (optional: a vertex, sketch point or reference point, moved onto the face's plane; the face's middle without one), params stone_diameter, girdle_depth (default 0.3 mm), pavilion_angle (default 41 degrees, a round brilliant; 10 to 80 allowed), prongs (0 to 12, default 4), prong_diameter (default 12 percent of the stone, at least 0.6 mm) and prong_height (default 40 percent of the stone). The seat is a straight wall the stone's diameter wide and the girdle depth deep, opening 0.01 mm above the face so no skin is left, then a cone narrowing to a point at the pavilion angle; it is cut first. The prongs are cylinders with round tips standing with their middles a quarter diameter outside the girdle (so each overlaps the stone's edge), spaced evenly from the face's first direction and sunk one diameter into the part; they are added in one general fuse. Faces: seat/wall, seat/cone and prong<k>/side. Bezels, bearing notches cut into the prongs and stones other than round are not offered.

D2411: Sprue Tree and kit frame (2026-11-08, TR408 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type sprue_tree (core/features/sprue_tree.py; command feature.sprue_tree in the same dropdown; a body tools form), FDEF owner items: refs.feed_points (vertices, sketch points or reference points, at least one, at most 200), refs.cup (a point, tree only), params layout (tree, the default, or kit_frame), cup_diameter, cup_height, sprue_diameter, gate_diameter and margin. A tree has a pouring cup (a cone from the cup diameter at the cup point to the sprue diameter, cup_height deep) on the line from the cup point to the middle of the feed points; the trunk runs on along that line as far as the farthest point; a gate runs square from the trunk to each point, with balls at the joints. A kit frame is a rectangular runner in the plane through the points' middle (square to their least spread by an SVD, or the model Z for fewer than three points or points on a line) with its sides along model X (or Y) laid in that plane, margin outside the points, and a gate from each point straight to the nearest side. Everything is joined to the part in one general fuse (the pieces overlap each other, so a compound would be invalid as one argument). Faces: cup, trunk, gate<k>, frame. The tree's layout is the simplest one a caster builds by hand; branching trees with several trunks are not offered.

D2412: Local deform modes (2026-11-08, TR67, Phase 7B Stage 3). Three new deform feature types in core/deform/local.py (FDEF owner items), on the shared DeformFeature (bodies pick, NURBS deformation, tolerance and approximate warning, D393) but without a triad or trim planes in their panels (the triad params stay valid and unused): deform_point (refs point, direction, fixed; distance, radius, stiffness), deform_curve (refs initial, target, fixed; radius) and surface_push (refs point, direction; tool sphere, ellipsoid or rectangle, depth, tool_x, tool_y, reach). Deform Point moves points by distance times (1 - t^2)^2, t running from 0 at stiffness times the radius to 1 at the radius (smooth at both ends); without a direction it uses the outward normal of the face nearest the point. Curve to Curve samples both curves at 96 points by length and moves each point by the Gaussian weighted average of the nearby sample moves (width the sample spacing), faded by the same falloff over the radius from the initial curve; Match Tangent is not offered, since the move field is already smooth across the curve. Surface Push moves points along the push by the tool's profile (a sphere cap, an ellipsoid as deep as tool_x, or a flat rectangle with sides rounded over a fifth of its size) faded to nothing over reach below the touch point, so the volume taken is the tool's cap. Fixed faces and edges hold by a factor from 0 on them to 1 a radius away, measured to a 24 by 24 parameter grid on each face and 32 points on each edge with the grid's own spacing taken off; all maps are numpy arrays in chunks. A picked body as a push tool is not offered: its profile is not a height field over the face. Commands in a dropdown in the Bodies tab's Deform group.

D2413: Single line fonts not built (2026-11-08, TR75 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Sketch text is laid out from the system's outline fonts as closed regions (D323), and Wrap's scribe splits faces along wrapped regions. A single line font needs its own glyph strokes (an FDCAD font or a GPL compatible one) and then open stroke curves through text layout, sketch display, DXF and SVG export and a Wrap that wraps open curves rather than faces. That is a new text path end to end, larger than this round's time for the item, so it is left open on the PLAN line.

D2414: Roof (2026-11-08, TR258, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type roof (core/features/roof.py; command feature.roof in the Features tab's Modify group, a dropdown with Dome, no key; a body tools form), FDEF owner items: refs.sketch and params slope (default 30 degrees, 1 to 85 allowed), max_height (optional flat cut) and operation (boss or cut). The roof's top over a point is tan(slope) times the point's distance to the nearest outline edge, which is the equal pitch roof for any outline, convex or not, with holes as courtyards: it is built as each region's prism less, for every outline edge (curves as 16 straight pieces, at most 400), the space above that edge's tent (cones at both ends and a wedge along it, together the stadium shaped set over the piece), all in one general cut. The new icons for this round's commands (roof, stone setting, sprue tree, deform point, curve to curve, surface push) are drawn for FDCAD on the 24 grid. Item 2, growing a body by a sphere, is the existing Offset Body with Rounded corners (D825), which the guide now points to; growing by another shape (a Minkowski sum with a box or a picked body) is not built, since the kernel has no Minkowski sum and a box grow is the sharp corner offset already there.

D2415: Move Body by relations (2026-11-08, TR268 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). Move and Copy Body gets mode "relations" with refs.rel_from and refs.rel_to (paired picks in order) and relations (text, one relation per pair: coincident, distance <mm>, angle <degrees>, parallel), FDEF owner items (core/features/body_relations.py, no Qt). A pick is a plane when resolve_placement reads it as one (a flat face, a plane feature), else an axis (a round face or edge, a straight edge, an axis feature). Coincident planes face each other (normals opposite, offset 0) and distance adds the gap; coincident axes are the same line; angle compares the normals or axes; parallel makes them point the same way. The six unknowns of one rigid move (a turn vector and a shift about the bodies' centre) are solved together by damped least squares (Levenberg Marquardt with a numeric Jacobian, at most 200 steps), started from no move and from half turns about X, Y and Z so a body can flip over, keeping the best; every residual must be under 1e-6, else the feature error says the relations cannot all hold. No other mate types (tangent, symmetric) and no limits: it is a placement, not an assembly solver. Copies repeat the move as in the other modes.

D2416: Transform handle pivot and axes (2026-11-08, TR268 item 3, Phase 7B Stage 3). Move and Copy Body gets pivot (body_centre, the default, or picked with refs.pivot_point: a vertex, sketch point or reference point) and handle_axes (model, the default, or plane_axes with refs.handle_plane: a plane or flat face, whose own X, Y and normal are used), FDEF owner items, shown for Delta X, Y, Z and for turns about the centre, the two moves the transform handles write. The pivot sets where the arrows and rings sit and the point turns about the centre go about; picking a point moves only the handle, not the body, which is the spec's handle only mode. With plane axes, Delta X, Y, Z run along the plane's X, Y and normal and the turns go about them, and the arrows and rings point that way. The spec's 'last pick' pivot is the picked point; a body's own axes are not offered, since a body has no stored frame (Frame to frame, D1815, covers turning to a body's faces).

D2417: Linked Body Copy (2026-11-08, TR154, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type linked_copy (core/features/linked_copy.py; command feature.linked_copy in the Bodies tab's dropdown with Move and Copy Body; a body tools form), FDEF owner items: refs.bodies, params place (offset, the default, with dx, dy, dz and rx, ry, rz turned about the bodies' centre before the shift; or on_frame with refs.frame, a coordinate system or plane: the copy sits on it as the original sits on the model origin) and data link (true unless broken). So that it follows changes made to the original further down the tree, the rebuild engine builds linked copies, and every later feature whose references name a deferred feature (its id or its faces), after all other features, each group in its own order (deferred_order, one line in RebuildEngine.rebuild; body_before for the live preview uses the same order). The tree keeps the user's order. Break Link (feature tree menu) turns the link off and moves the features into the order they are built in, in one undo step (MoveFeature steps and a ReplaceFeature), so the copy is then built in its place and stays as it is; the copy keeps its id and face names (<fid>/copy/<name>), so features on it stay attached. Changing the rebuild order is a rebuild engine change (CLAUDE.md 1A item 2) and is the smallest form found: features that refer to the copy simply wait for it.

D2418: Lasting face relations (2026-11-08, TR266, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type face_relation (core/features/face_relation.py; command feature.face_relation in the Direct Editing group, a dropdown with Merge Faces; a body tools form), FDEF owner items: param relation (coplanar, offset, concentric, parallel, perpendicular, equal_radius, fixed) and refs.faces (two faces; one or more for fixed). It leaves the part as it is (makes_solid off), checks the relation holds now (a warning with a next step when not; wrong face kinds are an error) and is listed in the tree like any feature, so the user's own tree folders hold them together rather than a special folder. Every later Move Face reads the relations above it (core/features/face_relation.partners, called next to the locked size partners of D800): a picked fixed face is a feature error naming the relation; otherwise the partner face joins the move when the mode needs it to keep the relation (coplanar and offset: offset, translate, rotate, with the Offset factor the dot of the two normals so opposite faces of a wall move the same way; concentric: translate and rotate; parallel and perpendicular: rotate; equal radius: offset and resize). Tangent and symmetric are not offered: keeping them needs the partner moved by a different motion than the picked face, which the Move Face engine does not do.

D2419: Move the part origin (2026-11-08, TR343, Phase 7B Stage 3). The built in origin feature takes optional ox, oy, oz (lengths) and rx, ry, rz (angles, turned about X, then Y, then Z, like Move and Copy Body's origin turns), FDEF owner items on an existing type (core/features/reference.py). With any of them set, the origin's result carries its frame as a datum, the three main planes are built moved by the same placement, origin axis picks ({feature: f1, axis: x}) and origin point picks follow it. Geometry that is not built on the main planes or the origin, such as an imported body, stays where it is in the world; features built on the main planes follow them, so every reference keeps working, which is how the spec's 'geometry stays' and 'features keep their references' fit together. The feature tree menu of Origin gets Move Part Origin: a choice of the box centre of the bodies, their centre of volume, the selected vertex or face (its box centre), or back to the model origin, written as the origin's ox, oy, oz in one undo step (turns are kept; they are typed in the values for now, since the origin has no panel). Export and the coordinates the status bar shows stay in the model's own coordinates.

D2420: Insert Part (2026-11-08, TR71, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new feature type insert_part (core/features/insert_part.py; command feature.insert_part in the Bodies tab's Import dropdown, which asks for the file first and works on an empty part too; a body tools form), FDEF owner items: params part_file (the path as picked), link (default true), keep_bodies (text, body numbers from 1), with_sketches and with_planes (booleans), place with dx, dy, dz, rx, ry, rz or refs.frame (as Linked Body Copy, D2417, about the source's own origin), and refs.embedded after Break Link. Linked, the source is read with the part file reader (data only, CLAUDE.md 5 item 10) and rebuilt with a fresh engine at each rebuild; key_data is the file's path, size, time and SHA1, so the rebuild cache rebuilds it exactly when the file changes. A missing file is a feature error naming the path it looked at; a damaged one names the error type; a part that inserts itself, directly or through other inserted parts, is refused (a per thread stack of real paths). The bodies are new bodies with faces named <fid>/part/face<k> in the kernel's order; sketch outlines (the edges of each sketch's regions) and the source's ref_plane features (square outlines) come in as reference lines in extras, not as features, since references name features of this part. Break Link (tree menu) writes the kept bodies as a STEP block into this part (FDEF_SPEC 11 blocks, as Import STEP Body does) and turns the link off, in one undo step for the feature; the block stays after an undo, as unused data. A list picker of the source's items is the Bodies to bring in text field, since the panel has no list widget for another file's contents.

D2421: Bodies to linked part files (2026-11-08, TR280, Phase 7B Stage 3). Tools, Bodies to Part Files (command tools.bodies_to_files, no key; ui/main_window/bodies_to_files.py) saves the selected bodies, or every body, each to its own file in a folder: Linked FDCAD parts, FDCAD parts, STEP, STL or 3MF. A linked part (core/io/save_bodies.save_linked_parts, no kernel work) is a new part whose only feature is an Insert Part (D2420) of that body number of the master, by the master's absolute path, with the link on, so changes saved to the master flow on when the linked part rebuilds; the master must be saved first, and a file that would replace the master is refused. The other formats use the existing Save Bodies writers (D528) on a worker. The pieces of a Split are bodies of the part, so they are covered; files are named '<part> body <n>'. Body numbers follow the master's body order, so a change that reorders the master's bodies changes which body a linked part shows; the linked part's Bodies to bring in field can be edited then.

D2422: Library feature rest not built (2026-11-08, TR72, Phase 7B Stage 3). A library file still holds one feature and its sketch (D2115) and is inserted through Paste. Several features in one file, asking for each face the saved feature was attached to, hiding internal dimensions and keeping a link to the file (item 3) all need a placement model of their own: a list of attachment faces stored with the features and mapped to new picks at insert time, and a feature that re-reads the file. That is a larger design than this round left time for after Insert Part (D2420), whose linked file and Break Link are the model a library link would follow. The PLAN line stays open with a note.
D2500: Section View chooses the bodies it cuts (2026-11-08, TR213, Phase 7B Stage 3). The section panel gets a Bodies Cut list (shown with two or more bodies), every body ticked by default. An unticked body is kept whole: `SectionState.whole` holds its index in the part's solids, and the saved section stores it as `whole` (absent when every body is cut, so older files read the same). The 3D view hides the kept bodies in the part drawing and draws them again as one unclipped, unpicked drawing in the part colour, because the view's clipping planes apply to whole drawings, not to one body inside the part. The kept bodies cannot be picked while the section is on; turning the section off or ticking them again restores picking.

D2501: Section Planes tree folder with arrows and rings (2026-11-08, TR213, Phase 7B Stage 3). While a part's section is on, the feature tree shows a Section Planes folder below the global variables, one row per plane named "Section 2 (Right)" and so on (Section 1 turning about an axis says Axis). It is a view row, not document data, so it never changes the file. Clicking a plane makes it the active plane: the section panel opens if it was closed and the 3D view shows that plane's offset arrow and two rotation rings; double click or Edit Section opens the panel; Turn Off Section turns it off. The X ring turns about the plane's reference X axis and the Y ring about its Y axis after the X turn, the order `cut_plane` uses, so each ring's tip stays in the turned plane. Ring handle values are kept between 0 and one turn (handle values stay positive) and read back as minus half a turn to half a turn. Ring radius is three arrow sizes. Section 1's offset arrow keeps its old parameter name `section_offset`; the others are `section_offset:N`, `section_rot_x:N` and `section_rot_y:N`. Also fixed: reopening the panel on a section with two or three planes raised an error while the panel was still being built.

D2502: Measure on section cut faces (2026-11-08, TR213, Phase 7B Stage 3). The section caps are drawn by the viewer's clipping, so they are not faces. `fdcad/core/section_faces.py` builds real faces: for each zone cut away and each of its planes, the plane (a square face larger than the part) in common with every body that is cut, then in common with the half space in front of each other plane of that zone. With several zones, a face whose inside point, stepped a micrometre behind its plane, is itself cut away lies between two removed zones and is dropped. A kernel failure gives no faces, never an error. The faces are built on the kernel worker 200 ms after the section stops changing and after each rebuild, and the 3D view draws them 95 percent see through over the caps, never clipped and pickable with the same selection filters as the part, so Measure, the status bar values and the selection read them like any face. They are view data and never saved.

D2503: Curvature Colors on faces (2026-11-08, TR199 item 1, Phase 7B Stage 3). A new checkable command, Curvature Colors (`evaluate.curvature_colors`, Evaluate tab, Curves group beside Zebra Stripes; no default key; original icon), colours each face by one value, blue to red through a five stop ramp, with a small tool window holding the kind, the scale and its end values, and the value under the cursor. One colour per face, not per mesh point: per point colours would need a colour per mesh node, which the kernel's drawing only takes one node at a time (a Python loop over mesh points, against CLAUDE.md 5A). Planes, cylinders and spheres get their exact value; other faces are sampled on a fixed 5 by 5 parameter grid (at most 25 evaluations per face, whatever the mesh) and take the sample of largest size, so a face shows its tightest spot. Kinds: Largest (the larger principal curvature by size, 1/mm, the default, read as one over the tightest radius), Mean (1/mm, signed) and Gaussian (1/mm squared, zero on flat and singly curved faces). The scale runs from the smallest to the largest value on the part. The readout under the cursor projects the cursor point onto the face and evaluates there, a single small kernel call on the UI thread like the hover status (D1611); the face colouring runs on a worker after every rebuild (the analysis overlay base). Values show in 1/mm or 1/in, squared for Gaussian. Display only, never saved.

D2504: Start page and the part picture (2026-11-08, TR218 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). While no part is open the document area shows a start page (a widget laid over the empty tab area, so the central widget stays the tab widget): New Part and Open buttons, then the recent parts as 128 px pictures in a grid, pinned parts first in pin order, then the other recent files. Double click or Enter opens a part (a missing file gives a status message); the right click menu has Open, Pin or Unpin, Remove from List (also unpins and takes it off the recent files) and Show in Folder (opens the containing folder through the desktop services, without selecting the file, which needs platform code). Pins are a setting (`files/pinned`) and are never pushed off by the ten recent files limit. Dropping files on the window already opened them (TR377, D765); the grid leaves drops to the window. Each save renders a 128 px picture of the 3D view and keeps it in the part file as the new top level key `thumbnail` (a base64 PNG, written only once a picture exists, so parts saved without a 3D view, such as samples and tests, are unchanged) and a copy in the data folder's thumbnails cache, named by a hash of the full path, so the start page need not read part files; without a cached copy it reads the picture from part files of up to 4 MB. A save without a 3D view keeps the old picture. A failed picture never stops a save. The new FDEF key `thumbnail` is for the owner to add to FDEF_SPEC.md.

D2505: First run lessons that check the result (2026-11-08, TR291 item 2, Phase 7B Stage 3). Help, Lessons (a Help menu entry after Welcome, and a Start Lessons button on the first run welcome) opens a non modal tool window. Two lessons ship, kept in `fdcad/core/lessons.py` as data with a check per step: Your First Part (draw a rectangle, fully define the sketch, extrude a solid, add a fillet, save) and Cuts, Holes and Patterns (make a solid, cut with an extruded or revolved cut or a hole, repeat with a linear or circular pattern, mirror). Each check reads the part after the last rebuild: features of the type that rebuilt without an error and are not suppressed, a sketch with four or more non construction lines, a sketch whose solve status is fully defined, a body count above zero, and the part saved with no changes since (a part never saved does not count). Checks run after every rebuild, when the part's saved state changes, when the shown part changes and when the window opens, so the user may work any way they like; a ticked step stays ticked, and a check that raises does not tick. The next step is bold. Resume Later hides the window and keeps the progress; Start Over clears the lesson's ticks. Progress and the lesson shown are settings (`help/lessons`, `help/lesson_current`), never part data. The window does not move the user through the tools itself: checks only read the part.

D2506: Taskbar and Dock progress (2026-11-08, TR380 item 4, Phase 7B Stage 3). The status bar progress (StatusFeedback, D673) also drives the taskbar: when the progress bar shows (after the 300 ms delay), the Windows taskbar button shows a moving bar, or a filled one while steps are known, and the Mac Dock icon shows a badge with the percentage, or "..." while the amount is not known; both go when the last work ends. This covers rebuilds and exports, which already used StatusFeedback, and the hand off to the slicer, which now does too (key "slice"). No new dependency: Windows uses the shell's ITaskbarList3 COM object through ctypes (vtable slots HrInit 3, SetProgressValue 9, SetProgressState 10) on the window's handle, and the Mac uses the Objective-C runtime through ctypes (NSApplication's dockTile, setBadgeLabel: and display), since a Dock progress bar would need a custom view. The backend is made on first use, only while the system integration is on (D948), so tests and other platforms never touch the taskbar; repeated states are skipped and a failed platform call is ignored. Both platform paths are checked by hand on the target machines (CI has no taskbar); the shared logic is tested with a recording backend.

D2507: Freeze bar (2026-11-08, TR98, Phase 7B Stage 3, owner approved in D750). The bar's place is the id of the last frozen feature, kept in the part file under the new top level key `freeze_bar` (in `Document.extra`, so the document model and the file reader need no change and older FDCAD versions keep the key; absent when nothing is frozen; a place naming a missing feature or one of the default planes and origin counts as nothing). Frozen features are the features from the first one after the default planes and origin down to the bar. On a rebuild the engine keeps the first good result each frozen feature had while frozen (in `RebuildEngine.frozen_results`, so the first rebuild after opening a part builds them once) and reuses it whatever changed above or in it, listing it as reused; a feature that leaves the frozen set drops its kept result and builds normally from the cache keys. Features after the bar use the kept result's body and key as usual. Frozen features cannot be edited: Edit Feature (and a double click) says why in the status bar and names the fix. The tree shows a "Freeze bar" row below the last frozen feature, in the selection colour, with a tooltip; frozen rows add the same tooltip line. A feature's right click menu offers Freeze Up to Here, or Move Freeze Bar Above Here for a frozen feature; the bar's menu offers Unfreeze All. Each move is one undo step (SetFreezeBar). The bar is independent of the rollback bar: frozen features below the rollback bar are simply not built. Not built: dragging the freeze bar with the mouse or arrow keys (the menu commands move it). The new FDEF key `freeze_bar` is for the owner to add to FDEF_SPEC.md.

D2508: Custom command tabs and a simple mode (2026-11-08, TR222, Phase 7B Stage 3, owner approved in D750; RIBBON_SPEC R1 to R3 still hold for the built in tabs). Right clicking a command button offers Add to My Commands (or Remove from My Commands) and, on the built in tabs, Hide Button. My Commands is one user tab, made from the setting `appearance/custom_commands` in the order added, with large buttons and their names, eight to a group (each group under 900 px wide, round 14 rule 4), placed after the other tabs and shown only while it has a command. Hidden buttons are the setting `appearance/hidden_buttons`; a group whose buttons are all hidden hides too; Show Hidden Buttons on the tab bar menu brings them back. Simple Mode (tab bar menu, setting `appearance/simple_mode`, off by default) shows only the Features, Sketch, Evaluate and My Commands tabs, and on Features and Evaluate only Sketch, Extruded Boss, Revolved Boss, Extruded Cut, Hole Tool, Revolved Cut, Fillet, Chamfer, Linear and Circular Pattern, Mirror, Shell, Plane, Measure, Mass Properties, Section View and Rebuild; the Sketch tab keeps every tool and My Commands keeps what the user put there. A dropdown button counts as the command of its first tool. Simple mode never writes the user's own hidden tabs: the tab tick boxes now remember the user's choice by tab name, so leaving simple mode shows exactly what the user had. Commands stay reachable from the menus and the command search in every mode. All of it is settings, never part data.

D1028: Surfacing, assemblies and drawings out of scope (2026-11-08, owner). (1) The owner said to keep assemblies, surfacing and drawings out of scope. Assemblies and drawings were already out of scope (PLAN.md section 2). (2) Surfacing is taken back out: this reverses D850. PLAN.md Phase 8 (SF0 to SF17) is removed and nothing in it is built. `docs/SURFACE_SPEC.md` stays in the repository as history. The Delete option of Delete Face stays greyed (D510, D529 item 4). (3) The section 2 out of scope line now names all surface modelling. D6 and the D750 note that surface building tools stay out of scope hold again.

D1029: Phase 7B closes with its leftovers in IDEAS.md (2026-11-09, owner). (1) After round 14 every Phase 7B TR line had its buildable parts done. What was left on 27 lines (TR7, TR59, TR63, TR72, TR136, TR163, TR166, TR171, TR279, TR282, TR293, TR379, TR394, TR395, TR53, TR64, TR75, TR100, TR111, TR138, TR147, TR170, TR223, TR270, TR321, TR329, TR380) is one of: a kernel limit (setback and transition settings, D1814; Minkowski sums, D2414), an owner choice (a key for rigid drag, the up direction for new parts, a 3D mouse, a texture from an image, the Windows jump list New Part task, the F1 key, where forming tool files live), or a large piece recorded as not built in its decision (Vary Sketch, single line fonts, a chain editing widget, view handles for loft connectors and pick volumes, and the like). D1030: CI checks clean again (2026-11-09, Phase 7B close). (1) GitHub has not started a CI job for some time: the account's payments failed or its spending limit is used up, an owner setting. While CI did not run, rounds 12 to 14 left 1 unformatted file, 9 lint errors (tests only) and 141 mypy errors in `fdcad/ui` (`fdcad/core`, the strict part, stayed clean). All are fixed and the checks were run by hand on Windows. (2) Several were latent bugs, not typing noise: attributes that hid Qt's own methods (`size` on the polygon, gear and code tag dialogs and on Pick in Volume, `window` on the lessons, start page and display states windows, `result` on Configuration Preview, which hid `QDialog.result()`, and `size` on Display Quality). They are renamed (`size_box`, `size_label`, `size_boxes`, `main`, `built`, `part_size`). (3) Attributes that installers set on the main window, the document tab and the sketch canvas (Print fit, undercut, edge angle and layer preview tools, the pause action, breadcrumbs, the sketch grid) are now declared on their classes. (4) The rest are None checks for Qt getters that can return None, `bool()` round comparisons with Any, and named methods in place of `x and y()` lambdas. Behaviour is unchanged.
Status: Locked

D1031: Feature previews use the overlay look (2026-11-09, owner request). The owner asked that the previews of Fillet, Chamfer, Extrude and every other feature look like the overlay style common in CAD tools, and chose it over keeping the finished part look of D583. `docs/PREVIEW_SPEC.md` PV1 to PV8: the part stays opaque and unchanged; only the added or removed material, or the faces a modify feature makes, is drawn over it, see-through in the preview colour with its edges, never hidden by the part. A depth offset keeps it free of the stripes that led to D583. Partial (D585), None, handles, callouts and the before and after slider (TR224 item 4, now fading the overlay) stay. Fillet and Chamfer faces also show their two long edges and cross lines (arcs for a round, straight lines for a chamfer) joining them (PV3 item 2, owner's description). This replaces the Full preview of D583.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request; the overlay shows the old and new shape together.

D1032: Preview overlay built (2026-11-09, Phase 7C). Fillet, Chamfer, Shell, Draft, Move Face and the Detailed preview no longer ghost the part or draw the finished result. The part stays as it is. `show_preview` draws only the faces the feature makes (and held and stretched faces for Move Face, changed faces in the second colour for the Detailed preview) as `overlay_solid` items: `preview_solid` look (accent colour, `PREVIEW_TRANSPARENCY`, thin face edges, the polygon offset of PV4), moved to `Graphic3d_ZLayerId_Topmost` so the part cannot hide them while the faces still hide each other, and displayed with selection mode -1 so the part stays pickable. `_ghost_part` and `result_solid` are gone. `set_preview_blend` fades the overlay from its normal transparency (After) to fully clear (Before); the cross lines have no transparency, so they hide past the half way point. In core, `_result_view` now returns a compound of only the accent, held and stretched faces as `PreviewGeometry.shape`, so the view meshes nothing but what it draws (PV7); `ResultPreview.full` is still built by the modify code but no longer reaches the view. New `PreviewGeometry.lines` and `core/features/preview_lines.py`: for each Fillet and Chamfer accent face, iso curves of its surface across the short direction at evenly spaced parameters along the longer one, from 3 to 40 per face (one about every 3 mm), including both end lines: arcs for a round, straight lines for a chamfer, drawn 1 px wide in the accent colour in the topmost layer. The two long edges come from the face edges already drawn. Shell, Draft and Move Face draw only face edges.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request (D1031); the overlay shows old and new shape together, and meshing only the new faces keeps it as fast as before.

D1033: Workspace room, start picture and portable mode (2026-11-10, Phase 7D, owner request: "make it better: UI, reliability, user workflow, optimise, and a portable exe for Windows"). (1) `RibbonGroup.add_column` wraps a list longer than `COLUMN_ROWS` (3) into further columns, so one long group no longer makes every command tab taller (the tabs went from about 235 to 148 px); `RibbonPanel.minimumSizeHint` caps the width a wrapped group can ask for, since tabs scroll sideways (D632). (2) The left panel has a set minimum width of 18 em (was the property panel's 371 px hint) and a default of 22 em; `MainWindow._fit_left_panel` widens it to the property panel's hint while a panel is open and puts the width back after. The tree filter box and state list are stacked (IDEAS 19, owner). (3) The empty part made at start is marked `DocumentSession.auto_blank`; `add_session` closes it when another part opens and it has no undo steps. A part made with New Part is never closed this way. (4) `fdcad/ui/splash.py`: a `QSplashScreen` in the system palette colours (the theme is not loaded yet), shown right after the `QApplication` exists, not shown for the bundle check, the startup report or the offscreen platform. (5) `fdcad/portable.py`: a packaged FDCAD with `portable.txt` beside the program, or "portable" in the program's file name, sets `FDCAD_DATA_DIR` and `FDCAD_CACHE_DIR` to `FDCAD Data` beside the program, stores preferences in `FDCAD Data/settings.ini` (`portable.settings()` replaces the two direct `QSettings("FDCAD", "FDCAD")` calls) and leaves the system recent list alone. A folder that cannot be written falls back to the normal places. The sheet metal rule library default now uses `data_dir()`. (6) Packaging: `FDCAD_ONEFILE=1` makes `packaging/fdcad.spec` build one `FDCAD-portable.exe`. This is an addition to D43, not a change: the installer and the portable folder stay one folder builds, which start faster; the single file unpacks to a temporary folder on every start (PLAN 11.3 item 9) and is offered for convenience.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request. Measured before: window visible in 1.7 s, ready in 3.9 s, both inside the PLAN 11.2 budgets, so the work went to screen room and to what the owner sees while waiting.

D1034: The Datum look (2026-11-10 and 11, Phase 7D, owner request: "redesign UI and colours and logos and feature icons"). Described in `docs/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md`. (1) Colours: all four palettes and chromes in `themes/theme.py` retuned to cool greys with a cobalt accent (`#1F54E6` light, `#7FA6FF` dark); every pair of `themes/contrast.py` still passes in every theme. New `Chrome.cut` (ember, `#CF5409` light, `#FF9D5C` dark) for material a tool takes away, 3:1 or more on every panel colour and more than 90 degrees of hue from the accent. New `BRAND` colours, the same in every theme. (2) Radii: `states.radii` gives 6 px for controls and 10 px for panels, plates and popups (were 4 and 6; U3.2's sizes change, its rule of two radii stays). (3) Command tabs: the tools sit on one raised, rounded card (`QScrollArea#ribbon_scroll`) on the window colour, the chosen tab is a raised pill, and `COLUMN_ROWS` is 4 with rows of at least 24 px (U3.3). `build_panel` flows a group's small tools into columns in their listed order (RIBBON_SPEC R3A replaces the fixed columns of three of R2): the columns are balanced (six tools make three and three, which keeps R2's Modify columns), each is filled from the top, and the block of columns is centred. A compact dropdown button is as wide as the tool it shows, not its longest hidden name, and the tab lays out again when the shown tool changes. Measured on the owner's 1680 px wide screen: the Sketch tab was 1993 px wide with wrapped columns of three and is 1551 px now, every tab fits without scrolling, and the ribbon is 170 px tall. (4) Icons: new placeholder `#CUT`; `tools/icon_duotone.py` gave about 260 icons a body tint (closed outlines filled at 12 percent in ink, 20 percent in an active colour; dashed and half strength outlines left empty) and moved 23 removing tools from `#ACCENT` to `#CUT`; `tools/icon_heroes.py` holds 32 hand drawn icons (the main tools of every tab and the tree's part icon) as lit solids (left face 8 percent, right face 22 percent). The audit rules are unchanged apart from allowing `#CUT`, and all 468 icons pass. (5) Mark: `tools/make_brand.py` draws the app icon, an extruded letter F on the cobalt tile, replacing the Ember block of D581; PNG, ICO, ICNS and installer pictures were made again from it. (6) Start picture: the brand tile with the mark, the name in a new `Role.DISPLAY` (34 px, outside the working scale) and the version; it replaces the system colour picture of D1033 item 4. (7) Preferences: every page sits in a scroll area, so the window is no taller than its 560 px request needs; before, the General page made it about 1100 px tall and its buttons could be off screen. (8) The left panel's tab row takes the panel colour and its chosen tab is a tinted pill; the view toolbar plate is a pill. (9) Start page: a head with the mark, the name and what FDCAD is; New Part is the main button (the `main` property gives a button the accent fill, like `panel_ok`); a part without a picture shows `start_page.placeholder`, a theme coloured tile with the part icon at its own size, in place of the file icon blown up to 128 px. (10) Property panel: the header has two rows (icon, name, help and Pin; then OK and Cancel at equal width), because in one row the buttons overlapped below about 400 px; the panel's own minimum width fell from 371 to about 240 px, so `_fit_left_panel` now also fits the width of the fields (`groups_box`), after the panel has laid them out. The first use hint is a tinted card. (11) The light view's bottom colour stays a neutral grey (`#C6CBD2`, channels within 12 of each other), the owner's request of D434. (12) The sketch panel and the Edit Sketch Plane panel get the same two row header. Message bars are tinted cards: the state colour mixed 8 percent into the raised colour, a 6 px radius and the full state colour on the left edge. (13) The single file build shows `packaging/splash.png` (made by `tools/make_installer_images.py`) from its boot loader while it unpacks, through PyInstaller's `Splash`, which needs Tcl/Tk in the build Python only; `app._close_boot_picture` closes it when the app's own start picture is up, and does nothing unless `_PYI_SPLASH_IPC` is set. (14) The first start welcome opens 0.7 s after the window is ready, so the 3D view has drawn and is not a white area behind it. (15) About shows the mark beside the name. (16) Node editor: `NodeView.fit` asked for while the view is hidden is done again when the view is first shown at its real size (it used to fit to the size of a widget not yet laid out), and the dock opens at 42 percent of the window width, at least 520 px, the first time. (17) `core.mass.tidy` sets a value to 0 when it is 1e-9 times smaller than the largest value beside it (for the centre of mass, beside the part's size, the cube root of its volume), and `report` uses it for the centre, the principal axes and the inertia rows; computed values are not changed, only what is shown and copied. (18) The Properties window opens at 680 by 440 and Equations at 960 by 520 with a filter box at least 160 px wide. (19) Tables and their headers are styled (`QTableView`, `QHeaderView::section`). The Variables table stretches its Name, Expression and Value columns, sizes Kind to its box and has no row numbers; a left tab may set `preferred_width` (Variables: 380) and `MainWindow._fit_left_tab` widens the panel to it while that tab shows. (20) From a review of the tool windows in the new look: Suggest Orientation makes Apply the default button after its buttons are in the dialog (set before that, Qt gave the look to Cancel); the Manufacturing Check rule column stretches; the Draft Analysis plane box is at least 140 px wide; on the start page, parts with the same name also show their folder.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request. Kept to rules that are already tested (contrast, smallest click size, icon audit) so the new look cannot quietly break reading or clicking.

D1035: Crash guard (2026-11-11, Phase 7D, owner request: reliability). A fault inside the kernel's native code, or a rebuild stopped from the Task Manager, closes FDCAD, and the part that caused it then closed FDCAD again on every open, because opening rebuilds it. IDEAS 12 and 13 (run fillets and imports in a second process) would stop the fault itself but change the import and fillet paths and double the time of an import; this guard is small, costs a few microseconds per built feature and covers every feature type. (1) `RebuildEngine.on_build(feature)` is called just before a feature is built (never for a cached result) and `on_done()` when a rebuild ends, however it ends; errors in them are swallowed. (2) `ui/main_window/crash_guard.py`: each `DocumentSession` has a `BuildJournal` that writes the part's file, the feature id and name to `<data>/Journal/<id>.json` (kept open, rewritten and flushed per feature, emptied at the end of a rebuild, removed when the part closes) and holds a `QLockFile` beside it. (3) At start `collect` reads the notes whose lock is free (their process is gone): a note with a feature in it is a `Suspect`. Notes of a FDCAD that is still running are left alone. (4) `apply`, called by `add_session` before the first rebuild, matches a suspect to the part by file (or, for a part that never had a file, to a part brought back from autosave) and calls `session.hold(fid)`. A held session sets the rollback bar of the copy each rebuild works on to the feature before the held one, the same way checkpoints do (TR276), so the document is not changed and nothing is saved. A warning bar in the view names the feature and offers Suppress, which is one undo step. The hold ends when the feature's data changes, when it is suppressed or deleted, or on Force Rebuild. (5) `applog` turns on `faulthandler` into `<data>/logs/crash.log`, so a native fault leaves the Python stack of every thread to send with a bug report. Tested with a real second process that exits without cleaning up while a note is open.
Status: Default
Reason: It removes the one failure a user cannot work around (a part that can never be opened again) without touching how features are built.

D1036: The mark is the letters F and D (2026-11-11, Phase 7D, owner request: "the F in 3D looks nice, let us make a D next to it, in the opposite isometric view: imagine F carved out of one face of the cube and D carved out of the adjacent face", then "keep the F exactly as you had before and just add D next to it"). This changes D1034 item 5. (1) `tools/make_brand.py` draws two solid letters on two neighbouring faces of a cube that is not drawn: the F on the left face, pushed back to the right, with the proportions and colours it had alone (stem 1.9, arm 1.7, depth 3.0 in a box 5 by 7), and a D on the right face, pushed back to the left, so its top and its left walls show. Both use the same white front and the same lit and shaded ember. (2) Each letter stops its own depth plus half a slot before the corner line (slot 0.6 units in the full drawing, 1.0 in the small one), so the back of one never reaches the other, nothing needs hidden surface work, and a line of the tile separates the letters. The unit is 14.6 px (was 17.5) so that both fit the tile with the same margin; the F is the same drawing at 83 percent. (3) The walls of the D that are curved are drawn as flat pieces, 48 per quarter turn (14 showed as stripes), each in a colour between the lit and the shaded ember by how far it faces up, with the shade taken from the end of the straight wall it joins (light at the top, dark at the foot); straight walls keep the two gradients, so the F is drawn exactly as before. The walls of the opening in the D are drawn first, because they are only seen through it. (4) The small drawing gives the D a 1.95 stroke (the F keeps 2.3), or its opening would close at 16 px. (5) `full_icon()` and `small_icon()` hold the numbers; the test compares both committed SVG files with them. PNG, ICO, ICNS, installer pictures and `packaging/splash.png` were made again. Three other drawings were shown to the owner and not chosen: letters with a thinner F, and F and D cut into a white or a blue block.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request. FD is the name; one letter did not say it.

D1037: The F and the D of the mark are joined at the corner (2026-11-11, Phase 7D, owner request: "overlap one on the other, that way one acts as a corner, so F is face plus corner and D is adjacent face"). This replaces D1036 item 2. (1) The F runs to the corner line (gap 0), so the end of its top arm, one depth wide, lies in the plane of the D's front face: the F is the left face and the corner. The D starts one depth after the corner line, where that end stops, with its left wall on the back plane of the F. The two solids touch on those planes and share no volume, so no hidden surface work is needed beyond drawing order: the D is drawn first and the F after it, because the F's middle arm and stem stand in front of the D's left wall. (2) Without the two gaps of D1036 the letters are 13 units wide, not 16.6, so the unit is 17.5 px again: the F is the drawing and the size it had alone in D1034. The small drawing uses 18.0 (the F alone had 19.0). (3) New `DEEP_TOP` and `DEEP_BOTTOM` (`#C24A08`, `#8A2E04`) for the D's side walls, in place of the F's shade (`#F4680E`, `#B83E05`). With one ember for both, the F's stem wall, the end of its middle arm and the D's left wall met as one orange shape in the middle of the mark; the darker D wall reads as behind the F. The F's own colours are unchanged. (4) The slot numbers of D1036 are removed from `icon()`.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request. Joined, the two letters read as one object, the corner of a block, and the F keeps its full size.

D1038: The corner face of the F has its own colour (2026-11-11, Phase 7D, owner request: "change the colours of the face on the edge of F so it does not blend with the adjacent face of D"). The end of the F's top arm, the face that lies on the D's side of the corner (D1037), used the F's shade gradient, which is dark at its foot (`#B83E05`), and the D's side wall starts just below it at almost the same colour (`#C24A08` at its top, about `#A63C06` where the two meet). It now uses `CORNER_TOP` and `CORNER_BOTTOM` (`#FF7A1F`, `#EE650D`), a bright ember that hardly darkens, so there is a clear step to the D's wall below it, and it is still an orange face beside the D's white front and under the F's lighter top. `solid()` gives this fill only to a right facing wall of the left letter that reaches the corner line (gap 0). The F's other walls keep the shade of D1034. Tried and not used: a pale cream, which stood apart from the D's wall but ran into the D's white front beside it.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner request.

D1039: The front faces of the mark are off white (2026-11-11, Phase 7D, owner choice). `FRONT_TOP` and `FRONT_BOTTOM` are `#FFFEFB` and `#F3EEE4` (were `#FFFFFF` and `#E6ECFF`, white fading to a cool blue white). The owner asked whether the flat faces could be another colour and was shown sky blue, bright blue, mint, cream and lavender, then asked for the cream to be more off white and less cream, and chose the lightest of three off whites. The brand text colour on the tile (`BRAND["on_tile"]`) stays white.
Status: Default
Reason: Owner choice.

D1040: The feature panel comes in front when a feature opens (2026-11-11, Phase 7D, reliability; found by a layout review that opens every command's panel). The Properties tab is a stack: the property panel, plus any side panel shown with `show_side_panel` (sketch, sketch plane, Appearance, Section View, reference geometry). Nothing put the property panel back in front when a feature opened, so with Appearance, Section View or a reference panel open, `window.editing` was "feature" while the side panel stayed on top and the feature's fields and its OK and Cancel could not be seen. (1) New `MainWindow._show_feature_panel`, connected to `PropertyPanel.started`: it closes Appearance, accepts Section View (the same as its OK: the section stays on, which is the rule `show_side_panel` already uses when another side panel opens), closes an unfinished reference feature (the same as its Cancel: nothing is added to the part), makes the property panel the stack's current widget and shows the Properties tab. It does nothing while a sketch is open, which keeps its own panel. (2) `hide_side_panel` goes to the Properties tab when a feature is open, and to the tree as before when none is: closing Section View in the middle of a Fillet used to leave the tree in front of the open feature. Tests: `tests/ui/test_feature_panel_front.py`, which fail without the change.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature open with its panel hidden looks like a frozen program, and the only ways out were the confirmation corner or Esc.

D1041: Rounds that run past the end of their edge are built by FDCAD (2026-11-11 and 12, Phase 7D, reliability; the owner's part: a 50 by 50 by 10 block, top edges rounded 2 mm, bottom face chamfered 1 mm, then a side edge rounded 2 mm, which failed). Measured in the kernel on that edge: `BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet` builds every radius up to 1.95 mm and none from 1.99 mm up, with any of its three fillet shapes. At 2 mm the round has to end on the rounds above it, and the kernel has no end for that. (1) New `core/features/fillet_overflow.py`, used by `Fillet._round_core` only after the kernel has failed on a constant radius fillet with the Radius method. Edges the kernel rounds on their own are still rounded by the kernel, together; each other edge must be straight, an outside edge, between two flat faces, with the round's two lines lying on those faces (tested on the part at three places along the edge, so a radius wider than a face is refused as before). Its round is a plain cylinder: the cross section between the corner and the arc (`fillet_profile.prism`, already used for the conic and curvature profiles of D1402) is extruded along the edge and cut away. (2) Ends. An end is closed when any other face that meets the edge there faces back along it (dot product of its normal and the direction out of the edge below -0.05): a wall or a floor, where the part goes on, so the cut stops flush. Otherwise the end is free. (3) A free end gets a ball corner when the two arcs where an eighth of a ball of the same radius would join the faces past the end lie on the part's surface (three points each, within 1e-5 mm) and the ball's middle is inside the part: the cube of the corner less the ball is cut away too. This is the exact result for three rounds of one radius on a square corner. It is found from the part's shape, not from which features made it. (4) Any other free end (a chamfer, a flat cap, rounds of another radius) has the cylinder carried past it until a thin slice of the cross section holds none of the part, tried at 1.5, 3, 6 and 12 times the radius; the kernel does the same at a chamfer, and the pictures of both at 1.9 mm (kernel) and 2 mm (here) match there. If the cut never leaves the part, or the result is not a valid solid, or nothing was removed, the fillet fails with the message it had before. (5) The radius and the edges are the ones asked for, so this is not a fix that changes geometry and needs no button (PLAN 5A): only the kernel is replaced for this shape of round. Inside edges, curved edges, variable radius and the other fillet types are not covered and fail as before. (6) Names: the cylinder is `<fillet>/fillet/<edge>` as from the kernel; a ball is `<fillet>/fillet/<edge>/corner_start` or `corner_end`. Nothing is added to the file format. (7) `rebuild.change_line.Change` has `failed`; the status bar shows `CHANGE_ERROR` for a failed feature. It showed `CHANGE_NONE` ("built; the solid did not change") because a failed feature keeps the body before it.
Status: Default
Reason: Rounding the top edges of a block and then a side edge with the same radius is among the first things anyone does in a part modeller, and it failed.

D1042: A closed feature's pre check box is removed from the panel (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the same layout review as D1040, which also takes a picture of every panel and reads them). `FeatureForm.check`, the box that shows a pre check note and its fix buttons (PLAN 5A items 4 and 5), is a widget of the panel's `groups_box`, not of the form, which is a plain object. `PropertyPanel._clear` deleted the form and left the box, so every box that held a note when its feature closed stayed visible above the groups of every later feature: after Corner Relief and Lip Groove were cancelled, the Modeled Thread panel listed both of their notes. `_clear` now takes the box out of the layout, hides it and deletes it. Also: the two choice boxes of Compare Bodies size to their choices (`AdjustToContents`, at least 12 characters), because they are filled on each open and a box sized while empty cut "STEP file..." short. The review's check for cut off text and overlapping controls found nothing else on the 247 panels, dialogs and tool windows of the plate sample; it is a script of the session, not part of the test suite.
Status: Default
Reason: A note about another feature in the panel of the one being edited reads as an error in the feature being edited.

D1043: A failing fillet or chamfer answers quickly and names the right edges (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). A fillet on the frame's joints that the kernel refuses in 0.2 s took 12 to 46 s to report, and one never came back. (1) The search for the largest radius that works (`fillet.largest_radius`, `chamfer._largest`) halved the radius eight times, down to 1/256 of the one asked for. On a curved joint the kernel did not return from a 0.047 mm round. The search now stops below 1/16 of the wanted size (`SMALLEST_SHARE`): four steps down, and still eight steps in all when something works. A round under a sixteenth of what was asked is no help, and the message then names the edge with no "largest radius". (2) `check_edges` tried every picked edge alone, but the kernel rounds an edge with its whole smooth chain, so a chain of eight edges was tried and searched eight times. `chains_of` asks the kernel which chain each edge is in; a chain is tried once and its answer given to all its edges. At most six failing chains are searched (`_SEARCH_CHAINS`). (3) Two picked edges can have one name, because an edge is named by the two faces it lies between and two faces can meet in more than one edge (a stay through a plate, a joint cut in two by a seam). `Item.index` was found by looking the name up in the picked list, so both got the first place: the message read "edge 1, edge 1", and Fillet the rest, which removed picks by name, took out the good edge too. `fillet.positions` gives each resolved edge its own place, the message names each failing place once, and the `skip_items` fix carries `positions`, which `fixes.fixed_feature` uses in place of the names. (4) The fixes that split a fillet or limit failing areas work on lists of names, so they are not offered when two picks share a name. (5) Those two fixes each need many trial rounds. They are looked for only while naming the failing edges has taken under 4 s (`EXTRAS_SECONDS`): on a part of several hundred faces a four edge fillet took 34 s to say it had failed. Fillet the rest and Reduce the radius are always offered. This makes the offered buttons depend on the computer's speed on large parts; the result of a click does not.
Status: Default
Reason: An error that takes half a minute, or never comes, reads as a hang, and a button that removes the wrong edge loses the user's picks.

D1044: The Project wrap thickens the picked face when the body cannot be offset (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). `wrap_project._slab` offset the whole solid by the height to get a skin to cut the swept sketch to. The kernel cannot offset the frame, so text on the down tube failed with "the body could not be grown by the height". When the offset fails, `_thick_face` makes only the picked face thick by the height and keeps it to the material (deboss) or to the room outside (emboss). Under the sketch this is the same skin. Bodies the kernel can offset build as before.
Status: Default
Reason: Text on one face should not depend on the kernel being able to offset every other face of the part.

D1045: A Geometry pattern of features falls back on what the features added and removed (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). A Mounting Boss on the lofted down tube could not be patterned. As a feature it "cannot be copied as a feature ... turn on Geometry pattern" (it adds a boss and cuts a hole, so it has no single tool). With Geometry pattern on, its faces could not be patched away from the spline face, and the message said to "pick the feature instead", which was what was picked. When the faces cannot be patched (`NotWholeFeatureError`), `patterns._pattern_history` takes each seed feature in build order, finds what it added (the part after it less the part before it) and what it removed, and copies both to every placement, the removed first, with the same touch tests and the same face names as a face pattern. Seeds that are faces, not features, have no history and keep the old message.
Status: Default
Reason: The two messages pointed at each other and left no way to pattern the feature.

D1046: The root of a boss never reaches the far wall (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). A boss on a curved face is rooted a little below the face so it meets it all round (`fastening.reach_down`, D316): for 16 points of the boss's outline the nearest crossing of a line with the face is found. On the hollow down tube one point lay over the seam of the face, its near crossing was missed, and the far wall 36 mm down was taken for the face: the boss became a 10 mm column through the inside of the tube that came out of the other side (2684 mm3 where 171 mm3 was right). A crossing farther down than twice the outline's radius is now ignored. Used by Mounting Boss, Snap Hook and Hose Fitting.
Status: Default
Reason: Wrong geometry with no error is the worst kind of fault.

D1047: A separate body warning goes when a later feature joins the body to the part (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). The head tube is made before the top tube that joins it to the seat tube, so "Head Tube created a separate body" stayed on it for good though the part was one body. After a rebuild `engine._drop_joined_body_warnings` takes the warning off a feature when any later feature leaves fewer bodies than it did. The report gets a copy without the warning; the kept result is not changed, so the warning is back when the joining feature is deleted or suppressed.
Status: Default
Reason: A warning that can never be cleared teaches the user to ignore warnings.

D1048: A Geometry pattern of features gives no notes about picked faces (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). The faces of the seed features are listed from the part by name and found again by name. Two faces of the frame's dropout round had one name, so each was "found by its position" and the mirror warned twice to "check it and reselect it", with nothing the user had picked. `apply_pattern` drops these notes for seeds that are features. Faces the user picked keep them.
Status: Default
Reason: The note asked the user to fix a pick that was not theirs.

D1049: A solid the kernel returns inside out is made again, not flagged (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). The head badge, an analytical wrap on the head tube, built with no error and added 0.27 mm3 where 342 mm3 was right. The kernel had made the thickened face inside out (its volume read below zero). The code set the solid's reversed flag, which makes the volume read right, and the kernel's own `OrientClosedSolid` does no more than that. But a fuse that gets such a solid inside a compound takes it for the room around it and returns the part unchanged, and reports success. Measured: the same solid fused bare added 342 mm3; in a compound, 0.7 mm3. `solids.right_side_out` makes the solid again from its shells turned over, with no flag. It is used where a volume below zero was answered with `Reversed()`: the analytical and spline wraps, Rib, Modeled Thread and thread relief. `combine` passes every tool through it too. The volume check after a boolean (`volume_sane`, D705) could not see this: its slack is 1 percent of the part, and it is off above 100 faces.
Status: Default
Reason: Wrong geometry with no error. It also made the same part differ between a session and its file, since which way the kernel made the solid changed with the last digits of the sketch.

D1050: The thread marks of a tapped hole end where the material ends (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). `hole.thread_marks` drew every mark as long as the table's thread depth, so an M10 thread 20 mm deep in the 6 mm hanger ran 14 mm out into the air behind it. With the part before the holes, `material_depth` finds where the hole's axis first leaves the material, and the mark is no longer than that. The length in the thread's description changes the same way. An existing test expected 12 mm of thread in a 10 mm plate; it now expects 10.
Status: Default
Reason: A thread drawn outside the part reads as a display fault.

D1051: The pick list takes two edges that share a name (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). `PickList.add` refused a pick whose name was already listed. Where a stay crosses a dropout it meets one face of the plate in two edges with one name (D1043 item 3), so a click on the second added nothing and said nothing: it could not be picked. Two references are now the same pick when they have the same name and, where both keep a snapshot point, the same place. `PickList.remove_edges_at` removes edges by their place among the edges, and the Fillet and Chamfer panels use it for a `skip_items` fix that gives `positions`.
Status: Default
Reason: A click that does nothing, with no message, on an edge that can be rounded.

D1052: Faces are put in order of position with a tolerance, not by rounded numbers (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by building a bike frame of 103 features at the owner's request: lofted and swept tubes, bores, joint fillets, a mirror, patterns, tapped holes, a wrapped badge and engraved text). `names.order_by_position` (FDEF_SPEC 8.2: by centroid X, then Y, then Z) rounded each coordinate to six decimals and sorted. Two mirror image faces have the same X and Y but for the last digits of the arithmetic (measured on the frame: 1e-13 to 4e-10 mm apart), and when their X fell on either side of a rounding step that noise ordered them, not their Z. Two faces of the engraved text swapped their numbers between the part as built and the same part opened from its file, where numbers are kept to twelve digits. Coordinates within 1e-6 mm now count as equal (`ORDER_TOLERANCE`) and the next coordinate decides. Faces whose coordinates clearly differ are ordered as before, so saved names do not change. With D1049 this was the whole difference: the frame as built and as opened from its file now have the same faces under the same names in all 103 features. The frame as first built reopened with eleven features in error ("missing reference f34/cap/end#1").
Status: Default
Reason: A part must open as it was saved.
