D1053: The dome asks the kernel again when its intersection comes back empty (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the bike frame of D1043, built in four sizes and each opened again from its file). The size L frame built, and failed when opened: "Chain Stay End: the dome cannot rise from every edge of this face". A dome is the picked face pushed up, cut to a sphere (`dome._cap`). The kernel's intersection of the pushed up end of the swept stay with the sphere reported success and returned an empty shape at the usual tolerance (1e-5), and the right shape (372 mm3) at 1e-4; with the face pushed up 1.05 or 1.2 times the height it was right, at 1.5 and 2 times empty again. Which it was changed with the last digits of the sketch, so the session and the file differed. `dome._common` now tries 1e-5, 1e-4, 1e-6 and no tolerance in turn and takes the first answer that is not empty. When all are empty the shapes do not overlap (an edge dome on a face that is not convex) and the message is the one from before. Other features call the kernel's intersection with one tolerance too; they are not changed here, since only the dome is known to fail and only it knows that its two shapes must overlap. After this fix and D1049 and D1052 the frame opens from its file as built in sizes S, M, L and XL.
Status: Default
Reason: A part must open as it was saved.

D1054: Lightening Pockets cuts each rib strip as its own tool (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by a gearbox part of 318 features and 106 feature types in 60 bodies, built through the feature interface to try as many feature types as one solid part can hold). On a 160 by 100 cover the pockets left a solid that was not valid and about five times too heavy, with no error. The rib strips cross each other, and they were handed to the kernel as one bundled tool; the kernel does not sort the pieces of one tool out against each other. `lightening_pockets.cut_each` now passes each strip as a tool of its own, turns an inside out strip the right way round (D1049), and the feature fails with a message when the result is not a valid solid.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature must not leave a broken solid without saying so.

D1055: Stone Setting, Face Seats, Sprue Tree and the patterns join only the bodies they reach (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054). Each fused its new material with the whole part in one kernel call. That call also joins any two bodies of the part that share a face with each other, wherever they are: a stone setting on the cover turned the twelve inlay letters back into cover, Face Seats on a drum joined two blocks elsewhere that were locked together with Interlock teeth, and a sprue tree joined the two halves of a bar split for printing. Nothing was reported. All three now go through `solids.combine` with `pieces=True`, which joins the tool to the bodies it reaches and leaves the rest as they were. Face Seats keeps its `seat#` face names. The shared `booleans.boolean_named`, which patterns and about thirty other callers use, did the same: a table pattern of studs on one plate joined the same two blocks, and Corner Ears on one block joined six other bodies and lost 234 faces. Neither said a word; the gearbox was first counted at 53 bodies and has 60. On a part of several bodies it now joins the tool to the bodies it reaches only, adds a tool that touches nothing as bodies of its own without asking the kernel, and cuts each body it reaches on its own (D1056). Other features still fuse with the whole part directly (Hinge, Interlock, Joint Helper, Landing Pad, Lattice Fill, Rib, Roof, Split for Printing connectors, Twist Lock, Vent); the gearbox did not catch them joining bodies, so they are not changed here and are listed in IDEAS item 52.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature changes the bodies it works on and no others.

D1056: A cut on a part of several bodies cuts each body alone (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054). The kernel's cut needs bodies that do not touch each other, and the bodies of one part often do: a cover on its flange, a pin in its hole. A hole through two touching bodies left the drilled plug behind as a new body, or left the second body whole. `solids.each_body` cuts every body the tool reaches in its own kernel call and puts the part together again; `combine` uses it for a cut when the part has more than one body, and so does `hole.cut_all`. `WholeBodyCutError` says so when a cut would remove a whole body.
Status: Default
Reason: Parts of several bodies are normal, and a cut through two of them must give the same result as on one.

D1057: The "bodies touch along an edge" warning counts new contacts only (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054). Two faults. First, an inlay with round letters was reported as touching its pocket along an edge: the test for bodies that share a whole face looked at flat and cylinder faces only, so the spline walls of a letter were not seen as shared. `_contact_faces` now takes every kind of face, with `_lies_on` checking the corners and edge middles of the smaller face on the larger. Second, once a part had one such contact, every later feature gave the same warning again, though it had nothing to do with it. `check_result` now warns only when the feature leaves more contacts than it was given (`_touch_count`).
Status: Default
Reason: A warning that is wrong, or repeated on forty features, teaches the user to ignore warnings.

D1058: Edge names are looked up through one map per body (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, speed; found by the gearbox of D1054). A fillet on the four corners of the cover took 29.96 s. Naming an edge asked the kernel for the map from edges to faces of the whole body, once for every edge named: 234 maps for one fillet. `NamedShape._lookup` builds the map and the face name table once per body and keeps them with it. The same fillet takes 0.32 s. `tests/core/naming/test_name_lookup_speed.py` counts the map builds.
Status: Default
Reason: The time to name an edge must not grow with the square of the part.

D1059: Shaft Shape no longer slices a stepped shaft (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054). A flat, hexagon or keyway on the middle step of a stepped shaft cut the shaft into three bodies. The feature removes a sleeve round the step and leaves the profile inside it; the sleeve was made a little longer than the step, so its end discs cut through the larger steps on each side. The sleeve is now exactly as long as the shape and the kept profile a little longer, so the ends stay joined.
Status: Default
Reason: A shaft with a flat is still one shaft.

D1060: A knurl stops at a shoulder and cuts only its own body (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054). A knurl on a stem below a wider head removed nothing and left 110 edge contacts. The grooves run past both ends of the face so they leave clean ends; at a shoulder they ran into the head, and all grooves were one bundled tool though they cross (D1054). `knurl._goes_on` now looks whether the body goes on past each end of the face and stops the grooves there; each groove is its own tool; only the body of the picked face is cut; and the result is checked.
Status: Default
Reason: The same as D1054, and a knurl beside a shoulder is the usual case on a knob.

D1061: A primitive made with Merge Result off does not warn of a separate body (2026-11-12, Phase 7D; found by the gearbox of D1054). The user asked for a separate body, and the rebuild then warned "created a separate body". The primitive now passes its warnings through `solids.expected_issues`, which drops that one when the user chose it, as Extrude, Revolve, Sweep and Loft do.
Status: Default
Reason: A warning for what the user asked for is noise.

D1062: The sheet standing for a cut plane is centred over the bodies (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054). Split, Intersect and Split for Printing cut with a large square sheet in place of the endless plane. The sheet was centred on the plane's own origin, and was sized by the bodies. A bar 510 mm from the origin, cut by a plane made from a base plane, was not reached: "the cut planes miss the part". `endless_plane` and `split_for_print._tool_face` now centre the sheet on the point of the plane nearest the middle of the bodies.
Status: Default
Reason: A plane is endless, so where its origin is must not matter.

D1063: Section Cut is marked as changing the part (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054). `SectionCut.makes_solid` was False. The rebuild gives the next feature the part of the last feature that makes a solid, so the feature after a Section Cut was built on the part from before the cut: the cut was gone as soon as anything was added, and references to its cut face failed ("missing reference"). It is now True.
Status: Default
Reason: A kept section cut must stay cut.

D1064: Sensor, Contour and Parting Line say that they read the part (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found while fixing D1063). These three read the whole part without a picked face, and did not override `reads_body`. The rebuild kept their result when a feature before them changed: a volume sensor on a 10 mm plate still reported 25000 mm3 after the plate was made 30 mm thick. They now return True, as Measurement does, so their result is keyed on the part (D250).
Status: Default
Reason: A sensor that shows an old value is worse than none.

D1065: The rebuild cache counts the faces a feature made, not the whole part (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, speed; found by the gearbox of D1054). Past about 165 features every added feature took 90 to 100 s, even a reference point: the whole part was built again each time. The cache charged each kept result 16 KB for every face of the part (D71), though the kernel shares all faces but the changed ones between one result and the next. At 3000 faces that is 50 MB a feature, so the 2 GB limit (D44) was reached; the oldest results were dropped first, and those are the ones every later feature is built on. `estimate_size` now takes the part the feature started from and counts only the faces not in it. The limit and the 16 KB figure are unchanged. Also: `RebuildEngine(cache)` ignored a cache passed to it while empty, since an empty cache is falsy; it now tests for None. The cache test of D44 passed before only because of that, with a cache nobody used.
Status: Default
Reason: A long tree is the normal case for a real part, and the cache exists for it.

D1066: Heal Edges works on a copy and never leaves a body worse (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054). The part was valid before Heal Edges and not after it. Two causes. First, the heal changed the body where it was: the kernel's fixer and the tolerance updates after it write into edges and corners, and a body shares most of them with the results of the features before it. Those kept results were changed too, and one shaft came out with an edge 36 mm loose that had gone in exact. `heal_edges.heal` now copies the body first (`BRepBuilderAPI_Copy`, with its geometry) and `Healed` carries each face name over to the copy. Second, a bar fitted by Deform Curve to Curve was valid only with its loose edges (1.5 mm); with them cut back it was not valid. A body that would not be valid after healing, or whose loosest edge would come out looser, now stays as it was, and the feature warns: "1 body would be worse after healing and stays as it was. Rebuild the loose faces, or make the feature that fitted them more exact."
Status: Default
Reason: A repair tool must not damage what it is given, nor anything else.

D1067: Every boolean runs in the kernel's safe mode (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054, while looking for the cause of D1066). The kernel's boolean operations may write into the shapes they are given, unless told not to (`SetNonDestructive`). A body shares almost all of its faces with the results of the features before it, and the rebuild keeps those results to start from after an edit. On the gearbox, the grille cut in the cover left three faces of the housing not valid in the results kept for 41 earlier features. The same damage made a face merge fail without a word: in the sample `printable_enclosure` the lip's inner wall and the cavity wall are one flat face, the merge after the fuse (`unify_faces`) made a face that failed the check and was dropped, and the part kept four faces too many; its golden counts change from 64 faces and 134 edges to 60 and 126, with the same volume. `fdcad.core.occ` now holds the kernel's Cut, Fuse, Common, Section and Splitter as classes with the safe mode switched on, under the kernel's own names, and all 84 modules that used a boolean import it from there. The two shape form builds at once, as the kernel's does. `tests/core/test_safe_booleans.py` fails when a module takes a boolean straight from the kernel. Not covered: `BRepAlgoAPI_Defeaturing` (Delete and Patch), which has no safe mode in this kernel build, and other kernel tools that might write into their inputs (fillets, offsets); none was seen to. The gearbox test now checks that no kept result is spoiled after the whole part is built.
Status: Default
Reason: What a rebuild starts from must be what the feature made.

D1068: Indent and Half Lap number their new faces by position (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the gearbox of D1054, built in a session, built again from nothing and opened from its file, with every face name compared). All 318 features gave the same bodies, face counts and volumes three ways, but 95 results differed in names, all from two features: `indent/<k>` and `lap/<k>` were numbered in the order the kernel listed the faces of a shape it had made, and that order is not the same from one run to the next. A reference to such a face could point at another face after the part was opened again. `names.in_order` gives the faces of a shape in position order (D1052) and both features number by it. The numbers of a part saved before this can therefore change, so these names are now weak names (D720): a reference to one is checked against where it was picked and found again by position. Other features number faces in listing order too (Base Pad, Finger Joint, Hose Fitting, Twist Lock, Sweep Body, two sheet metal tools). The first four are in the gearbox and their names were the same three ways; none is changed here, and all are listed in IDEAS item 55.
Status: Default
Reason: A part must open as it was saved.

D1069: The gearbox ships as a sample part (2026-11-12, Phase 7D; the owner asked for it "as one of the defaults for people to learn and see things"). `samples/gearbox.fdprt` is the part of D1054 as its builder makes it: 318 features of 106 types in 60 bodies. The packaging takes every part file in `samples`, so it shows under File, Samples with no other change. Its builder stays with the tests (`tests/core/features/gearbox_builder.py`), since it is driven by picks on the built part, not by the sample builder's helpers; the slow gearbox test checks that the file is what the builder makes, and a quick test that it is listed and loads. It is not in the `SAMPLES` table, so the per sample tests (golden counts, STEP export, old file forms that rebuild) do not run it: one rebuild takes a minute and a half (D1070), and the naming stress test lists it as heavy. Two features carry a warning, and both are true: the parting line of a housing with holes in every wall crosses faces, and Heal Edges leaves the loosely fitted deformed bar as it was (D1066). Known cost: the first time it is opened the part takes about two minutes to build.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner's request; a large real part is also the best thing to learn the feature tree from.

D1070: The edge contact check looks only at the bodies a feature changed (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, speed; found by timing the gearbox sample of D1069). After D1055 the two blocks locked with Interlock teeth stay two bodies, as they should, and every feature after them took 6 s longer: the check for bodies that touch along an edge (PLAN 5A item 2) looked at the whole part after each feature, and the hundreds of edges those blocks share were measured again each time though nothing had touched them. Building the gearbox from its file went from 233 s to 421 s; with this change it takes 94 s, since the same check had been slow on every part with touching bodies. `solids.new_touches` compares the bodies before and after the feature, and `zero_thickness` takes the bodies to look at: the ones the feature made or changed. The touches between bodies it left alone are the same before and after, so the answer is the same. The kept count of D1057 (`_touch_count`) is gone. `tests/core/features/test_zero_thickness_contact.py` counts the contact measurements: none for a stud put on a plate far from two locked blocks.
Status: Default
Reason: The time a feature takes must not grow with what other bodies of the part look like.

D1071: A picked corner edge or wall end is matched to the wall it is on (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by a sheet metal part of eleven bodies and 104 features, built through the feature interface to try every sheet metal feature type, after the bike frame of D1043 and the gearbox of D1054; the owner said to go on with the third test part). On a tray with four walls, Break Corner on the back wall cut the corner of the front wall, and on the left wall that of the right wall; Closed Corner on the back or left wall closed a corner of the front or right wall. Nothing was reported. `locate.thickness_edge` took the first wall in whose frame the edge runs through the thickness, and an edge through a parallel wall does too; `locate.wall_end` did not ask whether the face is in the wall's own layer. Both now do (from one face of the wall to the other), and of two walls side by side in one layer the one whose outline has a corner there is taken. Every earlier test had two walls at most, never two that face each other. Every feature of the new part is followed by a check that material is where it should be and nowhere else (`Sheet.expect`, 112 checks), since this fault built with no error.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature must act where the user picked.

D1072: Perforation and Flat Marks find the wall under each line (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the sheet metal part of D1071). The two brims of a hat section lie in one plane. A row of slots drawn on the second brim failed ("no slot falls on the wall"), and marks drawn there were stored on the first brim, so they would be written to the flat pattern files in the wrong place. Both took the first wall whose face lies in the sketch's plane (`perforation.wall_of`). It now takes a point as well and gives the wall that has sheet under it; each line of a perforation and each piece of a mark is placed on its own wall. Sketched Bend, Jog, Rip, Forming Tool, Stamp and Tab already looked under the line.
Status: Default
Reason: The same as D1071.

D1073: Cross Break and Flat Marks hand back their own sheet (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the sheet metal part of D1071). Both change the sheet model and no shape, and returned the whole part as their result. The rebuild takes a sheet feature's result for that sheet's own solid and puts the part's other bodies back beside it (D2312): in a part with a second sheet the other bodies were added once more (two bodies became three), and the next feature of the sheet took all of them for its own and dropped them (three became one). `common.own_body` gives the sheet's own solid as it stands, and both features return it.
Status: Default
Reason: A part of several sheets is allowed (D2312), so every sheet feature must leave the other bodies alone.

D1074: The wall under a picked face is found by a point on the face (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the sheet metal part of D1071). `locate.wall_face` looked for sheet under the centre of the picked face. On a plate with a hole in its middle the centre is in the hole, and Cross Break, Gusset, Tab and Slot and the Flat Pattern's Leave Out said "the face is not a flat face of a wall". `locate.face_point` gives a point that is on the face (the middle of its parameter box, or the first of a 9 by 9 grid that is), and the wall is looked for under that.
Status: Default
Reason: A plate with a hole in the middle is the most common sheet metal part there is.

D1075: A Flat Pattern that is on keeps the part's other bodies (2026-11-12, Phase 7D; found by the sheet metal part of D1071). With one Flat Pattern switched on, the part of eleven bodies showed one: the flat sheet. D2312 does not say what the other bodies do then, but it does say that the features of another sheet below a Flat Pattern go on being built, and they cannot when their sheet is gone. `common.beside_other_bodies` puts the other bodies beside the flat sheet (and beside the part folded sheet of the fold progress, D1112), as the rebuild does for every other sheet feature. A part of one sheet is as before.
Status: Default
Reason: Flattening one sheet must not remove the others; the owner can turn this round if he wants the flat view alone.

D1076: The safe boolean mode is used only when the two sides share no face (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the sheet metal part of D1071; this amends D1067). With two gussets on the tray, Fold said "a feature after Unfold adds material" for a slot that only removes it. Fold cuts the part after the slot by the part before it, and the two share nearly every face. In the kernel's safe mode (D1067) that cut came back as the whole part (94246 mm3 where nothing should be left) and the opposite cut as 221 mm3 where 320 are removed. The kernel's own mode gave 0 and 320, and so did the safe mode on copies that share nothing: the safe mode is wrong for shapes that share faces, on a body of this size. The classes of `fdcad.core.occ` now choose at every `Build`: the safe mode when no shape on one side shares a face with a shape on the other (`occ.share_a_face`), the kernel's own mode when one does. A tool made for the feature never shares a face with the part, so the case of D1067 (a later cut spoiling the kept results) stays covered, and the gearbox test that checks it still passes. What is given up: a boolean between two versions of one body runs as all booleans did before D1067.
Status: Default
Reason: A right answer comes before a protected input.

D1077: Lightening Pockets, Living Hinge and Landing Pad work on the body they were put on (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; idea 52, which the owner said to go on with). Each feature that hands the whole part to the kernel was put on a plate in a part that also held a block lying on the plate and two blocks locked with Interlock teeth elsewhere. Three disturbed the other bodies, with no message: through pockets and living hinge slits went on through the block lying on the plate (it lost more than half its volume), and Landing Pad, which fuses its pad with the whole part, joined the two locked blocks (D1055). All three now run on one body with `bodies.in_body_of` (D622): the body of the picked plate face, the body of the picked wall, and for Living Hinge the body of the face its sketch was drawn on (`bodies.sketch_face`; a sketch on a plane still slits every body it meets). Edge Profile, Ring Groove, O Ring Groove, Shaft Shape, Lattice Fill and Split for Printing with pins left the other bodies as they were in the same part and are not changed.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature put on a body changes that body.

D1078: A boss that touches nothing is put beside the other bodies with no kernel call (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; idea 52). The gearbox and the sheet metal part were built again with four bodies in the part from the start that no feature works on: two blocks locked with Interlock teeth and two blocks that share a face. Any change to them is a fault. The sheet metal part left them alone. In the gearbox the first feature, a plain Extrude of a block that touches nothing, joined the two locked blocks: `solids.combine` runs a boss on the bodies it reaches (D620), but for a boss that reaches none it still ran the fuse on the whole part, to add the new body, and the kernel then joined bodies that only touch each other (D1055). `solids._beside` now puts such a boss beside the others without the kernel, as `boolean_named` does. With that the whole gearbox leaves the four bodies as they were, but for its Section Cut, which cuts every body on one side of its plane by design.
Status: Default
Reason: Adding a body must not change the bodies that are there. Extrude is the first feature of nearly every part.

D1079: FDEF_SPEC.md names every feature type and every parameter (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, documentation; idea 59, which the owner said to go on with). The schema tests walk the sample files, so a key no sample writes could ship without a word in the spec. The gearbox sample (D1069) showed how far behind the spec was: 64 of the 137 feature types had no section, and 42 of the others had parameters that were added after their sections were written. Section 5.3.34 now has a section for each of the 64, section 5.3.35 the later parameters of the 42, and 5.3.36 a few references and keys named only in passing. The text was made from each feature module's own description (the contract its implementer wrote), with the names of code objects taken out of code marks so that only real file keys are marked; a parameter with no description there is listed with what it holds (length, angle, number, boolean, or its choices) from the feature type's parameter table. Nothing about the format changed: this writes down what the files already hold. `test_every_parameter_of_every_feature_type_is_in_its_section` fails when a type has no section or a parameter is not named in it, and the list of samples waiting for the spec is empty (the living hinge sample of D908 and the gearbox are off it). The test also took a type name with a digit (`sketch3d`) for having no section; that is fixed.
Status: Default
Reason: The file format is public, and a reader of the spec must find every key a file can hold.

D1080: A cut in one sheet of a part of several bodies keeps the other bodies (2026-11-12, Phase 7D, reliability; found by adding a plain hole to the sheet metal part of D1071). A plain Extrude cut in a sheet metal part is made square to the sheet and kept in the sheet model (Normal Cut, D700). `Extrude._normal_cut` took the newest sheet of the part, whichever body the cut was in, and handed back that sheet's solid alone. Since a part may hold several bodies (D2312), a hole in one sheet therefore removed every other body of the part (seven bodies became one), and a hole in any sheet but the newest was not made at all. The cut now looks for the sheet its tool reaches (`common.current_sheets`: the latest result of every sheet whose own solid is still in the part as that result left it), makes the square cut in that sheet's model and puts the other bodies back beside it. When the tool also reaches another body, or two sheets, the plain cut through them all is made as before. A part of one sheet is as it was.
Status: Default
Reason: A hole must not delete the rest of the part.

D1081: A history copy of features copies the patterns among them too (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, reliability; found by place checks on the gearbox, idea 60). The gearbox mirrors a foot, its hole, a pattern of the foot and the hole's follow pattern with Geometry pattern on. The face copy could not be patched away (the foot's bottom lies in the housing's bottom face), so the mirror fell back on the part's history (D1045). That history copy skipped every seed that is itself a pattern, as the face copy must (a pattern's faces are only its copies, D604), but what a pattern added or removed when it was built is exactly its copies, and nothing is counted twice. So the far side got the first foot and not the second, with no word. `patterns._pattern_history` now takes the patterns among the seeds like any other seed.
Status: Default
Reason: A mirror must copy everything it was given.

D1082: Points are tested against each body on its own (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, reliability; found by place checks on the gearbox). The kernel's point classifier counts the faces a ray from the point crosses, and given a compound of two bodies that share a face it counts that face twice: a point inside the upper of two stacked blocks comes back outside. A part's shape is such a compound whenever one body sits on another. `fdcad.core.occ.point_inside` asks each solid in turn, after a box test. Corner Relief used the whole part for its corner test, so a pocket in a body that sits on another got two of its four reliefs, with no word; it now uses the helper (test). The layer fit check of printing walls (D1209) used the whole part too and uses the helper now; on the test parts tried the kernel's ray happened to miss the shared face, so no fault was shown there, and its new test is only cover. Interlock, Rib, Hole, Knurl and Twist Lock already test one solid at a time. The test harness's own point test had the same fault, which made a check on the gearbox cover fail falsely.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature on a body that sits on another must see that body as solid.

D1083: Lip and Groove warns when the lip runs into the other body (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, reliability; found by place checks on the gearbox). The lip is made along the inside edge of its rim and the groove along the inside edge of its own rim (D318). On the gearbox the cover's recess was 2 mm wider than the housing's opening, so the lip stood 2 mm inside the groove, in the cover, and the two bodies overlapped by about 1500 cubic mm, with the feature OK. After building, the volume each lip shares with bodies other than its own is measured (a box test first, so only nearby bodies are measured), and above a millionth of the lip a warning names it: "the lip runs into the other body (N cubic mm), so the two do not fit together", with what to do. The geometry is left as it is (CLAUDE.md 5.12). The gearbox's recess now matches the opening, as was meant.
Status: Default
Reason: A lip that does not fit its groove must not pass as done.

D1084: A Fillet warns when a picked edge is a seam (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, usability; found by place checks on the gearbox). A seam is where a round face meets itself. It is not an edge between two faces, so there is nothing to round, and the kernel leaves it out with no word. On the gearbox shaft a pick on the end of a step's outline found the seam that starts there, and a fillet of three shoulders rounded two and was OK. `modify.seam_picks` finds picked edges that are closed on one of their faces, and Fillet gives a warning that highlights them; the other edges are rounded as before. Chamfer already refuses such a pick with "A picked edge has only one face", so it is not changed. The gearbox pick is moved onto the circle.
Status: Default
Reason: A pick that does nothing must be named.

D1085: The leaves of a pin hinge have room cut for each other's knuckles (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the overlap check on the gearbox). Each leaf gets every other knuckle, and room (the knuckle grown by the clearance) is cut from the other leaf where it goes. For the pin form the rooms and the pin hole were cut as one tool. The hole runs through every room, and with crossing pieces in one tool the kernel left the rooms uncut (the fault behind D1055): each leaf's knuckles stood in the other leaf, about 140 cubic mm a knuckle on the gearbox, and a printed hinge would come out fused, with the feature OK. The rooms are now cut alone; the hole is cut after the knuckles are on, as it already was. The print in place form never put the hole in that cut and was right. The test parts now check that no two bodies share material (`Kit.overlaps`).
Status: Default
Reason: The two halves of a hinge must be apart, or it does not turn.

D1086: An Extrude cut that removes no material warns (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, usability; found while writing the test for D1082). A cut drawn on the top face of a plate goes up, away from the plate, unless Reverse direction is on. It removed nothing and was OK with no word, where Hole, Inlay and Indent each say when they miss the part. After an Extrude cut, `extrude.cut_misses` looks at the faces the cut left in the part: each has the removed material on its outer side, so a point 0.01 mm outside one of them must have been inside the part before the cut. When none is, the warning says "<name> removes no material: its solid does not reach into the part. Turn on Reverse direction, or change the depth or the sketch." Whether the cut's faces are in the part at all does not tell, because a cut that only touches the part gives its name to the face it touches. At most twelve faces are tried, one point test each, so the check does not grow with the part. Revolve and other cuts are not changed; none was found to miss in this way.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature that does nothing must say so.

D1087: Big cutting boxes are sized from where they are centred (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the overlap check on the gearbox's joints built on their own). Finger Joint cuts its fingers out of the corner block with slabs centred on the model origin, sized as 4 times the part's diagonal plus 10 mm. On two small plates 340 mm from the origin the slabs stopped short of them: every finger came out empty, nothing was cut, the plates still overlapped, and the feature was OK. Half Lap centres its half spaces on a line through the origin in the same way, and Replace Face centres the slab that trims a moved face on the target plane's origin: on a 20 mm block 600 mm away it said the face "already lies on the target". `solids.reach_from(origin, shapes)` gives twice the distance from the centre to the far corner of the box round the shapes, plus 10 mm, and these use it; so does the slab of Revolve's Up to Face end, which is centred on a point of the target plane (no failing case was built for it; it is the same pattern). Finger Joint also refuses to report success when no finger could be made. Extrude ends, Living Hinge and Twist Lock centre their boxes on the geometry itself and are not changed.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature must work wherever the part is.

D1088: Tooltips show in every window, active or not (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner report: "nothing says anything on hover"). Qt shows a tooltip only when the window under the mouse is the one it counts as active. The 3D view is a native window, and on Windows, after a click or a turn in it, Qt could count no FDCAD window as active, so every tooltip went quiet until the window was clicked again. A test that moved a real mouse over the view toolbar showed tooltips first and none after using the view. The app style now sets Qt's "always show tooltips" flag on every window as it is polished.
Status: Default
Reason: A tooltip is how an icon says what it does; it must always work.

D1089: The view toolbar says what each button does, and a Hide or Show Items button (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner request: options to hide planes and show sketches and axes, and clearer icons). Three of the seven buttons were drawn as nearly the same cube (Section View, Standard Views, Display Style), and Zoom to Fit and Previous View were both drawn as corner marks. New drawings: Zoom to Fit is a lit solid inside the corner marks; Zoom to Area a dashed box with a magnifier; Previous View a screen with a back arrow; Section View a solid cut level with its cut face marked and the removed half dashed; Appearance a palette with dots in several colours; Standard Views a cube with one face marked and an arrow looking at it (its own icon, view.standard_views, so the Isometric command keeps its own). A new eye button, Hide or Show Items, lists View > Show Types (planes, axes, points, coordinate systems, curves, sketches, origins, temporary axes, dimensions, Hide All Types) and Show All Hidden Bodies. It uses the same actions, so a tick in one place shows in the other. The two dropdowns and the eye also say in one line what they hold.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner could not tell the buttons apart or find how to hide planes.

D1090: Three slow steps on parts with large curved faces are quicker, with the same results (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner report: "opening the bike frame takes time"). Opening the bike frame took 51 s; two features took 22 s of it. (1) Delete and Patch checks that no removed face is still there: it measured every face of the part once per removed face (435 surface integrals on lofted tubes, 1.4 s). Now a face is measured only when its bounding box holds the stored centre of area (a match must lie within 1e-3 mm of it, and a face's centre of area is always inside its box), and at most once. (2) A pattern of a face group works out what the group added by cutting the part with and without it, both ways. The two shapes share almost every face, the kernel's slowest case (4.7 s). Now the cuts are made in a box round the removed faces, grown by 1 mm or a tenth of their size. The change is one piece that fills where the faces were, so when no piece of it reaches a wall of the box the box held it all; when one does, or when the box holds no change, the whole part is used as before. (3) Wrap's Project method kept the pieces that touch the picked face by a distance from each piece to the face (4.5 s for ten letters on a down tube). Now apart bounding boxes answer no and a corner on the face answers yes, and only the rest are measured; sketch regions whose sweeps' boxes do not meet are cut out of the skin in one boolean. All 103 features of the bike frame give the same state, face count and exact volume as before. Text 11.6 s to 7.6 s, bottle boss pattern 10.0 s to 5.5 s. The rest of the open time is spread over many booleans on the frame, 0.5 to 2 s each, and is left for the performance pass.
Status: Default
Reason: Speed is a requirement (CLAUDE.md 5A); the same answers, found with less work.

D1091: Opening a part stores its shape for the next open (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, found while timing the bike frame). The shape cache, which shows a part at once on its next open (PLAN 11.2 item 2), was written only by Save. A part opened, looked at and closed without saving rebuilt in full every time it was opened: 51 s each time for the bike frame, and the cache folder had nothing newer than a week. Now a finished rebuild is stored too when the part has a file and is unchanged since it was opened or saved, and no checkpoint or hold stopped the rebuild early: then the document is exactly what the file holds, so its key is the file's. A part with unsaved changes stores nothing until it is saved, as before. The write runs off the UI thread, as Save's does (D723).
Status: Default
Reason: The cache exists to make the second open quick; it must be written when it can be.

D1092: Turning a kind off in Show Types takes it off the screen at once, and the plane picker draws only the planes on show (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner report: "i hid planes and stuff but it still shows"). The bike frame's 17 construction planes are reference planes, which show until hidden (D251), each drawn at the size of the part with its name, so they covered the frame. Show Types redrew only the part, not the planes, axes, points and sketches drawn with it, so they stayed until the next rebuild. A tab's new `refresh_types` draws all of them, and the rebuild uses it too. The plane picker (a sketch started with nothing picked) drew every plane of the part; it now draws the three main planes and the planes on show, and any other plane is picked in the tree (the status bar says so). Previous View is also taken off the view toolbar at the owner's request; it stays in the View menu and on Ctrl+Shift+Z. This does idea 65 in part: the labels still draw at the part's size.
Status: Default
Reason: Hiding a kind must hide it.

D1093: The Hide or Show Items menu leaves the Show Types actions alone (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner report: Hide All Types failed with "Internal C++ object (QAction) already deleted"). The eye menu of D1089 emptied itself with `clear()` each time it opened, to list the current actions again. Qt's `clear()` deletes the actions the menu holds, and it deleted Planes, Axes, Points, Coordinate Systems and Curves, which belong to View > Show Types; Hide All Types then met deleted actions. It now removes each action without deleting it, and deletes only its own separators.
Status: Default
Reason: A fix for D1089, which brought the fault in.

D1094: A selected face is drawn a little nearer the camera than the face under it (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner report: "surface colors look broken, jagged at times", with a screenshot of a selected seat stay covered in blotches). The kernel draws highlights as a see-through copy of the face. The hover highlight goes in a layer with its own depth and drew cleanly, but the selection highlight stayed in the part's own layer, at the very depth of the face it covers, and the two fought over each pixel. The selection styles now go in the kernel's Top layer, which keeps the part's depth (so parts in front still hide a selection) and is drawn with a polygon offset of -1 and -4 toward the camera, the values the feature preview uses for the same fault (PV2.3).
Status: Default
Reason: A selected face must look selected, not broken.

D1095: Hover highlights share the part's depth too (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner report: the colour is still broken "when you move the cursor over it", after D1094). The kernel drew the hover highlight of a face in its Topmost layer, which has a depth buffer of its own; a see-through face writes no depth, so the far side of a tube showed through its near side in patches. All four highlight styles (hover and selection, of an object and of a face) now go in the Top layer of D1094: the part's depth, a little nearer the camera. The owner checked it on the bike frame.
Status: Default
Reason: Hover is the most used highlight; it must draw cleanly.

D1096: The eye button hides everything on a click and lists each kind on hover (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner request: "hover brings the drop down menu and eye click acts as the hide unhide click"). D1089 made the eye a dropdown. Now a click runs Hide All Types, a second click shows every kind again as it was, and the button looks pressed in between. Resting the pointer on it for a quarter of a second opens a list under it (`HoverList` in `view_bar.py`) with a check box per kind and buttons for Hide All Types and Show All Hidden Bodies, the same actions as View > Show Types. The list is a frameless window that takes no mouse grab: a Qt menu grabs the mouse while open, so a click on the eye would only have closed it. It closes when the pointer has left both the button and the list, and the button's tooltip is held back while it is open. The owner checked it.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner's way to work: one click for all, a glance for each kind.

D1097: Each feature's result is stored beside the finished part, so a reopened part rebuilds in moments (2026-11-13, Phase 7D, owner request: "research what we can do to open the parts faster and implement that"; PLAN 11.3 item 2 and FDEF_SPEC 13 item 3 asked for it). Research first: OCCT is 8.0 and its thread pool already uses all 12 cores; oriented boxes, no fuzzy value, no inverted solid check and destructive mode gave the same 30 s of booleans on the bike frame (65 recorded booleans replayed); a boolean on a box round the tool costs half the full one, so local booleans would not pay; the frame is mostly planes and cylinders. So the work is what it is, and the answer is not to do it twice. Since D1091 the finished part is stored and shown at once, but every feature was built again behind it (41 s). `cache/history.py` now writes, with the finished part, the result of every feature that makes solids: the bodies in one BinTools compound without display meshes (faces shared between steps are written once: 1.6 MB for the 103 feature frame), and a JSON list of each result's engine key, body index, face names, issues with fixes, cosmetic threads and plain extras (hole centres and count, report lines). Opening a part loads them into the engine's memory cache before the rebuild, which then reuses them by key and builds only sketches, planes and other quick features: the bike frame shows in 0.14 s and its rebuild is done in 0.5 s, not 41 s, with the same result. Each file carries a stamp of the FDCAD build (its version and the size and time of every core module, or of the program file when packaged), and a history of another build is never used, so a fixed feature is always built again. Results with sketches, planes, reference geometry or other extras are left to the rebuild. The part file is not changed: it still holds no solid (FDEF_SPEC 1 item 3), so a part's very first open on a computer still builds everything.
Status: Default
Reason: Opening a part again should take a moment, not a rebuild.

D1098: A Rib finds its body when only one body holds its sketch (2026-11-14, Phase 7D, found by the gearbox place checks of idea 60 with the canary bodies of D1078). A Rib on a part of several bodies with no body picked failed with "the part has several bodies. Pick the body for the rib." The gearbox's Inside Gusset, a line inside the housing, failed as soon as the part also held two blocks 1.2 m away. Now, with no body picked, the Rib uses the one body whose bounding box holds the whole sketch, exactly as if that body were picked; when no body or more than one does, it asks as before. This is the rule of D1077 for Lightening Pockets, Living Hinge and Landing Pad.
Status: Default
Reason: A rib drawn inside one body should not need its body picked.

D1099: Lattice Fill groups its faces into shells without sewing, and refuses a sheet of more than 60,000 faces with a cell size that fits (2026-11-14, Phase 7D, found because the slow app sweep hung on the enclosure sample). The default gyroid (10 mm cells, 1 mm wall) in the enclosure's 80 by 60 by 40 mm box is 513,644 faces. D2004 capped the grid at 400,000 cubes, which this is well under (about 112,000), but the time goes with the faces, and much faster than they grow: sewing 46,152 faces took 29 s and the boolean after it 13.5 s, and 513,644 never ended, so OK on Lattice Fill hung the app. Two changes. (1) The STL reader already shares each edge between its two triangles (46,152 faces had 69,228 edges, three halves of the faces), so sewing found nothing to join: `BOPAlgo_ShellSplitter` groups the faces into closed shells in 1.8 s with the same 27 valid solids and the same volume. (2) A gyroid or diamond sheet of more than 60,000 faces is refused before any kernel work: "the lattice would have 513,644 faces, too many to build in good time (60,000 at most); a cell of 21 mm or more fits". The faces of one cell are fixed, so the count goes with the cube of the cell size and the size that fits is worked out from it. Handing the faces to the splitter is a loop in Python over the faces (0.1 s for 46,000), kept because it replaces 29 s of sewing.
Status: Default
Reason: OK on a feature must never hang the app.

D1100: The slow tests that run over every sample treat the gearbox as heavy (2026-11-14, Phase 7D). Since the gearbox became a sample (D1069) the slow suite (`--run-slow`) could not finish: the full naming stress made 40 seeded edits on it, each rebuilding its 319 features three times (over three hours, and it was still going), and the full app sweep would then run every command with every selection on it. The quick stress test already listed it in HEAVY. Now the full naming stress makes 4 edits on the gearbox (40 on every other sample) and the full command sweep leaves it out; its own tests build it three ways and check where its material is (test_gearbox_part.py). The suite runs earlier tonight had skipped the slow tests, which is how the Lattice Fill hang of D1099 went unseen.
Status: Default
Reason: A test suite that cannot finish checks nothing.

D1101: Delete and Patch works on the body that holds the faces only (2026-11-14, Phase 7D, found by the gearbox naming stress test of the slow suite, D1100). After a change upstream, the gearbox rebuilt from the cache differed from a full rebuild: the part had 16 more faces after Square The Corner (Remove Fillets on a block). The kernel's defeaturing was given the whole part, 52 bodies, and rebuilds every body it is given; two plates locked with teeth, far from the block, came back with their touching faces split another way and renamed. Checks made first: two full builds give the same part; no feature changes the tolerances of a result kept for an earlier feature. `direct.patch` (Delete Face, Remove Fillets, patterns of face groups) now runs on the one body that holds all the faces through `bodies.in_body_of`, as D1077 does for other features, and on the whole part only when the faces lie in several bodies. A test patches a boss beside two locked blocks: they must come back the very same shapes with the same names (they did not before).
Status: Default
Reason: A feature must not rebuild bodies it does not work on.

D1102: A part file may carry the finished solid of its last rebuild (2026-11-14, Phase 7D, owner's decision: of three choices offered, the solid inside the .fdprt file, a file beside it, or neither, the owner chose the first). This changes FDEF_SPEC section 1 item 3, which said a part file does not store the rebuilt solid. Why: after D1090, D1091 and D1097 a part opened before shows at once and rebuilds in moments, but the first open on a computer still built every feature before showing anything (about 40 s for the bike frame); every way to build faster was tried first (D1097). What: an optional top level key `solid` (FDEF_SPEC 2 item 16 and 13A): the body in BinTools binary BRep without display meshes, gzip compressed and base64 encoded, its face names as indices in the body's face order, each feature's state and messages, and the cache key of the document it was built from. Save writes it from the last rebuild when that rebuild finished for the document being saved, encoding it on a worker thread that Save waits for (CLAUDE.md 5 item 2), and leaves it out otherwise. Opening a part with no local cache entry shows that solid at once, but only when its key matches the document as read, so a file changed outside FDCAD, or saved by an older FDCAD that kept the key as unknown, is built from its tree; the rebuild still runs behind it as with the local cache. `Document.solid` is not part of equality or the cache key, and parts saved without a solid save byte for byte as before. Each feature's results (D1097) are not put in the file: they are tied to the FDCAD build that made them.
Status: Default
Reason: The owner wants parts to open at once, also the first time on a new computer.

D1103: The gearbox sample opens with no warnings (2026-11-14, Phase 7D, owner request after asking about the two features with warnings). Both warnings were true: the parting line of the finished housing crossed every hole, round and groove, whose faces have both kinds of draft, and Heal Import, which heals every body of the part, left one deformed bar as it was because healing would have made it not valid (D1066). The Parting Line now stands right after the Housing Block, on the plain block, where it runs round the bottom and crosses no face; it only adds a curve, so nothing after it changes. Heal Edges is taken out of the gearbox: it cannot be pointed at one body, and every way to keep it left the warning; test_heal_edges.py keeps both of its warning cases (D1066). Split Faces on the parting line was tried first and dropped: it split faces a later feature picks. The sample is 318 features of 105 types in 60 bodies; all 545 place checks pass.
Status: Default
Reason: A sample part should open clean.

D1104: Delete and Patch says so when it changes nothing (2026-11-14, Phase 7D, found by the single body machine bed). A through hole in a block had its top raised by Move Face, which gave the hole a second wall face, a 2 mm band. Delete Face with Patch on the old wall face reported OK: the kernel removed that face and let the band grow down into its place, so the hole stayed open and no material came or went. The checks that the picked faces are gone passed, because they were. `direct.patch` (Delete Face, Remove Fillets, patterns of face groups) now also compares the part's volume before and after, to a part in a billion, and when nothing changed it fails: "<feature> changed nothing: removing <faces> let the faces next to them grow back into their place. Pick every face of the hole or boss." The same principle as D1086 for cuts.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature that does nothing must say so.

D1105: On a large body a face is moved with a slab before the whole body offset (2026-11-14, Phase 7D, owner: the machine bed "should open under 1 minute"). A profile of the 768 feature machine bed (1146 s) put 207 s in one Push/Pull and 199 s in one Move Face, each lifting one small flat face 2 or 3 mm. Both go through `direct.offset_faces`, which gave the kernel's BRepOffset_MakeOffset the whole body with a zero offset on every face but the moved one, and that works on all 5400 faces. A slab added on the face (or cut into it) already existed as the fallback when the offset failed, for faces whose neighbours all meet them square; it is the same shape and costs one boolean. On a body of more than 600 faces the slab is now tried first. On smaller bodies the offset is kept, because rounds made again after a move (Reapply Fillets) rely on the face names it gives: trying the slab first on every body broke two such tests. A cut of a 5 mm hole on the finished bed takes 1.7 s in the kernel, with no option making it faster, so a rebuild of 768 features from nothing cannot be brought under a minute; opening without a rebuild is the answer (D1102 and after).
Status: Default
Reason: Moving one face must not cost minutes because the part is large.

D1106: A saved part whose rebuild is slow opens as saved, without a rebuild, when no stored results would make the rebuild quick (2026-11-14, Phase 7D, owner: the machine bed "should open under 1 minute"). Opening the 768 feature machine bed with its saved solid (D1102) on a computer without its history showed nothing for more than 50 s and the window stopped responding. Showing the solid takes 3.5 s (0.2 s to read it, 2.9 s to mesh it), but the rebuild started at once behind it and builds all 768 features again (16 minutes). A test showed the kernel holds Python's lock for each call: while a worker made three cuts on the bed (6.6 s), the main thread ran 5 times, waiting up to 2.6 s each time, so the window could not paint. The rebuild on open is now skipped when the part was shown from its saved solid or the shape cache, no stored per-feature results were found (D1097), and the features' saved build times add up to more than 30 s (SLOW_OPEN_SECONDS). Each feature's state now carries `seconds` for this, in the file's `solid` (FDEF_SPEC 13A, an optional key inside the entry approved for D1102) and in the shape cache. The status bar says the saved shape is shown and that sketches and planes appear after Ctrl+B; any change rebuilds as usual. Saving a part shown this way unchanged keeps the saved solid. Quick parts still rebuild on open, so their sketches and planes show at once.
Status: Default
Reason: A part that took 16 minutes to build must still open in seconds and leave the window usable.

D2600: Long rebuilds run in a helper process, so the window never waits on the kernel (2026-11-15, Phase 7D, owner: "we want all features to load faster, not this gimmick" about D1106, then "run these tasks in order" for the release list). The kernel holds Python's lock for the whole of each call, so a rebuild on a worker thread starved the window (IDEAS 68): the machine bed (768 features) froze it for its whole 16 minute rebuild and Cancel could not be clicked. A rebuild that is expected to take more than 8 s (`remote.REMOTE_SECONDS`: the saved build times of every feature from the first one that changed, `remote.estimate`, from `RebuildEngine.built`), or a saved part shown at open whose build took more than 30 s, now runs in a second FDCAD process (`fdcad.core.rebuild.remote`; the packaged app starts itself with `--rebuild-helper`, see packaging/launcher.py). The two talk over a local pipe with a random key (`multiprocessing.connection`, a named pipe on Windows, a socket file on macOS); the document goes across as a pickle of the snapshot the rebuild works on, so the helper builds exactly the same numbers. The helper starts from the stored results of the part's recent states (`RebuildEngine.history_keys`), builds the rest, and writes every result to the history cache (D1097) and the finished part to the shape cache. The app then reads them back into its memory cache and runs its own rebuild, which builds only sketches, planes and other quick features. While the helper works the app makes no kernel calls and does not hold the kernel lock. Cancel and a newer edit ask the helper to stop; it writes what it has built under `<key>.partial`, so the next rebuild goes on from there. A helper that ends with no word (a native fault in the kernel) names the feature it was building: the rebuild is held before it, as the crash guard does (D1035), with a message bar and a Suppress button; FDCAD itself stays open. A helper that cannot start falls back to the app's own rebuild (or, for a slow saved part, to D1106's kept shape). `FDCAD_REBUILD_HELPER=0` turns the helper off. D1106 now applies only then. The history cache is now format 2: face names are two arrays of numbers and a table of names, made into named faces only when something asks (`history.LazyNamedShape`), each result carries its memory size, and display extras may hold dicts, tuples, lists and shapes (O-ring grooves, contours and measurements were left to the app's rebuild before). Measured on the machine bed: cold rebuild in the helper 951 s with the window free; the app's part after it 1.0 s to read the results (was 7.1 s), 0 s to seed them (was 6.4 s) and 11.8 s of sketches and planes (was 47 s, in steps of at most 0.75 s); an edit to a pocket near the end, expected at 44 s, took 74 s in the helper and 1.9 s in the app. The helper also meshes the finished part at the part's display quality and the history keeps triangles (meshing the bed again took 2.7 s in the app, checking a stored mesh 0.6 s; the meshing code moved to `fdcad.core.display_mesh`). A timer on the window's thread while the bed opened and rebuilt from nothing (1000 s): the longest wait during the helper's build was 0.17 s; after it 1.0 s (reading the results) and 0.65 s; at open 2.5 s, meshing the solid saved in the file, which happens only on the first open on a computer (the shape cache keeps the mesh).
Status: Default
Reason: The window must stay usable during any rebuild, however large the part.

D2601: Cuts and joins on large bodies are made only where the tool is (2026-11-16, Phase 7D, IDEAS 66 stage 1, owner: "run these tasks in order"). On the machine bed (one body of 5400 faces) the kernel's boolean took about 2 s for every cut, even a 3 mm hole, because it works on every face of both shapes and rebuilt the 955 holes of the bed's top face each time; booleans were 58 percent of the cold rebuild. `fdcad.core.local_boolean` now makes a cut or join of one solid of at least 1000 faces with one solid tool (no glue, the caller's fuzzy value) from the faces whose boxes meet the tool's box only: those go to the kernel's splitter (BOPAlgo_Builder, safe mode), a big flat face whose outline is away from the tool is stood in for by a patch of its plane that carries the face's holes inside it, tool pieces are sorted by counting ray crossings over the body's faces (face boxes in numpy, the kernel's face intersectors kept per face), body pieces by the kernel's classifier on the tool, and pieces on a face of the other shape by the directions of the two faces. The kept pieces go into a copy of the body's shell. Before a result is used it must be sound: every new face valid (for a patched face, the patch with its loops), every edge of the new and removed faces that is still in the shell used twice with opposite directions, and the faces round the change all in one connected piece (which is enough, since the shell was one piece before). Anything else, or any doubt, goes to the kernel's own boolean: a hollow inside, a lump beside, a cut in two, several shells, an unclear ray. The safe boolean classes in `fdcad.core.occ` try it in `Build` and answer `Shape`, `History`, `Modified`, `IsDeleted`, `IsDone` from it; the history holds every face of both shapes, so names follow as before (where the kernel keeps a tool face itself the splitter may give an equal copy, which takes the same name). Each result's face index is kept for the next feature (six bodies at most). `FDCAD_LOCAL_BOOLEAN=0` turns it off; `FDCAD_LOCAL_BOOLEAN_CHECK=1` also runs the kernel and raises `LocalMismatchError` when the material, the face count or validity differ. Measured on the bed: each cut 0.16 to 0.37 s where the kernel took 1.6 to 3.4 s, same results; the whole bed built with the check on: 262 local cuts and joins all equal to the kernel's, 9 handed to the kernel (7 edge checks, 2 patches split), all 768 features OK and all 1178 place checks right; a cold rebuild of the bed 666 s, was 951 s.
Status: Default
Reason: A large part must not pay for its whole size in every small cut.

D2602: A weak name whose number went to another piece is found by position (2026-11-16, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the edit storm, `tests/core/features/edit_storm.py`, owner: "run these tasks in order", step 4). The storm opens a finished part and changes each of its numbers in turn by one percent (a count by one), rebuilding with the same engine as the app, then checks that no feature that built before fails, that a new engine gives the same part, and that putting the number back gives the first part. On the bike frame (size M, 103 features, 75 numbers) five edits made features fail, and a new engine failed the same way, so the reused results were right and the fault was in naming. A one percent change to the end size of the right chain stay lost four weld edges of Weld Stays to Dropouts. The dome on the stay's end has four faces, numbered by position (D1052); two are mirror images above and below the stay's middle, but the dome's surface is fitted, so their centres agree only to about 2e-5 mm (also with the kernel's most careful integration: the difference is in the surface, not the sum). That difference ordered them, and the edit swapped `face#2` and `face#3`. D720 checks a weak name against its snapshot, but only the face the name gives counted: when that was the other piece and the right one had moved a little, nothing matched exactly and the reference was lost; an edge named from the swapped number (`edge(f27/dome/1/face#2|f34/cap/end)`) found no edge at all and went straight to the exact snapshot match, which an edit always misses. `resolve._judge` now also takes another member of the family when it is the clearly nearest (D720's ratio) and has not moved more than half its size, with the "now names another face" warning; and a weak face, edge or vertex name that gives nothing is judged over its family (`_family_pick`), with the "found by its position" warning. Two equally near pieces are still never chosen between, and a piece that moved far for its size is still lost. Widening the 1e-6 mm order tolerance instead would renumber faces in saved parts (FDEF_SPEC 8.2) and only moves the edge of the problem. Of the five edits, two (the stay's end size, the dome's height) now build with warnings only. Moving the right dropout plane: Dropout Corners and six of eight weld edges are found; two short edges really became one edge 1.5 mm from both, beyond half their size, and stay lost. Making the dropout 1 percent thicker: six features are found; Hanger Thread M10 still fails, rightly: the hanger and the dropout were both 6 mm, so their tops were one face, and at 6.06 mm the hanger's top is a face of its own, 0.06 mm lower, under the hole's point. The fifth, the head tube's revolve angle, was the storm's own fault: a full turn was turned down to 356 degrees, which opens the tube; the storm now leaves full turns alone. Tests: `tests/core/naming/test_weak_swap.py` (a plate whose two top pieces swap numbers when moved 0.3 mm: a face and an edge failed before the change; a small edit without a swap, a piece that moved too far and two equally near pieces are the guards).
Status: Default
Reason: A one percent edit must not lose what the user picked when the picked piece is plainly still there.

D2603: Layer Preview cuts every layer in one kernel call (2026-11-16, Phase 7D, speed; found by the app sweep on the nut and bolt sample, `tests/ui/test_app_sweep.py`, which runs only with the slow tests). Layer Preview on the nut and bolt took 40 s, over the sweep's 30 s limit for one step: `layer_lines` asked the kernel for one section per layer, 127 calls of 0.3 s each, almost all of it intersecting the thread's surfaces again for every layer (the safe mode of D1067 costs nothing here: 3.25 s against 3.18 s for 20 layers). It now gives the kernel every layer at once, as square faces of the layer planes reaching past the whole part, so each face of the part is prepared once: 16.5 s, the same 755 edges. When that one call fails it cuts each layer alone as before and keeps the layers that work. Cutting the display mesh with numpy would take milliseconds, but the lines would then need a new way to draw segments in the 3D view (the kernel's segment arrays cannot be filled from numpy through OCP), so that is left as IDEAS item 69. Test: `tests/core/test_layer_lines.py` counts the kernel calls (one, was one per layer), and a tilted build direction still cuts every layer.
Status: Default
Reason: The budgets of PLAN section 11 are tests, and a preview must not take most of a minute on a small part.

D2604: A fillet names edges that round on their own but not with the others (2026-11-16, Phase 7D, reliability; found by the edit storm of D2602 on the gearbox). With the draft of Output Bearing Boss at 3.03 degrees (3 as built), Boss Roots failed: "failed on 1 of 4 edges: edge 4. The radius is larger than the faces next to these edges allow". Each of the four root edges rounds on its own, and the kernel fails only when the last two, the roots of the two mirrored bosses, which overlap and meet at a corner, are rounded in one call with the first two; at 3, 2.97 and 3.06 degrees all four round together. So the message was wrong about the cause. Rounding the edges in passes automatically was tried and dropped: the edges of each wall meet at a corner, and rounds made one after the other meet differently at a corner than one call (D1405), which would change the part without the user's click (CLAUDE.md 5.12). D1405's fixes already offer it, and here "Fillet each chain as its own feature (2 fillets)" builds. `fillet.pinpoint` now marks such an edge "(rounds on its own)", and when every failing edge is one, the message says the kernel cannot round them together and to use a fix to round them as separate fillets. Tests: `tests/core/features/test_fillet_together.py` (a kernel that fails on two edges in one call; a radius that is really too large keeps the old words; the gearbox case, slow). The other gearbox storm problems so far (Housing Block depth, Middle Plane distance, Input Bearing Boss depth) are right: faces that were one face because two features ended at the same number split, and points or picks end up over the other piece (IDEAS 70).
Status: Default
Reason: An error must say what failed and why; blaming the radius sent the user to the wrong value.

D2605: Lattice Fill refuses a sheet too costly to fit a curved body (2026-11-17, Phase 7D, reliability and memory; found by the full app sweep on the swept spring and the twisted sweep). The sweep pressed OK on Lattice Fill with the panel's values (10 mm gyroid, 1 mm wall, 1.2 mm skin). On the spring the sheet had 51,632 faces, under the face limit of D1099, but every one met the box of the spring's one freeform face, so the boolean that keeps the sheet inside the body ran for over 15 minutes and took about 20 GB, until the machine ran out of memory. On the twisted sweep the same fill took 165 to 190 s. The time goes with the number of lattice faces that meet the box of a curved face of the body, and with how heavy that face is: about 1 ms each for a cylinder, 2 ms for the twisted sweep's simple splines (14 control points), 20 ms for the spring's spline (396 control points, degree 6 by 9), little for a plane. Lattice Fill now counts these crossings in numpy before any kernel work (one pass per curved face of the body, not per triangle), weighted 1 for a cylinder, cone, sphere or torus, the larger of 2 and one per 20 control points for a spline, 2 for other freeform faces, and refuses more than 10,000, with the cell size that fits. A skin adds two more booleans of the same size, so the limit keeps the whole feature under the 30 s the app sweep allows one step. The spring is refused in 0.9 s and builds at the 44 mm the message names in 4.5 s; the twisted sweep at 18 mm in 13.3 s. Honeycomb is not counted: it is exact and capped at 4000 hexagons. No sample uses a gyroid or diamond fill.
Status: Default
Reason: One OK with the default values must not take all the memory of the machine. The count is fixed by the shapes, not by the clock, so the same part gives the same answer on every machine.

D2606: The Shell fix search tries fewer faces on a large body and stops on Cancel (2026-11-17, Phase 7D, speed; found by the full app sweep on the attractor plate). A 1 mm shell of the attractor plate (83 faces, 77 of them holes) fails in the kernel. The search of D1406 then shells the body again with each of the 25 tightest faces left open, both corner kinds each, to find one face to offer as Skip Face. That took 33 s of the 35 s, the live preview ran it again before OK, and Cancel waited for it, so one step of the sweep took 34 to 120 s. The search now offsets at most 1000 faces over all its tries (a body of up to 40 faces keeps all 25 tries, the attractor plate gets 12) and stops between tries when the build is cancelled. The shell now fails in 17 s with the same message. A face that only a later try would have found is no longer offered on a large body; the plain message tells the user what to change.
Status: Default
Reason: A fix search is a help, and must not cost more than the build it helps. The limit is set by the body's faces, not the clock, so every machine gives the same answer.

D2607: The right click sweep leaves out the gearbox, as the command sweep does (2026-11-17, Phase 7D, tests). The app sweep runs every item of the view menu and of every feature tree row's menu, Cancel and OK. On the gearbox that is 319 rows, and items such as Suppress, Roll Back and Delete each rebuild the part from that row on; after more than an hour the test was still on it, using a whole core. D1100 left the gearbox out of the command sweep for the same reason. Its own tests build it three ways and check where its material is (test_gearbox_part.py), and the right click menus are swept on every other sample. On a tree of more than 60 rows the row menus are swept on the first and the last 20 rows only: on generated_200 (about 200 rows) each row took 20 to 40 s, so the test ran for two hours or more, and the items are the same on every row. The first rows are the costly ones, since they rebuild the most.
Status: Default
Reason: A test that would run for days is not run at all; the menus are the same code on every part.

D2608: Delete Face refuses an end cap at once (2026-11-17, Phase 7D, speed; found by the right click sweep on the lofted handle). Delete Face with Patch on the flat end of the lofted handle ran the kernel's defeaturing for 176 to 253 s, then failed with "the faces around ... cannot grow to close the gap". The faces round an end cap grow on straight along its normal, so they can only make an open tube; on the handle's spline sides the kernel took minutes to find that out (on its sides, deleting a face takes 0.2 s). Before the kernel call, Delete Face now looks at each edge of the gap: when every face next to it grows on within 5 degrees of the removed faces' outward normal, and none of them goes round the gap on an inner loop (as the top of a plate goes round a hole wall), the same message is given at once. The check takes 0.01 s. It passes a hole wall, a chamfer, a whole boss and the loft's sides, and refuses a box top, a boss top alone and the loft's caps; the kernel fails on each refused case as well, so no result that built before is lost. Delete Face, Remove Fillets, Reapply Fillets and Move Face share the patch step and their tests pass.
Status: Default
Reason: A fix that cannot work should say so at once, not after minutes with the window waiting.

D2609: A sketch works out the part's silhouette only when a tool asks for it (2026-11-17, Phase 7D, speed; found by the right click sweep on the nut and bolt). Every sketch that opened worked out three sets of part curves for TR6 in a kernel job: where the plane cuts the part, the part turned about the sketch's X axis, and its outline seen square to the plane. The outline comes from the kernel's hidden line removal, which took 27.6 s on the threads of the nut and bolt (the other two took 0.1 s), and the kernel holds Python's lock for the whole call (idea 68), so the window waited about 30 s each time a sketch opened on that part. Only the Silhouette tool and Close Sketch to Model use the outline. The sketch now works out the other two when it opens, and the outline when one of those tools is picked; the tool says it is working out the curves until they come. Curves worked out for an older plane or cut away state are dropped when they arrive.
Status: Default
Reason: Work nobody asked for must not hold the window; the outline costs nothing until a tool needs it.

D2610: Temporary axes no longer fail on a part whose round faces share a later axis (2026-11-17, Phase 7D, bug; found while timing the sketch jobs of D2609). When a cylinder or cone face lay on an axis that was not the first one found, the code looked the axis up with list.index, which compares tuples holding numpy arrays and raised. The sketch's projection job catches errors so that snapping never breaks sketching, so the sketch lost every part snap target, not only the axes, each time it opened with temporary axes shown on such a part: the nut and bolt, or any part with two counterbored holes. The axis is now replaced by its position in the list. All 34 samples now give their axes without an error.
Status: Default
Reason: A bug fix; the axis lines are unchanged where they worked before.

D2611: Saving again writes the solid it wrote before (2026-11-17, Phase 7D, bug; found by the Save As test of the app sweep, failing since D1102). Each save encoded the finished solid again (D1102), and two encodings of the same shape from the same rebuild differed in a few bytes near the end: flags the kernel keeps on a shape changed after it was first written. So a part saved twice with no change gave two different files, which shows as a change in version control, and the encoding was done twice. The session now remembers which rebuild the document's solid was encoded from, and a save with the same rebuild and the same document key writes that solid as it is. A new rebuild is encoded again.
Status: Default
Reason: A save of an unchanged part must give the same file; it is also less kernel work on each save.

D2612: Offset Face on a flat face whose neighbours are all flat adds or cuts a tapered slab on a body with free form faces (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; found by the right click sweep, idea 75). Moving one side of the hexagon head of the nut and bolt by 1 mm took 35 to 37 s, over the sweep's 30 s limit for one command: the kernel's offset works on every face of the body, and the time went on the thread's spline faces, far from the head (on a 6 face piece of the head it took no time). When the moved face and each face next to it are flat, the result is known: the face goes to the parallel plane and each neighbour carries on in its own plane. The slab between the old and the new face is built from those planes (each new corner is where the new plane meets the planes of the corner's two neighbours), sewn into a solid and added or cut as the square slab of D1105 is, with its far face taking the face's names. It is used on bodies the offset is slow on: more than 600 faces (D1105) or any spline, Bezier, offset, revolved or extruded surface. Only a face with one loop of straight edges qualifies, where each corner touches the face and its two edge neighbours only; any other face, or a slab the kernel finds invalid, uses the offset as before. On the nut and bolt the result has the same volume, faces and face names as the offset, in 0.06 s.
Status: Default
Reason: Same shape as the offset, built from planes near the face instead of reworking the whole body; plain small bodies keep the offset, as D1105 chose for Reapply Fillets.

D2613: The early refusal of D2608 is only made on bodies the kernel is slow on (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by the full suite: a face pattern of a boss top failed). D2608 refused a Delete Face whose neighbours can only grow into a tube before calling the kernel, on the grounds that the kernel fails there too. That holds on the spline sides of the lofted handle, but on plain faces the kernel answers in 0.03 s, and removing the top of a square boss alone takes the whole boss with it. Face patterns of a boss top find the boss's volume that way, so D2608 broke them ("the picked faces do not form a whole feature"). The early refusal is now made only where the kernel is slow, the same test as D2612: more than 600 faces or any free form surface. Elsewhere the kernel decides, as before D2608.
Status: Default
Reason: The check exists to save minutes of waiting; on plain parts it cost nothing to ask the kernel and refusing lost results that built before.

D2614: The check of D1086 (a cut that removes no material warns) skips its point test when a face of the cut is new (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; idea 76). Each point test classifies a point against the whole part, about 2.2 ms on generated_200's 202 faces, 0.22 s over its 98 cuts, which took the sample's full rebuild close to the 3 s budget so the budget test failed when the machine was busy. When a cut leaves a face that carries only the cut's own names, that face is a new surface inside the old material, so the cut removed some. Where the cut only touches the part, the face it touches also keeps the part's names, and the point test still runs there. On generated_200 the check now makes no point tests and takes 0.015 s for all 98 cuts; the cut that points away from the plate still warns.
Status: Default
Reason: The names already say which faces are new; asking the kernel costs a classification against every face.

D2615: Layer Preview cuts the mesh of a part with free form faces, in numpy (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; found by the app sweep on the lofted handle).
