The one kernel section of D2603 still took 10 to 22 s on spline faces (lofted handle 19.6 s, nut and bolt 22 s, twisted bar 10 s with the PC busy), and the kernel holds Python's lock (idea 68), so the window waited and the sweep's 30 s step limit was passed. On a part the kernel is slow on (the test of D2612: more than 600 faces or any free form surface) the part's triangles are now taken in one array (as Overhang Analysis does) and each triangle is cut at the layer heights it spans in numpy; each segment becomes a kernel edge and all of them one compound, shown as one item instead of one item per edge. The three samples now take 0.3 to 0.5 s. The lines lie on the mesh, so they follow the part as it is drawn. Parts of planes, cylinders and the like keep the exact kernel lines, which are quick there.
Status: Default
Reason: The preview is display only; on spline parts the exact cut cost 40 times more for lines that the shaded mesh shows the same.

D2616: Shell names two faces too close for a wall on each before searching for a face to skip (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; found by the app sweep on the attractor plate). Two holes of the attractor plate are 2 mm apart, so a 1 mm inward shell cannot be made: the moved hole walls meet. After the kernel failed, the search of D1406 and D2606 shelled the plate 12 more times, about 1.1 s each, and found no face, so Shell held the window for about 16 s and then gave the plain message. When an inward shell without face thicknesses fails, Shell now looks for two flat faces or hole walls facing each other across less than two walls of material, with the gaps worked out in numpy from the surfaces. The closest pairs are confirmed on the faces themselves: the faces must not share an edge, their own distance must be the surfaces' gap, and the point between them must be inside the part. A confirmed pair gives "faces A and B are 2 mm apart, too close for a 1 mm wall on each. Use a wall thinner than 1 mm, or move those faces apart." with both faces highlighted, and the search is not run. The check takes under 0.01 s on the plate, and the step now fails in about 1.5 s. It runs only after the kernel has failed, so it never refuses a shell the kernel can make. Outward shells, other surfaces and parts with face thicknesses keep the search.
Status: Default
Reason: The kernel's offset needs room for both walls; naming the two faces tells the user exactly what to change, where the search could only say the offset failed.

D2620: Typed values accept exponent notation (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; idea 53). A pasted number such as 2e+06 failed with "Unknown unit 'e'", since the tokenizer read 2 as the number and e as a unit name. A number may now end in e or E, an optional sign and digits: 2e6, 2E+06, 1.5e-3, 2e3 mm. The exponent needs its digits, so 2e, 2e+ and 2e-mm still fail as before, and a name such as e or e3 in a formula is still a variable. No unit name starts with e, so no unit is read differently. FDEF_SPEC 12.2 item 1 describes the form.
Status: Default
Reason: Numbers copied from a spreadsheet, a calculator or a printout often come in this form, and the old message did not say why.

D2621: A dome tests the outline of a face by its shape, not its kind (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; idea 54). The round end of a loft or a scaled sweep is bounded by a spline that is a circle in shape, and the dome took only a circle edge as round, so a distance of 0 failed with "only works on a round face" and any other distance asked for Continuous dome. When the outline of a flat face with no holes is not one circle edge and has no straight edge, 64 points are taken along each of its edges and a circle is fitted to them in numpy (the plane of the points, then a least squares circle in that plane). The face counts as round when no point is further than 1e-4 times the radius from that plane or that circle; the spline ends of a scaled sweep and of a loft are within 1e-7. A circle made of several arcs counts as well. Polygon faces never get as far as the fit. On a round end that used Continuous dome before (such as the bike frame's seat stay) the dome is the same cap: Continuous dome sphered the face from its centroid through its rim, which is the round path's cap.
Status: Default
Reason: Whether a face is round is a question about where its edge lies; the kernel's curve kind only says how the edge is stored.
D2617: FDCAD's own clipboard data goes through one helper that clears an in process clipboard before Python shuts down (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, test infrastructure; IDEAS 71). A long UI test passed and then the process ended with an access violation (exit code 139), so CI would see a passing run fail. Bisecting the app sweep of the attractor plate found one command: Copy (Ctrl+C) of a tree row. A five line script shows it: on the offscreen platform, a QMimeData made in Python and put on the clipboard crashes the process at exit, and plain text does not. The offscreen and minimal platforms keep the clipboard's data in a store of their own that Qt frees after Python has shut down, and data made in Python carries a Python wrapper. On the Windows platform the same script exits cleanly, because the system clipboard takes the data while the app closes. `fdcad/ui/clipboard.py` `put` now sets the data and registers an exit hook once, which clears the clipboard on the offscreen and minimal platforms only. The feature copy, the node editor copy, the sketch entity copy and two tests use it, and a test checks that no other module calls `setMimeData`. The real platforms keep the copied data after FDCAD closes, as before.
Status: Default
Reason: The fault is in where the test platform keeps clipboard data, not in FDCAD's teardown order; clearing it on the real platforms would lose what the user copied.
D2618: The Silhouette sketch tool finds the outline of a part with free form faces from its mesh (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; idea 74). The outline came from the kernel's exact hidden line removal, which took 37 s on the nut and bolt seen from the side and more than eight minutes looking down the bolt's axis, most of it in the thread's spline faces, and the kernel holds Python's lock (idea 68), so the window waited. The kernel's mesh based removal took 0.03 s but gives every visible mesh edge, and many of them lie on one outline (the nut's thread seen along its axis gave over 600 pieces of one circle), so it was not used. On a part the kernel is slow on (the test of D2612: more than 600 faces or any free form surface) the part's triangles are now taken in one array (as D2615 does) and laid flat on the sketch plane; their union is the part's shadow, and its edge, holes included, is the outline the exact removal keeps. In numpy: the shadow is filled into a grid of cells about a thousandth of the part's size (each triangle marks the span between its sides on each row it crosses), the grid's edge is traced into closed loops by marching squares and joined in order by binary lifting, and each loop point is moved from its cell along the grid step to the shadow's true edge, as far as the nearby triangles cover the step without a gap. Each loop is then split at the point farthest from its chord until every piece lies within twice the mesh's deviation of a line or an arc; a whole loop that fits a circle is a circle, lines that meet at a corner meet where their lines cross, and lines that meet at a turn under 20 degrees become one spline. On the nut and bolt both views take about 0.6 s together, meshing included: down the axis two hexagons of 6 lines and the nut's hole as a circle, from the side 94 lines and an arc, within 0.044 mm of the exact outline. The swept spring, lofted handle, twisted bar, twisted sweep and flowed strap take 0.04 to 0.4 s a view once meshed. Details narrower than one cell are left out. Parts of planes, cylinders and the like keep the exact removal, which is quick there.
Status: Default
Reason: The outline is reference geometry for sketching; on spline parts the exact removal cost minutes for curves that the mesh gives within the shaded view's own accuracy, and the grid makes the result clean where many mesh edges meet one outline.

D2627: A hinge whose edge no longer lies where its two bodies meet offers to move to the nearest edge where they do (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, fix button; IDEAS 72, found by the edit storm on the gearbox). The gearbox's Leaf Hinge sits on the top edge of the wall where Hinge Leaf One and Hinge Leaf Two meet. Made 4.04 mm thick instead of 4, Leaf One's top edge rises 0.04 mm above Leaf Two, and the hinge fails with "no second body touches the edge", which is right. The error now looks for a straight edge parallel to the picked one, overlapping it along its length, on one of the flat faces of the picked edge's body next to that edge (the same wall), where one body lies and another touches, as the hinge itself needs. The nearest such edge is offered as "Move the hinge to <edge>", a fix of the new kind `set_ref`, which puts the one reference in place of the pick and keeps a listed pick a list. The message says how far apart the two bodies' edges now are and names the edge, which is highlighted. On the gearbox that is the top of the thinner leaf, 0.04 mm away; applied, the hinge builds. Nothing changes until the user clicks the fix (CLAUDE.md section 5 item 12). When no edge qualifies, the message is the plain one, with no button. The main window applies `set_ref` like the other data fixes, and a test checks that it applies every action the core offers.
Status: Default
Reason: The user's pick stays the truth until they choose; the edge offered is the one a person would pick on the same wall, and the distance says why the hinge stopped working.
D2628: A picked face that split because two features no longer line up is named in the message, with fixes that tie the two depths to one variable (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, usability; idea 70). Two features that end at the same number make one face, which carries the names of both (the bike frame's hanger and dropout, both 6 mm). A pick on it stores its first name and its snapshot only. When one number changes, the face splits; the stored name gives its own piece, so what was picked lies over the wrong piece, and the feature fails with a message that is right but does not say why (D2602: "point is not over the picked face"). After each rebuild, as the cause search of D773 does, every flat face reference of a feature with an error or a warning is checked against the body the feature was built on. The face is taken as split when the face its name gives is smaller than the snapshot, and it and other faces parallel to it, within the picked face's size of its plane, made by two or more features, add up to the snapshot's area (to 0.1 percent) and centre. Faces inside the named piece's outer edge (the floor of a later hole in it) are never pieces. The first error then gets: "The picked face f6/cap/end was one face of Dropout and Hanger, which no longer line up: their faces are now 0.06 mm apart. Change the values so the faces meet again, or pick the face again.", with the pieces highlighted; a feature with only warnings gets this as a warning. When the two pieces are the end faces of two blind extrudes, two fixes are offered, "Use Dropout's Depth for Both" and the same for the other. Each adds a length variable that holds that depth as typed and sets both depths to it, the other with the offset that lines its face up again (a boss end moves with its depth, a cut's floor against it): "=Dropout_depth", or "=Dropout_depth - 6mm" for a pocket floor level with a plate's top. The fix is applied only on a click, as one undoable step, and only then do the two depths move together. Other features (a revolve, a mid plane extrude) get the message without a fix. A known limit: a blind cut inserted upstream after the pick, whose floor is beside the picked face, looks the same as a split, since the stored reference does not keep the face's other names; the message then names the cut, and one of the fixes would set the plate's depth to the cut's floor (the user sees the label first). The check runs only on features with issues, so a part with none pays nothing.
Status: Default
Reason: The user changed one number and something else broke; naming both features and the gap says why, and a shared variable is the usual way to keep two values equal on purpose.

D2632: The check that a cut removed material skips points of a cut face that were already the part's surface (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found while writing the tests of D2628). A 4 mm pocket over the whole top of a 14 mm block, beside a 10 mm plate, warned "removes no material" though it removed 400 mm3. Its floor is level with the plate's top, so the two merge into one face that carries the plate's name too, and the quick test of D2614 (a cut face with only the cut's names) does not apply. The point test of D1086 then took the first sample point of the face that lies on it, the middle of its parameter range, which is over the plate; just outside the face there had never been material, and the test stopped after that one point. A sample point that lies on the surface of the part before the cut is now skipped and the next one tried, so the test looks only where the cut made the face. A cut that only touches the part (drawn on a face and pointing away) has every point on the old surface and still warns. Each skip costs one point classification and happens only on this fallback path: on generated_200 and the nut and bolt it never runs.
Status: Default
Reason: The test asks whether material was just outside a face the cut made; a point of a face that was already there cannot answer that.
D2622: Edge Profile, Ring Groove, O Ring Groove, Shaft Shape, Mark, Lattice Fill and Wrap work on the body they were put on (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; idea 62). Each handed the whole part to the kernel for its cut or join, the pattern behind D1055, D1056 and D1078. Each was put on a body with a second body touching it or near it, and all seven changed the second body with no message, or failed: Edge Profile cut a sliver from a block standing against the plate's side (its section reaches 0.05 mm past the faces); Ring Groove and O Ring Groove cut into a hub on the shaft (the ring tool reaches 1 mm past the round); Shaft Shape on a shaft cut the hub away (its sleeve reaches 2 D plus 10 mm out), and in a bore its fill joined a pin standing in the bore; Mark cut into whichever side removed more, which on a thin plate with a block lying on it was the block; Wrap's emboss joined a block it touched, since a boss that reaches every body is fused with the whole part; Lattice Fill with no bodies picked filled all bodies as one, and on two touching blocks failed ("the skin could not be made"). All now run on one body with `bodies.in_body_of`: the body of the picked face (Edge Profile, Ring Groove, Shaft Shape, Wrap, O Ring Groove on a round), or the body of the face the sketch was drawn on (Mark, O Ring Groove face seal; a sketch on a plane still works on every body it meets, as Living Hinge does in D1077). Lattice Fill fills each body on its own, inside one lattice made over all of them so the cells still line up. Lattice Fill with one body picked already left the others alone and is not changed there. On a part of one body every feature runs as before, so face names are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature put on a body changes that body. The test part of D1077 showed no fault in these; a hub on a shaft, a pin in a bore and a block against a side do.

D2623: A boolean tool made of crossing pieces is taken apart before the kernel sees it (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; idea 64). The kernel never intersects the solids of one compound with each other, so a tool that is a compound of solids sharing material is taken badly, with no error: a cross of two bars cut from a plate as one tool left the plate whole, the join counted the middle twice and the intersection was empty; the rooms and pin hole of a pin hinge cut as one tool left the rooms uncut (D1085, 6303.5 cubic mm left where 6869.0 is right). Idea 52 lists six features that pass such tools. The cut, join and intersection of `fdcad.core.occ` now look at each tool before they build: a compound of two or more solids whose boxes overlap by more than 0.0001 mm on every axis has those pairs tested with an intersection, and when one pair shares material the tool is replaced by its pieces as separate tools. The kernel intersects separate tools with each other, which is the same as fusing them first, and the history still covers every face of the tool, so face names carry as before. An intersection takes separate tools as several, so for it the pieces are fused first. Pieces that only touch or stand apart, and tools that are one solid, are passed as they were. The check found no crossing tool in the gearbox or the sample parts, and it took 0.08 s of the gearbox's 116 s rebuild (4588 booleans).
Status: Default
Reason: One check where every boolean passes, instead of each feature having to know the kernel's rule, so no feature can bring the fault back.

D2629: Flip puts a tangent reference plane on the other side of the cylinder (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, reference geometry; IDEAS 51). A tangent plane picked with a cylinder face and a plane touched the side the plane's normal points to (D903), and the other side could only be had by picking a point there. The `tangent` method now reads `flip`, as `offset`, `angle` and `mid_plane` do, and the property panel shows Flip for it. Flip turns the side for a picked point too, so the plane touches the side away from the point. `flip` is written only when true, so a file without it keeps the side it had; the panel never offered Flip for this method before, so no saved part has it set.
Status: Default
Reason: Flip already means "the other side" for the other plane methods; reusing it needs no new parameter and leaves every saved part as it was.

D2630: Labels of parallel planes step down their corner, one row per plane (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, 3D view; the rest of IDEAS 65 after D1092). Every plane in the plane picker, and every plane on show, is drawn as a square of the same size round its own origin, with its name just inside one corner. Planes with the same axes, such as a row of offset planes, put their names at the same corner, apart only along the normal, so on the bike frame with 17 construction planes the names sat on top of each other. `plane_look.label_rows` now groups the planes by their axes and gives each plane in a group a row in the order they lie along the normal; row k sits `LABEL_STEP` (0.035 of the plane's size) further down the corner than row k minus 1, and after `LABEL_ROWS` (20) rows the labels start again at the corner. A plane with axes of its own keeps row 0, where its label was before. The labels were already drawn at a fixed height in pixels (12 px, `LABEL_HEIGHT`): the 3D view's text labels do not grow or shrink with zoom unless asked to. The label now sets that on purpose (`SetZoomable(False)`), and a test checks it. The "More planes" choice of the idea is not added: since D1092 the status bar says a plane not drawn is picked in the tree, and the picker takes a plane picked there.
Status: Default
Reason: Rows follow the planes' order in space, so the stack of names reads like the stack of planes; the offset is worked out once when the planes are drawn and needs no screen work on every frame.

D2631: FDEF_SPEC.md names every choice value and every reference of every feature type (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, docs; IDEAS 59). Idea 59 asked for a section for each of the 54 types of the gearbox sample (D1069) that had none, and for the 112 keys it writes. D1079 did that for all 137 types and emptied the list of samples waiting for the spec, and the gearbox has passed both sample tests since then. This pass checked the sections against each type's parameter table and module, not only the parameter names. 36 types had choice values their sections did not name, such as the later hole types, the loft's Tangent and Curvature ends, the sweep's orientations, and the preview, region and check options of five patterns. 10 types had references their code reads but their sections did not name, such as `refs.hole_axis`, `refs.guides` on a loft and `refs.pull` on a wrap. Section 5.3.37 now lists them per type, with what each value does, taken from the module's own description and code, and section 6 items 11 and 12 add the sketch's `refs.derived_from` and `refs.pierce`. `test_every_choice_and_reference_of_every_feature_type_is_in_its_section` fails when a choice value of a parameter table, or a reference its module reads, is not named in the type's section. The references are found in the module's source (`refs.get`, `refs[...]` and the resolve helpers), so one read another way is not caught. Nothing about the format changed.
Status: Default
Reason: A file should be readable from the spec alone. A parameter name without its choices, or a reference the code needs but the spec does not name, leaves a reader guessing.

D2633: The exponent of a number is not read as a variable name when global variables are put in order or the graph cycle rule looks for driven values (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by the review of D2620). D2620 made the tokenizer read 2e3 as one number, but two other places still found names with a pattern of their own that took every word of a formula: the order of global variables (`units/variables.py`) and the cycle rule of graphs (`graph/drive.py`). So a variable e3 typed as =2e3 was its own circular reference, e2 = a with a = 3e2 was a loop, and a feature above a graph that typed =1e1 was refused for using a variable e1 the graph sets. Both now take the names from `references`, which reads the formula's own tokens, as the equation engine already did.
Status: Default
Reason: A formula's names must be read the way the formula is evaluated; a second pattern drifts from the tokenizer.

D2625: A part file stores the path of an inserted part in its own folder tree relative to itself (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; idea 61). Insert Part kept the path as picked, so a folder of parts moved to another folder or computer failed with "the source part was not found". In memory the path stays absolute; only the file text changes, in `core.io.part_links`. Writing a part to a file (Save, Save As, Bodies to Files linked parts) stores the path relative to that file, with / between folders, when the inserted part is in the same folder or a folder below it, and the full path otherwise. Reading a file turns a relative path into an absolute one from the file's folder. A full path, as every older file has, is used when its file is there, and when it is not, a part of the same name beside the file is used, as for a linked equations file (D749); so older files open as before and also work once copied with their parts. Save As to another folder writes the path again for the new place from the absolute path in memory, so it stays right, relative or full. Paths that climb out of the part's folder (..) are stored in full: moving the part alone then still finds the other file on the same computer. Because the path in memory is absolute both in the session that saved and after opening, the document key, and so the saved solid of D1102, still match on open in the same place. FDEF_SPEC 5.3.34.24 describes the form.
Status: Default
Reason: A path relative to the part is the only one that survives moving the folder; keeping memory absolute means undo, the rebuild cache and the rebuild helper never see a path that depends on where the file is.

D2626: Every feature is built from the numbers the part file keeps (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; idea 49). A part file keeps numbers to twelve significant digits, and a session built from the full numbers in memory, so where a kernel result hangs on the last digits the same part could come out differently when opened again (D1049, D1052 and D1053 each fixed one such place). The rebuild already wrote each feature as the file does for its cache key. `rebuild.engine.SavedNumbers` now keeps that data for the rebuild, uses it for the key (one write per feature instead of two), and builds each feature from it read back. `BuildContext.document` is a shallow copy of the part made of such copies, so a feature that reads another (the seeds of a pattern, a derived sketch) gets saved numbers too; the copy shares everything else (variables, measured values, embedded data) with the part. A typed value that the equations solve works out from its text keeps its full value: the file keeps the text and opening it works the value out again the same way, so rounding would only lose digits (a first try rounded them too, and 90 degrees typed into a coordinate system then left 5e-12 in its X direction; 360 degrees would come out just over a turn). Sketch point positions and other plain numbers are what the file rounds, and they are rounded. The document itself keeps its numbers, so typing, undo and saving are unchanged. The copy is made only when a feature has to build, and made again after a graph or a measured value changes values further down. Measured: on generated_200 the copy costs 2.4 ms per rebuild that builds anything, and a rebuild from the cache is quicker, as each feature is written once; on the gearbox, which solves its values again 12 times for measured values, the copies cost 0.48 s of a cold rebuild of about 150 s. A sketch corner at 10.0000000000003 now builds at 10 in the session as in the file, to the last digit.
Status: Default
Reason: A session and its file can only build the same if they start from the same numbers, and the saved ones are the only numbers both have.
D2634: The mesh outline of D2618 keeps a sharp corner as a corner, and each triangle of its lookup grid holds only the cells it overlaps (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by the review of D2618). A cylinder of free form faces 400 mm long, lying at 45 degrees and seen from above, gave one flat end as an arc of 19.5 mm radius, and a 1000 by 3 mm one gave both ends as arcs. A run of the loop made of the flat end and a little of the side lay within the tolerance (twice the mesh deviation, 0.4 mm there) of one circle, and the arc fit was tried before the split at the farthest point. Inside the tolerance or not, a flat end shown round is wrong geometry to a user. A run that misses its chord is now first tested for a corner at its farthest point: both halves straight, each less than a tenth as far from its chord as the whole run is (an arc's halves are about a quarter as far), and a turn of at least 20 degrees there (one mesh step of a curved face turns less, MESH_ANGLE). A corner is split; only a run without one may become an arc. Lines in a row that lie within the tolerance of one line, which such a split can leave, now become that line instead of a spline of two points (a 120 by 4 mm cylinder gave one side as a spline). Rounds, a shallow 60 mm arc and full circles come out as before. The lookup grid that finds the triangles under a point entered each triangle in every cell of its box, so a long thin triangle across the part at an angle took most of the 256 by 256 cells (65,536 entries for one triangle), so a mesh of many such triangles could need arrays of hundreds of millions of entries. Each row of cells now takes only the span the triangle has in that row (its corners in the row and where its sides cross the row's edges), so such a triangle holds a few cells a row. A test checks the lookup against every triangle for random points.
Status: Default
Reason: The outline is reference geometry that users snap to and build on; a corner must stay a corner. The lookup's memory should follow the triangles' area, not their boxes.

D2635: Layer Preview and the Silhouette sketch tool say so when the part cannot be meshed (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by the review of D2615 and D2618). On parts drawn from their mesh, a failed or incomplete mesh gave no lines and no outline, with no word, so the tool looked broken or the part looked empty. The mesh's own message (for example "The part's mesh is incomplete. Rebuild it and try again.") is now carried in a new `problem` field of the result (`LayerLines`, `ProjectedCurve`) as "Layer Preview failed: ..." or "Silhouette failed: ...". Layer Preview shows it in the status bar in place of the layer count, and the Silhouette tool shows it as its prompt and as the message when Add Curves is pressed. A part that meshes has an empty `problem`, and the messages for a plane that misses the part are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: A tool that cannot work must say what failed and what to do next (CLAUDE.md section 8 item 4); an empty result reads as "nothing there".
D2624: Lattice Fill fits its lattice to curved bodies at the panel's cell (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; IDEAS 73). D2605 refused the panel's 10 mm gyroid with a 1.2 mm skin on the swept spring and the twisted sweep, because each lattice face whose box meets the box of a curved face of the body costs a surface intersection, and one curved face has a box round the whole lattice. Measured first: a lattice triangle against the spring's spline face cost 10 to 60 ms whether it lay on the surface or 7 mm from it, so the cost is in the pairs the boxes let through; and every boolean of the feature was built twice, because the fuzzy value was set after the two shape form had already built it. Bodies with plane faces only are made as before. For a body with any other face: (1) Behind a skin the region (the body less its skin) is made of the kernel's triangles of its faces, a twentieth of the skin from them, when their volume is within 2 percent of the region's. The lattice then meets flat faces only, which cost little. The parts of the region outside the lattice lie inside the skin, so their closed shells are added to the body turned inside out, as cavities: no boolean touches the body's faces, which keep their names, and the skin stays as thick to within that twentieth. A void that is not one plain shell, or that no solid of the body holds, falls back to a cut. (2) Without a skin, or where the triangles miss the region (on the swept spring's 0.3 mm core they hold a quarter less), the region keeps its faces, cut into patches by planes across its box a quarter of a cell apart (at most 16 along an axis) and meshed, so each patch has a box close round it and a lattice face is only tested against the patches near it. After the boolean the patches are merged back across the edges the cut made, and only those: every other edge is kept, so two faces of the body, or two lattice faces that lie in one plane, are never merged. The names follow the cut, the boolean and the merge as one history; a filled cylinder has the faces, volume and names the plain boolean gives. (3) The sheet is closed off three grid steps outside the region's triangles and nothing farther out is made: grid points reached from the edge of the grid without coming that near are left out, found with a difference array and a growing mask in numpy. Inside the region the triangles are the same as before. (4) Booleans are built once, on all cores, with oriented boxes (about half the face pairs of the twisted sweep). (5) The cut that makes the cavities takes the lattice as its object, so the check of D2623 does not run on it: the lattice's solids are the shells of one closed mesh and cannot cross, and the check made a boolean of each two pieces whose boxes meet, 6 s for the 25 pieces of the twisted sweep. The crossings of D2605 are now counted against the patches, so only lattice faces near the surface count, and the limit is 20,000 where it was 10,000: the fill is one boolean built once where it was three built twice. Timings with the test PC fully loaded by other work (about five times slower than idle): the twisted sweep at 10 mm with the skin builds in about 9.5 s (the cut is about 4.5 s of one core), where it took 165 to 190 s; the spring at 20 mm builds (4,085 crossings, 51,984 before) and at 15 mm in about 28 s, of which 10 s is preparing the region, and its 10 mm gyroid (63,000 crossings) is refused before the boolean with 15 mm named, where 44 mm was. Honeycomb had the same cost on a curved body: on the spring with the panel's values the old fuse took 144 s, now about 21 s loaded; on the twisted sweep 4.3 s, now 2.6 s. It is still not counted (at most 4000 hexagons).
Status: Default
Reason: A lattice face far from the body's surface should cost nothing, and behind a skin nothing needs the exact surface: it is inside the part. Where the exact surface is needed, patches keep it and keep the names.
D2656: The tie of D2628 takes a cut's depth from a fixed sum when its face moves the other way (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by review of D2628). A boss end rises along the picked face's normal as its depth grows and a cut floor sinks, as `_blind_end` says, but the tie gave the follower the leader's variable plus an offset whatever the two directions were. For a pocket floor level with a plate top that was "=Plate_depth - 6mm": right at today's value, but a plate made 12 mm thick then asked for a 6 mm pocket in the 14 mm block, whose floor lies at 8 mm, 4 mm below the plate's top, so the face split again and the hole on it failed, though the fix had said the two would now move together. When the two faces move the same way the tie is as before; when they move opposite ways the follower gets the sum less the variable, "=14mm - Plate_depth", which keeps them level at every value. `tied_values` takes a `head` before the variable for this. The test of D2628 that asked for the offset form now asks for the sum.
Status: Default
Reason: The fix promises that the two values move together; only the sum keeps a rising face and a sinking face level.

D2657: The hinge's search for the edge where its bodies meet looks only near the picked edge's walls (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; found by review of D2627). `meeting_edge` read every edge of every body and measured each straight edge parallel to the picked one against the walls, and every body against the picked edge to find its own. On the gearbox with Hinge Leaf One at 4.04 mm (60 bodies, 3025 faces) the search took 8.2 s with the PC busy, while the window waited for the error; a test part with thirty blocks before the leaves made 397 distance calls. Bodies and edges whose boxes are clear of the walls (by 0.002 mm) are now passed over, the body of the picked edge is found among the bodies whose box holds it, and the candidates are tried nearest first, so the first on the wall where two bodies meet is the answer. The edge offered is the same: on the gearbox the top of the thinner leaf, 0.04 mm away, found in 0.05 s.
Status: Default
Reason: The search runs on the error path of a part being edited; a body that cannot reach the wall cannot give the edge.

D2641: Rib, Roof, Vent and the Split for Printing connectors work on the body they were put on (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; IDEAS 52). Each still combined its new material with the whole part in one kernel call (D1055). Test parts of separate bodies, one of them touching the body the feature is on, show the fault in four of the seven features named in idea 52 for this pass. A gusset Rib in the corner of an angle, with a block on the angle's floor against the rib's side, joined the block to the angle. A Roof cut flat on a plate joined to the plate a block of its own resting on the roof's top. A Vent through a plate lying on a block cut 0.01 mm into the block, since the wall was measured through both bodies, and its ribs were fused with the whole part. Split for Printing with screws, on a bar with a block against its end, ran the screw hole on through the block and put the nut trap where the line left the block. Now Rib fuses its rib with the body it was built against (the picked body, or the one body round its sketch, D1098) through the new `bodies.in_body_at`, which `in_body_of` now uses; a rib network whose walls are on different bodies still meets the whole part. Roof runs on the body of the face its sketch was drawn on, and on the whole part when the sketch is on a plane, as Living Hinge does (D1077). Vent measures its wall in the body of the vent face and runs on that body only. Split for Printing keeps for every piece the body it was cut from: a glue gap and connectors go only on the pieces of a body the cuts went through, connectors are measured in that body (the inside test, the nut trap, the key taper) and are cut from its pieces alone. A part of one body is one group, so its kernel calls and face names are as before; the sample golden tests and every test of the seven features pass unchanged. Interlock, Joint Helper and Twist Lock already worked on their bodies one at a time (each fuse or cut is given one solid, and the other bodies are put back as they were), so they are not changed; a test for each, with a third body touching, keeps it so. Hinge and Lattice Fill are left to other work, and so are the features of idea 62.
Status: Default
Reason: A feature changes the body it was put on; a body that only touches it is another part of the print and must stay as it was.
D2619: A boss or cut is checked at a point of its tool, not only by the volume of the part (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, reliability; idea 50). The volume check of D705 is off on bodies of more than 100 faces and its slack is 1 percent of the whole part, so a small boss or cut that the kernel loses on a large part built with no error (the head badge of D1049 was 0.05 percent of the bike frame). After every boss and cut in `solids.combine`, `tool_check.tools_kept` now picks a point inside each tool solid where the part must change: outside the body for a boss, inside it for a cut. After a boss the point must be inside the result, after a cut outside it. The point comes from the tool alone: a point on one of its three largest faces is moved in along the face's normal to the middle, then a quarter or three quarters, of the chord to the tool's far side. It is placed against the body and the result by counting the faces one ray from it crosses, as the local booleans of D2601 do: the faces a ray can reach are found from their boxes in numpy, and the boxes are kept from one boolean to the next, since a body shares nearly all of its faces with the result before it; only new faces are measured. The rays are tried in the order of what their faces cost to ask: a new flat face with many holes costs about 27 us an edge to prepare (2.7 ms for the plate of generated_200), a spline face about a hundred times a plane. A ray that grazes an edge or a face is not used; with no clean ray there is no verdict. A result that looks wrong is confirmed by the kernel's own point classifier on the tool, the body and the result, with a tolerance of 1e-3 mm or 1e-4 of the tool's size, a hundred times the boolean's fuzzy value; a point that lies on a surface within it gives no verdict. When the check fires the feature fails, as it does when the volume check fires: "<name> failed: the kernel left out the material it adds. Change its values slightly so faces do not almost touch." (for a cut: "left material where it cuts"). A tool of many solids (a pattern) is sampled at 12 of them. The volume check stays as it was. Modeled Thread cuts leave the point check out (`combine(..., check_tools=False)`): their own check of D607 compares the removed volume with what the thread overlaps and gives a message that says what to change, and the point check, which fires first, took that message away. Cost on generated_200 (98 cuts on bodies of about 200 faces): about 1 ms a boolean, 0.09 to 0.12 s over the rebuild (about 4 percent); the kernel's classifier takes about 2.7 ms just to load on such a body, and the check would need it on both the body and the result. The happy path never builds one. False alarms: over tests/core/features, tests/core/rebuild and the sample golden tests (1943 checks, among them the bike frame, the gearbox parts, the machine bed station and the sheet metal part) the check fired only in its own tests and on two Modeled Thread cuts the kernel gets wrong (one expected to fail with the thread's own message, one marked as a known Windows kernel fault), each confirmed by the kernel's classifier. Test: `tests/core/features/test_tool_check.py`, with a boss and a cut that the kernel gives back unchanged (simulated) where the volume check cannot see it, and the fault of D1049 itself with the repair of the inside out solid taken away; `tests/perf/test_tool_check_budget.py` keeps the checks of generated_200 under 0.3 s with no kernel classifier built.
Status: Default
Reason: A check sized to the tool sees a small loss on any part, and its cost does not grow with the part.
D2658: The crossing pieces check of D2623 is skipped where the pieces cannot cross, and many pairs are tested with one fuse (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; follow up to D2624). The check made a boolean of each two pieces of a tool whose boxes meet. A lattice's pieces interleave, so almost every pair meets: 6.4 s for the 25 pieces of the twisted sweep's 10 mm gyroid, and 255 s for the 102 pairs of the 71 pieces of a gyroid over 30 by 20 by 20 mm, though none of them share material. Lattice Fill on a body of planes with a skin still joined the skin and the lattice with the lattice's pieces as the tool, so it paid this. Two changes. (1) The cut, join and intersection of `fdcad.core.occ` take `pieces_apart=True` from a caller that knows the tool's solids cannot share material; then the check does not run. Lattice Fill passes it for the join of skin and lattice and for the cut of cavities that D2624 falls back to, as the pieces are the closed shells of one mesh. The tool is passed as before, so the faces and their names (`lattice#k`) are the same. A 12 mm cube with a 1 mm skin and a 10 mm gyroid now makes no check at all (it made one, and took 5.8 s where it now takes 2.9 s with the PC loaded). (2) For every caller, more than four pairs of pieces whose boxes meet are tested with one fuse of those pieces, whose volume is set against the sum of theirs (shared material is more than 0.000001 of the sum, or 1e-12 cubic mm): the 71 pieces take 18 s instead of 255 s, the 25 pieces 5.8 s instead of 6.4 s. A fuse that fails counts as crossing, so the pieces are passed apart, which is always right. Four pairs or fewer are tested pair by pair as before.
Status: Default
Reason: The caller that made the pieces knows they stand apart; the check is for tools whose pieces nobody has looked at, and for those one fuse costs far less than a boolean per pair once there are many.

D2642: Delete and Patch hands the kernel a copy of the body (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; IDEAS 56). The kernel's defeaturing tool has no safe mode in this kernel build (D1067), so it could write into the faces, edges and corners it is given, and a body shares almost all of them with the results the rebuild keeps for earlier features. `direct._patch_part` now copies the body with its geometry first (`BRepBuilderAPI_Copy`, as Heal Edges does since D1066), gives the tool the copy and the copies of the picked faces, and carries each face name over to its copy. The copier hands each face back turned forward, so a copied face is turned the way the original was; without that, the check of D1090 that a removed face did not come back measured a reversed face's normal the wrong way, and a Delete Face of a hole and a plain block end reported success though the end stayed. In the new test (a boss removed from a block with a hole) the kernel did not write into the body even without the copy, and the gearbox check of D1067 found nothing spoiled before either: the guard is kept anyway, since nothing in this kernel build promises it. The test checks that the body handed in is unchanged and that the result holds none of its faces, edges or corners (before, it held 11).
Status: Default
Reason: The kept results of earlier features must never change under a later feature; a copy costs a little time on each Delete Face and removes the risk for good.

D2643: A table value filled into an inch part keeps its length (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; bug hunt round 10b O10). The fastening and shape panels write a table value (a tap drill, a fit gap, a thickness) into a length field as text in the part's units, and `spec_form.number_text` gave inches four digits: the M5 tap drill of 4.2 mm became 0.1654 in, which reads back as 4.2012 mm, and 2.5 mm became 0.09843 in, read back as 2.5001 mm. The text is now the shortest inch number of 4 to 6 digits that reads back as the same length to a part in a billion (an inch table value such as 0.201 or 0.25 stays as short as before). A metric value that has no such inch number keeps its millimetres with the unit, "4.2 mm", which the field reads as 4.2 mm in any part. Millimetre parts and angles are as before.
Status: Default
Reason: A filled value must be the table's value; the unit says where a metric size came from, where a long inch number would only hide it.

D2644: Three messages that named the wrong cause (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; bug hunt round 10b O12). (1) A fillet with Multiple radius and an edge's own radius of 0 failed with "the radius is larger than the faces next to these edges allow": `round_edges` refuses a radius of 0 or less without asking the kernel, and the search that followed blamed the size. Before any rounding, `fillet.no_radius` now names the edges whose radius is 0 or less, by their place in the list as the other fillet messages do, highlights them and says to enter a radius greater than 0 or leave them out. Variable fillets go through the same check; the Chord width method, whose radius comes from the width, does not. (2) An asymmetric chamfer that is too large gave "largest distance 0.199 mm" for a 1 by 50 mm chamfer: the search scales both distances together, so the number was the first distance at the scale that fits, and changing only that one did not help. The message now gives both, "largest distances 0.199 and 9.96 mm". Symmetric chamfers, widths and angle chamfers keep the one value and the Reduce fix. (3) A reference point along an edge at a negative distance or percentage said "the distance is longer than the edge". It now says the distance (or percentage) is less than 0, and to enter 0 or more or turn on Reverse direction to measure from the other end.
Status: Default
Reason: CLAUDE.md section 8 item 4: a message must say what failed; these sent the user to change the wrong value.

D2645: Body tool length defaults are round inch values in an inch part (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; bug hunt round 10c R10c.O2). The body tool forms (Move Face, Offset Face, the patterns, Move and Copy Body and the rest) keep their defaults as millimetre texts, such as "1" for a Move Face distance and "10" for a pattern spacing. A length field reads a bare number in the part's unit, so in an inch part a new Move Face was 1 in (25.4 mm) and a new pattern spaced its copies 10 in apart. `body_tools.flow.inch_defaults` now runs when a body tool starts in an inch part: each length default other than 0 becomes its millimetres in inches rounded to one significant digit, so 1 mm gives 0.04 in and 10 mm gives 0.4 in, the same sizes the deform tools (`INCH_DEFAULTS`) and Extrude (bug hunt E5) already use there. Values the command itself presets, the fit tolerance of D413 and the deform tools' own values are kept. Millimetre parts are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: A default must be the same small size in either unit; a 25 times larger first value surprised the user and could make a pattern leave the part.

D2646: A deleted feature leaves its tree folder and its comment (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; audit 2026-11-02 D3 item 20, deferred by D744). Delete removed the feature but left its id in its tree folder and its comment in the part file. A folder whose features were all deleted stayed in the file with nothing to show, and its name stayed taken: making a new folder of that name said "A folder is already called Holes". `DeleteFeature` now also stores the tree data before and after `tree_info.forget` (which existed but was never called), so the feature leaves its folder, an empty folder goes, and its comment goes; Undo puts all three back. Configuration overrides of a deleted feature were already dropped on save (`configurations.to_file` keeps overrides of features that exist). Folder members split by a drag still show only the first run of neighbours, as `tree_info.runs` documents (D692): that is a rule of folders, not this bug.
Status: Default
Reason: Data the user cannot see must not block what they can do; Delete and its Undo keep the tree data and the features in step.

D2647: A cosmetic thread longer than its face is shown as long as the face, with a warning (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; bug hunt round 10b O9). A Cosmetic Thread with Blind and a length past the end of its shaft or hole (50 mm on a 30 mm shaft) was stored, drawn and written to the STEP description 50 mm long, with no message. The thread mark is now cut to the length of the round face (the farther end from the picked edge, as Full Length uses), and the feature warns: "the thread is 50 mm long but its face is only 30 mm long, so it is shown 30 mm long. Enter a shorter length, or choose Full Length." The typed length is kept, so a longer shaft later shows the whole thread again. Tapped hole marks were already cut to the material depth (`material_depth` in the Hole Tool). The part's geometry is not changed: a cosmetic thread is a mark only.
Status: Default
Reason: The suggested fix of the bug hunt (clamp with a warning); the mark must not claim thread where there is no material, and the user's value stays theirs to change.

D2648: Escape after Smart Dimension picks a part edge takes its copy away (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; bug hunt round 10a O10a-6). A click on a straight part edge with Smart Dimension adds a fixed construction copy of the edge to measure to (D113). Escape dropped the pick but left the copy in the sketch, and so did leaving the tool or a pick that gave no dimension; only Undo removed it. The canvas now remembers, for each copy a pick made (not a copy already in the sketch, which `reference_line` reuses), the sketch undo depth before it. Escape on that pick, another tool, or "this dimension is not possible" takes the copy away again: by rolling the sketch back when nothing else changed since, else by deleting the line in an undo step of its own. A copy that a placed dimension uses stays, as before.
Status: Default
Reason: Escape cancels the pick, so it cancels what the pick added; leftover fixed lines also clutter the sketch and its relations.

D2649: A sweep along a helix refuses a round profile wider than the pitch (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; bug hunt round 10b O6). A 6 mm round profile swept along a helix of pitch 4 mm runs each turn into the next, and the sweep reported OK with a body that overlaps itself. A full self intersection check took over two minutes, so `sweep_pitch.check_turns` makes the cheap pitch check the hunt suggested, before the kernel sweeps. It applies to a path that is a Helix feature of constant pitch, with no taper, no closed end coils, more than one turn, and a sweep without start or end scale; the profile must be round: the Circular profile, or a sketch or face profile that is one whole circle. The section of a round tube through the helix axis is an ellipse, 1/cos(lead angle) times the tube's diameter along the axis (exactly the diameter for a sketch circle whose plane holds the axis, so the diameter is used there as the smaller value). When that is more than the pitch, the sweep fails with "the profile is 6.01 mm across along the helix, more than its pitch of 4 mm, so each turn runs into the next. Use a smaller profile or a larger pitch." A profile exactly as wide as the pitch only touches and still builds. Other profiles are not checked: a thin profile set at a slant reaches far along the axis yet can pass the next turn, so its reach proves nothing. The swept spring sample builds as before; the gearbox and machine bed springs (3 mm on a 7 mm pitch) are well inside the check. Nothing in the part is changed; the sweep only stops reporting OK.
Status: Default
Reason: A body that overlaps itself is not a valid solid and breaks later features and printing; the check costs nothing and refuses only what surely overlaps.
D2673: A formula solved only after a measure keeps its full value in the rounded build of D2626 (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by review of D2626). D2626 builds each feature from its saved numbers but keeps the full value of a typed value the equations worked out, and it took the list of those from the solve at the start of the rebuild only. A measured value is 0 until its feature has built, so on a part just opened a formula such as "=1000mm / length@Bounding Box 1 / 3" fails with a division by zero at the start and is solved again after the Bounding Box measures it. That value was then rounded to twelve digits (6.66666666667 mm), while a later rebuild in the same session, which starts with the measured value known, built it at 6.666666666666667 mm: the same part built from two numbers, which is what D2626 was made to end. The solve after a measure now adds the cells it worked out to the list (`SavedNumbers.changed(solved)`, `_resolve_after_measure` gives them), so both builds use the full value. Test: `tests/core/rebuild/test_rounded_build.py::test_a_value_solved_only_after_a_measure_keeps_its_digits`.
Status: Default
Reason: Whether a typed value keeps its digits must not hang on whether a measured value was known when the rebuild started.

D2670: A value the file cannot keep, in a feature that does not build, no longer stops every rebuild (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by the check of D2626). D2626 builds from a copy of the part made of each feature's saved data read back, and the copy holds every feature, also those suppressed or below the rollback bar that the rebuild never keys or builds. A value the file cannot write, such as nan, in one of those raised "Cannot save the value nan" from the copy, so the whole part could not rebuild; before D2626 it rebuilt as usual. `SavedNumbers._saved_copy` now gives such a feature to the copy as it is: the file cannot keep it, so there is no saved number to match. A feature that does build still stops at its own cache key, as before D2626, since its key is made from the same saved data.
Status: Default
Reason: The copy of the part must not fail on features the rebuild never builds; the saved numbers only matter for what is built.
D2674: Lattice Fill keeps walls thinner than its grid (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by review of D2624). The sheet of D2004 was the zero of the unsigned distance from the gyroid or diamond surface less half the wall, sampled every eighth of a cell. At the panel's 10 mm cell the grid step is 1.25 mm, wider than the 1 mm wall, and where both ends of a grid edge lay just outside the wall on its two sides the wall between them was lost: a 30 mm box held 3,746 mm3 of the 10 mm gyroid where its walls are about 7,950 mm3, and the region of a 30 mm cylinder at a 15 mm cell held 5.8 mm3 in 207 pieces. A finer grid was measured first and does not do: the walls come within 5 percent only at about a third of the wall (an eighteenth of a cell here), which makes about six times the faces, so the face limit of D1099 would refuse the panel's values on almost any part. Instead the grid samples the signed distance, which has no crease at the surface, and the sheet is the band between its two levels at plus and minus half the wall. In each tetrahedron of the grid the distance and the box are taken as linear, so the band is the tetrahedron cut by two parallel planes and the box's plane: each plane is cut out by marching tetrahedra and clipped by the others, and a point is shared by the grid edge or tetrahedron face it lies on, so the mesh is closed. The points of the two faces are then moved along their grid edges onto the true levels (two steps of false position), which takes the volume from about 0.90 to within 2 percent of the field's (5 percent for a 20 mm diamond cell). Checked against the volume of the band found by sampling the field at 400,000 random points: gyroid and diamond, 0.5 to 4 mm walls, 8 to 20 mm cells, all closed, and one piece where the old mesh had up to 207. The grid still follows the cell only, so the face count goes with the cube of the cell as before, and a thicker wall does not lower it; the refusals of D1099 and D2605 still name a larger cell, not a wall. As the walls are no longer lost a sheet has about 1.5 times the faces, so the cell named now comes from trying the estimate and larger cells (up to six) against both limits: at 24 mm, the estimate for the D1099 box, the sheet still had 62,244 faces. The panel's 10 mm gyroid on the swept spring is now over the face limit before the crossing limit, and the cell named is under both. Tests: `tests/core/features/test_lattice_fill.py::test_the_sheet_keeps_walls_thinner_than_the_grid`; the volume ranges of two tests that were set to the old mesh are now about 0.3 of the box, as the 3.1 per cell of a gyroid's area gives.
Status: Default
Reason: A lattice of 1 mm walls must hold 1 mm walls; the grid's step should set how smooth the walls are, not whether they are there.

D2671: A feature holding a value the part file cannot keep fails with a feature error, and such values are refused where they come in (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by the check of D2626). A nan or an infinite number in a feature that builds made `rebuild()` raise "Cannot save the value nan" from the feature's cache key, so the part showed nothing and no feature was named (CLAUDE.md section 5 item 7). The rebuild now gives that feature an ERROR with code `unsaved_value` and a message naming the value, such as "Extrude 2 failed: its value depth is not a number (nan). Type a new value for it, or undo the change that set it.", and goes on: features below build on the part from before it, as after any failed feature (TR352), and the feature builds again once the value is fixed. The sources were checked one by one. Typed text and formulas already refused an infinite result, but a plain number in a length field takes the part unit after that check (D66), so 1e308 typed in an inch part, or set by a design table, a CSV lookup or an equation, came out as inf millimetres: `units.evaluate` now refuses it. In a graph, Arithmetic gave inf for 1e200 times 1e200 and nan for inf minus inf with no error, and Set Feature Parameter put it into the feature: Arithmetic, Set Variable and Set Feature Parameter now fail as nodes, so the driven value keeps its typed value and the node editor shows where the graph went wrong. A part file or a library feature file with NaN, Infinity or a number too large for a float, such as 1e400, opened with an infinite or nan value: both readers now refuse it as damaged (FDCAD never writes such a value). A measured value that is nan or infinite is not kept, so formulas never read it (min(3, nan) is 3 but min(nan, 3) is nan); the value from the last good measure stays. An equation such as 0/0 already failed as a division by zero. A configuration override is read from the file, so the file check covers it.
Status: Default
Reason: One bad value must cost one feature, never the whole rebuild; blocking each source keeps such values out of the part, and the engine check catches any source not yet known.

D2660: A mesh is tested for being closed by sorting one flat array of edge keys (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed). Measuring an imported mesh and cutting it with a plane each ask whether the mesh is closed, and the answer came from `np.unique` over the rows of every triangle edge pair. On the 300,000 triangle mesh of `test_large_mesh_is_measured_with_whole_arrays` that took 2.4 s a call with the PC busy, twice in the test, so the test took 8 s against its 3 s limit. Each edge is now one int64 key, its lower corner index times the vertex count plus its higher one; the keys are sorted, and the mesh is closed when they come in pairs and no pair runs on into the next. The answer is the same for closed, open, doubled and finned meshes. Measured with the PC busy, old and new code in the same run (CPU time, best of six): the test's measure and section took 2.58 s before and 0.42 s after; the closed test alone 2.36 s before and 0.07 s after. `tests/perf/test_headroom.py` checks the answers against the old row count and that `np.unique` is not called.
Status: Default
Reason: A sort of one flat array is the whole array way; a unique over rows sorts records and is many times slower.

D2661: A rebuild measures each solid once, and the thread check measures only the bodies a cut changed (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed). In the nut and bolt each thread's helical solid was measured four times (turned right side out twice, the size check after the boolean, the thread cut check), the thread check measured the whole part before and after although the other body was untouched, and the identical body check measured both bodies though their face counts differ: 25 volume measures in `solids` for a part of two threads, about 0.1 s each on spline faces. Now: (1) inside a rebuild `volume_of` keeps the last 16 shapes it measured, by shape, place and orientation (an inside out copy has its own entry), in a context the rebuild engine opens and closes, so nothing is held after the rebuild and other threads never see it; a compound of one solid also keeps that solid with the same value, which is bit for bit the volume the kernel gives for the solid (checked on 37 shapes of six samples); (2) `check_thread_cut` takes the volume removed from the bodies the cut changed, before less after, and leaves out bodies that are the same shape on both sides; (3) `identical_groups` counts faces, edges and vertices first and measures only bodies whose counts another body shares; (4) ordering one face for its name skips its centroid. Volumes kept are never changed values, so every result is the same; the thread check compares with a 1 percent margin. Measured on the nut and bolt with the PC busy, old and new code in the same run (best of six): 25 measures before, 12 after; CPU time of the rebuild 4.05 s before, 3.61 s after, of which the Python thread 1.25 s before, 0.97 s after; wall time 1.78 s before, 1.56 s after (the full rebuild budget is 3 s). The rest is the thread's cut (0.82 s) and the independent common of the thread check (0.90 s), which stays: sharing the cut's intersection with it would make the check agree with the cut by construction. `tests/perf/test_headroom.py` counts the measures and checks the kept values.
Status: Default
Reason: The same shape has the same volume; measuring it again only repeats the kernel's slowest step on spline faces.

D2662: The checks after a boolean map the part once (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed). The merge check and the validity check each asked for the new faces and edges of a feature, three passes per boolean, each walking every face or edge of the part in Python, and the merge check worked out the bounds of every face it compared, which on generated_200's top face with 98 holes cost about 7 ms. Now `_new_of` maps all sub shapes of both shapes in the kernel, subtracts them in one call and keeps the last pair, so a feature's checks map the part once; the shapes left are each listed once, where the walk listed an edge once per face. Both checks only ask whether some shape qualifies, so the order and the doubles do not change their answers. `_same_surface` reads the surfaces without the face bounds, which it never used. On the last cut of generated_200, with the PC busy: the merge check 9.2 ms before, 2.5 ms after; the validity check 6.2 ms before, 1.9 ms after; the whole result check 7.9 ms before, 3.9 ms after. `tests/perf/test_headroom.py` checks the new shapes against the old walk, that four questions map the part once, and the surface answers against the bounded form.
Status: Default
Reason: The checks look at what a feature changed; finding that should not cost a walk over the whole part in Python per question.

D2663: A rebuild makes each feature's data once and reads a typed plain value once (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed). Each feature's file data was made twice per rebuild (for its cache key and for the time estimate of D2600), and the equations read all 395 typed values of generated_200 again in every rebuild, though a value with no formula uses no names. The data is now made once and kept for the estimate, except for a feature that was just built, whose data is made again after its build as before; a plain value is read once per text, kind and unit system (`functools.lru_cache`, 4096 entries), and an error is raised every time and never kept. Formulas are read every time. Measured on the edit near the end of generated_200 (budget 3), with the PC busy, old and new code in the same run, together with D2662 and D2664: CPU time 0.125 s before, 0.047 s after; wall time 0.122 s before, 0.059 s after (budget 0.75 s). `tests/perf/test_headroom.py` counts the data made in an edit and checks that formulas see changed values.
Status: Default
Reason: An edit of one dimension should cost the features it touches; the 198 kept features need their keys, not their data made twice.

D2664: A cut or join on a body of 100 to 999 faces is made locally when every face near the tool is a big flat face (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed). Of generated_200's 2.0 to 3.5 s full rebuild, about two thirds was its 98 hole cuts in the kernel, each dearer than the last, because the kernel rebuilds every hole of the plate's top face in each cut. The local boolean of D2601 stands such a face in for by a small patch, but only on bodies of 1000 faces or more. Bodies from `PATCH_MIN_FACES` (100) faces now take the local path too, but only when every face whose box meets the tool's box is a big flat face that a patch stands in for (40 edges or more, the tool away from its outline): the tool then meets nothing but the inside of those faces, as a hole in a perforated plate does. Anything else on such a body goes to the kernel as before ("not only big faces near"). A first try that also took bodies where only some near faces were patched changed the gearbox: its Filler Bore cut kept one side face where the kernel makes two. With the rule as it is, all 35 sample parts (the gearbox included) were rebuilt with local booleans off and on, and the face names of the result, its precise volume (to the last digit) and every feature's state and messages are equal; the gearbox's face names were also compared after every feature; generated_200 makes 51 of its cuts locally and the gearbox 2 joins. With `FDCAD_LOCAL_BOOLEAN_CHECK=1` every local cut of generated_200 matched the kernel's material, faces and validity. Measured with the PC busy (CPU time, same run, local booleans off and on): generated_200 3.59 s off, 2.59 s on. With D2661 to D2663, old and new code in the same run (best of six): CPU time 3.58 s before, 2.02 s after; wall time 3.03 s before, 2.03 s after (budget 3 s). `tests/core/test_local_boolean.py` checks that a plate of 118 faces is cut locally and matches the kernel, that a cut at its outline and a plate of 86 faces go to the kernel.
Status: Default
Reason: The face that makes each cut dearer is the one the patch was made for; limiting the path to tools that meet only such faces keeps every result the kernel would give.

D2678: Opening a part reports what it left out (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; audit D3 item 21). A damaged configuration entry (not an object, or with no name) was dropped when the file was read, and so were damaged values of a configuration, a damaged configurations block and an active name that names nothing, all with no word to the user, because reading had no way to warn. The reader now collects warnings in `Document.load_warnings`, a list of sentences that is never saved and is not part of equality, so the file format is unchanged. `configurations.from_file` adds one sentence for each thing it leaves out, naming the entry by its place ("Configuration entry 3 of 4 has no name and was left out, with its 2 configured values."), the configuration whose values were damaged, or the active configuration that was not found and the one used instead. The schema 1 to 2 migration no longer drops entries that are not objects itself, so they are reported too. When a part is added to a tab, the window shows the notes in one warning bar above the view ("Bracket opened, but parts of the file were damaged: ... Check the part, then save it to keep it this way, or open another copy of the file.") and clears the list, so it shows once. The bar has no Don't Show Again, since each damaged file is its own news. The same channel carries the name fixes of D2679. Opening still refuses a file whose damage is not safe to skip, as before.
Status: Default
Reason: The part still opens, as before, but the user learns what is missing while the original file may still be at hand; silent loss is the worst outcome for a damaged file.

D2679: Names are checked when a part is read (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; audit D5 item 4, second half). Saved view and tree folder names were taken from the file as they were, so two views or folders could share a name (ignoring case, as the create and rename checks do), have an empty name or be longer than the limit; a second view of the same name could not be reached, since views are found by name. Create and rename already refused such names (`saved_views.name_problem` and `tree_info.name_problem`, D690 and D692, used by Save View, Rename View, New Folder, Rename Folder and the slice folders), so nothing changed there. On read, `saved_views.usable_names` and `tree_info.usable_names` now give each view and folder a name those checks accept: spaces trimmed, cut to 60 or 80 characters, an empty name becomes "View 1" or "Folder 1", and a taken name gets the next free number ("Top 2"), in file order so the first keeps its name. Configuration names get the same: a repeated name gets a number, and a name with commas, quotes, line breaks or extra spaces is cleaned as `check_name` would, with the active name, parents and design table rows that named it following the new name; links to a repeated name stay on the first, which is what they always reached. Each change is a sentence in the load warnings (D2678), and saving writes the fixed names. Feature and variable names are not renamed on read: formulas name them, and a repeated variable is already an error on rebuild ("Variable 'w' is defined twice. Rename one of them.").
Status: Default
Reason: A name the app cannot make should not stay, but renaming silently would surprise; a numbered name is the smallest change that makes every item reachable.

D2680: A fillet whose rounds meet names every edge alike, with the radius that works (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; audit E item 8, second half). Reproduced on the four upright corners of a 50 by 50 plate filleted at 25 mm or more: each corner rounds on its own, but the rounds of neighbouring corners meet. `fillet.pinpoint` added the edges one at a time while the result built (D2604), so corners 1 and 3 were kept and only 2 and 4 were named, "(rounds on its own)", with no largest radius and no Reduce fix, and the message said the kernel could not round them together. The four edges along the top of the plate, where each round is limited by the plate's thickness, were already reported evenly. Now, when some edges round alone but not with the others, `fillet.meeting_limit` tries those edges in pairs with each kept edge (at most 24 pairs). A pair counts as meeting only when it fails at the fillet's radius and also at 5 percent more, so a kernel quirk at one size is not taken for meeting rounds. When some pair meets, the radius is searched as for one edge: every radius times a share, halved eight times, down to a sixteenth (D1043), with all the edges in one call. When a share works, every edge that was left out and every kept edge whose round meets one of them is named, in list order, with that radius ("edge 1 (largest radius 24.4 mm)", the same rounded value as the fix), the message says "At this radius the rounds of these edges run into each other. Reduce the radius, or fillet some of these edges and leave the others out.", and Reduce the Radius is offered. Fillet the Rest still skips only the edges the partial result leaves out (2 of the 4 corners), since the other two round together. The search runs only for a fillet with one radius, and only while the fix search is within its time (D1043). It runs after the other ways to split the fillet (D1405), which keep the radius, so a slow part still gets those. The gearbox case of D2604 changes: at a draft of 3.03 degrees, edges 3 and 4, the roots of the two mirrored bosses, fail as a pair from about 1.86 mm up, so both are now named with 1.82 mm, beside the fix that rounds each chain as its own fillet. The chamfered tube end in `test_fillet.py`, two rims whose rounds cross in a 1 mm ring, now names both rims, not only the second.
Status: Default
Reason: Equal edges should get equal words, and when the cause is the radius, the user needs the radius that works and a button for it; a pair test tells meeting rounds from the kernel's trouble with a whole set, which keeps D2604's message for that case.

D2681: Select Chain shows in the sketch item menu when no item was hit (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; audit D11 item 9, second half). With sketch items selected, the right click menu opened from the keyboard (Shift+F10 or the Menu key) or by a right click off the items is the menu for the selection (TOOL_SPEC T9.8 and T9.12), but Select Chain was added only when the click hit an item, since it chained from that item. TOOL_SPEC T9.8 lists Select Chain for the sketch entity menu with no condition, and T9.12 says the keyboard menu is the menu for the current selection, so it should show; the empty sketch menu (T9.2) does not list it, and with nothing selected that menu still shows. `select_chain` now takes several items: with nothing hit it selects every curve joined end to end with any selected item, in sketch order, and Ctrl still adds to the selection (TR39). A right click on an item chains from that item, as before.
Status: Default
Reason: The spec lists Select Chain for every sketch item menu, and a menu opened from the keyboard should offer what a click on the item offers.

D2682: New parts are named Untitled, Untitled 2 and so on (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; bug hunt round 10a O10a-9, second half). A part with no file and no name was shown as "Untitled" by its tab, the window title, the breadcrumbs, the save dialog and the close prompt, so with several new parts every close prompt said "Save changes to Untitled before closing?" and the tabs could not be told apart either. When a session is added to a tab, a part with no file and no name of its own now gets `session.untitled`: "Untitled", or the lowest of "Untitled 2", "Untitled 3" and so on that no open part's title uses (ignoring case), so a name closed earlier is used again. The empty part made at start (D1033), which closes when another part is added, does not count, so the first new part is still Untitled. `session.display_name` is the part's own name or this name; the tab, window title, close prompt, breadcrumbs and the Save As and Save a Copy names use it, so a second new part saves as "Untitled 2.fdprt" by default. Export names of an unsaved part still fall back to "Part", and parts named from a sample, an import or the calibration tool keep those names.
Status: Default
Reason: Numbered names are the usual way to tell new documents apart, and the close prompt must name the part it is about.

D2636: A strut lattice leaves out struts that lie wholly past its bounding body (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by the edit storm, `tests/core/features/edit_storm.py`, on the lattice block). The storm now also edits each driving sketch dimension and each number of a node, as users do, and can nudge down by one percent (one less for a count) as well as up (`--down`); `--part=K/N` shares a large part between N runs. Over every sample, up and down, one edit failed outside the gearbox: on `samples/graphs/lattice_block.fdprt` a cell of 9.9 mm in place of 10 made Graph Body 1 fail with "This boolean has 235 bodies, which may take a long time. Click Run Anyway". The cells start at the box's low corner (D377), so 30 / 9.9 needs a fourth row of cells that covers the last 0.3 mm, and every strut of the row's far side lay wholly outside the box: 91 of the 235 struts, made, fused and then cut away whole. `strut_ends` now takes how far a strut's ball stands out from its line (the ball's radius, larger than the strut's) and leaves out each strut whose box starts further than that past the body's box. The cut result is the same, as the cut removed all of each such strut (a test compares it with the lattice made from every strut); the Struts output counts the struts that reach the body; at 9.9 mm the lattice has 144 struts and builds without asking. Where the cells fit the box exactly nothing changes. Tests: `tests/core/graph/test_patterns.py` (the 9.9 mm cell, cubic and octet) and `tests/core/features/test_edit_storm.py` (the storm's new edits are made and put back).
Status: Default
Reason: The confirmation guards real cost; counting struts that the cut throws away whole made a 1 percent edit ask, and made the kernel fuse them for nothing.

D2637: A pick on a piece of a face that is no longer split off blames no feature that did not take it (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, bug; found by the edit storm on the gearbox). The gearbox's two bearing bosses are both 10 mm deep, so their front faces are one face, and Cap Screw Position sits on a piece of it, `f20/cap/end#1#1` (cut in two at Output Bearing Boss and again by the crush ribs). Made 10.1 mm deep, the Output Bearing Boss stands 0.1 mm proud and the two fronts are separate faces again, with no pieces: the sketch fails, rightly (IDEAS 70), but the error said "It was lost at Input Bearing Boss" and offered Show Cause on it, though Input Bearing Boss was not changed and still makes its front, `f20/cap/end`. The cause finder of D773 looked only for the exact name, and a name that no feature's body ever had sent it to the feature its name starts with. It now also follows the faces the name is a split piece of, by taking off the `#n` numbers one at a time: when one of them is still in the part up to the failing feature, no feature took the face away and no cause is named, so the error keeps its plain words ("Reselect the face"); when that face was taken away, the feature that took it is the cause, as for any face. Position numbers that are not pieces (`f6/face#3`) have no such face and keep the old rule. Which earlier feature no longer splits the face is not known from the results of one rebuild, so it is not guessed. Tests: `tests/core/rebuild/test_causes.py` (a slot that no longer cuts a plate's top in two, and the same with the whole top then cut away).
Status: Default
Reason: Show Cause must point at a feature that changed the picked face; sending the user to a feature that was not touched is worse than naming none.

D2683: A sketch cuts a spline part on its mesh for its outline and works out the intersection curves only when a tool asks (2026-11-18, Phase 7D, speed; found by the right click sweep on the nut and bolt). Starting a sketch on the nut and bolt's Top Plane took 17 to 22 s.
