The plane runs along the bolt, and two kernel cuts of the part with the sketch plane went through the thread's spline faces: the reference outline drawn while sketching (8.7 s) and the intersection curves of TR6 (8.3 s), on every sketch that opened. On a part the kernel is slow on (the test of D2612: more than 600 faces or any free form surface) the reference outline is now cut from the part's mesh in numpy, as Layer Preview does (D2615), in 0.16 s; it has no circles to snap centres to there. The intersection curves are now worked out like the silhouette of D2609: only when Intersection Curves or Close Sketch to Model is picked. A sketch then works out only the turned outline of TR319 when it opens (0.05 s on the nut and bolt). Picking Intersection Curves on such a part still waits for the kernel's cut; fitting lines and arcs to the mesh cut, as D2618 does for the silhouette, would remove that wait.
Status: Default
Reason: The outline is a guide drawn while sketching and the mesh is how the part is shown; the exact cut matters only to the tools that copy it into the sketch.

D2659: App event filters do nothing off the GUI thread, and the smoke test stops the app with kill -9 (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, exit; IDEAS 48). Git Bash's plain `kill` ends a native Windows program by starting a thread in it that calls ExitProcess (exit code 143). Windows stops every other thread, the GUI thread among them, and the program's libraries shut down on the new thread. Qt still hands that thread events whose C++ objects are gone, and the key position filter on the whole app (TR354) was the first Python code they reached: its first line, `event.type()`, read freed memory and `crash.log` recorded an access violation. The packaging smoke test did this on every run of the built app, and the source app did it in 6 of 6 runs killed 40 s after start. Both filters on the whole app, the key position filter and the macOS file open filter in `app.py`, now ask `fdcad.ui.gui_thread.off_gui_thread()` first. It is plain Python that compares thread ids and never calls Qt, and off the GUI thread the filter returns False before it touches the event. With the guard no FDCAD code is in the fault any more, but the same exit still ends in an access violation in 6 of 6 runs, now inside the shut down of Qt and its Python bindings with no Python frame. It happens with no FDCAD filter installed too, once the window has finished loading, and no Python code runs before a forced exit starts, so nothing in FDCAD can reach it. A normal quit, the close button, End Task and `kill -9` (TerminateProcess: nothing runs in the process) leave no entry, so `packaging/smoke_test.sh` now stops the app with `kill -9`; three runs on the built app left no access violation. The crash guard (D1035) reads its own journal notes, not `crash.log`, so this entry never holds a feature. A test calls each filter from another thread with an event that fails on any use, and checks that no other filter on the whole app is added without the guard.
Status: Default
Reason: Python code must not run on a thread whose GUI thread was stopped mid way; the rest of the fault is in the libraries' own shut down, which the smoke test now avoids instead of reporting it as FDCAD's.

D2690: UI review of 2026-11-19, node editor (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, owner request: "looks like a million bucks; make it look like a billion bucks"). The review is `docs/UI_REVIEW_2026-11-19.md`; `tools/ui_review_shots.py` takes its screenshots (every main screen, in each theme, at any display scale, into the ignored `.shots` folder). Numbers D2684 to D2689 were left free for work going on beside this branch. (1) The band behind a node's title was built from a rounded rectangle and a plain one that overlap, and filled with Qt's default odd even rule, which leaves the overlap empty: the lower half of the band was not painted, so the white title stood half on the card's own colour and could not be read in the light themes. The band's path now uses the winding rule. (2) The node list drew "title, four spaces, category" as one text, so the categories did not line up and a long title pushed its category out of sight behind a sideways scroll bar. A delegate draws the title at the left and the category at the right in the muted colour; a long title is cut short with dots; the list no longer scrolls sideways. The row's own text is unchanged, for screen readers and type to find. (3) The panel's title bar is styled: semibold title on the window colour, and FDCAD's own float and close marks. Qt draws these two buttons 10 px wide whatever the style says, so the marks are drawn heavy and to the edge of their box; a title bar of FDCAD's own with 24 px buttons is listed in the review as a proposal, because it replaces Qt's dragging of the panel. (4) The square where two scroll bars meet is clear in every scroll area (it was a white box), the canvas has a 1 px outline in the border colour, and the status line under it is in the muted colour.
Status: Default
Reason: A title that cannot be read is a fault, not a matter of taste; the rest brings the newest panel up to the Datum rules the other panels already follow.

D2691: The search box and the tab list button sit level with the command tabs (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review). Qt hangs a tab widget's corner widgets from the foot of the tab row. The search box was therefore 6 px lower than the tab names, 1 px above the card of tools, and ran to the window's edge with no margin. Tests require the box and the button to be the corner widgets themselves (`test_command_search`, `test_command_tabs`), so they are not wrapped in a holder: the style sheet gives `QLineEdit#command_search` a margin of 6 px below and at the right, the same margins a tab has, and `CommandSearch` adds that margin to its fixed width. `QToolButton#command_tabs_button` gets the same margin below. The box now ends in line with the right edge of the card.
Status: Default
Reason: The top right corner is the first place the eye lands; a box that hangs low and touches two edges reads as unfinished.

D2692: Property and sketch panels share one field column, one header and one kind of card (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review). (1) `groups.icon_label` was a 16 px label at the top of its row, so a field icon sat 4 px above the middle of its 24 px field, and a row that starts with an icon put its field at 24 px while a row that starts with a button (Reverse Direction, Draft) put it at 33 px. The label is now one cell with the icon in its middle. The cell's side is measured once from a small icon button in the current style (`groups.icon_cell`), not written as a number, because the button's size comes from the style sheet and the font. Fields of both kinds of row share a left edge. Rows with a word in front (Along, the Hole Tool's Type and Size) keep the form's own label column; lining those up with the icon rows needs the forms rebuilt and is not done. (2) Lists inside a group, a group box or a window (`QFrame#panel_group QListView`, `QGroupBox QListView`, `QDialog QListView`) get the field colour and the 3:1 outline of a text field (U1.2); before, the list of picked edges was a grey area without an edge. The tree, the start page and the node list are not in such a parent and keep their look. The list that drops from a drop down is a list view inside the same parents, so a second, more specific rule (`... QComboBox QAbstractItemView`) gives it back its raised colour and quiet edge; without it, drop downs in panels and windows went dark in the dark themes. (3) The header's OK and Cancel are words only. OK had the `corner.ok` tick, which is drawn in the accent, on a button filled with the accent: it could not be seen and pushed the word off centre. Cancel loses its cross so the two match, as in every window. The confirmation corner in the view keeps both icons. (4) Help and Pin are two small buttons of one height at the right of the title; Pin was 90 px wide because every button in the header took the main button's least width. (5) The sketch panel's OK and Cancel are two buttons at equal width across the panel, in place of a button box that put them at the right at their smallest size, and its body has the header's 12 px padding (was 8). (6) `QGroupBox` is a card with its title inside, semibold, 8 px from the top and 12 px from the left, like `QFrame#panel_group`. The title used to sit in a 16 px margin above the card in the normal weight: the `font-weight` on `QGroupBox::title` was never applied, because Qt takes a group box's title font from the box itself. The weight is now set on `QGroupBox`; a style sheet font does not pass to child widgets, so the fields inside stay normal. The Reference Geometry and Section View panels have their own one row headers and are listed in the review to follow.
Status: Default
Reason: U2.3 asks for fields on one left edge; two panels that open in the same place should not teach two layouts.

D2693: The left panel is one colour on every tab, with a centred empty state and aligned colour swatches (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review). (1) `QWidget#left_panel_body` named no widget, so pages that paint no background of their own (Errors, the margins of Variables) showed the window colour while the tree showed the panel colour. The rule is now `QTabWidget#left_tabs > QStackedWidget`, which holds every page. (2) "No warnings or errors." is `QLabel#empty_state`: centred, muted, 24 px under the two ticks, and it takes the table's room so the ticks do not move when the table comes and goes. (3) The Kind column of the Errors table is as wide as its word, so the Message column gets the room at the panel's default width. (4) `appearance.tree_rows.swatch` drew a bare 14 px square: narrower than the 18 px row icons, so "Appearances" began 4 px left of its neighbours; without an edge, so a white colour vanished on the panel; and at one size, so it was soft on a high DPI screen. It is a rounded square with a 1 px edge in the theme's strong border colour, in the middle of a cell of the row icon size, drawn at one and two times. The colour inside is the user's own and is not themed (U1.6).
Status: Default
Reason: DESIGN_LANGUAGE 3.2 says the left panel is one colour from its tab row to the bottom.

D2694: Message bars carry a mark, one leading button and grid spacing (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review). (1) A warning bar and an information bar differed only in the colour of their edge, which U4.4 does not allow. Each bar starts with a 16 px mark: `tree.warning_mark`, or the new `ui.info_mark` drawn all in the text colour (`plain`), so it sits on any edge colour. (2) A bar had up to three outlined buttons of equal weight. Don't Show Again and Close are flat now, and the button that does what the message asks (Suppress, Save) stays outlined, so it leads. The words are unchanged. (3) Padding (12, 4, 4, 4), 8 px between items, the edge and the corner come from the spacing step (they were fixed 8, 4, 2 and 6 px, which did not grow with the font). The stack has 8 px at the sides and the foot and 4 px between bars, on the colour of the view's top, so the strip of view tools, the bars and the view read as one area. `MessageBars.restyle` sets these colours and each bar's mark again, and the window calls it when the theme changes, as it does for the strip of view tools; before, a bar kept the colours of the theme it was made in. (4) Not changed: the information bar keeps the green of `state_ok` on its edge (D1034 item 12). Green says "done", which a notice is not; a neutral or cobalt edge is listed for the owner.
Status: Default
Reason: The bar's job is to get one action taken; the action must be the loudest thing on it.

D2695: The start page has an empty state in the list's place, the panel colour and main size buttons (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review). (1) With no recent part the page showed the empty list, a white card of about 1100 by 500 px, with "No recent parts yet..." in a line under it. The list is hidden while it is empty and the same words are centred in its place inside a dashed outline (`QLabel#start_empty`); the "Drop a part file..." line is hidden then, because the empty state says it. (2) `QWidget#start_page { background: surface }` was never painted: a plain `QWidget` subclass ignores a style sheet background unless `WA_StyledBackground` is set, so the page had the window's darker grey. The attribute is set. The page now has the tone of the view it stands in for, so opening a part no longer flips the middle of the window from dark to light. (3) New Part and Open are 28 px tall, the main button size of U3.3, and at least 80 px wide.
Status: Default
Reason: U8.3 says an empty place says what to do; a large blank card says nothing.

D2696: Message windows show FDCAD's own marks (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review). `AppStyle.standardIcon` returns `tree.warning_mark`, `tree.error_mark`, `ui.info_mark` and the new `ui.question_mark` for the four message box pictures; every other standard picture is Fusion's. Qt's stock pictures are filled, glossy and the same bright yellow and blue in all four themes, beside FDCAD's 1.5 px line icons in theme colours. The two new icons pass the audit: a rounded square in the text colour with a light body tint, and the letter in the accent. The square keeps them apart from the warning triangle and the error circle by shape (U4.4).
Status: Default
Reason: CLAUDE.md section 7 item 4 asks for FDCAD's own icons everywhere; a message window is where a user looks hardest.

D2697: Spin boxes match text fields, the progress bar is slim, the tree filter is on the grid (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review). (1) Qt adds a style sheet's vertical padding to a spin box on top of its inner field's own margins, and does not apply the left padding to the inner field at all. So a spin box was 28 px tall beside 25 px fields, and its number began 3 px from the edge where a text field's text begins at 9. `QAbstractSpinBox` now has 1 px of vertical padding (0 with the 2 px focus ring, so the size does not change with focus), which leaves it 1 px taller than a text field at the default font, and `AppStyle.polish` gives the inner field a 6 px left text margin. (2) The status bar's progress bar is 10 px tall with its outline (was 14), with a round end and no percent text (`setTextVisible(False)`). The text was drawn in the text colour over the accent fill (under 3:1 in the Light theme) in a bar 12 px tall inside with 13 px letters. The step is named in the status text beside the bar. A progress bar elsewhere keeps its text. (3) The tree's filter box and state choice were 2 px apart with fixed 4 px margins; both are one spacing step now, so they grow with the font.
Status: Default
Reason: U2.2 puts every gap on the 4 px grid, and U2.3 puts values in the same place in every value field.

D2698: Pictures on labels are drawn at the screen's pixel ratio (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review, CLAUDE.md section 9 item 5). `QIcon.pixmap(16, 16)` and `pixmap(QSize(...))` return the picture for a 100 percent screen, and a label stretches it at 150 and 200 percent. Five labels did this: the mark on the start page and in About, the relation icons in the sketch panel and in the Relations panel, and the marks in the tree's problem box. They pass `devicePixelRatioF()`. `tests/ui/test_ui_review.py` scans `src/fdcad/ui` for a `setPixmap(... .pixmap(...))` that names no ratio, so a new one fails the suite. Cursor pictures (`plane_pick`, `canvas`) are not labels and are left as they are.
Status: Default
Reason: One soft icon among sharp ones is what a high DPI user notices first.

D2699: The Gestures page fits its window, and ticks in lists match check boxes (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review). (1) Each drop down on the Gestures page of Preferences listed every command and took the width of the longest one, so the Part and Sketch cards together were wider than the 720 px window. The page does not scroll sideways (D1034 item 7), so the Sketch card was cut off and the arrows of its drop downs could not be reached. The drop downs now size to a least text length of 12 letters and stretch with their card; the list that drops down keeps the width of the longest command (`view().setMinimumWidth`), so nothing in it is cut short. (2) A tick box in a row of a list, tree or table was Fusion's own small black box, beside check boxes drawn with the accent fill and FDCAD's tick. `QListView::indicator`, `QTreeView::indicator` and `QTableView::indicator` now have the check box's size, outline, accent fill, tick, dash and disabled looks. Seen on the Shortcut Bar page of Preferences.
Status: Default
Reason: A control that cannot be reached is a fault; and one kind of control has one look (U3.1).

D2700: An information bar has a neutral edge; a green edge means success only (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P1, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). An information bar took its left edge and its tint from `state_ok`, the green of "this worked" (D1034 item 12, noted as open in D2694 item 4). A notice such as "This part was opened to look at" is not a success. The edge is now the theme's muted text colour (`Chrome.muted`), in all four themes, in the colour vision safe colours and in the system contrast colours; the tint and the thin outline are mixed from the same colour as before, so the card is a quiet grey. `message_bars.edge_colour` holds the rule. A warning bar keeps `state_warning`. Neutral was chosen over cobalt for two reasons: DESIGN_LANGUAGE principle 2 keeps cobalt for what a tool adds or acts on, and with the colour vision safe preference (TR292) `state_ok` is itself a blue, so a cobalt edge would again sit beside the colour of success. The kind of a bar still never shows by colour alone: the mark of D2694 stays. `contrast.pairs` measures the new edge ("notice edge" on the raised colour and on the top of the view, 3:1 as a mark, U1.2); it is 4.1:1 or more in every theme. No theme colour changed; this is a change of which colour is used where, which D745 leaves to the owner.
Status: Default
Reason: One colour, one meaning: if green also marks a plain notice, a green edge can no longer say "this worked".

D2701: Close on a message bar, and Help and Pin in the panel header, are icons (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P5, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). (1) Close on a message bar shows `ui.close_tab`, the cross that closes a part's tab, in place of the word. (2) Help in the property panel header shows `help.tool`, the icon of Help for This Tool, the command the button runs; it was a bare "?". (3) Pin shows a pin. No pin existed, so two were drawn for FDCAD in the house style and pass the icon audit: `ui.pin`, a loose pin lying at an angle, in the text colour; and `ui.pin_on`, the same pin standing upright, pushed into a line, with its head in the accent. Pinned therefore shows twice, the checked look of the button (tinted fill, accent outline) and a different drawing, so it never shows by colour alone (U4.4). (4) Each keeps its word: the accessible names are "Close", "Help" and "Pin" (Help's was its whole tooltip), and each tooltip starts with the word. `PANEL_PIN_TIP` and `PANEL_HELP_TIP` were reworded to do so; the Close tooltip already did. (5) Each is a 24 px square at the default font (U3.3), from one style rule; the cross and the pin are 16 px icons. Pin was 34 px wide, and Close was as wide as its word. (6) `PropertyPanel.refresh_icons` and `MessageBar.restyle` set the icons again when the theme changes, so they are never left in the old theme's text colour. Don't Show Again stays a word: no icon says it. The Pin tick box of the Measure box is a different control and is unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: The three are small, often seen and sit in narrow places; an icon with its word in the tooltip and for screen readers saves the width without losing the name.

D2702: Empty states for the left panel with no part, the Variables table and the two sketch relation cards (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P9, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). `fdcad/ui/empty_state.py` holds the one look for all of them: one line in the muted colour, centred in the place the content will take (DESIGN_LANGUAGE section 3 item 9, D2693, D2695). (1) Left panel, no part open: the tree is hidden and its place holds "No part is open. Use New Part or Open to start." in the dashed outline the start page uses beside it (`QLabel#empty_box`, the same rule as `QLabel#start_empty`). The filter box and the state choice stay in place but are greyed, since there is nothing to filter; they are not hidden, so the panel's top does not jump when a part opens. `FeatureTree.refresh` now sends `refreshed` when there is no part too, which is how `TreeFilter` hears that the last part closed. The hint of a new part with no features (D673) is unchanged. (2) Variables table with no rows: "No variables yet. Use Add Variable to make one." in the middle of the table, or "No part is open. Use New Part or Open, then add variables here." when no part is open. It is an `EmptyOverlay`, a label over the table's own area that lets clicks through and follows the table's rows and size, so the table does not change size when the first variable arrives. (3) Add Relation card: the card stays in view whenever no sketch tool is active, as `test_tool_panel_shows_while_a_tool_is_active` pins; the review's idea of hiding it was not followed. While it has no buttons it says "Relations that fit what you select show here.", or "No relation fits this selection. Select other items." when something is selected. The line goes when a button comes. (4) Relations of the selection: the empty list says "Select an item to see its relations.", or "The selection has no relations yet.", in its middle, again as an overlay, so the list keeps its size. The lines in (3) and (4) are new wording; "Select sketch items to add relations." above the cards is unchanged. Each line that says nothing can be shown also says what to do next, which `tests/core/test_message_next_steps.py` checks for the strings named `NO_...` (CLAUDE.md section 8 item 4).
Status: Default
Reason: U8.3 says an empty place says what to do; a blank box reads as something that failed to load.

D2703: Right click menus show the icons of their commands (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P4, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). The menu bar showed an icon beside most commands; the right click menus of the tree, the view and the sketch showed none for the same commands. `fdcad/ui/menu_icons.py` finds the icon of an entry, and the two helpers every such menu is built with call it: `context_menu.add` (view and sketch menus, and the view orientation popup) and `FeatureTree._add` (tree menus). No icon was drawn for this; every name it can return was already in `icons/NAMES.md`. The icon is found in this order: (1) the entry's key, from the `KEYS` map (`zoom_fit` is `view.fit`); (2) a key that is a command id itself, a sketch tool (`tool.line` is `sketch.line`), a relation or a display style; (3) the `LABELS` map, for an entry worded differently from its command; (4) the entry's label, when exactly one command with an icon has that label. A label that two commands share (Point, Mirror, Corner Relief) picks none, because the menu cannot tell which is meant. Edit Feature, Edit Sketch, Hide and Show take the icons the context toolbar already shows for them (`context.edit` and so on), since the menu opens just below that toolbar (T8.3); OK and Cancel take the confirmation corner's tick and cross, Reverse Direction the icon of the panel's own button, and Edit Material the icon of Material. About a third of the entries in the menus of two sample parts have an icon. The rest (Rename, Suppress, Comment, Roll Back to Here, Grid Spacing and others) have no icon anywhere in FDCAD and stay without one, as the owner asked: drawing them is separate work. Their text stays in line, because `app_style` gives every menu row the icon column whether or not it holds an icon (U3.4); a test checks that a row is as wide without an icon as with one. Rows that show a name from the part (a feature in Recently Edited, a saved view) are added without the helper, so a part's own names can never pick an icon by accident. A ticked entry with an icon shows the tick as a frame round the icon, as in the menu bar. Menus are built each time they open, so the icons follow the theme.
Status: Default
Reason: One command, one picture, wherever it is offered (U3.1); the icon is the fastest way to find Delete or Zoom to Fit in a long menu.

D2740: Accent text on rows under the pointer and on selected rows is measured like every other pair; no theme colour changed (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P2, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). The owner approved changing theme colours so that accent text on a row under the pointer and on a selected row reaches 4.5:1. D745 listed those pairs at 4.20 to 4.48, and the review of this morning repeated the figures without measuring. Measured again before any change, they pass in all four themes: Beige 4.61 and 4.70, Light Gray 4.93 and 4.79, Dark Grey 5.48 and 4.77, Stealth 6.91 and 6.15 (hover, then selected). The Datum colours of D1034 closed them on 2026-11-11; the figures in D745 are of the colours before that. So no colour was changed: the approval was for a fault that is gone, and D745 leaves every other colour change to the owner. What changed is the bookkeeping. (1) `contrast.pairs` measures "accent text on hover" and "accent text on selected" at 4.5:1, so a later colour change that breaks them fails `test_every_text_input_and_view_pair_is_readable` at once. (2) `test_open_pairs_meet_their_limits` lost its strict expected failure and passes: it checks those two pairs in each theme. It could not pass before only because `open_pairs` also held the edges of the 3D view. (3) `open_pairs` is now two lists, each with its own strict expected failure, so one can be closed without the other. `open_edge_pairs` is the edge colour on the bare view (Dark Grey 1.55 and 1.17, Stealth 1.27 and 1.56, against 3.0). It was not touched: the view's own drawing and its theme tokens are being worked on in another session, and one colour cannot be 3:1 on the grey face and on a dark view at once, so the fix is in how wireframe draws. `open_pressed_pairs` is new, found while measuring: the pressed fill is also what a selected row shows while the pointer is on it (`QTreeView::item:selected:hover`), and U1.1 names pressed fills. Plain text on it passes and was already measured. Coloured text does not everywhere: in Beige accent 3.98 and "ok" green 4.38; in Light Gray accent 4.16 and danger 4.49; in Dark Grey muted 3.95, accent 3.70, danger 4.00 and error 4.06; Stealth passes. No row shows accent text today; muted (a suppressed feature), danger and the state colours do show on rows. Closing it means a lighter pressed fill in the light themes and a darker one in Dark Grey, which makes pressed look closer to selected. That is a change of look the owner did not approve, so it is listed in the review as P11 and left.
Status: Default
Reason: A limit that is met should be a test that passes, and a colour is not changed to fix a number that is already right.

D2741: The unit selector has the outline of an input (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P3, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). The drop down at the right of the status bar was outlined in `Chrome.border`, the colour of quiet dividers: 1.16:1 to 1.51:1 against the status bar, where U1.2 asks 3:1 for the outline of a drop down. `QToolButton#unit_selector` now uses `Chrome.input_border`, the outline of every text field and drop down: Beige 3.70, Light Gray 3.32, Dark Grey 5.04 and Stealth 4.80 against the window colour. No theme colour changed; this is which colour is used where. The review weighed a quiet selector against the rule and offered an exception in U1.2; the owner chose the rule, so U1.2 stands without an exception. The pair was already measured ("input outline on window" in `contrast.pairs`); a test now reads the outline's pixel from the selector itself in each theme.
Status: Default
Reason: A control that opens a list has to read as a control; the status bar has one, and it was the only input in the window without a 3:1 outline.

D2742: One label column for a whole property panel (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P6, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). D2692 put the rows that start with a field icon and the rows that start with a small button on one left edge. Rows with a word in front (Along; Type, Standard and Size in the Hole Tool) kept the label column of their own group, as wide as that group's longest word, so the fields of one panel still began at two places in Extrude and at eight in the Hole Tool, where a row can have a word and an icon (Diameter). `fdcad/ui/property_panel/columns.py` gives every row of every group of a panel one column. (1) The column is as wide as the widest lead on show: a word, or the cell of a field icon or small button. In Extrude that is "Along", so the icon rows moved 9 px; in the Hole Tool it is "Thread Diameter", so the fields of the first group start where those of the others do. (2) Word rows take the width as the least width of their label, so each group's form has the same label column. Rows that lead with an icon or a button get a spacer after the lead, and the icon stays where it was, in line with the icons above and below it. No form was rebuilt and no label changed; the review had expected both. (3) A row that leads with a word shows no field icon as well. The word says what the icon says, and the icon was what pushed that one field out of line. The icon is hidden, not removed, so a form is built as before. (4) The column follows the rows on show. A row hidden by a choice (Depth measured in Extrude, the counterbore sizes in the Hole Tool) does not count, since one long word that is out of sight would push every field to the right for nothing; when such a row shows or hides, the panel lines up again after the events of that turn. Folding a group does not change the column, so folding never moves the fields of the other groups. (5) The column stops at 32 spacing steps (128 px at the default font; the longest label today is 123 px). A longer word keeps its width and the rows of its own group follow it; the other groups stay at the column. (6) A drop down beside a word may be narrower than its longest entry (least width of 8 letters), or a wider column would send it under its word, since the forms wrap a row that does not fit. The list that drops down keeps the width of its longest entry, as D2699 did in Preferences. Qt keeps the least size of a drop down it worked out earlier and only a change of style makes it work it out again, so the box is sent one. (7) `PropertyPanel.begin` lines the panel up after it is built, for every feature type; a form that adds rows later can call `PropertyPanel.align_columns`. A group that is being replaced is hidden at once, so its rows are out of the column before it is deleted. Not lined up: rows with no lead at all (a list, a tab row, a full width button or drop down), which span the group as before.
Status: Default
Reason: U2.3 asks for labels in one column and fields on one left edge; a ragged edge down a column of fields is the first thing the eye catches in a panel.

D2743: The Reference Geometry and Section View panels have the property panel's header (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P8, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). These two panels open in the place of the property panel, but kept a header of their own: the name in bold, then OK and Cancel at their smallest size beside it, each with the tick or cross of the confirmation corner. They now have the header of D2692: the tool's icon and its name in the title role, then OK and Cancel at equal width across the panel, words only, OK as the main button, with 12 px of padding and the line under the header. `fdcad/ui/property_panel/header.py` holds it as one widget, `PanelHeader`, and both panels use it; the property panel and the sketch panel still build the same layout themselves, and a test compares the measurements of all three against the property panel's. (1) The Plane, Axis, Point and Coordinate System panels show the icon of their feature type (`feature.ref_plane` and so on) and the feature's name as plain text, so a name is never read as markup. OK greys while the feature is not fully defined, as before, in the look of a disabled main button. Their OK and Cancel take the tooltips of the property panel; they had none. (2) The Section View panel shows the icon of the Section View command and keeps its own two tooltips. (3) The body of both panels has the header's 12 px padding and rows 8 px apart. (4) Help and Pin are not in this header, as in the sketch panel: what they do (Help for This Tool, and starting the same command again after OK) is wired to the property panel only. `PanelHeader.name_row` takes such buttons when a panel has them. (5) The header draws its icon again when the theme changes. Nothing in the body of either panel changed: the fields, their order and their words are as they were.
Status: Default
Reason: Panels that open in one place should have one header (DESIGN_LANGUAGE section 3 item 6); OK was also the one main button still drawn with a tick that a filled button hides.

D2744: The dropdown arrow of a large command button sits under the last line of its label (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P10, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). Every large button keeps room for two lines of label, and the arrow of a dropdown was drawn in the row under that room. Under a two line label (Linear Pattern, Helix and Spiral) it sat 3 px under the words. Under a one line label (Fillet, Plane) it sat a whole empty line lower, cut off from its word. RIBBON_SPEC R3.1 says the arrow sits under the label, and D642 put the arrows of all dropdowns on one row; the two disagree for a one line label, and the owner chose R3.1. `LargeButton.text_rect` is the lines a label really has, and `arrow_rect` puts the arrow under it with the gap a two line label always had, so under one line the arrow is where the second line would be. Unchanged: every label still starts on the same line (R3.3), every large button has the same height and width rule, the arrow is centred in its button, and the whole strip under the icon still opens the list. The arrows of a tab are therefore on two rows, one per label length, and an arrow moves when its button shows another tool of its group with a label of the other length. `docs/RIBBON_SPEC.md` records it as R3B and words R3.1 and R4.3 to match; `test_every_tab_lays_out_evenly` checks the arrow against the label's own lines on every tab at 1280 and 1920 px.
Status: Default
Reason: An arrow belongs to the word it sits under; a line of empty space between them made Fillet and Plane look misprinted beside their neighbours.

D2745: The node editor has a title bar of FDCAD's own, with 24 px buttons (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, UI review item P7, approved by the owner on 2026-11-19). Qt draws the float and close buttons of a panel that can float 10 px wide whatever the style sheet says (D2690 item 3), under the 24 px of U3.3. `fdcad/ui/node_editor/title_bar.py` holds `DockTitleBar`, set with `QDockWidget.setTitleBarWidget`: the panel's name in the title role on the window colour, then two buttons of 24 px with 16 px icons. (1) The first button floats a docked panel and docks a floating one where it was. Its word, tooltip and drawing follow: Float shows `ui.float_panel`, a panel with an arrow leaving it; Dock shows `ui.dock_panel`, a window with the panel at its side. Both were drawn for FDCAD and pass the icon audit. Close shows `ui.close_tab`, the cross of a part's tab and of a message bar. Each word is the accessible name and starts the tooltip, as in D2701. (2) Qt's own handling is kept, which was the worry that held this back. The bar and its label take no mouse press, so the press reaches the panel and Qt drags it, docks it at the side it is dropped on, and floats or docks it on a double click. Tests click both buttons, double click the name twice and drag the panel off by the bar. (3) Close hides the panel through `QDockWidget.close`, so the Node Editor command is unticked as before and shows the panel again. (4) The buttons take no keyboard focus, as Qt's own did not: a click on them leaves the keys with the canvas. Closing has the Node Editor command; floating has the double click. (5) A button the panel does not allow (not floatable, not closable) is hidden, and the icons are drawn again when the theme changes. (6) A floating panel now shows this same bar in place of the system's window frame, because Qt gives a panel with a title bar of its own no system frame. It can still be moved by the bar and resized at its edges. On Windows it therefore has no system close button; Close in the bar does that. (7) The style rules for Qt's own two buttons and their two pictures in `themes/style.py` are removed, since no panel shows those buttons now; the left panel has an empty title bar and cannot float.
Status: Default
Reason: U3.3 gives every target 24 px; the two smallest buttons in the window sat on the one panel a user moves about most.
D2704: Windows only names of ctypes are read with getattr, so the type check passes on a Mac (2026-11-19, Mac run, CLAUDE.md section 9 item 6). `uv run mypy` on the owner's Mac gave three errors that the Windows run does not: `ctypes.windll` in `system_integration.add_to_system_recent`, and `ctypes.oledll` and `ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE` in `taskbar_progress._Windows`. mypy checks for the platform it runs on, and the type stubs give ctypes those names on Windows only. Both places choose the platform from a `platform` argument, which the tests pass in, so mypy cannot see that the lines run on Windows only. The three reads are now `getattr(ctypes, "windll")` and so on, the form `sysinfo.py` and `themes/motion.py` already use. Nothing changes when the app runs. `tests/core/test_windows_only_ctypes.py` scans `src/fdcad` for a direct `ctypes.<name>` of a Windows only name, so a new one fails the suite on every platform; a use under `if sys.platform == "win32":` (as in `core/cache/memory.py`) and a line with `# type: ignore[attr-defined,unused-ignore]` (as in `themes/system_contrast.py`) are let through, because mypy accepts both on every platform.
Status: Default
Reason: The macOS CI job runs `uv run mypy` too, so it would have stopped at the type check and never reached the tests.

D2705: On a Mac the 3D view does not start on a Qt platform with no real window (2026-11-19, Mac run, CLAUDE.md section 5 item 7 and section 9 item 8). `uv run pytest` on the owner's Mac (macOS 27, Apple Silicon) ended with a segmentation fault at the first test that shows a `ViewportWidget` by itself (`tests/ui/test_view_centre.py::_view`, used by twelve test files), so no later test ran. On macOS the kernel uses the window id as an NSView. Qt's offscreen and minimal platforms give a made up number, and `V3d_View.SetWindow` on it ends the process; no Python `except` can catch that. On Windows the kernel refuses such an id with an error, the view reports that it could not start, and those tests skip. `native.native_window_usable(qt_platform, os_name)` is False for macOS with the offscreen or minimal platform, and `ViewportWidget._init_view` raises before it makes the kernel window when it is False. `showEvent` already turns that into the `failed` signal, so the Mac now does what Windows does: the view says it could not start and the tests that need it skip. The main window and the configuration preview never make a 3D view on these platforms (`viewport_supported`), so the app itself was not at risk; the guard is for any other caller. Nothing changes on Windows or Linux, and nothing changes on a Mac with a screen. Tests in `tests/ui/test_native_handle.py`: the rule itself, and that a view told its window is unusable never passes the id to the kernel.
Status: Default
Reason: A crash in one test hides the result of every test after it, and a kernel fault must never end the process (CLAUDE.md section 5 item 7).

D2706: Spline inflection marks do not depend on rounding noise (2026-11-19, Mac run). `tests/core/sketch/test_spline_aids.py` failed on Apple Silicon: the arch through (0, 0), (10, 8), (20, 0) got an inflection mark at x = 16.67, and the S curve got its first mark there and not at 20. `spline_aids` marks a point where the curvature of two samples next to each other has opposite signs. With the handles `spline_handles` gives, the end pieces of these splines do change side at one third of the piece, which is exactly a sample. There the curvature is zero on x64 and 2.8e-18 on Apple Silicon, so the Mac saw a change of sign and Windows saw none. A curvature below 1e-9 of the spline's largest now counts as zero in `spline_aids`, so both give what Windows gave: no mark at such a sample. The comb itself is unchanged. The test passes a comb with 0, 3e-18 and -3e-18 at that sample and asks for the same marks. Left open for the manager session: a change of side that falls exactly on a sample is not marked on any platform (it never was on Windows). Marking it would add marks to freshly drawn splines and change what `test_a_c_curve_has_no_inflection` asks, so it is a question of behaviour, not a Mac fix.
Status: Default
Reason: The same sketch must show the same marks on both platforms; which marks is a separate question.

D2707: Low disk warnings tell disks apart without drive letters (2026-11-19, Mac run). `resources.shortages` listed each disk once by `Path.anchor`. On a Mac every full path has the anchor `/`, so a second volume that was low was never listed, and a path with no anchor fell back to its own text, so `test_shortages_list_each_disk_once_and_memory` (which uses `C:/a` and `C:/b`) listed one disk twice there. `resources.disk_of` names the disk: the drive when the path has a drive letter, as before on Windows; otherwise the device (`st_dev`) of the nearest folder that exists. Nothing changes on Windows.
Status: Default
Reason: "Each disk once" must hold on the Mac too, where volumes sit under one root.

D2708: Four Mac test fixes with no change to the app (2026-11-19, Mac run). (1) `test_steps_then_puts_the_sketch_back` expected the first step to be half the dimension exactly. The Step box shows its From value to four figures, and on the Mac the drawn rectangle's side is 39.875 mm, so the first step is 19.94, not 19.9375. The test now expects the value as the box shows it. (2) `test_window_uses_shortcuts_md` expected Redo to be Ctrl+Y only; on a Mac it is Cmd+Shift+Z and Cmd+Y (SHORTCUTS.md section 1, D19), and the test now expects that there. (3) `test_ctrl_tab_in_the_tree` pressed Qt's Control modifier, which is the Cmd key on a Mac; Next Part is Control+Tab on a Mac (Qt's Meta), and the test presses that there. (4) See D2709.
Status: Default
Reason: These tests had Windows values written in; the app already did what SHORTCUTS.md and D922 say.

D2709: The installer icon check compares pixels, not bytes (2026-11-19, Mac run). `test_installer_icons_are_up_to_date` drew the icons again and compared the files byte for byte with the committed ones. Qt on Apple Silicon rounds a few edge pixels differently from Qt on x64: 2 to 88 pixels per size, by 1 or 2 levels of 255. The test now compares each of the nine PNG sizes as pixels and allows 4 levels, and checks that `fdcad.ico` and `fdcad.icns` hold the committed PNGs byte for byte (`maker.ico`, `maker.icns`). A second test shows that one changed pixel, or a wrong size, still fails. The committed icons are unchanged: they are the ones drawn on Windows.
Status: Default
Reason: The check is there to catch a changed drawing that was not rendered again, which it still does on both platforms.

D2710: Two pixel checks of the UI review are skipped on a Mac without a screen (2026-11-19, Mac run, CLAUDE.md section 9 item 8). `test_spin_box_matches_a_text_field` (D2697) and `test_panel_fields_share_one_left_edge_and_icons_sit_level` (D2692) failed on the Mac by 3 px. On macOS the Fusion style takes 72 dots per inch as its base. A Mac screen reports 72, but Qt's offscreen platform reports 96, so there Fusion makes its own sizes a third larger: a spin box frame is 4 px, not 3. Measured on this Mac: offscreen, spin box 27 px and field 24; on the real screen (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=cocoa`), spin box 25 and field 24, and both tests pass. The app is right on a real Mac screen, so nothing in it changed. `skip_where_the_style_is_scaled` in `tests/ui/test_ui_review.py` skips the two tests on macOS when the screen does not report 72. To check them on a Mac, run that file with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=cocoa`.
Status: Default
Reason: A check that can only fail for a reason that is not in the app tells nobody anything; the skip says why and how to run it for real.

D2711: The startup memory budget counts the footprint on a Mac (2026-11-19, Mac run, PLAN 11.2 budget 7, follows D491). `test_startup_and_empty_part_memory` failed on the owner's Mac (macOS 27, Apple Silicon): 436 MB against 400 MB. The figure was peak resident memory, which counts the pages of library files the kernel library, VTK and Qt map. Three starts measured 418 to 438 MB resident and 209 MB of footprint each time; the footprint is what the app allocated itself and is the figure Activity Monitor shows as Memory. This is the case D491 settled for Linux. `sysinfo.private_memory` now gives the footprint on macOS (`proc_pid_rusage` of the system's libproc, through ctypes, no new dependency), and the test checks it against the same 400 MB on macOS as on Linux. Windows keeps its working set check. The budget itself is unchanged. `process_memory` and the rebuild statistics panel are unchanged. This sets aside the last sentence of D491 for macOS only; if the owner wants resident memory under 400 MB on a Mac too, that is about 40 MB of work on what is loaded at start, not a change to this test.
Status: Default
Reason: The budget is about what FDCAD uses; mapped library files are shared, can be dropped by the system at no cost, and are larger on Apple Silicon because its pages are 16 KB.
D2760: A part is drawn in its own colour, and the lights are set for it (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, view review, `docs/VIEW_REVIEW_2026-11-19.md` item A1). The first two UI reviews could not see the 3D view, which draws blank offscreen; this one drew it on the owner's PC with `tools/view_review_shots.py`. `ViewportWidget._hex`, which turns a `#RRGGBB` colour into a kernel colour for the part, its faces, sketches, planes, previews and the analysis maps, passed the numbers on as linear RGB. The kernel then lightened them for the screen: a part given the red `#C0392B` was drawn salmon (199, 114, 100 on its brightest face), and the grey part `#B4BCC4` lost its cool cast (193, 197, 201). D111 fixed the same fault for the view background only. `_hex` now gives sRGB, as `look.colour` always did, so every colour of the view is the theme's or the user's. With true colours the old lights left a part darker than its colour, so `look.LIGHTS` changed: ambient 0.30 to 0.60, key 0.72 to 0.78, fill 0.26 to 0.32, directions unchanged. `look.face_shade` holds the rule the kernel follows, measured on screen: a face gives back a quarter of the ambient light and all of the directed light that reaches it (`AMBIENT_SHARE` 0.25). The old test counted the ambient light in full, so it passed while a side face was at 0.33 of its colour. Now in the isometric view the top face is at 0.90 of the part's colour, the front at 0.54 and the side at 0.46, and no face of any direction is above 1.02, so a white part keeps its shading. Measured after the change: the red part's top face is (183, 54, 40) and the grey part's is (171, 179, 187), both within one step of what `face_shade` predicts. The feature preview's see-through amount (`PREVIEW_TRANSPARENCY`) goes from 0.55 to 0.70: it was tuned while the accent arrived paler than it is, and with the true cobalt the same solid hid the part. A test marked to run only on a screen (`FDCAD_VIEW_PIXELS=1`) reads these pixels from a real view.
Status: Default
Reason: The colour a user picks for a part is the colour they must see, and the grey part is the face every view colour is checked against (U1.3).

D2761: Lines with no face behind them take the outline colour (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, view review item A2). In Wireframe, Hidden Lines Removed and Hidden Lines Visible the kernel drew the part's lines in the part's own colour, because setting a part's colour sets every line of it. On the Light and Beige views that is a pale grey on a pale ground, 1.2 to 1.8:1: the three styles were all but blank, and in Hidden Lines Visible the dashed hidden edges were darker than the seen ones. `look.style_part` now gives the wire, line, free boundary, shared boundary and seen line settings the `silhouette` colour, the token that is checked at 3:1 against both ends of the view (D654). A body shown as wireframe on its own (TR216) takes it too; it used `edge`, which is 1.2 to 1.6:1 on the dark views. `edge` stays for edges drawn on faces. Hidden edges fade 40 percent from the outline colour toward the view (they faded from `edge`), which gives 2.7 to 4.9:1 in the four themes, always less than the seen lines. `look.bare_line_colour` names that colour, and a test holds its contrast on the view in each theme: 15.96 and 10.58 in Light, 13.83 and 9.93 in Beige, 4.66 and 8.45 in Dark, 5.57 and 6.86 in Stealth (top and bottom of the view), where `edge` gave 1.55 and 1.17 in Dark and 1.27 and 1.56 in Stealth. That was the pair of D745 still open. The `edge` token did not change and cannot: no colour is 3:1 on the grey part and on a dark view at once (D654). `themes/contrast.py` and its test are left as they were, because the `ui-polish-3` branch moves that pair to `contrast.open_edge_pairs`; once both branches are merged, that function should measure `silhouette`, the colour now drawn, and its test can lose its expected failure mark. Edges of a see-through part are still `edge` over a face that is partly the view; they read in the pictures and were left.
Status: Default
Reason: U1.3 says edges always read against the view; the outline colour is the one made for lines on the view, so no theme colour had to change.

D2762: Text the kernel draws uses the window's font (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, view review item A3). The letters of the corner triad, plane names, values and the origin's letters were drawn in the kernel's default faces: a serif for text labels and a typewriter face for the triad. `look.use_ui_font` points the two names the kernel asks for (`serif` and `courier`, found by trying each) at the application font, once, when the first 3D view is made. When the kernel does not know that font (the Mac system font has a private name) its own sans serif font is used; when it has none, nothing changes. This is a setting of the kernel's font manager for this process and touches no font on the machine. Text sizes are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: U6.7 says the triad uses the type scale; a second, serif face in the middle of the window read as a part of another program.

D2763: A value in the view sits on a plate and is drawn after the preview (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, view review item A4). The depth beside a drag arrow, the values of fields without an arrow and dimension values on the model were accent text with nothing behind it, and the first lay under the see-through preview: blue text under a blue solid, with the arrow across it. Two causes. The kernel draws the see-through items of layers that share a depth together, after their solid items, so text in the last layer still got the preview's tint; `look.text_over_previews` makes that layer clear the depth, which starts it after them (the layer has no depth test, so nothing else changes). And the text had no ground of its own: `look.style_value` draws it on the kernel's plate in the colour of the sketch editor's value plate (`label_plate` without its alpha, white in the light themes and black in the dark ones), with a space each side as a margin. Accent and sketch blue read at 6:1 or more on it in every theme. The text height is 14 px as before and now grows with the screen scale for dimension values too.
Status: Default
Reason: The value is the one thing the user reads while dragging; it must not depend on what is behind it.

D2764: A highlighted face is a flat tint with its outline (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, view review item B1). Selection and the highlight under the cursor were a copy of the face in the highlight colour, lit like the part and 15 percent see through. Lit, the burnt orange went brick on a top face and dark brown on a side face, and the teal went grey green, so one colour looked like four; no outline was drawn, though the widths for one were set. The highlight is now unlit and 35 percent see through (`HIGHLIGHT_TRANSPARENCY`), so it is the theme's colour on every face while the face's own shading still shows under it, and the face's outline is drawn in the full colour at the highlight width (2.5 px under the cursor, 3 px selected, D651). Colours, widths and layers (D1094, D1095) are unchanged. On a part whose own colour is near the highlight (a red part, selected) the tint is weak and the outline carries it; that limit stays, see the review's proposals.
Status: Default
Reason: U1.4 asks that selection never rest on colour alone and read on any face; an outline of fixed width does both.

D2765: The outline round the part is 1.5 px (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, view review item B2). `SILHOUETTE_WIDTH` was 2. The kernel makes the outline from a shell drawn behind the part, and at 2 px the shell cut into neighbouring faces wherever two faces lie close in depth: a dot pattern between the turns of a thread and in tight grooves. At 1.5 px the pattern is gone on the sample parts and the outline is still heavier than the 1 px edges. Four sample smoothing stays (D653): eight samples drew thin lines a little more evenly, but double the memory of the view on every screen.
Status: Default
Reason: A fault seen on the nut and bolt sample; the lighter outline also sits better beside the dark edges in the dark themes.

D2766: Planes are quieter and the origin has the triad's colours (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, view review items B3 and B4). A reference plane's outline goes from 1.5 px to 1 px (`plane_look.OUTLINE_WIDTH`), no heavier than an edge of the part, and it and the plane's name now grow with the screen scale; at 200 percent they were half size. The part origin (View, Origins) was the kernel's own: white axes and yellow letters, lost on the light views. `look.style_origin` gives it the theme's three axis colours, as the corner triad has, letters in the view's text colour and axes 1.5 px wide. Plane colours and the 88 percent see-through fill are unchanged.
Status: Default
Reason: The part comes first (DESIGN_LANGUAGE 1.1): reference geometry must not outweigh the part's own edges, and one axis has one colour everywhere.

D2767: `tools/view_review_shots.py` and the pixel test (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, view review). The tool opens the main window on the real screen, since the 3D view is blank offscreen, and saves the view's own picture (`ViewportWidget.dump`) of the sample parts, highlights, a red part, the five display styles, planes and the origin, two previews, the triad and a sketch, in the themes asked for, with enlarged cuts for judging line quality. It is run by hand; no test or CI job needs it (CLAUDE.md section 9 item 8). `tests/ui/test_view_polish.py` checks every value of D2760 to D2766 as a number, a colour or a kernel setting on the offscreen platform. One more test starts `tests/ui/view_pixels_probe.py` on the real screen and reads pixels; it is skipped unless `FDCAD_VIEW_PIXELS=1` is set.
Status: Default
Reason: The view could not be reviewed for want of a way to see it; the next review can run one command.

D2780: A closed part's 3D view is freed at once, in a set order, while its window still exists (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 F1, `docs/VIEW_REVIEW_2026-11-19.md` F1). With one part kept open while others were opened and closed, a view could stop drawing ("wglMakeCurrent() has failed. The handle is invalid"). The cause: closing a tab deleted its Qt widgets, and with them the view's native window, but the Python half of `ViewportWidget` sits in reference cycles, so its kernel view, interactive context and window handle lived on until the garbage collector ran, often several parts later. The kernel then freed the view's drawing context with its window long gone: it could not make that context current, and the clean up ran on whichever view's context was current, a live one. Reading the kernel's own messages per step (`Message_Report`) showed every such error inside a collection, and a live view failing right after one. `ViewportWidget.release` now frees, on the UI thread: first the shown items (`RemoveAll`), then the kernel view (`V3d_View.Remove`, which frees its context while the window is there), then the window handle. It runs once, and the view never starts again. `DocumentTab.release_views` closes the split panes' views first, then the main one, and `close_tab` calls it after the session is closed and before `deleteLater`. A later collection then has no drawing context left to free. A pane's `close_view` also drops its window handle. `tools/view_review_shots.py` no longer runs a collection when a tab is destroyed. Tests: `tests/ui/test_view_release.py` checks the order and the call from `close_tab` offscreen. `tests/ui/view_release_probe.py` opens and closes parts quickly on the real screen, saves the kept view and each new view, and counts every drawing error the kernel reports, also during collections; its test runs with `FDCAD_VIEW_PIXELS=1`. Before the change every run had errors (16 to 40 in 37 checks, and one or two views that drew black); after it, runs of 37, 49 and 73 checks had none.
Status: Default
Reason: The fault is in when the kernel frees a view, not in when Python collects, so the view is freed where the tab is closed; an extra collection only made the race rarer.

D2781: What lies under the cursor is read from each detected owner (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 F2, `docs/VIEW_REVIEW_2026-11-19.md` F2). `ViewportWidget.detected_at` asked the kernel for `DetectedCurrentShape`, which is the whole shape of the shown item: for the part, the part itself, never the face, edge or vertex under the cursor. Its three callers all mean the item under the cursor: Select Other lists faces, edges and vertices nearest first; the view's right click menu selects the nearest one and builds the menu for its kind; Paste on a face (Ctrl drag from the tree) looks for the first flat face. With the whole part, Select Other listed one "Face" that was the part, the right click selected the part, and Paste on a face never found a face. The same call was made in three more places with the same meaning, and they had the same fault: Select Through Faces never found the edge behind a face, picking through a see through body never got past it, and a drag handle never snapped to a vertex or face with Alt. The function is fixed, not the callers: `_detected` reads the shape from each detected owner (`StdSelect_BRepOwner.Shape`, the face, edge or vertex), with whether it belongs to the part; `_detected_on_part` keeps the part's items, nearest first, without repeats or faces hidden for now. `detected_at`, `_edge_through`, `_through_pick` and `_snap_target` use them. Regions keep the kernel's call: each region is a shown item of its own whose whole shape is its face. Tests (`tests/ui/test_view_detect.py`) run offscreen: the view gets a kernel view without a window and the cursor becomes a ray, so the kernel's own picking runs without a graphics card. They check each reader and the three callers in the main window on the bracket sample; all but one failed before the change.
Status: Default
Reason: Every caller means the item under the cursor, so one fix in the function serves them all, and the kernel's owner is where that item is held.

D2790: Fillet and Chamfer never ask for more than the left panel's default width, and their groups sit on tabs (2026-11-19, Phase 7D, owner request on the Mac: "the side bar for setting fillet is too wide, define it in a way it never uses more space than default, rearrange, make extra tabs"). The left panel is 260 px by default and widens itself for a property panel that needs more (D1033). Measured before: 531 px for Fillet and 349 px for Chamfer, and 349 px for every panel with a Favourites box. What was wide: Favourites (three buttons a row, and "New ones start with" beside its list), the fillet assistant (a list and two long buttons in one row, 471 px), Add Feature beside its list, the rule row, Pick Limit beside its tick box, Add Point and Delete Point in one row, the three buttons of an ordered pick list (Partial Edges by Reference), and every drop down as wide as its longest entry. (1) Tabs. `property_panel/tabs.py` holds `PanelTabs`: a tab bar above the scrolling groups and one page of groups per tab. `PropertyPanel.use_tabs` turns it on for a form; a panel that does not call it is as before. Fillet and Chamfer have Main (type, items, face sets, parameters, variable radii), More (Add Edges, Partial Edges, Limits, and any group not named) and Favourites. A form still shows and hides its groups as before; a page only decides whether they are on screen, and a tab whose page has nothing to show is hidden (More, for a face fillet). A new page starts at its top. The Hole Tool's own two tabs, Type and Positions, are a different thing and are unchanged. (2) Add Edges. The three ways to add many edges to a fillet at once (Add Feature, the assistant, the rules) moved out of Items to Fillet into their own group, Add Edges, on More. They still add to the list on Main. (3) Rows. Controls that were side by side are one under the other (`groups.stacked`); Favourites has two buttons a row and its start choice under its words; an ordered pick list has Remove on one row and Move Up and Move Down on the next (this is every ordered pick list, so Loft and Sweep too); the variable radius, edge radius and point rows put the field under its word when both do not fit; the chamfer's Corners word sits above its list, since beside it the word set the column of the whole panel (D2742) and cut the type's name short. (4) Drop downs. `columns.narrow_boxes` lets every drop down of these two panels, and the two of Favourites, be as narrow as 5 letters; the list that drops down keeps the width of its longest entry (as D2699, D2742). After: Fillet needs 223 px and Chamfer 239 px at most, measured on the Mac offscreen. `MainWindow.default_left_width` and `panel_width_needed` name the two numbers. `tests/ui/test_narrow_panels.py` opens both panels in a window, with edges picked, in every type, with every Partial Edges kind, on every tab, with every group open, and fails if one needs more than the default width or if the left panel's width changes. Other panels still widen the left panel when they need to; Favourites no longer makes them.
Status: Default
Reason: The tree and the 3D view should not jump sideways each time a fillet opens; a long panel is easier to use as three short pages than as one wide, long one.

D2791: No tool's panel makes the left panel wider than it is by default (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, owner request on the Mac: "make sure this extra wide panel thing doesn't happen with any feature or tool"; follows D2790, changes D1033 item 2). Before, the left panel widened itself to whatever an open panel asked for. A sweep of every command found 19 tools that asked for more than the default 260 px, up to 336 px: Extrude, Draft, Helix, Hole Tool, Sweep, Contour, Curve Array, Split and others. (1) The rule. `MainWindow._fit_left_panel` never widens the left panel beyond `default_left_width()` for a panel. If the user made the left panel narrower than the default, it still widens to what the panel needs, up to the default, and goes back after. A user who made it wider keeps that. (2) Fitting. `property_panel/narrow.py` holds `fit(root, limit)`. It walks the layouts under a widget and changes a row only where the row is wider than the room it has: a drop down may be narrower than its longest entry (its list keeps its width); a label of several words wraps; the words of a button or a tick box go on two lines (the full words stay as the accessible name and in the `full_text` property); a field goes under its word in a form; a row of controls becomes a column and a grid becomes one column, in reading order. A row that leads with a field icon or a small button keeps its lead beside its field (D2692, D2742); a width a panel set on purpose is not changed. A row that already fits is untouched, so a panel on a wider left panel can look as before, but a change made for a narrow panel stays for as long as that panel is open. `Fitter` runs `fit` again whenever the layout under it changes, so a row that a choice shows is fitted when it shows. The window keeps two: one on the feature panel's groups and one on the stack that holds every other tool's panel (reference geometry, section view and the rest). (3) The lead column. In these panels the shared lead column of D2742 is at most 18 steps (72 px), not 32, and a group no longer moves its fields right for a longer word (`columns.set_narrow`): there is no room, so the field of a longer word goes under it. A panel shown outside the main window, as in most panel tests, is not fitted and keeps the 32 steps. A group is now as tall as its rows need at its width (`Group.sizeHint`): Qt's own hint counts each row as one line, and the group is never taller than its hint, so rows whose field went under its word were squeezed (seen in Sweep, Options). (4) Last resort. The groups of the feature panel may now scroll sideways. Nothing does today, but a row that could not be fitted (one long word on a button) can still be reached. (5) Tests. `tests/ui/test_panel_widths.py` starts every command of the window with nothing, a face, an edge and a sketch selected, opens every group of what shows in the left panel, on every tab, and fails with the name of the command and its three widest controls if it needs more than the default width or if the left panel grew. The slow test also goes through every choice of every drop down of each panel. `tests/ui/test_narrow_fit.py` checks each rule of `fit` by itself. Not covered: the Variables tab still asks for 380 px (D1034); it is a tab of the left panel, not a tool's panel. The fitting works on the sizes Qt reports at run time, so it holds for any font, scale and platform; the sweep was run on the Mac offscreen.
Status: Default
Reason: The tree and the 3D view should stay where they are whatever tool opens; one rule in one place holds for panels added later, where sixty panels laid out by hand would not.

D2800: A drop down with no room for its entry ends it with an ellipsis (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, Windows look review of D2790 and D2791 on a real screen at 100, 150 and 200 percent). Qt draws the entry of a drop down up to the edge of the box and cuts it there, in the middle of a letter: at the left panel's default width Sweep showed "Sketch prof" and Extrude "Square to the sketc". `property_panel/elide.py` holds `elide_when_cut`: an event filter draws the box as Qt does, with the entry (or the placeholder) elided at its right end, and answers the tooltip with the whole entry, followed by the box's own tooltip. It does nothing while the entry fits, and nothing for an editable drop down, whose text field scrolls. `columns.let_narrow` turns it on, so it holds for exactly the drop downs that may be narrower than their longest entry: those of a panel fitted to the default width (D2791), those beside a word (D2742) and those of Favourites. The list that drops down keeps the width of its longest entry. One filter object serves every box. The style sheet style draws the entry itself, so a proxy style under it would never be asked; that is why it is a filter on the box. The sweep of every command (`tests/ui/test_panel_widths.py`) now also fails for a drop down on show whose entry is cut and not elided. On the Windows screen at 100 percent, after D2801 and D2807, four entries of the nine tools looked at are still elided (two of Loft's constraints, one of Sweep's twist choices and "An edge picked in the view..." in Extrude), and the long placeholders ("Choose a sketch with one circle").
Status: Default
Reason: A word cut in the middle looks broken; an ellipsis says there is more, and the tooltip gives it.

D2801: In a panel fitted to the default width a long word no longer sets the lead column, and the drop downs of a group with a long word sit under their words (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, same review; changes D2791 item 3 and keeps D2742 wherever the words fit). (1) The column. D2791 capped the shared lead column at 18 steps (72 px), and a word longer than that set the column to the cap. In Sweep "Section values" did so: every field that follows an icon started 72 px in, to line up with a field that did not line up with them anyway, and the drop downs of Profile and Path had 74 px for their entry. A word wider than the cap now does not count (`columns.column_width`). Sweep's fields after an icon start one icon cell in. (2) The cap is 8 letters of average width (`NARROW_WORD_LETTERS`, 48 px in Segoe UI at 100 percent), not a number of spacing steps. A step follows the height of the font; the room a word takes follows its width. The font Qt falls back to offscreen on Windows is as wide as it is tall (13 px a letter), so "Along" was 65 px there, the drop down went under it, and `test_extrude_panel_has_one_field_column` failed with fields at 37 and 102 px. (3) Drop downs after a word are decided group by group (`columns.settle_under`). When the word of one of them is wider than the cap, every drop down of that group that follows a word goes under its word, flush with it and as wide as the group: Sweep's Options, the Hole Tool, Loft's Centerline. In a group whose words all fit the cap they stay beside their words in the one column of D2742: Along in Extrude. Before, each row was left to its form, which puts a field under its word only when the two do not fit, so one group had drop downs beside words, under words and after icons, at three left edges. Once under, a drop down stays there while its panel is open. The word of a drop down that sits under it does not count for the column. (4) How. A form puts a field under its word when the two do not fit side by side, so `narrow.boxes_under_words` gives such a drop down a least width of the fit limit, and `fit` takes it back to the width of its row. A form also lines a field it wrapped up with the fields beside their words, when the field asks for no more than that column; with no such field in the form, that column starts one gap in, which left the drop down under "Along" 8 px to the right of everything else. `columns.ask_for_row` has the drop down ask for the whole row (through its least number of letters), and the form then starts it at the left edge. (5) Not changed: a text field stays beside its word whatever the length of the word ("Section values", "Head Clearance"), in the label column of its own form; a drop down after an icon stays after its icon and elides (D2800); a panel shown outside the main window keeps D2742 as it was. Tests: `tests/ui/test_narrow_fit.py` (the column, beside, under) and `tests/ui/test_panel_look.py` (Sweep and the Hole Tool in the window).
Status: Default
Reason: The one column the owner approved is kept wherever the words are short enough to lead it. Where they are not, the drop downs of a group all look the same and show their entries whole, which reads better than a column kept by cutting every entry.

D2802: Fitting order: a row is stacked before its controls are cut, and words that must break give lines of about one length (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, same review; changes the order of D2791 item 2). (1) `narrow._fit_row` let each control of a row give way first, so a drop down was cut and the words of a button went on two lines, and only then was the row stacked. Split had "FDCAD Par" beside "Save / Bodies" and Loft had "Choose a" beside Add Profile. Now the labels of a row wrap first; if that is not enough the row becomes a column of whole controls: the list at the full width and the button under it, as Fillet's Add Edges was laid out by hand (D2790). A row with an icon or an icon button in it stays a row and its controls give way as before, since an icon on a line of its own looks lost. (2) Words that must break (`narrow._wrapped`) take as few lines as before, but of the breaks with that many lines the one whose longest line is shortest is taken: "Keep size when / the type changes", "Pick operation / from where it sits", "Other angle below / the neutral plane". Filling the first line left one word on the second ("... the type / changes"). No label is shortened. On the Windows screen at the default width six buttons and tick boxes of all tools are still broken, each at a sensible word; "Add Faces That Need Draft" fits on one line there. (3) A number box may be as narrow as its room, like a list. It asks for room for its longest value (1000000.0000); in a wide font that was more than a group has, and 3D Sketch needed 316 px offscreen on Windows, where the sweep of every command had never run to the end.
Status: Default
Reason: A column of whole controls reads better than a row of cut ones, and two lines of about one length read better than a full line and a leftover word.

D2803: The tabs of Fillet and Chamfer fill their row; Favourites has no button alone; Add Edges reads as three ways (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, same review; follows D2790). (1) The look of the tabs is FDCAD's tab row for inside a panel: muted words, the chosen one in the text colour with a 2 px cobalt line under it, as the Hole Tool's Type and Positions and the pages of Preferences (`QTabBar` in `themes/style.py`). The pill belongs to the left panel's own tabs and the command tabs, one level up (DESIGN_LANGUAGE 3.1 and 3.2), so nothing was drawn differently. What was off: the three tabs kept their own widths and stopped two thirds of the way across. They now share the width of the panel (`setExpanding(True)`), as the Hole Tool's two tabs do and as OK and Cancel do above them; with two tabs (a face fillet has no More) each has half. (2) Favourites, in every panel: seven buttons two a row left Rename alone on the last row. Apply acts on the name chosen in the list, so it sits under the list at the full width; then Save and Update, Rename and Delete, Export and Import. (3) Add Edges on More holds three ways to add edges (a feature, the convex or concave edges of a scope, a rule), each a list and its buttons. They stand 16 px apart with 4 px inside each. Before, the rows of the group were 8 px apart like the rows of any group, and the nine controls read as one column. No caption was added. (4) Chamfer's Flip stays in the lead column when Angle Distance hides the list beside it; it stood alone in the middle of the row.
Status: Default
Reason: The tabs, the Favourites box and the More tab are seen every time a fillet is made; each now looks laid out on purpose.

D2804: The tables of tool panels and the Hole Tool's bolt circle fit the default width (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, same review). (1) The X and Y columns of the Hole Tool's points table share the width of the table (`QHeaderView.Stretch`). At 100 px each they were a little wider than the room, and the table showed a sideways scroll bar: the one sideways scroll bar found in the panels looked at. The sweep of every command (`tests/ui/test_panel_widths.py`) now fails for any table on show whose columns are wider than it is. It found three more, fixed the same way: the points of Curve Through Points (X, Y, Z), the rows of Table Pattern (the tick column takes what it needs, X and Y share the rest) and the curves of Vent (the name takes what it needs, the role has the rest, and its drop down elides, D2800). (2) The bolt circle's two fields share a row and Make has the next. With all three in one row the start angle had room for "St..." of its placeholder. Each field is at least as wide as its placeholder.
Status: Default
Reason: Nothing in a panel should scroll sideways or show two letters of a word.

D2805: A part's tab has no least width of its own, so the left panel opens at its default width in any window (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, same review). Three width tests failed offscreen on Windows with the left panel at 234 px where its default is 286 px. Where the 3D view cannot run (Qt's offscreen platform, a display without the graphics FDCAD needs), a part's tab shows the message `NO_3D_VIEW`. It was one line of 93 letters, so its width was the least width of the tab: 1209 px in the font Qt falls back to offscreen on Windows. The window grew past the size it was given and Qt took the difference from the left panel, down to its least width of 18 em. The Mac's font is narrower, so the message fitted and the tests passed there. The message now wraps and sits in the middle of the view. Two things showed once the window kept its size. (1) `test_draw_dimension_trim_offset_and_exit`: the sketch sweep's click helper worked the point out again after one turn of the event loop; a tool's panel is fitted the turn after its layout changes (D2791), so the view got its size one turn later and the Offset click went to where the line had been. The helper now waits 5 ms, twice. Nothing a user does depends on this: the test sets the size of the view by hand. (2) The arrows of a tab row that scrolls, D2807.
Status: Default
Reason: The cause was a message that could not wrap, not the tests: with it gone they pass unchanged, in a window of 1200 px.

D2806: A button is found by its words through `narrow.words_of`, and the fitter breaks the words a button has now (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, same review). (1) A button or tick box whose words the fitter put on two lines has a line break in its `text()`. `words_of` gives the words on one line. A search of tests and tools for controls of the main window found by their words gave five places: `tools/test_plan_run/numeric.py` and `shots.py` (a tick box found by its words), `sweep_app.py` and `refs.py` (words written to a log) and `tests/ui/test_manufacturing_ui.py` (the words of the Fix button). None failed on the Windows screen, where six controls are broken and none of them is looked up; all five now ask `words_of`. The many other comparisons of `text()` in the tests are of labels, the status bar, menu items and panels outside the window, which the fitter never changes. (2) The fitter kept a button's first words in the `full_text` property and broke those again at every later fit. A panel that gave a broken button new words (the Fix button of Manufacturing Check, a count) got the old words back, and the accessible name stayed the old one. It now breaks the words on show, and at each fit brings the property and the name it gave up to date. A name the panel gave is left alone.
Status: Default
Reason: One helper says how to find a control by its words, so the next test does not have to know about the line break.

D2807: A drop down gives its width to its entry, and the arrows of a tab row that scrolls are 24 px wide (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, same review; two rules of the style sheet). (1) `QComboBox` had a right padding of 5 steps (20 px) to keep the entry clear of the arrow.
