Qt takes the arrow's own 16 px off as well, so between the entry and the arrow there were 20 px that nothing used: a drop down 200 px wide showed 156 px of its entry. The entry now has the same padding on both sides and the arrow keeps its 16 px: 170 px of 200. Every drop down of the app shows 14 px more of its entry, and one that sizes itself to its entries is 14 px narrower. At the left panel's default width "Square to the sketch" fits beside Along in Extrude, and three of Loft's four long constraints fit after their icon. A number box keeps the padding, which is the room of its two arrows. (2) The two arrows a tab row shows when its tabs do not fit were 12 px wide, half the 24 px of U3.3. The Fillet tabs show them when the user makes the left panel narrow, and the command tabs show them in a narrow window. `test_window_controls_meet_the_minimum_size` saw them as soon as the test window kept its 1200 px (D2805). `QTabBar::scroller` is 12 steps wide, 24 px for each arrow.
Status: Default
Reason: Room that was reserved twice is better spent on the entry; a control to click is 24 px wide everywhere.

D2808: What the Windows look review of the narrow panels saw, and what it left alone (2026-11-20, Phase 7D; record of the review behind D2800 to D2807). How: FDCAD was run on the real Windows platform, not offscreen, on a 1680 by 1050 screen with `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` at 1, 1.5 and 2, with the sample enclosure open. Fillet and Chamfer on each tab in every type and every Partial Edges kind, and Extrude, Draft, Sweep, Loft, Hole Tool (both tabs), Helix and Split, with every group open and every choice of every drop down tried, were grabbed to PNG and checked by eye and by a script: a control past the right edge, a sideways scroll bar, words or an entry wider than their control, the width of the left panel. Seen at all three scales alike, since Qt scales the whole layout: the left panel kept its default width (264 px on Windows: 22 em of Segoe UI) while every panel opened and closed; no control was cut off at the right; one sideways scroll bar (D2804); cut drop down entries in Extrude, Sweep, Loft, Helix and Split (D2800, D2801, D2807); "Save / Bodies" in Split and an orphan word in two tick boxes (D2802). Six before and after pairs at 100 percent are in `docs/screenshots/panel_width_2026-11-20/`. Left alone, and why: (1) At 200 percent this screen is 840 by 525 logical pixels. The window is then so short that the hint card at the top of a panel is squeezed by 6 to 12 px when a message shows under it. No width is involved, and a screen that is used at 200 percent is taller. (2) Empty rows: a hidden note (the Hole Tool's fit note and drill name, a row of Draft) still takes the gap of a row, so a group can end with a blank line. It was so before D2790. (3) The label of Split's list of results reads "keep", the name of its field; a label is not this review's to write. (4) In Fillet's Variable Radii the fields of "Point 1 at (%)" and of "Edge 1 point 1" start 8 px apart: two forms, each with its own label column. (5) The offscreen font on Windows is so wide that many more words break there than on any real screen (62 controls against 6); the tests hold there, the look is not judged there.
Status: Default
Reason: The next person to look at these panels should know what was checked, on what screen, and what was seen and not changed.

D2810: Every drop down of a fitted panel ends a cut entry with an ellipsis; one test count follows the font (2026-11-20, Mac run on 42770bab). Two tests failed on the Mac only. (1) The slow panel sweep (`test_no_choice_of_any_panel_is_wider_than_the_default`): in Linear Pattern, with Front Plane or Right Plane chosen, the entry was cut short without an ellipsis. D2800 gave the ellipsis to the drop downs the fitter makes narrower (`columns.let_narrow`). This one was never made narrower: it takes the width of its row, and in the Mac's font "Front Plane" is wider than that, where in the Windows font it fits. `narrow.elide_all` now gives the ellipsis of D2800 to every drop down under a fitted panel that is not editable, each time the fitter runs. Nothing changes while an entry fits. `tests/ui/test_narrow_fit.py` has a drop down the fitter leaves alone and checks that it elides. (2) `test_drop_downs_under_long_words_fill_their_group` asked for three drop downs under their words in the Hole Tool. A drop down goes under its word only in a group with a word wider than the lead column (D2801), and that depends on the font: three in the Windows font, two in the Mac's. The test asks for two or more; what it checks about each of them is unchanged. No change to the app for (2).
Status: Default
Reason: Whether an entry fits depends on the font, so the ellipsis cannot depend on which drop downs one font happened to need narrowed.

D2811: The panel width sweep leaves out the commands that only show a dialog (2026-11-20, Mac run on 42770bab). One of three full `pytest` runs on the Mac ended with a segmentation fault in `tests/ui/test_panel_widths.py::test_no_panel_is_wider_than_the_default`, and so did one of six runs of that file after `test_panel_presets.py`; twelve runs of the file by itself had none. The macOS crash report is the same each time: a `QDialog` that holds a tab widget, a scroll area, a group box and a list is deleted by a deferred delete, and PySide faults in `Shiboken::Object::destroy` while the list's items are destroyed. That is the shape of the Preferences dialog. The sweep started every command four times, once per kind of selection, and deleted what it opened at once, as the app sweep does (`sweep_support.pump`). A dialog has nothing in the left panel to measure, so the 14 commands that only show one are now left out (`DIALOGS` in the test file), and a new command of that kind is started once and the test then asks for it to be added. After that, five runs after `test_panel_presets.py` and the full suite had no fault. Not found: why PySide faults there, and whether it can happen when a person closes Preferences in the app. It needs other tests to have run first, it was seen on the Mac only, and it is the kind of fault D639 dealt with (objects with Python halves destroyed at the wrong moment). The crash report is `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/python3.13-2026-11-20-035507.ips` on the owner's Mac. This is for the manager session to look at.
Status: Default
Reason: A test of panel widths should not be the place where a rare fault in closing dialogs ends the whole run; the fault itself is written down, not hidden.

D2840: New pressed fills in Light Gray, Beige and Dark Grey, so coloured text on a selected row under the pointer reads at 4.5:1 (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, UI review item P11, approved by the owner on 2026-11-20, colour change included). The pressed fill is also what a selected row shows while the pointer is on it (`QTreeView::item:selected:hover`). D2740 measured coloured text on it below 4.5:1 in three themes and left the colour to the owner (D745). The fix is the `pressed` token of those three themes and nothing else: no text colour changed, `selected` and `hover` did not change, and Stealth, which passed, keeps `#1C376B`. Light Gray `#C5D6FF` to `#D1DFFF`: accent 4.16 to 4.53, danger 4.49 to 4.89. Beige `#C3D2F0` to `#D1DFFD`: accent 3.98 to 4.52, "ok" green 4.38 to 4.97. Dark Grey `#2C4886` to `#1B3980`: muted 3.95 to 4.83, accent 3.70 to 4.53, danger 4.00 to 4.90, error 4.06 to 4.96. The lowest coloured text on a pressed fill is now 4.52 (accent, Beige) and plain text on it is 9.30 or more. How the values were chosen: contrast is a matter of lightness only, and the accent, which was not to change, sets the limit. Accent text on `selected` is 4.70 to 4.79, so a fill that keeps it at 4.5 can be only about 1.4 to 2.2 L* past the selected fill (it was 5.3 to 7.1). A fill moved straight toward the selected fill until it passed (`#D4DFF4` in Beige, `#243B70` in Dark Grey) could hardly be told from it: 1.9 and 1.7 in CIE76, where about 2.3 can just be seen. So each new fill takes the step in lightness the limit allows and makes up the rest in strength of colour, on the hue the fill already had (within 2 degrees): it is a colour close to the old one that passes and is still a clear step from `selected`. By the same measure pressed against selected is 3.94 in Light Gray (the blue channel is already full there, so there is no more colour to add), 6.11 in Beige, 12.88 in Dark Grey and 10.48 in Stealth. A selected row under the pointer is quieter than it was; it is still a different row. The same token is the fill of a pressed button, a pressed tab, a pressed tick box, a checked tool button under the pointer and the menu bar's open item: there it follows `hover`, from which it is 13.7 or more apart, so a press still shows. Bookkeeping: `test_coloured_text_on_the_pressed_fill_meets_its_limit` lost its strict expected failure and passes; `test_the_old_pressed_fills_were_short` runs the same check on the old fills and finds the eight pairs of P11, so the check is known to bite; `test_a_pressed_row_is_not_a_selected_row` holds the other side: pressed is at least `contrast.STATE` (3.45 in CIE76, one and a half times what can just be seen) from selected, on the far side of it from the panel, and twice that from hover, so a later change cannot pass the contrast test by making the two fills one. `contrast.difference` (CIE76) is new for it, because `ratio` sees lightness only. Not touched: `src/fdcad/ui/viewport` and the view's theme tokens, which another session is working on. Pictures: `docs/screenshots/ui_leftovers_2026-11-20/01_pressed_fill_*.png`, the sheet of every row text colour on every row fill, Light and Dark, before and after.
Status: Owner approved
Reason: A selected row is where a user reads state colours (a suppressed or failed feature), so the fill under them must not cost the text its contrast; and the smallest change that does that is one token in three themes.

D2841: No panel shows the bare name of a field; Split's list is labelled "Keep" (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, point 3 of D2808, approved by the owner on 2026-11-20). A field of a body tool form takes its label from `strings_phase3.LABELS` and a choice its words from `CHOICES`; one with no entry showed its own name. Split's list of results read "keep". A scan of every form and a sweep of every panel found six more: "exclude" (Intersect's list of regions), "angle2" (Circular Pattern, Direction 2), "form" and its choice "pin" (Hinge), the choice "axis" (Move Face and Offset Face, Turn about) and the choice "flat" (sheet metal Gusset, Profile, whose two words had been put in the table of labels). They read Keep, Keep, Angle, Type, Pin, An axis and Flat now, and Keep, Keep and Type have a tooltip that says what they do. Why "Keep" and not "Bodies to keep": Split's other labels are Trim tools, Bodies and Tolerance, one short word or two in the panel's one column (D2742). "Bodies to keep" was tried on screen: it is wider than that column may be in a panel fitted to the default width (D2801), so the Cut button, the list and Save Bodies started 29 px to the right of the fields of the group above and lost that width. "Keep" sits in the column, the list starts where the other fields start, and with the ticks it reads as a sentence: keep Body 1, Body 2. The group's title, Resulting Bodies, and the hint under Cut say the rest. Hinge's "Type" follows Move Face, whose first drop down is Type; "Hinge type" would put the drop down under its word (D2801) in a group named Hinge. Two tests keep it so. `test_every_field_of_every_form_has_a_label_and_every_choice_a_name` reads the form tables, sheet metal included, with no window. The sweep of `tests/ui/test_panel_widths.py` (D2791), which opens every tool's panel, now also looks at every label, button, tick box and short drop down on show for a bare name (`tests/ui/panel_checks.py`: a word all in small letters, with or without underscores and figures; a label of FDCAD starts with a capital, and units are let through). The sweep runs once and three tests read what it found, so the quick suite is no slower; the slow sweep does the same for every choice of every drop down.
Status: Owner approved
Reason: A field's name is written for the code. A label that is that name tells the user nothing, and the next one should fail a test the day it is added.

D2842: A note with no words and a holder with no rows take no row of a group (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, point 2 of D2808, approved by the owner on 2026-11-20). D2808 saw groups that end with a blank line. The cause was not a hidden widget: a form skips the row of a hidden widget. It was a widget on show with nothing in it. (1) A label with no words is still a line high, and its row keeps the 8 px gap of a row: the Hole Tool's fit note at the end of Options (23 px), Draft's note under Add Faces That Need Draft (31 px in the middle of Faces to Draft) and Shell's answer under Check Walls (23 px at the end of Parameters). They are a `groups.Note` now: a label that wraps its words and hides itself while it has none, so its row comes and goes with its words. (2) A bare widget that only holds the rows of a form has no height when the form is empty, but its own row in the group keeps the gap: Shell's Multi Thickness before a face is picked (8 px at the end) and Fillet's Variable Radii with no control point (16 px between Set All and Add Point) or no edge (8 px at the end). `groups.show_if_filled` hides such a holder while its form has no row. Nothing else changed: no row moved and no gap of a row with something in it is smaller. The Hole Tool's drill name, which D2808 also named, was already right, since it is hidden while it has no name. The check is `panel_checks.blank_rows`: in every group on show it finds the stretches no control with content covers (a label needs words or a picture, a bare holder does not count) and reports one at the start, one of the row gap plus 4 px or more between two rows, and one of 4 px or more at the end. The sweep of D2841 runs it on every panel, and the slow sweep on every choice. Seen by that check and left: in the offscreen font, which is far wider than a real one (D2808 point 5), the label "Instances to skip" of Curve Array breaks in two lines, and after another row hides Qt lays it out one line high until the next change, with the height of its second line at the end of the group. No row is empty there and no real font breaks that label, so the check lays the rows of a group out again before it measures.
Status: Owner approved
Reason: An empty line at the end of a card reads as something missing. A note should cost a row when it has something to say and not before.

D2843: The two sets of fields of Fillet's Variable Radii share one column (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, point 4 of D2808, approved by the owner on 2026-11-20). The positions of the control points ("Point 1 at (%)") and the radii ("Edge 1 point 1") are the rows of two forms, with Add Point and Delete Point between them, and a form sizes the column of its own words. So the fields of the two sets started 8 px apart. `fillet_form.share_columns` gives the words of both forms the width of the widest of them, each time the rows are filled, so every field of both sets starts at one x. It gives the fields one least width too: a form puts a field under its word when the two do not fit side by side, and it decides that from the field's least width, which is not the same for a length and for a plain number. Without it the radii went under their words in a narrow panel and the positions stayed beside theirs. The two forms stay two forms, so Add Point and Delete Point stay between the positions and the radii, and no label changed. Not done: lining these fields up with the two rows of the group that begin with an icon (the number of control points, the transition). Those follow the panel's one column (D2742), which in a panel fitted to the default width leaves out words as long as these (D2801).
Status: Owner approved
Reason: Two columns 8 px apart in one card look like a mistake, and the rows of one group should be laid out by one rule.

D2844: Fillet's Variable Radii has rows for every edge again (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, found while testing D2843). Since TR133 (D1403) the rows of radii were counted by the control points, not by the edges: `FilletForm._fill_rows` reused the name `count`, the number of edges, for the number of control points. Three edges with one control point showed the start, point and end radius of Edge 1 only, and with no control point, the default, no radius at all; one edge with two control points showed rows for an Edge 2 that was not picked. The edges without rows were built at the main radius, since the kernel reads `vr_<k>_start` and `vr_<k>_end` per edge and falls back to `radius`. The control points have their own name now and the rows follow the edges. `test_fillet_variable_radii_has_rows_for_every_edge` failed before. The test of TR133 used one edge and two points, where the two counts could not be told apart.
Status: Default
Reason: Variable Size is there to give each edge its own radii, and the panel could not do that for more than as many edges as it had control points.
D2820: Eight smoothing samples below 150 percent, where the graphics card has room (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 P1, `docs/VIEW_REVIEW_2026-11-19.md` P1; changes D653's four samples for some views, the owner approved closing the six proposals). Measured first, on the review PC (1680 by 1050 at 100 percent, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti, 4 GiB) with `tools/view_smoothing_measure.py`, one process per setting, the screen's frame lock off, the nut and bolt turning. Graphics memory more than with no samples: a view of 1176 by 597 pixels took 31 MiB with 4 samples and 77 MiB with 8; one of 1416 by 728 took 52 and 119 (45 and 111 with an empty part). That is 16 bytes for each sample of each pixel: the kernel keeps two smoothed buffers a view, each with 4 bytes of colour and 4 of depth. So eight samples cost 64 bytes a pixel more than four: 63 MiB more on the larger view, and each open part has a view. The process's own working set did not move (382 MB with an empty part, 410 MB with the nut and bolt, at every setting); what it has committed went from 873 to 923 MB. Frame time, mean of 300 frames: 1.41, 2.13 and 2.95 ms with 0, 4 and 8 samples on the smaller view and 1.62, 2.52 and 3.84 ms on the larger, the slowest twentieth 4.40 ms. Then the lines, with `tools/view_line_steadiness.py`: a box in Wireframe from three sides, and for each slanted edge the ink of every pixel column across it. A steady line has the same ink all along; the figure is the spread (standard deviation over mean), Light and Dark. At 100 percent 0.216 and 0.132 with 4 samples, 0.154 and 0.095 with 8. At 125 percent 0.219 and 0.120, then 0.145 and 0.075. At 150 percent 0.110 and 0.118, then 0.106 and 0.072. At 200 percent 0.130 and 0.081, then 0.085 and 0.062. Shaded With Edges at 100 percent 0.065 and 0.063, then 0.054 and 0.060. So below 150 percent eight samples draw a thin line a quarter to a third more evenly, which shows in Wireframe and the hidden line styles as less of a beaded look (pair 01 of the screenshots); on the edges of a shaded part the gain is small. From 150 percent, lines are one and a half pixels wide or more and four samples already give about what eight give at 100 percent, while a view has 2.25 to 4 times the pixels to pay for. The rule (`look.msaa_samples`): eight samples when the screen scale is under 1.5, the driver tells the card's memory, and the four extra samples cost the view no more than a sixteenth of that memory (`MSAA_FINE_CARD_SHARE`); four samples otherwise. A 2 GiB card gives a view up to a whole Full HD screen eight samples, a 4 GiB card up to a QHD screen, an 8 GiB card a 4K screen. The kernel reads the memory from the driver (`look.card_memory`, asked once): NVIDIA and AMD cards and the Mac tell it, most built in graphics do not, and those keep four. That is on purpose: the measurement speaks for a card with memory of its own, and on built in graphics the buffers come out of the machine's memory, which PLAN 11.2 budgets (the plan's Windows baseline is such a laptop, and the Mac draws at 200 percent). `ViewportWidget._apply_smoothing` sets the number when the view starts and when its size or screen changes; a large part still turns with none (TR214) and gets its own number back. The extra panes of a split view keep four. Save Image draws into buffers of the picture's size, so a picture takes the samples the rule gives for that size, and never more than the view has. Not adopted: eight samples for every view at 100 percent, which is what the proposal said. It would double the buffers on the machines the budgets are written for, with no measurement there. Tests: `tests/ui/test_view_proposals.py` (the rule, the cost model against the measured figures, the view's use of it) and `tests/perf/test_view_smoothing.py` (the baseline machines keep four; the cost stays under a sixteenth of the card). `tests/perf` passes as before: its budgets measure the process offscreen, where no buffer exists. With `FDCAD_VIEW_PIXELS=1` a test measures the cost and the frame time again on the screen it runs on.
D2820: Eight smoothing samples below 150 percent, where the graphics card has room (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 P1, `docs/VIEW_REVIEW_2026-11-19.md` P1; changes D653's four samples for some views, the owner approved closing the six proposals). Measured first, on the review PC (1680 by 1050 at 100 percent, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti, 4 GiB) with `tools/view_smoothing_measure.py`, one process per setting, the screen's frame lock off, the nut and bolt turning. Graphics memory more than with no samples: a view of 1176 by 597 pixels took 31 MiB with 4 samples and 77 MiB with 8; one of 1416 by 728 took 52 and 119 (45 and 111 with an empty part). That is 16 bytes for each sample of each pixel: the kernel keeps two smoothed buffers a view, each with 4 bytes of colour and 4 of depth. So eight samples cost 64 bytes a pixel more than four: 63 MiB more on the larger view, and each open part has a view. The process's own working set did not move (382 MB with an empty part, 410 MB with the nut and bolt, at every setting); what it has committed went from 873 to 923 MB. Frame time, mean of 300 frames: 1.41, 2.13 and 2.95 ms with 0, 4 and 8 samples on the smaller view and 1.62, 2.52 and 3.84 ms on the larger, the slowest twentieth 4.40 ms. Then the lines, with `tools/view_line_steadiness.py`: a box in Wireframe from three sides, and for each slanted edge the ink of every pixel column across it. A steady line has the same ink all along; the figure is the spread (standard deviation over mean), Light and Dark. At 100 percent 0.216 and 0.132 with 4 samples, 0.154 and 0.095 with 8. At 125 percent 0.219 and 0.120, then 0.145 and 0.075. At 150 percent 0.110 and 0.118, then 0.106 and 0.072. At 200 percent 0.130 and 0.081, then 0.085 and 0.062. Shaded With Edges at 100 percent 0.065 and 0.063, then 0.054 and 0.060. So below 150 percent eight samples draw a thin line a quarter to a third more evenly, which shows in Wireframe and the hidden line styles as less of a beaded look (pair 01 of the screenshots); on the edges of a shaded part the gain is small. From 150 percent, lines are one and a half pixels wide or more and four samples already give about what eight give at 100 percent, while a view has 2.25 to 4 times the pixels to pay for. The rule (`look.msaa_samples`): eight samples when the screen scale is under 1.5, the driver tells the card's memory, and the four extra samples cost the view no more than a sixteenth of that memory (`MSAA_FINE_CARD_SHARE`); four samples otherwise. A 2 GiB card gives a view up to a whole Full HD screen eight samples, a 4 GiB card up to a QHD screen, an 8 GiB card a 4K screen. The kernel reads the memory from the driver (`look.card_memory`, asked once): NVIDIA and AMD cards tell it and most built in graphics do not; the Mac is not asked, since its graphics memory is the machine's own. Those keep four. That is on purpose: the measurement speaks for a card with memory of its own, and on built in graphics the buffers come out of the machine's memory, which PLAN 11.2 budgets (the plan's Windows baseline is such a laptop, and the Mac draws at 200 percent). `ViewportWidget._apply_smoothing` sets the number when the view starts and when its size or screen changes; a large part still turns with none (TR214) and gets its own number back. The extra panes of a split view keep four. Save Image draws into buffers of the picture's size, so a picture takes the samples the rule gives for that size, and never more than the view has. Not adopted: eight samples for every view at 100 percent, which is what the proposal said. It would double the buffers on the machines the budgets are written for, with no measurement there. Tests: `tests/ui/test_view_proposals.py` (the rule, the cost model against the measured figures, the view's use of it) and `tests/perf/test_view_smoothing.py` (the baseline machines keep four; the cost stays under a sixteenth of the card). `tests/perf` passes as before: its budgets measure the process offscreen, where no buffer exists. With `FDCAD_VIEW_PIXELS=1` a test measures the cost and the frame time again on the screen it runs on.
Status: Default
Reason: The gain is real but small, so it is taken only where it was measured to be cheap; a rule that reads the card keeps every machine the budgets name exactly as it was.

D2821: A highlight has a rim: a thin line in the view's ground colour beside its outline (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 P2; follows D2764). The selection and pre-selection colours read at 3:1 on the view, and a part can have any colour. On a red part (`#C0392B`) the burnt orange outline was 1.1:1 and the tint over the face came out nearly the outline's own colour, so a selected face was all but unmarked. The outline of what is selected and of what is under the cursor now has a line 1 px wide on each side of it (`look.RIM_WIDTH`, times the screen scale) in the plate colour of the theme: white in Light and Beige, black in Dark and Stealth (`look.rim_colour` takes the plate colour or the view's text colour, whichever stands out more from the highlight; in the four themes that is the plate colour). The outline is 5.9:1 or more against its rim, so it has the same strong neighbour on every part, and on the red part the rim itself is 5.4:1 in the light themes, where the outline was 1.1:1. On red, orange (`#D9731A`) and yellow (`#E3B81C`) parts one of the two lines is 3:1 or more against the part in every theme; on a part of any brightness, lit faces included, never under 2.4:1, with the two lines 5.9:1 or more from each other. It is drawn on every part, also the grey one: a rule that turned it on by the part's colour would have to know the colour of each face (imported and painted faces have their own), and a look that changes with the part is harder to learn. On the grey part it is a faint light line in the light themes and reads as one more edge in the dark ones (compared on screen with a rim in the text colour, which made the outline heavy). How: `viewport/rim.py` draws the same edges again as lines, wider than the outline, in the part's own layer; the kernel draws highlights after that layer, so the outline lies on top and the rim shows on both sides. An item in a layer of its own under the Top layer, and one in the Top layer at the lowest priority, both hid the outline, so the part's layer it is. The rim is never picked, takes no part in the hidden line pass, and has no kernel curves across curved faces (D2823). The selection's rim follows `selection_changed`; the hover's is set after each look under the cursor, in the main view and the split panes, and the view is drawn once more only when the face under the cursor changes. Vertices have none. Not changed: the highlight colours, widths, tint and layers (D651, D1094, D2764).
Status: Default
Reason: U1.4 asks that selection read on any face. One line cannot contrast with every part colour; an outline that brings its own ground does, and costs one thin line.

D2822: The corner triad grows with the screen, and its click areas with it (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 P3; follows D1600 and D2766). The kernel draws the triad at a size in device pixels, so at 200 percent it was half size while everything round it had grown. `look.show_triad` now asks for `TRIAD_SCALE` times the screen scale and sets the letters to 16 px times the scale (they were the kernel's 16 px at any scale). `viewport/triad.py` holds the kernel's numbers at 100 percent and multiplies every one by the scale: the centre (the kernel puts it `TRIAD_SCALE` times 500 pixels from the left and bottom edges, cut to a whole pixel: 35, 52 and 70 at 100, 150 and 200 percent, `triad.centre`), the arrow length of 26 px, the 7 px of room round an arrow and the 5 px at the centre. `ViewportWidget._triad_axis` passes its scale, and the triad is shown again when the window moves to a screen of another scale. Read from a real view at 100, 125, 150 and 200 percent: the arrows reach 21 to 22 px at 100 percent in the isometric view at every scale, and every pixel of an arrow beyond the first third picks that arrow. Tests: the click areas at 1, 1.5 and 2, a click at the old place missing the larger triad, and the kernel's own triad (scale, letter height, offset) on a view without a window.
Status: Default
Reason: A thing to click must not shrink as the screen gets finer (U3.3), and where it is drawn and where it is clicked have to come from the same numbers.

D2823: Wireframe draws real edges only (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 P4; follows D2761). The kernel draws one curve of its own each way across every curved face: a ring round the middle of a hole, a line along a fillet, in a faint grey and as a coarse polygon. They are no edges of the part, and on fillets they read as edges that are not there. The number is now none: for the context (`look.real_edges_only`) and for each item that has line settings of its own, which is every item given a colour before it is shown (`look.drop_face_curves`: the part through `style_part`, a body shown as wireframe by itself, the other bodies of Isolate, the outline preview, the rim of D2821, the layers of the print tools). Wireframe now shows the edges the shaded view draws on its faces, in the same colour and width as the seen lines of the two hidden line styles (a test holds the three together). Not done: the outline of curved faces, which the proposal also asked for. A shaft in Wireframe is its circles and one seam line, with no line down its sides, as before (the kernel's curves were not outlines either). The hidden line styles have those outlines because the kernel works them out again for every frame, on the UI thread: measured with `tools/view_smoothing_measure.py`, a frame takes 9 ms on the enclosure, 77 ms on the nut and bolt and 179 ms on the 200 feature part, where Wireframe takes 2 ms on each. Drawing Wireframe that way would put it under 30 frames a second on a 200 feature part (PLAN 11.2 budget 6), so it stays a still drawing. Outlines worked out off the UI thread when the view comes to rest are IDEAS item 86, with the frame times of the hidden line styles.
Status: Default
Reason: A wireframe should show the part's edges and nothing else; the outlines would cost the one display style that is always fast.

D2824: Sketches, reference curves and marks grow with the screen (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 P5; follows D2766). Their widths were set in device pixels, so at 200 percent a sketch shown in the view was as thin as an edge of the part, which does grow. The widths are named in `look` in pixels at 100 percent and go through `look.line_width`, which multiplies by the screen scale (never under 1): sketches 2 px, reference curves 2 px, the mark of a lost pick 2 px, the preview of reference geometry 2 px, the lines to pick a revolve axis from and the mark of a Select Other row 3 px, the shapes an error points at 4 px, curvature combs 1 px, the layers of the print and evaluate tools 2 px unless a tool asks for another width, and the dashed smooth edges 1 px. No value changed at 100 percent. Read from a real view: a sketch line is 2.2 px wide at 100 percent and 4.1 px at 200. A test fails for any width written as a bare number in the view's modules.
Status: Default
Reason: A sketch is twice as heavy as an edge by design; that should hold on every screen.

D2825: See-through amounts looked at again: regions and the mirror image changed, the graph ghost kept (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83 P6; follows D2760). How it was measured: pixels of a real view showed that the kernel mixes a see-through item with what is under it in linear light, and lights the item like any face (a picked region on the front face of the grey part was (95, 107, 163), the model gives the same to one step). `look.seen_through`, `look.lit` and `look.colour_gap` hold that, so the amounts are tested in all four themes without a screen. A tint often has the brightness of the face under it, so the measure is the colour gap in CIE L*a*b* (about 2 is the least step an eye sees, 10 is plain), not a contrast ratio. (1) Sketch regions, in the accent over the part: idle, under the cursor, picked, picked and under the cursor. With the old amounts (0.90, 0.70, 0.45, 0.35) the smallest step from one state to the next, over the top, front and side face of the grey part, was 3.5 for an idle region and 4.0 for the cursor over a picked one, both in the dark themes: an idle region was all but unseen there. Idle is now 0.85 and picked and under the cursor 0.30; hover and picked are unchanged. Every step is 5.8 or more in every theme. (2) The mirror image, in the reference grey at 0.65: every face of it stands 9.5 or more off the view at both its ends, so the amount is kept. But on the light themes its top and front face were 0.9 apart, and no amount helps (1.6 at 0.50): the image was a flat shadow with no form to compare with the part. It is now drawn with its edges, 1 px times the screen scale in the same grey, and reads as a see-through body. (3) The graph ghost, in the accent at the preview's 0.70 (set in D2760): every face stands 12.9 or more off the view, and over the part's top face it is 14 to 19 from the bare face with the part's edges showing through. Kept. Seen and left: a curved ghost shows two glints, from the kernel's default material, as every item has; IDEAS item 86.
Status: Default
Reason: Each state of a thing to click must be a step the eye sees in every theme, and a mirror image is there to compare shapes, which a flat shadow cannot do.

D2826: The tools and tests of the six view proposals, and what they found (2026-11-20, Phase 7D, IDEAS item 83; record). `tools/view_review_shots.py` has five more groups (`near`, `corner`, `wire`, `widths`, `see`) and the options `--scale` and `--samples`; it was run on `origin/main` (`90ee14a4`) for the before pictures and on the branch for the after pictures, at 100 and 200 percent. `tools/view_smoothing_measure.py` prints graphics memory, process memory and frame time of a real view for a number of samples, a part and a display style. `tools/view_line_steadiness.py` prints how evenly thin lines are drawn. All three need a screen and are run by hand. `tests/ui/test_view_proposals.py` checks D2820 to D2825 offscreen; `tests/ui/view_proposals_probe.py` reads a real view (the samples in use, the triad against its click areas, the rim, a cylinder in Wireframe, the width of a sketch line, a region's colour against the model) and its test runs it at 100, 150 and 200 percent with `FDCAD_VIEW_PIXELS=1`. Twelve pictures, six pairs, are in `docs/screenshots/view_proposals_2026-11-20/`. Found and not changed, all in IDEAS item 86: the hidden line styles turn a 200 feature part at under 6 frames a second; `tests/ui/test_view_look.py` leaves the kernel's owner class replaced, so `test_view_detect.py` fails when run after it (the suite runs them the other way round); glints on curved see-through items.
Status: Default
Reason: The next look at the view can start from the same pictures and numbers.

D2860: Third party notices are written from data, checked against the build (2026-11-20, owner approved the legal review's must fix items 1 and 2). `packaging/notices/*.toml` holds one entry per shipped project: name, exact version and how it is known, SPDX licence, copyright lines, the licence texts it needs, the patterns of the build files it covers, the platforms, the exact source archive or tag, whether it is GPL or LGPL, and whether anyone changed it. The licence texts are kept in `packaging/licenses`, fetched once from each project's own release tag (or copied from the installed package), so a build needs no network. `tools/third_party_notices.py write` turns this into `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` (plain text, not Markdown, so licence texts stay exactly as written) and `SOURCE_OFFER.md` at the repository root; a text two or more components use is printed once and named where it is used, and the GPL 3 points at `LICENSE`. `check` fails when the written files are out of date. `inventory` lists every DLL, pyd, so, dylib, framework library, zip and data folder of a build; `inventory-windows.txt` is that list for the folder build of 2026-11-20, with the version each file states. `check-dist` fails when a build file has no entry; the release workflow runs it on both platforms after the smoke test. Count: 116 entries, 68 for FDCAD's dependencies and the libraries inside them, 48 for the third party parts of Qt. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is gone.
Status: Default
Reason: About forty bundled components had no notice. Notices written by hand drift with every upgrade; a test that knows every shipped file does not.

D2861: Where the lists inside Qt and VTK come from (2026-11-20, D2860). Qt: the `qt_attribution.json` files of qtbase and qtimageformats at tag v6.12.0 (qtsvg has none), 48 entries, each with its own licence file or, when it has none, the SPDX text from qtbase `LICENSES`. Left out: tests, examples, tools, CMake helpers, testlib, and the Android, WebAssembly, Wayland, X11 (xcb), SQLite and D-Bus parts, none of which are in the libraries FDCAD ships. Kept even when one platform only (Windows D3D12, Wintab, macOS Cocoa): listing too much does no harm. VTK: the third party libraries that ship as their own DLL, plus the header only libraries the shipped VTK modules depend on (ExprTk, fast_float, KWIML, nlohmann JSON, PEGTL, UTF8-CPP, from their `vtk.module` files at v9.6.2), with versions from each `update.sh`.
Status: Default
Reason: The projects' own attribution data is the most exact list there is.

D2862: macOS facts come from the macOS wheels, not from a Mac build (2026-11-20, D2860). No Mac build was at hand. The file lists of the cadquery-ocp, vtk and numpy (cp313 arm64) and PySide6-Essentials and shiboken6 (universal2) wheels were read from PyPI without downloading the wheels (HTTP range requests on the zip index). They add jxrlib, {fmt} and libc++ inside OCP, libquadmath and the GCC run time inside numpy, and the Mac Qt plugins. The Mac Python's own libraries and the Mac builds of the OCP libraries were not checked file by file; the file names give the same versions as on Windows. `check-dist` on the Mac release job reports anything missed. Record a Mac inventory (`inventory dist/FDCAD.app --record packaging/notices/inventory-macos.txt`) the first time a Mac build is at hand.
Status: Default
Reason: Mac work is verified through CI only (CLAUDE.md 9.6).

D2863: Where the Open CASCADE, FreeImage and LibRaw binaries come from, and what that means for "unmodified" (2026-11-20, D2860). OCCT 8.0.1: the cadquery-ocp 8.0.1.1.0 wheel is made by CadQuery/ocp-build-system at tag v8.0.1.1.0 (`eace4e42`). It clones the OCCT tag V8_0_1, applies one patch (`switch-vtk-freetype-cmake-order.patch`, which only moves the FreeType section after the VTK section of `CMakeLists.txt`) and on Windows appends VTK link libraries to `TKIVtk/EXTERNLIB.cmake`. Both are build files; no OCCT source is changed. FDCAD changes nothing. FreeImage 3.18.0, LibRaw 0.22.2 and the image libraries come from conda-forge (micromamba environment `build-ocp`, `freeimage=3.18.*`, `freetype=2.12.*`). FreeImage is conda-forge build 25 (`h81f0cfa_25` on Windows, `h87663b4_25` on macOS, feedstock commit `436a9750`): the only build whose pins accept the shipped OpenEXR 3.4.15 and LibRaw 0.22.2. conda-forge patches FreeImage (eight patches and its own CMake files, to use the separate libraries), so the notices say "not changed by FDCAD" and name the recipe as part of the source, rather than "unmodified". LibRaw is built from the unchanged 0.22.2 source with LibRaw-cmake `eb98e432`; its recipe has no patches. FreeImage is used under the GPL 3, not the FreeImage Public License: the FIPL is based on the MPL 1.1, which the FSF lists as GPL incompatible. LibRaw is used under the LGPL 2.1, not the CDDL. FreeType, Zstandard and Qt's FreeType are used under their permissive licence, not the GPL 2. Versions the files do not state (Lerc 4.2.0, libdeflate 1.25, libffi 3.4.4, RapidJSON, pybind11, libc++, Eigen, Boost, the GCC run time) are marked as inferred in the notices, with how they were inferred.
Status: Default
Reason: The legal review asked to check the build origin before writing "unmodified".

D2864: The Windows build takes Python's own DLLs, never a copy on PATH (2026-11-20, found while listing the build). PyInstaller looks on PATH for the DLLs a module needs. Built from Git Bash, the bundle got `libssl-3-x64.dll` and `libcrypto-3-x64.dll` from `C:\Program Files\Git\ucrt64\bin` (an MSYS2 build of OpenSSL 3.5.9) instead of the Python install's. The spec now puts the Python folder and its `DLLs` folder first on PATH, and stops the build when any DLL comes from outside the project and the Python install.
Status: Default
Reason: What ships must not depend on the shell the build ran in.

D2865: Development only packages are kept out of the bundle (2026-11-20, legal review). numpy asks for PyYAML in a `try` (`numpy.__config__`) and its type stubs name typing_extensions, so PyInstaller bundled both whenever the dev group was installed. Neither is a runtime dependency (`uv.lock`: pre-commit needs PyYAML, mypy and pytest-qt need typing_extensions). The spec excludes `yaml`, `_yaml` and `typing_extensions`. A test works out the dev only packages from `uv.lock` and fails when the recorded inventory or the last build holds one of their modules.
Status: Default
Reason: Shipping what is not needed adds notices and size for nothing.

D2866: FDCAD's own copyright line (2026-11-20, owner brief). "Copyright (C) 2026 the FDCAD contributors" in the About box (`strings_help.ABOUT_COPYRIGHT`), the installer's `AppCopyright`, the Mac `NSHumanReadableCopyright` and the notices. No person's name. `LICENSE` is unchanged. README still ends with the D36 line "Copyright (C) 2026 Muffism.", left for the owner to decide.
Status: Default
Reason: GPL v3 section 5(d) counts a copyright notice among the appropriate legal notices of an interactive program.

D2867: How the notices ship (2026-11-20, D2860). The spec bundles `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` and `SOURCE_OFFER.md` as data (so the About box finds them, and on macOS they land in `Contents/Resources`), and copies them beside `FDCAD.exe` in `dist/FDCAD` (so the installer, which copies that folder, and the hand made folder zip carry them) and beside `FDCAD-portable.exe` in `dist`. The installer stops at compile time when one is missing, adds a Start menu shortcut to the notices, and shows the GPL as an information page (`InfoBeforeFile`) instead of an "I accept" page: the GPL needs no acceptance to run the program. `make_dmg.sh` copies the three files beside the app on the disk image and stops when one is missing. Help, About has the copyright line and a link to the notices and the source offer, which opens them on the Licenses tab; the Licenses tab lists the source offer too.
Status: Default
Reason: The notices must reach every person who gets a copy, whichever package they get.

D2868: Licence points left for a lawyer (2026-11-20, D2860). (1) Whether links to upstream source archives meet LGPL 2.1 section 6 and GPL 3 section 6, or whether the exact archives must be mirrored with each release; the written offer covers the gap meanwhile. (2) The written offer asks people to write "through the person or page you got FDCAD from", because the repository is private and there is no public contact address; whether that is enough under GPL 3 section 6(b), or a real address is needed. (3) Whether conda-forge's FreeImage patches and recipe must be offered as part of the Corresponding Source (the notices name them, to be safe). (4) The FreeImage licence choice (GPL 3, not the FIPL) and the LibRaw choice (LGPL 2.1, not the CDDL). (5) Whether the Microsoft Visual C++ DLLs need any notice beyond the one given. (6) The one file portable exe, whose LGPL libraries cannot be swapped in place: the source offer points to the folder build and to rebuilding from source, as LGPL 3 section 4(d)(0) allows. (7) The versions the files do not state and that are inferred (D2863), including the GCC version of the LGPL libquadmath in the Mac numpy wheel.
Status: Open
Reason: The owner asked for judgement calls to be written down, not guessed.

D2870: Contact address for the source offer (2026-11-20, owner). The written offer in `SOURCE_OFFER.md` asks people to write to FDCAD@proton.me, a mailbox the owner made for FDCAD, instead of "through the person or page you got FDCAD from". This settles point 2 of D2868. The wording lives in `packaging/notices/components.toml` and `tools/third_party_notices.py write` puts it in `SOURCE_OFFER.md`.
Status: Decided
Reason: GPL 3 section 6(b) wants an offer anyone holding the object code can act on; a fixed address works for a private and a public release, and keeps the owner's own address out of the files.

D2871: Problem reports the user sends from their own mail app (2026-11-20, owner). `fdcad.ui.help.report` builds a plain text report: system info, the last 300 lines of `fdcad.log`, the newest `crash.log` session that holds a fault (of the newest two sessions only, since the running session never holds one; at most 200 lines), then the error details and a note. It is saved as `FDCAD-report-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS.txt` in the log folder, put on the clipboard, and a `mailto:` link to `REPORT_ADDRESS` (FDCAD@proton.me, the D2870 address; a test checks it against `SOURCE_OFFER.md`) goes to `QDesktopServices.openUrl`. FDCAD sends nothing (CLAUDE.md 5.8 and 5.9): the user reads the message and presses Send. Privacy (`fdcad.ui.help.privacy`): the home folder becomes `<home>` in every spelling (`\` and `/`, doubled `\` as a repr shows it, any case, the 8.3 short name from `GetShortPathNameW`, and `HOME` when set), and the login name (`getpass.getuser()`, `USERNAME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, and the home folder's own name) becomes `<user>` as a whole word, in any case. The log folder line of Copy System Info is scrubbed the same way. The mail body is short (a question, the version, the OS, a one line summary and where the report is) and shows the report's place with `%USERPROFILE%` (Windows) or `~` instead of the home folder, so the user can still type it; it is fully percent encoded (spaces as %20, line breaks as %0D%0A) and kept under 1800 characters by shortening the summary, then the path. The summary is the last line of the trace, else the error message's first sentence, else "FDCAD closed unexpectedly"; from the Help menu it is "Reported from the Help menu". When no mail app opens, a box says where the report is and on the clipboard, with Open Folder. Where the user gets it: Report Problem beside Copy Details in every error box with details (so also the uncaught error box), which keeps the box open; Help, Diagnostics, Report a Problem, a plain menu item like Copy System Info (no command, so no icon); and after `crash_guard.collect` finds FDCAD closed unexpectedly, a Report Problem button in the status bar beside the message, because message bars belong to a part and no part is open yet at start. That button goes once used and otherwise stays for the session. Tests: `tests/conftest.py` replaces `report.open_mail` (and already `QDesktopServices.openUrl`) in every test, so no test opens a mail app or a folder.
Status: Decided
Reason: The owner wants reports that are easy to send, without FDCAD ever sending anything or the report carrying the user's name.

D2872: FDCAD goes public from a fresh repository (2026-11-22, owner). The owner made FDCAD a public project. The public repository `muffism/fdcad` starts from one commit holding the files of version 1.0.0, so the private history is not published: some of its commits carry the owner's real name and email, and its older commits hold the clean room record. The old repository is kept private as `muffism/fdcad-archive` with its full history. The clean room record and the legal review stay private, outside the repository. This ends the condition of D35 (private until the owner makes it public). The README copyright line now reads "the FDCAD contributors", as D2866 left open. CONTRIBUTING.md gains the clean room rules for outside contributors, and SECURITY.md says where to report a security problem.
Status: Decided
Reason: A fresh start publishes only what the owner chose; rewriting 1,500 commits could miss something in an old one.
